children.translated_text: From whom arise the birth and other states of this world, who, directly and indirectly, is aware of purposes and self-ruling;

children.text: tene brahma hṛdā ya ādikavaye muhyanti yat sūrayaḥ
children.translated_text: who imparted brahma in the heart to the first poet, and about whom the wise become bewildered;
in whom, as with fire, water, and earth, interchange makes the threefold creation appear real though false;

children.text: dhāmnā svena sadā nirastakuhakaṃ satyaṃ paraṃ dhīmahi ||
children.translated_text: by whose own radiance illusion is forever dispelled: let us meditate on the supreme truth.
Here the highest <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), with deceit cast away, is for the good who are free from envy;

children.text: vedyaṃ vāstavam atra vastu śivadaṃ tāpatrayonmūlanam
children.translated_text: here the real substance, bestowing blessedness and uprooting the threefold suffering, is to be known.

children.text: śrīmadbhāgavate mahāmunikṛte kiṃ vā parair īśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: In the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s>, composed by the great sage, what need is there of other works? The Lord

children.text: sadyo hṛdy avarudhyate 'tra kṛtibhiḥ śuśrūṣubhis tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: is immediately held fast in the heart here by the capable who wish to hear, at that very moment.
The ripened fruit fallen from the wish-fulfilling tree of the Veda,
joined with the nectar-fluid from <s>Śuka</s>'s mouth,
drink the <s>Bhāgavata</s>, the abode of rasa,
again and again, O connoisseurs and sensitive people on earth.
In <s>Naimiṣa</s>, the field of the sleepless Lord, sages led by <s>Śaunaka</s>
sat in a sacrifice lasting a thousand years for the heavenly world.
One day those sages, after offering into the fires in the morning,

children.text: satkṛtaṃ sūtam āsīnaṃ papracchur idam ādarāt ||
children.translated_text: respectfully asked this of <s>Sūta</s>, who had been honored and was seated.
The sages said:
You, O faultless one, have indeed recounted and also studied the purāṇas together with the itihāsas,

children.text: ākhyātāny apy adhītāni dharmaśāstrāṇi yāny uta ||
children.translated_text: and whatever <s>dharmaśāstras</s> (treatises on duty) there are.
Those which the blessed <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, best of knowers of the Veda,

children.text: anye ca munayaḥ sūta parāvaravido viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: and other sages, O <s>Sūta</s>, know as knowers of higher and lower things.

children.text: vettha tvaṃ saumya tat sarvaṃ tattvatas tadanugrahāt
children.translated_text: You know all that truly, gentle one, through his favor;

children.text: brūyuḥ snigdhasya śiṣyasya guravo guhyam apyuta ||
children.translated_text: teachers tell even a secret to an affectionate disciple.
Therefore, long-lived one, what has been decisively determined by you, plainly and in each case,

children.text: puṃsām ekāntataḥ śreyastan naḥ śaṃsitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: that which is absolutely the highest good for human beings, you ought to tell us.

children.text: prāyeṇālpāyuṣaḥ sabhya kalāv asmin yuge janāḥ
children.translated_text: Generally, worthy sir, people in this Kali age are short-lived,
sluggish, of very poor understanding, unlucky, and afflicted.
There are many things to be heard, and many kinds of rites, in separate divisions;

children.text: ataḥ sādho 'tra yat sāraṃ samuddhṛtya manīṣayā
children.translated_text: therefore, good man, extracting here the essence with your discernment,
tell it for the welfare of beings, by which the self becomes fully serene.

children.text: sūta jānāsi bhadraṃ te bhagavān sātvatāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>, you know, may there be good for you, the blessed Lord, master of the <s>Sātvatas</s>,
who was born from <s>Devakī</s> as son of <s>Vasudeva</s> for the sake of accomplishing his purpose.
For us who are eager to hear, dear one, you ought to describe him,

children.text: yasyāvatāro bhūtānāṃ kṣemāya ca bhavāya ca ||
children.translated_text: whose descent is for the security and prosperity of beings.

children.text: āpannaḥ saṃsṛtiṃ ghorāṃ yan nāma vivaśo gṛṇan
children.translated_text: One who has fallen into terrible transmigration, uttering his name helplessly,

children.text: tataḥ sadyo vimucyeta yadbibheti svayaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: would at once be freed from it; fear itself fears him.
Those sages who take refuge at his feet, O <s>Sūta</s>, and whose path is tranquility,
purify at once those touched by them, while the waters of the heavenly river purify only through repeated service.
Who, desiring purification, would not hear the fame of that Lord,
whose deeds are worthy of praise in sacred verses and whose fame removes the stain of Kali?
His noble deeds, sung all around by the wise,

children.text: brūhi naḥ śraddadhānānāṃ līlayā dadhataḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: tell us, who have faith, as he playfully assumes portions.
Then, wise one, recount the auspicious tales of <s>Hari</s>'s descents,
of the Lord freely performing playful acts through his own <s>māyā</s> (creative power).
But we are not satiated with the prowess of him who is praised in the finest verses,

children.text: yacchṛṇvatāṃ rasajñānāṃ svādu svādu pade pade ||
children.translated_text: which, for knowers of rasa who hear it, is sweet, sweet at every step.

children.text: kṛtavān kila karmāṇi saha rāmeṇa keśavaḥ
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Keśava</s>, together with <s>Rāma</s>, surely performed deeds
beyond mortal measure, hidden in a deceptive human form.

children.text: kalim āgatam ājñāya kṣetre 'smin vaiṣṇave vayam
children.translated_text: Knowing that Kali had arrived, we
are seated in this Vaiṣṇava field through a long sacrifice, with time for the story of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ naḥ saṃdarśito dhātrā dustaraṃ nistitīrṣatām
children.translated_text: You have been shown to us by the Creator as we wish to cross over
Kali, hard to cross and stealing men's clarity, like a helmsman across the ocean.
Tell us: when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, lord of yoga, friend of brahman, armor of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: svāṃ kāṣṭhām adhunopete dharmaḥ kaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: has now gone to his own station, to what refuge has <s>dharma</s> gone?
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
Thus delighted by the well-formed questions of the brahmins, the son of <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>,
honoring their words in return, began to speak.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: yaṃ pravrajantam anupetam apetakṛtyaṃ dvaipāyano virahakātara ājuhāva
children.translated_text: I bow to that sage, the heart of all beings, whom <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, distressed by separation, called after as he went forth, uninitiated into household duties and leaving obligations behind,

children.text: putreti tanmayatayā taravo 'bhinedus taṃ sarvabhūtahṛdayaṃ munim ānato 'smi ||
children.translated_text: crying, 'my son!' and, because they were absorbed in him, the trees echoed back.

children.text: yaḥ svānubhāvam akhilaśrutisāram ekam adhyātmadīpam atititīrṣatāṃ tamo 'ndham
children.translated_text: I approach as guru of the sages that son of <s>Vyāsa</s>, who, out of compassion for transmigrating beings wishing to cross the blind darkness,

children.text: saṃsāriṇāṃ karuṇayāha purāṇaguhyaṃ taṃ vyāsasūnum upayāmi guruṃ munīnām ||
children.translated_text: spoke the hidden purāṇa, the single lamp of the self and essence of all revelation.
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,

children.text: devīṃ sarasvatīṃ vyāsaṃ tato jayam udīrayet ||
children.translated_text: to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> and to <s>Vyāsa</s>, then one should utter victory.
O sages, I have been well asked by you about the welfare of the world,
since you have asked the question about <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, by which the self becomes fully serene.

children.text: sa vai puṃsāṃ paro dharmo yato bhaktiradhokṣaje
children.translated_text: That indeed is the highest <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty) for human beings, from which there is devotion to <s>Adhokṣaja</s>,
without motive and unobstructed, by which the self becomes fully serene.
When <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (discipline of devotion) is applied to the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
it quickly produces detachment and knowledge, which is without motive.
The <s>dharma</s> (religious duty) well performed by human beings which, toward the tales of <s>Viṣvaksena</s>,

children.text: notpādayedyadi ratiṃ śrama eva hi kevalam ||
children.translated_text: does not produce delight, is only toil and nothing more.
For <s>dharma</s> (duty) whose aim is liberation is not meant to serve wealth;

children.text: nārthasya dharmaikāntasya kāmo lābhāya hi smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the aim of wealth wholly devoted to <s>dharma</s> is not held to be the attainment of desire.
The aim of desire is not gratification of the senses; its proper gain is only enough for one to live.
The aim of life is inquiry into reality, not the objects gained here through actions.

children.text: vadanti tat tattvavidastattvaṃ yaj jñānam advayam
children.translated_text: Those who know reality say that that reality is nondual knowledge,
called <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Paramātman</s>, and <s>Bhagavān</s>.
Sages who have faith, endowed with knowledge and detachment,
see the self within the self through devotion received by hearing.
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, by people according to the divisions of varṇa and āśrama,
the perfection of one's own well-performed dharma is the satisfaction of <s>Hari</s>.
Therefore, with one-pointed mind, the Blessed Lord, lord of the Sātvatas,

children.text: śrotavyaḥ kīrtitavyaś ca dhyeyaḥ pūjyaśca nityadā ||
children.translated_text: is always to be heard about, praised, meditated on, and worshiped.
Those wise ones who are yoked by constant meditation on him

children.text: chindanti kovidāstasya ko na kuryāt kathāratim ||
children.translated_text: cut the binding knot of karma; who would not delight in his story?
For one who wishes to hear, has faith, and has a taste for the story of <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
such taste arises, O brahmins, through service to the great and resort to holy places.
For those who listen to his own stories, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose hearing and praise are meritorious,
dwelling within the heart, removes inauspicious things, as the friend of the good.
When inauspicious things are almost destroyed by constant service to the <s>Bhāgavata</s>,
firm devotion arises toward the Blessed Lord who is praised in the highest verses.
Then the states born of rajas and tamas, such as desire and greed,

children.text: ceta etair anāviddhaṃ sthitaṃ sattve prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: no longer pierce the mind; established in sattva, it becomes clear.
Thus, for one whose mind is serene through the yoga of devotion to the Lord,
knowledge of the reality of the Lord arises in one who is free from attachment.
The knot of the heart is split, and all doubts are cut away;
his karmas are exhausted when the Lord as the self is seen directly.

children.text: ato vai kavayo nityaṃ bhaktiṃ paramayā mudā
children.translated_text: Therefore seers always, with supreme joy,
practice devotion to the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, which brings peace to the self.

children.text: sattvaṃ rajastama iti prakṛterguṇāstair yuktaḥ paramapuruṣa eka ihāsya dhatte
children.translated_text: Sattva, rajas, and tamas are the guṇas of prakṛti; joined with them, the one supreme Person here assumes

children.text: sthityādaye hariviriñcihareti saṃjñāḥ śreyāṃsi tatra khalu sattvatanor nṝṇāṃ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the names <s>Hari</s>, <s>Viriñci</s>, and <s>Hara</s> for preservation and the rest; among these, benefits for human beings indeed come from the body of sattva.
From earth-born wood comes smoke, and from that comes fire, which is formed by the three Vedas;
so from tamas comes rajas, and from that comes sattva, by which <s>brahman</s> is seen.
Therefore, in the beginning, the sages worshiped the Blessed <s>Adhokṣaja</s>,

children.text: sattvaṃ viśuddhaṃ kṣemāya kalpante ye 'nu tān iha ||
children.translated_text: pure sattva; those who follow them here become fit for well-being.
Those who desire liberation, abandoning the lords of beings with terrible forms,
being peaceful and free from envy, worship the portions of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
People whose natures are rajas and tamas worship those of similar character,
such as ancestors, spirits, and Prajāpatis, desiring prosperity, power, and progeny.
The Vedas have <s>Vāsudeva</s> as their goal; sacrifices have <s>Vāsudeva</s> as their goal;
yoga has <s>Vāsudeva</s> as its goal, and ritual acts have <s>Vāsudeva</s> as their goal.
Knowledge has <s>Vāsudeva</s> as its goal; austerity has <s>Vāsudeva</s> as its goal;
dharma has <s>Vāsudeva</s> as its goal, and the final destination has <s>Vāsudeva</s> as its goal.
He alone, the Blessed Lord, created this in the beginning by his own māyā,
which has the forms of being and nonbeing and consists of guṇas, while he, the all-pervading one, is without guṇas.

children.text: tayā vilasiteṣv eṣu guṇeṣu guṇavān iva
children.translated_text: When these guṇas are displayed by that māyā, he appears as if endowed with guṇas,
having entered within and becoming manifest through consciousness.
For just as one carefully kindled fire in pieces of wood, its own wombs,

children.text: nāneva bhāti viśvātmā bhūteṣu ca tathā pumān ||
children.translated_text: appears as if many, so the universal self, the Person, appears among beings.
He, entering into beings made by himself with states composed of guṇas,
subtle elements, senses, and mind, experiences their qualities among beings.

children.text: bhāvayaty eṣa sattvena lokān vai lokabhāvanaḥ
children.translated_text: By sattva this creator of worlds sustains the worlds,
delighting in playful descents among gods, animals, humans, and others.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The Blessed Lord assumed the cosmic Person's form, together with mahat and the other principles,
arisen with sixteen parts at the beginning, with the desire to create the worlds.
As he lay upon the waters, spreading out yogic sleep,
from the lotus in the lake of his navel arose <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the creators of the universe.
By the arrangement of whose limbs the expanse of the worlds was fashioned.

children.text: tadvai bhagavato rūpaṃ viśuddhaṃ sattvam ūrjitam
children.translated_text: That form of the Blessed Lord is indeed pure, powerful sattva;
they behold that form with abundant vision, wonderful with a thousand feet, thighs, arms, and faces.
It has a thousand heads, ears, eyes, and noses, shining with a thousand crowns, garments, and earrings.
This is the source, the imperishable seed, of the many avatāras,
by a portion of whose portion gods, animals, humans, and others are created.

children.text: sa eva prathamaṃ devaḥ kaumāraṃ sargam āśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He himself, the first deity, took on the Kumāra creation;
he practiced the difficult, unbroken brahmacarya.
Second, for the welfare of this world, when the earth had gone down to <s>Rasātala</s>,
<s>Yajñeśa</s>, intending to raise it up, took on a boar body.

children.text: tṛtīyam ṛṣisargaṃ vai devarṣitvam upetya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Third, in the creation of seers, he assumed the status of a divine seer,

children.text: tantraṃ sātvatam ācaṣṭa naiṣkarmyaṃ karmaṇāṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: and taught the Sātvata tantra, from which comes the non-action of actions.
In the fourth, in the creation of the portions of dharma, as the sages <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
he performed difficult austerity endowed with self-restraint.
Fifth, named <s>Kapila</s>, lord of the siddhas, when it had been lost through time,
he proclaimed Sāṃkhya, the determination of the group of principles, to <s>Āsuri</s>.
Sixth, chosen by <s>Anasūyā</s>, he obtained birth as the son of <s>Atri</s>;
he taught ānvīkṣikī, philosophical inquiry, to <s>Alarka</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, and others.
Then, seventh, as <s>Yajña</s>, he was born from <s>Ākūti</s> and <s>Ruci</s>;
with the hosts of gods headed by the <s>Yāmas</s>, he protected the age of <s>Svāyambhuva</s>.
In the eighth, <s>Urukrama</s> was born from <s>Nābhi</s> in <s>Merudevī</s>;
he showed the path honored by all āśramas for the steadfast.
Asked by the seers, he accepted a ninth, kingly body.

children.text: dugdhemām oṣadhīr viprās tenāyaṃ sa uśattamaḥ
children.translated_text: The learned brahmins milked this earth for herbs; therefore he is that most excellent one.
He assumed the form of a fish at the flood of the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> age.
After placing <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s> on a boat, he protected him.
When the gods and asuras were churning the ocean, he held up <s>Mandara</s> mountain.
The mighty lord, in his eleventh manifestation, bore it on his back in the form of a tortoise.
The twelfth was <s>Dhanvantari</s>, and the thirteenth indeed was another form.

children.text: apāyayat surān anyān mohinyā mohayan striyā
children.translated_text: As <s>Mohinī</s>, bewildering the others by means of a woman, he caused the gods to drink the nectar.
Bearing the fourteenth form, <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, he seized the powerful lord of the Daityas.
He tore him on his lap with his claws, as a carpenter splits a reed.
Making himself the fifteenth form, a little dwarf, he went to the sacrifice of <s>Bali</s>.
Asking for three steps of ground, he intended to take back the threefold heaven.
In the sixteenth avatāra, seeing kings who were hostile to brahmins,
he became angry and twenty-one times made the earth devoid of kṣatriyas.
Then, in the seventeenth, he was born from <s>Parāśara</s> in <s>Satyavatī</s>.
Seeing that men had little understanding, he divided the branches of the tree of the Veda.
Having assumed divine status among men in order to accomplish the work of the gods,
thereafter he performed heroic deeds such as the restraint of the ocean.
In the nineteenth and twentieth births, having taken birth among the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
Bhagavān, as <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, removed the burden of the earth.
Then, when the Kali age has begun, for the delusion of the enemies of the gods,
<s>Buddha</s>, by name, the son of <s>Añjana</s>, will arise among the <s>Kīkaṭas</s>.
And at the junction of the age, when kings are mostly brigands,
the lord of the world will be born as <s>Kalki</s>, bearing the name of the son of <s>Viṣṇuyaśas</s>.
The avatāras of <s>Hari</s>, the treasury of sattva, are indeed countless, O brahmins,
just as thousands of streams flow from an inexhaustible lake.
Sages, Manus, gods, and the greatly powerful sons of Manu,
together with the Prajāpatis, are all remembered as portions of <s>Hari</s> alone.

children.text: ete cāṃśakalāḥ puṃsaḥ kṛṣṇastu bhagavān svayam ||
children.translated_text: These are parts and partial parts of the Puruṣa, but <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is Bhagavān himself.
Age after age they show mercy to the world, which is troubled by the enemies of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: janma guhyaṃ bhagavato ya etat prayato naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The man who, purified and devoted, recites this secret birth of Bhagavān
morning and evening with devotion is released from the mass of sorrows.
This form of Bhagavān, who is formless and whose self is consciousness,
is fashioned in the self by the qualities of māyā, beginning with mahat.
As a mass of clouds appears in the sky, or earthly dust in the wind,
so visible objecthood is superimposed upon the seer by the unintelligent.
Beyond this is that unmanifest reality, not enlarged by unfolded qualities,
and because it is not an object seen or heard, that is the jīva by which rebirth occurs.
Where these forms of existence and nonexistence, made in the self by ignorance,
are denied by self-awareness, that is the vision of Brahman.
When this goddess Māyā has ceased, then discriminating understanding
knows him as fully attained; he is exalted in his own greatness.

children.text: evaṃ ca janmāni karmāṇi hy akartur ajanasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus poets describe the births and deeds of him who is unborn and a non-agent,
the lord of the heart, whose mysteries are hidden in the Vedas.

children.text: sa vā idaṃ viśvam amoghalīlaḥ sṛjaty avaty atti na sajjate 'smin ||
children.translated_text: He, whose play is unfailing, creates, protects, and consumes this universe, yet is not attached to it.

children.text: bhūteṣu cāntarhita ātmatantraḥ ṣāḍvargikaṃ jighrati ṣaḍguṇeśaḥ
children.translated_text: Hidden within beings and self-governed, the lord of the six qualities perceives the sixfold field.

children.text: na cāsya kaścin nipuṇena dhātur avaiti jantuḥ kumanīṣa ūtīḥ ||
children.translated_text: No creature of poor understanding knows, even by cleverness, the purposes of this creator.

children.text: nāmāni rūpāṇi manovacobhiḥ saṃtanvato naṭacaryām ivājñaḥ
children.translated_text: He extends names and forms through mind and speech, like an actor’s performance unknown to the ignorant.

children.text: sa veda dhātuḥ padavīṃ parasya durantavīryasya rathāṅgapāṇeḥ ||
children.translated_text: He knows the path of the supreme creator, the wielder of the discus and of unfathomable power,
who without deceit worships the fragrance of his lotus feet through constant service.
Blessed indeed here are the devotees who thus, toward <s>Vāsudeva</s>, lord of all worlds,

children.text: kurvanti sarvātmakam ātmabhāvaṃ na yatra bhūyaḥ parivarta ugraḥ
children.translated_text: make their disposition wholly self-dedicated, where there is no further terrible return.
This <s>Purāṇa</s> called the <s>Bhāgavata</s>, equal to Brahman,
telling the deeds of the one praised in excellent verses, was composed by the blessed seer.
For the supreme good of the world, it is blessed, a great path to welfare.
He caused his son, the best of self-possessed men, to receive it.
It was drawn out as the very essence of all the Vedas and Itihāsas.
He then recited it to the great king <s>Parīkṣit</s>,
who was fasting until death on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, surrounded by supreme sages.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had gone to his own abode, together with dharma, knowledge, and the rest,
this sun of a Purāṇa has now arisen in Kali for those whose sight is lost.
There, O brahmins, while the highly brilliant brahmin-seer was reciting it,
I too learned it there, seated by his favor.
So I shall cause you to hear it as I learned it and according to my understanding.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
After praising <s>Sūta</s>, who was speaking thus, among the sages engaged in the long sacrificial session,
the aged house-chief, the Bahvṛca <s>Śaunaka</s>, addressed him.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: sūta sūta mahābhāga vada no vadatāṃ vara
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>, O <s>Sūta</s>, greatly fortunate one, best of speakers, tell us

children.text: kathāṃ bhāgavatīṃ puṇyāṃ yadāha bhagavāñ chukaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the holy <s>Bhāgavata</s> story that the blessed <s>Śuka</s> spoke.

children.text: kasmin yuge pravṛtteyaṃ sthāne vā kena hetunā
children.translated_text: In what age did this begin, in what place, and for what reason?

children.text: kutaḥ saṃcoditaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛtavān saṃhitāṃ muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: By what prompting did <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the sage, compose the Saṃhitā?
His son was a great yogin, equal-sighted and free from conceptual division,
single-minded, sleepless, hidden; he moved about as if he were a fool.

children.text: dṛṣṭvānuyāntam ṛṣim ātmajam apyanagnaṃ devyo hriyā paridadhurna sutasya citram
children.translated_text: Seeing the sage, even his own son, following him naked, the divine women covered themselves from shame; toward the son, strangely, they did not.

children.text: tadvīkṣya pṛcchati munau jagadustavāsti strīpumbhidā na tu sutasya viviktadṛṣṭeḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, when the sage asked them, they said, “For you there is distinction between woman and man, but not for your son, whose vision is pure.”
How was he noticed by the townspeople when he had reached the <s>Kurujāṅgala</s> country,
wandering in <s>Gajasāhvaya</s> like a mad, mute, and dull-witted man?
And how, dear father, did the conversation of the royal sage descended from <s>Pāṇḍu</s> with the sage

children.text: saṃvādaḥ samabhūt tāta yatraiṣā sātvatī śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: come about, in which this <s>Sātvata</s> sacred teaching was given?
For that greatly fortunate pilgrim remains in the houses of householders only for the time of milking a cow,
thereby making that dwelling into a place of pilgrimage.
O <s>Sūta</s>, they call the son of <s>Abhimanyu</s> the foremost of the <s>Bhāgavatas</s>;

children.text: tasya janma mahāścaryaṃ karmāṇi ca gṛṇīhi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: tell us of his most wondrous birth and of his deeds.

children.text: sa samrāṭ kasya vā hetoḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ mānavardhanaḥ
children.translated_text: For what reason did that emperor, the increaser of the honor of the <s>Pāṇḍus</s>,
sit down for fasting unto death on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, disregarding the sovereignty of an overlord?

children.text: namanti yatpādaniketam ātmanaḥ śivāya hānīya dhanāni śatravaḥ
children.translated_text: Enemies bowed at the resting-place of his feet, bringing wealth for their own welfare;

children.text: kathaṃ sa vīraḥ śriyam aṅga dustyajāṃ yuvaiṣatotsraṣṭum aho sahāsubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: how then, dear one, did that hero desire to abandon such hard-to-renounce fortune together with his life-breaths?

children.text: śivāya lokasya bhavāya bhūtaye ya uttamaślokaparāyaṇā janāḥ
children.translated_text: Those people who are devoted to <s>Uttamaśloka</s> live for the welfare, becoming, and prosperity of the world,

children.text: jīvanti nātmārtham asau parāśrayaṃ mumoca nirvidya kutaḥ kalevaram ||
children.translated_text: not for their own sake. Why then did he, becoming disillusioned, cast off his body, which was a refuge for others?

children.text: tat sarvaṃ naḥ samācakṣva pṛṣṭo yadiha kiṃcana
children.translated_text: Tell us all of that, whatever we have asked here,

children.text: manye tvāṃ viṣaye vācāṃ snātam anyatra chāndasāt ||
children.translated_text: for I think you are thoroughly immersed in the whole field of speech, apart from the Vedic metres.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When <s>Dvāpara</s> had arrived, in the third turn of the yuga-cycle,
the yogin born from <s>Parāśara</s>, through <s>Vāsavī</s>, was born as a portion of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: sa kadācit sarasvatyā upaspṛśya jalaṃ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Once, after touching the water of the <s>Sarasvatī</s> and becoming pure,
he sat alone in a secluded place as the orb of the sun rose.
That sage, knower of the higher and the lower, saw that through time, whose force is unmanifest,
a confusion of the duties proper to the ages had arisen on earth in age after age.

children.text: bhautikānāṃ ca bhāvānāṃ śaktihrāsaṃ ca tatkṛtam
children.translated_text: He saw also the decline in the powers of material beings caused by that,
and people who were faithless, lacking strength of being, dull-minded, and short-lived.
Seeing with divine sight that people were unfortunate,
the unfailing seer reflected on what would be beneficial for all classes and life-stages.

children.text: cāturhotraṃ karma śuddhaṃ prajānāṃ vīkṣya vaidikam
children.translated_text: Seeing that the pure Vedic rite of the four priests was for the people,
he divided the one Veda into four forms for the continuity of sacrifice.
The four Vedas called <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Atharvan</s> were drawn out,
and the <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s> are called the fifth Veda.
Among them <s>Paila</s> became the bearer of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, and the poet <s>Jaimini</s> the chanter of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>;
<s>Vaiśampāyana</s> alone was deeply versed in the <s>Yajus</s> texts as well.
The stern sage <s>Sumantu</s> became the master of the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> texts,
and my father <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s> was the master of the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s>.

children.text: ta eta ṛṣayo vedaṃ svaṃ svaṃ vyasyann anekadhā
children.translated_text: These sages divided each his own Veda in many ways,
and through their pupils, their pupils' pupils, and those pupils again, those Vedas became branched into schools.
So that those Vedas might be retained by men of dull intellect,
the blessed <s>Vyāsa</s>, compassionate toward the wretched, acted in this way.
For women, <s>Śūdras</s>, and relatives of twice-born men, the threefold Veda is not within hearing;
for those confused about the good of action, welfare might arise here in this way.

children.text: iti bhāratam ākhyānaṃ kṛpayā muninā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, the sage compassionately composed the narrative called the <s>Bhārata</s>.

children.text: evaṃ pravṛttasya sadā bhūtānāṃ śreyasi dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: O twice-born ones, although he was always engaged in this way for the welfare of beings,
his heart was still not satisfied by that all-embracing work.
With his heart not fully pleased, on the pure bank of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
he remained in solitude, reflecting, and, as a knower of <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), said this:
With firm vows, I have honored the Vedic hymns, the teachers, and the fires,
and without deceit I have accepted their instruction.
Under the title of the <s>Bhārata</s>, I have displayed the meaning of the sacred tradition,
where <s>dharma</s> and the other aims are visible even to women, <s>Śūdras</s>, and others.

children.text: tathāpi bata me daihyo hy ātmā caivātmanā vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: And yet, alas, my embodied self, though inwardly vast through the Self,
appears as if unfulfilled, deficient in the radiance of brahman, O best of the virtuous.

children.text: kiṃ vā bhāgavatā dharmā na prāyeṇa nirūpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Or perhaps the <s>Bhāgavata</s> dharmas have for the most part not been expounded,

children.text: priyāḥ paramahaṃsānāṃ ta eva hy acyutapriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those which are dear to the <s>Paramahaṃsas</s> and indeed dear to <s>Acyuta</s>.
As he was thinking of himself in this way as incomplete and was distressed,
<s>Nārada</s> came to the previously mentioned hermitage of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Recognizing him at once, the sage rose up as he arrived
and worshiped <s>Nārada</s>, who is worshiped by the gods, according to rule.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: atha taṃ sukham āsīna upāsīnaṃ bṛhacchravāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when he was seated comfortably and the great-famed one was sitting near him,

children.text: devarṣiḥ prāha viprarṣiṃ vīṇāpāṇiḥ smayann iva ||
children.translated_text: the divine sage, holding a vīṇā in his hand and as if smiling, addressed the brahmin sage.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
O son of <s>Parāśara</s>, greatly fortunate one, is your bodily self,

children.text: parituṣyati śārīra ātmā mānasa eva vā ||
children.translated_text: or your mental self, satisfied by yourself?
What you wished to know has been well accomplished, and it is very wonderful,
for you have made the <s>Bhārata</s>, enlarged with every meaning.

children.text: jijñāsitam adhītaṃ ca brahma yat tat sanātanam
children.translated_text: The eternal brahman too has been investigated and studied;
nevertheless, my lord, you grieve for yourself as if you had not achieved your purpose.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: astyeva me sarvam idaṃ tvayoktaṃ tathāpi nātmā parituṣyate me
children.translated_text: All this that you have said is indeed present in me; nevertheless my self is not satisfied.
I ask you about the hidden root of that, profound in understanding, for you are one whose self is born from <s>Ātmabhū</s>.

children.text: sa vai bhavān veda samastaguhyam upāsito yat puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed you know the whole secret, because you have worshiped that ancient Person,
the lord of the higher and the lower, who by mind alone creates, preserves, and consumes the universe through the guṇas, while remaining unattached.

children.text: tvaṃ paryaṭann arka iva trilokīm antaścaro vāyurivātmasākṣī
children.translated_text: You wander through the three worlds like the sun, and, like the wind, move within as the witness of selves.

children.text: parāvare brahmaṇi dharmato vrataiḥ snātasya me nyūnam alaṃ vicakṣva ||
children.translated_text: Tell me fully the deficiency in me, who by <s>dharma</s> and vows have bathed in the higher and lower brahman.
The venerable <s>Nārada</s> said:
The spotless fame of the Blessed Lord has, for the most part, not been proclaimed by you.

children.text: yenaivāsau na tuṣyeta manye taddarśanaṃ khilam ||
children.translated_text: By that by which he himself would not be satisfied, I think that presentation is incomplete.
Just as <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty) and the other aims have been recounted by the best of sages,

children.text: na tathā vāsudevasya mahimā hy anuvarṇitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so the greatness of <s>Vāsudeva</s> has not, indeed, been described.

children.text: na yad vacaś citrapadaṃ hareryaśo jagatpavitraṃ pragṛṇīta karhicit
children.translated_text: Speech whose ornate words never at any time proclaim the fame of <s>Hari</s>, which purifies the world,

children.text: tadvāyasaṃ tīrtham uśanti mānasā na yatra haṃsā niramanty uśikkṣayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise regard as a place of pilgrimage for crows, where swans do not delight, however pure their dwelling.
But that creation of speech is a revolution against the sins of people, in which, even if each verse is irregularly composed,

children.text: nāmānyanantasya yaśo 'ṅkitāni yat śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇanti sādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the names of <s>Ananta</s>, marked with his glory, are heard, sung, and uttered by the good.

children.text: naiṣkarmyam apyacyutabhāvavarjitaṃ na śobhate jñānam alaṃ nirañjanam
children.translated_text: Even <s>naiṣkarmya</s> (freedom from works), and spotless knowledge enough in itself, does not shine when devoid of feeling for <s>Acyuta</s>.

children.text: kutaḥ punaḥ śaśvadabhadram īśvare na cārpitaṃ karma yadapyakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: How much less, then, does action, always inauspicious and not offered to the Lord, shine, even if it is without selfish motive?

children.text: atho mahābhāga bhavān amoghadṛk śuciśravāḥ satyarato dhṛtavrataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, greatly fortunate one, you whose vision is unfailing, whose fame is pure, who are devoted to truth and firm in vow,
remember in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) the deeds of <s>Urukrama</s>, for release from all bondage.
For one who wishes to speak anything otherwise, with a separate vision, through forms and names fashioned by that power,

children.text: na karhicit kvāpi ca duḥsthitā matir labheta vātāhatanaurivāspadam ||
children.translated_text: the mind, badly situated, would never anywhere find a foundation, like a boat struck by the wind.
For one who, in the name of <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty), instructs what is blameworthy to people naturally attached to it, there is a great transgression.

children.text: yadvākyato dharma itītaraḥ sthito na manyate tasya nivāraṇaṃ janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, taking his statement as '<s>dharma</s>,' the other person remains fixed and does not think that it should be restrained.

children.text: vicakṣaṇo 'syārhati vedituṃ vibhor anantapārasya nivṛttitaḥ sukham
children.translated_text: The discerning man is fit to understand, through withdrawal, the happiness of the Lord, whose far shore is endless.

children.text: pravartamānasya guṇairanātmanas tato bhavān darśaya ceṣṭitaṃ vibhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who moves on through the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and is not self-possessed, therefore you should show the deeds of the Lord.

children.text: tyaktvā svadharmaṃ caraṇāmbujaṃ harer bhajann apakvo 'tha patet tato yadi
children.translated_text: If someone, abandoning his <s>svadharma</s> (own duty), worships the lotus feet of <s>Hari</s>, and then, still immature, falls from that,

children.text: yatra kva vābhadram abhūdamuṣya kiṃ ko vārtha āpto 'bhajatāṃ svadharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: what misfortune has happened to him anywhere? And what gain has one obtained who does not worship, though he keeps to his own <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: tasyaiva hetoḥ prayateta kovido na labhyate yadbhramatām uparyadhaḥ
children.translated_text: For that alone the wise person should strive, which is not obtained by those wandering above and below.

children.text: tal labhyate duḥkhavadanyataḥ sukhaṃ kālena sarvatra gabhīraraṃhasā ||
children.translated_text: Happiness, like suffering, is obtained from another source in due time everywhere, by time with its deep force.

children.text: na vai jano jātu kathaṃcanāvrajen mukundasevyanyavad aṅga saṃsṛtim
children.translated_text: A person who has served <s>Mukunda</s> never, in any way, returns to <s>saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration) like others, dear one.

children.text: smaran mukundāṅghryupagūhanaṃ punar vihātum icchen na rasagraho janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Remembering the embrace of <s>Mukunda</s>'s feet, a person who has tasted the rasa would not wish to abandon it again.

children.text: idaṃ hi viśvaṃ bhagavān ivetaro yato jagatsthānanirodhasambhavāḥ
children.translated_text: This universe is indeed the Lord, and yet it is other, since from him arise the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the world.

children.text: taddhi svayaṃ veda bhavāṃstathāpi te prādeśamātraṃ bhavataḥ pradarśitam ||
children.translated_text: You yourself know that; nevertheless only a small portion of your own nature has been shown to you.

children.text: tvam ātmanātmānam avehy amoghadṛk parasya puṃsaḥ paramātmanaḥ kalām
children.translated_text: You, by your own self, should understand yourself, O unfailing seer, as a portion of the supreme person, the <s>Paramātman</s> (supreme self).

children.text: ajaṃ prajātaṃ jagataḥ śivāya tan mahānubhāvābhyudayo 'dhigaṇyatām ||
children.translated_text: He is unborn, yet born for the welfare of the world; let the arising of that Great One be recounted.

children.text: idaṃ hi puṃsastapasaḥ śrutasya vā sviṣṭasya sūktasya ca buddhidattayoḥ
children.translated_text: This indeed is the unfailing purpose of a man's austerity, learning, sacrifice, good recitation, intelligence, and gifts:
the poets have determined it to be the description of the qualities of <s>Uttamaśloka</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ purātītabhave 'bhavaṃ mune dāsyāstu kasyāścana vedavādinām
children.translated_text: I, O sage, in a former past birth was born from a certain maidservant of men who expounded the Veda.

children.text: nirūpito bālaka eva yogināṃ śuśrūṣaṇe prāvṛṣi nirvivikṣatām ||
children.translated_text: While still only a boy, I was appointed to serve yogins who wished to dwell apart during the rainy season.
Those sages showed mercy to me, a child from whom all fickleness had gone, self-controlled, not clinging to playthings, and obedient,

children.text: cakruḥ kṛpāṃ yadyapi tulyadarśanāḥ śuśrūṣamāṇe munayo 'lpabhāṣiṇi ||
children.translated_text: though they saw all equally, because I served them and spoke little.

children.text: ucchiṣṭalepān anumodito dvijaiḥ sakṛt sma bhuñje tadapāstakilbiṣaḥ
children.translated_text: With the brahmins' permission I once ate the remnants smeared on their vessels; by that, my sin was removed.

children.text: evaṃ pravṛttasya viśuddhacetasas taddharma evātmaruciḥ prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: As I proceeded in this way, with purified mind, a taste for that very <s>dharma</s> arose in me.
There, day after day, by their grace, I heard delightful stories of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> from those who sang them aloud.

children.text: tāḥ śraddhayā me 'nupadaṃ viśṛṇvataḥ priyaśravasyaṅga mamābhavadruciḥ ||
children.translated_text: As I listened to them step by step with faith, dear one, a taste arose in me for what was lovely to hear.
Then, O great-minded one, when I had gained taste for those dear accounts, my mind became unwavering.

children.text: yayāham etat sadasat svamāyayā paśye mayi brahmaṇi kalpitaṃ pare ||
children.translated_text: By it I saw this existent and non-existent world, projected by its own <s>māyā</s> (creative illusion), in me, in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: itthaṃ śaratprāvṛṣikāv ṛtū harer viśṛṇvato me 'nusavaṃ yaśo 'malam
children.translated_text: Thus, through the autumn and rainy seasons, as I listened constantly to the stainless fame of <s>Hari</s>,
being chanted by great-souled sages, <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) arose, removing the self's <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>.
To me, thus attached, humble, and with sin destroyed,
trusting, a boy, controlled, and following them,
they taught that most secret knowledge, spoken directly by the Lord himself,
as they were about to depart, out of compassion, being tender toward the poor.
By it I understood the <s>māyā</s>-power of the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the creator,
and by it people go to his state.
This has been indicated to you, O brahmin: the remedy for the three kinds of suffering,
namely, action directed toward the Lord, the blessed <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: āmayo yaśca bhūtānāṃ jāyate yena suvrata
children.translated_text: The substance by which a disease arises among beings, O good-vowed one,

children.text: tadeva hy āmayaṃ dravyaṃ na punāti cikitsitam ||
children.translated_text: that very substance, when treated as medicine, does it not cure the disease?
In this way all ritual actions of human beings are causes of <s>saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration).
Those very actions, when arranged for the Supreme, become fit for dissolving the false self.
Whatever action is performed here for the satisfaction of the Lord,
and whatever knowledge depends on that, is joined with <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (the discipline of devotion).
Where people repeatedly perform actions according to the instruction of the Lord,
they sing the qualities and names of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and remember him.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate tubhyaṃ vāsudevāya dhīmahi
children.translated_text: Om. Homage to you, Blessed Lord; let us meditate on <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Homage to <s>Pradyumna</s>, to <s>Aniruddha</s>, and also to <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>.
Thus, under the designation of an image, he worships the one whose form is mantra, yet who is formless,

children.text: yajate yajñapuruṣaṃ sa samyag darśanaḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: and he worships the Person of sacrifice; that man has right vision.
O Brahman, knowing this own revealed teaching of mine, practiced by me,

children.text: adān me jñānam aiśvaryaṃ svasmin bhāvaṃ ca keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> gave me lordly knowledge and a disposition fixed on himself.

children.text: tvam apyadabhraśruta viśrutaṃ vibhoḥ samāpyate yena vidāṃ bubhutsitam
children.translated_text: You too, O vastly learned one, proclaim that celebrated teaching of the Lord, by which what the wise long to know is attained.
Those whose selves are repeatedly afflicted by suffering desire it as the extinction of distress, and not otherwise.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ niśamya bhagavān devarṣerjanma karma ca
children.translated_text: Having thus heard of the birth and deeds of the divine sage,

children.text: bhūyaḥ papraccha taṃ brahman vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O Brahman, <s>Vyāsa</s>, the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, questioned him again.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
When the mendicants, your instructors in knowledge, had gone away,
while you were still in that first age of life, what then did you do?

children.text: svāyambhuva kayā vṛttyā vartitaṃ te paraṃ vayaḥ
children.translated_text: O son of the Self-born, by what way of life was your later span of life passed?

children.text: kathaṃ cedam udasrākṣīḥ kāle prāpte kalevaram ||
children.translated_text: And how did you give up this body when the time had come?
O best of sages, this memory of yours concerning a former kalpa

children.text: na hy eṣa vyavadhāt kāla eṣa sarvanirākṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: has not been interrupted by time, though time removes everything.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
When the mendicants, my instructors in knowledge, had gone away,
while I was still in that first age of life, I then did this.

children.text: ekātmajā me jananī yoṣin mūḍhā ca kiṃkarī
children.translated_text: My mother was a woman with only one child, simple-minded and a servant;
because I, her son, was her only refuge, she bound herself to me with affection.
Being dependent, she was not capable, though she wished for my welfare and security;

children.text: īśasya hi vaśe loko yoṣā dārumayī yathā ||
children.translated_text: for the world is in the power of the Lord, like a woman made of wood.
And I lived in that brahmin household, under her care,
a child of five years, ignorant of direction, place, and time.

children.text: ekadā nirgatāṃ gehād duhantīṃ niśi gāṃ pathi
children.translated_text: Once, when she had gone out from the house at night on the road to milk a cow,
a snake, touched by her foot and driven by time, bit that pitiable woman.

children.text: tadā tadaham īśasya bhaktānāṃ śam abhīpsataḥ
children.translated_text: Then I considered that to be the grace of the Lord,
who seeks the peace of his devotees, and I set out toward the northern direction.
There I passed through prosperous countries, cities, villages, cowherd settlements, and mines,
market towns, hamlets, enclosed gardens, forests, and groves,
mountains variegated with colorful minerals, and trees whose branches had been broken by elephants,
reservoirs with wholesome water, and lotus ponds frequented by divine beings,
made beautiful by birds of varied cries and by the splendor of roaming bees,
dense with reeds, bamboo, śara grass, clumps of stalks, kuśa grass, and kīcaka cane.
Having gone on alone beyond them, I saw a great forest,
terrible and fearsome in form, full of snakes, owls, and jackals.
My senses and body were exhausted; I was overcome by thirst and hunger.

children.text: snātvā pītvā hrade nadyā upaspṛṣṭo gataśramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After bathing and drinking in a pool of a river, and after sipping water ritually, I was freed from fatigue.
In that uninhabited forest, taking shelter at the base of a pippal tree,
I contemplated, according to what I had heard, the Self established in the self, by means of the self.
As I meditated on his lotus feet, with my mind conquered by devotion,
<s>Hari</s> gradually appeared in my heart, while my eyes were marked by tears of longing.
Pierced by the excessive weight of love, with my limbs thrilled and utterly fulfilled,
immersed in a flood of bliss, I was aware of neither myself nor anything else, O sage.

children.text: rūpaṃ bhagavato yat tan manaḥkāntaṃ śucāpaham
children.translated_text: When that form of the Blessed Lord, delightful to the mind and removing grief,
was no longer seen, I suddenly rose up, distressed, as if downcast.
Wishing to see it again, I fixed my mind in my heart;
but though I looked, I did not see it, and I was like one unsatisfied and afflicted.

children.text: evaṃ yatantaṃ vijane mām āhāgocaro girām
children.translated_text: As I strove in this way in the lonely place, he who is beyond the reach of speech addressed me,
with a deep and smooth voice, as if pacifying my grief:

children.text: hantāsmiñ janmani bhavān mā māṃ draṣṭum ihārhati
children.translated_text: Alas, in this birth you are not fit to see me here.
I am hard to see for poor yogins whose impurities have not yet ripened away.
That form was shown to you once, O blameless one, for the sake of your desire for me.

children.text: matkāmaḥ śanakaiḥ sādhu sarvān muñcati hṛcchayān ||
children.translated_text: A good man who desires me gradually abandons all wishes lodged in the heart.
Through service to the good, even though it was not long, firm thought of me has arisen in you.

children.text: hitvāvadyam imaṃ lokaṃ gantā majjanatām asi ||
children.translated_text: Leaving this blameworthy world, you will become one of my people.
This understanding of yours, bound to me, will never perish;
even at the creation and dissolution of beings, your memory will remain by my grace.

children.text: etāvad uktvopararāma tan mahad bhūtaṃ nabholiṅgam aliṅgam īśvaram
children.translated_text: Having said only this much, that great Being, whose sign was the sky and yet who was signless, the Lord, ceased speaking.

children.text: ahaṃ ca tasmai mahatāṃ mahīyase śīrṣṇāvanāmaṃ vidadhe 'nukampitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And I bowed my head to him, the most venerable among the great, after receiving his compassion.

children.text: nāmānyanantasya hatatrapaḥ paṭhan guhyāni bhadrāṇi kṛtāni ca smaran
children.translated_text: Chanting without shame the secret and auspicious names of the Endless One, and remembering his deeds,

children.text: gāṃ paryaṭaṃstuṣṭamanā gataspṛhaḥ kālaṃ pratīkṣan vimado vimatsaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: I wandered the earth content in mind, free from longing, waiting for time, free from pride and envy.
Thus, O Brahman, for me whose mind was on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, unattached and pure in self,

children.text: kālaḥ prādurabhūt kāle taḍit saudāmanī yathā ||
children.translated_text: time appeared at the proper time, like a flash of lightning.

children.text: prayujyamāne mayi tāṃ śuddhāṃ bhāgavatīṃ tanum
children.translated_text: As that pure body belonging to the devotees of the Lord was being joined to me,
the body made of the five elements fell away, its begun karma brought to an end.
At the end of the kalpa, when the Lord lay in the waters of the ocean, taking this universe within himself,
I entered, along with his breath, into the interior of the Mighty One as he wished to sleep.
At the end of a thousand yugas, when he arose and wished to create this world,
the sages, headed by <s>Marīci</s>, and I were born from his vital breaths.
I wander through the three worlds, within and without, with my vow unbroken,
and by the grace of <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s> my movement is nowhere obstructed.
Setting in motion this vīṇā given by the gods, adorned with the brahman of sound,
I wander while singing the story of <s>Hari</s>.
As I sing aloud his own powers, he whose feet are holy places and whose hearing is dear

children.text: āhūta iva me śīghraṃ darśanaṃ yāti cetasi ||
children.translated_text: quickly comes into sight in my mind, as if summoned.
For those whose minds are afflicted, through repeated desire for contact with sense objects,
the recounting of <s>Hari</s>'s conduct is seen as a boat across the ocean of becoming.
By paths of yoga beginning with restraint, the self, repeatedly struck down by desire and greed,
is not directly calmed as it is by service to <s>Mukunda</s>.

children.text: sarvaṃ tadidam ākhyātaṃ yat pṛṣṭo 'haṃ tvayānagha
children.translated_text: All this has been told, O sinless one, whatever I was asked by you:
the mystery of my birth and deeds, and what brings satisfaction to your own self.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Nārada</s> addressed the son of <s>Vāsavī</s>;

children.text: āmantrya vīṇāṃ raṇayan yayau yādṛcchiko muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, sounding his vīṇā, the chance-wandering sage went away.
Ah, blessed indeed is this divine seer, since he sings the fame of the wielder of <s>Śārṅga</s>;

children.text: gāyan mādyann idaṃ tantryā ramayatyāturaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: exulting, he delights this suffering world with this stringed instrument.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
When <s>Nārada</s> had departed, O <s>Sūta</s>, what then did the blessed, powerful <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s> do,
after he had heard what <s>Nārada</s> intended?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
On the sacred river <s>Sarasvatī</s>, on its western bank, there is a hermitage
called <s>Śamyāprāsa</s>, which nourishes the sacrificial sessions of the seers.
There, in his own hermitage adorned with a grove of badarī trees, <s>Vyāsa</s>
sat down, sipped water, and himself concentrated his mind.
When his stainless mind had been properly fixed through <s>bhakti-yoga</s> (devotional discipline),

children.text: apaśyat puruṣaṃ pūrṇaṃ māyāṃ ca tadapāśrayam ||
children.translated_text: he saw the complete Puruṣa and also <s>māyā</s> (cosmic illusion), dependent on him.
Deluded by that <s>māyā</s>, the jīva, though transcendent, thinks itself composed of the three guṇas,
and undergoes misfortune produced by that same <s>māyā</s>.
Knowing direct <s>bhakti-yoga</s> toward <s>Adhokṣaja</s> to be the calming of misfortune,
the wise one composed the Sātvata Saṃhitā for people who did not know it.
When that work is heard, devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the supreme Puruṣa,
arises in a person, removing grief, delusion, and fear.
After composing the Bhāgavata Saṃhitā and arranging it in order,
the sage taught it to his son <s>Śuka</s>, who was devoted to renunciation.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
That sage was indeed devoted to renunciation, indifferent everywhere,

children.text: kasya vā bṛhatīm etām ātmārāmaḥ samabhyasat ||
children.translated_text: and delighted in the self; for what reason did he thoroughly study this vast work?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Even self-delighting sages, though free from bonds, perform causeless devotion toward <s>Urukrama</s>;
such are the qualities of <s>Hari</s>.
The blessed son of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>, his mind drawn by the qualities of <s>Hari</s>,
studied the great narrative, always dear to the people of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Now I shall tell of the birth and deeds of the royal sage <s>Parīkṣit</s>, the lamentation,
and the departure of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, where the story of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> arises.

children.text: yadā mṛdhe kauravasṛñjayānāṃ vīreṣvatho vīragatiṃ gateṣu
children.translated_text: When, in the battle of the <s>Kauravas</s> and the <s>Sṛñjayas</s>, the heroes had gone to the hero's fate,
and the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> had the shafts of his thighs broken by the blow of <s>Vṛkodara</s>'s mace,

children.text: bhartuḥ priyaṃ drauṇiriti sma paśyan kṛṣṇāsutānāṃ svapatāṃ śirāṃsi
children.translated_text: <s>Drauṇi</s>, thinking it would please his master, brought the heads of the sleeping sons of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>,

children.text: upāharadvipriyam eva tasya jugupsitaṃ karma vigarhayanti ||
children.translated_text: but it was only displeasing to him; people condemn that loathsome act.

children.text: mātā śiśūnāṃ nidhanaṃ sutānāṃ niśamya ghoraṃ paritapyamānā
children.translated_text: The mother, hearing of the terrible killing of her young sons, was overcome with grief;

children.text: tadārudad bāṣpakalākulākṣī tāṃ sāntvayann āha kirīṭamālī ||
children.translated_text: then she wept, her eyes confused with streams of tears, and the crowned warrior consoled her and said:

children.text: tadā śucaste pramṛjāmi bhadre yadbrahmabandhoḥ śira ātatāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, O noble lady, I shall wipe away your grief, when I bring you the head of that brahmin-kinsman, that aggressor,

children.text: gāṇḍīvamuktairviśikhair upāhare tvākramya yat snāsyasi dagdhaputrā ||
children.translated_text: cut off by arrows released from <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, and when, bereft of your burned sons, you bathe after setting foot on it.
Thus, after consoling his beloved with gentle and varied words, he, the son whose friend was <s>Acyuta</s>,

children.text: anvādravad daṃśita ugradhanvā kapidhvajo guruputraṃ rathena ||
children.translated_text: armored, bearing a fierce bow and the ape-banner, pursued the guru's son with his chariot.

children.text: tam āpatantaṃ sa vilakṣya dūrāt kumārahodvignamanā rathena
children.translated_text: Seeing him coming from afar, the young man, troubled in mind,
fled over the earth in his chariot, desiring to save his life, as far as he could go, like one afraid of <s>Rudra</s>.
When the twice-born one's son saw himself without refuge and his horses exhausted,
he thought the brahmaśiras weapon to be his protection.
Then, having sipped water, he set it in place with concentrated mind,
although he did not know how to withdraw it, when danger to his life had arisen.
Then a fierce radiance manifested itself in every direction;
seeing danger to life, <s>Jiṣṇu</s> addressed <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Arjuna</s> said:
O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, mighty-armed one, maker of fearlessness for devotees,
you alone are release from saṃsṛti for those who are being burned.

children.text: tvam ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣādīśvaraḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: You are the primordial Puruṣa, directly the Lord, beyond prakṛti;

children.text: māyāṃ vyudasya cicchaktyā kaivalye sthita ātmani ||
children.translated_text: having cast off <s>māyā</s> by your power of consciousness, you stand in the self in isolation.
For this world of living beings, whose minds are deluded by <s>māyā</s>,
you establish, by your own power, welfare marked by <s>dharma</s> and the other aims.
Likewise, this avatāra of yours is for the wish to remove the burden of the earth,
and also for the constant contemplation of your own people, who have no other disposition.

children.text: kim idaṃ svit kuto veti devadeva na vedmyaham
children.translated_text: What this is, or whence it comes, O God of gods, I do not know;
a supremely terrible radiance is approaching from every side.
The Blessed Lord said:
Know this to be the brahmic weapon displayed by the son of <s>Droṇa</s>;
he does not know how to withdraw it, now that danger to his life has arisen.

children.text: na hy asyānyatamaṃ kiṃcid astraṃ pratyavakarśanam
children.translated_text: There is no other weapon at all that can counteract it.

children.text: jahy astrateja unnaddham astrajño hy astratejasā ||
children.translated_text: Destroy this swelling weapon-radiance with weapon-radiance, for you know the weapons.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Hearing what was spoken by the Blessed Lord, <s>Phālguna</s>, slayer of enemy heroes,
touched water, circumambulated him, and set a brahmic weapon against the brahmāstra.
The two radiances of both weapons, enclosed in showers of arrows, struck against one another,
and, covering heaven, earth, and sky, they grew like the sun and fire.

children.text: dṛṣṭvāstratejastu tayos trīṃ lokān pradahan mahat
children.translated_text: But seeing the great radiance of the two weapons burning the three worlds,
all the creatures, being scorched, thought it was the fire of cosmic dissolution.
Seeing the distress of the creatures and that disorder of the worlds,
and knowing the intention of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Arjuna</s> withdrew both weapons.
Then, swiftly reaching the fearsome son of <s>Gautamī</s>,
with eyes reddened by anger he bound him, as one binds an animal with a rope.

children.text: śibirāya ninīṣantaṃ rajjvā baddhvā ripuṃ balāt
children.translated_text: As he was forcibly tying his enemy with a cord and intending to take him to the camp,
the blessed lotus-eyed Lord, enraged, said to <s>Arjuna</s>:

children.text: mainaṃ pārthārhasi trātuṃ brahmabandhum imaṃ jahi
children.translated_text: O <s>Pārtha</s>, you should not protect this mere kinsman of brahmins. Kill him,

children.text: yo 'sāv anāgasaḥ suptān avadhīn niśi bālakān ||
children.translated_text: for he murdered innocent sleeping boys at night.

children.text: mattaṃ pramattam unmattaṃ suptaṃ bālaṃ striyaṃ jaḍam
children.translated_text: One who knows <s>dharma</s> does not kill an enemy who is drunk, careless, insane, asleep, a child, a woman, dull-witted,

children.text: prapannaṃ virathaṃ bhītaṃ na ripuṃ hanti dharmavit ||
children.translated_text: one who has surrendered, one whose chariot is gone, or one who is afraid.
A merciless villain who nourishes his own life by the lives of others:

children.text: tadvadhastasya hi śreyo yad doṣād yātyadhaḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: his death is indeed better for him, since through that fault a man goes downward.

children.text: pratiśrutaṃ ca bhavatā pāñcālyai śṛṇvato mama
children.translated_text: And you promised <s>Pāñcālī</s>, while I was listening,
'I shall bring the head of the man who killed your sons, O proud lady.'
Therefore this sinner deserves to be killed: an aggressor, murderer of his own kin,
and, O hero, a defiler of his family who has done what is hateful to his master.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ parīkṣatā dharmaṃ pārthaḥ kṛṣṇena coditaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus urged by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who was testing <s>dharma</s>,
great <s>Pārtha</s> did not wish to kill the son of his guru, although he had killed his own children.
Then, with <s>Govinda</s> as his dear charioteer, he came to his own camp

children.text: nyavedayat taṃ priyāyai śocantyā ātmajān hatān ||
children.translated_text: and presented him to his beloved wife, who was grieving for her slain sons.
Seeing him brought in that way, bound with ropes like an animal, face downward because of his detestable deed,

children.text: nirīkṣya kṛṣṇāpakṛtaṃ guroḥ sutaṃ vāmasvabhāvā kṛpayā nanāma ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, seeing the son of the guru wronged, bowed to him out of compassion, for she was tender by nature.
The virtuous woman, unable to bear his being brought in bonds, said:

children.text: mucyatāṃ mucyatām eṣa brāhmaṇo nitarāṃ guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Release him, release him. He is a brahmin, and all the more he is a guru.
By whose grace you learned the secret-bearing <s>Dhanurveda</s>, with release and withdrawal,
and the whole array of weapons.

children.text: sa eṣa bhagavān droṇaḥ prajārūpeṇa vartate
children.translated_text: He himself is the blessed <s>Droṇa</s>, continuing in the form of his son.
His other half, his wife <s>Kṛpī</s>, the mother of a hero, did not follow him into death.
Therefore, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, O greatly fortunate one, this venerable family, honored by you,

children.text: vṛjinaṃ nārhati prāptuṃ pūjyaṃ vandyam abhīkṣṇaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: does not deserve to come to misfortune; it is to be honored and repeatedly revered.

children.text: mā rodīd asya jananī gautamī patidevatā
children.translated_text: Let his mother, <s>Gautamī</s>, devoted to her husband, not weep
as I, afflicted by dead children, weep again and again with a tearful face.
When self-uncontrolled warriors provoke a brahmin family,
that family quickly burns up their line, together with its dependents, when grief is set upon it.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: dharmyaṃ nyāyyaṃ sakaruṇaṃ nirvyalīkaṃ samaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Her words were righteous, just, compassionate, sincere, impartial, and noble.
O brahmins, the king, son of <s>Dharma</s>, approved the queen's speech.
<s>Nakula</s>, <s>Sahadeva</s>, <s>Yuyudhāna</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,

children.text: bhagavān devakīputro ye cānye yāśca yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the blessed son of <s>Devakī</s>, and all the others, including the women, approved it too.
There <s>Bhīma</s>, angered, said that killing him was considered better,

children.text: na bharturnātmanaścārthe yo 'han suptān śiśūn vṛthā ||
children.translated_text: for he had pointlessly slain sleeping children, neither for his master's sake nor for his own.
Hearing what <s>Bhīma</s> had said, and also <s>Draupadī</s>'s words, the four-armed Lord

children.text: ālokya vadanaṃ sakhyur idam āha hasann iva ||
children.translated_text: looked at his friend's face and said this, almost smiling:
The Blessed Lord said:
'A kinsman of brahmins is not to be killed, yet an aggressor deserves death.
Both have been taught by me. Preserve the command.

children.text: kuru pratiśrutaṃ satyaṃ yat tat sāntvayatā priyām
children.translated_text: Make true the promise that you made while consoling your beloved,

children.text: priyaṃ ca bhīmasenasya pāñcālyā mahyam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: and do what is pleasing to <s>Bhīmasena</s>, to <s>Pāñcālī</s>, and to me as well.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then <s>Arjuna</s>, quickly understanding <s>Hari</s>'s intention, with his sword
took the jewel from the brahmin's head, along with his hair.
Releasing him, who had been bound with the rope and whose splendor was struck down by the killing of children,
and who was deprived of the brilliance of his jewel, he drove him out from the camp.
Shaving the head, taking away wealth,

children.text: eṣa hi brahmabandhūnāṃ vadho nānyo 'sti daihikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and expulsion from one's place: this indeed is the killing prescribed for brahmin-kinsmen; there is no other bodily killing.
All the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, together with <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, were distressed by grief for their sons.
They performed what had to be done for their dead relatives, beginning with the carrying out of the bodies.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: atha te samparetānāṃ svānām udakam icchatām
children.translated_text: Then they, wishing to offer water for their departed kinsmen,

children.text: dātuṃ sakṛṣṇā gaṅgāyāṃ puraskṛtya yayuḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went to the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, together with <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, placing the women in front.

children.text: te ninīyodakaṃ sarve vilapya ca bhṛśaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: All of them offered the water, lamented deeply again,
and bathed in the river water purified by the dust of <s>Hari</s>'s lotus feet.
There <s>Mādhava</s> consoled the lord of the <s>Kurus</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, seated with his younger brother,

children.text: gāndhārīṃ putraśokārtāṃ pṛthāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ ca mādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gāndhārī</s>, afflicted by grief for her sons, <s>Pṛthā</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>,
along with the sages, consoling those whose kinsmen had been killed and who were overcome by grief,

children.text: bhūteṣu kālasya gatiṃ darśayan na pratikriyām ||
children.translated_text: showing that among beings the course of Time has no remedy.
Having secured for <s>Ajātaśatru</s> his own kingdom, which had been seized by gamblers,
and having caused the wicked king, whose life had been damaged by the touch of hair, to be killed,
having had him perform three horse sacrifices furnished with excellent rites,
he spread his purifying fame through the directions like that of <s>Śatamanyu</s>.
Taking leave of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, accompanied by <s>Śaineya</s> and <s>Uddhava</s>,
and being honored in return by honored brahmins headed by <s>Dvaipāyana</s>,
O brahmin, resolved to go to <s>Dvārakā</s>, he mounted his chariot
and saw <s>Uttarā</s> running toward him, bewildered by fear.
<s>Uttarā</s> said:
'Protect me, protect me, O great yogin, God of gods, Lord of the universe!'

children.text: nānyaṃ tvadabhayaṃ paśye yatra mṛtyuḥ parasparam ||
children.translated_text: I see no other source of fearlessness than you, where death rushes upon us from every side.
O Lord, O mighty one, a fiery arrow of heated iron is advancing upon me.

children.text: kāmaṃ dahatu māṃ nātha mā me garbho nipātyatām ||
children.translated_text: Let it burn me as it will, O master, but let my embryo not be destroyed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having understood her words, the Blessed Lord, affectionate to his devotees,
recognized that this was the weapon of <s>Drauṇi</s>, meant to make the world without <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
Then, at that very moment, O best of sages, the five <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, seeing five blazing shafts
coming toward themselves, took up their weapons.
Seeing that calamity of theirs, whose minds had no other object,
the mighty Lord made protection for his own people with his own weapon, the <s>Sudarśana</s>.
<s>Hari</s>, the inner Self of all beings and Lord of yoga, dwelling within,
covered the embryo of <s>Virāṭa</s>'s daughter by his own māyā, for the continuation of the <s>Kuru</s> line.
Although the weapon was the <s>brahmaśiras</s>, unfailing and without countermeasure,
on reaching the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> radiance it was pacified, O descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: mā maṃsthā hy etad āścaryaṃ sarvāścaryamaye acyute
children.translated_text: Do not think this a wonder in <s>Acyuta</s>, who is made of every wonder,

children.text: ya idaṃ māyayā devyā sṛjatyavati hantyajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for he, though unborn, by his divine māyā creates, protects, and destroys this world.
Together with her sons, freed from the brahminic fire, and with <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>,

children.text: prayāṇābhimukhaṃ kṛṣṇam idam āha pṛthā satī ||
children.translated_text: the virtuous <s>Pṛthā</s> spoke these words to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who was ready to depart.
<s>Kuntī</s> said:

children.text: namasye puruṣaṃ tvādyam īśvaraṃ prakṛteḥ param
children.translated_text: I bow to you, the primeval <s>puruṣa</s>, the Lord beyond prakṛti,
unseen by all beings, abiding within and without.
You are covered by the curtain of māyā, imperishable <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, hidden from the ignorant;

children.text: na lakṣyase mūḍhadṛśā naṭo nāṭyadharo yathā ||
children.translated_text: you are not perceived by foolish eyes, just as an actor in costume is not recognized.
Likewise, you are for the supreme swans and sages of stainless self,
for the establishment of bhakti-yoga; how indeed could we women see you?
Repeated homage to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and to the joy of <s>Devakī</s>,
to the son of <s>Nandagopa</s>, to <s>Govinda</s>: homage again and again.
Homage to the lotus-naveled one; homage to the one garlanded with lotuses;
homage to the lotus-eyed one; homage to you whose feet are lotuses.

children.text: yathā hṛṣīkeśa khalena devakī kaṃsena ruddhāticiraṃ śucārpitā
children.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Devakī</s>, long imprisoned by the wicked <s>Kaṃsa</s> and given over to grief,

children.text: vimocitāhaṃ ca sahātmajā vibho tvayaiva nāthena muhurvipadgaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: was freed by you alone as her protector, O mighty one, so I too was freed repeatedly from hosts of dangers, together with my sons.
From poison, from the great fire, from the sight of man-eaters, from the wicked assembly, from the hardships of forest exile,
from the weapons of many great chariot-warriors in battle after battle, and from <s>Drauṇi</s>'s weapon, O <s>Hare</s>, we have been protected.

children.text: vipadaḥ santu tāḥ śaśvat tatra tatra jagadguro
children.translated_text: Let those calamities be present forever, here and there, O teacher of the world,
if through them there may be sight of you, the sight after which rebirth is not seen.
A man whose pride swells through birth, sovereignty, learning, and beauty
is surely not able to address you, who are accessible to those who possess nothing.
Homage to you, the wealth of the possessionless, whose activity in the guṇas has ceased,
self-delighting, peaceful, lord of liberation: homage to you.

children.text: manye tvāṃ kālam īśānam anādinidhanaṃ vibhum
children.translated_text: I consider you to be Time, the ruling Lord, beginningless and endless, all-pervading,

children.text: samaṃ carantaṃ sarvatra bhūtānāṃ yan mithaḥ kaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: moving equally everywhere, while there is mutual strife among beings.

children.text: na veda kaścidbhagavaṃścikīrṣitaṃ tavehamānasya nṛṇāṃ viḍambanam
children.translated_text: No one knows what you intend, O Blessed Lord, as you act here in the world in a play among human beings;

children.text: na yasya kaściddayito 'sti karhicid dveṣyaśca yasmin viṣamā matir nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: for no one is ever dear to him, nor anyone hateful, though in him men's thought becomes unequal.
Your birth and action, O Self of the universe, though you are unborn, actionless, and the Self,
among animals, men, sages, and aquatic beings, is utterly astonishing play.

children.text: gopy ādade tvayi kṛtāgasi dāma tāvad yā te daśāśrukalilāñjanasambhramākṣam
children.translated_text: When the cowherdess took up a rope against you after you had offended, and your face, with eyes confused as their collyrium was washed by ten streams of tears,

children.text: vaktraṃ ninīya bhayabhāvanayā sthitasya sā māṃ vimohayati bhīr api yadbibheti ||
children.translated_text: was lowered while you stood in fear, that sight bewilders me, since fear itself fears you.
Some say that the unborn one has been born for the fame of the one celebrated in sacred verses,
in the lineage of dear <s>Yadu</s>, like sandalwood on <s>Malaya</s>.
Others say that, though unborn, you came when requested by <s>Vasudeva</s>, in <s>Devakī</s>,

children.text: ajastvam asya kṣemāya vadhāya ca suradviṣām ||
children.translated_text: for this world's welfare and for the destruction of the enemies of the gods.
Others say that you were born to remove the burden of the earth, like a boat upon the ocean,
when she was sinking under a heavy load, at the request of the self-born <s>Brahmā</s>.
Some say that, for those tormented in this becoming by ignorance, desire, and actions,
you would perform deeds worthy of hearing and remembering.

children.text: śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇantyabhīkṣṇaśaḥ smaranti nandanti tavehitaṃ janāḥ
children.translated_text: The people who constantly hear, sing, praise, remember, and rejoice in your deeds

children.text: ta eva paśyantyacireṇa tāvakaṃ bhavapravāhoparamaṃ padāmbujam ||
children.translated_text: very soon see your lotus foot, where the stream of worldly becoming ceases.

children.text: apyadya nastvaṃ svakṛtehita prabho jihāsasi svit suhṛdo 'nujīvinaḥ
children.translated_text: O Lord, benefactor of your own, do you perhaps wish today to abandon us, your friends and dependents,

children.text: yeṣāṃ na cānyadbhavataḥ padāmbujāt parāyaṇaṃ rājasu yojitāṃhasām ||
children.translated_text: for whom there is no refuge other than your lotus foot, now that sins have been set in motion among kings?

children.text: ke vayaṃ nāmarūpābhyāṃ yadubhiḥ saha pāṇḍavāḥ
children.translated_text: What are we <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, together with the <s>Yadus</s>, in name and form,
when we have no sight of you, like the senses without their ruler?
This land will not shine then as it does now, O <s>Gadādhara</s>,
for it now shines marked by your feet, distinguished by their own auspicious marks.
These prosperous countries, with well-ripened herbs and plants,
with forests, mountains, rivers, and seas, thrive because of your glances.

children.text: atha viśveśa viśvātman viśvamūrte svakeṣu me
children.translated_text: Therefore, O Lord of the universe, Self of the universe, form of the universe, among my own people

children.text: snehapāśam imaṃ chinddhi dṛḍhaṃ pāṇḍuṣu vṛṣṇiṣu ||
children.translated_text: cut this firm bond of affection toward the <s>Pāṇḍus</s> and the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.
May my thought, having no object other than you, O <s>Madhupati</s>, again and again
bear steadfast love toward you, just as the <s>Gaṅgā</s> bears her flood to the ocean.
O glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, friend of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bull of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, destroyer of earth-oppressing royal lines, whose valor never fails,
O <s>Govinda</s>, incarnation who removes the distress of cows, brahmins, and gods, O Lord of yoga, teacher of all, Blessed Lord, homage to you.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus, with artful words, <s>Pṛthā</s> praised him whose every manifestation of greatness is complete;

children.text: mandaṃ jahāsa vaikuṇṭho mohayann iva māyayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> smiled gently, as if bewildering her by his <s>māyā</s> (power of illusion).
Having answered her, ‘So be it,’ and having entered <s>Gajasāhvaya</s>,

children.text: striyaśca svapuraṃ yāsyan premṇā rājñā nivāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as he was about to go with the women to his own city, he was restrained by the king out of love.
Although he was awakened by <s>Vyāsa</s> and the others, who knew the Lord’s intention, and by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of wondrous deeds,
and even by histories, he did not regain understanding, for he was overwhelmed by grief.
The king, the son of <s>Dharma</s>, thinking of the slaughter of his kinsmen, spoke,
O brahmins, having fallen under the power of affection and delusion through his ordinary human self:

children.text: aho me paśyatājñānaṃ hṛdi rūḍhaṃ durātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: ‘Ah! See the ignorance rooted in my heart, wicked as I am.
For the sake of this body, which truly belongs to others, many <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s> have been slain by me.
I have harmed boys, twice-born men, well-wishers, friends, fathers, brothers, and teachers;

children.text: na me syān nirayān mokṣo hy api varṣāyutāyutaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: there can be no release for me from hell, even in tens of thousands upon tens of thousands of years.
“For a king, protector of his subjects, the killing of enemies in a righteous war is no sin” --

children.text: iti me na tu bodhāya kalpate śāsanaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that injunctional statement is not able to bring me understanding.
The offense against the women whose husbands and kinsmen have been killed by me, which has arisen here,
I am not capable of removing by the ritual acts of householders.

children.text: yathā paṅkena paṅkāmbhaḥ surayā vā surākṛtam
children.translated_text: As muddy water is not cleansed by mud, nor liquor-stained water by liquor,

children.text: bhūtahatyāṃ tathaivaikāṃ na yajñair mārṣṭum arhati ||
children.translated_text: so one act of killing living beings cannot rightly be wiped clean by sacrifices.’
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus terrified by the offense against his subjects, and desiring to know all forms of <s>dharma</s>,
he then went to <s>Vinaśana</s>, where <s>Devavrata</s> had fallen.

children.text: tadā te bhrātaraḥ sarve sadaśvaiḥ svarṇabhūṣitaiḥ
children.translated_text: At that time all his brothers, with excellent horses adorned in gold,
followed in chariots, and so too did the brahmins, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Dhaumya</s>, and the rest.
The Blessed Lord also, O brahmin sage, went in a chariot together with <s>Dhanañjaya</s>;

children.text: sa tairvyarocata nṛpaḥ kubera iva guhyakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with them that king shone forth like <s>Kubera</s> surrounded by the <s>Guhyakas</s>.
Seeing <s>Bhīṣma</s> fallen on the ground like an immortal dropped from heaven,

children.text: praṇemuḥ pāṇḍavā bhīṣmaṃ sānugāḥ saha cakriṇā ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, with their attendants and with the discus-bearer, bowed down to him.
There all the brahmin seers and divine seers, O best one,
and royal seers were present to see the foremost of the <s>Bharatas</s>.
<s>Parvata</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Dhaumya</s>, the Blessed <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>,
<s>Bṛhadaśva</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, and the son of <s>Reṇukā</s> with his disciples were there.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Indrapramada</s>, <s>Trita</s>, <s>Gṛtsamada</s>, and <s>Asita</s>,
<s>Kakṣīvān</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, and then <s>Sudarśana</s> were there.
And other stainless sages, O brahmin, beginning with <s>Brahmarāta</s>,
came with their disciples, including <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and the rest.
Perceiving those greatly blessed ones assembled, the best of the <s>Vasus</s>,
knower of <s>dharma</s>, aware of distinctions of place and time, honored them.
And knowing the power of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, seated there as the Lord of the universe,
he honored him, who dwelt in his heart and had assumed a body through <s>māyā</s>.
Seeing the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> sitting near him, united in humility and love,
he addressed them, his sight blinded by tears of affection.
‘Ah, hardship! Ah, injustice! You, sons of <s>Dharma</s>,
do not deserve to live afflicted, for you have taken refuge in brahmins, <s>dharma</s>, and <s>Acyuta</s>.
When the mighty warrior <s>Pāṇḍu</s> had died, <s>Pṛthā</s>, a young widow with young children,

children.text: yuṣmatkṛte bahūn kleśān prāptā tokavatī muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: repeatedly suffered many hardships for your sake while she still had little ones.

children.text: sarvaṃ kālakṛtaṃ manye bhavatāṃ ca yadapriyam
children.translated_text: All the unpleasant things that have befallen you, I think, were wrought by Time,
