under whose control the world with its guardians moves like a mass of clouds under the wind.
Where the king is the son of <s>Dharma</s>, where the mace-bearing <s>Vṛkodara</s> is,

children.text: kṛṣṇo 'strī gāṇḍivaṃ cāpaṃ suhṛt kṛṣṇastato vipat ||
children.translated_text: where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the wielder of weapons, where the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow is, and where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is a friend, how can there be calamity?

children.text: na hyasya karhicidrājan pumān veda vidhitsitam
children.translated_text: For no man, O king, ever knows what he intends to do,
and in trying to understand it even the wise become bewildered.
Therefore, resolve that this is governed by divine will, O bull of the <s>Bharatas</s>;
following that will, protect the subjects, O lord and protector of the helpless.

children.text: eṣa vai bhagavān sākṣādādyo nārāyaṇaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: This one is indeed the Blessed Lord himself, the primal person <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> directly;
bewildering the world by his <s>māyā</s>, he moves hidden among the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>.
The blessed <s>Śiva</s> knows his most secret power,
as do the divine seer <s>Nārada</s> and the blessed <s>Kapila</s> himself, O king.

children.text: yaṃ manyase mātuleyaṃ priyaṃ mitraṃ suhṛttamam
children.translated_text: You regard him as your maternal cousin, dear friend, and finest well-wisher;
out of friendship you made him your counselor, envoy, and then charioteer.
He is the Self of all, equal-sighted, nondual, and free from egoity;
for that faultless one there is never any unevenness of mind because of such acts.
Even so, look at his compassion toward those kings who are devoted to him alone:

children.text: yan me 'sūṃstyajataḥ sākṣāt kṛṣṇo darśanam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: as I am giving up my life-breaths, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself has come within my sight.

children.text: bhaktyāveśya mano yasmin vācā yannāma kīrtayan
children.translated_text: The yogin who fixes his mind on him through devotion and chants his name with speech
is released from desire and karma when abandoning the body.

children.text: sa devadevo bhagavān pratīkṣatāṃ kalevaraṃ yāvadidaṃ hinomyaham
children.translated_text: May that God of gods, the Blessed Lord, wait while I cast off this body,
his lotus face shining with a gracious smile, ruddy eyes, and four arms, the path of my meditation.’
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard him then as he lay upon the cage of arrows, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>
asked about various forms of <s>dharma</s>, while the sages listened.
He asked about the twofold marks taught according to caste and according to life-stage,
established by human nature and conditioned by detachment and attachment.
He asked separately about the duties of giving, royal duties, and duties leading to liberation,
about women’s duties and duties toward the Blessed Lord, both briefly and in detail,
and about <s>dharma</s>, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, together with their means, O sage.
The knower of truth explained them through various narratives and histories.
As he was teaching <s>dharma</s>, that time approached for him.
the northern course, desired by yogins who can choose the time of their death, had come.

children.text: tadopasaṃhṛtya giraḥ sahasraṇīr vimuktasaṅgaṃ mana ādipūruṣe
children.translated_text: Then, drawing in his speech, he fixed his mind, free from attachment, upon the primal Person,

children.text: kṛṣṇe lasatpītapaṭe caturbhuje puraḥ sthite 'mīlitadṛg vyadhārayat ||
children.translated_text: upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, clad in shining yellow cloth, four-armed, standing before him, while he held his eyes open.
With pure <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), his inauspiciousness destroyed, and by that very sight his weariness from weapons quickly gone,
with all the wavering functions of the senses withdrawn, he praised <s>Janārdana</s> as he abandoned his body born of this world.
<s>Śrī Bhīṣma</s> said:

children.text: iti matirupakalpitā vitṛṣṇā bhagavati sātvatapuṅgave vibhūmni
children.translated_text: Thus may my thought, fashioned and free from thirst, rest in the Blessed Lord, the best of the <s>Sātvatas</s>, the all-pervading one,

children.text: svasukham upagate kvacidvihartuṃ prakṛtim upeyuṣi yadbhavapravāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who has attained his own bliss, yet at times enters <s>prakṛti</s> (manifest nature) for play, he from whom the stream of becoming arises.
May my faultless love be for him, whose color is like the <s>tamāla</s> tree, wearing a splendid garment bright as the rays of the sun,
whose lotus face is covered by curling locks; O friend of <s>Vijaya</s>, may my love be for you.
In battle, when the dust of the horses had made every direction smoky, when his hair was disheveled and his face adorned with drops of exertion,

children.text: mama niśitaśarairvibhidyamāna tvaci vilasatkavace 'stu kṛṣṇa ātmā ||
children.translated_text: and when his skin was being pierced by my sharp arrows while his armor shone, may my self be fixed on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: sapadi sakhivaco niśamya madhye nijaparayorbalayo rathaṃ niveśya
children.translated_text: At once, hearing his friend's words, he placed the chariot between his own army and the opposing army,
and, standing there, stole away the lifespans of the enemy soldiers with his glance; may my love be for the friend of <s>Pārtha</s>.
Seeing the faces of the armies arrayed before him, and seeing one turned away from killing his own kin through a sense of fault,

children.text: kumatim aharadātmavidyayā yaś caraṇaratiḥ paramasya tasya me 'stu ||
children.translated_text: he removed that wrong understanding by knowledge of the self; may love for the feet of that Supreme One be mine.

children.text: svanigamam apahāya matpratijñām ṛtam adhikartum avapluto rathasthaḥ
children.translated_text: Abandoning his own vow in order to make my pledge true, he leapt down from the chariot,

children.text: dhṛtarathacaraṇo 'bhyayāc caladgur haririva hantum ibhaṃ gatottarīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seized a chariot wheel and rushed toward me, the earth trembling, his upper garment fallen, like a lion going to kill an elephant.
Struck by sharp arrows, his armor shattered, covered with blood,

children.text: prasabham abhisasāra madvadhārthaṃ sa bhavatu me bhagavān gatirmukundaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that Blessed <s>Mukunda</s> charged fiercely at me, his attacker, to kill me; may he be my final refuge.
As the attendant of <s>Vijaya</s>'s chariot, holding the whip and the reins of the horses, beautiful to behold in that splendor,

children.text: bhagavati ratirastu me mumūrṣor yam iha nirīkṣya hatā gatāḥ svarūpam ||
children.translated_text: may my love, as I am about to die, be for the Blessed One, whom those slain here attained their own true form by seeing.
The cowherd women, whose great pride was shaped by his graceful gait, playful movements, charming smiles, and loving glances,

children.text: kṛtamanukṛtavatya unmadāndhāḥ prakṛtim agan kila yasya gopavadhvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: became blind with madness, imitated his acts, and, it is said, attained their own nature through him.
In the inner assembly crowded with hosts of sages and the best of kings, at King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s <s>Rājasūya</s>,

children.text: arhaṇam upapeda īkṣaṇīyo mama dṛśigocara eṣa āvirātmā ||
children.translated_text: he, worthy of being seen, received the worship of them all; this manifest Self now stands within the range of my sight.

children.text: tam imam aham ajaṃ śarīrabhājāṃ hṛdi hṛdi dhiṣṭhitam ātmakalpitānām
children.translated_text: This very unborn one, established in the heart of every embodied being whose body is imagined by the self,

children.text: pratidṛśam iva naikadhārkam ekaṃ samadhigato 'smi vidhūtabhedamohaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I have fully realized as one, though appearing many to each eye like the single sun, my delusion of difference shaken off.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus, with the activities of mind, speech, and sight fixed upon blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
placing himself within the Self, he ceased his inner breathing.
Knowing that <s>Bhīṣma</s> was merging into the partless <s>Brahman</s>,
all those present became silent, like birds at the end of the day.
There kettledrums sounded, played by gods and humans,

children.text: śaśaṃsuḥ sādhavo rājñāṃ khāt petuḥ puṣpavṛṣṭayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the good proclaimed praises among the kings, and showers of flowers fell from the sky.
O <s>Bhārgava</s>, after <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> had performed for that departed one the funeral acts, beginning with carrying out the body,
he remained sorrowful for a moment.
The delighted sages praised <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with his secret names,
and then, their hearts fixed on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, they returned again to their own hermitages.
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, going with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to <s>Gajāhvaya</s>,
consoled his father and the ascetic <s>Gāndhārī</s>.
Approved by his father and encouraged by <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
the mighty king ruled by <s>dharma</s> over the kingdom of his father and grandfather.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: hatvā svarikthaspṛdha ātatāyino yudhiṣṭhiro dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: After killing the aggressors who coveted his own inheritance, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, foremost among the upholders of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sahānujaiḥ pratyavaruddhabhojanaḥ kathaṃ pravṛttaḥ kim akārṣīt tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: with his younger brothers and his enjoyment checked, how did he proceed, and what did he do thereafter?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
After reviving the line of <s>Kuru</s>, which had been consumed by the forest fire of its own lineage, <s>Hari</s>, the sustainer of becoming,

children.text: niveśayitvā nijarājya īśvaro yudhiṣṭhiraṃ prītamanā babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: installed <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> in his own kingdom, and the Lord became pleased in heart.
Then, having heard what <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Acyuta</s> had said, his confusion washed away by arisen knowledge,

children.text: śaśāsa gām indra ivājitāśrayaḥ paridhyupāntām anujānuvartitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he ruled the earth bounded by the seas like <s>Indra</s>, taking shelter in the unconquered Lord and followed by his younger brothers.
The rain-cloud poured down what was desired, and the earth yielded every wish,
while joyful cows, full-uddered, drenched the pastures with milk.
The rivers, oceans, mountains, trees, creepers, and plants,

children.text: phalantyoṣadhayaḥ sarvāḥ kāmam anvṛtu tasya vai ||
children.translated_text: all bearing fruit, fulfilled his desires according to the seasons.
There were no mental afflictions, diseases, or troubles arising from divine, elemental, or bodily causes,
among living beings at any time while <s>Ajātaśatru</s> was king.
<s>Hari</s> stayed in <s>Hāstinapura</s> for several months,
to remove the grief of his friends and because he desired the happiness of his sister.
Taking leave, receiving permission, embracing him and bowing to him,
he mounted the chariot, while some embraced him and others bowed to him.
<s>Subhadrā</s>, <s>Draupadī</s>, <s>Kuntī</s>, and the daughter of <s>Virāṭa</s>,
as well as <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Yuyutsu</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and the twins,
<s>Vṛkodara</s>, <s>Dhaumya</s>, and the women beginning with the daughter of <s>Matsya</s>,
bewildered, could not endure separation from the wielder of <s>Śārṅga</s>.
A wise person, freed from bad association through the company of the good, cannot bear to abandon that company.
How could the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>, whose minds had been placed in him, endure separation from him,

children.text: tasmin nyastadhiyaḥ pārthāḥ saheran virahaṃ katham
children.translated_text: when his fame, being sung, is delightful after being heard even once?
Through seeing him, touching him, conversing with him, lying down, sitting, and eating with him,
all of them, with unblinking eyes and with their minds running after him,
looked upon him, bound by affection, and moved about here and there.
The kinswomen held back the tears that were welling up from longing for the son of <s>Devakī</s>,
thinking, "May no inauspiciousness be ours as he goes out from the houses."
Mṛdaṅgas, conches, bherīs, vīṇās, paṇavas, and gomukha horns,
together with dhundhurīs, ānakas, bells, and dundubhis, sounded there.
The women of the <s>Kurus</s>, having climbed onto the palace roofs out of desire to see him,
showered <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with flowers, their glances smiling with love and bashfulness.
<s>Guḍākeśa</s>, dear to the dearest one, took up the white parasol,
adorned with strings of pearls and with a jeweled handle.
<s>Uddhava</s> and <s>Sātyaki</s> took up two exceedingly wondrous fans,
and, while flowers were being scattered over him, the lord of <s>Madhu</s> shone upon the road.
True blessings, uttered by brahmins, were heard here and there,
both not befitting and yet befitting him who is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> and is the soul of the <s>guṇas</s>.
Among those whose minds were fixed on the one praised in highest verses, there arose mutual conversation,
among the women of the capital of the <s>Kauravas</s>, charming to all who heard it.

children.text: sa vai kilāyaṃ puruṣaḥ purātano ya eka āsīdaviśeṣa ātmani
children.translated_text: "Surely this is that ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>, who alone existed in the undifferentiated self,

children.text: agre guṇebhyo jagadātmanīśvare nimīlitātman niśi suptaśaktiṣu ||
children.translated_text: before the <s>guṇas</s>, within the Lord, the self of the universe, when the powers slept in the night with the self withdrawn.

children.text: sa eva bhūyo nijavīryacoditāṃ svajīvamāyāṃ prakṛtiṃ sisṛkṣatīm
children.translated_text: Again he, impelled by his own power, followed his own living <s>māyā</s>, <s>prakṛti</s>, as she desired to create,
intending to establish forms and names in what was by nature without name and form, he who is the maker of scripture.

children.text: sa vā ayaṃ yat padam atra sūrayo jitendriyā nirjitamātariśvanaḥ
children.translated_text: This indeed is he whose state the sages here behold, having conquered the senses and mastered the breath,

children.text: paśyanti bhaktyutkalitāmalātmanā nanveṣa sattvaṃ parimārṣṭum arhati ||
children.translated_text: with pure selves overflowing with devotion; surely this one is able to cleanse <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: sa vā ayaṃ sakhyanugītasatkatho vedeṣu guhyeṣu ca guhyavādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: This indeed is he whose true stories are sung by his friends, and by speakers of secrets in the Vedas and secret teachings,

children.text: ya eka īśo jagadātmalīlayā sṛjatyavatyatti na tatra sajjate ||
children.translated_text: the one Lord who, by his play as the self of the universe, creates, protects, and devours, yet is not attached there.

children.text: yadā hyadharmeṇa tamodhiyo nṛpā jīvanti tatraiṣa hi sattvataḥ kila
children.translated_text: For when kings whose minds are darkened live by <s>adharma</s>, then this one, truly established in <s>sattva</s>,

children.text: dhatte bhagaṃ satyam ṛtaṃ dayāṃ yaśo bhavāya rūpāṇi dadhadyuge yuge ||
children.translated_text: assumes majesty, truth, cosmic order, compassion, and fame for the welfare of beings, taking forms age after age.

children.text: aho alaṃ ślāghyatamaṃ yadoḥ kulam aho alaṃ puṇyatamaṃ madhorvanam
children.translated_text: Ah, greatly praiseworthy indeed is the family of <s>Yadu</s>; ah, exceedingly holy indeed is the forest of <s>Madhu</s>,

children.text: yadeṣa puṃsām ṛṣabhaḥ śriyaḥ patiḥ svajanmanā caṅkramaṇena cāñcati ||
children.translated_text: since this bull among men, the husband of <s>Śrī</s>, adorns it by his birth and by his wandering there.

children.text: aho bata svaryaśasastiraskarī kuśasthalī puṇyayaśaskarī bhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, blessed <s>Kuśasthalī</s> eclipses the fame of heaven and gives holy fame to the earth,

children.text: paśyanti nityaṃ yadanugraheṣitaṃ smitāvalokaṃ svapatiṃ sma yatprajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for its people, by his grace, constantly see the smiling glance of their own lord.
Surely the Lord has been worshiped with vows, baths, oblations, and the like by these women whose hands he has taken in marriage,

children.text: pibanti yāḥ sakhyadharāmṛtaṃ muhur vrajastriyaḥ saṃmumuhuryadāśayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for they repeatedly drink, O friend, the nectar of his lips, for whose longing the women of <s>Vraja</s> were utterly bewildered.

children.text: yā vīryaśulkena hṛtāḥ svayaṃvare pramathya caidyapramukhān hi śuṣmiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who were won by the bridal price of valor at their svayaṃvara, after he crushed mighty men headed by the <s>Caidya</s>,
and the others, with sons such as <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Sāmba</s>, and <s>Amba</s>'s son, and those carried off by thousands when <s>Bhauma</s> was slain,

children.text: etāḥ paraṃ strītvam apāstapeśalaṃ nirastaśaucaṃ bata sādhu kurvate
children.translated_text: these women indeed make womanhood supremely good, though it is set aside as unrefined and devoid of purity,

children.text: yāsāṃ gṛhāt puṣkaralocanaḥ patir na jātvapaityāhṛtibhirhṛdi spṛśan ||
children.translated_text: for the lotus-eyed husband never departs from their houses, touching their hearts with gifts.
While the women of the city were speaking such words,
<s>Hari</s> went on, acknowledging their speech with a smiling glance.
<s>Ajātaśatru</s>, anxious about enemies and acting from affection, appointed a fourfold army
for the protection of the slayer of <s>Madhu</s> from hostile forces.
Then <s>Śauri</s>, having turned back the <s>Kauravas</s> who had come from afar and were pained by separation,

children.text: saṃnivartya dṛḍhaṃ snigdhān prāyāt svanagarīṃ priyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who were firmly attached to him, set out with his dear companions toward his own city.
He passed the <s>Kurujāṅgalas</s>, the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, the <s>Śūrasenas</s> along with the <s>Yamunā</s>,
<s>Brahmāvarta</s>, <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, the <s>Matsyas</s>, and then the <s>Sārasvatas</s>;
crossing the desert and the lands beyond the <s>Sauvīras</s> and <s>Abhīras</s>,
the mighty one, O <s>Bhārgava</s>, reached the <s>Ānartas</s>, his horses somewhat fatigued.
Here and there <s>Hari</s> was met by the local people, who came forward with honors,

children.text: sāyaṃ bheje diśaṃ paścādgaviṣṭho gāṃ gatastadā ||
children.translated_text: and at evening he reached the western direction, as the sun then goes to its setting.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ānartān sa upavrajya svṛddhāñ janapadān svakān
children.translated_text: Having approached the prosperous <s>Ānarta</s> lands, his own countrymen,

children.text: dadhmau daravaraṃ teṣāṃ viṣādaṃ śamayann iva ||
children.translated_text: he blew his excellent conch, as if dispelling their sorrow.
That conch, white-bellied though it was, shone with the red redness of <s>Urukrama</s>'s lower lip,
as it was being blown within the joined lotus of his hand, like a calling royal swan among lotus stalks.
Hearing that sound, which brought fear to the fear of the world,
all the subjects came forward, eager for the sight of their lord.
There, respectfully bringing offerings, as one brings a lamp to the sun,
they approached him who delights in himself and is ever completely satisfied by his own attainment.
With faces blooming from love, they spoke in voices choked by joy,
like children speaking to a father, to the friend of all and protector.

children.text: natāḥ sma te nātha sadāṅghripaṅkajaṃ viriñcavairiñcyasurendravanditam
children.translated_text: "We are always bowed to your lotus feet, O Lord, worshiped by <s>Brahmā</s>, the sons of <s>Brahmā</s>, and the lord of the gods,

children.text: parāyaṇaṃ kṣemam ihecchatāṃ paraṃ na yatra kālaḥ prabhavet paraḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the supreme refuge and highest welfare for those who seek security here, where Time, the supreme ruler, has no power.

children.text: bhavāya nastvaṃ bhava viśvabhāvana tvam eva mātātha suhṛtpatiḥ pitā
children.translated_text: For our welfare, be gracious to us, O source of the universe; you alone are mother, friend, husband, and father.

children.text: tvaṃ sadgururnaḥ paramaṃ ca daivataṃ yasyānuvṛttyā kṛtino babhūvima ||
children.translated_text: You are our true teacher and our supreme deity; by following you we have become fulfilled."

children.text: aho sanāthā bhavatā sma yadvayaṃ traiviṣṭapānām api dūradarśanam
children.translated_text: Ah, through you we have become people with a protector; may we see what is hard to see even for those in heaven:
your form, all-auspicious in beauty, its face softened by loving smiles and affectionate glances.

children.text: yarhyambujākṣāpasasāra bho bhavān kurūn madhūn vātha suhṛddidṛkṣayā
children.translated_text: Whenever, O lotus-eyed one, you go away, sir, to the <s>Kurus</s> or the <s>Madhus</s>, wishing to see your friends,

children.text: tatrābdakoṭipratimaḥ kṣaṇo bhaved raviṃ vinākṣṇoriva nastavācyuta ||
children.translated_text: there a single moment becomes like ten million years for us, O <s>Acyuta</s>, as eyes are useless without the sun.

children.text: kathaṃ vayaṃ nātha ciroṣite tvayi prasannadṛṣṭyākhilatāpaśoṣaṇam
children.translated_text: How shall we live, O lord, when you have stayed away for long,

children.text: jīvema te sundarahāsaśobhitam apaśyamānā vadanaṃ manoharam ||
children.translated_text: not seeing your charming face, bright with a beautiful smile and drying up every pain by its gracious glance?
As the people spoke these words, the lover of his devotees,
hearing them and extending his favor with his glance, entered the city.
It was protected by the <s>Madhus</s>, <s>Bhojas</s>, <s>Daśārhas</s>, <s>Arhas</s>, <s>Kukuras</s>, <s>Andhakas</s>, and <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
who were equal to himself in strength, like <s>Bhogavatī</s> protected by serpents.
It had the splendor of lotus ponds, with sacred trees, creepers, and retreats rich in every season and every abundance,
and was encircled by gardens, groves, and pleasure parks.
At its gateways, doors, and roads festive arches had been made,
and their bright flags and banners blocked the heat of the sun within.
Its great roads, streets, shops, and crossroads had been swept clean,
sprinkled with fragrant waters, and strewn with fruits, flowers, unbroken rice, and sprouts.
At every doorway of the houses it was adorned with yogurt, unbroken rice, fruits, and sugarcane,
with full water pots, offerings, incense, and lamps.
Hearing that their dearest one was arriving, high-minded <s>Vasudeva</s>,
<s>Akrūra</s>, <s>Ugrasena</s>, and <s>Rāma</s> of wondrous valor,
<s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>, and <s>Sāmba</s>, son of <s>Jāmbavatī</s>,
rose up from beds, seats, and meals, swept upward by the force of great joy.
Placing a lordly elephant in front, together with brahmins bearing auspicious things,
honored by the sound of conches and drums and by the chanting of sacred words,
they went out in chariots to meet him, delighted and filled with the reverent timidity born of love.
Hundreds of foremost women too, eager for the sight of him, came in vehicles,
the beauty of their faces and cheeks shining with glittering earrings.
Actors, dancers, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Sūtas</s>, <s>Māgadhas</s>, and panegyrists
sang the wondrous deeds of <s>Uttamaśloka</s>.
There the Blessed Lord approached according to rule his relatives, the citizens, and his attendants,
and accepted the honor of them all.
The mighty Lord reassured them with bows, greetings, embraces, touches of the hand, smiles, and glances,
and even those as lowly as dog-cookers he comforted with boons that fulfilled their wishes.
He himself, joined by blessings from his elders, the brahmins, and old men together with their wives,
and by others, including bards, entered the city.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had come onto the royal road of <s>Dvārakā</s>, the women of noble families, O brahmin,
climbed up onto the palaces, making the sight of him their great festival.
Though the residents of <s>Dvārakā</s> looked at him constantly every day,

children.text: na vitṛpyanti hi dṛśaḥ śriyo dhāmāṅgam acyutam ||
children.translated_text: their eyes were never satisfied by <s>Acyuta</s>, whose body was the abode of beauty.

children.text: śriyo nivāso yasyoraḥ pānapātraṃ mukhaṃ dṛśām
children.translated_text: His chest was the dwelling place of <s>Śrī</s>; his face was the drinking cup of the eyes;
his arms were the refuge of the guardians of the worlds, and his lotus feet were for the bees.
Attended by a white parasol and fans, and showered on the road with rains of flowers,
he shone in his yellow garment and forest garland like a cloud with sun, moon, rainbow, and lightning.
Having entered the house of his parents, embraced by his own mothers,
he joyfully bowed his head to the seven of them, headed by <s>Devakī</s>.
They placed their son on their laps, their breasts wet with the milk of affection,
and, overwhelmed with joy, bathed him with water from their eyes.
Then he entered his own unsurpassed residence, fulfilling every desire,

children.text: prāsādā yatra patnīnāṃ sahasrāṇi ca ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: where there were sixteen thousand palaces for his wives.

children.text: patnyaḥ patiṃ proṣya gṛhānupāgataṃ vilokya saṃjātamanomahotsavāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing their husband, who had been away, returned to the houses, his wives felt a great festival arise in their minds,
and suddenly rose from seats and couches from afar, together with their observances, their eyes and faces bashful.
With their sons, with their gazes, and with their inner selves, those whose feelings were hard to fathom embraced their husband,

children.text: niruddham apyāsravadambu netrayor vilajjatīnāṃ bhṛguvarya vaiklavāt ||
children.translated_text: and though they held it back, water flowed from the eyes of the embarrassed women, O best of the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, because of their agitation.

children.text: yadyapyasau pārśvagato rahogatas tathāpi tasyāṅghriyugaṃ navaṃ navam
children.translated_text: Although he was beside them in private, the pair of his feet appeared ever new to them,

children.text: pade pade kā virameta tatpadāc calāpi yacchrīrna jahāti karhicit ||
children.translated_text: step after step; what woman could turn away from that foot which even fickle <s>Śrī</s> never abandons?
Thus, among kings born as the burden of the earth, whose power was surrounded by armies of akṣauhiṇīs,

children.text: vidhāya vairaṃ śvasano yathānalaṃ mitho vadhenoparato nirāyudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he created enmity, as wind kindles fire, and, weaponless himself, brought them to rest through mutual slaughter.
This very Blessed Lord descended into this human world by his own <s>māyā</s>,
and took pleasure, as if he were an ordinary man, among heaps of jewel-like women.
Even Love was struck down by the spotless, charming smiles and bashful glances of those women, which revealed their overflowing passion;

children.text: saṃmuhya cāpam ajahāt pramadottamāstā yasyendriyaṃ vimathituṃ kuhakairna śekuḥ ||
children.translated_text: bewildered, he dropped his bow, yet those excellent women could not disturb the Lord's senses by their wiles.

children.text: tam ayaṃ manyate loko hyasaṅgam api saṅginam
children.translated_text: This ignorant world thinks him, though unattached, to be attached,
a man acting like a human being, because it judges him by comparison with itself.
This is the lordship of the Lord: though he stands within <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature),
he is not joined to its <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), just as the intelligence of those resting in him and always established in the Self is not joined to them.

children.text: taṃ menire 'balā mūḍhāḥ straiṇaṃ cānuvrataṃ rahaḥ
children.translated_text: The foolish women thought him, in secret, a lover of women and devoted to them,
not knowing the true measure of their husband, the Lord, just as ordinary opinions fail to know him.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
By the <s>Brahmaśiras</s> weapon released by <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, with its terrible brilliance,
the embryo of <s>Uttarā</s> was struck down, yet the Lord brought it back to life again.

children.text: tasya janma mahābuddheḥ karmāṇi ca mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: We wish to hear of the birth of that greatly intelligent and great-souled one, and of his deeds,

children.text: nidhanaṃ ca yathaivāsīt sa pretya gatavān yathā ||
children.translated_text: and also how his death came about and where he went after he had passed away.

children.text: tadidaṃ śrotum icchāmo gadituṃ yadi manyase
children.translated_text: We wish to hear this, if you think it fit to tell it.

children.text: brūhi naḥ śraddadhānānāṃ yasya jñānam adācchukaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Speak to us, who are full of faith, about the one to whom <s>Śuka</s> gave knowledge.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Dharmarāja</s> ruled the subjects, delighting them like a father,
free from longing for all desires through service to the feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: sampadaḥ kratavo lokā mahiṣī bhrātaro mahī
children.translated_text: Wealth, sacrifices, worlds, his queen, his brothers, the earth,
sovereignty over <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, and fame that had gone to heaven:

children.text: kiṃ te kāmāḥ suraspārhā mukundamanaso dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: what desires, envied even by the gods, O twice-born ones,
could bring joy to the king whose mind was on <s>Mukunda</s>, any more than other things can to a hungry man?
While still in his mother's womb, O descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, that hero,
burning then from the power of the weapon, saw a certain person.
He was the size of a thumb, stainless, with a flashing golden diadem,
beautiful to behold, dark, wearing a garment like lightning: <s>Acyuta</s>.
He was splendid, tall, four-armed, with earrings of heated gold,
with reddish eyes and a mace in his hand, moving around him in every direction.
He kept circling like a firebrand and repeatedly whirling the mace.
With his own mace he was scattering the weapon's blaze,
like the sun scattering mist nearby; the child looked on, wondering, 'Who is this?'
Having dispelled that force, the immeasurable Lord, the mighty protector of <s>dharma</s>,
<s>Hari</s> vanished there itself before the eyes of the ten-month-old child.
Then, when all excellent qualities were rising and the planets had arisen favorably,
the heir of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>'s line was born, again like <s>Pāṇḍu</s> in vigor.
The king, delighted in heart, had the birth-rite performed for him by brahmins
such as <s>Dhaumya</s> and <s>Kṛpa</s>, after having auspicious benedictions recited.

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ gāṃ mahīṃ grāmān hastyaśvān nṛpatirvarān
children.translated_text: At that holy moment of birth, the king, knowing holy rites, gave gold, cows, land, villages,

children.text: prādāt svannaṃ ca viprebhyaḥ prajātīrthe sa tīrthavit ||
children.translated_text: elephants, horses, excellent food, and fine gifts to the brahmins.
The satisfied brahmins spoke to the king, who was filled with humility:
'This child, O bull among the <s>Pauravas</s>, is born in this line of the <s>Pūrus</s>.
When the pure line had been brought to an end by irresistible fate,
he was given to you as a favor by powerful <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tasmān nāmnā viṣṇurāta iti loke bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Therefore in the world he will be named <s>Viṣṇurāta</s>,
and there is no doubt, greatly fortunate one, that he will be a great devotee of the Lord.'
The venerable king said:
Will this best one follow the royal sages of his line,
the great-souled men of holy fame, by his glory and by the praise of the good?
The brahmins said:
O son of <s>Pṛthā</s>, he will be a protector of subjects like <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, son of <s>Manu</s> himself,
devoted to brahmins and true to his word like <s>Rāma</s>, son of <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: eṣa dātā śaraṇyaśca yathā hyauśīnaraḥ śibiḥ
children.translated_text: He will be a giver and a refuge, just as <s>Śibi</s>, son of <s>Uśīnara</s>, was,
and he will spread the fame of his own people like the son of <s>Duṣyanta</s> among sacrificers.
He will be foremost among archers and equal to the two <s>Arjunas</s>;

children.text: hutāśa iva durdharṣaḥ samudra iva dustaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: he will be unassailable like fire and hard to cross like the ocean.

children.text: mṛgendra iva vikrānto niṣevyo himavān iva
children.translated_text: He will be bold like a lion and worthy of service like <s>Himavān</s>;
he will be patient like the earth and forbearing like parents.
In impartiality he will be equal to the grandsire, and in graciousness like <s>Giriśa</s>;
he will be a refuge for all beings, like the Lord who is the refuge of <s>Ramā</s>.
In the greatness of all good qualities, he will follow <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
he will be generous like <s>Rantideva</s> and righteous like <s>Yayāti</s>.

children.text: hṛtyā balisamaḥ kṛṣṇe prahrāda iva sadgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: In firmness he will be equal to <s>Bali</s>, and in true devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> like <s>Prahrāda</s>.
He will perform horse sacrifices and will attend upon the elders.
He will be the progenitor of royal sages and the chastiser of those who go astray.
He will restrain <s>Kali</s> for the sake of the earth and of <s>dharma</s>.
When he hears that his own death will come from <s>Takṣaka</s>, sent by a brahmin's son,
he will become free from attachment and resort to the feet of <s>Hari</s>.
Seeking to know the true nature of the self from the sage, the son of <s>Vyāsa</s>,
he will abandon this on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, O king, and go directly to the fearless state.
Thus instructing the king, the brahmins skilled in birth-rites
all received honor and returned to their own homes.

children.text: sa eṣa loke vikhyātaḥ parīkṣiditi yat prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: That lord became famous in the world as <s>Parīkṣit</s>,
because, meditating on the one he had seen before, he would examine people here.

children.text: sa rājaputro vavṛdhe āśu śukla ivoḍupaḥ
children.translated_text: That prince grew swiftly, like the bright moon,
being filled day by day by his guardians, as the moon is filled by its phases.
The king, intending to sacrifice with a horse sacrifice in order to remove the guilt of injury to his kinsmen,
obtained wealth, but he considered no source other than taxes and penalties.
Perceiving what he intended, his brothers, urged by <s>Acyuta</s>,
brought back abundant lost wealth from the northern direction.
With the materials thus gathered, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, son of <s>Dharma</s>, still fearful,
worshiped <s>Hari</s> with three horse-sacrifices.
The Blessed Lord, summoned by the king, had the twice-born priests conduct the king's sacrifice,
and stayed for some months, desiring the happiness of his friends.
Then, permitted by the king, by <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, and by his relatives,
he went to <s>Dvāravatī</s>, O brahmin, accompanied by <s>Arjuna</s> and surrounded by the <s>Yadus</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
On pilgrimage, <s>Vidura</s> learned from <s>Maitreya</s> the course of the self,
and, having gained the object he wished through that teaching, went to <s>Hāstinapura</s>.
The chamberlain had asked all the questions he had before <s>Kauṣārava</s>;
but, because exclusive devotion to <s>Govinda</s> had arisen in him, he ceased from them.

children.text: taṃ bandhum āgataṃ dṛṣṭvā dharmaputraḥ sahānujaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that kinsman arrived, <s>Dharmaputra</s>, together with his younger brothers,
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Yuyutsu</s>, <s>Sūta</s>, <s>Śāradvata</s>, and <s>Pṛthā</s>

children.text: gāndhārī draupadī brahman subhadrā cottarā kṛpī
children.translated_text: <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Draupadī</s>, O brahmin, <s>Subhadrā</s>, <s>Uttarā</s>, and <s>Kṛpī</s>,
and the other daughters-in-law of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, relatives, and women with their sons
went forth to meet him with great joy, as if life had returned to their bodies.
Having met him properly with embraces and salutations,
they, distressed by the longing of separation, shed floods of tears of love.
The king honored him after he had been given a seat.

children.text: taṃ bhuktavantaṃ viśrāntam āsīnaṃ sukham āsane
children.translated_text: When he had eaten, rested, and was sitting comfortably on the seat,

children.text: praśrayāvanato rājā prāha teṣāṃ ca śṛṇvatām ||
children.translated_text: the king, bowing down respectfully, spoke while they were listening.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
Do you still remember us, who grew up in the shade of your protection,
we who, with our mother, were rescued from many dangers, from poison, fire, and the like?
By what livelihood did you maintain yourselves while wandering over the circle of the earth?
Were the sacred fords and the chief holy fields on this earth visited?
Devotees of the Blessed Lord like you are themselves <s>tīrthas</s> (places of pilgrimage), O master;
they make the <s>tīrthas</s> into true <s>tīrthas</s> by the mace-bearer dwelling within their hearts.
Dear uncle, have our friends and kinsmen, whose deity is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭāḥ śrutā vā yadavaḥ svapuryāṃ sukham āsate ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Yādavas</s>, been seen or heard of by you? Are they dwelling happily in their own city?
Thus addressed by <s>Dharmarāja</s>, he described all of that,
in order, just as he had experienced it, except for the destruction of the <s>Yadu</s> clan.
For that unbearable and unpleasant event had indeed befallen men of itself;
compassionate and unable to see them distressed, he did not report it to those already sorrowing.

children.text: kaṃcit kālam athāvātsīt satkṛto devavat sukham
children.translated_text: Then for some time he stayed there happily, honored like a god,
bringing welfare to his elder brother and bringing happiness to all.
<s>Aryaman</s> bore the rod of punishment properly against wrongdoers,
while <s>Yama</s>, because of a curse, bore the state of a <s>śūdra</s> for a hundred years.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, having regained his kingdom and seen his grandson, the bearer of the family line,
rejoiced in supreme prosperity with his brothers, who resembled the guardians of the worlds.
For those attached to their houses and heedless through activity on his behalf,
Time, very hard to cross, passed unnoticed.
Understanding this, <s>Vidura</s> addressed <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:

children.text: rājan nirgamyatāṃ śīghraṃ paśyedaṃ bhayam āgatam ||
children.translated_text: O king, leave quickly. See this danger that has arrived.

children.text: pratikriyā na yasyeha kutaścit karhicit prabho
children.translated_text: There is no countermeasure against it here, from anywhere or at any time, O lord.

children.text: sa eṣa bhagavān kālaḥ sarveṣāṃ naḥ samāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is that Blessed Lord, Time, who has come upon us all.
When seized by him, a person is at once separated
even from his dearest life-breaths; how much more from other things, such as wealth?
Your fathers, brothers, friends, and sons have been slain; your lifetime has passed away.

children.text: ātmā ca jarayā grastaḥ parageham upāsase ||
children.translated_text: Your own body is gripped by old age, yet you stay in another's house.
You were blind from birth, and now you are deaf and dull in understanding;
your teeth are broken, your digestion is weak, and you are phlegmatic and bringing up phlegm, though still full of attachment.
Ah, how mighty is a creature's hope of life, since you,
like a house dog, eat morsels cast aside by <s>Bhīma</s>.
You set fire, gave poison, and defiled their wife;

children.text: hṛtaṃ kṣetraṃ dhanaṃ yeṣāṃ taddattairasubhiḥ kiyat ||
children.translated_text: you seized the kingdom and wealth of those men. What worth is life sustained by their gifts?
Even this body of yours, wretched and desirous of living,
passes away against your will, worn out by old age like garments.
Detached and freed from bonds, one should abandon this body whose own purpose is gone,
going on a path unknown; such a man is called steadfast.

children.text: yaḥ svakāt parato veha jātanirveda ātmavān
children.translated_text: He who, self-possessed, has become disenchanted here through his own insight or another's instruction,

children.text: hṛdi kṛtvā hariṃ gehāt pravrajet sa narottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who, placing <s>Hari</s> in his heart, leaves home, is the best of men.
Now let Your Majesty go northward, moving freely, with your path unknown;
from now on, Time will for the most part draw away the qualities of men.
Thus the king, the descendant of <s>Ājamīḍha</s>, whose wisdom was his eye, was awakened by his younger brother <s>Vidura</s>;

children.text: chittvā sveṣu snehapāśān draḍhimno niścakrāma bhrātṛsandarśitādhvā ||
children.translated_text: cutting the strong nooses of affection for his own people, he went out on the path shown by his brother.

children.text: patiṃ prayāntaṃ subalasya putrī pativratā cānujagāma sādhvī
children.translated_text: The daughter of <s>Subala</s>, a faithful and virtuous wife, followed her husband as he departed,

children.text: himālayaṃ nyastadaṇḍapraharṣaṃ manasvinām iva sat samprahāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: toward the <s>Himālaya</s>, a joy to those who have laid down the rod, like a true battle for the high-spirited.

children.text: ajātaśatruḥ kṛtamaitro hutāgnir viprān natvā tilagobhūmirukmaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having performed the morning rite, offered in the fire, and bowed to the brahmins with sesame, cows, land, and gold,

children.text: gṛhaṃ praviṣṭo guruvandanāya na cāpaśyat pitarau saubalīṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: entered the house to salute his elders, but he did not see his fathers or <s>Saubalī</s>.
There he asked <s>Sañjaya</s>, who was seated, his mind disturbed:

children.text: gāvalgaṇe kva nastāto vṛddho hīnaśca netrayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: O son of <s>Gavalgaṇa</s>, where is our old father, deprived of his two eyes?

children.text: ambā ca hataputrārtā pitṛvyaḥ kva gataḥ suhṛt
children.translated_text: And where is mother, pained by the loss of her sons? Where has my well-wishing uncle gone?
Has he, whose kinsmen were slain, expecting some wrong from foolish me,
fallen in sorrow into the <s>Gaṅgā</s> together with his wife?

children.text: pitaryuparate pāṇḍau sarvān naḥ suhṛdaḥ śiśūn
children.translated_text: When our father <s>Pāṇḍu</s> had died, those two paternal uncles
protected all of us, helpless children, from calamity. Where have they gone from here?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Out of compassion, weakened by affection and wasted by separation, the charioteer
could not see his own lord and, being greatly distressed, did not reply.
Wiping his tears with his hands and steadying himself by himself,
he answered <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, remembering the feet of his master.
<s>Sañjaya</s> said:
I do not know the resolve of your two fathers, O joy of the family,
nor of <s>Gāndhārī</s>, O mighty-armed one; I have been deprived by those great souls.
Then the blessed <s>Nārada</s> arrived together with <s>Tumburu</s>.
Rising to meet him, bowing, and honoring the sage together with his younger brothers, he said:
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:

children.text: nāhaṃ veda gatiṃ pitrorbhagavan kva gatāvitaḥ
children.translated_text: I do not know the course of my two fathers, Blessed one, nor where they have gone from here.

children.text: ambā vā hataputrārtā kva gatā ca tapasvinī ||
children.translated_text: Or where has that poor mother gone, afflicted with grief for her slain sons?
like a helmsman on the shoreless sea, the Blessed Lord, who sees the farther shore.
Then the Blessed Lord <s>Nārada</s>, best of sages, spoke.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: mā kañcana śuco rājan yadīśvaravaśaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Do not grieve for anyone, O king, since the world is subject to the power of the Lord.

children.text: lokāḥ sapālā yasyeme vahanti balim īśituḥ
children.translated_text: All these worlds, together with their protectors, bring tribute to him as ruler.

children.text: sa saṃyunakti bhūtāni sa eva viyunakti ca ||
children.translated_text: He joins beings together, and he alone separates them.

children.text: yathā gāvo nasi protāstantyāṃ baddhāśca dāmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Just as cattle are strung by the nose and bound with ropes to a cord,
so beings, bound by names to the cord of speech, bring tribute to the ruler.
Just as the joining and separation of toys here
come about by the will of the player, so also do those of human beings by the will of the Lord.

children.text: yan manyase dhruvaṃ lokam adhruvaṃ vā na cobhayam
children.translated_text: Whether you think the world permanent, impermanent, or neither,

children.text: sarvathā na hi śocyāste snehādanyatra mohajāt ||
children.translated_text: in every way they are not to be lamented by you; grief arises only from affection born of delusion.
Therefore abandon, dear one, this weakness of yourself, produced by ignorance,

children.text: kathaṃ tvanāthāḥ kṛpaṇā varteraṃste ca māṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'How will these helpless, pitiable people live without me?'
This body, made of the five elements, is subject to time, karma, and the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).

children.text: katham anyāṃstu gopāyet sarpagrasto yathā param ||
children.translated_text: How could it protect others, like one seized by a serpent protecting another?
The handless are the food of those with hands, and the footless of four-footed creatures;

children.text: phalgūni tatra mahatāṃ jīvo jīvasya jīvanam ||
children.translated_text: the weak are the food of the strong there: one living being is the livelihood of another.

children.text: tadidaṃ bhagavān rājann eka ātmātmanāṃ svadṛk
children.translated_text: This, O king, is the Blessed Lord, the one Self of selves, self-seeing,
who appears within and without; behold him made manifold by <s>māyā</s>.
This same Blessed Lord, O great king, the source of beings,
has now descended in the form of Time into this world for the destruction of the enemies of the gods.
The task of the gods has been accomplished; he waits for what remains.
Until the Lord remains here, so long should you watch over things.

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saha bhrātrā gāndhāryā ca svabhāryayā
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, together with his brother and with <s>Gāndhārī</s>, his wife,
has gone to the hermitage of the seers on the southern side of <s>Himavat</s>.

children.text: srotobhiḥ saptabhiryā vai svardhunī saptadhā vyadhāt
children.translated_text: There the heavenly river, by her streams, divided herself sevenfold,
in various ways for the pleasure of the seven; they call it the seven-streamed.
Having bathed there at the three daily times and offered oblations into the fires according to rule,
subsisting on water, with his self pacified, he remains free from desires.
He has mastered his posture, mastered his breath, and withdrawn the six senses,
his impurity of rajas, sattva, and tamas destroyed by meditation on <s>Hari</s>.
Joining it to the self that is knowledge, and dissolving that into the knower of the field,
he will place the self in <s>Brahman</s>, the support, like the space in a pot into space.
With the surge of <s>māyā</s>'s qualities destroyed, his organs and mind restrained,
with all intake of food stopped, he remains motionless like a post.
Do not become an obstacle to him, who has renounced all action.
From today, O king, on the fifth day thereafter,

children.text: kalevaraṃ hāsyati svaṃ tac ca bhasmībhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: he will abandon his own body, and it will become ashes.
When her husband's body is being burned by the fires along with the hut,

children.text: bahiḥ sthitā patiṃ sādhvī tam agnim anu vekṣyati ||
children.translated_text: his virtuous wife, standing outside, will gaze upon him and enter that fire after him.
But then <s>Vidura</s>, O delight of the <s>Kurus</s>, hearing of that wonder,
will depart from there, filled with both joy and sorrow, devoting himself to sacred fords.
Having spoken thus, <s>Nārada</s> ascended to heaven together with <s>Tumburu</s>.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, placing his words in his heart, gave up his grief.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
After <s>Jiṣṇu</s> had set out for <s>Dvārakā</s> out of a desire to see his relatives,

children.text: jñātuṃ ca puṇyaślokasya kṛṣṇasya ca viceṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: and to learn the doings of the meritoriously famed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: vyatītāḥ katicin māsās tadā nāyāt tato 'rjunaḥ
children.translated_text: some months passed, and then <s>Arjuna</s> had not returned from there.
The bearer of the <s>Kuru</s> line saw omens of dreadful form.
He saw the fierce course of time, in which the nature of the seasons was overturned,
and the increasingly sinful behavior of people whose selves were anger, greed, and falsehood.
Conduct was mostly crooked, friendship mixed with deceit,
and there was discord among fathers, mothers, friends, brothers, and husbands and wives.
Seeing the extremely inauspicious omens as time went on among men,
and seeing their nature become greed and adharma, the king spoke to his younger brother.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
<s>Jiṣṇu</s> was sent to <s>Dvārakā</s> out of a desire to see his relatives

children.text: jñātuṃ ca puṇyaślokasya kṛṣṇasya ca viceṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: and to learn the doings of the meritoriously famed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Seven months have now passed, <s>Bhīmasena</s>, and your younger brother

children.text: nāyāti kasya vā hetor nāhaṃ vededam añjasā ||
children.translated_text: does not return. For what reason, I do not know this plainly.
Has that time, foretold by the divine seer, now arrived,
when the Blessed Lord wishes to abandon his own body, the playground of his Self?

children.text: yasmān naḥ sampado rājyaṃ dārāḥ prāṇāḥ kulaṃ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: From whose favor our wealth, kingdom, wives, lives, lineage, and subjects
came to be, along with victory over rivals and the worlds.
Look, tiger among men, at these portents, celestial, earthly, and bodily,
fearful ones announcing nearby danger to us, bewildering the mind.
My thighs, eyes, and arms, dear one, throb again and again,
and there is trembling in my heart; from near at hand they will bring something unwelcome.
This she-jackal, her mouth like fire, cries at the rising sun,
and this dog, dear one, barks at me without fear.

children.text: śastāḥ kurvanti māṃ savyaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ paśavo 'pare
children.translated_text: The auspicious animals pass me on the left, and others on the right,
and, tiger among men, I observe my mounts weeping.
This pigeon is a messenger of death, and the owl shakes my mind;

children.text: pratyulūkaśca kuhvānair viśvaṃ vai śūnyam icchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: with their hooting, the rival owls seem to wish the whole world empty.

children.text: dhūmrā diśaḥ paridhayaḥ kampate bhūḥ sahādribhiḥ
children.translated_text: The directions are smoky, halos surround the luminaries, and the earth shakes together with the mountains.
There is a great thunderclap, dear one, together with thunderclouds.
The wind blows harsh to the touch, spreading darkness with dust.

children.text: asṛg varṣanti jaladā bībhatsam iva sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The clouds rain blood, hideous, as it were, on every side.

children.text: sūryaṃ hataprabhaṃ paśya grahamardaṃ mitho divi
children.translated_text: Look at the sun, its brilliance destroyed, and at the planets striking one another in the sky.
With the hosts of beings thrown into confusion, heaven and earth seem as if they are blazing.

children.text: nadyo nadāśca kṣubhitāḥ sarāṃsi ca manāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: Rivers and streams are agitated, and so are lakes and minds.
Fire does not blaze up with ghee. What will this time bring about?

children.text: na pibanti stanaṃ vatsā na duhyanti ca mātaraḥ
children.translated_text: The calves do not drink from the udder, nor do the mothers give milk.
The cows, their faces wet with tears, cry, and the bulls do not rejoice in the cowherd settlement.
The images of the deities seem to weep; they sweat and indeed tremble.
These countries, villages, towns, gardens, mines, and hermitages

children.text: bhraṣṭaśriyo nirānandāḥ kim aghaṃ darśayanti naḥ ||
children.translated_text: are stripped of prosperity and joyless. What calamity are they not showing us?
I think that by these great portents the earth is surely
deprived of the Lord's feet, whose splendor belongs to no other person, and has had her good fortune slain.
As he was thinking thus, with a mind that had seen evil omens,
O brahmin, <s>Kapi-dhvaja</s> returned to the king from the city of the <s>Yadus</s>.
Seeing him fallen at his feet, unlike before, distressed,
his face downcast, letting drops fall from the lotuses of his eyes,
the king, his heart alarmed, looked at his younger brother, whose complexion had faded,

children.text: pṛcchati sma suhṛn madhye saṃsmaran nāraderitam ||
children.translated_text: and questioned him in the midst of his friends, remembering what <s>Nārada</s> had said.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> said:
Are our kinsmen dwelling happily in the city of <s>Ānarta</s>,
the <s>Madhus</s>, <s>Bhojas</s>, <s>Daśārhas</s>, <s>Arhas</s>, <s>Sātvatās</s>, <s>Andhakas</s>, and <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>?

children.text: śūro mātāmahaḥ kaccit svastyāste vātha māriṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Is grandfather <s>Śūra</s> still well, my dear one?
And is my maternal uncle <s>Anakadundubhi</s>, together with his younger brothers, in good health?
Are his seven sisters, his wives, my maternal aunts, together with their sons,
headed by <s>Devakī</s>, themselves safe together with their daughters-in-law?
Is King <s>Āhuka</s> alive, though his son is wicked, and is his younger brother alive?
Are <s>Hṛdīka</s> with his son, <s>Akrūra</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Gada</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>
well, and those headed by <s>Śatrujit</s> too?

children.text: kaccidāste sukhaṃ rāmo bhagavān sātvatāṃ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Does the Blessed <s>Rāma</s>, lord of the <s>Sātvatās</s>, remain in happiness?
Is <s>Pradyumna</s>, the great chariot-warrior of all the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, dwelling happily?
And is the Blessed <s>Aniruddha</s>, whose force is profound, prospering?
<s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>, and <s>Sāmba</s>, son of <s>Jāmbavatī</s>,
and the other foremost sons of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with their sons, headed by <s>Ṛṣabha</s>,
and likewise the attendants of <s>Śauri</s>, headed by <s>Śrutadeva</s> and <s>Uddhava</s>,
<s>Sunanda</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Śīrṣaṇya</s>, and the other bulls among the <s>Sātvatās</s>:
are they all dwelling in welfare, sheltered by the arms of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?
Do they, bound to us by friendship, remember our welfare?
And is the Blessed <s>Govinda</s>, devoted to brahmins and loving to his devotees,

children.text: kaccit pure sudharmāyāṃ sukham āste suhṛdvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: dwelling happily in the city, in the <s>Sudharmā</s> hall, surrounded by friends?

children.text: maṅgalāya ca lokānāṃ kṣemāya ca bhavāya ca
children.translated_text: For the auspiciousness of the worlds, and for their security and well-being,
the primordial person, friend of <s>Ananta</s>, dwells in the ocean of the <s>Yadu</s> clan.
In their own city, protected by the staffs of his arms, the honored <s>Yadavas</s>
sport in supreme bliss, like associates of the Great Person.
By the chief act of service to his feet, <s>Satyā</s> and the other sixteen thousand women
conquered the gods in battle and carry off the blessings fit for the beloved of the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Living under the rise of his staff-like arms, the heroic <s>Yadus</s>, fearless on every side,
again and again tread with their feet the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly, fit for the best of the gods, which was brought by force.

children.text: kaccit te 'nāmayaṃ tāta bhraṣṭatejā vibhāsi me
children.translated_text: Dear one, are you free from illness? You appear to me bereft of splendor.
Have you failed to receive honor, or been insulted, or, dear one, stayed away for a long time?
Surely you have not been struck by inauspicious absences, sounds, and the like?

children.text: na dattam uktam arthibhya āśayā yat pratiśrutam ||
children.translated_text: Was something promised and spoken to petitioners in hope left ungiven?

children.text: kaccit tvaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bālaṃ gāṃ vṛddhaṃ rogiṇaṃ striyam
children.translated_text: Surely you, a giver of refuge, did not abandon a brahmin, a child, a cow, an old man, a sick person, a woman,
or any being that had come to you seeking shelter?

children.text: kaccit tvaṃ nāgamo 'gamyāṃ gamyāṃ vāsatkṛtāṃ striyam
children.translated_text: Surely you did not approach a woman not to be approached, or a woman fit to be approached but not honored?
Or were you defeated on the road by men neither superior nor equal to you?
Perhaps you ate while the aged and children, who deserved to be fed, had not been fed?

children.text: jugupsitaṃ karma kiṃcit kṛtavān na yadakṣamam ||
children.translated_text: Have you done some detestable act that was unfit for you?
Or else, without your dearest one, your heart and kinsman of the self,

children.text: śūnyo 'smi rahito nityaṃ manyase te 'nyathā na ruk ||
children.translated_text: do you think, 'I am empty, always bereft'? There is no other reason for your pain.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ kṛṣṇasakhaḥ kṛṣṇo bhrātrā rājñā vikalpitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the friend of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, was questioned in many ways by his brother, the king,
his appearance giving grounds for many suspicions, wasted by separation from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
With the lotus of his face and heart drying up from grief, his splendor gone,
remembering only that mighty one, he was unable to answer.
With difficulty he steadied his sorrow and wiped his eyes with his hand.
Distressed by love and longing bound tight through absence,

children.text: sakhyaṃ maitrīṃ sauhṛdaṃ ca sārathyādiṣu saṃsmaran
children.translated_text: remembering friendship, companionship, affection, and acts such as his service as charioteer,
he spoke thus to the king, his elder brother, in a voice choked and stammering with tears.
<s>Arjuna</s> said:
I have been deceived, great king, by <s>Hari</s> in the form of a kinsman,
by whom my great splendor, astonishing even the gods, has been taken away.
When separated from him even for a moment, the world is indeed unpleasant to behold,

children.text: ukthena rahito hyeṣa mṛtakaḥ procyate yathā ||
children.translated_text: just as this body, deprived of life-breath, is called a corpse.
By reliance on him, at <s>Drupada</s>'s house, at the opening of the svayaṃvara, before kings maddened by desire,

children.text: tejo hṛtaṃ khalu mayābhihataśca matsyaḥ sajjīkṛtena dhanuṣādhigatā ca kṛṣṇā ||
children.translated_text: their brilliance was indeed taken away by me, the fish was struck, and <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> was won with the strung bow.

children.text: yatsannidhāvaham u khāṇḍavam agnaye 'dām indraṃ ca sāmaragaṇaṃ tarasā vijitya
children.translated_text: In whose presence I gave <s>Khāṇḍava</s> to <s>Agni</s>, after swiftly conquering <s>Indra</s> and the hosts of gods in battle,

children.text: labdhā sabhā mayakṛtādbhutaśilpamāyā digbhyo 'haran nṛpatayo balim adhvare te ||
children.translated_text: and through whom the assembly hall, made by <s>Maya</s> with marvelous craft and illusion, was obtained, while kings from every quarter brought tribute to your sacrifice.

children.text: yattejasā nṛpaśiro'ṅghrim ahan makhārtham āryo 'nujastava gajāyutasattvavīryaḥ
children.translated_text: By whose splendor, O king, your noble younger brother, whose strength and valor equaled ten thousand elephants, made the heads of kings fall at your feet for the sake of the sacrifice,

children.text: tenāhṛtāḥ pramathanāthamakhāya bhūpā yanmocitāstadanayan balim adhvare te ||
children.translated_text: and the kings who had been brought for the sacrifice of the lord of the <s>Pramathas</s>, when released by him, brought tribute to your sacrifice.
Your wife's lovely braided hair, most worthy of praise after the great consecration arranged for your sacrifice, was touched in the assembly by the cheats;
and she, foremost among the tearful, scattered it and fell at his feet; he made those men's wives loosen their hair after their lords had been slain.

children.text: yo no jugopa vana etya durantakṛcchrād durvāsaso 'riracitādayutāgrabhug yaḥ
children.translated_text: He who came to the forest and protected us from the unbearable danger caused by <s>Durvāsas</s>, arranged by our enemy,

children.text: śākānnaśiṣṭam upayujya yatastrilokīṃ tṛptām amaṃsta salile vinimagnasaṅghaḥ ||
children.translated_text: used up the leftover vegetable food, so that the company immersed in the water thought the three worlds satisfied.

children.text: yattejasātha bhagavān yudhi śūlapāṇir vismāpitaḥ sagirijo 'stram adān nijaṃ me
children.translated_text: By whose splendor the blessed <s>Śūlapāṇi</s> himself, together with <s>Girijā</s>, was astonished in battle and gave me his own weapon;

children.text: anye 'pi cāham amunaiva kalevareṇa prāpto mahendrabhavane mahadāsanārdham ||
children.translated_text: and others too, so that in this very body I reached the palace of great <s>Indra</s> and obtained half of his great seat.

children.text: tatraiva me viharato bhujadaṇḍayugmaṃ gāṇḍīvalakṣaṇam arātivadhāya devāḥ
children.translated_text: There, while I was dwelling, the gods together with <s>Indra</s> took refuge in my pair of club-like arms, marked by <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, for the killing of enemies;

children.text: sendrāḥ śritā yadanubhāvitam ājamīḍha tenāham adya muṣitaḥ puruṣeṇa bhūmnā ||
children.translated_text: that was produced by his power, O <s>Ājamīḍha</s>; today I have been robbed by that supreme Person.

children.text: yadbāndhavaḥ kurubalābdhim anantapāram eko rathena tatare 'ham atīryasattvam
children.translated_text: As his kinsman, I alone crossed in my chariot the endless, shoreless ocean of the <s>Kuru</s> army, though its strength was uncrossable,

children.text: pratyāhṛtaṃ bahu dhanaṃ ca mayā pareṣāṃ tejāspadaṃ maṇimayaṃ ca hṛtaṃ śirobhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and I took back much wealth from the enemies, and from their heads I seized jewel-studded crowns, the seats of their splendor.
In the armies of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, the preceptor, and <s>Śalya</s>, adorned with circles of the chariots of foremost kings,

children.text: agrecaro mama vibho rathayūthapānām āyurmanāṃsi ca dṛśā saha oja ārchat ||
children.translated_text: he, O lord, went before me among the leaders of chariot troops and, with his glance, took away their life, minds, and strength.
The weapons of unfailing power aimed at me by the preceptor, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, the grandson, the <s>Trigartas</s>, <s>Śalya</s>, the <s>Saindhava</s>, <s>Bāhlika</s>, and others,
did not touch me, just as the weapons of demons do not touch a servant of <s>Nṛhari</s>.

children.text: sautye vṛtaḥ kumatinātmada īśvaro me yatpādapadmam abhavāya bhajanti bhavyāḥ
children.translated_text: Though I, foolish-minded, chose as my charioteer my Lord, the self-giving master whose lotus feet the blessed worship to escape becoming,

children.text: māṃ śrāntavāham arayo rathino bhuviṣṭhaṃ na prāharan yadanubhāvanirastacittāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the enemy chariot-warriors did not strike me when my horses were weary and I stood on the ground, because their minds had been driven away by his power.

children.text: narmāṇyudārarucirasmitaśobhitāni he pārtha he 'rjuna sakhe kurunandaneti
children.translated_text: His jokes, adorned with noble and beautiful smiles, and his words to me, 'O <s>Pārtha</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>, friend, son of the <s>Kurus</s>,'

children.text: saṃjalpitāni naradeva hṛdispṛśāni smarturluṭhanti hṛdayaṃ mama mādhavasya ||
children.translated_text: those conversations, O king, touching the heart, tear my heart apart when I remember <s>Mādhava</s>.
In lying down, sitting, walking, boasting, eating, and the like, because of our oneness I deceived him, the truthful, undivided one;

children.text: sakhyuḥ sakheva pitṛvat tanayasya sarvaṃ sehe mahān mahitayā kumateraghaṃ me ||
children.translated_text: yet the great one endured all the sin of my foolishness, as a friend does for a friend or a father for his son, by his honored greatness.

children.text: so 'haṃ nṛpendra rahitaḥ puruṣottamena sakhyā priyeṇa suhṛdā hṛdayena śūnyaḥ
children.translated_text: So I, O king of men, bereft of <s>Puruṣottama</s>, my friend, beloved companion, well-wisher, and heart, am empty;
on the road, guarding the women taken under <s>Urukrama</s>'s protection, dear one, I have been defeated by wicked herdsmen, like a powerless woman.

children.text: tadvai dhanusta iṣavaḥ sa ratho hayāste so 'haṃ rathī nṛpatayo yata ānamanti
children.translated_text: That is the same bow, those are the same arrows, that is the same chariot, those are the same horses, and I am the same chariot-warrior before whom kings bowed;

children.text: sarvaṃ kṣaṇena tadabhūdasadīśariktaṃ bhasman hutaṃ kuhakarāddham ivoptam ūṣyām ||
children.translated_text: yet all that in a moment became unreal, bereft of the Lord, like an oblation poured into ashes, a magic trick, or seed sown in barren soil.
O king, as for the friends of ours in the city of our friend about whom you asked,
they were bewildered by a brahmin's curse and killed one another with their fists.
After drinking the liquor called <s>Vāruṇī</s>, their minds were churned by intoxication;
as if not recognizing one another, only four or five remained.
For the most part this is the working of the Blessed Lord, the sovereign master:

children.text: mitho nighnanti bhūtāni bhāvayanti ca yan mithaḥ ||
children.translated_text: beings kill one another, and they also sustain one another mutually.
Just as among water-creatures in water the great eat the smaller,

children.text: durbalān balino rājan mahānto balino mithaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the strong eat the weak, O king, while the great and strong eat one another,
so the powerful Lord, by means of the mightiest and greatest <s>Yadus</s>, removed the others who were burdens of the earth,
and then removed the <s>Yadus</s> themselves through the <s>Yadus</s> killing one another.
The words spoken by <s>Govinda</s>, suited to place, time, and purpose and able to soothe the burning of the heart,
carry away my mind when I remember them.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
As <s>Jiṣṇu</s> thus contemplated the lotus of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet,
his stainless mind became peaceful through very deep friendship.
Through devotion, whose force was increased by meditation on <s>Vāsudeva</s>'s feet,
<s>Arjuna</s>'s understanding had all its impurities churned away.

children.text: gītaṃ bhagavatā jñānaṃ yat tat saṅgrāmamūrdhani
children.translated_text: The knowledge that had been sung by the Blessed Lord on the front of the battle,
though blocked by time, action, and darkness, that lord regained once more.
Free from grief through attaining <s>Brahman</s>, with the doubt of duality cut off,
with his nature dissolved, beyond the qualities, without the subtle mark, he was no longer subject to birth.
Having heard of the Blessed Lord's departure and the end of the <s>Yadu</s> family,
self-contained <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> set his mind on the path to heaven.

children.text: pṛthāpyanuśrutya dhanañjayoditaṃ nāśaṃ yadūnāṃ bhagavadgatiṃ ca tām
children.translated_text: <s>Pṛthā</s> too, hearing from <s>Dhanañjaya</s> of the destruction of the <s>Yadus</s> and that course of the Blessed Lord,
fixed her self on the Blessed <s>Adhokṣaja</s> with single-minded devotion and ceased from saṃsāra (worldly existence).
The unborn one abandoned that body by which he had removed the burden of the earth,
like removing a thorn with a thorn; both were alike for the Lord.
Just as an actor assumes and casts off forms such as that of a fish,

children.text: bhūbhāraḥ kṣapito yena jahau tacca kalevaram ||
children.translated_text: he abandoned that body by which the earth's burden had been destroyed.

children.text: yadā mukundo bhagavān imāṃ mahīṃ jahau svatanvā śravaṇīyasatkathaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Mukunda</s>, the Blessed Lord whose true and noble stories are worth hearing, left this earth with that very body,
then on that very day <s>Kali</s>, the cause of misfortune for unawakened minds, followed after.

children.text: yudhiṣṭhirastat parisarpaṇaṃ budhaḥ pure ca rāṣṭre ca gṛhe tathātmani
children.translated_text: Wise <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, perceiving its creeping advance in the city, the kingdom, the household, and likewise in himself,
seeing the wheel of <s>adharma</s> beginning with greed, falsehood, crookedness, and violence, prepared for departure.

children.text: svarāṭ pautraṃ vinayinam ātmanaḥ susamaṃ guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: The sovereign installed his grandson, humble and very equal to himself in virtues,
as lord of the ocean-girdled earth at <s>Gajāhvaya</s>.
Then in <s>Mathurā</s> he likewise made <s>Vajra</s> lord of <s>Śūrasena</s>;
after arranging the prājāpatya sacrifice, the lord took the sacred fires into himself.
Having cast off there all that, the fine garments, bracelets, and the rest,
free from possessiveness and ego, with every bond completely severed,

children.text: vācaṃ juhāva manasi tat prāṇa itare ca tam
children.translated_text: he offered speech into the mind, that mind into breath, and the other senses into that,
and he offered the apāna, together with its discharge, into death, and that into the fivefold elements.

children.text: tritve hutvā ca pañcatvaṃ tac caikatve 'juhonmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Having offered the fivefold into the threefold, and that too into oneness, the sage offered
everything into the self, and the self into imperishable <s>Brahman</s>.
Clad in rags, without food, with speech restrained and hair loosened,
showing the form of his self like one inert, mad, or possessed,
looking at nothing, he went forth, hearing nothing, as though deaf;
he entered the northern quarter, already traveled by great souls,

children.text: hṛdi brahma paraṃ dhyāyan nāvarteta yato gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: meditating in his heart on the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, from which one who has gone does not return.
All his brothers followed after him, firmly resolved,
when they saw that the people on earth had been touched by <s>Kali</s>, the friend of <s>adharma</s>.
They had well accomplished all their purposes and knew the ultimate good of the self;
in their minds they fixed the lotus feet of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.
With their understanding purified by devotion intensified through meditation on him,
and with minds wholly fixed on that state of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the goal,
they attained what is hard to attain for the unreal and sense-absorbed,
cleansed of sin, reaching that place by the stainless self alone.
<s>Vidura</s> too, abandoning his own body at <s>Prabhāsa</s>,
with his mind absorbed in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, went with the ancestors to his own abode.
And <s>Draupadī</s>, then understanding that her husbands no longer looked back,
with her mind fixed solely on the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, reached him.

children.text: yaḥ śraddhayaitadbhagavatpriyāṇāṃ pāṇḍoḥ sutānām iti samprayāṇam
children.translated_text: Whoever faithfully hears this departure of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, dear to the Lord,

children.text: śṛṇotyalaṃ svastyayanaṃ pavitraṃ labdhvā harau bhaktim upaiti siddhim ||
children.translated_text: fully auspicious and purifying, gains devotion to <s>Hari</s> and attains perfection.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ parīkṣiddvijavaryaśikṣayā mahīṃ mahābhāgavataḥ śaśāsa ha
children.translated_text: Then <s>Parīkṣit</s>, the great devotee, governed the earth according to the instruction of the best of the twice-born,

children.text: yathā hi sūtyām abhijātakovidāḥ samādiśan vipra mahadguṇastathā ||
children.translated_text: just as those skilled in birth omens had foretold at his birth, O brahmin; he was indeed of great qualities.
He married <s>Irāvatī</s>, the daughter of <s>Uttara</s>,
and by her begot four sons, <s>Janamejaya</s> and the others.
He performed three horse-sacrifices on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, rich in gifts,
taking <s>Śāradvata</s> as priest, where the gods became visible to the eye.
The hero, by his might, subdued <s>Kali</s> somewhere during his conquest of the quarters,
a śūdra wearing the marks of a king and striking a pair, cow and bull, with his foot.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
For what reason did the king subdue <s>Kali</s> during his conquest of the quarters?

children.text: nṛdevacihnadhṛk śūdra ko 'sau gāṃ yaḥ padāhanat
children.translated_text: Who was that śūdra, bearing the signs of a ruler, who struck the cow with his foot?
Tell that, O greatly fortunate one, if it rests on the story of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Or rather, for the holy ones who lick the nectar of his lotus feet,
what use are other unreal conversations, by which life is uselessly wasted?

children.text: kṣudrāyuṣāṃ nṛṇām aṅga martyānām ṛtam icchatām
children.translated_text: O dear one, for men of short life, mortals who desire immortality,
the Blessed Lord <s>Death</s> has been summoned here for the sacrificial office of slaughterer.

children.text: na kaścin mriyate tāvadyāvad āsta ihāntakaḥ
children.translated_text: No one dies so long as <s>Antaka</s> remains here;
for this purpose the Blessed One was summoned by the supreme seers,
so that in the world of men the nectar-like words of <s>Hari</s>'s play may be drunk.
For a dull man, of dull understanding and short life,

children.text: nidrayā hriyate naktaṃ divā ca vyarthakarmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the night is carried away by sleep, and the day by futile activities.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: yadā parīkṣit kurujāṅgale 'vasat kaliṃ praviṣṭaṃ nijacakravartite
children.translated_text: When <s>Parīkṣit</s> was dwelling in <s>Kurujāṅgala</s> and heard the unwelcome report that <s>Kali</s> had entered his own imperial realm,

children.text: niśamya vārtām anatipriyāṃ tataḥ śarāsanaṃ saṃyugaśauṇḍirādade ||
children.translated_text: then, skilled in battle, he took up his bow.

children.text: svalaṃkṛtaṃ śyāmaturaṅgayojitaṃ rathaṃ mṛgendradhvajam āśritaḥ purāt
children.translated_text: Mounted from the city on a well-adorned chariot yoked with dark horses and bearing a lion-banner,
surrounded by his own army furnished with chariots, horses, elephants, and infantry, he went out to conquer the quarters.

children.text: bhadrāśvaṃ ketumālaṃ ca bhārataṃ cottarān kurūn
children.translated_text: Having conquered <s>Bhadrāśva</s>, <s>Ketumāla</s>, <s>Bhārata</s>, and the northern <s>Kurus</s>,
and the regions such as <s>Kimpuruṣa</s>, he took tribute.
Cities and forests, and rivers of clear water,
men like gods and women lovely to behold,
prosperous and never seen before, <s>Dhanañjaya</s> saw;
also shining mansions and women resembling apsarases.
There, wherever he went, he heard the fame of his great forefathers
being sung, indicating the greatness of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
He heard how he himself had been saved from the fiery power of <s>Aśvatthāman</s>'s weapon,

children.text: snehaṃ ca vṛṣṇipārthānāṃ teṣāṃ bhaktiṃ ca keśave ||
children.translated_text: and of the affection between the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and the <s>Pārthas</s>, and their devotion to <s>Keśava</s>.
Being supremely pleased with them, his eyes widening with love,
the high-minded king gave them great wealth, garments, and necklaces.
Charioteering, attendance, service, friendship, embassy, the hero's seat, following, praise, and prostration...

children.text: snigdheṣu pāṇḍuṣu jagatpraṇatiṃ ca viṣṇorbhaktiṃ karoti nṛpatiścaraṇāravinde ||
children.translated_text: Among the affectionate, pale ones the king performs the bowing of the world and devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> at his lotus feet.
While he was thus conducting himself, day after day following the way of the former kings,

children.text: nātidūre kilāścaryaṃ yadāsīt tan nibodha me ||
children.translated_text: there occurred, it is said, not far away a wonder; hear that from me.

children.text: dharmaḥ padaikena caran vicchāyām upalabhya gām
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, moving on one foot, saw the Earth without luster
and questioned her, her face tearful, like a mother bereft of her calf.
<s>Dharma</s> said:
Is there, good lady, no illness in your own self? You are without luster, and your face is somewhat withered.

children.text: ālakṣaye bhavatīm antarādhiṃ dūre bandhuṃ śocasi kaṃcanāmba ||
children.translated_text: I perceive some inner distress in you. Are you grieving for some relative far away, mother?

children.text: pādairnyūnaṃ śocasi maikapādam ātmānaṃ vā vṛṣalairbhokṣyamāṇam
children.translated_text: Do you grieve for me, deficient in feet and having only one foot, or for yourself, soon to be enjoyed by low men?

children.text: āho surādīn hṛtayajñabhāgān prajā uta svin maghavatyavarṣati ||
children.translated_text: Or for the gods and others whose shares in sacrifice have been taken away, or perhaps for the subjects when <s>Maghavat</s> does not rain?

children.text: arakṣyamāṇāḥ striya urvi bālān śocasyatho puruṣādairivārtān
children.translated_text: Do you grieve, O Earth, for women unprotected, and for children afflicted as if by man-eaters,

children.text: vācaṃ devīṃ brahmakule kukarmaṇyabrahmaṇye rājakule kulāgryān ||
children.translated_text: or for the goddess Speech in a family of brahmins given to bad acts, and for the foremost families in a royal line that is hostile to brahmanical order?

children.text: kiṃ kṣatrabandhūn kalinopasṛṣṭān rāṣṭrāṇi vā tairavaropitāni
children.translated_text: Or for kṣatriyas in name only, invaded by <s>Kali</s>, or for kingdoms cast down by them,
or for the people of the world turned here and there toward food, drink, clothing, bathing, and sexual intercourse?
Or, mother Earth, are you remembering the deeds, delayed until liberation,
of <s>Hari</s>, who took an avatāra in order to remove your great burden and has now disappeared, leaving you abandoned?

children.text: idaṃ mamācakṣva tavādhimūlaṃ vasundhare yena vikarśitāsi
children.translated_text: Tell me this, O <s>Vasundharā</s>, the root of your distress, by which you are emaciated.

children.text: kālena vā te balināṃ balīyasā surārcitaṃ kiṃ hṛtam amba saubhagam ||
children.translated_text: Has your fortune, worshiped by the gods, been taken away by time, which is stronger than the strong, mother?
The Earth said:

children.text: bhavān hi veda tat sarvaṃ yan māṃ dharmānupṛcchasi
children.translated_text: You indeed know all that about which you question me, O <s>Dharma</s>,
you by whose four feet, bringing happiness to the world, you stand.

children.text: satyaṃ śaucaṃ dayā kṣāntistyāgaḥ santoṣa ārjavam
children.translated_text: Truth, purity, compassion, patience, generosity, contentment, uprightness,
tranquility, self-restraint, austerity, impartiality, endurance, withdrawal, sacred learning,

children.text: jñānaṃ viraktiraiśvaryaṃ śauryaṃ tejo balaṃ smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: knowledge, detachment, lordly power, heroism, splendor, strength, memory,

children.text: svātantryaṃ kauśalaṃ kāntirdhairyaṃ mārdavam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: independence, skill, beauty, steadfastness, and gentleness,

children.text: prāgalbhyaṃ praśrayaḥ śīlaṃ saha ojo balaṃ bhagaḥ
children.translated_text: boldness, humility, good conduct, forbearance, vigor, strength, prosperity,
depth, stability, faith, fame, honor, and absence of pride:

children.text: ete cānye ca bhagavan nityā yatra mahāguṇāḥ
children.translated_text: these and other great qualities, O blessed one, are eternally present where he is,
