children.text: prārthyā mahattvam icchadbhirna viyanti sma karhicit ||
children.translated_text: qualities sought by those who desire greatness, and they never depart from him.
Therefore, now deprived of that abode of qualities, the dwelling of <s>Śrī</s>,
I grieve for the world, which is watched by sinful <s>Kali</s>.
I grieve for myself, and for you, best of the immortals,

children.text: devān pitṝn ṛṣīn sādhūn sarvān varṇāṃstathāśramān ||
children.translated_text: for the gods, the ancestors, the seers, the holy, and all the varṇas and āśramas.
For many days <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, desiring the release of his sidelong glance, practiced austerity, having taken refuge in the Blessed Lord.

children.text: sā śrīḥ svavāsam aravindavanaṃ vihāya yatpādasaubhagam alaṃ bhajate 'nuraktā ||
children.translated_text: That same <s>Śrī</s>, leaving her own abode, the lotus grove, lovingly serves the full beauty of his feet.
My body was adorned with the glorious footprints of the Blessed Lord, marked by lotus, thunderbolt, goad, and banner,

children.text: trīn atyaroca upalabhya tato vibhūtiṃ lokān sa māṃ vyasṛjadutsmayatīṃ tadante ||
children.translated_text: and, having obtained that splendor, I surpassed the three worlds; yet at the end he left me, as I was becoming proud.
He, self-ruling, removed my excessive burden, the hundred akṣauhiṇīs of kings of demonic lineages,

children.text: tvāṃ duḥstham ūnapadam ātmani pauruṣeṇa sampādayan yaduṣu ramyam abibhradaṅgam ||
children.translated_text: and, by his own heroic power, restored you, distressed and deficient in feet, while bearing a beautiful body among the <s>Yadus</s>.

children.text: kā vā saheta virahaṃ puruṣottamasya premāvalokarucirasmitavalgujalpaiḥ
children.translated_text: Who could endure separation from the Supreme Person, with his loving glance, charming smile, and graceful words,

children.text: sthairyaṃ samānam aharan madhumāninīnāṃ romotsavo mama yadaṅghriviṭaṅkitāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who robbed the proud women of their firmness? A thrill rose on me, marked by his feet.
While those two, Earth and <s>Dharma</s>, were speaking in this way at that time,

children.text: parīkṣin nāma rājarṣiḥ prāptaḥ prācīṃ sarasvatīm ||
children.translated_text: the royal seer named <s>Parīkṣit</s> reached the eastern <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
There the king saw a pair, a cow and a bull, being beaten as if without a protector,
and a lowborn man holding a staff, bearing the marks of a king.
He saw the bull, white as a lotus fiber, urinating as if from fear,
trembling, standing on one foot, and sinking down as he was struck by the śūdra.

children.text: gāṃ ca dharmadughāṃ dīnāṃ bhṛśaṃ śūdrapadāhatām
children.translated_text: And he saw the cow, giver of the milk of dharma, miserable, heavily kicked by the śūdra's foot,
bereft of her calf, tearful-faced, thin, and longing for grass.
Having mounted his chariot fitted with gold,
with his bow strung, he questioned him in a voice deep as thunderclouds:
Who are you, strong man, who in a world under my protection violently strikes the powerless by force?
In dress you are like a god among men, but in action, like an actor, you are no twice-born man.
Since you, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has gone far away together with the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow,
are striking in secret those who should not be grieved, you are pitiable and deserve death.

children.text: tvaṃ vā mṛṇāladhavalaḥ pādairnyūnaḥ padā caran
children.translated_text: Or are you, white as a lotus fiber, deficient in feet and moving on one foot,
some god in the form of a bull, causing us distress?
Never, on this earth embraced by the staff-like arms of the lords of the <s>Kauravas</s>,
do sorrows of living beings fall upon it, apart from yours.

children.text: mā saurabheyātra śuco vyetu te vṛṣalādbhayam
children.translated_text: Do not grieve here, O son of <s>Surabhī</s>; let your fear of the lowborn man depart.

children.text: mā rodīr amba bhadraṃ te khalānāṃ mayi śāstari ||
children.translated_text: Do not weep, mother. May there be welfare for you, while I am the punisher of the wicked.
The intoxicated king in whose realm all subjects, O virtuous one, are terrified by the wicked
loses his fame, lifespan, fortune, and final state.

children.text: eṣa rājñāṃ paro dharmo hyārtānām ārtinigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: This is the highest dharma of kings: the restraint of the suffering of the afflicted.
Therefore I shall kill this lowest of the wicked, this injurer of beings.
Who cut off your three feet, O son of <s>Surabhī</s>, you who had four feet?
May no such men as you be in the realm of kings who follow <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: ākhyāhi vṛṣa bhadraṃ vaḥ sādhūnām akṛtāgasām
children.translated_text: Tell me, O bull; good fortune to you, to the virtuous who have done no wrong.
Tell me the one who has disfigured you and sullied the fame of the <s>Pārthas</s>.
By joining suffering to an innocent being, he has fear of me from every side.
For there will be only welfare for the virtuous when the wicked are subdued.
Whoever, unrestrained, commits an offense here against innocent creatures,
I shall tear off his arm, with its bracelet, even if he were an immortal himself.
For the highest <s>dharma</s> of a king is the protection of those who stand in their own <s>dharma</s>,
while he punishes others here according to the <s>śāstra</s>, those who stray from the path when there is no emergency.
<s>Dharma</s> said:
This word of yours, removing fear from the afflicted, is fitting for the descendants of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,

children.text: yeṣāṃ guṇagaṇaiḥ kṛṣṇo dautyādau bhagavān kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose host of virtues caused the Blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to serve as envoy and in other roles.

children.text: na vayaṃ kleśabījāni yataḥ syuḥ puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: We do not know, O bull among men, the seeds of suffering from which they arise,
being bewildered by differences of doctrine about that person.
Some, dwelling in speculation, say that the self itself is the cause of the self's suffering;

children.text: daivam anye 'pare karma svabhāvam apare prabhum ||
children.translated_text: others say it is fate, others karma, and still others say that nature is the lord.
Among some there is the settled view that it is beyond reasoning and indescribable.
Therefore, O royal seer, consider what is appropriate here by your own judgment.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When <s>Dharma</s> had spoken thus, that emperor, O best of twice-born men,
with a collected mind and free from distress, answered him.
The king said:
You speak <s>dharma</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s>; you are <s>Dharma</s>, bearing the form of a bull.
For the place of the doer of <s>adharma</s> would also belong to the informer against him.
Or indeed the course of divine <s>māyā</s> is surely inaccessible
to the mind and even to the speech of living beings; this is the settled conclusion.

children.text: tapaḥ śaucaṃ dayā satyam iti pādāḥ kṛte kṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Austerity, purity, compassion, and truth were your feet, complete in the Kṛta age.
Three of them have been broken by portions of <s>adharma</s>, by pride, attachment, and intoxication.
Now, O <s>Dharma</s>, your remaining foot is truth, by which you may continue.
This <s>Kali</s>, strengthened by falsehood, wishes to seize that foot.
And this Earth, whose great burden was laid aside by the Blessed Lord,
was made wondrous everywhere by his glorious footfalls.
That virtuous lady grieves with tears, like an unfortunate woman abandoned by her husband,

children.text: abrahmaṇyā nṛpavyājāḥ śūdrā bhokṣyanti mām iti ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'Men hostile to Brahmins, Śūdras disguised as kings, will enjoy me.'

children.text: iti dharmaṃ mahīṃ caiva sāntvayitvā mahārathaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the great chariot-warrior consoled <s>Dharma</s> and the Earth,
and took up his sharpened sword against <s>Kali</s>, the cause of <s>adharma</s>.
Realizing that he wished to kill him, <s>Kali</s> abandoned his royal emblem
and, bewildered with fear, approached the root of his feet with his head.
When he had fallen at his feet, the heroic, compassionate lover of the lowly,

children.text: śaraṇyo nāvadhīcchlokya āha cedaṃ hasann iva ||
children.translated_text: worthy of praise and a giver of refuge, did not kill him, but spoke this, as if smiling.
The king said:

children.text: na te guḍākeśayaśodharāṇāṃ baddhāñjalervai bhayam asti kiṃcit
children.translated_text: There is no fear at all for you, standing with joined hands, from those who uphold the fame of <s>Guḍākeśa</s>.

children.text: na vartitavyaṃ bhavatā kathañcana kṣetre madīye tvam adharmabandhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But you, ally of <s>adharma</s>, must in no way dwell in my realm.
When you dwell in the bodies of human rulers, this mass of <s>adharma</s> follows after you:

children.text: lobho 'nṛtaṃ cauryam anāryam aṃho jyeṣṭhā ca māyā kalahaśca dambhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: greed, falsehood, theft, ignoble conduct, sin, misfortune, deceit, quarrel, and hypocrisy.

children.text: na vartitavyaṃ tadadharmabandho dharmeṇa satyena ca vartitavye
children.translated_text: Therefore you must not dwell, ally of <s>adharma</s>, where <s>dharma</s> and truth are to prevail,
in <s>Brahmāvarta</s>, where those skilled in the spread of sacrifice worship the Lord of sacrifice with sacrifices.

children.text: yasmin harirbhagavān ijyamāna ijyātmamūrtiryajatāṃ śaṃ tanoti
children.translated_text: There the Blessed Lord <s>Hari</s>, being worshiped as the very embodied self of worship, grants welfare to the worshipers,
and unfailing desires to moving and unmoving beings, as this Self does, like the air within and without.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus commanded by <s>Parīkṣit</s>, that <s>Kali</s>, born trembling,
spoke this to him, who had raised his sword and stood ready like one with staff in hand.
<s>Kali</s> said:

children.text: yatra kva vātha vatsyāmi sārvabhauma tavājñayā
children.translated_text: Wherever I may dwell, O sovereign, by your command,
there too I see you with bow and arrows taken up.

children.text: tan me dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha sthānaṃ nirdeṣṭum arhasi
children.translated_text: Therefore, best of upholders of <s>dharma</s>, you should designate a place for me,
where, controlled, I may dwell, abiding by your command.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then, when he was entreated, the lord gave places to that <s>Kali</s>:
gambling, drinking, women, and slaughter, where <s>adharma</s> is fourfold.
And when he begged again, the lord gave him gold.

children.text: tato 'nṛtaṃ madaṃ kāmaṃ rajo vairaṃ ca pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: From that came falsehood, intoxication, lust, passion, and enmity as the fifth.
In these five places, the sources of <s>adharma</s>, <s>Kali</s>
dwelt by the command of the son of <s>Uttarā</s>, who had granted them.

children.text: athaitāni na seveta bubhūṣuḥ puruṣaḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: Therefore a man who desires well-being should never resort to these places,
especially a king, a protector of the people and a teacher, who is devoted to <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: vṛṣasya naṣṭāṃstrīn pādān tapaḥ śaucaṃ dayām iti
children.translated_text: The three lost feet of the bull, namely austerity, purity, and compassion,
he restored; and, having reassured the Earth, he strengthened her.
That very king now occupies the throne suited to a ruler,
set down by his grandfather the king when he wished to enter the forest.
Now that royal seer sits in <s>Gajāhvaya</s>, shining with the splendor of the lord of the <s>Kauravas</s>,
greatly fortunate, a universal monarch of vast fame.
Such is the power of this king, the son of <s>Abhimanyu</s>,

children.text: yasya pālayataḥ kṣauṇīṃ yūyaṃ satrāya dīkṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: during whose rule over the earth you have been consecrated for the sacrificial session.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: yo vai drauṇyastravipluṣṭo na māturudare mṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: He who, though scorched by the weapon of <s>Drauṇi</s>, did not die in his mother's womb,
by the grace of the Blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose deeds are wondrous,
and who, when the danger to his life came from <s>Takṣaka</s>, arisen from a Brahmin's wrath,
did not become bewildered from great fear, because his mind was offered to the Blessed Lord,
renouncing attachment on every side and having understood the state of the unconquered Lord,
as a disciple of the son of <s>Vyāsa</s>, he abandoned his own body on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
For those who relish the nectar of his story, the accounts of <s>Uttamaśloka</s>,
there would be no bewilderment even at the time of death, as they remember the lotus of his feet.
<s>Kali</s>, though he had entered here everywhere, could not prevail so long
as the great lord, the son of <s>Abhimanyu</s>, was sole emperor on the earth.

children.text: yasminn ahani yarhyeva bhagavān utsasarja gām
children.translated_text: On the very day when the Blessed Lord released the earth,
on that very day <s>Kali</s>, born from <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), followed him here.

children.text: nānudveṣṭi kaliṃ samrāṭ sāraṅga iva sārabhuk
children.translated_text: The emperor did not hate <s>Kali</s>, being like a bee that takes only the essence,
because through him good deeds quickly succeed, while other deeds, though done, do not.

children.text: kiṃ nu bāleṣu śūreṇa kalinā dhīrabhīruṇā
children.translated_text: What indeed can cowardly <s>Kali</s> do among the childlike while a hero is present, since he fears the steadfast?

children.text: apramattaḥ pramatteṣu yo vṛko nṛṣu vartate ||
children.translated_text: He is alert among the heedless, moving among men like a wolf.
This holy tale of <s>Parīkṣit</s> has been described to you by me,
joined with the story of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, just as you asked.
Whatever stories of the Blessed Lord, whose deeds are vast, are fit to be told,
being founded on his qualities and actions, those should be cultivated by men who desire blessedness.
The sages said:

children.text: sūta jīva samāḥ saumya śāśvatīrviśadaṃ yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>, gentle one, live for endless years with stainless fame,

children.text: yastvaṃ śaṃsasi kṛṣṇasya martyānām amṛtaṃ hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: since you proclaim to us mortals the nectar of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
In this rite, where certainty is lacking, for us whose selves are darkened by smoke,
you make us drink the honeyed liquor from the lotus feet of <s>Govinda</s>.
We do not weigh heaven, nor even freedom from rebirth, as equal to a single moment
of association with those associated with the Blessed Lord; how much less mortal blessings?
What knower of flavor could ever be satisfied in the story of him who is the exclusive final refuge of the greatest souls?

children.text: nāntaṃ guṇānām aguṇasya jagmur yogeśvarā ye bhavapādmamukhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The masters of yoga, beginning with <s>Bhava</s> and <s>Padma</s>, have not reached the end of the qualities of the qualityless one.

children.text: tan no bhavān vai bhagavatpradhāno mahattamaikāntaparāyaṇasya
children.translated_text: Therefore may you, whose chief concern is the Blessed Lord,

children.text: harerudāraṃ caritaṃ viśuddhaṃ śuśrūṣatāṃ no vitanotu vidvan ||
children.translated_text: O learned one, unfold for us who long to hear the noble, pure deed of <s>Hari</s>, the exclusive final refuge of the greatest souls.

children.text: sa vai mahābhāgavataḥ parīkṣid yenāpavargākhyam adabhrabuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: That great devotee <s>Parīkṣit</s>, with vast understanding,
through the knowledge voiced by <s>Vaiyāsaki</s>, reached the root of the feet of him whose banner bears the king of birds, called liberation.

children.text: tan naḥ paraṃ puṇyam asaṃvṛtārtham ākhyānam atyadbhutayoganiṣṭham
children.translated_text: Tell us that supremely holy narrative, whose meaning is unconcealed, fixed in most wondrous yoga,
endowed with the deeds of <s>Ananta</s>, concerning <s>Parīkṣit</s>, delightful to the devotees of the Blessed Lord.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: aho vayaṃ janmabhṛto 'dya hāsma vṛddhānuvṛttyāpi vilomajātāḥ
children.translated_text: Ah! Today we who bear birth, though born from a mixed and lower lineage,

children.text: dauṣkulyam ādhiṃ vidhunoti śīghraṃ mahattamānām abhidhānayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are honored even by following the elders; connection with the names of the greatest quickly shakes off the distress of bad birth.
How much more, then, for one who chants the name of that one, the exclusive final refuge of the greatest souls,
the Blessed Lord <s>Ananta</s> of infinite power, whom they call <s>Ananta</s> because of the greatness of his qualities.
Surely enough has been indicated by this much concerning him whose qualities have no equal and no superior:
his majesty, leaving others who pray for her, enjoys the dust of his feet, though he does not desire her.
And since the water released from his toenails, brought as worship by <s>Viriñca</s>,

children.text: seśaṃ punātyanyatamo mukundāt ko nāma loke bhagavatpadārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: purifies the world together with <s>Śeṣa</s>, who in the world, other than <s>Mukunda</s>, can be named by the word 'Bhagavat'?

children.text: yatrānuraktāḥ sahasaiva dhīrā vyapohya dehādiṣu saṅgam ūḍham
children.translated_text: In him, the steadfast, becoming attached, at once cast off deep clinging to the body and the like

children.text: vrajanti tat pāramahaṃsyam antyaṃ yasminn ahiṃsopaśamaḥ svadharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and reach that final <s>paramahaṃsya</s> (supreme ascetic state), in which nonviolence and tranquility are one's own <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ hi pṛṣṭo 'ryamaṇo bhavadbhir ācakṣa ātmāvagamo 'tra yāvān
children.translated_text: For I have been asked by you, O honorable ones; I shall explain here as much self-realization as there is.

children.text: nabhaḥ patantyātmasamaṃ patatriṇas tathā samaṃ viṣṇugatiṃ vipaścitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As birds fly in the sky according to their own capacity, so the wise equally attain the path of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Once, raising his bow and wandering in the forest on a hunt,
following deer, he became extremely weary, hungry, and thirsty.
Not seeing a body of water, he entered that hermitage
and saw a sage seated, peaceful, with eyes closed.
His senses, breath, mind, and intellect were restrained; he was withdrawn,
having gone beyond the three states, become <s>Brahman</s>, and changeless.
He was covered with scattered matted locks and with a skin of the ruru deer;
with his palate drying up, the king asked water of him in that condition.
Having not obtained grass, a seat, water, and the like, and not having received <s>arghya</s> (honor-water) or kind words,
he thought himself as if dishonored and became angry.
Suddenly, in him whose self was tormented by hunger and thirst, something unprecedented
arose toward the brahmin, O brahman: jealousy and anger.

children.text: sa tu brahmaṛṣeraṃse gatāsum uragaṃ ruṣā
children.translated_text: In anger he placed a lifeless snake on the shoulder of the brahmin seer
with the tip of his bow, and, going out, returned to the city.
'Is this man, with all his faculties withdrawn and his eyes closed,

children.text: mṛṣāsamādhir āhosvit kiṃ nu syāt kṣatrabandhubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: in false <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), or what? What indeed can be the case with kṣatriya-wretches?'
His son, a boy of exceeding splendor, was playing with other boys;

children.text: rājñāghaṃ prāpitaṃ tātaṃ śrutvā tatredam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: hearing that his father had been subjected to offense by the king, he spoke this there:

children.text: aho adharmaḥ pālānāṃ pīvnāṃ balibhujām iva
children.translated_text: 'Ah, what <s>adharma</s> of protectors grown fat, like tribute-eaters!
That servants, gatekeepers, like dogs, commit offense against their master!
For a kṣatriya-wretch has been appointed by brahmins as a house-protector;

children.text: sa kathaṃ tadgṛhe dvāḥsthaḥ sabhāṇḍaṃ bhoktum arhati ||
children.translated_text: how then can he, standing at the door of that house, deserve to eat from its vessels?
Now that the Blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the chastiser of those who go on wrong paths, has departed,

children.text: tadbhinnasetūn adyāhaṃ śāsmi paśyata me balam ||
children.translated_text: today I shall punish those breakers of boundaries; behold my power.'
Having said this, the sage's boy, his eyes copper-red with anger,
sipped water from the <s>Kauśikī</s> and released a thunderbolt of speech.
'On the seventh day <s>Takṣaka</s> will bite this violator of limits,

children.text: daṅkṣyati sma kulāṅgāraṃ codito me tatadruham ||
children.translated_text: this cinder of his family, who harmed my father, impelled by me.'
Then the boy, returning to the hermitage, saw the snake's body on his father's neck...

children.text: pitaraṃ vīkṣya duḥkhārto muktakaṇṭho ruroda ha ||
children.translated_text: Seeing his father, he was afflicted with grief and cried aloud with his throat unchecked.

children.text: sa vā āṅgiraso brahman śrutvā sutavilāpanam
children.translated_text: O Brahmin, that descendant of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, hearing his son's lamentation,
slowly opened his eyes and saw the dead snake on his shoulder.

children.text: visṛjya taṃ ca papraccha vatsa kasmāddhi rodiṣi
children.translated_text: He cast it away and asked, "Child, why are you crying?

children.text: kena vā te 'pakṛtam ityuktaḥ sa nyavedayat ||
children.translated_text: Or who has wronged you?" Thus addressed, he reported it.

children.text: niśamya śaptam atadarhaṃ narendraṃ sa brāhmaṇo nātmajam abhyanandat
children.translated_text: Hearing that the king, who did not deserve it, had been cursed, that Brahmin did not approve of his son.

children.text: aho batāṃho mahadadya te kṛtam alpīyasi droha ururdamo dhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Ah, alas! Today you have committed a great sin; for a slight offense you have imposed a heavy punishment.

children.text: na vai nṛbhirnaradevaṃ parākhyaṃ saṃmātum arhasyavipakvabuddhe
children.translated_text: O immature-minded one, you should not regard the king, who is called a god among men, as equal to ordinary men.

children.text: yattejasā durviṣaheṇa guptā vindanti bhadrāṇyakutobhayāḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Protected by his intolerable power, the subjects find welfare and live without fear.
Dear one, when the person bearing the name of king is not seen as the discus-bearing Lord,
then this world, unprotected and full of thieves, will perish at once like a flock without a keeper.

children.text: tadadya naḥ pāpam upaityananvayaṃ yan naṣṭanāthasya vasorvilumpakāt
children.translated_text: Then this sin comes upon us, causelessly, from the plundering of wealth belonging to one whose protector is lost:

children.text: parasparaṃ ghnanti śapanti vṛñjate paśūn striyo 'rthān purudasyavo janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: people, become numerous robbers, kill one another, curse one another, and seize cattle, women, and goods.
Then the noble <s>dharma</s> of men, joined with the conduct of the varṇas and āśramas and founded on the three Vedas, dissolves away.
After that, for those whose selves are absorbed in wealth and pleasure, there is mixture of classes, as among dogs and monkeys.
That king is a protector of <s>dharma</s>, a great emperor of vast fame,
directly a great devotee, a royal seer, and performer of horse sacrifices.
Being afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, and being helpless, he does not deserve our curse.
This sin has been committed by a child of immature understanding against innocent servants of his own.

children.text: pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tadbhagavān sarvātmā kṣantum arhati ||
children.translated_text: May the Blessed Lord, the Self of all, forgive that sin.

children.text: tiraskṛtā vipralabdhāḥ śaptāḥ kṣiptā hatā api
children.translated_text: Though insulted, deceived, cursed, abused, or even killed,

children.text: nāsya tat pratikurvanti tadbhaktāḥ prabhavo 'pi hi ||
children.translated_text: the Lord's devotees, though powerful, do not retaliate against such an act.
Thus the great sage, remorseful over the offense committed by his son,
did not consider as an offense what had been done to him personally by the king.
For in this world holy men, though placed by others amid the pairs of opposites,

children.text: na vyathanti na hṛṣyanti yata ātmāguṇāśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not distressed and do not rejoice, because the self is beyond the support of the guṇas."
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: mahīpatistvatha tatkarma garhyaṃ vicintayann ātmakṛtaṃ sudurmanāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, deeply dejected, reflected on that blameworthy act done by himself:

children.text: aho mayā nīcam anāryavat kṛtaṃ nirāgasi brahmaṇi gūḍhatejasi ||
children.translated_text: "Ah, I have acted basely, like an ignoble man, toward a blameless Brahmin of hidden power.

children.text: dhruvaṃ tato me kṛtadevahelanād duratyayaṃ vyasanaṃ nātidīrghāt
children.translated_text: Surely, because I have slighted one who is to be revered as divine, an unavoidable calamity will come upon me before long.

children.text: tadastu kāmaṃ hyaghaniṣkṛtāya me yathā na kuryāṃ punarevam addhā ||
children.translated_text: Let it be so, if it serves to remove my sin, so that I may certainly never again act in this way.

children.text: adyaiva rājyaṃ balam ṛddhakośaṃ prakopitabrahmakulānalo me
children.translated_text: Today let the fire of the angered Brahmin family burn up my kingdom, army, and abundant treasury,
so that such sinful thought toward Brahmins, gods, and cows may never again arise in me, an inauspicious man."

children.text: sa cintayann ittham athāśṛṇodyathā muneḥ sutokto nirṛtistakṣakākhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking in this way, he then heard how the ruin named <s>Takṣaka</s> had been pronounced by the sage's son.

children.text: sa sādhu mene na cireṇa takṣakā nalaṃ prasaktasya viraktikāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: He regarded <s>Takṣaka</s>, soon to come, as good, as a cause of detachment for one attached.

children.text: atho vihāyemam amuṃ ca lokaṃ vimarśitau heyatayā purastāt
children.translated_text: Then, having abandoned both this world and the next, after having judged them beforehand as things to be rejected,
and considering service to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet supreme, he sat down to fast unto death by the river of the immortals.
That river, whose waters are made especially powerful by the dust of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet mixed with shining, beautiful tulasī,

children.text: punāti lokān ubhayatra seśān kastāṃ na seveta mariṣyamāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: purifies the worlds, together with their lords, here and hereafter; what man about to die would not resort to her?

children.text: iti vyavacchidya sa pāṇḍaveyaḥ prāyopaveśaṃ prati viṣṇupadyām
children.translated_text: Thus, having made his decision, that descendant of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> undertook fasting unto death on the <s>Viṣṇupadī</s>,
and, with undivided devotion, keeping a sage's vow and freed from all attachment, fixed his mind on <s>Mukunda</s>'s feet.
There came to him great-souled sages with their disciples, purifying the world.

children.text: prāyeṇa tīrthābhigamāpadeśaiḥ svayaṃ hi tīrthāni punanti santaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For saints themselves purify holy places, usually under the pretext of visiting those places.
<s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, <s>Śaradvān</s>, <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
<s>Parāśara</s>, the son of <s>Gādhi</s>, then <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Utathya</s>, <s>Indrapramada</s>, and <s>Idhmavāha</s>,
<s>Medhātithi</s>, <s>Devala</s>, <s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s>, <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and <s>Pippalāda</s>,

children.text: maitreya aurvaḥ kavaṣaḥ kumbhayonir dvaipāyano bhagavān nāradaśca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s>, <s>Aurva</s>, <s>Kavaṣa</s>, <s>Kumbhayoni</s>, the blessed <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, and <s>Nārada</s>,
and other foremost divine seers, foremost Brahmin seers, foremost royal seers, and <s>Aruṇa</s> and others as well.

children.text: nānārṣeyapravarān sametān abhyarcya rājā śirasā vavande ||
children.translated_text: The king honored those assembled eminent descendants of many seers and bowed to them with his head.

children.text: sukhopaviṣṭeṣvatha teṣu bhūyaḥ kṛtapraṇāmaḥ svacikīrṣitaṃ yat
children.translated_text: Then, when they were comfortably seated, he bowed again and, with a clear mind,
standing before them with joined hands, informed them of what he wished to do.
The king said:
"Ah, we are most blessed among kings, whose nature is to be shown favor by the greatest souls.

children.text: rājñāṃ kulaṃ brāhmaṇapādaśaucād dūrādvisṛṣṭaṃ bata garhyakarma ||
children.translated_text: Alas, the family of kings, because of its censurable deeds, is kept far away from the water that has washed Brahmins' feet.
For me, whose mind has been repeatedly attached to household life, the Lord of high and low has made this very sin

children.text: nirvedamūlo dvijaśāparūpo yatra prasakto bhayam āśu dhatte ||
children.translated_text: take the form of a Brahmin's curse, rooted in detachment, whereby one who is attached quickly takes fear.

children.text: taṃ mopayātaṃ pratiyantu viprā gaṅgā ca devī dhṛtacittam īśe
children.translated_text: Let the Brahmins and the goddess <s>Gaṅgā</s> accept me, who have approached them with my mind fixed on the Lord.

children.text: dvijopasṛṣṭaḥ kuhakastakṣako vā daśatvalaṃ gāyata viṣṇugāthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether <s>Takṣaka</s>, sent by the Brahmin, or some deceiver should bite me, you should sing the songs of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
And may there again and again be love for the infinite Blessed Lord and attachment to those who depend on him,

children.text: mahatsu yāṃ yām upayāmi sṛṣṭiṃ maitryastu sarvatra namo dvijebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to the great ones, in whatever creation I may enter; may there be friendship everywhere. Reverence to the Brahmins."

children.text: iti sma rājādhyavasāyayuktaḥ prācīnamūleṣu kuśeṣu dhīraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the resolute king, steadfast, sat on kuśa grass whose tips faced east,
facing north on the southern bank of the ocean's wife, having placed the burden of his son upon himself.

children.text: evaṃ ca tasmin naradevadeve prāyopaviṣṭe divi devasaṅghāḥ
children.translated_text: And when that god among kings had thus sat down there in the vow of fasting unto death, the hosts of gods in heaven

children.text: praśasya bhūmau vyakiran prasūnair mudā muhurdundubhayaśca neduḥ ||
children.translated_text: praised him and scattered flowers upon the earth, while kettledrums sounded again and again in joy.

children.text: maharṣayo vai samupāgatā ye praśasya sādhvityanumodamānāḥ
children.translated_text: The great seers who had come there praised him and, approving with "well done,"
spoke words whose essence was kindness to creatures and which were fitting to the virtues of <s>Uttamaśloka</s>.

children.text: na vā idaṃ rājarṣivarya citraṃ bhavatsu kṛṣṇaṃ samanuvrateṣu
children.translated_text: This is not at all astonishing, best of royal seers, in those like you who are wholly devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
who at once abandoned a throne honored by royal crowns, desiring the side of the Blessed Lord.

children.text: sarve vayaṃ tāvadihāsmahe 'tha kalevaraṃ yāvadasau vihāya
children.translated_text: All of us shall remain here until this foremost <s>Bhāgavata</s>, having cast off his body,

children.text: lokaṃ paraṃ virajaskaṃ viśokaṃ yāsyatyayaṃ bhāgavatapradhānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: goes to the supreme world, stainless and free from sorrow.

children.text: āśrutya tadṛṣigaṇavacaḥ parīkṣit samaṃ madhucyudguru cāvyalīkam
children.translated_text: Having heard those words of the assembly of seers, which were even, honey-sweet, weighty, and free from falsehood, <s>Parīkṣit</s>
addressed them after welcoming the worthy ones, eager to hear the deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: samāgatāḥ sarvata eva sarve vedā yathā mūrtidharāstripṛṣṭhe
children.translated_text: You have all assembled here from every side, like the Vedas embodied on the heavenly height;

children.text: nehātha nāmutra ca kaścanārtha ṛte parānugraham ātmaśīlam ||
children.translated_text: neither here nor hereafter is there any purpose for you except helping others, which is your very nature.

children.text: tataśca vaḥ pṛcchyam imaṃ vipṛcche viśrabhya viprā iti kṛtyatāyām
children.translated_text: Therefore, trusting you, O Brahmins, I ask this question of you about what should be done:

children.text: sarvātmanā mriyamāṇaiśca kṛtyaṃ śuddhaṃ ca tatrāmṛśatābhiyuktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with full attention, consider the pure duty in that matter for those who are dying in every way.
Then the Blessed Lord, the son of <s>Vyāsa</s>, appeared there, wandering over the earth by chance, indifferent to all,
with his marks unrecognized, content in his own attainment, surrounded by children and dressed as an <s>avadhūta</s>.
They saw him as a tender youth of sixteen years, with delicate feet, hands, thighs, arms, shoulders, cheeks, and limbs,
with beautiful wide eyes, a high nose, even ears, fine brows, a lovely face, and a well-formed conch-like neck.
His collarbones were hidden, his chest broad and high, his navel whorled, and his abdomen handsome with folds;
he was naked, his hair scattered over his face, his arms long, and he shone like the best of the immortals.
He was dark, ever in the first bloom of youth, beautiful in every limb, pleasing to women with his lovely smile;

children.text: pratyutthitāste munayaḥ svāsanebhyas tallakṣaṇajñā api gūḍhavarcasam ||
children.translated_text: the sages rose from their seats, recognizing those signs, though his splendor was concealed.

children.text: sa viṣṇurāto 'tithaya āgatāya tasmai saparyāṃ śirasājahāra
children.translated_text: For that guest who had arrived, <s>Viṣṇurāta</s> offered worship with his head bowed,

children.text: tato nivṛttā hyabudhāḥ striyo 'rbhakā mahāsane sopaviveśa pūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then the ignorant women and children withdrew; worshiped, he sat down on the great seat.
There, surrounded by gatherings of brahmarṣis, royal seers, and divine seers, the great one among the great,
the Blessed Lord shone brilliantly like the moon encircled by hosts of planets, constellations, and stars.

children.text: praśāntam āsīnam akuṇṭhamedhasaṃ muniṃ nṛpo bhāgavato 'bhyupetya
children.translated_text: The king, a <s>Bhāgavata</s>, approached the tranquil seated sage of unobstructed intelligence;

children.text: praṇamya mūrdhnāvahitaḥ kṛtāñjalir natvā girā sūnṛtayānvapṛcchat ||
children.translated_text: bowing with his head, attentive and with joined hands, he bent down and asked him with truthful, gentle speech.
<s>Parīkṣit</s> said:

children.text: aho adya vayaṃ brahman satsevyāḥ kṣatrabandhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, today, O Brahmin, we kṣatra-bandhus have become worthy to serve the good;
through compassion, in the form of guests, you have made us into places of pilgrimage.

children.text: yeṣāṃ saṃsmaraṇāt puṃsāṃ sadyaḥ śudhyanti vai gṛhāḥ
children.translated_text: By remembering people such as you, men's houses are indeed purified at once;
how much more, then, by seeing, touching, washing your feet, offering a seat, and the like?
Through your presence, great yogin, even very great sins

children.text: sadyo naśyanti vai puṃsāṃ viṣṇoriva suretarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: at once perish for men, just as beings opposed to the gods perish before <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: api me bhagavān prītaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pāṇḍusutapriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Perhaps the Blessed Lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, dear to the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, is pleased with me,
and, out of love for the sons of his paternal aunt, has taken their lineage as his own kin.
Otherwise, how could the sight of you, whose path is hidden, come to us men,
especially to us who are dying, while you are fully perfected and most worthy to be sought?

children.text: ataḥ pṛcchāmi saṃsiddhiṃ yogināṃ paramaṃ gurum
children.translated_text: Therefore I ask you, the supreme guru of perfected yogins, about complete success:
what, in every way, is to be done here by a man who is dying?

children.text: yacchrotavyam atho japyaṃ yat kartavyaṃ nṛbhiḥ prabho
children.translated_text: Tell me, O lord, what is to be heard, what is to be recited, what is to be done by human beings,

children.text: smartavyaṃ bhajanīyaṃ vā brūhi yadvā viparyayam ||
children.translated_text: what is to be remembered or worshiped, and also whatever is the opposite.
Surely, O Brahmin, the presence of blessed ones in the houses of householders

children.text: na lakṣyate hyavasthānam api godohanaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: is not observed anywhere even for the time it takes to milk a cow.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evam ābhāṣitaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ sa rājñā ślakṣṇayā girā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed and questioned by the king with smooth speech,
the Blessed <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s>, replied.
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: varīyān eṣa te praśnaḥ kṛto lokahitaṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: This question you have asked, O king, is most excellent and serves the welfare of the world;
approved by knowers of the self, it is supreme among the matters to be heard and the rest.
There are thousands of things to be heard and so on, O king of kings, for men
who do not see the reality of the self and live as householders in their houses.

children.text: nidrayā hriyate naktaṃ vyavāyena ca vā vayaḥ
children.translated_text: At night their life is carried away by sleep and by sexual union,
and by day, O king, by the pursuit of wealth or by supporting the family.
Madly attached to body, children, wife, and the rest, though they are unreliable armies of the self,

children.text: teṣāṃ pramatto nidhanaṃ paśyann api na paśyati ||
children.translated_text: such people see their destruction and yet do not see it.
Therefore, O <s>Bhārata</s>, the Blessed Lord, the Self of all, the Lord <s>Hari</s>,
is to be heard of, praised, and remembered by one who desires fearlessness.
This much is the supreme gain of birth for human beings through <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, yoga,
and steadfastness in one's own <s>dharma</s>: remembrance of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> at the end.
For the most part, O king, sages who have withdrawn from injunction and prohibition,
and who stand in the state beyond the guṇas, delight in narrations of <s>Hari</s>'s qualities.
This <s>purāṇa</s> called the <s>Bhāgavata</s>, equal to Brahman,
I studied at the beginning of the <s>Dvāpara</s> age from my father <s>Dvaipāyana</s>.
Though firmly established in the state beyond the guṇas, by the play of <s>Uttamaśloka</s>
my mind was seized, O royal seer, and I studied this narrative.
Therefore I shall tell it to you, for you are greatly devoted to the Supreme Person.

children.text: yasya śraddadhatām āśu syān mukunde matiḥ satī ||
children.translated_text: For those who listen with faith, a true disposition toward <s>Mukunda</s> would quickly arise.
For those who are becoming dispassionate, and for those who desire fearlessness,
for yogins, O king, chanting the names of <s>Hari</s> has been determined as the sure means.
What use here are many unseen years for a careless man?

children.text: varaṃ muhūrtaṃ viditaṃ ghaṭate śreyase yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Better is a single known moment, since it can accomplish the highest good.
<s>Khaṭvāṅga</s>, a royal seer by name, having learned the measure of his life here,

children.text: muhūrtāt sarvam utsṛjya gatavān abhayaṃ harim ||
children.translated_text: within a moment gave up everything and went to <s>Hari</s>, the fearless one.
For you too now, O descendant of the <s>Kauravas</s>, the limit of life is seven days;
therefore prepare all that belongs to the hereafter within that time.
But when the final time has arrived, a person, free from fear,

children.text: chindyādasaṅgaśastreṇa spṛhāṃ dehe 'nu ye ca tam ||
children.translated_text: should cut off desire for the body and for those connected with it by the sword of non-attachment.
Having left home, steadfast, bathed in the water of a holy ford,
seated in a pure and solitary place, on a seat arranged according to rule,
he should practice mentally the pure, supreme threefold syllable of Brahman;
with breath mastered, he should restrain the mind, not forgetting the seed of Brahman.
With the mind, while intelligence is the charioteer, he should restrain the senses from their objects;
and with understanding he should hold the mind, distracted by activities, upon the auspicious goal.
There he should meditate on one limb with unbroken attention;

children.text: mano nirviṣayaṃ yuktvā tataḥ kiṃcana na smaret
children.translated_text: having joined the mind to what is free of sense objects, after that he should remember nothing else.

children.text: padaṃ tat paramaṃ viṣṇormano yatra prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: That is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, where the mind becomes serene.
When one's bewildered mind is seized by rajas and tamas,

children.text: yaccheddhāraṇayā dhīro hanti yā tatkṛtaṃ malam ||
children.translated_text: the steadfast man should restrain it by concentration, which destroys the impurity produced by them.
When that concentration is being maintained, for the yogin

children.text: āśu sampadyate yoga āśrayaṃ bhadram īkṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: yoga characterized by devotion quickly comes to perfection as he beholds the blessed support.
The king said:

children.text: yathā saṃdhāryate brahman dhāraṇā yatra saṃmatā
children.translated_text: O brahman, how is concentration to be maintained, and where is it approved?
And what is it like, so that it quickly removes the impurity of a person's mind?
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
With posture mastered, breath mastered, attachment mastered, and senses mastered,
one should fix the mind with understanding on the gross form of the Blessed Lord.
This body of his is the particular form, the grossest among the gross,

children.text: yatredaṃ vyajyate viśvaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhavacca sat ||
children.translated_text: in which this whole universe, past, future, and present, becomes manifest as real.
In this body, the cosmic egg joined with seven coverings,
that <s>Virāj</s> person, that Blessed Lord, is the support for concentration.

children.text: pātālam etasya hi pādamūlaṃ paṭhanti pārṣṇiprapade rasātalam
children.translated_text: They recite that <s>Pātāla</s> is the soles of his feet, and <s>Rasātala</s> his heels and toes;

children.text: mahātalaṃ viśvasṛjo 'tha gulphau talātalaṃ vai puruṣasya jaṅghe ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Mahātala</s> is the ankles of the creator of the universe, and <s>Talātala</s> the shanks of the Person.

children.text: dve jānunī sutalaṃ viśvamūrter ūrudvayaṃ vitalaṃ cātalaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Sutala</s> is the two knees of the cosmic form; <s>Vitala</s> and <s>Atala</s> are the two thighs;

children.text: mahītalaṃ tajjaghanaṃ mahīpate nabhastalaṃ nābhisaro gṛṇanti ||
children.translated_text: the earthly realm is his loins, O lord of the earth, and they declare the sky-realm to be the hollow of his navel.

children.text: uraḥsthalaṃ jyotiranīkam asya grīvā maharvadanaṃ vai jano 'sya
children.translated_text: The sphere of lights is his chest; <s>Mahar</s> is his neck; <s>Jana</s> is his face;

children.text: tapo varāṭīṃ vidurādipuṃsaḥ satyaṃ tu śīrṣāṇi sahasraśīrṣṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they know <s>Tapas</s> as the forehead of the primal Person, and <s>Satya</s> as the heads of the thousand-headed one.

children.text: indrādayo bāhava āhurusrāḥ karṇau diśaḥ śrotram amuṣya śabdaḥ
children.translated_text: They say <s>Indra</s> and the others are his arms; the directions are his ears, and sound is his hearing;

children.text: nāsatyadasrau paramasya nāse ghrāṇo 'sya gandho mukham agniriddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Nāsatyas</s> are the nostrils of the Supreme, smell is his sense of smell, and blazing fire is his mouth.

children.text: dyaurakṣiṇī cakṣurabhūt pataṅgaḥ pakṣmāṇi viṣṇorahanī ubhe ca
children.translated_text: Heaven is his eyes; the sun became his sight; the two eyelids of <s>Viṣṇu</s> are both day and night;

children.text: tadbhrūvijṛmbhaḥ parameṣṭhidhiṣṇyam āpo 'sya tālū rasa eva jihvā ||
children.translated_text: the play of his brows is the abode of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>; the waters are his palate, and taste itself is his tongue.

children.text: chandāṃsyanantasya śiro gṛṇanti daṃṣṭrā yamaḥ snehakalā dvijāni
children.translated_text: They declare the Vedas to be the head of the infinite one; <s>Yama</s> is his fangs, and affection his teeth;

children.text: hāso janonmādakarī ca māyā durantasargo yadapāṅgamokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his smile is <s>Māyā</s>, which maddens people, and the endless creation is the release of his sidelong glance.

children.text: vrīḍottarauṣṭho 'dhara eva lobho dharmaḥ stano 'dharmapatho 'sya pṛṣṭham
children.translated_text: Modesty is his upper lip and greed his lower lip; <s>dharma</s> is his breast and the path of <s>adharma</s> his back;

children.text: kastasya meḍhraṃ vṛṣaṇau ca mitrau kukṣiḥ samudrā girayo 'sthisaṅghāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ka</s> is his generative organ and <s>Mitra</s> his two testicles; the oceans are his belly, and the mountains his masses of bones.
His channels are the rivers, and his body hairs are the trees, O king,

children.text: anantavīryaḥ śvasitaṃ mātariśvā gatirvayaḥ karma guṇapravāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mātariśvan</s>, infinite in power, is his breath; time is his movement, and karma is the stream of the guṇas.

children.text: īśasya keśān vidurambuvāhān vāsastu sandhyāṃ kuruvarya bhūmnaḥ
children.translated_text: The clouds they know as the hair of the Lord, and twilight as the garment of the vast one, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>;
they call the unmanifest his heart, and the moon his mind, the storehouse of all transformations.
They declare the great principle to be his power of knowledge, and <s>Giritra</s> the inner organ of the Self of all.

children.text: aśvāśvataryuṣṭragajā nakhāni sarve mṛgāḥ paśavaḥ śroṇideśe ||
children.translated_text: Horses, mules, camels, and elephants are his nails, and all wild animals and domesticated beasts are at his hip-region.

children.text: vayāṃsi tadvyākaraṇaṃ vicitraṃ manurmanīṣā manujo nivāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Birds are his varied verbal expression; <s>Manu</s> is his thought, and humanity his dwelling;
the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, and <s>Apsarases</s> are his musical memory; the ranks of <s>Asuras</s> are his heroic force.
The brāhmaṇa is his mouth, the kṣatra his arms; the vaiśya is the great one's thigh, and the dark class dwelling at his feet is the śūdra.
Furnished with groups of many names and objects of worship, he is made of sacrificial substance and joined to the expanse of rites.

children.text: iyān asāvīśvaravigrahasya yaḥ saṃniveśaḥ kathito mayā te
children.translated_text: This much is the arrangement of the Lord's body

children.text: saṃdhāryate 'smin vapuṣi sthaviṣṭhe manaḥ svabuddhyā na yato 'sti kiṃcit ||
children.translated_text: that has been told by me to you; in this gross body the mind should be held by one's own understanding, for there is nothing apart from it.
He, the Self, by whom all is experienced through all the functions of intelligence, is one, like the single dreamer seen among dream-people;

children.text: taṃ satyam ānandanidhiṃ bhajeta nānyatra sajedyata ātmapātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should worship him, the real one, the treasure of bliss, and should not become attached elsewhere, since from that comes the fall of the self.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ purā dhāraṇayātmayonir naṣṭāṃ smṛtiṃ pratyavarudhya tuṣṭāt
children.translated_text: Thus in ancient times the self-born one, by concentration, recovered his lost memory from the pleased Lord,

children.text: tathā sasarjedam amoghadṛṣṭir yathāpyayāt prāg vyavasāyabuddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, with unfailing vision and resolute intelligence, created this world as before after dissolution.

children.text: śābdasya hi brahmaṇa eṣa panthā yan nāmabhirdhyāyati dhīrapārthaiḥ
children.translated_text: For this is the path of the Brahman constituted by words: the steadfast, purposeful one meditates by means of its names.

children.text: paribhramaṃstatra na vindate 'rthān māyāmaye vāsanayā śayānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wandering there, he does not find the true ends, lying asleep through habit in what is made of <s>māyā</s> (illusion).
Therefore the wise man, attentive and firm in practical understanding, should take from names and things only as much as has real use.

children.text: siddhe 'nyathārthe na yateta tatra pariśramaṃ tatra samīkṣamāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the goal can be accomplished otherwise, he should not strive for that, seeing the toil involved there.

children.text: satyāṃ kṣitau kiṃ kaśipoḥ prayāsair bāhau svasiddhe hyupabarhaṇaiḥ kim
children.translated_text: When the earth itself exists, why make efforts for a bed? When one's own arm is already available, what need is there of cushions?

children.text: satyañjalau kiṃ purudhānnapātryā digvalkalādau sati kiṃ dukūlaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the joined palms are available, what need is there of many food vessels? When the quarters, bark, and the like exist, what need is there of fine garments?

children.text: cīrāṇi kiṃ pathi na santi diśanti bhikṣāṃ naivāṅghripāḥ parabhṛtaḥ sarito 'pyaśuṣyan
children.translated_text: Are there no rags on the road? Do the trees that sustain others not give alms? Have the rivers dried up?

children.text: ruddhā guhāḥ kim ajito 'vati nopasannān kasmādbhajanti kavayo dhanadurmadāndhān ||
children.translated_text: Are the caves closed? Does <s>Ajita</s> not protect those who approach him? Why then do the wise serve men blinded by the arrogance of wealth?

children.text: evaṃ svacitte svata eva siddha ātmā priyo 'rtho bhagavān anantaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, within one's own mind, the Self, the beloved goal, the Blessed Lord <s>Ananta</s>, is established of himself.

children.text: taṃ nirvṛto niyatārtho bhajeta saṃsārahetūparamaśca yatra ||
children.translated_text: Content and fixed in purpose, one should worship him, in whom the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly wandering) comes to rest.

children.text: kastāṃ tvanādṛtya parānucintām ṛte paśūn asatīṃ nāma kuryāt
children.translated_text: Who, apart from beasts, would disregard that and engage in the unworthy so-called concern for others,

children.text: paśyañ janaṃ patitaṃ vaitaraṇyāṃ svakarmajān paritāpāñ juṣāṇam ||
children.translated_text: while seeing people fallen into the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, undergoing torments born from their own actions?
Some, by concentration, remember the <s>Puruṣa</s> dwelling in the inner space of their own body's heart, the size of a thumb-span,
four-armed, holding lotus, discus, conch, and mace.
They remember him with a gracious face, eyes long like lotuses, and garments yellowish like the filaments of the kadamba flower,
with great jeweled golden armlets shining, and with a great jeweled crown and earrings flashing.
His tender feet have been placed by the lords of yoga in the pericarp of the opened lotus of the heart.
He bears the mark of <s>Śrī</s>, the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel at his neck, and is adorned with a forest garland of unfading beauty.
He is ornamented with a girdle, rings, costly anklets, bracelets, and the like,
and his face shines charmingly with a smile, framed by glossy, spotless, curling dark locks.
With playful, gentle smiles and glances, and with the movement of his brows, he indicates abundant grace.

children.text: īkṣeta cintāmayam enam īśvaraṃ yāvan mano dhāraṇayāvatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: One should behold this Lord, formed in contemplation, as long as the mind remains steady in concentration.
One by one, with the intellect, he should contemplate the limbs of the mace-bearer, from the feet up to the smile.

children.text: jitaṃ jitaṃ sthānam apohya dhārayet paraṃ paraṃ śudhyati dhīryathā yathā ||
children.translated_text: Having mastered each place, he should withdraw from it and fix on the next higher one; in this way, step by step, the intellect becomes purified.

children.text: yāvan na jāyeta parāvare 'smin viśveśvare draṣṭari bhaktiyogaḥ
children.translated_text: So long as <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (devotional discipline) toward this Lord of the universe, the seer of higher and lower, has not arisen,

children.text: tāvat sthavīyaḥ puruṣasya rūpaṃ kriyāvasāne prayataḥ smareta ||
children.translated_text: until then, at the end of his rites, he should carefully remember the gross form of the <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: sthiraṃ sukhaṃ cāsanam āsthito yatir yadā jihāsurimam aṅga lokam
children.translated_text: When the ascetic, seated in a firm and comfortable posture, wishes to leave this world, O dear one,

children.text: kāle ca deśe ca mano na sajjayet prāṇān niyacchen manasā jitāsuḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should not attach his mind to time or place; with the mind he should restrain the life-breaths, having conquered the vital force.

children.text: manaḥ svabuddhyāmalayā niyamya kṣetrajña etāṃ ninayet tam ātmani
children.translated_text: Controlling the mind with his own purified intellect, as the knower of the field, he should lead that intellect into the Self.
Restraining the self within the Self, the steadfast man, having attained complete tranquility, should cease from action.

children.text: na yatra kālo 'nimiṣāṃ paraḥ prabhuḥ kuto nu devā jagatāṃ ya īśire
children.translated_text: There time, the supreme lord over the sleepless gods, has no sway; how then could the gods who rule the worlds have sway there?

children.text: na yatra sattvaṃ na rajastamaśca na vai vikāro na mahān pradhānam ||
children.translated_text: There is no <s>sattva</s>, no <s>rajas</s> or <s>tamas</s>, no transformation, no <s>mahat</s>, and no <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter).

children.text: paraṃ padaṃ vaiṣṇavam āmananti tad yan neti netītyatadutsisṛkṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: They call that the supreme <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> state, which those wishing to cast off what is not that approach by saying, 'not this, not this.'

children.text: visṛjya daurātmyam ananyasauhṛdā hṛdopaguhyārhapadaṃ pade pade ||
children.translated_text: Abandoning evil selfhood, with undivided friendship, they clasp in the heart, at every step, the feet worthy of worship.
Thus the sage, established in cessation, his inner nature firmly strengthened by the power of the vision of knowledge,

children.text: svapārṣṇināpīḍya gudaṃ tato 'nilaṃ sthāneṣu ṣaṭsūnnamayej jitaklamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should press the anus with his heel and then, free from fatigue, raise the breath upward through the six stations.

children.text: nābhyāṃ sthitaṃ hṛdyadhiropya tasmād udānagatyorasi taṃ nayen muniḥ
children.translated_text: Having lifted the breath stationed at the navel into the heart, the sage should then carry it, by the path of the upward breath, into the chest.
Then, joining it with the intellect, the mindful man should slowly lead it to the root of his own palate.
From there he should raise it to the space between the brows; with the seven openings restrained, without expectation,

children.text: sthitvā muhūrtārdham akuṇṭhadṛṣṭir nirbhidya mūrdhan visṛjet paraṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: remaining for half a muhūrta with unimpeded vision, he should pierce the crown of the head and release it, having gone to the supreme.

children.text: yadi prayāsyan nṛpa pārameṣṭhyaṃ vaihāyasānām uta yadvihāram
children.translated_text: If, O king, he intends to go to the realm of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, or to the aerial wandering-place,
or to lordship over the eight powers within the aggregate of the qualities, he may go there together with the mind and senses.
They say that this is the path of the lords of yoga, of those whose inner self is the wind, both within and beyond the three worlds.
People do not attain that path by works; it belongs to those who possess knowledge, austerity, yoga, and samādhi.

children.text: vaiśvānaraṃ yāti vihāyasā gataḥ suṣumṇayā brahmapathena śociṣā
children.translated_text: Traveling through the sky by the <s>suṣumṇā</s>, along the path of Brahman, by the flame, he goes to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: vidhūtakalko 'tha harerudastāt prayāti cakraṃ nṛpa śaiśumāram ||
children.translated_text: Then, with impurity shaken off, from above <s>Hari</s>'s realm, O king, he proceeds to the wheel called <s>Śaiśumāra</s>.
Passing beyond that world-navel of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, alone with a subtler, stainless self,

children.text: namaskṛtaṃ brahmavidām upaiti kalpāyuṣo yadvibudhā ramante ||
children.translated_text: he reaches the realm honored by knowers of Brahman, where the gods whose lives last a kalpa delight.

children.text: atho anantasya mukhānalena dandahyamānaṃ sa nirīkṣya viśvam
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the universe being burned by the fire from the mouth of <s>Ananta</s>,

children.text: niryāti siddheśvarajuṣṭadhiṣṇyaṃ yad dvaiparārdhyaṃ tad u pārameṣṭhyam ||
children.translated_text: he goes out to the station enjoyed by the lords of the perfected beings, that highest realm of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, lasting two parārdhas.

children.text: na yatra śoko na jarā na mṛtyur nārtirna codvega ṛte kutaścit
children.translated_text: There there is no grief, no old age, no death, no pain, and no agitation from any source,
except that which arises in the mind from compassion for those who do not know this, when one sees the source of their unbearable suffering.
Then, having attained a further distinction, fearless, he swiftly, by that self, passes through water, being fire-formed,

children.text: jyotirmayo vāyum upetya kāle vāyvātmanā khaṃ bṛhadātmaliṅgam ||
children.translated_text: and, luminous, reaches air at the proper time; with the self as air he reaches space, the sign of the great Self.

children.text: ghrāṇena gandhaṃ rasanena vai rasaṃ rūpaṃ ca dṛṣṭyā śvasanaṃ tvacaiva
children.translated_text: With the nose he takes in smell, with the tongue taste, with sight form, and with the skin the breath--

children.text: śrotreṇa copetya nabhoguṇatvaṃ prāṇena cākūtim upaiti yogī ||
children.translated_text: And with the ear the yogin approaches the quality of space; with the vital breath he attains intention.
Having reached the mutable principle made of mind and made of gods, in contact with the subtle elements and the senses,

children.text: saṃsādya gatyā saha tena yāti vijñānatattvaṃ guṇasannirodham ||
children.translated_text: together with that path he goes to the principle of knowledge, where the guṇas are fully restrained.
Through that self, being made of bliss, he attains at the end the peaceful Self, bliss itself.

children.text: etāṃ gatiṃ bhāgavatīṃ gato yaḥ sa vai punarneha viṣajjate 'ṅga ||
children.translated_text: Whoever has gone to this Bhāgavata path, dear one, certainly does not become entangled here again.

children.text: ete sṛtī te nṛpa vedagīte tvayābhipṛṣṭe ca sanātane ca
children.translated_text: These two courses, O king, sung by the Veda, about which you asked, are eternal;

children.text: ye vai purā brahmaṇa āha tuṣṭa ārādhito bhagavān vāsudevaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in former times the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, pleased by worship, told them to <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: na hyato 'nyaḥ śivaḥ panthā viśataḥ saṃsṛtāviha
children.translated_text: For one entering saṃsṛti here, there is no other auspicious path than this,
by which bhakti-yoga toward the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> may arise.
The blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, having examined everything fully three times with discernment,
steadfast, determined that by which delight in the Self would arise.
The Blessed <s>Hari</s> is perceived in all beings by one's own self;
he is the seer, inferred through visible indications such as intellect and the rest.

children.text: tasmāt sarvātmanā rājan hariḥ sarvatra sarvadā
children.translated_text: Therefore, with the whole self, O king, <s>Hari</s>, everywhere and always,
is to be heard, praised, and remembered by human beings as the Blessed Lord.

children.text: pibanti ye bhagavata ātmanaḥ satāṃ kathāmṛtaṃ śravaṇapuṭeṣu saṃbhṛtam
children.translated_text: Those who drink the nectar of the stories of the Blessed Lord, the Self of the good, gathered into the cups of their ears,
purify the mind polluted by sense-objects and go near his lotus feet.
<s>Śrīśuka</s> said:

children.text: evam etan nigaditaṃ pṛṣṭavān yadbhavān mama
children.translated_text: Thus I have told you this, what your honor asked me:
what is fitting for dying men, among thoughtful human beings.
One desiring brahmanic splendor should worship the lord of sacred speech;
one desiring power of the senses should worship <s>Indra</s>; one desiring offspring should worship the <s>Prajāpatis</s>.
One desiring prosperity should worship the goddess <s>Māyā</s>; one desiring brilliance should worship <s>Vibhāvasu</s>.
One desiring wealth should worship the <s>Vasus</s>; one desiring strength should worship the mighty <s>Rudras</s>.
One desiring food and sustenance should worship <s>Aditi</s>; one desiring heaven should worship the sons of <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: viśvān devān rājyakāmaḥ sādhyān saṃsādhako viśām ||
children.translated_text: One desiring rule should worship the <s>Viśvadevas</s>; one wishing to bring the people under control should worship the <s>Sādhyas</s>.
One desiring long life should worship the divine <s>Aśvins</s>; one desiring nourishment should worship <s>Ilā</s>.
A man desiring firm establishment should worship heaven and earth, the mothers of the world.
One desiring beauty should worship the <s>Gandharvas</s>; one desiring a woman should worship the apsaras <s>Urvaśī</s>.
One desiring lordship over all should worship <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
One desiring fame should worship <s>Yajña</s>; one desiring treasure should worship <s>Pracetasa</s>.
One desiring knowledge should worship <s>Giriśa</s>; for marriage one should worship <s>Umā</s>, <s>Satī</s>.

children.text: dharmārtha uttamaślokaṃ tantuḥ tanvan pitṝn yajet
children.translated_text: For <s>dharma</s> one should worship <s>Uttamaśloka</s>; one extending the thread of lineage should worship the ancestors.
One desiring protection should worship the <s>Puṇyajanas</s>; one desiring vital force should worship the hosts of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: rājyakāmo manūn devān nirṛtiṃ tvabhicaran yajet
children.translated_text: One desiring kingship should worship the divine <s>Manus</s>; one practicing hostile rites should worship <s>Nirṛti</s>.

children.text: kāmakāmo yajet somam akāmaḥ puruṣaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: One desiring desire should worship <s>Soma</s>; one without desire should worship the Supreme Puruṣa.
Whether without desire, or having every desire, or desiring mokṣa, a broad-minded person
should worship the Supreme Puruṣa with intense bhakti-yoga.
This alone is the rise of the highest good here for those who worship:
an unwavering disposition toward the Blessed Lord, born from association with Bhāgavatas.

children.text: jñānaṃ yad āpratinivṛttaguṇormicakram ātmaprasāda uta yatra guṇeṣvasaṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowledge there is where the wheel of the waves of the guṇas does not turn back, where there is clarity of self and non-attachment among the guṇas;

children.text: kaivalyasaṃmatapathastvatha bhaktiyogaḥ ko nirvṛto harikathāsu ratiṃ na kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: and then there is bhakti-yoga, the path approved for kaivalya. Who, being fulfilled, would not develop love for the stories of <s>Hari</s>?
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
Having heard what was thus spoken, what else did the king, the bull of the <s>Bharatas</s>,

children.text: kim anyat pṛṣṭavān bhūyo vaiyāsakim ṛṣiṃ kavim ||
children.translated_text: again ask the sage son of <s>Vyāsa</s>, the inspired seer?
O learned <s>Sūta</s>, you ought to tell this to us who desire to hear it,

children.text: kathā harikathodarkāḥ satāṃ syuḥ sadasi dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: for in the assembly of the good, stories surely have stories of <s>Hari</s> as their outcome.

children.text: sa vai bhāgavato rājā pāṇḍaveyo mahārathaḥ
children.translated_text: That king, the descendant of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, the great chariot-warrior, was indeed a Bhāgavata;
even while playing with children's toys, he took up play centered on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
And the blessed <s>Vaiyāsaki</s> was wholly devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>;
in a meeting of the good, there are indeed generous accounts of the qualities of <s>Urugāya</s>.

children.text: āyurharati vai puṃsām udyann astaṃ ca yann asau
children.translated_text: As it rises and sets, the sun indeed takes away the life-span of men,
except for the moment spent in discourse about <s>Uttamaśloka</s>.

children.text: taravaḥ kiṃ na jīvanti bhastrāḥ kiṃ na śvasantyuta
children.translated_text: Do trees not live? Do bellows not breathe?

children.text: na khādanti na mehanti kiṃ grāme paśavo 'pare ||
children.translated_text: Do the other animals in the village not eat and discharge?
A man praised by dogs, stool-eating pigs, camels, and asses is an animal
if the name of <s>Gadāgraja</s> has never entered the path of his ear.

children.text: bile batorukramavikramān ye na śṛṇvataḥ karṇapuṭe narasya
children.translated_text: Alas, the ear-holes of a man who does not hear the mighty strides of <s>Urukrama</s> are mere holes;
O <s>Sūta</s>, his tongue is like a frog's if it does not sing the songs of <s>Urugāya</s>.

children.text: bhāraḥ paraṃ paṭṭakirīṭajuṣṭam apyuttamāṅgaṃ na namen mukundam
children.translated_text: Even the head adorned with a turban and crown is merely a burden if it does not bow to <s>Mukunda</s>;

children.text: śāvau karau no kurute saparyāṃ harerlasatkāñcanakaṅkaṇau vā ||
children.translated_text: and the hands, though adorned with shining gold bracelets, are corpses if they do not perform service to <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: barhāyite te nayane narāṇāṃ liṅgāni viṣṇorna nirīkṣato ye
children.translated_text: Those eyes of men that do not behold the emblems of <s>Viṣṇu</s> are like painted eyes on peacock feathers;

children.text: pādau nṛṇāṃ tau drumajanmabhājau kṣetrāṇi nānuvrajato hareryau ||
children.translated_text: those feet of men that do not follow <s>Hari</s>'s sacred places are like things born as trees.

children.text: jīvañchavo bhāgavatāṅghrireṇuṃ na jātu martyo 'bhilabheta yastu
children.translated_text: A mortal who never obtains the dust of the feet of a Bhāgavata is a living corpse;

children.text: śrīviṣṇupadyā manujastulasyāḥ śvasañchavo yastu na veda gandham ||
children.translated_text: and a breathing corpse is the man who does not know the fragrance of the tulasī from blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s feet.
Alas, this heart is stone-hard if, when the names of <s>Hari</s> are being taken,

children.text: na vikriyetātha yadā vikāro netre jalaṃ gātraruheṣu harṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is not transformed; and when transformation occurs, there are tears in the eyes and horripilation on the limbs.
Now tell us, dear one, what is agreeable to the mind; you speak as the foremost of Bhāgavatas:
what <s>Vaiyāsaki</s>, skilled in knowledge of the self, said to the king when well questioned.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having taken to heart, as the settled truth of his own self, these words of the son of <s>Vyāsa</s>,

children.text: upadhārya matiṃ kṛṣṇe auttareyaḥ satīṃ vyadhāt ||
children.translated_text: the descendant of <s>Uttarā</s> fixed his pure mind on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Toward his own body, wife, sons, house, animals, wealth, and relatives,

children.text: rājye cāvikale nityaṃ virūḍhāṃ mamatāṃ jahau ||
children.translated_text: and toward his unimpaired kingdom, he abandoned the possessiveness that had always grown deep-rooted.

children.text: papraccha cemam evārthaṃ yan māṃ pṛcchatha sattamāḥ
children.translated_text: And, faithful and noble-minded in hearing of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s greatness, he asked this very matter
which you, best of the good, are asking me.

children.text: saṃsthāṃ vijñāya saṃnyasya karma traivargikaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Knowing his end, and renouncing action aimed at the three worldly aims,
he had attained firm self-identification with the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
The king said:
"Your speech is proper, O Brahmin, sinless one, for you are omniscient;

children.text: tamo viśīryate mahyaṃ hareḥ kathayataḥ kathām ||
children.translated_text: as you tell the tale of <s>Hari</s>, my darkness is scattered.
Again I wish to know how the Blessed Lord, through his own <s>māyā</s> (creative power),
creates this universe, which is hard even for the ruling gods to comprehend;
how the mighty Lord protects it, and how again he draws it in;

children.text: yāṃ yāṃ śaktim upāśritya puruśaktiḥ paraḥ pumān
children.translated_text: and relying on which particular power, the supreme Person of many powers,

children.text: ātmānaṃ krīḍayan krīḍan karoti vikaroti ca ||
children.translated_text: playing and making himself play, acts upon himself and transforms himself.
Surely, O Brahmin, the activity of the Blessed <s>Hari</s>, whose works are wondrous,
appears hard to comprehend, even when considered by poets and seers.
How, though one, does he bear the many <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of <s>prakṛti</s> (nature), whether all at once or in succession,
performing actions abundantly through his births?

children.text: vicikitsitam etan me bravītu bhagavān yathā
children.translated_text: Let the Blessed one tell me this matter that is in doubt, exactly as it is,

children.text: śābde brahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ parasmiṃśca bhavān khalu ||
children.translated_text: for you indeed are deeply versed in the verbal <s>brahman</s> and in the supreme as well."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus invited by the king to recount the qualities of <s>Hari</s>,
he remembered <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> and began to answer.
Śrī <s>Śuka</s> said:
Reverence to the supreme and greater Person, who by the play of creation, maintenance, and dissolution of beings
assumes the triad of powers, who dwells within embodied beings, and whose course is imperceptible.
Again reverence to him who cuts away the sins of the good, who is impossible for the wicked, and who is the form of all being,

children.text: puṃsāṃ punaḥ pāramahaṃsya āśrame vyavasthitānām anumṛgyadāśuṣe ||
children.translated_text: who grants what is sought by men established in the supreme ascetic state of the <s>pāramahaṃsya</s> (highest renunciant life).

children.text: namo namaste 'stvṛṣabhāya sātvatāṃ vidūrakāṣṭhāya muhuḥ kuyoginām
children.translated_text: Reverence, reverence to you, the foremost of the <s>Sātvatas</s>, who are at the farthest limit for bad yogins,

children.text: nirastasāmyātiśayena rādhasā svadhāmani brahmaṇi raṃsyate namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who delight in your own abode, in <s>brahman</s>, with prosperity that has no equal or superior.

children.text: yatkīrtanaṃ yatsmaraṇaṃ yadīkṣaṇaṃ yadvandanaṃ yacchravaṇaṃ yadarhaṇam
children.translated_text: His praise, his remembrance, his sight, his salutation, his hearing, and his worship

children.text: lokasya sadyo vidhunoti kalmaṣaṃ tasmai subhadraśravase namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: at once shake off the sin of the world; reverence, reverence to him of auspicious fame.
By approaching whose feet the discerning cast off attachment on both sides from the inner self,

children.text: vindanti hi brahmagatiṃ gataklamāstasmai subhadraśravase namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, freed from weariness, attain the course of <s>brahman</s>; reverence, reverence to him of auspicious fame.

children.text: tapasvino dānaparā yaśasvino manasvino mantravidaḥ sumaṅgalāḥ
children.translated_text: Ascetics, those devoted to giving, the famous, the high-minded, knowers of mantras, and the auspicious

children.text: kṣemaṃ na vindanti vinā yadarpaṇaṃ tasmai subhadraśravase namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not find welfare without offering to him; reverence, reverence to him of auspicious fame.
<s>Kirātas</s>, <s>Hūṇas</s>, <s>Andhras</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, <s>Pulkaśas</s>, <s>Ābhīras</s>, <s>Śumbhas</s>, <s>Yavanas</s>, <s>Khasas</s>, and others,

children.text: ye 'nye ca pāpā yadapāśrayāśrayāḥ śudhyanti tasmai prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even whatever other sinners there are, are purified when they take refuge in the refuge of those who belong to him; reverence to that mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
May that Blessed Lord be gracious, the Self and ruler of those who know the self, composed of the three Vedas, composed of <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), and composed of austerity,
whose sign is reasoned out by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and others whose deceit has departed.
May the Blessed Lord be gracious to me: lord of <s>Śrī</s>, lord of sacrifice, lord of creatures, lord of understanding, lord of worlds, lord of the earth,

children.text: patirgatiścāndhakavṛṣṇisātvatāṃ prasīdatāṃ me bhagavān satāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: lord and goal of the <s>Andhakas</s>, <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, and <s>Sātvatas</s>, lord of the good.
By a mind washed clean through meditation and <s>samādhi</s> on whose feet, men perceive the truth of the self,

children.text: vadanti caitat kavayo yathārucaṃ sa me mukundo bhagavān prasīdatām ||
children.translated_text: and poets describe it according to their own inclination; may that Blessed <s>Mukunda</s> be gracious to me.

children.text: pracoditā yena purā sarasvatī vitanvatājasya satīṃ smṛtiṃ hṛdi
children.translated_text: Long ago, impelled by him, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, as he expanded true memory in the heart of the unborn one,

children.text: svalakṣaṇā prādurabhūt kilāsyataḥ sa me ṛṣīṇām ṛṣabhaḥ prasīdatām ||
children.translated_text: manifested from his mouth with her own marks; may that foremost of seers be gracious to me.

children.text: bhūtairmahadbhirya imāḥ puro vibhurnirmāya śete yadamūṣu pūruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The mighty Lord, having fashioned these cities from the great elements, lies down in them as the Person;

children.text: bhuṅkte guṇān ṣoḍaśa ṣoḍaśātmakaḥ so 'laṃkṛṣīṣṭa bhagavān vacāṃsi me ||
children.translated_text: as the sixteenfold one, he experiences the sixteen qualities; may that Blessed Lord adorn my words.
Reverence to that Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the creator,
from whose lotus mouth, O gentle ones, they drank the nectar consisting of knowledge.
This very teaching, O king, the self-born one, womb of the Veda, directly spoke to inquiring <s>Nārada</s>,
which <s>Hari</s> had told him concerning himself.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
"God of gods, reverence to you, creator of beings, first-born one.
Know that knowledge which reveals the truth of the self.

children.text: yadrūpaṃ yadadhiṣṭhānaṃ yataḥ sṛṣṭam idaṃ prabho
children.translated_text: O Lord, tell truly that reality: what its form is, what its support is, whence this has been created,

children.text: yatsaṃsthaṃ yat paraṃ yac ca tat tattvaṃ vada tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: in what it rests, what is beyond it, and what it is.
For you know all this, lord of what has been, what will be, and what is;
the universe, fixed in your knowledge, is like a myrobalan fruit in your hand.
Having what knowledge, having what support, having what as your superior, and consisting of what,
do you alone create beings through beings, by your own <s>māyā</s>?

children.text: ātman bhāvayase tāni na parābhāvayan svayam
children.translated_text: O Self, relying on your own power, like a spider without fatigue,
you make those beings grow, while you yourself are not overcome by another.

children.text: nāhaṃ veda paraṃ hyasmin nāparaṃ na samaṃ vibho
children.translated_text: O mighty one, I know nothing in this that is higher, lower, or equal,
nor anything else, whether existent or nonexistent, that is to be conceived through name, form, and qualities.

children.text: sa bhavān acaradghoraṃ yat tapaḥ susamāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Yet you undertook terrible austerity, well concentrated;

children.text: tena khedayase nastvaṃ parāśaṅkāṃ ca yacchasi ||
children.translated_text: by that you make us troubled and produce suspicion about some superior."

children.text: etan me pṛcchataḥ sarvaṃ sarvajña sakaleśvara
children.translated_text: O omniscient lord of all, know all this that I ask of you,
exactly in such a way that I may understand it when instructed.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Dear child, this question of yours, compassionate one, is proper,
since I have been urged by you, gentle one, toward beholding the power of the Blessed Lord.

children.text: nānṛtaṃ tava tac cāpi yathā māṃ prabravīṣi bhoḥ
children.translated_text: What you say to me is not false either, O sir,

children.text: avijñāya paraṃ matta etāvat tvaṃ yato hi me ||
children.translated_text: for you regard me as so great because you do not know the supreme one beyond me.
By his own radiance the universe has been made bright, and by it I make it shine,
just as the sun, fire, moon, constellations, planets, and stars do.
To that Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> I bow; let us meditate on him,
by whose hard-to-conquer <s>māyā</s> (cosmic illusion) they call me the teacher of the world.
His <s>māyā</s>, ashamed, cannot remain in the path of his glance;
deluded by her, the dull-witted boast, 'This is mine; this is I.'

children.text: dravyaṃ karma ca kālaśca svabhāvo jīva eva ca
children.translated_text: Substance, action, time, inherent nature, and the living self itself,

children.text: vāsudevāt paro brahman na cānyo 'rtho 'sti tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Brahman</s>, are not beyond <s>Vāsudeva</s>; in truth there is no other reality.
The Vedas have <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as their highest aim; the gods are born from the limbs of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
The worlds have <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as their highest aim; sacrifices have <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as their highest aim.
Yoga has <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as its highest aim; austerity has <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as its highest aim.
Knowledge has <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as its highest aim; the final goal has <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as its highest aim.
Even of that seeing Lord, immutable and the Self of all,
I, having been created, create what is to be created, impelled solely by his glance.
<s>Sattva</s> (lucidity), <s>rajas</s> (activity), and <s>tamas</s> (inertia) are the three guṇas of the one beyond guṇas;
they are assumed through the mighty Lord's <s>māyā</s> for preservation, creation, and dissolution.
As the supports of substance, knowledge, and action in the states of effect, cause, and agency,

children.text: badhnanti nityadā muktaṃ māyinaṃ puruṣaṃ guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the guṇas bind the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the wielder of <s>māyā</s>, who is eternally free.
This very Blessed <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, marked by these three signs,
whose course is known only by himself, O <s>Brahman</s>, is the Lord of all and of me.

children.text: kālaṃ karma svabhāvaṃ ca māyeśo māyayā svayā
children.translated_text: The Lord of <s>māyā</s>, through his own <s>māyā</s>, took up time, action, and inherent nature,
which had come to his Self of its own accord, as he desired to become manifold.
From time came the disturbance of the guṇas; transformation arose from inherent nature;
from action came the birth of <s>mahat</s> (the great principle), presided over by the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
From <s>mahat</s>, as it transformed and was strengthened by <s>rajas</s> and <s>sattva</s>,
