there arose what is dominated by <s>tamas</s>, consisting of substance, knowledge, and action.

children.text: so 'haṅkāra iti prokto vikurvan samabhūt tridhā
children.translated_text: That is called <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle); as it transformed, it became threefold:
the <s>vaikārika</s>, the <s>taijasa</s>, and the <s>tāmasa</s>, according to its divisions,
namely the power of substance, the power of action, and the power of knowledge, O lord.
From the <s>tāmasa</s>, the origin of the elements, as it transformed, space arose;

children.text: tasya mātrā guṇaḥ śabdo liṅgaṃ yaddraṣṭṛdṛśyayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: its measure and quality is sound, the mark of both seer and seen.
Then from space, as it transformed, arose air, whose quality is touch;
by inheriting what preceded it, it possessed sound as well, and it is breath, vigor, force, and strength.
From air too, as it transformed through time, action, and inherent nature,
fire came forth, endowed with form and possessing touch and sound.
From fire, as it transformed, there came water, whose essence is taste;
water has form and touch, and, by inheriting what preceded it, sound as well.
From water, as it transformed, there arose the particular element possessing smell,
endowed, through inheritance from what preceded it, with the qualities of taste, touch, sound, and form.

children.text: vaikārikān mano jajñe devā vaikārikā daśa
children.translated_text: From the <s>vaikārika</s> arose mind, and the ten <s>vaikārika</s> deities:
the directions, <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Pracetas</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Vahni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and <s>Mitra</s>.
But from the <s>taijasa</s>, as it transformed, the ten senses arose.
The power of knowledge and the power of action, intellect and vital breath, are <s>taijasa</s>.
Hearing, skin, smell, sight, and tongue, and speech, arms, generative organ, feet, and anus arose.
When these entities, the elements, senses, mind, and guṇas, were uncombined,
they were not able to construct the abode, O best knower of Brahman.
Then, joined together with one another and impelled by the Blessed Lord's power,
they took up both being and non-being and created this universe.
At the end of many thousands of years, that egg lay in the waters;
the living principle, abiding in time, action, and inherent nature, gave life to what was lifeless.
That same <s>Puruṣa</s> then split the egg and came forth from it,
with a thousand thighs, feet, arms, and eyes, and with a thousand faces and heads.
By his limbs here the wise imagine the worlds:
seven below from his waist and the like, and seven above from his loins and the like.

children.text: puruṣasya mukhaṃ brahma kṣatram etasya bāhavaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is the mouth of the <s>Puruṣa</s>; the warrior class is his arms;
from the thighs of the Blessed Lord came the <s>vaiśya</s>, and from his feet the <s>śūdra</s> was born.
The earth-world was imagined from his feet, and the mid-air world from his navel;
the heaven-world from his heart, and the great world from the chest of the great Self.
In his neck is the world of <s>Jana</s>; the world of <s>Tapas</s> is from his two breasts;
but the world of <s>Satya</s>, the eternal world of <s>Brahmā</s>, is from his heads.

children.text: tatkaṭyāṃ cātalaṃ kﾱptam ūrubhyāṃ vitalaṃ vibhoḥ
children.translated_text: At his waist <s>Atala</s> is fashioned; from the thighs of the mighty Lord, <s>Vitala</s>;

children.text: jānubhyāṃ sutalaṃ śuddhaṃ jaṅghābhyāṃ tu talātalam ||
children.translated_text: from the knees, pure <s>Sutala</s>; and from the shanks, <s>Talātala</s>.
From the ankles comes <s>Mahātala</s>; from the foreparts of the feet, <s>Rasātala</s>;
from the soles of the feet, <s>Pātāla</s>. Thus the person consists of the worlds.
The earth-world was imagined from his feet, and the mid-air world from his navel;

children.text: svarlokaḥ kalpito mūrdhnā iti vā lokakalpanā ||
children.translated_text: the heaven-world was imagined from his head: so too there is this construction of the worlds.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: vācāṃ vahnermukhaṃ kṣetraṃ chandasāṃ sapta dhātavaḥ
children.translated_text: His mouth is the field of speech and of fire; his seven bodily constituents are the field of the metres.
His tongue is the field of oblations, ancestral offerings, nectar, food, and every taste.
His two nostrils are the supreme abode of all breaths and of <s>Vāyu</s>,
and his sense of smell is the field of the <s>Aśvins</s>, medicinal plants, fragrance, and delight.
His eye is the field of forms and lights; his two eyes are those of heaven and the sun.

children.text: karṇau diśāṃ ca tīrthānāṃ śrotram ākāśaśabdayoḥ
children.translated_text: His ears are the quarters and the sacred fords; his hearing belongs to space and sound.
His body is the receptacle of the essences of things and of beauty.

children.text: tvag asya sparśavāyośca sarvamedhasya caiva hi
children.translated_text: His skin is of touch and wind, and indeed of the universal sacrifice.
His hairs are the species of plants, by which the sacrifice is supplied.
His hair, beard, and nails are of stones, metals, clouds, and lightning.
His arms are those of the world-protectors, generally of deeds that secure welfare.

children.text: vikramo bhūrbhuvaḥ svaśca kṣemasya śaraṇasya ca
children.translated_text: His stride is <s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>Svaḥ</s>, and is the place of welfare and refuge;
the feet of <s>Hari</s> are the abode even of every desired boon.
Of the waters, virility, creation, <s>Parjanya</s>, and <s>Prajāpati</s>,
the <s>Puruṣa</s>'s penis and generative organ are for procreation, delight, and fulfillment.
His anus is remembered as belonging to <s>Yama</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and release, O <s>Nārada</s>;
his rectum is remembered as belonging to injury, <s>Nirṛti</s>, death, and hell.
His backside belongs to defeat, <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), and darkness as well;
his channels are the streams and rivers, and his framework of bones is the mountains.
The belly of the <s>Puruṣa</s> is known as the place of the unmanifest, of the oceans of fluid, of beings, and of their dissolution;

children.text: udaraṃ viditaṃ puṃso hṛdayaṃ manasaḥ padam ||
children.translated_text: and his heart is the seat of the mind.

children.text: dharmasya mama tubhyaṃ ca kumārāṇāṃ bhavasya ca
children.translated_text: His self is the ultimate refuge of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), of me and you, of the <s>Kumāras</s> and of <s>Bhava</s>,
and of discriminating knowledge, of <s>sattva</s> (lucidity), and of the supreme.

children.text: ahaṃ bhavān bhavaścaiva ta ime munayo 'grajāḥ
children.translated_text: I, you, <s>Bhava</s> himself, and these elder sages,
the gods, demons, men, Nāgas, birds, beasts, and reptiles,
the Gandharvas, Apsarases, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, hosts of Bhūtas, and serpents,
domestic animals, ancestors, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Cāraṇas, and trees,
and other various living beings dwelling in water, on land, and in the sky,
the planets, lunar mansions, comets, stars, lightning-flashes, and thunderclouds--

children.text: sarvaṃ puruṣa evedaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhavac ca yat
children.translated_text: all this is nothing but the <s>Puruṣa</s>, whatever has been, will be, and is;
by him this universe is enveloped, and he stands beyond it by a span.
As life-breath, he heats his own station and also heats outwardly;
so the <s>Puruṣa</s>, heating <s>Virāj</s>, shines within and without.
He is lord of immortality and fearlessness, for he has passed beyond mortal food;
therefore, O sage, this greatness of the <s>Puruṣa</s> is hard to overstep.
All beings are known to stand in the feet, the station-bearing quarters of the <s>Puruṣa</s>;
immortality, security, and fearlessness have been set upon the heads of the threefold form.
The three feet were outside, the <s>āśramas</s> (life-stages) of those who do not beget;
the other, inside the three worlds, was the householder, not bound to the great vow.
He strode through both courses, the whole world with eating and without eating;
for the <s>Puruṣa</s> is the support of both ignorance and knowledge.
From him the cosmic egg, <s>Virāj</s>, was born, consisting of beings, senses, and qualities;
shining like the sun with rays, he passed beyond that material universe.
When I arose from the lotus sprung from the navel of that great Self,
I did not know the materials of sacrifice apart from the limbs of the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Among them were the animals for the sacrifice, the sacrificial posts and plants, the <s>kuśa</s> grasses,
this divine place of worship, and time endowed with many qualities,
the substances, herbs, unguents, juices, metals, clay, and water,

children.text: ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni cāturhotraṃ ca sattama ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, <s>Yajus</s> formulas, <s>Sāman</s> chants, and the fourfold priesthood, O best one,
the names, the mantras, the fees for priests, and the vows,
the sequence of deities, the ritual procedure, the resolve, and the <s>tantra</s> (ritual system),
the courses and intentions, expiation, and offering;
these materials were gathered by me from the limbs of the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Thus, having gathered the materials from the limbs of the <s>Puruṣa</s>, I

children.text: tam eva puruṣaṃ yajñaṃ tenaivāyajam īśvaram ||
children.translated_text: sacrificed to that very <s>Puruṣa</s>, the sacrifice, the Lord, with that itself.

children.text: tataste bhrātara ime prajānāṃ patayo nava
children.translated_text: Then these brothers of yours, the nine lords of creatures,
with minds well concentrated, worshiped the manifest and unmanifest <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Then in due time the <s>Manus</s>, and other seers,
the ancestors, gods, Daityas, and human beings, worshiped the Lord with rites.
This whole universe is placed in the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;
at the beginning of creation he assumes the broad qualities of <s>māyā</s> (cosmic illusion), though by his own nature he is without qualities.
Assigned by him, I create it; <s>Hara</s>, subject to him, withdraws it;
bearing the three powers, he protects the universe in the form of the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Thus, my child, I have told you just what you asked about:
nothing, whether existent or nonexistent in nature, is to be conceived apart from the Blessed Lord.

children.text: na bhāratī me 'ṅga mṛṣopalakṣyate na vai kvacin me manaso mṛṣā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: My speech, dear one, is not seen to be false, nor does my mind ever move falsely;

children.text: na me hṛṣīkāṇi patantyasatpathe yan me hṛdautkaṇṭhyavatā dhṛto hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: my senses do not fall upon an unreal path, because <s>Hari</s> is held in my heart with longing.
I, made of sacred tradition and austerity, lord of the <s>Prajāpatis</s> and honored by them,

children.text: āsthāya yogaṃ nipuṇaṃ samāhitastaṃ nādhyagacchaṃ yata ātmasambhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: undertaking subtle yoga with concentration, did not find him from whom I am self-born.

children.text: nato 'smyahaṃ taccaraṇaṃ samīyuṣāṃ bhavacchidaṃ svastyayanaṃ sumaṅgalam
children.translated_text: I bow to that foot of his, approached by those who draw near, cutting off worldly becoming, a path to welfare, wholly auspicious;

children.text: yo hyātmamāyāvibhavaṃ sma paryagād yathā nabhaḥ svāntam athāpare kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for he alone fully comprehended the power of his own <s>māyā</s>, as space does its own extent; how then could others?

children.text: nāhaṃ na yūyaṃ yadṛtāṃ gatiṃ vidur na vāmadevaḥ kim utāpare surāḥ
children.translated_text: Neither I nor you know the true path of him, nor does <s>Vāmadeva</s>; how much less the other gods?
Our understanding is deluded by his <s>māyā</s>, and we perceive this created world as if equal to ourselves.
We and others sing of the deeds of his avatāras,

children.text: na yaṃ vidanti tattvena tasmai bhagavate namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet we do not know him in truth; homage to that Blessed Lord.

children.text: sa eṣa ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ kalpe kalpe sṛjatyajaḥ
children.translated_text: He is this primal <s>Puruṣa</s>, unborn, who in kalpa after kalpa creates,
restrains, and protects the self, by the self, within himself.

children.text: viśuddhaṃ kevalaṃ jñānaṃ pratyak samyag avasthitam
children.translated_text: He is pure, absolute knowledge, inward, and rightly established.

children.text: satyaṃ pūrṇam anādyantaṃ nirguṇaṃ nityam advayam ||
children.translated_text: It is the true, complete reality, without beginning or end, without guṇas, eternal, and non-dual.
O seer, sages whose selves, senses, and minds are tranquil know it,
even when that very reality is obscured and disturbed by unsound arguments.

children.text: ādyo 'vatāraḥ puruṣaḥ parasya kālaḥ svabhāvaḥ sadasanmanaśca
children.translated_text: The first avatāra is the Person of the Supreme: time, intrinsic nature, the existent and the nonexistent, and mind;

children.text: dravyaṃ vikāro guṇa indriyāṇi virāṭ svarāṭ sthāsnu cariṣṇu bhūmnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: matter, transformation, the guṇa, the senses, <s>Virāj</s>, <s>Svarāj</s>, and the fixed and moving universe belong to the Vast One.

children.text: ahaṃ bhavo yajña ime prajeśā dakṣādayo ye bhavadādayaśca
children.translated_text: I, <s>Bhava</s>, sacrifice, these lords of creatures, <s>Dakṣa</s> and the others, and you and the rest;
the guardians of heaven, the guardians of the bird-world, the guardians of the human world, and the guardians of the lower worlds;
the lords of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>, and the chiefs of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rakṣases</s>, serpents, and nāgas;

children.text: ye vā ṛṣīṇām ṛṣabhāḥ pitṝṇāṃ daityendrasiddheśvaradānavendrāḥ
children.translated_text: the foremost among seers and among ancestors, the lords of <s>Daityas</s>, the masters of perfected beings, and the lords of <s>Dānavas</s>;
and others too, the chiefs of ghosts, piśācas, bhūtas, kūṣmāṇḍas, aquatic beings, beasts, and birds;

children.text: yat kiñca loke bhagavan mahasvad ojaḥsahasvadbalavat kṣamāvat
children.translated_text: whatever in the world, O Blessed one, possesses splendor, vigor, strength, or forbearance,
whatever is endowed with beauty, modesty, power, selfhood, or wondrous abundance, is that supreme reality, possessing form yet formless in its own nature.

children.text: prādhānyato yān ṛṣa āmananti līlāvatārān puruṣasya bhūmnaḥ
children.translated_text: O seer, I shall now recount to you in order those charming līlā-avatāras of the infinite Person which the sages chiefly proclaim.

children.text: āpīyatāṃ karṇakaṣāyaśoṣān anukramiṣye ta imān supeśān ||
children.translated_text: Drink in these beautiful accounts, which dry up the bitter impurities of the ear.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: yatrodyataḥ kṣititaloddharaṇāya bibhratkrauḍīṃ tanuṃ sakalayajñamayīm anantaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Ananta</s> rose up to lift the surface of the earth, bearing a boar body made of all sacrifice,

children.text: antarmahārṇava upāgatam ādidaityaṃ taṃ daṃṣṭrayādrim iva vajradharo dadāra ||
children.translated_text: he tore apart with his tusk, as <s>Vajradhara</s> tears a mountain, the first demon who had entered the great ocean.

children.text: jāto rucerajanayat suyamān suyajña ākūtisūnuramarān atha dakṣiṇāyām
children.translated_text: Born from <s>Ruci</s>, <s>Suyajña</s>, son of <s>Ākūti</s>, then begot the immortal <s>Suyamas</s> in <s>Dakṣiṇā</s>.

children.text: lokatrayasya mahatīm aharadyadārtiṃ svāyambhuvena manunā harirityanūktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he removed the great distress of the three worlds, he was called <s>Hari</s> by <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>.

children.text: jajñe ca kardamagṛhe dvija devahūtyāṃ strībhiḥ samaṃ navabhirātmagatiṃ svamātre
children.translated_text: He was born in <s>Kardama</s>'s house, O twice-born one, from <s>Devahūti</s>; together with nine women, he taught his own mother the path of the self.

children.text: ūce yayātmaśamalaṃ guṇasaṅgapaṅkamasmin vidhūya kapilasya gatiṃ prapede ||
children.translated_text: By that teaching she washed away the impurity of the self, the mud of attachment to the guṇas, and attained the path of <s>Kapila</s>.

children.text: atrerapatyam abhikāṅkṣata āha tuṣṭo datto mayāham iti yadbhagavān sa dattaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Atri</s> desired a son, the satisfied Blessed one said, 'I have been given by myself'; therefore he was <s>Datta</s>.
The <s>Yadus</s>, <s>Haihayas</s>, and others, their bodies purified by the pollen of his lotus feet, obtained both kinds of yogic power.

children.text: taptaṃ tapo vividhalokasisṛkṣayā me ādau sanāt svatapasaḥ sa catuḥsano 'bhūt
children.translated_text: At the beginning, when I performed austerity from desire to create the various worlds, he became the four <s>Sanas</s> through his own austerity.

children.text: prākkalpasamplavavinaṣṭam ihātmatattvaṃ samyag jagāda munayo yadacakṣatātman ||
children.translated_text: Here he fully taught the truth of the self, which had been lost in the flood of the previous kalpa, and the sages perceived him as the Self.

children.text: dharmasya dakṣaduhitaryajaniṣṭa mūrtyāṃ nārāyaṇo nara iti svatapaḥprabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Dharma</s>, in <s>Mūrti</s>, the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, were born <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Nara</s>, whose power was their own austerity.

children.text: dṛṣṭvātmano bhagavato niyamāvalopaṃ devyastvanaṅgapṛtanā ghaṭituṃ na śekuḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the goddesses, the army of <s>Anaṅga</s>, saw no lapse in the Blessed one's discipline, they could not bring about his disturbance.

children.text: kāmaṃ dahanti kṛtino nanu roṣadṛṣṭyā roṣaṃ dahantam uta te na dahantyasahyam
children.translated_text: Indeed accomplished men burn desire with an angry glance, but they do not burn unbearable anger when it is burning.

children.text: so 'yaṃ yadantaram alaṃ praviśan bibheti kāmaḥ kathaṃ nu punarasya manaḥ śrayeta ||
children.translated_text: That very desire is afraid to enter even the space within him; how then could it take refuge again in his mind?

children.text: viddhaḥ sapatnyuditapatribhiranti rājño bālo 'pi sann upagatastapase vanāni
children.translated_text: Pierced by the arrow-like words uttered by his father's co-wife near the king, though still a child, he went to the forests for austerity.

children.text: tasmā adāddhruvagatiṃ gṛṇate prasanno divyāḥ stuvanti munayo yaduparyadhastāt ||
children.translated_text: Pleased with him as he praised him, the Lord granted <s>Dhruva</s> the fixed state, which divine sages extol from above and below.
When <s>Vena</s>, gone onto a wrong path, his manly glory burned away by the thunderbolt of the twice-borns' words, was falling into hell,

children.text: trātvārthito jagati putrapadaṃ ca lebhe dugdhā vasūni vasudhā sakalāni yena ||
children.translated_text: the Lord, entreated, saved him and took the status of his son in the world; by him the earth was milked of all its riches.

children.text: nābherasāvṛṣabha āsa sudevisūnuryo vai cacāra samadṛg jaḍayogacaryām
children.translated_text: That <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, son of <s>Sudevī</s>, was born as the son of <s>Nābhi</s>; he, equal-seeing, practiced the conduct of inert yoga.

children.text: yat pāramahaṃsyam ṛṣayaḥ padam āmananti svasthaḥ praśāntakaraṇaḥ parimuktasaṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sages call that state <s>pāramahaṃsya</s> (the highest renunciant state), self-contained, with the faculties calmed, and free from attachment.

children.text: satre mamāsa bhagavān hayaśīraṣātho sākṣāt sa yajñapuruṣastapanīyavarṇaḥ
children.translated_text: In my sacrifice the Blessed one then appeared directly as <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s>, the sacrifice-Person, golden in color.

children.text: chandomayo makhamayo 'khiladevatātmā vāco babhūvuruśatīḥ śvasato 'sya nastaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Made of the meters, made of the sacrifice, and the self of all the deities, beautiful sacred utterances arose from his nostrils as he breathed.
At the time of the end of the age, <s>Matsya</s>, perceived by <s>Manu</s>, was the sheltering sign of all groups of living beings in the earth-filled waters.

children.text: visraṃsitān urubhaye salile mukhān me ādāya tatra vijahāra ha vedamārgān ||
children.translated_text: He took from my mouths the Vedic paths that had slipped away into the terrifying great water, and there he sported.
When the leaders of the hosts of gods and dānavas were churning the milk-ocean to obtain nectar, the primeval God,
with the body of a tortoise, supported the mountain on his back, his eyes closing in sleep, as the mountain's turning scratched his itch.
Destroyer of the great fear of heaven, he assumed the form of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, with a terrible face, whirling brows, and tusk-like teeth.

children.text: daityendram āśu gadayābhipatantam ārādūrau nipātya vidadāra nakhaiḥ sphurantam ||
children.translated_text: He quickly threw onto his thighs the lord of the <s>Daityas</s>, who rushed near with his mace, and tore him open with his flashing nails.

children.text: antaḥsarasyurubalena pade gṛhīto grāheṇa yūthapatirambujahasta ārtaḥ
children.translated_text: In the lake, seized by the foot by a crocodile of mighty strength, the distressed lord of the herd, holding a lotus,
said this: 'Primeval Person, lord of all worlds, whose fame is a tīrtha, whose name is auspicious to hear!'
Hearing him as he sought refuge, immeasurable <s>Hari</s>, bearing the discus, mounted on the arms of the king of birds.

children.text: cakreṇa nakravadanaṃ vinipāṭya tasmāddhaste pragṛhya bhagavān kṛpayojjahāra ||
children.translated_text: With the discus he struck down the crocodile's mouth, and the Blessed one, grasping him by the hand, compassionately rescued him from it.

children.text: jyāyān guṇairavarajo 'pyaditeḥ sutānāṃ lokān vicakrama imān yadathādhiyajñaḥ
children.translated_text: Though younger among the sons of <s>Aditi</s>, he was greater in qualities; as <s>Adhiyajña</s> he traversed these worlds.

children.text: kṣmāṃ vāmanena jagṛhe tripadacchalena yācñām ṛte pathi caran prabhubhirna cālyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As <s>Vāmana</s>, by the stratagem of three steps, he took the earth from <s>Bali</s>, walking the path of begging and not to be displaced by lords.
For <s>Bali</s>, who bore on his head the water washing <s>Urukrama</s>'s feet, lordship over the gods was no worthwhile object.

children.text: yo vai pratiśrutam ṛte na cikīrṣadanyadātmānam aṅga manasā haraye 'bhimene ||
children.translated_text: He, indeed, wishing to do nothing other than what had been promised, O dear one, dedicated himself in his mind to <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: tubhyaṃ ca nārada bhṛśaṃ bhagavān vivṛddhabhāvena sādhu parituṣṭa uvāca yogam
children.translated_text: And to you, <s>Nārada</s>, the Blessed Lord, well pleased by your greatly increased devotion, spoke of <s>yoga</s> (spiritual discipline),

children.text: jñānaṃ ca bhāgavatam ātmasatattvadīpaṃ yadvāsudevaśaraṇā vidurañjasaiva ||
children.translated_text: and of <s>Bhāgavata</s> knowledge, the lamp of the true reality of the self, which those who take refuge in <s>Vāsudeva</s> know quite easily.

children.text: cakraṃ ca dikṣvavihataṃ daśasu svatejo manvantareṣu manuvaṃśadharo bibharti
children.translated_text: In the ten directions he bears the discus, unobstructed by its own brilliance, and through the <s>manvantaras</s> (ages of Manus) he upholds the lineage of <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: duṣṭeṣu rājasu damaṃ vyadadhāt svakīrtiṃ satye tripṛṣṭha uśatīṃ prathayaṃścaritraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among wicked kings he imposed punishment and spread his own lovely fame in the age of truth as <s>Tripṛṣṭha</s>, through his deeds.

children.text: dhanvantariśca bhagavān svayam eva kīrtirnāmnā nṛṇāṃ pururujāṃ ruja āśu hanti
children.translated_text: And the Blessed Lord himself became <s>Dhanvantari</s>, fame in person by name, who quickly removes the diseases of men afflicted by many ailments.

children.text: yajñe ca bhāgam amṛtāyuravāvarundhāyuṣyavedam anuśāstyavatīrya loke ||
children.translated_text: In the sacrifice he secured a share and deathless life; descending into the world, he taught the <s>Āyurveda</s> (science of life).

children.text: kṣatraṃ kṣayāya vidhinopabhṛtaṃ mahātmā brahmadhrug ujjhitapathaṃ narakārtilipsu
children.translated_text: The great-souled one, seeing the warrior power raised up by destiny for its own destruction, hostile to <s>brahman</s>, abandoning the path, and seeking the torments of hell,
will cut down that thorn of the earth, fierce in valor, twenty-one times with his broad-bladed axe.

children.text: asmatprasādasumukhaḥ kalayā kaleśa ikṣvākuvaṃśa avatīrya gurornideśe
children.translated_text: Favorable through our grace, the Lord of parts will descend in a portion in the line of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, and, abiding by his father's command,

children.text: tiṣṭhan vanaṃ sadayitānuja āviveśa yasmin virudhya daśakandhara ārtim ārchat ||
children.translated_text: he will enter the forest with his beloved wife and younger brother; by opposing him, the ten-necked one will meet distress.
For him, whose limbs trembled with mounting fear, the ocean at once gave a path, as he wished to burn the enemy city like <s>Hara</s>.
Its hosts of makaras, serpents, and crocodiles were being scorched from afar by the burning, deep-red eyes born of his friend-shaking anger.
The abductor of his wife, who bore loud laughter while the quarters he enjoyed seemed mocked by the tusks of <s>Mahendra</s>'s elephant broken on contact with his chest,
he will swiftly destroy, together with his life-breaths, by the twanging of his bow resounding over the army.
For the removal of the earth's distress, oppressed by the armies of the foes of the gods, he of white and black hair will be born in a portion.
He will perform deeds whose path is not perceived by ordinary people, deeds bound up with the greatness of his own self.

children.text: tokena jīvaharaṇaṃ yadulūkikāyāstraimāsikasya ca padā śakaṭo 'pavṛttaḥ
children.translated_text: As an infant he will take the life of the demoness; at three months old he will overturn the cart with his foot.
And while crawling between them, he will uproot the two sky-touching <s>Arjuna</s> trees; otherwise that could not have happened.
When in <s>Vraja</s> the cattle and cowherd boys have drunk poisoned water, he will revive them by the rain of his gracious glance.
To purify that water, while playing in the lake, he will drive out the serpent whose rolling tongues are charged with exceedingly deadly poison.

children.text: tat karma divyam iva yan niśi niḥśayānaṃ dāvāgninā śucivane paridahyamāne
children.translated_text: That deed will seem divine: at night, when all are asleep and the bright forest is being burned all around by a forest fire,

children.text: unneṣyati vrajam ato 'vasitāntakālaṃ netre pidhāpya sabalo 'nadhigamyavīryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he, together with <s>Bala</s>, of unfathomable power, will lead <s>Vraja</s> out from what had become its final hour, after making them close their eyes.

children.text: gṛhṇīta yadyadupabandham amuṣya mātā śulbaṃ sutasya na tu tat tadamuṣya māti
children.translated_text: Whatever bonds his mother takes up as rope for her son, each one of them does not measure him.

children.text: yaj jṛmbhato 'sya vadane bhuvanāni gopī saṃvīkṣya śaṅkitamanāḥ pratibodhitāsīt ||
children.translated_text: And when the cowherd woman saw the worlds in his mouth as he yawned, she became fearful in mind and was brought back to awareness.

children.text: nandaṃ ca mokṣyati bhayādvaruṇasya pāśādgopān bileṣu pihitān mayasūnunā ca
children.translated_text: He will free <s>Nanda</s> from the fear of <s>Varuṇa</s>'s noose, and the cowherds who had been shut in caves by the son of <s>Maya</s>.

children.text: ahnyāpṛtaṃ niśi śayānam atiśrameṇa lokaṃ vikuṇṭham upaneṣyati gokulaṃ sma ||
children.translated_text: And he once led <s>Gokula</s>, which by day was covered over and at night slept from extreme fatigue, to the world free from limitation.

children.text: gopairmakhe pratihate vrajaviplavāyadeve 'bhivarṣati paśūn kṛpayā rirakṣuḥ
children.translated_text: When the sacrifice was obstructed by the cowherds and the god rained down for the ruin of <s>Vraja</s>, wishing in compassion to protect the cattle,

children.text: dhartocchilīndhram iva saptadināni saptavarṣo mahīdhram anaghaikakare salīlam ||
children.translated_text: though only seven years old, O sinless one, he will playfully hold up the mountain for seven days with one hand, like an upraised mushroom.

children.text: krīḍan vane niśi niśākararaśmigauryāṃ rāsonmukhaḥ kalapadāyatamūrchitena
children.translated_text: Playing in the forest at night, bright with the rays of the moon, and intent on the <s>rāsa</s> dance, with the long swoon of his melodious notes,
he will take the head of the abductor, the follower of <s>Dhanada</s>, when the love-pain of the women of the cowherds of <s>Vraja</s> has been inflamed.
And those such as <s>Pralamba</s>, <s>Khara</s>, <s>Dardura</s>, <s>Keśin</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, the wrestlers, the elephant, <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the <s>Yavanas</s>, the monkey, <s>Pauṇḍraka</s>, and others,
and others headed by <s>Śālva</s>, <s>Kuja</s>, <s>Balvala</s>, <s>Dantavakra</s>, the seven bulls, <s>Śambara</s>, <s>Vidūratha</s>, and <s>Rukmin</s>,

children.text: ye vā mṛdhe samitiśālina āttacāpāḥ kāmbojamatsyakurusṛñjayakaikayādyāḥ
children.translated_text: or those armed with bows and powerful in battle and assembly, such as the <s>Kāmbojas</s>, <s>Matsyas</s>, <s>Kurus</s>, <s>Sṛñjayas</s>, <s>Kaikayas</s>, and others,

children.text: yāsyantyadarśanam alaṃ balapārthabhīmavyājāhvayena hariṇā nilayaṃ tadīyam ||
children.translated_text: will disappear and go to his own abode, struck down by <s>Hari</s> under the assumed names of <s>Bala</s>, <s>Pārtha</s>, and <s>Bhīma</s>.

children.text: kālena mīlitadhiyām avamṛśya nṝṇāṃ stokāyuṣāṃ svanigamo bata dūrapāraḥ
children.translated_text: Considering that men, their understanding closed by time and their lives brief, can scarcely cross to the far shore of his own Veda,

children.text: āvirhitastvanuyugaṃ sa hi satyavatyāṃ vedadrumaṃ viṭapaśo vibhajiṣyati sma ||
children.translated_text: he will appear, age after age, in <s>Satyavatī</s>, and divide the tree of the Veda branch by branch.

children.text: devadviṣāṃ nigamavartmani niṣṭhitānāṃ pūrbhirmayena vihitābhir adṛśyatūrbhiḥ
children.translated_text: For the enemies of the gods, who stand on the path of the Veda but, from invisible cities fashioned by <s>Maya</s>, destroy the worlds,

children.text: lokān ghnatāṃ mativimoham atipralobhaṃ veṣaṃ vidhāya bahu bhāṣyata aupadharmyam ||
children.translated_text: he will assume an alluring form that greatly bewilders the mind, and he will speak at length of a counterfeit <s>dharma</s> (religion).

children.text: yarhyālayeṣvapi satāṃ na hareḥ kathāḥ syuḥ pāṣaṇḍino dvijajanā vṛṣalā nṛdevāḥ
children.translated_text: When even in the houses of good people there are no stories of <s>Hari</s>, when twice-born men are heretics and kings are base men,

children.text: svāhā svadhā vaṣaḍiti sma giro na yatra śāstā bhaviṣyati kalerbhagavān yugānte ||
children.translated_text: and where the words 'svāhā,' 'svadhā,' and 'vaṣaṭ' are not heard, the Blessed Lord will become the chastiser at the end of the age of <s>Kali</s>.

children.text: sarge tapo 'ham ṛṣayo nava ye prajeśāḥ sthāne 'tha dharmamakhamanvamarāvanīśāḥ
children.translated_text: At creation there are austerity, I, the sages, the nine lords of creatures; in maintenance there are <s>dharma</s>, sacrifice, the <s>Manus</s>, the gods, and kings of the earth.
But at the end there are forms such as <s>Adharma</s>, <s>Hara</s>, wrath, and the demons; these are manifestations of <s>māyā</s> sharing in the power of the Person.

children.text: viṣṇornu vīryagaṇanāṃ katamo 'rhatīha yaḥ pārthivānyapi kavirvimame rajāṃsi
children.translated_text: Who here is capable of counting the powers of <s>Viṣṇu</s>? A wise man might even count the dust particles of the earth,

children.text: caskambha yaḥ svarahasāskhalatā tripṛṣṭhaṃ yasmāt trisāmyasadanādurukampayānam ||
children.translated_text: but he, by his unchecked force, upheld the three-peaked heaven when it shook greatly from his station in the threefold realm.

children.text: nāntaṃ vidāmyaham amī munayo 'grajāste māyābalasya puruṣasya kuto 'varā ye
children.translated_text: I do not know the limit of the <s>māyā</s>-power of the Person, nor do these sages, your elder brothers; how much less could lesser beings know it?

children.text: gāyan guṇān daśaśatānana ādidevaḥ śeṣo 'dhunāpi samavasyati nāsya pāram ||
children.translated_text: Singing hundreds of qualities, <s>Śeṣa</s>, the primeval god with a thousand mouths, even now has not reached his limit.

children.text: yeṣāṃ sa eṣa bhagavān dayayedanantaḥ sarvātmanāśritapado yadi nirvyalīkam
children.translated_text: Those upon whom this Blessed Lord, the endless one, should have mercy, if they have taken refuge at his feet with their whole self and without deceit,

children.text: te dustarām atitaranti ca devamāyāṃ naiṣāṃ mamāham iti dhīḥ śvaśṛgālabhakṣye ||
children.translated_text: they cross beyond the hard-to-cross divine <s>māyā</s>; they have no thought of "mine" and "I" toward this body, food for dogs and jackals.

children.text: vedāham aṅga paramasya hi yogamāyāṃ yūyaṃ bhavaśca bhagavān atha daityavaryaḥ
children.translated_text: O dear one, I know the <s>yogamāyā</s> of the Supreme; so do you, <s>Bhava</s>, the Blessed Lord, and the chief of the <s>Daityas</s>.

children.text: patnī manoḥ sa ca manuśca tadātmajāśca prācīnabarhirṛbhuraṅga uta dhruvaśca ||
children.translated_text: The wife of <s>Manu</s>, <s>Manu</s> himself, his sons, <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>, <s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Aṅga</s>, and also <s>Dhruva</s>,
<s>Ikṣvāku</s>, <s>Aila</s>, <s>Mucukunda</s>, <s>Videha</s>, <s>Gādhi</s>, <s>Raghū</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, <s>Sagara</s>, <s>Gaya</s>, <s>Nahuṣa</s>, and others,
<s>Māndhātṛ</s>, <s>Alarka</s>, <s>Śatadhanvan</s>, <s>Rantideva</s>, <s>Devavrata</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Amūrtaraya</s>, and <s>Dilīpa</s>,
<s>Saubhari</s>, <s>Utaṅka</s>, <s>Śibi</s>, <s>Devala</s>, <s>Pippalāda</s>, <s>Sārasvata</s>, <s>Uddhava</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, and <s>Bhūriṣeṇa</s>,
and those other excellent ones, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>Hanūmat</s>, <s>Upendradatta</s>, <s>Pārtha</s>, <s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s>, <s>Vidura</s>, and <s>Śrutadeva</s>,

children.text: te vai vidantyatitaranti ca devamāyāṃ strīśūdrahūṇaśabarā api pāpajīvāḥ
children.translated_text: they indeed know and cross beyond the divine <s>māyā</s>; so too women, <s>Śūdras</s>, <s>Hūṇas</s>, <s>Śabaras</s>, and even people of sinful livelihood,
if their character and training are devoted to the Lord of wondrous strides; even animal-born beings do so, how much more those who retain what they have heard.

children.text: śaśvat praśāntam abhayaṃ pratibodhamātraṃ śuddhaṃ samaṃ sadasataḥ paramātmatattvam
children.translated_text: The truth of the supreme self is eternally peaceful, fearless, pure awareness alone, stainless, equal, and beyond being and non-being.

children.text: śabdo na yatra purukārakavān kriyārtho māyā paraityabhimukhe ca vilajjamānā ||
children.translated_text: There speech, furnished with many agents and aimed at action, does not reach; and <s>māyā</s>, when facing it, turns away in shame.

children.text: tadvai padaṃ bhagavataḥ paramasya puṃso brahmeti yadvidurajasrasukhaṃ viśokam
children.translated_text: That indeed is the state of the supreme Blessed Person, which they know as <s>Brahman</s>, constant happiness and free from sorrow.

children.text: sadhryaṅ niyamya yatayo yamakartahetiṃ jahyuḥ svarāḍiva nipānakhanitram indraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having rightly restrained themselves, ascetics abandon the weapon made by discipline and action, as a self-ruling king gives up a tool for digging a watering place.

children.text: sa śreyasām api vibhurbhagavān yato 'sya bhāvasvabhāvavihitasya sataḥ prasiddhiḥ
children.translated_text: That Blessed Lord is lord even of the highest goods; from him comes the manifestation of this existent being, whose condition and nature are established by him.

children.text: dehe svadhātuvigame 'nuviśīryamāṇe vyomeva tatra puruṣo na viśīryate 'ñjaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the body, as its own constituents depart, is breaking apart after them, the person there does not break apart, like space.
O child, this Blessed Lord, the creator of the universe, has been declared to you
in summary; there is no being or non-being, from anything else, that is other than <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: idaṃ bhāgavataṃ nāma yan me bhagavatoditam
children.translated_text: This is the work named <s>Bhāgavata</s>, which the Blessed Lord spoke to me.
It is a compendium of his manifestations; you must expand it.
So that devotion to the Blessed Lord <s>Hari</s> will arise among men,
describe it with this intention: he is the self of all and the support of everything.
For one who describes the <s>māyā</s> of that Lord, who approves of it,

children.text: śṛṇvataḥ śraddhayā nityaṃ māyayātmā na muhyati ||
children.translated_text: and who hears it constantly with faith, the self is not bewildered by <s>māyā</s>.
The king said:
O <s>brāhman</s>, when <s>Nārada</s>, the seer of the gods, was urged by <s>Brahmā</s> to recount the qualities of the one beyond qualities,

children.text: yasmai yasmai yathā prāha nārado devadarśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to whom, to whom, and in what manner did he speak?
I wish to know this truth, O best of knowers of truth:
the auspicious stories for the worlds of <s>Hari</s>, whose power is wondrous.
Tell them, O greatly fortunate one, so that, fixing my detached mind
on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the self of all, I may abandon this body.
For one who constantly hears with faith and sings of his own deeds,
the Blessed Lord enters the heart before a very long time has passed.
Entering through the opening of the ear into the lotus of feeling of his own people,

children.text: dhunoti śamalaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ salilasya yathā śarat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> shakes off impurity, as autumn clears water.
A person whose self has been washed does not abandon the root of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet,
freed from every affliction, just as a traveler does not abandon his own shelter.
Since he is without material constituents, O <s>brāhman</s>, how did this body of his begin through constituents,

children.text: yadṛcchayā hetunā vā bhavanto jānate yathā ||
children.translated_text: whether by chance or by a cause, as you know?
There was the lotus from his belly, marked by the arrangement of the worlds.

children.text: yāvān ayaṃ vai puruṣa iyattāvayavaiḥ pṛthak
children.translated_text: As great as this <s>Puruṣa</s> is, with so many limbs individually,
so great that one is said to be, as if possessing structure and limbs.
The unborn one, the self of beings, creates beings by whose grace;
by him the one born from the navel-lotus saw that form.
And where also that <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose nature is the maintenance, arising, and dissolution of the universe,
the lord of <s>māyā</s>, having set aside his own <s>māyā</s>, lies as the indweller in every heart.
We have heard that the worlds with their guardians were formerly fashioned from the limbs of the <s>Puruṣa</s>,
and the limbs of that one from the worlds with their guardians.

children.text: yāvān kalpo vikalpo vā yathā kālo 'numīyate
children.translated_text: How great a <s>kalpa</s> or <s>vikalpa</s> is, and how time is inferred,
the terms past, future, and present, and the measure of the lifespan of an existent being,
the course of time that is observed, whether minute or vast,
and however many paths of action there are and of what sort, O best of twice-born ones,
in what locus the aggregate of action is gathered, and how and by what it is taken up,
for those desiring the transformation of the <s>guṇas</s> and of those possessing the <s>guṇas</s>,
the origin of earth, the underworlds, the directions, the sky, planets, constellations, and mountains,
of rivers, oceans, and islands, and of the inhabitants of these places,
the measure of the cosmic egg, according to its external and internal divisions,
the conduct of the great ones, and the determination of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>,

children.text: yugāni yugamānaṃ ca dharmo yaśca yuge yuge
children.translated_text: the ages, the measure of an age, and the <s>dharma</s> that exists in each age,
and the account of <s>Hari</s>'s avatāras, which is most wondrous,
the common <s>dharma</s> of human beings and what its special forms are,

children.text: śreṇīnāṃ rājarṣīṇāṃ ca dharmaḥ kṛcchreṣu jīvatām ||
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s> of guilds, of royal sages, and of those living in hardship,
the enumeration of the principles, their marks, and the marks of their causes,
the method of worshiping the <s>Puruṣa</s> and of inward yoga,
the course of yogic lordship and power, and the breaking of the subtle body for yogins,
and the <s>Vedas</s>, auxiliary <s>Vedas</s>, laws, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and <s>Purāṇa</s>.
the inundation of all beings, cosmic expansion, and reabsorption,

children.text: iṣṭāpūrtasya kāmyānāṃ trivargasya ca yo vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the rule concerning <s>iṣṭa-pūrta</s> rites, desired aims, and the <s>trivarga</s> (three human goals);

children.text: yo vānuśāyināṃ sargaḥ pāṣaṇḍasya ca sambhavaḥ
children.translated_text: or the creation of beings lying latent, and the rise of heresy,
and the bondage and liberation of the self, and its establishment in its own nature;
how the self-governed Blessed Lord sports through his own <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: visṛjya vā yathā māyām udāste sākṣivadvibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: or how, having cast off <s>māyā</s>, the all-pervading one remains apart like a witness;
all this, O blessed one, as I ask in due order,
you should explain truly to me, who have taken refuge in you, O great sage.

children.text: atra pramāṇaṃ hi bhavān parameṣṭhī yathātmabhūḥ
children.translated_text: For in this matter you are an authority, like the supreme-seated, self-born one;
and others follow what was done by the forefathers of the ancients.
My life-breaths do not depart, O brahman, despite this fasting,
as I drink the nectar of <s>Acyuta</s>, flowing from the ocean of your words.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: sa upāmantrito rājñā kathāyām iti satpateḥ
children.translated_text: Thus invited by the king into discourse on the Lord of the good,
<s>Brahmarāta</s>, greatly pleased by <s>Viṣṇurāta</s> in the assembly,
spoke the Purāṇa called <s>Bhāgavata</s>, equal to the Veda,
spoken by the Blessed Lord to <s>Brahmā</s> when the <s>Brahma-kalpa</s> had arrived.
Whatever <s>Parīkṣit</s>, bull of the <s>Pāṇḍus</s>, asked one after another,
he began to recount all that in sequence.
<s>Śrīśuka</s> said:
Without the self's <s>māyā</s>, O king, for the supreme one whose nature is pure experience,
connection with objects would not occur, plainly as for a dreamer.
Appearing as if many-formed through his many-formed <s>māyā</s>,
sporting among her <s>guṇas</s>, he thinks, 'mine' and 'I.'

children.text: yarhi vāva mahimni sve parasmin kālamāyayoḥ
children.translated_text: But whenever he delights in his own greatness, beyond time and <s>māyā</s>,
then, free from delusion, he abandons both and remains apart.
For the purification of knowledge of the self, the Blessed Lord spoke the truth,
showing his form to <s>Brahmā</s>, honored by his vow free from deceit.

children.text: sa ādidevo jagatāṃ paro guruḥ svadhiṣṇyam āsthāya sisṛkṣayaikṣata
children.translated_text: That primal god, the supreme teacher of the worlds, took his seat in his own abode and, desiring to create, looked about;

children.text: tāṃ nādhyagacchaddṛśam atra saṃmatāṃ prapañcanirmāṇavidhiryayā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: but he did not find there the approved vision by which the method for producing the manifest world would arise.

children.text: sa cintayan dvyakṣaram ekadāmbhasy upāśṛṇoddvirgaditaṃ vaco vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: As he pondered, the mighty one once heard in the water a two-syllabled utterance spoken twice,

children.text: sparśeṣu yat ṣoḍaśam ekaviṃśaṃ niṣkiñcanānāṃ nṛpa yaddhanaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: which, among the consonants, is the sixteenth and the twenty-first, O king, and which the possessionless know as their wealth.
Hearing it and wishing to see its speaker, he looked over the directions; seeing nothing else there,

children.text: svadhiṣṇyam āsthāya vimṛśya taddhitaṃ tapasyupādiṣṭa ivādadhe manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he took his seat in his own abode, considered it beneficial, and fixed his mind on <s>tapas</s> as if instructed.
For a divine thousand years, his vision unfailing, his breath and self conquered, and both sets of senses subdued,
he performed <s>tapas</s>, heating all the worlds; more intense than those who perform austerity, he was concentrated.

children.text: tasmai svalokaṃ bhagavān sabhājitaḥ saṃdarśayāmāsa paraṃ na yatparam
children.translated_text: To him, worshiped by him, the Blessed Lord revealed his own supreme world, beyond which there is nothing higher,
free from affliction, delusion, and fear, praised by persons whose vision is like his own.

children.text: pravartate yatra rajastamastayoḥ sattvaṃ ca miśraṃ na ca kālavikramaḥ
children.translated_text: There the mixed <s>sattva</s> of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> does not operate, nor the movement of time;

children.text: na yatra māyā kim utāpare harer anuvratā yatra surāsurārcitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is no <s>māyā</s>, much less its other effects; there dwell the followers of <s>Hari</s>, worshiped by gods and asuras.
Dark-blue and fair, lotus-eyed, dressed in yellowish garments, beautiful and well formed,
all four-armed, radiant with blazing jewel ornaments and excellent necklaces,
with the lustre of coral, beryl, and lotus fibers, wearing flashing earrings, crowns, and garlands.
That realm shines on every side with brilliant rows of splendid aerial palaces belonging to great souls,
and gleams with the radiance of foremost women, like the sky with rows of clouds lit by lightning.

children.text: śrīryatra rūpiṇyurugāyapādayoḥ karoti mānaṃ bahudhā vibhūtibhiḥ
children.translated_text: There <s>Śrī</s>, embodied, with manifold splendors, honors the feet of <s>Urugāya</s>,

children.text: preṅkhaṃ śritā yā kusumākarānugair vigīyamānā priyakarma gāyatī ||
children.translated_text: resting on a swing, and, sung by attendants from the flower-garden, she sings his beloved deeds.

children.text: dadarśa tatrākhilasātvatāṃ patiṃ śriyaḥ patiṃ yajñapatiṃ jagatpatim
children.translated_text: There he saw the lord of all <s>Sātvatas</s>, the lord of <s>Śrī</s>, the lord of sacrifice, the lord of the world,
the all-pervading one served by <s>Sunanda</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Prabala</s>, <s>Arhaṇa</s>, and other foremost attendants of his own.
His glance was nectar, turned graciously toward his servants; his face had a gentle smile and reddish eyes;

children.text: kirīṭinaṃ kuṇḍalinaṃ caturbhujaṃ pītāṃśukaṃ vakṣasi lakṣitaṃ śriyā ||
children.translated_text: he wore a crown and earrings, had four arms, wore a yellow garment, and was marked on the chest by <s>Śrī</s>.
Seated on a most worthy throne, supreme, surrounded by the four, sixteen, and five powers,

children.text: yuktaṃ bhagaiḥ svairitaratra cādhruvaiḥ sva eva dhāman ramamāṇam īśvaram ||
children.translated_text: endowed with his own sovereign excellences, while such excellences elsewhere are impermanent, the Lord delighted in his own abode.
His inner being overwhelmed with delight at that vision, his body thrilled, and his eyes tearful with the fullness of love,

children.text: nanāma pādāmbujam asya viśvasṛg yat pāramahaṃsyena pathādhigamyate ||
children.translated_text: the creator of the universe bowed to his lotus feet, which are reached by the path of the supreme swans.

children.text: taṃ prīyamāṇaṃ samupasthitaṃ kaviṃ prajāvisarge nijaśāsanārhaṇam
children.translated_text: To that seer, loved by him and standing before him, worthy of his own command for the creation of beings,

children.text: babhāṣa īṣatsmitaśociṣā girā priyaḥ priyaṃ prītamanāḥ kare spṛśan ||
children.translated_text: the Beloved one, pleased in mind, touching the beloved with his hand, spoke with speech brightened by a slight smile.
The Blessed Lord said:
You have fully satisfied me, O <s>Veda-garbha</s>, by your desire to create,
and by <s>tapas</s> sustained for a long time; I am hard to satisfy for false yogins.

children.text: varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te vareśaṃ mābhivāñchitam
children.translated_text: Choose a boon; welfare to you. From me, the lord of boons, ask what you desire.
O <s>Brahmā</s>, the culmination of human effort for the highest good is the vision of me.
This vision of my world is the realized experience of what you had in mind,
because, after hearing my word in solitude, you performed supreme <s>tapas</s>.
When you were bewildered about your task, this was prescribed by me to you there:
<s>tapas</s> is directly my heart, and I am the very self of <s>tapas</s>, O sinless one.
I create this by tapas alone, and by tapas I again consume it.

children.text: bibharmi tapasā viśvaṃ vīryaṃ me duścaraṃ tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By tapas I sustain the universe; my strength is tapas, difficult to perform.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
O Blessed Lord, overseer of all beings, you are established in the hidden chamber of the heart.
For you know, with unobstructed insight, what is intended to be done.
Even so, O Lord, grant the request of me who seeks a lord; be the lord of this petition.

children.text: parāvare yathā rūpe jānīyāṃ te tvarūpiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May I know your higher and lower forms, though you are formless.
How, through the connection of your own <s>māyā</s>, strengthened by many powers,
you destroy, send forth, take up, and sustain yourself by yourself.
You play, O one whose resolve is unfailing, as a spider spins out its thread.

children.text: tathā tadviṣayāṃ dhehi manīṣāṃ mayi mādhava ||
children.translated_text: Therefore place in me an understanding whose object is that, O <s>Mādhava</s>.
Taught by the Blessed Lord, I shall indeed act without weariness.
By your grace, may I not become bound while undertaking the creation of beings.

children.text: yāvat sakhā sakhyuriveśa te kṛtaḥ prajāvisarge vibhajāmi bho janam
children.translated_text: So long as, O Lord, appointed by you like a friend by a friend, I distribute the people in the creation of beings,

children.text: aviklavaste parikarmaṇi sthito mā me samunnaddhamado 'ja māninaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may I stand unshaken in your service; O Unborn One, may swelling pride not make me self-conceited.
The Blessed Lord said:
Receive my supreme and most secret knowledge, joined with realization,

children.text: sarahasyaṃ tadaṅgaṃ ca gṛhāṇa gaditaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: together with its mystery and its ancillary parts, as it is spoken by me.
As great as I am, of whatever nature, and possessing whatever form, qualities, and acts,
may knowledge of that reality be yours exactly so, through my grace.

children.text: aham evāsam evāgre nānyadyat sadasat param
children.translated_text: I alone existed before, and no other thing, whether existent, nonexistent, or beyond them.
Afterwards I am what this is, and whatever would remain, that too am I.

children.text: ṛte 'rthaṃ yat pratīyeta na pratīyeta cātmani
children.translated_text: What appears apart from the real object, and yet is not perceived in the self,
know that to be the self's <s>māyā</s>, like an appearance, like darkness.
Just as the great elements have entered into high and low beings,
and yet have not entered them, so I am in them and not in them.
Only this much is to be investigated by one who seeks the truth of the self:
what exists everywhere and always, by direct and inverse discernment.
Stand firmly in this view with supreme <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).
You will never be bewildered through the creations and dissolutions of the ages.
<s>Śuka</s> said:
Having thus instructed the unborn <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, the lord of creatures,
<s>Hari</s> withdrew that form of his own self while <s>Brahmā</s> looked on.
With folded hands offered to <s>Hari</s>, who had vanished from the range of the senses,
he, made of all beings, created this universe as before.
Once <s>Prajāpati</s>, the lord of <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), practiced restraints and observances,
seeking the welfare of creatures and desiring his own highest good.
To him came <s>Nārada</s>, dearest among his heirs and obedient to him,
eager to serve, through character, humility, and self-control.
The great sage, wishing to know the <s>māyā</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of <s>māyā</s>,
that great devotee, O king, pleased his father.
Seeing his father, the great-grandfather of the worlds, satisfied,
the divine seer asked fully what you are asking me.
To him this <s>Bhāgavata</s> Purāṇa, possessing ten characteristics,

children.text: proktaṃ bhagavatā prāha prītaḥ putrāya bhūtakṛt ||
children.translated_text: which had been spoken by the Blessed Lord, the maker of beings gladly spoke to his son.
<s>Nārada</s>, O king, spoke it to the sage on the bank of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
to <s>Vyāsa</s> of immeasurable splendor, who was meditating on the supreme <s>brahman</s>.
As for what I was asked by you, how this arose from <s>Virāj</s>, beginning with the <s>Puruṣa</s>,
I shall relate how it was, and all the other questions in full.
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: atra sargo visargaśca sthānaṃ poṣaṇam ūtayaḥ
children.translated_text: Here are primary creation, secondary creation, stability, protection, and impulses,
the manvantaras, accounts of the Lord, dissolution, liberation, and the support.
For the sake of clarifying the tenth,
great souls describe here the characteristics of the nine directly, by scriptural wording and meaning.
The birth of gross elements, subtle elements, senses, and intellect is called primary creation.
Arising from <s>Brahmā</s> through the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>, secondary creation is remembered as pertaining to the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Stability is the triumph of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>; protection is his favor.
The manvantaras are true <s>dharma</s>; impulses are the latent impressions of action.
The accounts of <s>Hari</s>'s avatāras and of those who follow him
are called stories of the Lord among people, enriched by many narratives.
Dissolution is the repose of this self together with its powers.
Liberation is abandoning an alien form and abiding in one's own true form.
That from which appearance and dissolution are ascertained

children.text: sa āśrayaḥ paraṃ brahma paramātmeti śabdyate ||
children.translated_text: is the support, called the supreme <s>brahman</s> and the supreme self.
This person who is the inner self is that very presiding divine principle.
The person through whom the two are distinguished there is indeed the element-based principle.
When, in the absence of one, we do not apprehend either one,

children.text: tritayaṃ tatra yo veda sa ātmā svāśrayāśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the one who knows the triad there is the self, the support of its own supports.
When that <s>Puruṣa</s> split open the cosmic egg and emerged,
seeking an abode for himself, the pure one created pure waters.
He dwelt in those waters, created by himself, for a thousand years.
Therefore he is named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, because the waters arose from the <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: dravyaṃ karma ca kālaśca svabhāvo jīva eva ca
children.translated_text: Substance, action, time, inherent nature, and the individual soul
exist by his favor and do not exist when he disregards them.
The one, seeking multiplicity, rose up from the couch of yoga.

children.text: vīryaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ devo māyayā vyasṛjat tridhā ||
children.translated_text: The god, through <s>māyā</s>, sent forth golden generative power in three ways.
The Lord made it the presiding divine, the inner self, and the element-based principle.
Now hear how that single power belonging to the <s>Puruṣa</s> was divided threefold.
From the space within the body of the <s>Puruṣa</s> as he stirred,

children.text: ojaḥ saho balaṃ jajñe tataḥ prāṇo mahān asuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Energy, vigor, and strength were born; then came <s>prāṇa</s>, the great life-breath.
The breaths breathe after him, while he breathes among all living beings,
and while he exhales, they exhale after him, like followers after a king among men.
When hunger and thirst arose within the mighty Lord, as <s>prāṇa</s> stirred him,
then, as he thirsted and wished to eat, the mouth first opened.
From the mouth the palate was opened, and the tongue arose there.
From that arose the many kinds of taste, which are apprehended by the tongue.
From the mouth of the Vast One, desiring to speak, came fire, speech, and utterance for the two of them;
and in water there arose a long restraint of this power.
The two nostrils were opened when the wind was being shaken forth.
There arose the odor-bearing wind, and smell in the nose, for him who wished to smell.
When, in himself, there was no illumination, and he wished to see himself,
his two eyes were opened; then light and sight arose, grasping visible qualities.
When the self was being awakened by the seers and wished to grasp that knowledge,

children.text: karṇau ca nirabhidyetāṃ diśaḥ śrotraṃ guṇagrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the two ears were opened; the directions and hearing arose, grasping sound qualities.
When he wished to apprehend the softness, hardness, lightness, heaviness, heat, and cold
of an object, the skin was opened; in it hairs and plants arose.
There, both the inner and outer wind, endowed with its quality through touch, was enclosed.
His two hands grew forth from his desire to perform various actions.
In them arose mighty <s>Indra</s>; taking and grasping had both as their support.
His two feet grew forth when he wished to obtain the desired movement.

children.text: padbhyāṃ yajñaḥ svayaṃ havyaṃ karmabhiḥ kriyate nṛbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the feet, <s>Yajña</s> himself became the oblation, which human beings perform through their rites.
The generative organ was opened for him who sought the immortal delight of progeny.
The organ of generation arose, the beloved object of desires, with both as its support.
For him who wished to expel the impurity of the bodily constituents, the anus was opened.
From that came the organ of evacuation; then <s>Mitra</s> arose, and excretion had both as its support.
For him who, through the downward breath, wished to move out from the city of the body, the navel-door opened.
There arose <s>apāna</s>; then came <s>Mṛtyu</s>, and separation had both as its support.
When he wished to take in food and drink, the belly, intestines, and channels came into being.
The rivers and oceans arose; satisfaction and nourishment had those two as their supports.
When he wished to contemplate his own <s>māyā</s>, the heart opened.

children.text: tato manaścandra iti saṅkalpaḥ kāma eva ca ||
children.translated_text: From that came the mind and the moon; also resolve and desire.
Skin, hide, flesh, blood, fat, marrow, bone, and the bodily constituents
are seven, made of earth, water, and fire; <s>prāṇa</s> is made through space, water, and wind.
The senses consist of the <s>guṇas</s>; the <s>guṇas</s> arise from the elemental principle.
The mind has the nature of all modifications, and intellect has the form of discernment.

children.text: etadbhagavato rūpaṃ sthūlaṃ te vyāhṛtaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: This gross form of the Blessed Lord has been described to you by me,
externally enclosed by the eight coverings, beginning with earth.
Beyond this is the subtlest, unmanifest, without distinguishing attributes,
without beginning, middle, or end, eternal, beyond speech and mind.
These two forms of the Blessed Lord have been described to you by me.

children.text: ubhe api na gṛhṇanti māyāsṛṣṭe vipaścitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wise people accept neither of them as ultimate, for they are created by <s>māyā</s>.
That Blessed Lord, bearing the form of <s>brahman</s> as both word and meaning,
assumes name, form, and action; though connected with action, he is beyond action.

children.text: prajāpatīn manūn devān ṛṣīn pitṛgaṇān pṛthak
children.translated_text: He assumes the <s>Prajāpatis</s>, the <s>Manus</s>, the gods, the seers, and the hosts of ancestors separately,
the <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Guhyakas</s>,
the <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, serpents, <s>Kimpuruṣas</s>, and human beings,
the Mothers, <s>Rakṣases</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, ghosts, spirits, and <s>Vināyakas</s>,
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, mad spirits, <s>Vetālas</s>, <s>Yātudhānas</s>, and also seizing spirits,

children.text: khagān mṛgān paśūn vṛkṣān girīn nṛpasarīsṛpān ||
children.translated_text: birds, wild animals, domestic animals, trees, mountains, reptiles, O king,
and the others, of two kinds and four kinds, dwelling in water, on land, and in the sky.
These are the auspicious, inauspicious, and mixed destinies of actions.
<s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are the three; they are divine, human, and hellish.
Even there, O king, the destinies are divided threefold in each individual case,
when the nature of any one of them is overpowered by the other two.
He alone, the Blessed Lord, the sustainer of the world, bearing the form of <s>dharma</s>,
nourishes the universe and keeps it established through animals, human beings, gods, and the rest.

children.text: tataḥ kālāgnirudrātmā yat sṛṣṭam idam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, as time, fire, and <s>Rudra</s>, he draws in what he himself has created,
at the proper time, like the wind drawing together a mass of clouds.
In this manner the most blessed Lord has been described according to such modes of being;

children.text: netthambhāvena hi paraṃ draṣṭum arhanti sūrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the wise are not able to see the Supreme in such modes of being.
No real action, such as birth and the rest, is ascribed to that transcendent one.
It is superimposed by <s>māyā</s> in order to deny actual agency.

children.text: ayaṃ tu brahmaṇaḥ kalpaḥ savikalpa udāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: This, then, has been stated as the <s>kalpa</s> of <s>Brahmā</s>, with its differentiations,
in which the common rule applies to the primary and secondary creations.
The measure of time and the form characterized by the <s>kalpa</s>

children.text: yathā purastādvyākhyāsye pādmaṃ kalpam atho śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: I shall explain later, as before; now hear the <s>Pādma</s> <s>kalpa</s>.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: yadāha no bhavān sūta kṣattā bhāgavatottamaḥ
children.translated_text: What you told us, O <s>Sūta</s>, was that the chamberlain, the foremost devotee of the Blessed Lord,
wandered over the sacred places of the earth, having abandoned kinsmen very hard to abandon.
The dialogue of that chamberlain with <s>Kauśārava</s> rested on the inner self,

children.text: yadvā sa bhagavāṃstasmai pṛṣṭastattvam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: or rather, when the blessed one was questioned by him, he told him the truth.
Tell us this, gentle one: the conduct of <s>Vidura</s>,
and the reason for his abandonment of his kinsmen, and also how he returned again.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
What the great sage said when asked by King <s>Parīkṣit</s>,
that I shall tell you; listen, in accordance with the king's questions.
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: evam etat purā pṛṣṭo maitreyo bhagavān kila
children.translated_text: So indeed, long ago, the blessed <s>Maitreya</s> was asked

children.text: kṣattrā vanaṃ praviṣṭena tyaktvā svagṛham ṛddhimat ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Vidura</s> had entered the forest, abandoning his prosperous home.

children.text: yad vā ayaṃ mantrakṛd vo bhagavān akhileśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Or why did this blessed lord, the counselor for you all, the lord of all,
leave the house of the king of the Pauravas and enter a state made his own?
The king said:
Where did <s>Vidura</s> have his meeting with the blessed <s>Maitreya</s>,

children.text: kadā vā sahasaṃvāda etad varṇaya naḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: and when did their conversation take place? Describe this to us, lord.
For the question of that pure-hearted <s>Vidura</s> could not have only a small result,
when it was put to that most excellent one and was strengthened by the approval of the good.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: sa evam ṛṣivaryo 'yaṃ pṛṣṭo rājñā parīkṣitā
children.translated_text: Thus questioned by King <s>Parīkṣit</s>, this best of seers,

children.text: praty āha taṃ subahuvit prītātmā śrūyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: very learned and pleased in heart, answered him, saying, "Listen."
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: yadā tu rājā svasutān asādhūn puṣṇan na dharmeṇa vinaṣṭadṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: When the king, his sight ruined, nourished his wicked sons contrary to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: bhrātur yaviṣṭhasya sutān vibandhūn praveśya lākṣābhavane dadāha ||
children.translated_text: and burned the sons of his youngest brother, bereft of allies, after making them enter the house of lac;

children.text: yadā sabhāyāṃ kurudevadevyāḥ keśābhimarśaṃ sutakarma garhyam
children.translated_text: when, in the assembly, he did not restrain his son's reprehensible act, the seizing of the hair

children.text: na vārayāmāsa nṛpaḥ snuṣāyāḥ svāsrair harantyāḥ kucakuṅkumāni ||
children.translated_text: of the queen of the Kuru lords, his daughter-in-law, as her tears washed away the saffron from her breasts;

children.text: dyūte tv adharmeṇa jitasya sādhoḥ satyāvalambasya vanaṃ gatasya
children.translated_text: when <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, a righteous man who held fast to truth, had been defeated by unlawful gambling and gone to the forest,

children.text: na yācato 'dāt samayena dāyaṃ tamojuṣāṇo yad ajātaśatroḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, though he asked for it, the king, delighting in darkness, did not give him his share at the agreed time;

children.text: yadā ca pārthaprahitaḥ sabhāyāṃ jagadgurur yāni jagāda kṛṣṇaḥ
children.translated_text: and when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, sent by <s>Pārtha</s>, spoke in the assembly those words

children.text: na tāni puṃsām amṛtāyanāni rājoru mene kṣatapuṇyaleśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that were nectar for human beings, the king, whose last trace of merit was destroyed, did not value them;

children.text: yadopahūto bhavanaṃ praviṣṭo mantrāya pṛṣṭaḥ kila pūrvajena
children.translated_text: when he had been summoned, had entered the palace, and was asked for counsel by his elder brother,

children.text: athāha tan mantradṛśāṃ varīyān yan mantriṇo vaidurikaṃ vadanti ||
children.translated_text: then that foremost of seers of counsel spoke what ministers call the counsel of <s>Vidura</s>.

children.text: ajātaśatroḥ pratiyaccha dāyaṃ titikṣato durviṣahaṃ tavāgaḥ
children.translated_text: "Return <s>Ajātaśatru</s>'s share to him, for he has endured your unbearable offense.

children.text: sahānujo yatra vṛkodarāhiḥ śvasan ruṣā yat tvam alaṃ bibheṣi ||
children.translated_text: There, together with his younger brothers, is the serpent <s>Vṛkodara</s>, breathing in anger, because of whom you are rightly afraid.

children.text: pārthāṃs tu devo bhagavān mukundo gṛhītavān sakṣitidevadevaḥ
children.translated_text: The blessed god <s>Mukunda</s>, lord of gods among rulers on earth, has taken the <s>Pārthas</s> under his protection,
and he dwells in his own city, the god of the Yadu lords, having conquered all kings without remainder.

children.text: sa eṣa doṣaḥ puruṣadviḍ āste gṛhān praviṣṭo yam apatyamatyā
children.translated_text: This fault, this hater of men, has entered your house, and you nurture him with the thought that he is your son.

children.text: puṣṇāsi kṛṣṇād vimukho gataśrīs tyajāśv aśaivaṃ kulakauśalāya ||
children.translated_text: Turned away from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and bereft of fortune, abandon this inauspicious one at once for the welfare of the family."
When he had spoken thus, <s>Vidura</s>, whose character was desired by the good, was insulted there by <s>Suyodhana</s>,
whose lips quivered with swelling anger, along with <s>Karṇa</s>, his brothers, and <s>Saubala</s>.

children.text: ka enam atropajuhāva jihmaṃ dāsyāḥ sutaṃ yadbalinaiva puṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: "Who invited this crooked son of a maidservant here, fed only by the food of the one whose strength he enjoys?

children.text: tasmin pratīpaḥ parakṛtya āste nirvāsyatām āśu purāc chvasānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since he stands here hostile, doing the work of enemies, let him be driven quickly from the city, breathing heavily."

children.text: svayaṃ dhanur dvāri nidhāya māyāṃ bhrātuḥ puro marmasu tāḍito 'pi
children.translated_text: Laying his bow at the door by himself, and though struck in his vital parts in his brother's presence,

children.text: sa ittham atyulbaṇakarṇabāṇair gatavyatho 'yād uru mānayānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he felt no pain from those extremely fierce arrows to the ear and went away, honoring the great Lord.

children.text: sa nirgataḥ kauravapuṇyalabdho gajāhvayāt tīrthapadaḥ padāni
children.translated_text: Having gone out from <s>Gajāhvaya</s>, obtained by the merit of the Kurus, he followed on earth
the holy footprints of the Lord whose feet are places of pilgrimage, which <s>Sahasramūrti</s> had established out of the wish to make the earth holy.
In cities, sacred groves, mountain bowers, clear-water rivers, and lakes,
in sanctuaries adorned with countless emblems of the Infinite, he wandered, undistracted.
Roaming the earth with a pure and solitary way of living, always bathed, sleeping on the ground, and detached,

children.text: alakṣitaḥ svair avadhūtaveṣo vratāni cere haritoṣaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: unrecognized by his own people and moving freely in the garb of an <s>avadhūta</s> (renunciant), he practiced vows pleasing to <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: itthaṃ vrajan bhāratam eva varṣaṃ kālena yāvad gatavān prabhāsam
children.translated_text: As he thus traveled through <s>Bhārata-varṣa</s>, when in time he had reached <s>Prabhāsa</s>,

children.text: tāvac chaśāsa kṣitim eka cakrāml ekātapatrām ajitena pārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by then <s>Pārtha</s>, aided by <s>Ajita</s>, ruled the earth as one realm under a single parasol.

children.text: tatrātha śuśrāva suhṛdvinaṣṭiṃ vanaṃ yathā veṇujavahnisaṃśrayam
children.translated_text: There he heard of the destruction of his friends, like a bamboo forest consumed by fire born from bamboo,

children.text: saṃspardhayā dagdham athānuśocan sarasvatīṃ pratyag iyāya tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: burned by rivalry; then, lamenting, he silently went westward toward the <s>Sarasvatī</s>.

children.text: tasyāṃ tritasyośanaso manoś ca pṛthor athāgner asitasya vāyoḥ
children.translated_text: On that river he visited the tīrthas (sacred fords) of <s>Trita</s>, <s>Uśanas</s>, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Asita</s>, and <s>Vāyu</s>,

children.text: tīrthaṃ sudāsasya gavāṃ guhasya yac chrāddhadevasya sa āsiṣeve ||
children.translated_text: and those of <s>Sudāsa</s>, the Cows, <s>Guha</s>, and <s>Śrāddhadeva</s>.

children.text: anyāni ceha dvijadevadevaiḥ kṛtāni nānāyatanāni viṣṇoḥ
children.translated_text: And he visited other various abodes of <s>Viṣṇu</s> established here by twice-born sages and gods of gods,
temples marked on every side with chief signs, by seeing which people remember <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: tatas tv ativrajya surāṣṭram ṛddhaṃ sauvīramatsyān kurujāṅgalāṃś ca
children.translated_text: Then, crossing beyond prosperous <s>Surāṣṭra</s>, <s>Sauvīra</s>, <s>Matsya</s>, and the <s>Kurujāṅgala</s> lands,

children.text: kālena tāvad yamunām upetya tatroddhavaṃ bhāgavataṃ dadarśa ||
children.translated_text: in time he came to the <s>Yamunā</s>, and there he saw <s>Uddhava</s>, a devotee of the Blessed Lord.

children.text: sa vāsudevānucaraṃ praśāntaṃ bṛhaspateḥ prāk tanayaṃ pratītam
children.translated_text: He embraced tightly and with affection the serene attendant of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, renowned formerly as a son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: āliṅgya gāḍhaṃ praṇayena bhadraṃ svānām apṛcchad bhagavatprajānām ||
children.translated_text: and asked that good man about the welfare of his own people, the people of the Blessed Lord.
"Are the two ancient <s>Puruṣas</s>, who descended here in accord with the lotus-born one from their own navel,

children.text: āsāta urvyāḥ kuśalaṃ vidhāya kṛtakṣaṇau kuśalaṃ śūragehe ||
children.translated_text: well in the house of <s>Śūra</s>, having secured the earth's welfare and made the time auspicious?

children.text: kaccit kurūṇāṃ paramaḥ suhṛn no bhāmaḥ sa āste sukham aṅga śauriḥ
children.translated_text: Dear one, is <s>Śauri</s>, our supreme friend among the Kurus, dwelling happily,

children.text: yo vai svasṇāṃ pitṛvad dadāti varān vadānyo varatarpaṇena ||
children.translated_text: the generous one who, like a father to his sisters, grants chosen boons by satisfying them with gifts?

children.text: kaccid varūthādhipatir yadūnāṃ pradyumna āste sukham aṅga vīraḥ
children.translated_text: Dear hero, is <s>Pradyumna</s>, commander of the Yadus' army, dwelling happily,

children.text: yaṃ rukmiṇī bhagavato 'bhilebhe ārādhya viprān smaram ādisarge ||
children.translated_text: whom <s>Rukmiṇī</s> obtained from the Blessed Lord, after worshiping the brāhmans, as <s>Smara</s> at the first creation?

children.text: kaccit sukhaṃ sātvatavṛṣṇibhojadāśārhakāṇām adhipaḥ sa āste
children.translated_text: Is the lord of the <s>Sātvatas</s>, <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, <s>Bhojas</s>, and <s>Dāśārhas</s> dwelling happily,

children.text: yam abhyaṣiñcac chatapattranetro nṛpāsanāśāṃ parihṛtya dūrāt ||
children.translated_text: whom the lotus-eyed one anointed after putting far away the hope for a royal throne?

children.text: kacciddhareḥ saumya sutaḥ sadṛkṣa āste 'graṇī rathināṃ sādhu sāmbaḥ
children.translated_text: Gentle one, is <s>Sāmba</s>, the son of <s>Hari</s>, resembling him and foremost among chariot-warriors, doing well?

children.text: asūta yaṃ jāmbavatī vratāḍhyā devaṃ guhaṃ yo 'mbikayā dhṛto 'gre ||
children.translated_text: whom <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, rich in vows, bore, the god <s>Guha</s>, who had previously been carried by <s>Ambikā</s>.

children.text: kṣemaṃ sa kaccid yuyudhāna āste yaḥ phālgunāl labdhadhanūrahasyaḥ
children.translated_text: Is <s>Yuyudhāna</s> well, he who obtained from <s>Phālguna</s> the secret of the bow,
and who easily, through service to <s>Adhokṣaja</s> alone, attained that goal of his which is hard for ascetics to reach?

children.text: kaccid budhaḥ svasty anamīva āste śvaphalkaputro bhagavatprapannaḥ
children.translated_text: Is the wise son of <s>Śvaphalka</s>, surrendered to the Blessed Lord, living safely and without illness,
he who rolled in the dust of the road marked by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet, his composure broken by love?

children.text: kaccic chivaṃ devakabhojaputryā viṣṇuprajāyā iva devamātuḥ
children.translated_text: Is all auspicious with <s>Devakī</s>, daughter of <s>Devakabhoja</s>, the mother of the god, like the mother of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s offspring,

children.text: yā vai svagarbheṇa dadhāra devaṃ trayī yathā yajñavitānam artham ||
children.translated_text: she who indeed bore the Lord in her own womb, as the threefold Veda bears the meaning, the full expanse of sacrifice?

children.text: apisvid āste bhagavān sukhaṃ vo yaḥ sātvatāṃ kāmadugho 'niruddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Is your Blessed Lord <s>Aniruddha</s>, the wish-fulfilling cow of the <s>Sātvatas</s>, dwelling happily,

children.text: yam āmananti sma hi śabdayoniṃ manomayaṃ sattvaturīyatattvam ||
children.translated_text: whom they indeed call the source of sound, mind-made, the fourth principle of pure being?

children.text: apisvid anye ca nijātmadaivam ananyavṛttyā samanuvratā ye
children.translated_text: And are the others, who with undivided devotion are wholly vowed to the deity who is their own Self,
<s>Hṛdīka</s>, the son of <s>Satyā</s>, <s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>, <s>Gada</s>, and the rest, faring well, gentle one?

children.text: api svadorbhyāṃ vijayācyutābhyāṃ dharmeṇa dharmaḥ paripāti setum
children.translated_text: Does <s>Dharma</s>, with his two arms, <s>Vijaya</s> and <s>Acyuta</s>, protect the boundary of dharma by dharma,
he in whose assembly <s>Duryodhana</s> burned with envy at the fortune of empire and the attendance of <s>Vijaya</s>?

children.text: kiṃ vā kṛtāgheṣv agham atyamarṣī bhīmo 'hivad dīrghatamaṃ vyamuñcat
children.translated_text: Or did <s>Bhīma</s>, intolerant toward those who had sinned, pour out his long-held wrath upon the guilty like a serpent,

children.text: yasyāṅghripātaṃ raṇabhūr na sehe mārgaṃ gadāyāś carato vicitram ||
children.translated_text: whose footfall the battlefield could not bear as he moved along the wondrous path of his mace?
Is the famed archer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, the chief of chariot-warriors whose enemies were laid low, living well,
he who, hidden unnoticed beneath a mass of arrows, pleased <s>Giriśa</s> when he appeared as the deceptive <s>Kirāta</s>?

children.text: yamāv utasvit tanayau pṛthāyāḥ pārthair vṛtau pakṣmabhir akṣiṇīva
children.translated_text: And are the twins, the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>, guarded by the <s>Pārthas</s> as eyelids guard the eyes,

children.text: remāta uddāya mṛdhe svarikthaṃ parāt suparṇāv iva vajrivaktrāt ||
children.translated_text: delighting after seizing back their inheritance in battle from the enemy, like two <s>Suparṇa</s>s from the mouth of <s>Vajrin</s>?

children.text: aho pṛthāpi dhriyate 'rbhakārthe rājarṣivaryeṇa vināpi tena
children.translated_text: Ah, does <s>Pṛthā</s> still live for the sake of her children, even without that best of royal sages,

children.text: yas tv ekavīro 'dhiratho vijigye dhanur dvitīyaḥ kakubhaś catasraḥ ||
children.translated_text: who, a single hero on his chariot, conquered the four quarters with his bow as his only second?

children.text: saumyānuśoce tam adhaḥpatantaṃ bhrātre paretāya vidudruhe yaḥ
children.translated_text: Gentle one, I grieve for that man as he falls downward, he who betrayed his brother after death,

children.text: niryāpito yena suhṛt svapuryā ahaṃ svaputrān samanuvratena ||
children.translated_text: by whom I, a well-wisher, was driven from my own city, while he followed the will of his sons.

children.text: so 'haṃ harer martyaviḍambanena dṛśo nṛṇāṃ cālayato vidhātuḥ
children.translated_text: So I, by the grace of <s>Hari</s>, who through his imitation of mortal life bewildered the vision of men and of the creator,

children.text: nānyopalakṣyaḥ padavīṃ prasādāc carāmi paśyan gatavismayo 'tra ||
children.translated_text: walk here along his path, seeing it, beyond wonder, though it is not recognized by others.

children.text: nūnaṃ nṛpāṇāṃ trimadotpathānāṃ mahīṃ muhuś cālayatāṃ camūbhiḥ
children.translated_text: Surely the Blessed Lord, though the kings had strayed from the path through triple intoxication and were repeatedly shaking the earth with armies,
overlooked the sin of the <s>Kurus</s>, because he wished, through their slaughter, to remove the distress of those who had sought refuge.

children.text: ajasya janmotpathanāśanāya karmāṇy akartur grahaṇāya puṃsām
