children.translated_text: The birth of the unborn is for the destruction of those who have gone astray; the actions of the actionless are for drawing human beings to himself.

children.text: nanv anyathā ko 'rhati dehayogaṃ paro guṇānām uta karmatantram ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, who, being beyond the <s>guṇas</s> and the machinery of karma, would deserve connection with a body?
Of him, before whom all the protectors of the worlds have surrendered and who stands firm in his own command,

children.text: arthāya jātasya yaduṣv ajasya vārttāṃ sakhe kīrtaya tīrthakīrteḥ ||
children.translated_text: who, though unborn, was born among the <s>Yadus</s> for their welfare, tell me the news, my friend, of him whose fame sanctifies sacred places.
Śrī <s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: iti bhāgavataḥ pṛṣṭaḥ kṣattrā vārttāṃ priyāśrayām
children.translated_text: Thus questioned by the <s>Bhāgavata</s>, by the <s>kṣattṛ</s>, about news connected with his beloved refuge,
he could not bring himself to answer, because in his longing he had been reminded of the Lord.
He who, when five years old, was asked by his mother for his morning meal,

children.text: tan naicchad racayan yasya saparyāṃ bālalīlayā ||
children.translated_text: did not want it, because in childish play he was arranging worship for him.

children.text: sa kathaṃ sevayā tasya kālena jarasaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: How then could he, grown old in time through service to him,

children.text: pṛṣṭo vārttāṃ pratibrūyād bhartuḥ pādāv anusmaran ||
children.translated_text: when asked, reply with news of his master while remembering his feet?

children.text: sa muhūrtam abhūt tūṣṇīṃ kṛṣṇāṅghrisudhayā bhṛśam
children.translated_text: For a moment he remained silent, deeply immersed in the nectar of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet,
and through intense <s>bhakti-yoga</s> he was fully absorbed and wholly satisfied.
With every limb bristling in horripilation, shedding tears from half-closed eyes,
he was seen by him as one whose purpose was fulfilled, flooded by a surge of affection.
Slowly he returned again from the worlds of the Blessed Lord to the world of men;
wiping his eyes, <s>Uddhava</s>, smiling, spoke to <s>Vidura</s> with affection.
<s>Uddhava</s> said:
When the sun that was <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had set and our houses had been swallowed by the great python,

children.text: kiṃ nu naḥ kuśalaṃ brūyāṃ gataśrīṣu gṛheṣv aham ||
children.translated_text: what welfare can I speak of for us, I whose homes have lost their splendor?

children.text: durbhago bata loko 'yaṃ yadavo nitarām api
children.translated_text: Unfortunate indeed is this world, and the <s>Yadus</s> most of all,

children.text: ye saṃvasanto na vidur hariṃ mīnā ivoḍupam ||
children.translated_text: who, though living together with <s>Hari</s>, did not know him, like fish that do not know the moon.
Skilled in reading signs, very mature, and sharing one delight, the <s>Sātvatas</s>
all regarded the bull of the <s>Sātvatas</s>, the abode of beings, as one of their own.

children.text: devasya māyayā spṛṣṭā ye cānyad asadāśritāḥ
children.translated_text: Those others who were touched by the god's <s>māyā</s> depended on what was unreal;

children.text: bhrāmyate dhīr na tadvākyair ātmany uptātmano harau ||
children.translated_text: the understanding of those whose selves were planted in <s>Hari</s> within was not made to wander by their words.
Having shown to men whose austerities were not yet heated and whose eyes were unsated

children.text: ādāyāntar adhād yas tu svabimbaṃ lokalocanam ||
children.translated_text: his own image, the object of the world's eyes, he took it away and disappeared within.
That form which he assumed, suitable for mortal play and displaying the power of his own <s>yogamāyā</s>,

children.text: vismāpanaṃ svasya ca saubhagarddheḥ paraṃ padaṃ bhūṣaṇabhūṣaṇāṅgam ||
children.translated_text: was a cause of wonder, a supreme state, its limbs adorning the very ornaments, born from the abundance of his own beauty.

children.text: yad dharmasūnor bata rājasūye nirīkṣya dṛksvastyayanaṃ trilokaḥ
children.translated_text: When, at the <s>Rājasūya</s> of <s>Dharmasūnu</s>, the three worlds beheld him, a blessing to the eyes,

children.text: kārtsnyena cādyeha gataṃ vidhātur arvāksṛtau kauśalam ity amanyata ||
children.translated_text: they thought that here, today, the creator's skill in later creation had come to complete perfection.
The women of <s>Vraja</s>, their pride regained through the glances of his love-flooded, laughing <s>rāsa</s>-play,
stood still, their minds following him through their eyes, as though their tasks remained unfinished.
Though he is worshiped in his own peaceful forms and in other forms, his self was moved by compassion;

children.text: parāvareśo mahadaṃśayukto hy ajo 'pi jāto bhagavān yathāgniḥ ||
children.translated_text: the unborn Blessed Lord, joined with a portion of the Great One and lord of higher and lower, was born like fire.

children.text: māṃ khedayaty etad ajasya janmaviḍambanaṃ yad vasudevagehe
children.translated_text: This pains me: the unborn one's mockery of birth, that he was born in the house of <s>Vasudeva</s>,

children.text: vraje ca vāso 'ribhayād iva svayaṃ purād vyavātsīd yadanantavīryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and dwelt in <s>Vraja</s>, as if from fear of enemies, he whose power is endless, when he had gone away from his own city.

children.text: dunoti cetaḥ smarato mamaitad yad āha pādāv abhivandya pitroḥ
children.translated_text: And this torments my heart when I remember what he said after bowing down to the feet of his parents:
"Father, mother, please forgive us, who were deeply afraid of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and have not repaid our debt to you."

children.text: ko vā amuṣyāṅghrisarojareṇuṃ vismartum īśīta pumān vijighran
children.translated_text: What person could be able to forget the dust from the lotus of his feet, once he had breathed it in,

children.text: yo visphuradbhrūviṭapena bhūmer bhāraṃ kṛtāntena tiraścakāra ||
children.translated_text: of him who, by the deathlike movement of the branching line of his eyebrow, removed the burden of the earth?

children.text: dṛṣṭā bhavadbhir nanu rājasūye caidyasya kṛṣṇaṃ dviṣato 'pi siddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Surely you saw, at the <s>rājasūya</s> (royal consecration), the perfection attained by <s>Caidya</s>, though he hated <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: yāṃ yoginaḥ saṃspṛhayanti samyag yogena kas tadvirahaṃ saheta ||
children.translated_text: a perfection for which yogins yearn through full discipline; who could endure separation from him?

children.text: tathaiva cānye naralokavīrā ya āhave kṛṣṇamukhāravindam
children.translated_text: Likewise other heroes in the world of men, who in battle drank with their eyes the lotus of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s face,

children.text: netraiḥ pibanto nayanābhirāmaṃ pārthāstrapūtaḥ padam āpur asya ||
children.translated_text: delighting the eyes, and who were purified by <s>Pārtha</s>'s weapons, attained his abode.
Yet he himself is without equal or superior, lord of the three worlds, with every desire fulfilled by the splendor of his own sovereignty,
his footstool praised by the tips of the crowns of the ancient world-protectors who bring him tribute.

children.text: tat tasya kaiṃkaryam alaṃ bhṛtān no viglāpayaty aṅga yad ugrasenam
children.translated_text: And that servant-like attendance of his quite overwhelms us servants, dear one: he stood before <s>Ugrasena</s>,

children.text: tiṣṭhan niṣaṇṇaṃ parameṣṭhidhiṣṇye nyabodhayad deva nidhārayeti ||
children.translated_text: who was seated on the throne of the highest lord, and instructed him, "O king, please take heed."

children.text: aho bakī yaṃ stanakālakūṭaṃ jighāṃsayāpāyayad apy asādhvī
children.translated_text: Ah! Wicked <s>Bakī</s>, who with murderous intent made him drink the deadly poison on her breast,

children.text: lebhe gatiṃ dhātryucitāṃ tato 'nyaṃ kaṃ vā dayāluṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajema ||
children.translated_text: received the state proper to a nurse. To what other merciful one, then, could we go for refuge?
I think the asuras were devotees of the lord of the three worlds, their minds fixed by the path of hostile fury,

children.text: ye saṃyuge 'cakṣata tārkṣyaputram aṃse sunābhāyudham āpatantam ||
children.translated_text: for in battle they saw the son of <s>Tārkṣya</s> descending on his shoulder, and the weapon with the bright hub.
The Blessed Lord was born from <s>Devakī</s> in <s>Vasudeva</s>'s line, in the prison of the lord of the <s>Bhojas</s>,
wishing to bring welfare to this earth, after he had been entreated by the unborn one.

children.text: tato nandavrajam itaḥ pitrā kaṃsād vibibhyatā
children.translated_text: Then, through his father who feared <s>Kaṃsa</s>, he went from there to <s>Nanda</s>'s <s>Vraja</s>,
and there, his radiance hidden, he lived for eleven years together with <s>Bala</s>.

children.text: parīto vatsapair vatsāṃś cārayan vyaharad vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by cowherd boys, the all-pervading Lord sported as he grazed the calves
in a grove beside the <s>Yamunā</s>, where the trees were filled with chattering birds.
Displaying childish acts that were delightful to the people of <s>Vraja</s>,
he seemed to cry, laughed, and looked on with the innocent gaze of a young lion.

children.text: sa eva godhanaṃ lakṣmyā niketaṃ sitagovṛṣam
children.translated_text: That very Lord, while grazing the wealth of cows, the abode of prosperity, with white bulls,
delighted the cowherds who followed him, as his flute resounded.
The magic-working, shape-shifting demons sent by the king of the <s>Bhojas</s>,

children.text: līlayā vyanudat tāṃs tān bālaḥ krīḍanakān iva ||
children.translated_text: the child drove away one after another in play, as if they were toys.
When the cows had fallen by drinking poison, he subdued the lord of serpents,
raised the cows up, and made them drink that water after it had been restored to its natural state.
The Lord had the cowherd king perform the <s>gosava</s> sacrifice with the best of twice-born priests,
wishing to make a good use of the great burden of wealth.
When <s>Indra</s>, angry, was raining and <s>Vraja</s> was in great distress as his pride was broken,
it was protected by the mountain used as a playful parasol, as he bestowed favor on the good.
Honoring the opening of the night, polished by the rays of the autumn moon,
he sang melodious words and sported as the ornament of the circle of women.
<s>Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ sa āgatya puraṃ svapitroś cikīrṣayā śaṃ baladevasaṃyutaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he came to the city together with <s>Baladeva</s>, wishing to bring welfare to his own parents,

children.text: nipātya tuṅgād ripuyūthanāthaṃ hataṃ vyakarṣad vyasum ojasorvyām ||
children.translated_text: and, casting down the chief of the enemy host from his lofty place, dragged him lifeless over the ground by his strength.
After studying in full from <s>Sāṃdīpani</s> the sacred knowledge once it had been spoken only once,

children.text: tasmai prādād varaṃ putraṃ mṛtaṃ pañcajanodarāt ||
children.translated_text: he gave him, as his chosen gift, his dead son from the belly of <s>Pañcajana</s>.

children.text: samāhutā bhīṣmakakanyayā ye śriyaḥ savarṇena bubhūṣayaiṣām
children.translated_text: The kings who had been summoned for <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>'s daughter, she who was equal in beauty to <s>Śrī</s>,

children.text: gāndharvavṛttyā miṣatāṃ svabhāgaṃ jahre padaṃ mūrdhni dadhat suparṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he robbed of his own share by the <s>gāndharva</s> rite while they looked on, setting his foot on their heads like <s>Suparṇa</s>.
After taming the humped bulls whose noses had not been pierced, he married <s>Nāgnajitī</s> at her self-choice ceremony;

children.text: tadbhagnamānān api gṛdhyato 'jñāñ jaghne 'kṣataḥ śastrabhṛtaḥ svaśastraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he, unharmed, slew with his own weapons the foolish weapon-bearers who still desired her though their pride was broken.

children.text: priyaṃ prabhur grāmya iva priyāyā vidhitsur ārcchad dyutaruṃ yadarthe
children.translated_text: Wishing to do what was dear for his beloved, like an ordinary man for his dear wife, the Lord seized the heavenly tree for her sake;

children.text: vajry ādravat taṃ sagaṇo ruṣāndhaḥ krīḍāmṛgo nūnam ayaṃ vadhūnām ||
children.translated_text: then the wielder of the thunderbolt, blind with anger, rushed at him with his hosts. Surely this one was the plaything of his brides.

children.text: sutaṃ mṛdhe khaṃ vapuṣā grasantaṃ dṛṣṭvā sunābhonmathitaṃ dharitryā
children.translated_text: Seeing in battle the son of the earth, whose body seemed to swallow the sky, crushed by his discus,

children.text: āmantritas tattanayāya śeṣaṃ dattvā tadantaḥpuram āviveśa ||
children.translated_text: he was invited by the earth, gave what remained to that demon's son, and entered his inner palace.

children.text: tatrāhṛtās tā naradevakanyāḥ kujena dṛṣṭvā harim ārtabandhum
children.translated_text: There those daughters of kings, carried off by <s>Kuja</s>, saw <s>Hari</s>, the kinsman of the distressed,
and at once rose up and accepted him with glances sent forth by joy, modesty, and love.
In a single moment, in the many separate houses of those women,
he took their hands in due form, assuming fitting forms by his own <s>māyā</s>.
In them he begot sons equal to himself in every respect,
ten in each woman, wishing to adorn manifest nature.
He himself struck down <s>Kālayavana</s>, <s>Māgadha</s>, <s>Śālva</s>, and others as they besieged the city with armies,

children.text: ajīghanat svayaṃ divyaṃ svapuṃsāṃ teja ādiśat ||
children.translated_text: and he assigned divine splendor to his own heroes.

children.text: śambaraṃ dvividaṃ bāṇaṃ muraṃ balvalam eva ca
children.translated_text: He slew <s>Śambara</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, <s>Mura</s>, and <s>Balvala</s> too,

children.text: anyāṃś ca dantavakrādīn avadhīt kāṃś ca ghātayat ||
children.translated_text: and others such as <s>Dantavakra</s>; some he caused to be killed.

children.text: atha te bhrātṛputrāṇāṃ pakṣayoḥ patitān nṛpān
children.translated_text: Then, when the kings had fallen on the two sides of your brother's sons,

children.text: cacāla bhūḥ kurukṣetraṃ yeṣām āpatatāṃ balaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the earth shook with the armies of those who were marching upon <s>Kurukṣetra</s>.
Seeing <s>Suyodhana</s>, whose fortune and life had been destroyed by the ripened evil counsel of <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, and <s>Saubala</s>,

children.text: suyodhanaṃ sānucaraṃ śayānaṃ bhagnorum ūrvyāṃ na nananda paśyan ||
children.translated_text: lying on the earth with his thighs broken, together with his followers, he did not rejoice.
How great now is this burden of the earth, although its heavy weight has been reduced by <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, and the others?

children.text: aṣṭādaśākṣauhiṇiko madaṃśair āste balaṃ durviṣahaṃ yadūnām ||
children.translated_text: For the unbearable army of the <s>Yadus</s>, eighteen akṣauhiṇīs strong and made up of my own portions, still remains.
When a quarrel among these men, their eyes copper-red from the intoxication of liquor, will arise among themselves,

children.text: naiṣāṃ vadhopāya iyān ato 'nyo mayy udyate 'ntardadhate svayaṃ sma ||
children.translated_text: there is no other means for their destruction so great as this; when I set it in motion, they themselves will disappear.

children.text: evaṃ saṃcintya bhagavān svarājye sthāpya dharmajam
children.translated_text: Having reflected in this way, the Blessed Lord established the son of <s>Dharma</s> in his own kingdom,
and he delighted his friends, showing the path of the good.
In <s>Uttarā</s> the lineage of <s>Pūru</s> was sustained through the noble <s>Abhimanyu</s>,

children.text: sa vai drauṇyastrasaṃpluṣṭaḥ punar bhagavatā dhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and though it had been scorched by the weapon of <s>Drauṇi</s>, it was again protected by the Blessed Lord.
The mighty Lord caused the son of <s>Dharma</s> to sacrifice with three horse-sacrifices,

children.text: so 'pi kṣmām anujai rakṣan reme kṛṣṇam anuvrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he too, protecting the earth with his younger brothers, rejoiced as one devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
The Blessed Lord also, the Self of the universe, following the paths of the world and the Veda,

children.text: kāmān siṣeve dvārvatyām asaktaḥ sāṃkhyam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: enjoyed pleasures in <s>Dvāravatī</s>, unattached and established in sāṃkhya (discriminating insight).
With his affectionate smiling glance, with speech like nectar,
with blameless conduct, and with his own person, the abode of splendor,

children.text: imaṃ lokam amuṃ caiva ramayan sutarāṃ yadūn
children.translated_text: he delighted this world and the other, and especially the <s>Yadus</s>;
he rejoiced through the nights, granting moments of affectionate glances to the women.
For him, thus rejoicing for many groups of years,
detachment arose toward household enjoyments.
When pleasures are ruled by fate, and the person himself is ruled by fate,
who would put trust in them, even by yoga, while devoted to the Lord of Yoga?
Once, in the city, the young princes of the <s>Yadus</s> and <s>Bhojas</s>, while playing,
angered sages, who knew the intention of the Blessed Lord, and the sages cursed them.
Then, after some months, the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, <s>Bhojas</s>, <s>Andhakas</s>, and the others,
joyfully went to <s>Prabhāsa</s> in chariots, bewildered by the gods.

children.text: tatra snātvā pitṝn devān ṛṣīṃś caiva tadambhasā
children.translated_text: There, after bathing, they satisfied their ancestors, the gods, and the seers with that water,
and then they gave many excellent cows to the brāhmans.
They gave gold, silver, beds, garments, deerskins, and blankets,

children.text: yānaṃ rathān ibhān kanyā dharāṃ vṛttikarīm api ||
children.translated_text: vehicles, chariots, elephants, maidens, and land that provided a livelihood as well.
After giving them abundant and well-flavored food as an offering to the Blessed Lord,
those heroes, whose very lives were for cows and brāhmans, bowed with their heads to the ground.
<s>Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: atha te tadanujñātā bhuktvā pītvā ca vāruṇīm
children.translated_text: Then, permitted by him, they ate and drank vāruṇī liquor,
and with their understanding overthrown by it, they struck one another's vital points with harsh words.
For them, whose minds had been made hostile by the fault of maireya liquor,

children.text: nimrocati ravāv āsīd veṇūnām iva mardanam ||
children.translated_text: as the sun was setting there was a crushing together like that of bamboos.

children.text: bhagavān svātmamāyāyā gatiṃ tām avalokya saḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord, seeing that course of his own māyā (power of manifestation),
sipped water from the <s>Sarasvatī</s> and sat down at the root of a tree.
And I too was told by the Blessed Lord, the remover of the distress of those who surrender:
'Go to <s>Badarī</s>,' for he wished to withdraw his own clan.
Even so, knowing what he intended, O subduer of foes,
I followed behind my master, unable to bear separation from his feet.

children.text: adrākṣam ekam āsīnaṃ vicinvan dayitaṃ patim
children.translated_text: Searching for my beloved lord, I saw him sitting alone,
the abode of splendor, beside the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, having made a resting place, yet himself without any fixed abode.
He was dark and pure, stainless, peaceful, with reddish eyes,
recognized by his four arms and by his yellow silk garment.
He had placed the lotus of his right foot upon his left thigh,
leaned against a young aśvattha tree, not emaciated, and had abandoned the pippala.
There a great devotee, the friend and companion of <s>Dvaipāyana</s>,
a perfected sage wandering through the worlds, arrived by chance.
To that devoted sage, whose neck was bowed in an emotion of joy, <s>Mukunda</s>,
while he listened, spoke; and with an affectionate smiling glance he gave me rest.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: vedāham antar manasīpsitaṃ te dadāmi yat tad duravāpam anyaiḥ
children.translated_text: I know the desire cherished within your mind; I shall give you what is difficult for others to obtain.

children.text: sattre purā viśvasṛjāṃ vasūnāṃ matsiddhikāmena vaso tvayeṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Long ago, in the sacrifice of the <s>Vasus</s>, among the creators of the universe, O <s>Vasu</s>, you worshiped me, desiring attainment of me.

children.text: sa eṣa sādho caramo bhavānām āsāditas te madanugraho yat
children.translated_text: O good man, this is your last birth; by my favor it has come to you,

children.text: yan māṃ nṛlokān raha utsṛjantaṃ diṣṭyā dadṛśvān viśadānuvṛttyā ||
children.translated_text: since, by good fortune, you have seen me in solitude as I leave the human worlds, through your pure devotion.

children.text: purā mayā proktam ajāya nābhye padme niṣaṇṇāya mamādisarge
children.translated_text: Formerly, at the beginning of my creation, I spoke to <s>Aja</s>, seated on the lotus from my navel,

children.text: jñānaṃ paraṃ manmahimāvabhāsaṃ yat sūrayo bhāgavataṃ vadanti ||
children.translated_text: the supreme knowledge that reveals my greatness, which the wise call the Bhāgavata.
Thus respectfully addressed by the Supreme Person, I, who received his favor at every moment,

children.text: snehottharomā skhalitākṣaras taṃ muñcañchucaḥ prāñjalir ābabhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: with hairs raised from affection and syllables faltering, spoke to him with folded hands, letting go of grief.

children.text: ko nv īśa te pādasarojabhājāṃ sudurlabho 'rtheṣu caturṣv apīha
children.translated_text: O Lord, for those who partake of your lotus feet, what among the four aims of life is truly hard to obtain here?
Even so, O Vast One, I do not choose them, for I am eager for service to the lotus of your feet.

children.text: karmāṇy anīhasya bhavo 'bhavasya te durgāśrayo 'thāribhayāt palāyanam
children.translated_text: Your deeds bewilder the understanding of the wise here: the birth of you who are birthless and desireless, your taking refuge in a fortress, and your flight from fear of enemies;

children.text: kālātmano yat pramadāyutāśramaḥ svātmanrateḥ khidyati dhīr vidām iha ||
children.translated_text: and the household life with ten thousand women of you who are the Self as Time and rejoice in your own self.

children.text: mantreṣu māṃ vā upahūya yat tvam akuṇṭhitākhaṇḍasadātmabodhaḥ
children.translated_text: In councils you would summon me, though your knowledge of the eternal self is unobstructed and undivided,

children.text: pṛccheḥ prabho mugdha ivāpramattas tan no mano mohayatīva deva ||
children.translated_text: and you would ask me, O Lord, like one bewildered though never inattentive; that seems to bewilder our mind, O God.

children.text: jñānaṃ paraṃ svātmarahaḥprakāśaṃ provāca kasmai bhagavān samagram
children.translated_text: To whom did the Blessed Lord speak in full the supreme knowledge that reveals the secret of the self?

children.text: api kṣamaṃ no grahaṇāya bhartar vadāñjasā yad vṛjinaṃ tarema ||
children.translated_text: If it is fit for us to receive, O Master, tell it plainly, by which we may cross over suffering.

children.text: ity āveditahārdāya mahyaṃ sa bhagavān paraḥ
children.translated_text: When I had thus revealed my heart, that supreme Blessed Lord,
the lotus-eyed one, instructed me in the highest state of the self.
I am he who, from the water that has washed his worshiped feet, learned the path of true self-awakening;

children.text: praṇamya pādau parivṛtya devam ihāgato 'haṃ virahāturātmā ||
children.translated_text: having bowed to the god's feet and circumambulated him, I have come here, my soul tormented by separation.
So I, joined with the joy of seeing him and the pain of separation from him, O lord,
shall go to his beloved region, the precinct of <s>Badaryāśrama</s>.

children.text: yatra nārāyaṇo devo naraś ca bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: There the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the blessed sage <s>Nara</s>,

children.text: mṛdu tīvraṃ tapo dīrghaṃ tepāte lokabhāvanau ||
children.translated_text: the benefactors of the worlds, perform gentle and severe austerity for a long time.
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: ity uddhavād upākarṇya suhṛdāṃ duḥsahaṃ vadham
children.translated_text: Having heard from <s>Uddhava</s> of the unbearable slaughter of his friends,
the wise <s>Kṣattṛ</s> stilled by knowledge the grief that had arisen.
As that great devotee was departing, the bull of the Kurus,
trustingly said this to him, the chief among those attached to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
<s>Vidura</s> said:

children.text: jñānaṃ paraṃ svātmarahaḥprakāśaṃ yad āha yogeśvara īśvaras te
children.translated_text: You should tell us the supreme knowledge, revealing the secret of the self, which your lord, the lord of yoga, spoke;

children.text: vaktuṃ bhavān no 'rhati yaddhi viṣṇor bhṛtyāḥ svabhṛtyārthakṛtaś caranti ||
children.translated_text: for the servants of <s>Viṣṇu</s> move about accomplishing the purposes of their own servants.
<s>Uddhava</s> said:
Surely the sage <s>Kauṣārava</s>, worthy of being fully served by you for truth, is nearby;
he was directly instructed by the Blessed Lord as he was about to leave the mortal world.
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: iti saha vidureṇa viśvamūrter guṇakathayā sudhayā plāvitorutāpaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, together with <s>Vidura</s>, the descendant of <s>Upagavi</s> was flooded by the nectar of discourse on the qualities of the Universal-formed Lord, and his great anguish was washed away.

children.text: kṣaṇam iva puline yamasvasus tāṃ samuṣita aupagavir niśāṃ tato 'gāt ||
children.translated_text: After spending that night on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> as if it were but a moment, he then went away.
The king said:
When the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Bhojas</s> had come to destruction, those foremost leaders of hosts upon hosts of great chariot-warriors,

children.text: sa tu katham avaśiṣṭa uddhavo yaddharir api tatyaja ākṛtiṃ tryadhīśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how then did <s>Uddhava</s> alone remain, when <s>Hari</s> himself, the lord of the three, abandoned his manifest form?
<s>Śuka</s> said:
By the pretext of the brāhman's curse, Time, whose desire never fails,

children.text: saṃhṛtya svakulaṃ sphītaṃ tyakṣyan deham acintayat ||
children.translated_text: having withdrawn his own flourishing clan and intending to abandon his body, reflected:

children.text: asmāl lokād uparate mayi jñānaṃ madāśrayam
children.translated_text: 'When I have departed from this world, knowledge that rests in me

children.text: arhaty uddhava evāddhā sampraty ātmavatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is now truly deserved by <s>Uddhava</s> alone, the best of the self-possessed.

children.text: noddhavo 'ṇv api mannyūno yad guṇair nārditaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Uddhava</s> is not in the least inferior to me, since as master he is not overcome by the guṇas (qualities of nature).

children.text: ato madvayunaṃ lokaṃ grāhayann iha tiṣṭhatu ||
children.translated_text: Therefore let him remain here, making the world understand my knowledge.'
Thus instructed by the teacher of the three worlds, the source of the Veda,
he reached <s>Badaryāśrama</s> and worshiped <s>Hari</s> through samādhi (meditative absorption).
<s>Vidura</s> too, having heard from <s>Uddhava</s> the praised deeds of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the supreme self,
who had assumed a body in play,
and also his laying aside of that body, which increases the steadfastness of the steadfast
but is very difficult for others, beast-like men whose selves are agitated,
and meditating on himself, O best of the Kurus, as having been regarded in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s mind,
when the devotee had gone, he wept, overwhelmed by love.
After a few days on the <s>Kālindī</s>, O bull of the Bharatas, he became composed
and reached the heavenly river, where the sage, the son of <s>Mitrā</s>, was staying.
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: dvāri dyunadyā ṛṣabhaḥ kurūṇāṃ maitreyam āsīnam agādhabodham
children.translated_text: At the gate of the heavenly river, the bull of the Kurus approached <s>Maitreya</s>, who was seated there, his understanding unfathomable.
<s>Kṣattṛ</s>, perfected in devotion to <s>Acyuta</s>, came near, deeply satisfied by his qualities of graciousness, and asked him.
<s>Vidura</s> said:

children.text: sukhāya karmāṇi karoti loko na taiḥ sukhaṃ vānyadupāramaṃ vā
children.translated_text: People perform actions for happiness, but by them they obtain neither happiness nor any other cessation of suffering;

children.text: vindeta bhūyas tata eva duḥkhaṃ yad atra yuktaṃ bhagavān vaden naḥ ||
children.translated_text: rather, from those very actions they obtain still more suffering. Let the Blessed One tell us what is fitting in this matter.

children.text: janasya kṛṣṇād vimukhasya daivād adharmaśīlasya suduḥkhitasya
children.translated_text: Surely the noble beings of <s>Janārdana</s> move about here to show favor

children.text: anugrahāyeha caranti nūnaṃ bhūtāni bhavyāni janārdanasya ||
children.translated_text: to people who, by fate, are turned away from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, given to adharma (unrighteous conduct), and deeply afflicted.

children.text: tat sādhuvaryādiśa vartma śaṃ naḥ saṃrādhito bhagavān yena puṃsām
children.translated_text: Therefore, best of the good, teach us the auspicious path by which the Blessed Lord is fully worshiped by human beings.

children.text: hṛdi sthito yacchati bhaktipūte jñānaṃ satattvādhigamaṃ purāṇam ||
children.translated_text: Dwelling in a heart purified by bhakti (devotion), he grants ancient knowledge that brings realization of truth.

children.text: karoti karmāṇi kṛtāvatāro yāny ātmatantro bhagavāṃs tryadhīśaḥ
children.translated_text: Tell us the deeds that the self-governing Blessed Lord, the lord of the three, performs when he has taken avatāras (descents),

children.text: yathā sasarjāgra idaṃ nirīhaḥ saṃsthāpya vṛttiṃ jagato vidhatte ||
children.translated_text: and how, being without desire, he first created this world, established its modes of livelihood, and maintains it.

children.text: yathā punaḥ sve kha idaṃ niveśya śete guhāyāṃ sa nivṛttavṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: Tell how again, placing this world in his own space, he lies in the cave, his activity withdrawn,

children.text: yogeśvarādhīśvara eka etad anupraviṣṭo bahudhā yathāsīt ||
children.translated_text: and how the one lord of the lords of yoga, having entered this universe, became many.

children.text: krīḍan vidhatte dvijagosurāṇāṃ kṣemāya karmāṇy avatārabhedaiḥ
children.translated_text: Playing, he performs deeds through various avatāras for the welfare of twice-borns, cows, and gods.

children.text: mano na tṛpyaty api śṛṇvatāṃ naḥ suślokamauleś caritāmṛtāni ||
children.translated_text: Even as we hear the nectar of the deeds of the crest-jewel of the well-praised, our minds are not satisfied.

children.text: yais tattvabhedair adhilokanātho lokān alokān saha lokapālān
children.translated_text: Tell us also those distinctions of principles by which the lord over the worlds
arranged the worlds and non-worlds together with the guardians of the worlds, where the diversity of all classes of beings is known as established.

children.text: yena prajānām uta ātmakarmarūpābhidhānāṃ ca bhidāṃ vyadhatta
children.translated_text: And tell us how <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the creator of the universe, self-born,

children.text: nārāyaṇo viśvasṛg ātmayonir etac ca no varṇaya vipravarya ||
children.translated_text: made the divisions among creatures, and among the forms and names arising from their own actions, O best of brāhmans.

children.text: parāvareṣāṃ bhagavan vratāni śrutāni me vyāsamukhād abhīkṣṇam
children.translated_text: O blessed one, I have often heard from <s>Vyāsa</s>'s mouth of the vows of higher and lower beings,
yet I have not been satisfied by them, for they bring only petty happiness, apart from the flood of nectar that is discourse on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: kas tṛpnuyāt tīrthapado 'bhidhānāt sattreṣu vaḥ sūribhir īḍyamānāt
children.translated_text: Who could be satisfied by the name of the One whose feet are tīrthas (sacred places), praised by your sages in sacrificial sessions?

children.text: yaḥ karṇanāḍīṃ puruṣasya yāto bhavapradāṃ geharatiṃ chinatti ||
children.translated_text: When it has entered a person's ear-channel, it cuts off household attachment, the source of worldly becoming.

children.text: munir vivakṣur bhagavadguṇānāṃ sakhāpi te bhāratam āha kṛṣṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Your friend, the sage <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, wishing to describe the qualities of the Blessed Lord, composed the <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: yasmin nṛṇāṃ grāmyasukhānuvādair matir gṛhītā nu hareḥ kathāyām ||
children.translated_text: in which the minds of men, first caught by accounts of village pleasures, are then surely drawn to the story of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: sā śraddadhānasya vivardhamānā viraktim anyatra karoti puṃsaḥ
children.translated_text: That story, growing in one who has faith, produces dispassion toward other things in a person;
for one made blissful by remembrance of <s>Hari</s>'s feet, it quickly brings about the disappearance of every suffering.

children.text: tāñchocyaśocyān avido 'nuśoce hareḥ kathāyāṃ vimukhān aghena
children.translated_text: I grieve for those pitiable, lamentable, ignorant people who, through sin, are turned away from the story of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: kṣiṇoti devo 'nimiṣas tu yeṣām āyur vṛthāvādagatismṛtīnām ||
children.translated_text: But the unwinking god cuts short the lifespan of those whose movements and memories are given to useless talk.

children.text: tad asya kauṣārava śarmadātur hareḥ kathām eva kathāsu sāram
children.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Kauṣārava</s>, from among all stories draw out only the essence, the story of <s>Hari</s>, the giver of happiness to him,

children.text: uddhṛtya puṣpebhya ivārtabandho śivāya naḥ kīrtaya tīrthakīrteḥ ||
children.translated_text: as one draws fragrance from flowers, O friend of the distressed, and narrate for our welfare the fame of him whose renown is a tīrtha (sacred ford).
He, the Lord, took avatāras (descents) for the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe, assuming his powers,

children.text: cakāra karmāṇy atipūruṣāṇi yānīśvaraḥ kīrtaya tāni mahyam ||
children.translated_text: and performed deeds beyond ordinary men. Tell me those deeds, O Lord.
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: sa evaṃ bhagavān pṛṣṭaḥ kṣattrā kauṣāravo muniḥ
children.translated_text: Thus questioned by <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, the venerable sage <s>Kauṣārava</s>,
honoring him highly, answered that question intended for the highest good of human beings.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā sādho lokān sādhv anugṛhṇatā
children.translated_text: Well have you asked, good man, as one who graciously benefits the worlds,
and as one spreading in the world your own fame, since your self is fixed in <s>Adhokṣaja</s>.
This is no wonder in you, O <s>Kṣattar</s>, born from the vigor of <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>,
that you have grasped <s>Hari</s>, the Lord, with undivided devotion.
Because of <s>Māṇḍavya</s>'s curse, the blessed <s>Yama</s>, restrainer of creatures,
was born, through the son of <s>Satyavatī</s>, in his brother's field, from a maidservant.

children.text: bhavān bhagavato nityaṃ saṃmataḥ sānugasya ha
children.translated_text: Indeed, you have always been honored by the Blessed Lord and by his followers,
for, as he departed, the Blessed Lord directed me for the teaching of knowledge to you.
Now I shall describe to you, in order, the līlās (divine plays) of the Blessed Lord, greatly expanded by <s>Yogamāyā</s>,
whose purpose is the arising, maintenance, and end of the universe.

children.text: bhagavān eka āsedam agra ātmātmanāṃ vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: Before this, the one Blessed Lord alone existed, the self, the all-pervading lord of selves, by himself,
the self who, according to his own will, is perceived through the many forms of understanding.

children.text: sa vā eṣa tadā draṣṭā nāpaśyad dṛśyam ekarāṭ
children.translated_text: At that time he, the seer, the sole sovereign, saw no object to be seen,
and he considered himself as if nonexistent, his powers asleep, though his sight was not asleep.

children.text: sā vā etasya saṃdraṣṭuḥ śaktiḥ sadasadātmikā
children.translated_text: That power of this seer, composed of being and non-being,

children.text: māyā nāma mahābhāga yayedaṃ nirmame vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: is called <s>Māyā</s>, O greatly fortunate one; by it the all-pervading Lord fashioned this world.
Then, by the operation of time, in <s>Māyā</s> made of the guṇas (qualities), <s>Adhokṣaja</s>,
the mighty one, through the puruṣa (cosmic person) who had become his own self, deposited his seed.
From that arose the mahattattva (great principle), from the unmanifest when impelled by time,
consciousness in nature, driving away darkness and manifesting the universe contained in its own body.
It too, consisting of a portion, the guṇas, and time, and falling within the Blessed Lord's glance,
unfolded itself, the self by itself, with the wish to create this universe.
From the transforming mahattattva arose the ahaṃtattva (principle of ego),
whose nature is effect, cause, and agent, and which consists of elements, senses, and mind.

children.text: vaikārikas taijasaś ca tāmasaś cety ahaṃ tridhā
children.translated_text: The ego is threefold: vaikārika, taijasa, and tāmasa.
From the transforming ahaṃtattva, mind arose from the vaikārika aspect,

children.text: vaikārikāś ca ye devā arthābhivyañjanaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the vaikārika deities also arose, from whom the manifestation of objects takes place.
From the taijasa aspect came the senses, both those made of knowledge and those made of action,

children.text: tāmaso bhūtasūkṣmādir yataḥ khaṃ liṅgam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from the tāmasa aspect came the subtle elements and the rest, from which arose ether, the mark of the self.
Ether, seen by the Blessed Lord through conjunction with time, <s>Māyā</s>, and a portion,
modified the touch-quality derived from ether and produced wind.
Wind too, transforming and endowed with the great strength of ether,
created the subtle element of form, light, the eye of the world.
Light, joined with wind and transforming under the supreme glance,
produced water, whose nature is taste, through conjunction with time, <s>Māyā</s>, and a portion.
Water, successively combined with light and transforming under <s>Brahmā</s>'s glance,
brought forth earth, endowed with the quality of smell, through conjunction with time, <s>Māyā</s>, and a portion.
Of the elements beginning with ether, whatever is later and lower,

children.text: teṣāṃ parānusaṃsargād yathā saṃkhyaṃ guṇān viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: they know its qualities in due order from its connection with the preceding higher elements.
These deities, portions of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, marked by time, <s>Māyā</s>, and portion,
being diverse and unable to perform their own functions, addressed the all-pervading Lord with joined palms.
The gods said:
We bow to your lotus feet, O god, an umbrella that calms the heat of those who have surrendered,
by whose root the ascetics easily cast outside the vast misery of saṃsāra (worldly existence).

children.text: dhātar yad asmin bhava īśa jīvās tāpatrayeṇābhihatā na śarma
children.translated_text: O creator, O Lord, since in this becoming living beings, struck by the threefold suffering,

children.text: ātman labhante bhagavaṃs tavāṅghricchāyāṃ savidyām ata āśrayema ||
children.translated_text: do not find peace in themselves, O Blessed Lord, we therefore take refuge in the shade of your feet, together with knowledge.

children.text: mārganti yat te mukhapadmanīḍaiś chandaḥsuparṇair ṛṣayo vivikte
children.translated_text: The sages seek that in solitude by the Vedic birds whose nest is your lotus mouth,
and the surrendered seek every step of <s>Tīrthapada</s>, whose excellent river of water washes away sin.

children.text: yac chraddhayā śrutavatyā ca bhaktyā saṃmṛjyamāne hṛdaye 'vadhāya
children.translated_text: When the heart is cleansed by faith, by hearing, and by devotion, and when we fix it there,

children.text: jñānena vairāgyabalena dhīrā vrajema tat te 'ṅghrisarojapīṭham ||
children.translated_text: may we, steadfast ones, reach the seat of your lotus feet through knowledge and the strength of dispassion.
May we all go for refuge to your lotus feet, you who have taken avatāra for the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe,

children.text: vrajema sarve śaraṇaṃ yad īśa smṛtaṃ prayacchaty abhayaṃ svapuṃsām ||
children.translated_text: for, O Lord, when they are remembered, they grant fearlessness to your own people.

children.text: yat sānubandhe 'sati dehagehe mamāham ity ūḍhadurāgrahāṇām
children.translated_text: For men who, attached to the unreal body and house, bear the stubborn false notion 'mine' and 'I,'

children.text: puṃsāṃ sudūraṃ vasato 'pi puryāṃ bhajema tat te bhagavan padābjam ||
children.translated_text: that lotus foot of yours, O Blessed Lord, is very far away, even though it dwells within the city of the body; let us worship it.

children.text: tān vai hy asadvṛttibhir akṣibhir ye parāhṛtāntarmanasaḥ pareśa
children.translated_text: Those whose inner minds are carried away by eyes following unreal conduct, O supreme Lord,

children.text: atho na paśyanty urugāya nūnaṃ ye te padanyāsavilāsalakṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: surely do not see, O widely sung one, the marks revealed by the playful placing of your feet.

children.text: pānena te deva kathāsudhāyāḥ pravṛddhabhaktyā viśadāśayā ye
children.translated_text: But those who drink the nectar of your stories, O god, with devotion increased and their hearts made clear,
having obtained knowledge whose essence is dispassion, would easily attain the unobstructed abode.
So too other steadfast ones, by the power of the yoga of self-concentration, conquering mighty prakṛti (primordial nature),

children.text: tvām eva dhīrāḥ puruṣaṃ viśanti teṣāṃ śramaḥ syān na tu sevayā te ||
children.translated_text: enter you alone, the puruṣa (supreme person); for them there may be effort, but not through service to you.

children.text: tat te vayaṃ lokasisṛkṣayādya tvayānusṛṣṭās tribhir ātmabhiḥ sma
children.translated_text: Therefore we, created by you today out of the desire to create the worlds, exist with three forms of self

children.text: sarve viyuktāḥ svavihāratantraṃ na śaknumas tat pratihartave te ||
children.translated_text: We are all separated from our own sphere of activity, and we cannot ward that off from you.

children.text: yāvad baliṃ te 'ja harāma kāle yathā vayaṃ cānnam adāma yatra
children.translated_text: So long as we bring you the offering at the proper time, O Unborn One, and we too eat food there,

children.text: yathobhayeṣāṃ ta ime hi lokā baliṃ haranto 'nnam adanty anūhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then these worlds of both groups, bringing the offering and eating food, will move without confusion.

children.text: tvaṃ naḥ surāṇām asi sānvayānāṃ kūṭastha ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the immutable, first, ancient <s>puruṣa</s> of us gods together with our descendants.

children.text: tvaṃ deva śaktyāṃ guṇakarmayonau retas tv ajāyāṃ kavim ādadhe 'jaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O god, by your power, in power as the womb of <s>guṇa</s> and <s>karma</s>, you, though unborn, placed the seed, the intelligent principle, in the unborn one.

children.text: tato vayaṃ matpramukhā yadarthe babhūvimātman karavāma kiṃ te
children.translated_text: Therefore we, with me at their head, have come into being for the sake of that purpose; O Self, what shall we do for you?

children.text: tvaṃ naḥ svacakṣuḥ paridehi śaktyā deva kriyārthe yadanugrahāṇām ||
children.translated_text: O god, by your power bestow on us our own faculty of sight for the work, since we depend on your favors.
The sage said:

children.text: iti tāsāṃ svaśaktīnāṃ satīnām asametya saḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, when those own powers of his, though existent, had not come together,
and when the systems of the worlds lay asleep, the Lord observed their condition.
Then <s>Urukrama</s>, bearing the goddess power called Time,
entered all at once the aggregate of the twenty-three principles.
The Blessed Lord, having entered that aggregate in the form of activity,
joined together what had been separated and awakened sleeping <s>karma</s> (action).
When its <s>karma</s> had been awakened by fate, the aggregate of twenty-three principles,
impelled, produced the ruling <s>puruṣa</s> by means of its own measures.
When the supreme entered into itself by a measure, the group of world-creators
was stirred, coming into mutual contact, in which the moving and unmoving worlds abide.
That golden <s>puruṣa</s>, for a thousand years,
dwelt in the egg-shell amid the waters, enlarged by all beings.
He indeed, the embryo of the world-creators, possessed the power of divine action and self-power,
and by himself divided himself in one way, in ten ways, and in three ways.
For he is the portion of the Supreme Self that is the self of all beings without remainder,
the first avatāra in whom this host of beings becomes manifest.

children.text: sādhyātmaḥ sādhidaivaś ca sādhibhūta iti tridhā
children.translated_text: As pertaining to the self, to the deities, and to the elements, he is threefold;

children.text: virāṭ prāṇo daśavidha ekadhā hṛdayena ca ||
children.translated_text: as <s>virāṭ</s> (the cosmic body), as the tenfold vital breath, and as one through the heart.
Remembering what had been made known by the world-creators, <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, the Lord,
heated the <s>virāj</s> with his own splendor for their development.
Now, as that being was thus heated, several seats

children.text: nirabhidyanta devānāṃ tāni me gadataḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: opened up for the gods. Hear them as I describe them.
When his mouth opened, <s>Agni</s>, the guardian of the world, entered that station,
with speech as his own portion, by which that being apprehends what is to be spoken.
When the palate of <s>Hari</s> opened, <s>Varuṇa</s>, the guardian of the world, entered it,
with the tongue as his portion, by which that being apprehends taste.

children.text: nirbhinne aśvinau nāse viṣṇor āviśatāṃ padam
children.translated_text: When the two nostrils of <s>Viṣṇu</s> opened, the two <s>Aśvins</s> entered that station,
with smell as their portion, so that apprehension of odor might arise.
When the two eyes of the Mighty One opened, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, the guardian of the world, entered them,
with sight as his portion, so that apprehension of forms might arise.
When his skin opened, <s>Anila</s>, the guardian of the world, entered it,
with breath as his portion, by which that being apprehends touch.

children.text: karṇāv asya vinirbhinnau dhiṣṇyaṃ svaṃ viviśur diśaḥ
children.translated_text: When his two ears opened, the directions entered their own seat,
with hearing as their portion, by which he attains the perception of sound.

children.text: tvacam asya vinirbhinnāṃ viviśur dhiṣṇyam oṣadhīḥ
children.translated_text: When his skin opened, the plants entered their seat,

children.text: aṃśena romabhiḥ kaṇḍūṃ yair asau pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: with the hairs as their portion, by which that being apprehends itching.

children.text: meḍhraṃ tasya vinirbhinnaṃ svadhiṣṇyaṃ ka upāviśat
children.translated_text: When his generative organ opened, <s>Ka</s> entered his own seat,
with semen as his portion, by which that being apprehends pleasure.

children.text: gudaṃ puṃso vinirbhinnaṃ mitro lokeśa āviśat
children.translated_text: When the anus of the <s>puruṣa</s> opened, <s>Mitra</s>, lord of the world, entered it,
with the organ of evacuation as his portion, by which that being apprehends discharge.

children.text: hastāv asya vinirbhinnāv indraḥ svarpatir āviśat
children.translated_text: When his two hands opened, <s>Indra</s>, lord of heaven, entered them,
with livelihood as his portion, by which a person attains his means of subsistence.

children.text: pādāv asya vinirbhinnau lokeśo viṣṇur āviśat
children.translated_text: When his two feet opened, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the world, entered them,

children.text: gatyā svāṃśena puruṣo yayā prāpyaṃ prapadyate ||
children.translated_text: with movement as his own portion, by which a person reaches what is to be reached.

children.text: buddhiṃ cāsya vinirbhinnāṃ vāgīśo dhiṣṇyam āviśat
children.translated_text: When his intellect opened, <s>Vāgīśa</s> entered that seat,
with understanding as his portion, so that apprehension of what is to be understood might arise.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ cāsya nirbhinnaṃ candramā dhiṣṇyam āviśat
children.translated_text: When his heart opened, the Moon entered that seat,
with mind as his portion, by which that being apprehends change of state.
When his self-sense opened, self-conceit entered that station,
with action as its portion, by which that being apprehends what is to be done.

children.text: sattvaṃ cāsya vinirbhinnaṃ mahān dhiṣṇyam upāviśat
children.translated_text: When his <s>sattva</s> opened, the Great Principle entered that seat,
with consciousness as its portion, by which that being apprehends knowledge.

children.text: śīrṣṇo 'sya dyaur dharā padbhyāṃ khaṃ nābher udapadyata
children.translated_text: From his head arose heaven, from his feet the earth, and from his navel the sky,
the regions in which the activities of the <s>guṇas</s> are perceived among the gods and others.
Through ultimate <s>sattva</s>, the gods reached heaven;

children.text: dharāṃ rajaḥsvabhāvena paṇayo ye ca tān anu ||
children.translated_text: through a nature of <s>rajas</s>, the merchants and those following them reached the earth.
Through the third nature, O Blessed One, the hosts of <s>Rudra</s>'s attendants

children.text: ubhayor antaraṃ vyoma ye rudrapārṣadāṃ gaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: took refuge in the navel, the atmosphere between the two.
From the mouth of the <s>puruṣa</s>, O scion of <s>Kuru</s>, came forth <s>brahman</s> (sacred authority),

children.text: yas tūnmukhatvād varṇānāṃ mukhyo 'bhūd brāhmaṇo guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because it faced upward, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the teacher, became chief among the classes.
From the arms came forth royal power; the <s>kṣatriya</s> was its follower,

children.text: yo jātas trāyate varṇān pauruṣaḥ kaṇṭakakṣatāt ||
children.translated_text: born from the <s>puruṣa</s>, who protects the classes from injury by thorns.
The peoples came forth from the thighs of that Mighty One, sustaining the livelihood of the world;

children.text: vaiśyas tadudbhavo vārttāṃ nṛṇāṃ yaḥ samavartayat ||
children.translated_text: the <s>vaiśya</s>, born from them, set in motion the livelihood of human beings.
From the feet of the Blessed Lord was born service, for the accomplishment of <s>dharma</s> (religious duty).

children.text: tasyāṃ jātaḥ purā śūdro yadvṛttyā tuṣyate hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: A śūdra was born there in former times; by that way of life <s>Hari</s> is satisfied.

children.text: ete varṇāḥ svadharmeṇa yajanti svaguruṃ harim
children.translated_text: These varṇas worship their own guru, <s>Hari</s>, by their own dharma,
with faith, for the purification of the self, having been born together with their livelihoods.
This, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, belongs to the Blessed Lord, whose form is divine action and self;
who could trust himself to describe the arising of the power of his <s>yogamāyā</s>?
Still, dear one, I shall recount it according to my understanding and according to what I have heard,

children.text: kīrtiṃ hareḥ svāṃ satkartuṃ giram anyābhidhāsatīm ||
children.translated_text: so as to honor <s>Hari</s>'s own glory with speech that would otherwise name other things.

children.text: ekāntalābhaṃ vacaso nu puṃsāṃ suślokamauler guṇavādam āhuḥ
children.translated_text: They say that the sole gain of speech for men is the praise of the virtues of him whose crown is noble fame,

children.text: śruteś ca vidvadbhir upākṛtāyāṃ kathāsudhāyām upasaṃprayogam ||
children.translated_text: and, when the nectar of sacred stories has been prepared by the learned from revelation, participation in it.
Dear child, the greatness of the self was ascertained by the ancient poet
only after a thousand years, with an understanding matured by yoga.

children.text: ato bhagavato māyā māyinām api mohinī
children.translated_text: Therefore the Blessed Lord's <s>māyā</s> bewilders even those who wield illusion;

children.text: yat svayaṃ cātmavartmātmā na veda kim utāpare ||
children.translated_text: even the self, whose path is the self, does not know it by itself; how much less do others?

children.text: yato 'prāpya nyavartanta vācaś ca manasā saha
children.translated_text: From him words turned back without reaching him, together with the mind.

children.text: ahaṃ cānya ime devās tasmai bhagavate namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: To that Blessed Lord, before whom I and these other gods stand, homage.
<s>Śuka</s> said:
As <s>Maitreya</s> was speaking thus, the wise son of <s>Dvaipāyana</s>,
<s>Vidura</s>, as if delighting him with his speech, replied.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
O brāhman, how can qualities and actions be connected, even in play, with the Blessed Lord,

children.text: līlayā cāpi yujyeran nirguṇasya guṇāḥ kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who is pure consciousness, changeless, and without guṇas?
In play, a child's exertion comes from desire, from a wish to play with something else;
but how could this apply to one who is satisfied in himself and always withdrawn from anything else?
The Blessed Lord created the universe by his own <s>māyā</s> composed of the guṇas;
by her he establishes it, and again he will draw it back.
How can that one, whose consciousness is never lost through place, time, condition, himself, or another,
be joined with <s>Ajā</s>, unborn nature?
This Blessed Lord alone is present in all fields of embodiment;

children.text: amuṣya durbhagatvaṃ vā kleśo vā karmabhiḥ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whence could misfortune for him, or suffering through actions, arise?
In this matter, learned one, my mind is troubled in the distress of ignorance.

children.text: tan naḥ parāṇuda vibho kaśmalaṃ mānasaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: Therefore drive away for us, mighty lord, this great mental impurity.
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: sa itthaṃ coditaḥ kṣattrā tattvajijñāsunā muniḥ
children.translated_text: Thus challenged by <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, who desired to know reality, the sage,
his mind fixed on the Blessed Lord, replied, smiling as it were, free from pride.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: seyaṃ bhagavato māyā yan nayena virudhyate
children.translated_text: This indeed is the Blessed Lord's <s>māyā</s>: that which is contrary to reason appears,
namely the wretchedness or bondage of the Lord who is free.
For without any real object, a reversal of the self appears to this witnessing person,
like the cutting off of one's own head and the like.

children.text: yathā jale candramasaḥ kampādis tatkṛto guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as in water trembling and the like of the moon, a quality caused by that water,
is seen, though unreal, so a quality of the non-self is seen in the self of the seer.
That very thing gradually disappears here through the dharma of cessation, by the compassion of <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
and through <s>bhagavadbhaktiyoga</s>, the yoga of devotion to the Blessed Lord.
When, then, the senses come to rest in the supreme seer-self, in <s>Hari</s>,
then all sufferings dissolve completely, like those of one asleep.
Hearing the praise of <s>Murāri</s>'s qualities brings about the calming of all afflictions;
how much more does love, gained in the self, for service to the pollen of his lotus feet do so?
<s>Vidura</s> said:

children.text: saṃchinnaḥ saṃśayo mahyaṃ tava sūktāsinā vibho
children.translated_text: My doubt has been cut off, mighty lord, by the sword of your good words.
Yet in both respects, Blessed one, my mind still runs on.

children.text: sādhv etad vyāhṛtaṃ vidvan nātmamāyāyanaṃ hareḥ
children.translated_text: This has been well spoken, learned one: the course of <s>Hari</s>'s own <s>māyā</s>

children.text: ābhāty apārthaṃ nirmūlaṃ viśvamūlaṃ na yad bahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: appears purposeless and rootless, though it is the root of the universe and nothing exists outside it.

children.text: yaś ca mūḍhatamo loke yaś ca buddheḥ paraṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: He who is utterly foolish in the world, and he who has gone beyond intellect,

children.text: tāv ubhau sukham edhete kliśyaty antarito janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: both flourish happily; the person between them is tormented.
Having determined the unreality of what has appeared, and that it is not the self,
I shall also drive that away through service to your feet.
By service to which, intense relish of love for the feet of the immutable Blessed Lord, the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>,
arises and removes distress.
For those of little austerity, service among those on the path to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is hard to obtain,
where <s>Janārdana</s>, god of gods, is constantly sung.
Having first created the mahat and the other principles, with their transformations, in sequence,

children.text: tebhyo virājam uddhṛtya tam anu prāviśad vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having drawn forth <s>Virāj</s> from them, the all-pervading one then entered it.
They call him the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, with a thousand feet, thighs, and arms,

children.text: yatra viśva ime lokāḥ savikāśaṃ ta āsate ||
children.translated_text: in whom these worlds exist with full expansion.
In whom there is the tenfold vital breath, together with the senses, sense-objects, and the threefold set,

children.text: tvayerito yato varṇās tadvibhūtīr vadasva naḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from whom, impelled by you, the varṇas arose: tell us his manifestations.

children.text: yatra putraiś ca pautraiś ca naptṛbhiḥ saha gotrajaiḥ
children.translated_text: Where creatures of varied forms existed with sons, grandsons, descendants, and clansmen,

children.text: prajā vicitrākṛtaya āsan yābhir idaṃ tatam ||
children.translated_text: by whom this world was spread out.

children.text: prajāpatīnāṃ sa patiś cakﾱpe kān prajāpatīn
children.translated_text: Which Prajāpatis the lord of the Prajāpatis appointed,
and the creations and secondary creations, the Manus and the rulers of the manvantaras,

children.text: eteṣām api vedāṃś ca vaṃśānucaritāni ca
children.translated_text: and also the divisions of the Vedas belonging to these, and the histories of their lineages,

children.text: upary adhaś ca ye lokā bhūmer mitrātmajāsate ||
children.translated_text: and the worlds that exist above and below the earth, O son of <s>Mitrā</s>:

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃsthāṃ pramāṇaṃ ca bhūrlokasya ca varṇaya
children.translated_text: describe their arrangement and measure, and that of <s>Bhūrloka</s>.
Tell us the ordered creation of animals, humans, gods, reptiles, and birds,
and of those born from womb, sweat, egg, and sprout.
Through avatāras associated with the guṇas, he is the support of the universe's creation, maintenance, and dissolution;
explain the noble exploits of <s>Śrīnivāsa</s> as he creates.
And explain the divisions of varṇa and āśrama according to form, conduct, and innate nature.
the births and deeds of the sages, and the division of the <s>Veda</s>,

children.text: yajñasya ca vitānāni yogasya ca pathaḥ prabho
children.translated_text: the extensions of <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), and the paths of <s>yoga</s>, O lord,

children.text: naiṣkarmyasya ca sāṃkhyasya tantraṃ vā bhagavatsmṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the doctrine of <s>naiṣkarmya</s> (actionlessness) and of <s>sāṃkhya</s>, or the <s>tantra</s> remembered as belonging to the Blessed Lord,
the irregularity of heretical paths, and the establishment of unions contrary to the proper order,

children.text: jīvasya gatayo yāś ca yāvatīr guṇakarmajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all the courses of the <s>jīva</s> (living being), as many as arise from <s>guṇa</s> and <s>karma</s>.
the causes of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, and liberation, without mutual conflict,

children.text: vārttāyā daṇḍanīteś ca śrutasya ca vidhiṃ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and the separate rules for livelihood, statecraft, and sacred learning;

children.text: śrāddhasya ca vidhiṃ brahman pitṝṇāṃ sargam eva ca
children.translated_text: the rite of <s>śrāddha</s>, O brāhman, and also the creation of the ancestors,
the arrangement of planets, lunar mansions, stars, and the divisions of time;

children.text: dānasya tapaso vāpi yac ceṣṭāpūrtayoḥ phalam
children.translated_text: the fruit of giving and of austerity, and also of works of sacrifice and public benefit,

children.text: pravāsasthasya yo dharmo yaś ca puṃsa utāpadi ||
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s> of one living abroad, and that of a man in distress;

children.text: yena vā bhagavāṃs tuṣyed dharmayonir janārdanaḥ
children.translated_text: and by what means the Blessed Lord <s>Janārdana</s>, the source of <s>dharma</s>, may be pleased,

children.text: samprasīdati vā yeṣām etad ākhyāhi me 'nagha ||
children.translated_text: or toward whom he becomes gracious. Tell me this, O sinless one.
To devoted followers, disciples, and sons, O best of twice-borns,
teachers compassionate toward the wretched should speak even when they have not been asked.
O blessed one, in how many ways is there the dissolution of those principles?

children.text: tatremaṃ ka upāsīran ka u svid anuśerate ||
children.translated_text: In that process, who attend upon this world, and who, indeed, lie down afterward?

children.text: puruṣasya ca saṃsthānaṃ svarūpaṃ vā parasya ca
children.translated_text: Tell also the constitution of the <s>puruṣa</s> (cosmic person), and the proper form of the supreme.

children.text: jñānaṃ ca naigamaṃ yat tad guruśiṣyaprayojanam ||
children.translated_text: Tell that Vedic knowledge, and the purpose of teacher and pupil.
The causes of that knowledge here have been declared by sinless seers.

children.text: svato jñānaṃ kutaḥ puṃsāṃ bhaktir vairāgyam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: Whence do human beings obtain knowledge of themselves, or <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) and dispassion?

children.text: etān me pṛcchataḥ praśnān hareḥ karmavivitsayā
children.translated_text: I ask you these questions out of a desire to know the deeds of <s>Hari</s>.
Speak to me, who am ignorant, out of friendship, for my eyes have been ruined by <s>ajā</s> (primordial nature).

children.text: sarve vedāś ca yajñāś ca tapo dānāni cānagha
children.translated_text: All the <s>Vedas</s>, all sacrifices, austerities, and gifts, O sinless one,
would not equal even a fraction of giving freedom from fear to living beings.
<s>Śrīśuka</s> said:
Thus questioned by the foremost of the Kurus, the foremost sage, versed in purāṇa and kalpa,

children.text: pravṛddhaharṣo bhagavatkathāyāṃ saṃcoditas taṃ prahasann ivāha ||
children.translated_text: his joy swelling at the tale of the Blessed Lord, prompted by him, answered as if smiling.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: satsevanīyo bata pūruvaṃśo yal lokapālo bhagavatpradhānaḥ
children.translated_text: Blessed indeed is the line of <s>Pūru</s>, fit to be served by the good, since its protector of the people has the Blessed Lord as his chief concern.
You have been born here to make the garland of <s>Ajita</s>'s fame ever new at every step.

children.text: so 'haṃ nṛṇāṃ kṣullasukhāya duḥkhaṃ mahad gatānāṃ viramāya tasya
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the cessation of the great suffering reached by people for the sake of petty happiness,

children.text: pravartaye bhāgavataṃ purāṇaṃ yad āha sākṣād bhagavān ṛṣibhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall set forth the <s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s>, which the Blessed Lord himself told to the sages.

children.text: āsīnam urvyāṃ bhagavantam ādyaṃ saṃkarṣaṇaṃ devam akuṇṭhasattvam
children.translated_text: They approached the primal Blessed Lord, the god <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, whose being is unobstructed, seated upon the earth.

children.text: vivitsavas tattvam ataḥ parasya kumāramukhyā munayo 'nvapṛcchan ||
children.translated_text: The chief sages, headed by the <s>Kumāras</s>, desiring to know the truth beyond this, questioned him.

children.text: svam eva dhiṣṇyaṃ bahu mānayantaṃ yad vāsudevābhidham āmananti
children.translated_text: He was greatly honoring his own seat, which they call by the name <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
and, for the awakening of the wise, was slightly opening the lotus-buds of his eyes, which had been turned inward.
With their own locks of matted hair moistened by the heavenly river,

children.text: padmaṃ yad arcanty ahirājakanyāḥ saprema nānābalibhir varārthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the serpent-king's daughters, seeking boons, worshiped with love and many offerings the lotus that was his foot-rest.
Those who knew his deeds repeatedly praised them, their words stumbling with affection as they spoke,
before him whose thousand mighty hoods were illumined by the brilliant rays of the jewels in his thousand crowns.
This was indeed spoken by that best of devotees to <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, who delighted in the <s>dharma</s> of renunciation.

children.text: sanatkumārāya sa cāha pṛṣṭaḥ sāṃkhyāyanāyāṅga dhṛtavratāya ||
children.translated_text: And he, when asked, told it to <s>Sāṃkhyāyana</s>, O dear one, who was firm in his vows.
<s>Sāṃkhyāyana</s>, foremost among the great <s>pāramahaṃsyas</s> (renunciant sages), wishing to describe the manifestations of the Blessed Lord,
told it to our teacher <s>Parāśara</s>, who was attentive, and then also to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: provāca mahyaṃ sa dayālur ukto muniḥ pulastyena purāṇam ādyam
children.translated_text: That compassionate sage, urged by <s>Pulastya</s>, proclaimed to me the primal <s>Purāṇa</s>.

children.text: so 'haṃ tavaitat kathayāmi vatsa śraddhālave nityam anuvratāya ||
children.translated_text: And I, my child, shall tell this to you, who are faithful and always devoted.

children.text: udāplutaṃ viśvam idaṃ tadāsīd yan nidrayāmīlitadṛṅ nyamīlayat
children.translated_text: At that time this universe was submerged in water, when he, closing his eyes as if in sleep, shut them.
He alone lay upon the couch of the king of serpents, having made the proper moment, delighting in his own self, without activity.
Having placed the subtle elements within his body, and setting in motion his power whose nature is time,

children.text: uvāsa tasmin salile pade sve yathānalo dāruṇi ruddhavīryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he dwelt in that water, in his own place, like fire whose force is confined in wood.

children.text: caturyugānāṃ ca sahasram apsu svapan svayodīritayā svaśaktyā
children.translated_text: Sleeping in the waters for a thousand cycles of four ages by his own power impelled by himself,
he, brought under the operation of <s>karma</s> called Time, saw the dissolved worlds within his own body.
For him, whose gaze was fixed on the subtle object, the object within, made very fine by rajas,

children.text: guṇena kālānugatena viddhaḥ sūṣyaṃs tadābhidyata nābhideśāt ||
children.translated_text: pierced by the quality that followed Time and about to be born, then burst forth from the region of the navel.
That lotus-bud suddenly arose, awakened by Time and <s>karma</s>,

children.text: svarociṣā tat salilaṃ viśālaṃ vidyotayann arka ivātmayoniḥ ||
children.translated_text: illuminating the vast water with its own radiance, like the self-born sun.

children.text: tal lokapadmaṃ sa u eva viṣṇuḥ prāvīviśat sarvaguṇāvabhāsam
children.translated_text: He, that very <s>Viṣṇu</s>, entered that world-lotus, which made all the qualities manifest.

children.text: tasmin svayaṃ vedamayo vidhātā svayambhuvaṃ yaṃ sma vadanti so 'bhūt ||
children.translated_text: In it the Veda-formed ordainer, whom they call <s>Svayambhū</s>, came into being.

children.text: tasyāṃ sa cāmbhoruhakarṇikāyām avasthito lokam apaśyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Situated in the pericarp of that lotus, and not seeing the world,

children.text: parikraman vyomni vivṛttanetraś catvāri lebhe 'nudiśaṃ mukhāni ||
children.translated_text: as he moved about in the sky with eyes turned all around, he obtained four faces, one toward each direction.
From those waters, whirled by the wind at the end of the age and by circles of waves, it had grown forth.

children.text: upāśritaḥ kañjam u lokatattvaṃ nātmānam addhāvidad ādidevaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having taken refuge in the lotus, the primordial god did not clearly know either the principle of the world or himself.

children.text: ka eṣa yo 'sāv aham abjapṛṣṭha etat kuto vābjam ananyad apsu
children.translated_text: Who is this one that I am, upon the back of a lotus? And from where has this lotus come, when there is nothing else in the waters?

children.text: asti hy adhastād iha kiṃcanaitad adhiṣṭhitaṃ yatra satā nu bhāvyam ||
children.translated_text: Surely there is something here below, where it is established, and where one must therefore reflect.

children.text: sa ittham udvīkṣya tadabjanālanāḍībhir antarjalam āviveśa
children.translated_text: Having looked upward in this way, through the tubular channels of that lotus stalk he entered the waters within.
But though he went downward and searched for the navel, the hard tubular source of that lotus stalk, the unborn one did not find it.

children.text: tamasy apāre vidurātmasargaṃ vicinvato 'bhūt sumahāṃs triṇemiḥ
children.translated_text: As he searched in the boundless darkness, seeking the source of his own being, a very great three-rimmed force came upon him,

children.text: yo dehabhājāṃ bhayam īrayāṇaḥ parikṣiṇoty āyur ajasya hetiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the weapon of the unborn Lord, which, driving fear into embodied beings, cuts short their lifespan.

children.text: tato nivṛtto 'pratilabdhakāmaḥ svadhiṣṇyam āsādya punaḥ sa devaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, turning back with his desire unfulfilled, that god reached his own seat again,
and slowly, with breath mastered and mind withdrawn, he sat down, having ascended to the yoga of <s>samādhi</s>.
In time that unborn one, through yoga undertaken for the span of a divine person's life, became firm in awakened knowledge,

children.text: svayaṃ tad antarhṛdaye 'vabhātam apaśyatāpaśyata yan na pūrvam ||
children.translated_text: and he saw manifested by itself within his heart what he had not seen before.
He saw the one <s>puruṣa</s> lying upon the couch of the long coils of <s>Śeṣa</s>, white like lotus fiber,
while the darkness in the waters of the cosmic dissolution was dispelled by the radiance of the jewels on the thousand umbrella-like hoods above his head.
He cast his glance from the golden summit of the emerald mountain, like a bank of clouds at twilight,
with garlands of forest flowers, arms like bamboos, feet and other limbs made gracious by streams of jewels, the ocean, herbs, and flowers.
In length and breadth, by the measure of his own body, he gathered within himself the three worlds,
his form adorned with the splendor of wondrous divine ornaments and garments, a body whose attire had become beautiful.
To men who worship by solitary paths for their own desired goal, he showed his wish-yielding lotus feet,
their lovely petal-like toes split by the moonbeams of his nails, out of compassion.
With a face that removed the distress of the worlds by its smile, adorned with flashing earrings,
reddened by the luster of his bimba-fruit lips, with a fine nose and fine brows, he honored them in return.
He was well adorned with garments tawny like kadamba filaments and with a girdle at his hips,
and, dear one, with a necklace of endless wealth dear to the chest marked by <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.
His thousand branch-like arms were like great trunks covered with the finest priceless armlets and jewels,
a lordly tree whose root was unmanifest and whose branches were wrapped about by the coils of the serpent king.
The Blessed Lord was like a great mountain, the dwelling of moving and unmoving beings, allied with the serpent king and embraced by the waters,
with a thousand golden peaks in the form of crowns, and with the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel appearing as its inner treasure.
He saw <s>Hari</s>, clothed in the beauty of the Veda-like bees by a forest garland made of his own fame,
inaccessible to the chief powers that circle him in three abodes as sun, moon, wind, fire, and sacred recitation.

children.text: tarhy eva tannābhisaraḥsarojam ātmānam ambhaḥ śvasanaṃ viyac ca
children.translated_text: Then the god, the maker of the world, saw that lotus lake at his navel, himself, the waters, breath, and space,

children.text: dadarśa devo jagato vidhātā nātaḥ paraṃ lokavisargadṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: but, for the vision of creating worlds, he saw nothing beyond this.

children.text: sa karmabījaṃ rajasoparaktaḥ prajāḥ sisṛkṣann iyad eva dṛṣṭvā
children.translated_text: Stained by <s>rajas</s>, the seed of action, and wishing to create progeny, after seeing only so much,

children.text: astaud visargābhimukhas tam īḍyam avyaktavartmany abhiveśitātmā ||
children.translated_text: he turned toward creation and praised that worshipful one, his mind fixed upon the unmanifest path.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: jñāto 'si me 'dya sucirān nanu dehabhājāṃ na jñāyate bhagavato gatir ity avadyam
children.translated_text: Today, after a very long time, I have known you. Indeed it is blameworthy that the course of the Blessed Lord is not known by embodied beings.

children.text: nānyat tvad asti bhagavann api tan na śuddhaṃ māyāguṇavyatikarād yad urur vibhāsi ||
children.translated_text: There is nothing apart from you, O Blessed Lord; and even that is not pure, since you appear vast through the intermixture of the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: rūpaṃ yad etad avabodharasodayena śaśvannivṛttatamasaḥ sadanugrahāya
children.translated_text: This form, arisen from the essence of awakening and forever freed from darkness, was assumed at the beginning for the favor of the good,

children.text: ādau gṛhītam avatāraśataikabījaṃ yan nābhipadmabhavanād aham āvirāsam ||
children.translated_text: as the single seed of hundreds of avatāras, from whose navel-lotus I came forth.

children.text: nātaḥ paraṃ parama yad bhavataḥ svarūpam ānandamātram avikalpam aviddhavarcaḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond this, O Supreme One, I do not see any higher true form of yours: sheer bliss, without division, with unobstructed radiance.

children.text: paśyāmi viśvasṛjam ekam aviśvam ātman bhūtendriyātmakamadas ta upāśrito 'smi ||
children.translated_text: O Self, I take refuge in you, the one creator of the universe, yet not the universe, this form composed of beings and senses.

children.text: tad vā idaṃ bhuvanamaṅgala maṅgalāya dhyāne sma no darśitaṃ ta upāsakānām
children.translated_text: O auspicious one for the worlds, this very form has been shown in meditation for the blessing of us, your worshipers.

children.text: tasmai namo bhagavate 'nuvidhema tubhyaṃ yo 'nādṛto narakabhāgbhir asatprasaṅgaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: To that Blessed Lord I bow; let us follow you, who are disregarded by those bound for hell through attachment to the unreal.

children.text: ye tu tvadīyacaraṇāmbujakośagandhaṃ jighranti karṇavivaraiḥ śrutivātanītam
children.translated_text: But those who smell the fragrance within the cup of your lotus feet, carried by the wind of scripture through the openings of the ears,

children.text: bhaktyā gṛhītacaraṇaḥ parayā ca teṣāṃ nāpaiṣi nātha hṛdayāmburuhāt svapuṃsām ||
children.translated_text: O Lord, you, whose feet are grasped by supreme devotion, never depart from the lotus-hearts of those men who are your own.

children.text: tāvad bhayaṃ draviṇadehasuhṛnnimittaṃ śokaḥ spṛhā paribhavo vipulaś ca lobhaḥ
children.translated_text: So long as there is fear caused by wealth, body, and friends, so long grief, longing, humiliation, and vast greed remain;

children.text: tāvan mamety asadavagraha ārtimūlaṃ yāvan na te 'ṅghrim abhayaṃ pravṛṇīta lokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so long the false grasping of 'mine,' the root of distress, remains, until the world chooses your fearless feet.

children.text: daivena te hatadhiyo bhavataḥ prasaṅgāt sarvāśubhopaśamanād vimukhendriyā ye
children.translated_text: By fate their understanding is ruined, and they turn their senses away from association with you, which removes every inauspicious thing.
Wretched, their minds overwhelmed by greed, they constantly do unwholesome deeds for only the tiniest particle of sensual pleasure.

children.text: kṣuttṛṭtridhātubhir imā muhur ardyamānāḥ śītoṣṇavātavarṣair itaretarāc ca
children.translated_text: Seeing these beings repeatedly tormented by hunger, thirst, and the three bodily humors, by cold, heat, wind, rain, and by one another,

children.text: kāmāgninācyutaruṣā ca sudurbhareṇa sampaśyato mana urukrama sīdate me ||
children.translated_text: and by the fire of desire and the unbearable anger of <s>Acyuta</s>, my mind sinks, O <s>Urukrama</s>.

children.text: yāvat pṛthaktvam idam ātmana indriyārthamāyābalaṃ bhagavato jana īśa paśyet
children.translated_text: As long as a person, O Lord, sees this separateness of self from the objects of the senses as the power of the Blessed Lord's <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: tāvan na saṃsṛtir asau pratisaṃkrameta vyarthāpi duḥkhanivahaṃ vahatī kriyārthā ||
children.translated_text: so long this <s>saṃsṛti</s> (cycle of transmigration), though futile and bearing a mass of suffering for the sake of action, does not turn back.

children.text: ahny āpṛtārtakaraṇā niśi niḥśayānā nānāmanorathadhiyā kṣaṇabhagnanidrāḥ
children.translated_text: By day their organs are distressed by toil; by night, lying sleepless, their sleep is broken in a moment by minds full of many desires.

children.text: daivāhatārtharacanā ṛṣayo 'pi deva yuṣmatprasaṅgavimukhā iha saṃsaranti ||
children.translated_text: Even sages, O god, whose plans for gain are struck down by fate and who turn away from association with you, wander here in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ bhaktiyogaparibhāvitahṛtsaroja āsse śrutekṣitapatho nanu nātha puṃsām
children.translated_text: You sit in the lotus-lake of men's hearts, made fragrant by the yoga of devotion, for your path is seen through hearing, O Lord.

children.text: yadyaddhiyā ta urugāya vibhāvayanti tattadvapuḥ praṇayase sadanugrahāya ||
children.translated_text: Whatever body they contemplate you with in thought, O <s>Urugāya</s>, that very body you assume in order to favor the good.

children.text: nātiprasīdati tathopacitopacārair ārādhitaḥ suragaṇair hṛdi baddhakāmaiḥ
children.translated_text: He is not so greatly pleased when worshiped with abundant offerings by hosts of gods whose desires are bound in their hearts,

children.text: yat sarvabhūtadayayāsadalabhyayaiko nānājaneṣv avahitaḥ suhṛd antarātmā ||
children.translated_text: as he is by compassion for all beings; hard for the wicked to attain, he alone is attentive among many peoples as the friend, the inner self.

children.text: puṃsām ato vividhakarmabhir adhvarādyair dānena cogratapasā paricaryayā ca
