children.translated_text: Therefore, the worship of you, the Blessed Lord, by people through various rites, sacrifices and the like, through gifts, stern austerity, and service,

children.text: ārādhanaṃ bhagavatas tava satkriyārtho dharmo 'rpitaḥ karhicin mriyate na yatra ||
children.translated_text: has the purpose of honoring you; when <s>dharma</s> is offered in that place, it never perishes.

children.text: śaśvat svarūpamahasaiva nipītabhedamohāya bodhadhiṣaṇāya namaḥ parasmai
children.translated_text: Obeisance to the supreme one, whose delusion of difference has forever been swallowed by the splendor of his own nature, and whose seat of intelligence is awakening;

children.text: viśvodbhavasthitilayeṣu nimittalīlārāsāya te nama idaṃ cakṛmeśvarāya ||
children.translated_text: to you, the Lord, whose play is the causal essence in the arising, continuance, and dissolution of the universe, we make this obeisance.
Those who, helpless at the departure of life, recite the names that reflect his avatāras, qualities, and deeds,

children.text: te 'naikajanmaśamalaṃ sahasaiva hitvā saṃyānty apāvṛtāmṛtaṃ tam ajaṃ prapadye ||
children.translated_text: at once abandon the impurity of many births and reach uncovered immortality; I take refuge in that unborn one.

children.text: yo vā ahaṃ ca giriśaś ca vibhuḥ svayaṃ ca sthityudbhavapralayahetava ātmamūlam
children.translated_text: From whom I, <s>Giriśa</s>, and the all-pervading Lord himself, the causes of maintenance, origination, and dissolution, have our root in the self,

children.text: bhittvā tripād vavṛdha eka uruprarohas tasmai namo bhagavate bhuvanadrumāya ||
children.translated_text: he alone, splitting the three-footed trunk, grew as a great shoot; homage to that Blessed Lord, the tree of worlds.

children.text: loko vikarmanirataḥ kuśale pramattaḥ karmaṇy ayaṃ tvadudite bhavadarcane sve
children.translated_text: This world is devoted to forbidden acts and careless about what is wholesome, while its own duty, proclaimed by you, is your worship;

children.text: yas tāvad asya balavān iha jīvitāśāṃ sadyaś chinatty animiṣāya namo 'stu tasmai ||
children.translated_text: homage to that unblinking one who immediately cuts off its strong hope of life here.

children.text: yasmād bibhemy aham api dviparārdhadhiṣṇyam adhyāsitaḥ sakalalokanamaskṛtaṃ yat
children.translated_text: I myself fear him, though I occupy the seat lasting two parārdhas, honored by all the worlds,

children.text: tepe tapo bahusavo 'varurutsamānas tasmai namo bhagavate 'dhimakhāya tubhyam ||
children.translated_text: and, desiring to attain him, I practiced tapas through many ages; homage to that Blessed Lord, the lord of sacrifice, to you.
He who, among births as animals, humans, gods, and others, by his own will and seeking to preserve the boundary he himself has made,

children.text: reme nirastaviṣayo 'py avaruddhadehas tasmai namo bhagavate puruṣottamāya ||
children.translated_text: delights, though beyond objects of sense, with a body held in limitation; homage to that Blessed Lord, the supreme <s>puruṣa</s>.
He who, though untouched by ignorance, took up sleep through the function of the half-ten senses,
with the course of the worlds contained in his belly, in the waters, on the serpent couch pleasant to the touch, amid a garland of dreadful waves, revealing comfort for people.

children.text: yan nābhipadmabhavanād aham āsam īḍya lokatrayopakaraṇo yadanugraheṇa
children.translated_text: From the lotus born from whose navel I came into being, O worshipful one, made an instrument for the three worlds by whose grace,
to that one who holds existence within his belly, whose lotus eyes open at the end of <s>yoganidrā</s>, homage to you.

children.text: so 'yaṃ samastajagatāṃ suhṛd eka ātmā sattvena yan mṛḍayate bhagavān bhagena
children.translated_text: He, this Blessed Lord, the one friend and self of all the worlds, gladdens them through <s>sattva</s> with his divine majesty;

children.text: tenaiva me dṛśam anuspṛśatād yathāhaṃ srakṣyāmi pūrvavad idaṃ praṇatapriyo 'sau ||
children.translated_text: by that very power may he touch my sight, so that I may create this world as before; he loves those who bow to him.

children.text: eṣa prapannavarado ramayātmaśaktyā yad yat kariṣyati gṛhītaguṇāvatāraḥ
children.translated_text: This giver of boons to the surrendered, together with <s>Ramā</s>, his own power, will do whatever he will, having assumed an avatāra made of the <s>guṇas</s>;

children.text: tasmin svavikramam idaṃ sṛjato 'pi ceto yuñjīta karmaśamalaṃ ca yathā vijahyām ||
children.translated_text: may my mind be joined to him even while I create this by my own prowess, and may I abandon the impurity of action.

children.text: nābhihradād iha sato 'mbhasi yasya puṃso vijñānaśaktir aham āsam anantaśakteḥ
children.translated_text: Here in the waters, from the navel-lake of that <s>puruṣa</s>, I arose as the power of discernment of him whose powers are endless;

children.text: rūpaṃ vicitram idam asya vivṛṇvato me mā rīriṣīṣṭa nigamasya girāṃ visargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as he unfolds this manifold form for me, may the outpouring of the Veda's words not fail.

children.text: so 'sāv adabhrakaruṇo bhagavān vivṛddhapremasmitena nayanāmburuhaṃ vijṛmbhan
children.translated_text: May that Blessed Lord of abundant compassion, the ancient <s>puruṣa</s>, open his lotus eye with a greatly expanded loving smile,

children.text: utthāya viśvavijayāya ca no viṣādaṃ mādhvyā girāpanayatāt puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: rise for the conquest of the universe, and dispel our despondency with honey-sweet speech.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having thus observed his own source through tapas, knowledge, and concentration,

children.text: yāvan manovacaḥ stutvā virarāma sa khinnavat ||
children.translated_text: and having praised him as far as mind and speech could reach, he ceased, as if exhausted.
Then <s>Madhusūdana</s>, perceiving what <s>Brahmā</s> intended,
and seeing him despondent because of the waters that had disrupted the kalpa,
as he was worn down in the knowledge of the arrangement of the worlds and of himself,

children.text: tam āhāgādhayā vācā kaśmalaṃ śamayann iva ||
children.translated_text: addressed him in a deep voice, as if calming his distress.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: mā vedagarbha gās tandrīṃ sarga udyamam āvaha
children.translated_text: Do not, O <s>Vedagarbha</s>, fall into sluggishness; bring forth effort for creation.

children.text: tan mayāpāditaṃ hy agre yan māṃ prārthayate bhavān ||
children.translated_text: For what Your Reverence asks of me has already been provided by me at the beginning.

children.text: bhūyas tvaṃ tapa ātiṣṭha vidyāṃ caiva madāśrayām
children.translated_text: Again, undertake tapas, and also knowledge that rests on me;

children.text: tābhyām antarhṛdi brahman lokān drakṣyasy apāvṛtān ||
children.translated_text: by those two, O <s>Brahman</s>, you will see the worlds unveiled within your heart.

children.text: tata ātmani loke ca bhaktiyuktaḥ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, joined with devotion and collected in the self and in the world,

children.text: draṣṭāsi māṃ tataṃ brahman mayi lokāṃs tvam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you will see me pervading, O <s>Brahman</s>, and you will see the worlds in me and in yourself.

children.text: yadā tu sarvabhūteṣu dāruṣv agnim iva sthitam
children.translated_text: But when the world perceives me established in all beings, like fire in pieces of wood,

children.text: praticakṣīta māṃ loko jahyāt tarhy eva kaśmalam ||
children.translated_text: then indeed it will abandon its impurity.
When one sees the self free from the traces of beings, senses, and <s>guṇas</s>,
and joined with me in its own form, one attains self-sovereignty.
For you, who wish to create many creatures through the expanse of manifold actions,
your self does not sink in this, for my grace upon you is greater.

children.text: ṛṣim ādyaṃ na badhnāti pāpīyāṃs tvāṃ rajoguṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The more harmful quality of <s>rajas</s> does not bind you, the first seer,

children.text: yan mano mayi nirbaddhaṃ prajāḥ saṃsṛjato 'pi te ||
children.translated_text: because your mind is fastened on me, even while you create creatures.

children.text: jñāto 'haṃ bhavatā tv adya durvijñeyo 'pi dehinām
children.translated_text: Today I have been known by you, though I am hard for embodied beings to know,
because you understand me as not joined with the entities of beings, senses, and <s>guṇas</s>.
When you were doubtful about me, my own self was shown to you, not outside,
as you searched in the water, through the stalk, for the root of the lotus.
The hymn to me that you have made, dear one, marked by the arising of my stories,

children.text: yad vā tapasi te niṣṭhā sa eṣa madanugrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or the firm devotion you have to tapas: this indeed is my grace.

children.text: prīto 'ham astu bhadraṃ te lokānāṃ vijayecchayā
children.translated_text: I am pleased. May there be well-being for you, because of your desire for the victory of the worlds.
by which you praised me, describing me as made of the <s>guṇas</s> and yet without <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: ya etena pumān nityaṃ stutvā stotreṇa māṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: The man who, having praised me with this hymn, worships me always
to him I, the lord who grants every desired boon, would quickly become gracious.
Through works of public merit, austerity, sacrifices, gifts, and absorption in yoga,
the supreme good accomplished for human beings is my pleasure; so those who know reality understand.

children.text: aham ātmātmanāṃ dhātaḥ preṣṭhaḥ san preyasām api
children.translated_text: I, O creator, am the self of selves, dearer even than all dear things.

children.text: ato mayi ratiṃ kuryād dehādir yatkṛte priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should set love on me, for whose sake the body and the rest are dear.
With this self of yours, made of all the Vedas, self-born from yourself,

children.text: prajāḥ sṛja yathāpūrvaṃ yāś ca mayy anuśerate ||
children.translated_text: create the creatures as before, including those that lie asleep within me.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
To him, the creator of the world, when he had spoken thus, the Lord of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>,
the lotus-naveled one, manifest in his own form, then disappeared.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
When the Blessed Lord had vanished, how many kinds of progeny did <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire of the worlds,

children.text: prajāḥ sasarja katidhā daihikīr mānasīr vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mighty one, create, both bodily and mental?

children.text: ye ca me bhagavan pṛṣṭās tvayy arthā bahuvittama
children.translated_text: And the matters about which I have asked you, O blessed one, most knowledgeable in their meaning,
tell them in order, and cut away all our doubts.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ saṃcoditas tena kṣattrā kauṣāravir muniḥ
children.translated_text: Thus urged by him, the <s>kṣattṛ</s>, the sage <s>Kauṣāravi</s>

children.text: prītaḥ pratyāha tān praśnān hṛdisthān atha bhārgava ||
children.translated_text: gladly answered those questions held in his heart, O <s>Bhārgava</s>.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: viriñco 'pi tathā cakre divyaṃ varṣaśataṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viriñci</s> too did so: for a hundred divine years he practiced austerity,

children.text: ātmany ātmānam āveśya yathāha bhagavān ajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: fixing the self in the Self, just as the unborn Blessed Lord had instructed.
Then the lotus-born one saw that the lotus on which he stood, and the water,
were shaken by the wind, whose force had been produced by time.
Through austerity that was increasing, and through knowledge established in the self,
his strength of insight grew, and he subdued the wind together with the water.
Seeing the sky-spanning lotus on which he was standing,
he thought, 'By this I am to arrange the worlds that were formerly dissolved.'
Then, entering the cup of the lotus, impelled by the Blessed Lord's work,

children.text: ekaṃ vyabhāṅkṣīd urudhā tridhā bhāvyaṃ dvisaptadhā ||
children.translated_text: he divided the one into many: into three, and then into fourteen.
This much has been summarized as the division of the world of living beings;

children.text: dharmasya hy animittasya vipākaḥ parameṣṭhy asau ||
children.translated_text: that supreme creator is indeed the fruition of causeless <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
As you have spoken of <s>Hari</s>, of many forms and wondrous deeds,

children.text: kālākhyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brahman yathā varṇaya naḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: so describe for us, O <s>brahman</s>, O lord, the defining mark called time.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
The <s>puruṣa</s>, whose form is the disturbance of the <s>guṇas</s>, undifferentiated and without fixed support,
playfully created himself as the material cause of that world.
The universe, in truth mere <s>brahman</s>, stood established by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>māyā</s>,
delimited by the Lord through time, whose form is unmanifest.

children.text: yathedānīṃ tathāgre ca paścād apy etad īdṛśam
children.translated_text: As it is now, so it was before, and afterward too it will be just so.

children.text: sargo navavidhas tasya prākṛto vaikṛtas tu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its creation is ninefold, both primordial and derivative.
Its return to dissolution is threefold, through time, substance, and the <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: ādyas tu mahataḥ sargo guṇavaiṣamyam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first creation is that of the <s>mahat</s>, the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> of the self.
The second is that of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, where substance, knowledge, and action arise.
The third is the creation of the elements, the subtle element endowed with the power of substance.

children.text: caturtha aindriyaḥ sargo yas tu jñānakriyātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: The fourth is the sensory creation, which consists of cognition and action.
The fifth is the <s>vaikārika</s> creation of the gods, of which mind is made.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhas tu tamasaḥ sargo yas tv abuddhikṛtaḥ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: The sixth is the creation from darkness, produced as uncomprehending by the Lord.

children.text: ṣaḍ ime prākṛtāḥ sargā vaikṛtān api me śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: These six creations are primordial; now hear from me also the derivative ones.
This is the play of the Blessed Lord, possessed of <s>rajas</s>, of <s>Hari</s> in his wisdom.

children.text: saptamo mukhyasargas tu ṣaḍvidhas tasthuṣāṃ ca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The seventh is the primary creation, the sixfold creation of stationary beings.
They are fruit-bearing trees, herbs, creepers, woody plants, shrubs, and trees.
Their current moves upward; they are mostly darkness, inwardly tactile, and individually distinct.
The eighth creation, that of creatures moving sideways, is held to be twenty-eightfold.
They are ignorant, filled with much darkness, knowing by smell and not inwardly discerning.

children.text: gaur ajo mahiṣaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sūkaro gavayo ruruḥ
children.translated_text: The cow, goat, buffalo, black antelope, boar, gayal, and <s>ruru</s> deer,

children.text: dviśaphāḥ paśavaś ceme avir uṣṭraś ca sattama ||
children.translated_text: these are the cloven-hoofed animals, along with the sheep and the camel, O best one.
The ass, horse, mule, <s>gaura</s>, <s>śarabha</s>, and <s>camarī</s> too:

children.text: ete caikaśaphāḥ kṣattaḥ śṛṇu pañcanakhān paśūn ||
children.translated_text: these are the single-hoofed animals, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>; hear now of the five-clawed animals.

children.text: śvā sṛgālo vṛko vyāghro mārjāraḥ śaśaśallakau
children.translated_text: The dog, jackal, wolf, tiger, cat, hare, and porcupine,

children.text: siṃhaḥ kapir gajaḥ kūrmo godhā ca makarādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lion, monkey, elephant, tortoise, monitor lizard, crocodile, and the rest.
Herons, vultures, cranes, hawks, <s>bhāsa</s> birds, <s>bhallūka</s> birds, and peacocks,
swans, <s>sārasa</s> cranes, cakravāka birds, crows, owls, and other birds.

children.text: arvāksrotas tu navamaḥ kṣattar ekavidho nṛṇām
children.translated_text: The ninth, with its current turned downward, is the single creation of human beings, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>.
They are dominated by <s>rajas</s>, devoted to action, and imagine happiness amid suffering.

children.text: vaikṛtās traya evaite devasargaś ca sattama
children.translated_text: These three alone are derivative, along with the creation of the gods, O best one;

children.text: vaikārikas tu yaḥ proktaḥ kaumāras tūbhayātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the one called <s>vaikārika</s>, the <s>kaumāra</s> creation, has both natures.
The creation of the gods is eightfold: the gods, the ancestors, the <s>asuras</s>,
the <s>gandharvas</s> and <s>apsarases</s>, the <s>siddhas</s>, the <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and <s>cāraṇas</s>,
as well as <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>vidyādharas</s>, <s>kiṃnaras</s>, and others.
These ten creations, O <s>Vidura</s>, have been described to you as made by the creator of the universe.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi vaṃśān manvantarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: After this I shall describe the lineages and the <s>manvantaras</s>.

children.text: evaṃ rajaḥplutaḥ sraṣṭā kalpādiṣv ātmabhūr hariḥ
children.translated_text: Thus at the beginnings of kalpas the self-born creator, <s>Hari</s>, steeped in <s>rajas</s>,
whose resolve is unfailing, creates himself by himself from himself.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
The atom should be known as the last of existent particulars, manifold, always uncombined,

children.text: paramāṇuḥ sa vijñeyo nṛṇām aikyabhramo yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: from which there arises among human beings the mistaken notion of unity.
That which belongs to an existent object, abiding in its own form...
singleness, the supreme greatness, without differentiation and uninterrupted.

children.text: evaṃ kālo 'py anumitaḥ saukṣmye sthaulye ca sattama
children.translated_text: Thus time too is inferred, O best of the good, in subtlety and grossness,
through the taking up of configurations and enjoyments; the Blessed Lord is unmanifest, the all-pervading enjoyer of the manifest.

children.text: sa kālaḥ paramāṇur vai yo bhuṅkte paramāṇutām
children.translated_text: That time which takes up the minuteness of a <s>paramāṇu</s> is indeed the atomic moment;

children.text: sato 'viśeṣabhug yas tu sa kālaḥ paramo mahān ||
children.translated_text: but that which takes up the undifferentiated existent is time as the supreme great.

children.text: aṇur dvau paramāṇū syāt trasareṇus trayaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Two <s>paramāṇus</s> make an <s>aṇu</s>; three are remembered as a <s>trasareṇu</s>,
seen in a lattice-sunbeam as it moves through the sky.

children.text: trasareṇutrikaṃ bhuṅkte yaḥ kālaḥ sa truṭiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The time that takes up a triad of <s>trasareṇus</s> is remembered as a <s>truṭi</s>;

children.text: śatabhāgas tu vedhaḥ syāt tais tribhis tu lavaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a hundredth division is a <s>vedha</s>, and by three of those a <s>lava</s> is remembered.

children.text: nimeṣas trilavo jñeya āmnātas te trayaḥ kṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>nimeṣa</s> should be known as three <s>lavas</s>; three of those are taught as a <s>kṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: kṣaṇān pañca viduḥ kāṣṭhāṃ laghu tā daśa pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: They know five <s>kṣaṇas</s> as a <s>kāṣṭhā</s>, and fifteen of those as a <s>laghu</s>.

children.text: laghūni vai samāmnātā daśa pañca ca nāḍikā
children.translated_text: Fifteen <s>laghus</s>, indeed, are traditionally called a <s>nāḍikā</s>;

children.text: te dve muhūrtaḥ praharaḥ ṣaḍ yāmaḥ sapta vā nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: two of those are a <s>muhūrta</s>, and for human beings a <s>prahara</s> or <s>yāma</s> is six or seven.
With a measure of six <s>palas</s>, four fingers across,
and with a hole made by four gold <s>māṣas</s>, it is measured until it is sunk in a <s>prastha</s> of water.

children.text: yāmāś catvāraś catvāro martyānām ahanī ubhe
children.translated_text: Four <s>yāmas</s> and four <s>yāmas</s> are the two parts, day and night, of mortals;

children.text: pakṣaḥ pañcadaśāhāni śuklaḥ kṛṣṇaś ca mānada ||
children.translated_text: a <s>pakṣa</s> is fifteen days, the bright and the dark, O giver of honor.

children.text: tayoḥ samuccayo māsaḥ pitṝṇāṃ tad aharniśam
children.translated_text: The combination of those two is a month; for the ancestors that is their day and night.

children.text: dvau tāv ṛtuḥ ṣaḍ ayanaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ cottaraṃ divi ||
children.translated_text: Two such months are a season; six months are an <s>ayana</s>, southern and northern, in heaven.

children.text: ayane cāhanī prāhur vatsaro dvādaśa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: They call the two <s>ayanas</s> day and night; twelve months are remembered as a year.
A hundred years is defined as the maximum lifespan of human beings.
Situated in the wheel of planets, lunar mansions, and stars, through measures beginning with the <s>paramāṇu</s>, the unblinking all-pervader
travels around the world by the end of a year.
<s>Saṃvatsara</s>, <s>Parivatsara</s>, and also <s>Iḍāvatsara</s>,
<s>Anuvatsara</s> and <s>Vatsara</s>: thus <s>Vidura</s> speaks of them.
He who, by his own power, causes the generative power to breathe forth widely,
the differentiator of beings, runs in heaven to remove the confusion of the person;
by the name of time, extending the <s>guṇa</s>-made world through sacrifices,
offer tribute to him, the five-year cycle.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
This has been remembered as the highest lifespan of ancestors, gods, and human beings.

children.text: pareṣāṃ gatim ācakṣva ye syuḥ kalpād bahir vidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell me the course of those others, O knower, who may be beyond a <s>kalpa</s>.

children.text: bhagavān veda kālasya gatiṃ bhagavato nanu
children.translated_text: Surely the Blessed One knows the course of time and of the Blessed Lord;
the wise perceive the universe with an eye made effective by yoga.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliś ceti caturyugam
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s>: this is the fourfold <s>yuga</s>.
It is determined, together with its transitional portions, as twelve thousand divine years.

children.text: catvāri trīṇi dve caikaṃ kṛtādiṣu yathākramam
children.translated_text: Four, three, two, and one, respectively beginning with <s>Kṛta</s>,
are counted as thousands, and as hundreds doubled as well.
The time between the dawn and twilight portions, reckoned in hundreds,

children.text: tam evāhur yugaṃ tajjñā yatra dharmo vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: that very time the knowers call a <s>yuga</s>, in which <s>dharma</s> is established.
In the <s>Kṛta</s> age, <s>dharma</s> follows human beings with four feet;

children.text: sa evānyeṣv adharmeṇa vyeti pādena vardhatā ||
children.translated_text: in the other ages that same <s>dharma</s> departs by one foot as <s>adharma</s> increases.

children.text: trilokyā yugasāhasraṃ bahir ā brahmaṇo dinam
children.translated_text: Beyond the three worlds, a thousand <s>yugas</s> make a day of <s>Brahmā</s>;

children.text: tāvaty eva niśā tāta yan nimīlati viśvasṛk ||
children.translated_text: just as long is the night, dear one, when the creator of the universe closes his eyes.
At the end of the night the world-<s>kalpa</s> begins and continues

children.text: yāvad dinaṃ bhagavato manūn bhuñjaṃś caturdaśa ||
children.translated_text: for the Blessed Lord's day, passing through fourteen <s>Manus</s>.

children.text: svaṃ svaṃ kālaṃ manur bhuṅkte sādhikāṃ hy ekasaptatim
children.translated_text: Each <s>Manu</s> occupies his own period, a little more than seventy-one <s>yugas</s>.
In the <s>manvantaras</s> there are the <s>Manus</s>, their descendants, the seers, and the gods,

children.text: bhavanti caiva yugapat sureśāś cānu ye ca tān ||
children.translated_text: and at the same time the lords of the gods and those who follow them.
This is the daily creation of <s>Brahmā</s>, the turning of the three worlds,
in which animals, human beings, ancestors, and gods arise through their actions.
In the <s>manvantaras</s> the Blessed Lord, bearing <s>sattva</s> in his own forms,
protects this universe through <s>Manu</s> and the others, his heroic power having arisen.
Taking on only a measure of darkness, his activity checked,
with all the remainder followed by time, he sits silent at the end of the day.

children.text: tam evānv api dhīyante lokā bhūr ādayas trayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the three worlds beginning with <s>Bhūr</s> are drawn into that very one,
when night has continued on, emptied of moon and sun.
As the three worlds are burned by the fire of <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>'s power,
<s>Bhṛgu</s> and the others, afflicted by its heat, go from <s>Maharloka</s> to <s>Janaloka</s>.
Then the seas, swollen at the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, at once the three worlds
flood with waves driven by fierce, violent winds and terrible tumult.

children.text: antaḥ sa tasmin salila āste 'nantāsano hariḥ
children.translated_text: Within that water <s>Hari</s> rests upon <s>Ananta</s> as his seat,
his eyes closed in yogic sleep, praised by the inhabitants of <s>Janaloka</s>.
By days and nights of this kind, marked by the movement of time,
even his maximum lifespan of a hundred years becomes as though diminished.

children.text: yad ardham āyuṣas tasya parārdham abhidhīyate
children.translated_text: That half of his lifespan is called a <s>parārdha</s>;
the former <s>parārdha</s> has passed away, and the latter proceeds now.

children.text: pūrvasyādau parārdhasya brāhmo nāma mahān abhūt
children.translated_text: At the beginning of the former <s>parārdha</s> there was a great <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Brāhma</s>,

children.text: kalpo yatrābhavad brahmā śabdabrahmeti yaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: in which <s>Brahmā</s> came into being, whom they know as <s>Śabdabrahman</s>.

children.text: tasyaiva cānte kalpo 'bhūd yaṃ pādmam abhicakṣate
children.translated_text: At its very end there was the <s>kalpa</s> which they call <s>Pādma</s>,
when the world-lotus arose from <s>Hari</s>'s navel-lake.

children.text: ayaṃ tu kathitaḥ kalpo dvitīyasyāpi bhārata
children.translated_text: But this <s>kalpa</s> has been described as belonging also to the second, O <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: vārāha iti vikhyāto yatrāsīc chūkaro hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: renowned as <s>Vārāha</s>, in which <s>Hari</s> was a boar.
This time, called two <s>parārdhas</s>, is conventionally treated as a <s>nimeṣa</s>
of the unmanifest, endless, beginningless soul of the world.
This time, beginning with the <s>paramāṇu</s> and ending with two <s>parārdhas</s>, is the Lord.
No lord among those proud of their abodes is able to enter it, because of its vastness.
Together with its transformations, and enveloped by the proper differentiations and the rest,
this outer shell of the cosmic egg extends for fifty crores.
There, entered with ten further coverings, it is perceived as if it were an atom,
and within it other masses of cosmic eggs are seen by the crores.
That they call the imperishable <s>brahman</s>, the cause of all causes,

children.text: viṣṇor dhāma paraṃ sākṣāt puruṣasya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, directly that of the great-souled <s>puruṣa</s>.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: iti te varṇitaḥ kṣattaḥ kālākhyaḥ paramātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, the greatness of the Supreme Self called time has been described to you;
now hear from me how the one whose womb is the Veda created.
First the original creator created <s>andhatāmisra</s>, then <s>tāmisra</s>,

children.text: mahāmohaṃ ca mohaṃ ca tamaś cājñānavṛttayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>mahāmoha</s>, <s>moha</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, the functions of ignorance.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā pāpīyasīṃ sṛṣṭiṃ nātmānaṃ bahv amanyata
children.translated_text: Seeing that very sinful creation, he did not think highly of himself.
Then, with a mind purified by meditation on the Blessed Lord, he created another.

children.text: sanakaṃ ca sanandaṃ ca sanātanam athātmabhūḥ
children.translated_text: The self-born one created <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sananda</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>,
and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, sages who were inactive and whose seed was drawn upward.

children.text: tān babhāṣe svabhūḥ putrān prajāḥ sṛjata putrakāḥ
children.translated_text: The self-born one said to those sons, 'Create offspring, my sons.'
But they, devoted to the <s>dharma</s> of liberation and wholly given to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, did not desire that.
Thus disrespected by his own sons, whose obedience to his command had been refused,
he began to restrain the unbearable anger that had arisen.
Though it was being held down by his intelligence, from the middle of the brows of <s>Prajāpati</s>
that anger was at once born as a boy, blue and red.

children.text: sa vai ruroda devānāṃ pūrvajo bhagavān bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: He, the Blessed <s>Bhava</s>, first-born of the gods, cried out,

children.text: nāmāni kuru me dhātaḥ sthānāni ca jagadguro ||
children.translated_text: 'Make names for me, O ordainer, and stations too, O teacher of the world.'

children.text: iti tasya vacaḥ pādmo bhagavān paripālayan
children.translated_text: In order to fulfill those words of his, the lotus-born Blessed Lord

children.text: abhyadhād bhadrayā vācā mā rodīs tat karomi te ||
children.translated_text: spoke with gracious speech: 'Do not cry; I shall do that for you.'

children.text: yad arodīḥ suraśreṣṭha sodvega iva bālakaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Because you cried, O best of the gods, like an anxious child,

children.text: tatas tvām abhidhāsyanti nāmnā rudra iti prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore creatures will call you by the name <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: hṛd indriyāṇy asur vyoma vāyur agnir jalaṃ mahī
children.translated_text: The heart, the senses, the life-breath, space, wind, fire, water, and earth,

children.text: sūryaś candras tapaś caiva sthānāny agre kṛtāni te ||
children.translated_text: the sun, the moon, and austerity: these stations were first made for you.
<s>Manyu</s>, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Mahinasa</s>, <s>Mahān</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Ṛtadhvaja</s>,
<s>Ugraretas</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and <s>Dhṛtavrata</s> are your names.
<s>Dhī</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Asalomā</s>, <s>Niyut</s>, <s>Sarpis</s>, <s>Ilā</s>, and <s>Ambikā</s>,

children.text: irāvatī svadhā dīkṣā rudrāṇyo rudra te striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Irāvatī</s>, <s>Svadhā</s>, and <s>Dīkṣā</s> are the <s>Rudrāṇīs</s>, your wives, O <s>Rudra</s>.
Accept these names and stations, together with wives.

children.text: ebhiḥ sṛja prajā bahvīḥ prajānām asi yat patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With these create many offspring, for you are the lord of creatures.'
Thus commanded by his own teacher, the Blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s>
created beings equal to himself, by the nature of his form made of being.
When <s>Prajāpati</s> observed the troops of <s>Rudras</s> created by <s>Rudra</s>,
innumerable on every side and devouring the world, he became afraid.
'Enough of creatures created like these, O best of the gods,

children.text: mayā saha dahantībhir diśaś cakṣurbhir ulbaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: burning the quarters together with me by their fierce eyes.
Undertake austerity, blessed be you, which brings happiness to all beings.

children.text: tapasaiva yathā pūrvaṃ sraṣṭā viśvam idaṃ bhavān ||
children.translated_text: By austerity alone, as before, you will create this whole universe.
By austerity alone a man readily finds the supreme light, the Blessed <s>Adhokṣaja</s>,
who dwells in the hidden heart of all beings.'
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Thus instructed by <s>Ātmabhū</s>, he circumambulated the lord of speech.

children.text: bāḍham ity amum āmantrya viveśa tapase vanam ||
children.translated_text: Saying 'Very well' and taking leave of him, he entered the forest for austerity.
Then, as he meditated on creation, ten sons were born
from him who was endowed with the Blessed Lord's power, as causes of the continuance of the worlds.
<s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Kratu</s>,

children.text: bhṛgur vasiṣṭho dakṣaś ca daśamas tatra nāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, and <s>Nārada</s> as the tenth were there.
<s>Nārada</s> was born from the lap, and <s>Dakṣa</s> from the thumb of <s>Svayambhū</s>.

children.text: prāṇād vasiṣṭhaḥ saṃjāto bhṛgus tvaci karāt kratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> arose from his breath, <s>Bhṛgu</s> from his skin, and <s>Kratu</s> from his hand.

children.text: pulaho nābhito jajñe pulastyaḥ karṇayor ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pulaha</s> was born from the navel; the sage <s>Pulastya</s> from the ears.
<s>Aṅgiras</s> came from the mouth, <s>Atri</s> from the eye, and <s>Marīci</s> from the mind.

children.text: dharmaḥ stanād dakṣiṇato yatra nārāyaṇaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> came from the right breast, where <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself abides.
<s>Adharma</s> came from the back, whence came Death, terrifying to the world.

children.text: hṛdi kāmo bhruvaḥ krodho lobhaś cādharadacchadāt
children.translated_text: Desire came from the heart, anger from the brows, and greed from the lower lip.

children.text: āsyād vāk sindhavo meḍhrān nirṛtiḥ pāyor aghāśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Speech came from the mouth, the rivers from the penis, and <s>Nirṛti</s>, the abode of sin, from the anus.

children.text: chāyāyāḥ kardamo jajñe devahūtyāḥ patiḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: From his shadow was born <s>Kardama</s>, the lord and husband of <s>Devahūti</s>.

children.text: manaso dehataś cedaṃ jajñe viśvakṛto jagat ||
children.translated_text: And from the mind and body of the maker of the universe this world was born.

children.text: vācaṃ duhitaraṃ tanvīṃ svayambhūr haratīṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Svayambhū</s> desired his slender daughter <s>Vāc</s>, who was stealing his mind.

children.text: akāmāṃ cakame kṣattaḥ sakāma iti naḥ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Though she did not desire him, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, he desired her; so we have heard.

children.text: tam adharme kṛtamatiṃ vilokya pitaraṃ sutāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing their father with his mind set on <s>adharma</s>,
the sages headed by <s>Marīci</s>, his sons, admonished him in confidence:

children.text: naitat pūrvaiḥ kṛtaṃ tvad ye na kariṣyanti cāpare
children.translated_text: 'This was not done by those before you, nor will others do it:

children.text: yas tvaṃ duhitaraṃ gaccher anigṛhyāṅgajaṃ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: that you, a lord, should approach your daughter without restraining the desire born from your body.

children.text: tejīyasām api hy etan na suślokyaṃ jagadguro
children.translated_text: Even for the most powerful this is not praiseworthy, O teacher of the world,

children.text: yadvṛttam anutiṣṭhan vai lokaḥ kṣemāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: for the world follows the conduct of such a one, and thereby becomes fit for its welfare.

children.text: tasmai namo bhagavate ya idaṃ svena rociṣā
children.translated_text: Obeisance to that Blessed Lord who, by his own radiance,

children.text: ātmasthaṃ vyañjayāmāsa sa dharmaṃ pātum arhati ||
children.translated_text: manifested this universe resting within himself; he should protect <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: sa itthaṃ gṛṇataḥ putrān puro dṛṣṭvā prajāpatīn
children.translated_text: Seeing before him those sons, the <s>Prajāpatis</s>, speaking thus,
the lord of the <s>Prajāpatis</s>, ashamed at that time, abandoned his body.

children.text: tāṃ diśo jagṛhur ghorāṃ nīhāraṃ yad vidus tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The quarters took up that dreadful body, which they know as mist, as darkness.

children.text: kadācid dhyāyataḥ sraṣṭur vedā āsaṃś caturmukhāt
children.translated_text: Once, as the creator was meditating, the Vedas came forth from the four mouths,

children.text: kathaṃ srakṣyāmy ahaṃ lokān samavetān yathā purā ||
children.translated_text: as he thought, "How shall I create the worlds, gathered together as before?"
The fourfold priestly rite, the system of ritual action, together with the subordinate Vedas,
the four feet of <s>dharma</s>, and likewise the modes of life of the āśramas came forth.
<s>Vidura</s> said:

children.text: sa vai viśvasṛjām īśo vedādīn mukhato 'sṛjat
children.translated_text: That lord of the creators of the universe created the Vedas and the rest from his mouths.

children.text: yad yad yenāsṛjad devas tan me brūhi tapodhana ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, O treasure of austerity, whatever the god created and by which mouth.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
The Vedas called <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Atharvan</s> he produced from his eastern and other mouths,

children.text: śāstram ijyāṃ stutistomaṃ prāyaścittaṃ vyadhāt kramāt ||
children.translated_text: and, in order, he established recitation, sacrifice, praise-hymn, and expiation.
From his own eastern and other mouths, in order, he created <s>Āyurveda</s>, <s>Dhanurveda</s>, <s>Gāndharvaveda</s>,

children.text: sthāpatyaṃ cāsṛjad vedaṃ kramāt pūrvādibhir mukhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the Veda of architecture, <s>Sthāpatyaveda</s>.
The lord, who sees all, created the histories and Purāṇas, the fifth Veda,
from all his faces together.
From his eastern face came the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> and <s>Uktha</s> sacrifices, then the <s>Purīṣya</s> and <s>Agniṣṭut</s>,
and also the <s>Āptoryāma</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Vājapeya</s>, and <s>Gosava</s>.

children.text: vidyā dānaṃ tapaḥ satyaṃ dharmasyeti padāni ca
children.translated_text: He also created knowledge, giving, austerity, and truth as the feet of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: āśramāṃś ca yathāsaṃkhyam asṛjat saha vṛttibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the āśramas, in their proper order, together with their ways of life.

children.text: sāvitraṃ prājāpatyaṃ ca brāhmaṃ cātha bṛhat tathā
children.translated_text: The <s>Sāvitra</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Brāhma</s>, and then the great <s>Bṛhat</s> were the vows of studentship;
trade, storing grain, living like one who gathers fallen grain, and gleaning were the householders' ways.
For the forest life there were the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>, <s>Vālakhilya</s>, <s>Audumbara</s>, and <s>Phenapa</s> modes;
in renunciation, first came the <s>Kuṭīcaka</s>, then the <s>Bahvoda</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>, and <s>Niṣkriya</s> modes.

children.text: ānvīkṣikī trayī vārttā daṇḍanītis tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Analytical inquiry, the triple Veda, economics, and the science of punishment,

children.text: evaṃ vyāhṛtayaś cāsan praṇavo hy asya dahrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the sacred utterances arose; indeed, the syllable <s>praṇava</s> came from his heart.

children.text: tasyoṣṇig āsīl lomabhyo gāyatrī ca tvaco vibhoḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Uṣṇih</s> metre came from his hairs, and <s>Gāyatrī</s> from the skin of the mighty one;

children.text: triṣṭum māṃsāt snuto 'nuṣṭub jagaty asthnaḥ prajāpateḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Triṣṭubh</s> from his flesh, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> from the sinews, and <s>Jagatī</s> from the bones of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
<s>Paṅkti</s> arose from his marrow, and <s>Bṛhatī</s> came from his life-breath.

children.text: sparśas tasyābhavaj jīvaḥ svaro deha udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Touch was his life-principle, and sound is declared to be his body.

children.text: ūṣmāṇam indriyāṇy āhur antaḥsthā balam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: They call the sibilants his senses, and the semivowels the strength of his self;

children.text: svarāḥ sapta vihāreṇa bhavanti sma prajāpateḥ ||
children.translated_text: the seven notes came into being through the movement of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
For him whose self was the <s>śabdabrahman</s> (brahman as sound), whose nature was manifest and unmanifest,
the supreme, all-pervading <s>brahman</s> shines, strengthened by many powers.

children.text: tato 'parām upādāya sa sargāya mano dadhe
children.translated_text: Then, taking up another body, he set his mind on creation,
for even the creation of the sages of abundant power had not expanded.
Knowing this in his heart, he again reflected, O descendant of <s>Kuru</s>:

children.text: aho adbhutam etan me vyāpṛtasyāpi nityadā ||
children.translated_text: "Ah, this is astonishing for me: although I am constantly engaged,

children.text: na hy edhante prajā nūnaṃ daivam atra vighātakam
children.translated_text: the creatures surely do not increase; here fate must be obstructing them."

children.text: evaṃ yuktakṛtas tasya daivaṃ cāvekṣatas tadā ||
children.translated_text: While he was thus intent on his work and was also observing fate at that time,

children.text: kasya rūpam abhūd dvedhā yat kāyam abhicakṣate
children.translated_text: his body became divided into two forms, which people call <s>kāya</s>.
From those two divided forms a pair came into being.

children.text: yas tu tatra pumān so 'bhūn manuḥ svāyambhuvaḥ svarāṭ
children.translated_text: The male among them became <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>, the self-ruling sovereign,

children.text: strī yāsīc chatarūpākhyā mahiṣy asya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the female was named <s>Śatarūpā</s>, the queen of that great-souled one.
Then, through the law of pairing, creatures began to increase,
and he also begot five children on <s>Śatarūpā</s>.
They were <s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s>, and three daughters, O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>:

children.text: ākūtir devahūtiś ca prasūtir iti sattama ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ākūti</s>, <s>Devahūti</s>, and <s>Prasūti</s>, O best of the virtuous.

children.text: ākūtiṃ rucaye prādāt kardamāya tu madhyamām
children.translated_text: He gave <s>Ākūti</s> to <s>Ruci</s>, and the middle daughter to <s>Kardama</s>.

children.text: dakṣāyādāt prasūtiṃ ca yata āpūritaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: He gave <s>Prasūti</s> to <s>Dakṣa</s>, from whom the world was filled.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: niśamya vācaṃ vadato muneḥ puṇyatamāṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: Hearing the supremely holy speech spoken by the sage, O king,
the <s>Kaurava</s>, intent on the tale of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, asked again.
<s>Vidura</s> said:

children.text: sa vai svāyambhuvaḥ samrāṭ priyaḥ putraḥ svayambhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: That emperor <s>Svāyambhuva</s>, dear son of the self-born one,

children.text: pratilabhya priyāṃ patnīṃ kiṃ cakāra tato mune ||
children.translated_text: after obtaining his beloved wife, what did he do then, O sage?
Tell me, who am full of faith, the conduct of that royal sage, the first king, O best one,

children.text: brūhi me śraddadhānāya viṣvaksenāśrayo hy asau ||
children.translated_text: for he took refuge in <s>Viṣvaksena</s>.

children.text: śrutasya puṃsāṃ suciraśramasya nanv añjasā sūribhir īḍito 'rthaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely the easily attained purpose of men's long labor in hearing, praised by the wise,
is repeated hearing of the qualities of him whose lotus-feet, <s>Mukunda</s>'s, dwell in their hearts.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: iti bruvāṇaṃ viduraṃ vinītaṃ sahasraśīrṣṇaś caraṇopadhānam
children.translated_text: As the humble <s>Vidura</s> spoke thus, resting at the feet of the thousand-headed Lord,
the sage, his hair bristling with joy in the story of the Blessed One, being drawn onward, replied.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: yadā svabhāryayā sārdhaṃ jātaḥ svāyambhuvo manuḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s> had arisen together with his own wife,
with joined palms and bowed down, he addressed him who held the Veda in his womb:

children.text: tvam ekaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ janmakṛd vṛttidaḥ pitā
children.translated_text: "You alone are the creator of birth, the giver of livelihood, and the father of all beings.

children.text: tathāpi naḥ prajānāṃ te śuśrūṣā kena vā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Even so, by what service may we, your creatures, serve you?

children.text: tad vidhehi namas tubhyaṃ karmasv īḍyātmaśaktiṣu
children.translated_text: Therefore ordain it; homage to you. Tell us the actions connected with your praiseworthy powers,

children.text: yat kṛtveha yaśo viṣvag amutra ca bhaved gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by doing which fame may arise everywhere here, and there may be a goal hereafter."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: prītas tubhyam ahaṃ tāta svasti stād vāṃ kṣitīśvara
children.translated_text: I am pleased with you, dear son. May there be well-being for you both, O lord of the earth,

children.text: yan nirvyalīkena hṛdā śādhi mety ātmanārpitam ||
children.translated_text: since with a guileless heart you have surrendered yourself and said, "Command me."

children.text: etāvaty ātmajair vīra kāryā hy apacitir gurau
children.translated_text: This much, O hero, is indeed the honor that sons must render to a teacher:
with all their power, vigilant, respectful, and free from envy, they should receive his instruction.

children.text: sa tvam asyām apatyāni sadṛśāny ātmano guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: So you, begetting in this woman offspring equal to yourself in qualities,

children.text: utpādya śāsa dharmeṇa gāṃ yajñaiḥ puruṣaṃ yaja ||
children.translated_text: rule the earth according to <s>dharma</s>, and worship the <s>Puruṣa</s> with sacrifices.

children.text: paraṃ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ mahyaṃ syāt prajārakṣayā nṛpa
children.translated_text: The highest service to me, O king, will be through protecting the subjects;
the Blessed <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> will be pleased with you as protector of the people.

children.text: yeṣāṃ na tuṣṭo bhagavān yajñaliṅgo janārdanaḥ
children.translated_text: But those with whom the Blessed <s>Janārdana</s>, whose sign is sacrifice, is not pleased

children.text: teṣāṃ śramo hy apārthāya yad ātmā nādṛtaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: Their toil is indeed for no purpose, since the self itself is not honored.
<s>Manu</s> said:
At the command of the Blessed Lord I shall act, O destroyer of foes.

children.text: sthānaṃ tv ihānujānīhi prajānāṃ mama ca prabho ||
children.translated_text: But here, O lord, grant a dwelling place for my offspring and for me.

children.text: yad okaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ mahī magnā mahāmbhasi
children.translated_text: The earth, the home of all beings, is sunk in the great waters.

children.text: asyā uddharaṇe yatno deva devyā vidhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: O god, let effort be undertaken to raise this goddess up.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: parameṣṭhī tv apāṃ madhye tathā sannām avekṣya gām
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, seeing the earth thus sunk amid the waters,

children.text: katham enāṃ samunneṣya iti dadhyau dhiyā ciram ||
children.translated_text: pondered for a long time in his mind, 'How shall I lift her up?'

children.text: sṛjato me kṣitir vārbhiḥ plāvyamānā rasāṃ gatā
children.translated_text: 'As I create, the earth, being flooded by waters, has gone down to the Rasā region.
So what should now be done here by us, who have been appointed to the work of creation?

children.text: yasyāhaṃ hṛdayād āsaṃ sa īśo vidadhātu me ||
children.translated_text: May that Lord from whose heart I arose direct me.'
While he was reflecting in this way, O sinless one, from the opening of his nostril
there suddenly came forth a young boar, the size of a thumb.
As he watched, it stood in the sky and, in a moment, O <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: gajamātraḥ pravavṛdhe tad adbhutam abhūn mahat ||
children.translated_text: grew to the size of an elephant; that became a great wonder.
Together with the sages headed by <s>Marīci</s>, with the <s>Kumāras</s>, and with <s>Manu</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tat saukaraṃ rūpaṃ tarkayāmāsa citradhā ||
children.translated_text: he saw that boar-form and reasoned about it in many ways.

children.text: kim etat sūkaravyājaṃ sattvaṃ divyam avasthitam
children.translated_text: 'What is this divine being standing here in the guise of a boar?

children.text: aho batāścaryam idaṃ nāsāyā me viniḥsṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Ah, indeed, this wonder has come out of my nostril.
Seen first as only the tip of a thumb, in a moment it is like a massive boulder.

children.text: api svid bhagavān eṣa yajño me khedayan manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Can this perhaps be the Blessed Lord, <s>Yajña</s> (sacrifice), bewildering my mind?'

children.text: iti mīmāṃsatas tasya brahmaṇaḥ saha sūnubhiḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Brahmā</s> was thus deliberating with his sons,
the Blessed Lord, the <s>yajña-puruṣa</s> (sacrificial person), roared like a lordly elephant.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ harṣayāmāsa haris tāṃś ca dvijottamān
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, the mighty one, gladdened <s>Brahmā</s> and those best of twice-born sages
with his own roar, which made the quarters resound.
Hearing the rumbling sound of the magical boar, which would destroy their distress,

children.text: janastapaḥsatyanivāsinas te tribhiḥ pavitrair munayo 'gṛṇan sma ||
children.translated_text: the sages dwelling in <s>Janas</s>, <s>Tapas</s>, and <s>Satya</s> praised him with the three sacred Vedas.
For those holy ones, he was the embodied expanse of the Veda; discerning <s>Brahmā</s>'s praise of his own qualities,

children.text: vinadya bhūyo vibudhodayāya gajendralīlo jalam āviveśa ||
children.translated_text: he roared again for the awakening of the gods and, playing like a lordly elephant, entered the water.

children.text: utkṣiptavālaḥ khacaraḥ kaṭhoraḥ saṭā vidhunvan khararomaśatvak
children.translated_text: With tail raised, moving through the sky, fierce, shaking his mane, with rough bristling hide,

children.text: khurāhatābhraḥ sitadaṃṣṭra īkṣājyotir babhāse bhagavān mahīdhraḥ ||
children.translated_text: striking the clouds with his hooves, white-tusked, and bright with the light of his gaze, the Blessed Lord shone like a mountain.

children.text: ghrāṇena pṛthvyāḥ padavīṃ vijighran kroḍāpadeśaḥ svayam adhvarāṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: Smelling out the path of the earth with his snout, he himself, under the designation of a boar, was the limb of the sacrifice.

children.text: karāladaṃṣṭro 'py akarāladṛgbhyām udvīkṣya viprān gṛṇato 'viśat kam ||
children.translated_text: Though his tusks were terrible, with eyes not terrible he looked up at the praising sages and entered the water.
The ocean, its belly split by the speed of the fall of his body, hard as a thunderbolt peak, thundered aloud,

children.text: utsṛṣṭadīrghormibhujair ivārtaś cukrośa yajñeśvara pāhi meti ||
children.translated_text: and, as if distressed, cried out with long wave-arms flung up, 'O Lord of sacrifice, protect me!'

children.text: khuraiḥ kṣuraprair darayaṃs tad āpa utpārapāraṃ triparū rasāyām
children.translated_text: Tearing those waters with his razor-edged hooves, he passed beyond their far shore and into the Rasā region.

children.text: dadarśa gāṃ tatra suṣupsur agre yāṃ jīvadhānīṃ svayam abhyadhatta ||
children.translated_text: There he saw the earth lying as if asleep, the bearer of living beings, which he himself had previously deposited there.

children.text: pātālamūleśvarabhogasaṃhatau vinyasya pādau pṛthivīṃ ca bibhrataḥ
children.translated_text: Placing his feet upon the mass formed by the serpent-lords' hoods at the base of <s>Pātāla</s>, and bearing the earth,

children.text: yasyopamāno na babhūva so 'cyuto mamāstu māṅgalyavivṛddhaye hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Acyuta</s>, to whom there was no comparison, may <s>Hari</s> be for the increase of my auspiciousness.

children.text: svadaṃṣṭrayoddhṛtya mahīṃ nimagnāṃ sa utthitaḥ saṃruruce rasāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Having raised the sunken earth with his own tusk, he rose up from the Rasā region and shone forth,
while even there a daitya, falling upon him with a mace, had his fierce anger inflamed by the discus <s>Sunābha</s>.

children.text: jaghāna rundhānam asahyavikramaṃ sa līlayebhaṃ mṛgarāḍ ivāmbhasi
children.translated_text: He slew that one, who was blocking him with irresistible valor, as a lion playfully kills an elephant in the water.
His cheeks and snout were marked with that blood like a lordly elephant breaking through the earth.
Seeing him dark blue like a tamāla tree, lifting the earth on the tip of his white tusk with the playfulness of an elephant,
the sages headed by <s>Viriñci</s>, with hands joined, approached the Lord with Vedic recitations.
The sages said:

children.text: jitaṃ jitaṃ te 'jita yajñabhāvana trayīṃ tanuṃ svāṃ paridhunvate namaḥ
children.translated_text: Victory, victory to you, O unconquered nourisher of sacrifice; homage to you who shake your own body, the triple Veda.

children.text: yadromagarteṣu nililyur addhayas tasmai namaḥ kāraṇasūkarāya te ||
children.translated_text: In the pits of whose hairs the sacrifices lay hidden, to you, the causal boar, homage.

children.text: rūpaṃ tavaitan nanu duṣkṛtātmanāṃ durdarśanaṃ deva yad adhvarātmakam
children.translated_text: This form of yours, O god, which is made of sacrifice, is indeed hard to behold for evildoing souls.

children.text: chandāṃsi yasya tvaci barhiromasv ājyaṃ dṛśi tv aṅghriṣu cāturhotram ||
children.translated_text: The metres are upon its skin, the sacred grass is in its hairs, the ghee is in its eyes, and the four priestly offices are in its feet.

children.text: srak tuṇḍa āsīt sruva īśa nāsayor iḍodare camasāḥ karṇarandhre
children.translated_text: The garland was your snout, O Lord; the ladle was in your nostrils, the iḍā vessel in your belly, and the cups in the openings of your ears.

children.text: prāśitram āsye grasane grahās tu te yac carvaṇaṃ te bhagavann agnihotram ||
children.translated_text: The sacrificial portion was in your mouth, the grahas were in your throat, and your chewing, O Blessed One, is the agnihotra.
Consecration is your birth, the upasads are your neck, and your tusks are the prāyaṇīya and udayanīya rites.

children.text: jihvā pravargyas tava śīrṣakaṃ kratoḥ satyāvasathyaṃ citayo 'savo hi te ||
children.translated_text: Your tongue is the pravargya; your head is the head of the rite; the satyā and āvasathya fires, and the piled altars, are indeed your vital breaths.

children.text: somas tu retaḥ savanāny avasthitiḥ saṃsthāvibhedās tava deva dhātavaḥ
children.translated_text: The soma is your seed, the pressings are your bodily states, and the different conclusions of sacrifice are your bodily constituents, O god.

children.text: sattrāṇi sarvāṇi śarīrasaṃdhis tvaṃ sarvayajñakratur iṣṭibandhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All sattra rites are the joints of your body; you are every sacrificial rite and the bond of the iṣṭis.
Homage, homage to you, who are all mantras, deities, and substances, who are every rite and whose nature is action.
Homage again and again to you, whose knowledge is realized through detachment, devotion, and mastery of the self, the teacher of wisdom.

children.text: daṃṣṭrāgrakoṭyā bhagavaṃs tvayā dhṛtā virājate bhūdhara bhūḥ sabhūdharā
children.translated_text: O Blessed one, O bearer of the earth, the earth with its mountains, held by you on the tip of your tusk, shines forth,

children.text: yathā vanān niḥsarato datā dhṛtā mataṃgajendrasya sapattrapadminī ||
children.translated_text: like a lotus plant with leaves held by the tusk of a lordly elephant as he emerges from a forest.

children.text: trayīmayaṃ rūpam idaṃ ca saukaraṃ bhūmaṇḍalenātha datā dhṛtena te
children.translated_text: And this boar-form of yours, made of the triple Veda, with the orb of the earth held upon your tusk, O Lord,

children.text: cakāsti śṛṅgoḍhaghanena bhūyasā kulācalendrasya yathaiva vibhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: shines like the splendor of the chief of great family-mountains, whose peak bears a dense cloud.

children.text: saṃsthāpayaināṃ jagatāṃ satasthuṣāṃ lokāya patnīm asi mātaraṃ pitā
children.translated_text: Establish her, the mother of the worlds of moving and unmoving beings, for their welfare; you are the father, and she is your wife.

children.text: vidhema cāsyai namasā saha tvayā yasyāṃ svatejo 'gnim ivāraṇāv adhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with you we pay homage to her with bowed reverence, she in whom you placed your own splendor as fire is placed in the fire-sticks.

children.text: kaḥ śraddadhītānyatamas tava prabho rasāṃ gatāyā bhuva udvibarhaṇam
children.translated_text: Who could believe that anyone other than you, O Lord, could lift up the earth after she had gone down to <s>Rasā</s>?

children.text: na vismayo 'sau tvayi viśvavismaye yo māyayedaṃ sasṛje 'tivismayam ||
children.translated_text: Yet this is no wonder in you, the wonder of the universe, who by <s>māyā</s> created this exceedingly wondrous world.

children.text: vidhunvatā vedamayaṃ nijaṃ vapur janastapaḥsatyanivāsino vayam
children.translated_text: As you shook your own body, made of the Veda, we who dwell in <s>Jana</s>, <s>Tapas</s>, and <s>Satya</s>
were intensely purified, O Lord, by the auspicious drops of water flung from the tips of your bristles.

children.text: sa vai bata bhraṣṭamatis tavaiṣate yaḥ karmaṇāṃ pāram apārakarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Alas, one whose mind has fallen away is the man who seeks the limit of your deeds, though your deeds are boundless.

children.text: yad yogamāyāguṇayogamohitaṃ viśvaṃ samastaṃ bhagavan vidhehi śam ||
children.translated_text: O Blessed Lord, bring peace to the whole universe, deluded by the conjunction of the <s>guṇas</s> through your <s>yogamāyā</s>.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Thus being praised by sages who speak of <s>brahman</s>,
he, standing in the water pressed by his own hoofs, set down the earth he had protected.

children.text: sa itthaṃ bhagavān urvīṃ viṣvaksenaḥ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: In this way the Blessed Lord, <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, lord of creatures,

children.text: rasāyā līlayonnītām apsu nyasya yayau hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: having playfully lifted the earth from <s>Rasā</s>, placed her upon the waters and departed as <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: ya evam etāṃ harimedhaso hareḥ kathāṃ subhadrāṃ kathanīyamāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever thus hears with devotion, or causes others to hear, this auspicious tale of <s>Hari</s>, whose wisdom is divine and whose <s>māyā</s> is worthy of narration,

children.text: śṛṇvīta bhaktyā śravayeta vośatīṃ janārdano 'syāśu hṛdi prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: for that person <s>Janārdana</s> quickly becomes gracious in the heart.

children.text: tasmin prasanne sakalāśiṣāṃ prabhau kiṃ durlabhaṃ tābhir alaṃ lavātmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: When he, the lord of all blessings, is pleased, what is hard to obtain? Enough of those blessings, which are only tiny in measure.

children.text: ananyadṛṣṭyā bhajatāṃ guhāśayaḥ svayaṃ vidhatte svagatiṃ paraḥ parām ||
children.translated_text: For those who worship with undivided vision, the Supreme, dwelling in the hidden heart, himself grants his own highest state.

children.text: ko nāma loke puruṣārthasāravit purākathānāṃ bhagavatkathāsudhām
children.translated_text: Who in the world, knowing the essence of the aims of human life, after drinking through cupped ears the nectar of ancient tales, the tales of the Blessed Lord,

children.text: āpīya karṇāñjalibhir bhavāpahām aho virajyeta vinā naretaram ||
children.translated_text: which remove worldly existence, would ever turn away from it, except one who is less than human?
<s>Śrīśuka</s> said:
Having heard from <s>Kauṣāravi</s> the story of <s>Hari</s> in the form of the causal boar,

children.text: punaḥ sa papraccha tam udyatāñjalir na cātitṛpto viduro dhṛtavrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidura</s>, firm in his vow and not yet fully satisfied, again questioned him with raised, folded hands.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
By that very <s>Hari</s>, best of sages, whose form is sacrifice,
we have heard that <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, the primordial <s>Daitya</s>, was killed.
As he was playfully lifting the earth on the tip of his own tusk,

children.text: daityarājasya ca brahman kasmāddhetor abhūn mṛdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for what reason, O <s>brahman</s>, did battle arise with the king of the <s>Daityas</s>?
Tell me, a faithful devotee, the full account of his birth,

children.text: ṛṣe na tṛpyati manaḥ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me ||
children.translated_text: O seer; my mind is not satisfied, for I have the highest curiosity.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: sādhu vīra tvayā pṛṣṭam avatārakathāṃ hareḥ
children.translated_text: Well asked, O hero: you ask about the tale of <s>Hari</s>'s avatāra,
which cuts apart the noose of death for mortals.
By that tale, sung by the sage, the son of <s>Uttānapāda</s>, though only a child,

children.text: mṛtyoḥ kṛtvaiva mūrdhny aṅghrim āruroha hareḥ padam ||
children.translated_text: placed his foot upon the very head of death and ascended to the abode of <s>Hari</s>.
And this ancient story too was heard by me here, described long ago
by <s>Brahmā</s>, the god of gods, when the gods questioned him.

children.text: ditir dākṣāyaṇī kṣattar mārīcaṃ kaśyapaṃ patim
children.translated_text: <s>Diti</s>, daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, O <s>Kṣattar</s>, desiring offspring, desired her husband <s>Kaśyapa</s>, descendant of <s>Marīci</s>,
being afflicted by the desire in her heart at twilight.
After worshiping with milk the <s>Puruṣa</s> whose tongue is fire, the lord of the <s>Yajus</s>,
he was seated, composed, in the fire-chamber as the sun was setting.
<s>Diti</s> said:

children.text: eṣa māṃ tvatkṛte vidvan kāma āttaśarāsanaḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>Kāma</s>, learned one, has taken up his bow because of you,

children.text: dunoti dīnāṃ vikramya rambhām iva mataṃgajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, attacking, torments me in my distress, as a rutting elephant torments a plantain tree.
Therefore may you, blessed sir, show favor to me, who am burning

children.text: prajāvatīnāṃ bhadraṃ te mayy āyuṅktām anugraham ||
children.translated_text: because of the prosperity of my co-wives who have children.
The fame of women who have obtained honor through their husband enters the worlds;

children.text: patir bhavadvidho yāsāṃ prajayā nanu jāyate ||
children.translated_text: for a husband such as you is indeed born again through the offspring of those women.

children.text: purā pitā no bhagavān dakṣo duhitṛvatsalaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago our blessed father <s>Dakṣa</s>, affectionate toward his daughters,

children.text: kaṃ vṛṇīta varaṃ vatsā ity apṛcchata naḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: asked each of us separately, 'Children, whom do you choose as your husband?'
Knowing the disposition of us, his own daughters, and concerned for offspring,

children.text: trayodaśādadāt tāsāṃ yās te śīlam anuvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: he gave to you thirteen of them, those whose nature followed yours.

children.text: atha me kuru kalyāṇaṃ kāmaṃ kamalalocana
children.translated_text: Now fulfill my desire, lotus-eyed one, and do me this good,
O abundant one; approaching the great in distress is never fruitless.

children.text: iti tāṃ vīra mārīcaḥ kṛpaṇāṃ bahubhāṣiṇīm
children.translated_text: Thus, O hero, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, son of <s>Marīci</s>, replied to her, pitiable and speaking at length,
soothing her with words, though she was stained by greatly increased passion.

children.text: eṣa te 'haṃ vidhāsyāmi priyaṃ bhīru yad icchasi
children.translated_text: Here I am; I shall do for you the pleasing thing that you desire, timid one.

children.text: tasyāḥ kāmaṃ na kaḥ kuryāt siddhis traivargikī yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who would not satisfy the desire of her from whom success in the three aims of life comes?
The married man, supporting all the <s>āśramas</s> by means of his own <s>āśrama</s>,
crosses the ocean of misfortunes as one crosses the ocean by boats.

children.text: yām āhur ātmano hy ardhaṃ śreyaskāmasya mānini
children.translated_text: She whom they call half of one's own self for a man who seeks welfare, O proud lady,

children.text: yasyāṃ svadhuram adhyasya pumāṃś carati vijvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: upon whom a man places his own burden, he then acts free from fever.
Relying on her, we may easily conquer the hostile senses, hard to conquer by the other <s>āśramas</s>,

children.text: vayaṃ jayema helābhir dasyūn durgapatir yathā ||
children.translated_text: as the lord of a fortress conquers bandits.

children.text: na vayaṃ prabhavas tāṃ tvām anukartuṃ gṛheśvari
children.translated_text: We are not able to repay you, O mistress of the house,

children.text: apy āyuṣā vā kārtsnyena ye cānye guṇagṛdhnavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even with an entire lifetime, nor are others who prize good qualities able to do so.

children.text: athāpi kāmam etaṃ te prajātyai karavāṇy alam
children.translated_text: Even so, I shall fulfill this desire of yours for the sake of offspring; that is enough.
Wait for one <s>muhūrta</s>, so that people do not reproach me.
This is a most dreadful time, frightful and dreadful to behold,
during which beings, the attendants of the lord of beings, wander about.
At this twilight, good lady, the Blessed <s>Bhūtabhāvana</s>,
the king of beings, surrounded by hosts of beings, roams on his bull.
His mass of matted hair gleams, scattered and smoky with dust raised by the wind circling the cremation ground.

children.text: bhasmāvaguṇṭhāmalarukmadeho devas tribhiḥ paśyati devaras te ||
children.translated_text: The god, your kinsman by marriage, whose spotless golden body is covered with ashes, sees with three eyes.

children.text: na yasya loke svajanaḥ paro vā nātyādṛto nota kaścid vigarhyaḥ
children.translated_text: In this world he has no one who is his own or another's, no one specially honored, and no one condemned.

children.text: vayaṃ vratair yac caraṇāpaviddhām āśāsmahe 'jāṃ bata bhuktabhogām ||
children.translated_text: Alas, by vows we long for that unborn power, already enjoyed, which has been cast off by his feet.
The wise, wishing to pierce the veil of ignorance, sing of his blameless conduct.

children.text: nirastasāmyātiśayo 'pi yat svayaṃ piśācacaryām acarad gatiḥ satām ||
children.translated_text: Though he himself has no equal or superior, he, the goal of the good, adopted the conduct of a <s>piśāca</s>.

children.text: hasanti yasyācaritaṃ hi durbhagāḥ svātman ratasyāviduṣaḥ samīhitam
children.translated_text: Unfortunate fools laugh at the conduct of him who delights in his own self, not knowing his intention.
With garments, garlands, ornaments, and ointments they cherish as the self a body that is food for dogs.

children.text: brahmādayo yatkṛtasetupālā yatkāraṇaṃ viśvam idaṃ ca māyā
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and the others guard the limits established by him; this universe and <s>māyā</s> exist for his purpose.

children.text: ājñākarī yasya piśācacaryā aho vibhūmnaś caritaṃ viḍambanam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>piśāca</s>-like conduct of him whose command they obey is, ah, a deceptive display of his greatness.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
When she had thus been understood by her husband, her senses stirred up by passion,
she seized the garment of the brahmin-sage, shameless like a low-born woman.

children.text: sa viditvātha bhāryāyās taṃ nirbandhaṃ vikarmaṇi
children.translated_text: Then, knowing that insistence of his wife upon an improper act,
he bowed to fate and privately sat down with her.
Afterward he sipped water, restrained his breaths, and, controlling his speech,

children.text: dhyāyañ jajāpa virajaṃ brahma jyotiḥ sanātanam ||
children.translated_text: meditated and recited the stainless, eternal light of <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: ditis tu vrīḍitā tena karmāvadyena bhārata
children.translated_text: But <s>Diti</s>, ashamed by that blameworthy act, O <s>Bhārata</s>,
approached the brahmin-sage and, with her face lowered, spoke to him.
<s>Diti</s> said:

children.text: na me garbham imaṃ brahman bhūtānām ṛṣabho 'vadhīt
children.translated_text: O brahmin, may <s>Rudra</s>, the foremost of beings, not kill this embryo of mine,

children.text: rudraḥ patir hi bhūtānāṃ yasyākaravam aṃhasam ||
children.translated_text: for he is the lord of beings, against whom I have committed an offense.
Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, the great god, the fierce one, the gracious giver of rain.
Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, who has laid aside the rod, and to wrath, which bears the rod.

children.text: sa naḥ prasīdatāṃ bhāmo bhagavān urvanugrahaḥ
children.translated_text: May the radiant Blessed One, whose grace is vast, be pleased with us.
The god, husband of <s>Satī</s>, shows compassion even to women whom a hunter would pity.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
As she trembled, hoping for a worldly blessing for her own offspring,
the progenitor, whose twilight observance was finished, spoke to his wife.
<s>Kaśyapa</s> said:

children.text: aprāyatyād ātmanas te doṣān mauhūrtikād uta
children.translated_text: Because of your own impurity, because of the fault of the moment,
because you transgressed my instruction and greatly insulted the gods,
two inauspicious, lowest beings will arise from your womb, O inauspicious fierce woman,

children.text: lokān sapālāṃs trīṃś caṇḍi muhur ākrandayiṣyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and again and again they will make the three worlds, together with their protectors, cry out.
When helpless living beings, who have done no wrong, are being killed,
when women are being oppressed, and when the great-souled are provoked,
then the Blessed Lord, the Lord of the universe and creator of the worlds, will become angry,
and he will descend and kill them, as the bearer of the hundred-jointed thunderbolt strikes mountains.
<s>Diti</s> said:
I hope for the death of my two sons directly by the Blessed Lord, whose navel is beautiful and whose arms are noble,

children.text: āśāse putrayor mahyaṃ mā kruddhād brāhmaṇāt prabho ||
children.translated_text: and not from an angry brahmin, O lord.
For one burned by a brahmin's rod, and one who causes fear to beings,

children.text: nārakāś cānugṛhṇanti yāṃ yāṃ yonim asau gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: are not favored even by hellish beings, whatever womb such a person enters.
<s>Kaśyapa</s> said:
Because of your grief and remorse, because you reflected immediately,

children.text: bhagavaty urumānāc ca bhave mayy api cādarāt ||
children.translated_text: because of your great respect for the Blessed Lord, and because of your regard for <s>Bhava</s> and for me,

children.text: putrasyaiva ca putrāṇāṃ bhavitaikaḥ satāṃ mataḥ
children.translated_text: one among the sons of your son will be approved by the good.
They will sing his pure fame, equal to the fame of the Blessed Lord.
As impure gold is refined by processes, so the virtuous will purify themselves
through freedom from enmity and the like, in order to follow his character.
By his grace this universe, whose essence is that Lord, becomes gracious.

children.text: sa svadṛg bhagavān yasya toṣyate 'nanyayā dṛśā ||
children.translated_text: The self-seeing Blessed Lord is pleased by his undivided vision.

children.text: sa vai mahābhāgavato mahātmā mahānubhāvo mahatāṃ mahiṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: He will indeed be a great devotee, a great soul, mighty, the greatest among the great.

children.text: pravṛddhabhaktyā hy anubhāvitāśaye niveśya vaikuṇṭham imaṃ vihāsyati ||
children.translated_text: With his inner being formed by deepening devotion, he will set <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> within it and leave this world behind.

children.text: alampaṭaḥ śīladharo guṇākaro hṛṣṭaḥ pararddhyā vyathito duḥkhiteṣu
children.translated_text: Free from greed, firm in conduct, a storehouse of virtues, joyful at others' prosperity and pained among the distressed,

children.text: abhūtaśatrur jagataḥ śokahartā naidāghikaṃ tāpam ivoḍurājaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he will have no enemy, and will remove the world's sorrow like the moon removing the heat of summer.
Your grandson will see, within and without, the spotless lotus-eyed Lord, whose form is graciously assumed according to his devotee's wish,
with <s>Śrī</s>, the ornament among women, and with a face adorned by flashing earrings.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: śrutvā bhāgavataṃ pautram amodata ditir bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Hearing of her grandson, a devotee of the Blessed Lord, <s>Diti</s> rejoiced greatly.

children.text: putrayoś ca vadhaṃ kṛṣṇād viditvāsīn mahāmanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And knowing that her two sons would be slain by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, she became high-minded.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: prājāpatyaṃ tu tat tejaḥ paratejohanaṃ ditiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Diti</s> bore that seed of the progenitor, destructive of others' power,
for a hundred years, fearing that it would bring harm to the gods.
When the worlds' light had been struck down by it, the guardians of the worlds, their brilliance lost,
reported to the creator of the universe the thick darkness of the directions.
The gods said:

children.text: tama etad vibho vettha saṃvignā yad vayaṃ bhṛśam
children.translated_text: O lord, you know this darkness, because of which we are deeply alarmed.
For nothing is unmanifest to the Blessed One, whose path is untouched by time.
O god of gods, sustainer of the universe, crest-jewel of the lords of the worlds,

children.text: pareṣām apareṣāṃ tvaṃ bhūtānām asi bhāvavit ||
children.translated_text: you know the dispositions of higher and lower beings.
Homage to you whose power is knowledge, who has approached this world through <s>māyā</s>.
Homage to you who have taken on the distinctions of the <s>guṇas</s>, whose source is unmanifest.
Those who contemplate you with undivided devotion, as the source of the self,
as the supreme reality, whose nature is being and non-being, in whom the worlds are woven within the self,
those whose yoga is well ripened, whose breath, senses, and self are conquered,
and who have obtained your grace, suffer defeat from no quarter.

children.text: yasya vācā prajāḥ sarvā gāvas tantyeva yantritāḥ
children.translated_text: By his speech all creatures are controlled, like cattle by a rope.

children.text: haranti balim āyattās tasmai mukhyāya te namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those dependent beings bring tribute to him, the chief; homage to you.

children.text: sa tvaṃ vidhatsva śaṃ bhūmaṃs tamasā luptakarmaṇām
children.translated_text: Therefore you, O mighty one, grant welfare to those whose actions have been lost in darkness;
with your abundant compassion and your glance, you ought to behold those who are distressed.

children.text: eṣa deva diter garbha ojaḥ kāśyapam arpitam
children.translated_text: This, O god, is the embryo of <s>Diti</s>, the vigor of <s>Kaśyapa</s> deposited in her;
darkening all the quarters, it grows like fire in fuel.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Then, O mighty-armed one, the Blessed Lord, who is known through sound, smiled
and answered the gods, pleasing them with charming speech.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
My mind-born sons, beginning with <s>Sanaka</s>, your elders,
moved through the worlds by the path of the sky, free from longing amid the worlds.
One day they went to the abode of the Blessed <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, whose self is stainless,
the dwelling called <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, honored by all the worlds.
There dwell persons who all have forms like <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,
who worship <s>Hari</s> through <s>dharma</s> (righteous devotion) that has no ulterior cause.

children.text: yatra cādyaḥ pumān āste bhagavān śabdagocaraḥ
children.translated_text: There the primeval Person, the Blessed Lord known through sound, abides,

children.text: sattvaṃ viṣṭabhya virajaṃ svānāṃ no mṛḍayan vṛṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: upholding stainless <s>sattva</s> and kindly favoring his own people, the embodiment of righteousness.

children.text: yatra naiḥśreyasaṃ nāma vanaṃ kāmadughair drumaiḥ
children.translated_text: There is a forest named <s>Naiḥśreyasa</s>, with trees that yield every desire,
shining with the beauties of all seasons, like liberation itself embodied.

children.text: vaimānikāḥ salalanāś caritāni śaśvad gāyanti yatra śamalakṣapaṇāni bhartuḥ
children.translated_text: There the aerial beings, together with their women, constantly sing the deeds of their Lord, deeds that destroy impurity,
while, though their minds are broken by the fragrance of blooming <s>madhū</s> and <s>mādhavī</s> flowers in the water, they toss the breeze onward.
The clamor of pigeons, cuckoos, cranes, cakravākas, water-cocks, swans, parrots, partridges, and peacocks

children.text: kolāhalo viramate 'ciramātram uccair bhṛṅgādhipe harikathām iva gāyamāne ||
children.translated_text: ceases for only a moment when the lord of bees sings loudly, as if singing the tale of <s>Hari</s>.
<s>Mandāra</s>, jasmine, kurava, blue lotuses, campaka, arṇa, puṃnāga, nāga, bakula, lotuses, and pārijāta flowers

children.text: gandhe 'rcite tulasikābharaṇena tasyā yasmiṃs tapaḥ sumanaso bahu mānayanti ||
children.translated_text: there hold the fragrant <s>tulasī</s>, honored by his ornament, in high esteem among the flowers as austerity itself.
That place is crowded with airplanes made of lapis, emerald, and gold, seen only by those who bow deeply to <s>Hari</s>'s feet;

children.text: yeṣāṃ bṛhatkaṭitaṭāḥ smitaśobhimukhyaḥ kṛṣṇātmanāṃ na raja ādadhur utsmayādyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: their ladies, with broad hips and smiling, beautiful faces, did not stir passion in those whose selves are fixed on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, even by their smiles and charms.

children.text: śrī rūpiṇī kvaṇayatī caraṇāravindaṃ līlāmbujena harisadmani muktadoṣā
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> herself, in bodily form, free from fault in <s>Hari</s>'s dwelling, makes her lotus feet ring as she plays with a lotus;
she is seen beside crystal walls edged with gold, as if sweeping there, while another effort is made to win his grace.

children.text: vāpīṣu vidrumataṭāsv amalāmṛtāpsu preṣyānvitā nijavane tulasībhir īśam
children.translated_text: In ponds with coral banks and pure nectar-like waters, attended by maidservants, in her own grove with <s>tulasī</s> plants, she worships the Lord;

children.text: abhyarcatī svalakam unnasam īkṣya vaktram uccheṣitaṃ bhagavatety amatāṅga yacchrīḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing her own face, with curling locks and raised nose, reflected there, O dear one, she considered that beauty a remainder left by the Blessed Lord.

children.text: yan na vrajanty aghabhido racanānuvādāc chṛṇvanti ye 'nyaviṣayāḥ kukathā matighnīḥ
children.translated_text: Those who, instead of going there through recounting the arrangement of the destroyer of sin, listen to evil talk on other subjects that kills the mind,

children.text: yās tu śrutā hatabhagair nṛbhir āttasārās tāṃs tān kṣipanty aśaraṇeṣu tamaḥsu hanta ||
children.translated_text: such stories, once heard by unfortunate men whose essence has been taken away, cast them into one helpless darkness after another. Alas!

children.text: ye 'bhyarthitām api ca no nṛgatiṃ prapannā jñānaṃ ca tattvaviṣayaṃ sahadharmaṃ yatra
children.translated_text: Those who have obtained the human state, though it is sought even by us, and knowledge concerning reality along with <s>dharma</s>,
