children.text: nārādhanaṃ bhagavato vitaranty amuṣya saṃmohitā vitatayā bata māyayā te ||
children.translated_text: yet do not offer worship of that Blessed Lord, are indeed deluded by his far-spread <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: yac ca vrajanty animiṣām ṛṣabhānuvṛttyā dūre yamā hy upari naḥ spṛhaṇīyaśīlāḥ
children.translated_text: And those whose conduct, through following the best of the unwinking gods, is worthy of longing even above us, where restraints are far away, go there,
their bodies bristling with horripilation from the tearful tremor born of love for telling one another the excellent fame of their Lord.
The sages then reached that divine <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, entrusted to the teacher of the universe, worshiped by all beings,

children.text: āpuḥ parāṃ mudam apūrvam upetya yogamāyābalena munayas tad atho vikuṇṭham ||
children.translated_text: radiant with the varied airplanes of the foremost gods, and they attained supreme, unprecedented joy through the power of <s>yogamāyā</s>.

children.text: tasminn atītya munayaḥ ṣaḍ asajjamānāḥ kakṣāḥ samānavayasāv atha saptamāyām
children.translated_text: In that place the sages passed through six enclosures without being obstructed, and then, at the seventh,
they saw two divine beings of equal age, holding maces, adorned with splendid armlets, earrings, crowns, and costly garments.
They were encircled by garlands of forest flowers with intoxicated bees, set between their four dark arms,

children.text: vaktraṃ bhruvā kuṭilayā sphuṭanirgamābhyāṃ raktekṣaṇena ca manāg rabhasaṃ dadhānau ||
children.translated_text: and with bent brows, flaring nostrils, and red eyes, their faces bore a slight agitation.

children.text: dvāry etayor niviviśur miṣator apṛṣṭvā pūrvā yathā puraṭavajrakapāṭikā yāḥ
children.translated_text: As the two looked on, the sages entered through their gate without asking, as they had done through the earlier gates with panels of gold and diamond;

children.text: sarvatra te 'viṣamayā munayaḥ svadṛṣṭyā ye saṃcaranty avihatā vigatābhiśaṅkāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for those sages, seeing all places as equal, move everywhere unhindered and free from fear.

children.text: tān vīkṣya vātaraśanāṃś caturaḥ kumārān vṛddhān daśārdhavayaso viditātmatattvān
children.translated_text: Seeing those four <s>Kumāras</s>, naked as the wind, old yet appearing five years of age, knowers of the truth of the self,

children.text: vetreṇa cāskhalayatām atadarhaṇāṃs tau tejo vihasya bhagavatpratikūlaśīlau ||
children.translated_text: those two, whose conduct was hostile to the Blessed Lord, blocked them with a staff, though they were not fit to be treated so, and laughed at their radiance.

children.text: tābhyāṃ miṣatsv animiṣeṣu niṣidhyamānāḥ svarhattamā hy api hareḥ pratihārapābhyām
children.translated_text: Though most worthy of honor, they were being barred by those two gatekeepers of <s>Hari</s> while the unwinking gods looked on;

children.text: ūcuḥ suhṛttamadidṛkṣitabhaṅga īṣat kāmānujena sahasā ta upaplutākṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, their eyes suddenly disturbed by a little anger at the frustration of their desire to see their dearest friend, they spoke.
The sages said:

children.text: ko vām ihaitya bhagavatparicaryayoccais taddharmiṇāṃ nivasatāṃ viṣamaḥ svabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Who are you two here, who by lofty service to the Blessed Lord dwell among those who share his nature, yet have an uneven disposition?

children.text: tasmin praśāntapuruṣe gatavigrahe vāṃ ko vātmavat kuhakayoḥ pariśaṅkanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In him, the peaceful Person in whom conflict is gone, what could be suspected by you two deceivers, as if toward one like yourselves?

children.text: na hy antaraṃ bhagavatīha samastakukṣāv ātmānam ātmani nabho nabhasīva dhīrāḥ
children.translated_text: For here, in the Blessed Lord whose belly contains all things, the wise see no distinction between the self and the Self, as between space and space;

children.text: paśyanti yatra yuvayoḥ suraliṅginoḥ kiṃ vyutpāditaṃ hy udarabhedi bhayaṃ yato 'sya ||
children.translated_text: so what fear, splitting the belly, has been produced in you two who bear the marks of gods, and from what could it arise?

children.text: tad vām amuṣya paramasya vikuṇṭhabhartuḥ kartuṃ prakṛṣṭam iha dhīmahi mandadhībhyām
children.translated_text: Therefore, for you two, servants of that supreme Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, we of dull understanding deem it fitting here to perform a severe act,

children.text: lokān ito vrajatam antarabhāvadṛṣṭyā pāpīyasas traya ime ripavo 'sya yatra ||
children.translated_text: that you go from here to the worlds where those three most sinful enemies of his dwell, with a vision of inner difference.

children.text: teṣām itīritam ubhāv avadhārya ghoraṃ taṃ brahmadaṇḍam anivāraṇam astrapūgaiḥ
children.translated_text: When the two attendants heard this terrible <s>brahmadaṇḍa</s> (brahminic punishment), pronounced by them and impossible to ward off with masses of weapons,

children.text: sadyo harer anucarāv uru bibhyatas tatpādagrahāv apatatām atikātareṇa ||
children.translated_text: the attendants of <s>Hari</s>, greatly afraid, at once fell at their feet, grasping them in extreme distress.

children.text: bhūyād aghoni bhagavadbhir akāri daṇḍo yo nau hareta surahelanam apy aśeṣam
children.translated_text: May the punishment imposed by you, O blessed ones, fall upon our sin, a punishment that will wholly remove even our contempt toward <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: mā vo 'nutāpakalayā bhagavatsmṛtighno moho bhaved iha tu nau vrajator adho 'dhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But as we go lower and lower from here, may no delusion that destroys remembrance of the Lord arise for us through even a trace of your remorse.

children.text: evaṃ tadaiva bhagavān aravindanābhaḥ svānāṃ vibudhya sadatikramam āryahṛdyaḥ
children.translated_text: At that very moment the Blessed Lord, lotus-naveled and dear to noble hearts, learned of the transgression committed by his own attendants,

children.text: tasmin yayau paramahaṃsamahāmunīnām anveṣaṇīyacaraṇau calayan sahaśrīḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he came there together with <s>Śrī</s>, setting in motion those feet sought by the great <s>paramahaṃsa</s> sages.

children.text: taṃ tv āgataṃ pratihṛtaupayikaṃ svapuṃbhis te 'cakṣatākṣaviṣayaṃ svasamādhibhāgyam
children.translated_text: When he had come, accompanied by his own attendants and fitly received by the doorkeepers, they saw him, now an object for their eyes and the blessed fruit of their own <s>samādhi</s>.
He was shaded by a white parasol, whose moonlike pearl fringe was stirred by the auspicious breeze from a pair of fans lovely as swans.
His face was wholly gracious and smiling, his abode was desirable, and he touched their hearts with the slightest affectionate glance.

children.text: śyāme pṛthāv urasi śobhitayā śriyā svaścūḍāmaṇiṃ subhagayantam ivātmadhiṣṇyam ||
children.translated_text: With <s>Śrī</s> shining upon his broad dark chest, he seemed to make his own dwelling fortunate, like its crest-jewel.

children.text: pītāṃśuke pṛthunitambini visphurantyā kāñcyālibhir virutayā vanamālayā ca
children.translated_text: He wore yellow silk over broad hips, a flashing girdle sounding with rows of little bells, and a forest garland.

children.text: valguprakoṣṭhavalayaṃ vinatāsutāṃse vinyastahastam itareṇa dhunānam abjam ||
children.translated_text: Lovely bracelets encircled his wrists; one hand rested on the shoulder of <s>Garuḍa</s>, while with the other he waved a lotus.
His face, with raised cheeks fit for the adornment of makara earrings flashing like lightning, was crowned with a jeweled diadem.

children.text: dordaṇḍaṣaṇḍavivare haratā parārdhyahāreṇa kaṃdharagatena ca kaustubhena ||
children.translated_text: Between the great staffs of his arms he was adorned by a most precious necklace and by the <s>Kaustubha</s> resting at his neck.

children.text: atropasṛṣṭam iti cotsmitam indirāyāḥ svānāṃ dhiyā viracitaṃ bahusauṣṭhavāḍhyam
children.translated_text: His body, rich in abundant elegance, seemed fashioned by the minds of his own devotees, and <s>Indirā</s> smiled as though thinking, 'He has been set here for me.'

children.text: mahyaṃ bhavasya bhavatāṃ ca bhajantam aṅgaṃ nemur nirīkṣya na vitṛptadṛśo mudā kaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that body worshiped by me, by <s>Bhava</s>, and by you, they bowed with joy, their eyes not satisfied; who indeed could be satisfied by looking?
The breeze bearing the honey of <s>tulasī</s> mixed with the pollen of the lotus feet of that lotus-eyed one

children.text: antargataḥ svavivareṇa cakāra teṣāṃ saṃkṣobham akṣarajuṣām api cittatanvoḥ ||
children.translated_text: entered through their nostrils and stirred both the minds and bodies of those sages, though they were devoted to the imperishable.

children.text: te vā amuṣya vadanāsitapadmakośam udvīkṣya sundaratarādharakundahāsam
children.translated_text: They looked up at the dark lotus-bud of his face, with its more beautiful lips and jasmine-white smile,

children.text: labdhāśiṣaḥ punar avekṣya tadīyam aṅghridvaṃdvaṃ nakhāruṇamaṇiśrayaṇaṃ nidadhyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, having received his blessing, they again looked down and meditated on the pair of his feet, the refuge of ruby-red nails.

children.text: puṃsāṃ gatiṃ mṛgayatām iha yogamārgair dhyānāspadaṃ bahumataṃ nayanābhirāmam
children.translated_text: He displayed to those seeking the human goal here by paths of yoga a form that was an object of meditation, highly honored and delightful to the eyes,

children.text: pauṃsnaṃ vapur darśayānam ananyasiddhair autpattikaiḥ samagṛṇan yutam aṣṭabhogaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: his manly body, endowed with eight innate excellences attained by no other means; and they praised him.
The <s>Kumāras</s> said:

children.text: yo 'ntarhito hṛdi gato 'pi durātmanāṃ tvaṃ so 'dyaiva no nayanamūlam ananta rāddhaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Ananta</s>, you who are hidden within and have entered even the hearts of the wicked have today become manifest at the root of our eyes.

children.text: yarhy eva karṇavivareṇa guhāṃ gato naḥ pitrānuvarṇitarahā bhavadudbhavena ||
children.translated_text: In just this way you had entered the cave of our hearts through the opening of our ears, when your secret path was described by our father, who was born from you.

children.text: taṃ tvāṃ vidāma bhagavan param ātmatattvaṃ sattvena samprati ratiṃ racayantam eṣām
children.translated_text: O Blessed Lord, we know you as the supreme truth of the self, now creating delight in these devotees through purity of being.

children.text: yat te 'nutāpaviditair dṛḍhabhaktiyogair udgranthayo hṛdi vidur munayo virāgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Detached sages, whose knots in the heart have been loosened by firm devotional yoga made known through repentance, know that truth of yours within the heart.

children.text: nātyantikaṃ vigaṇayanty api te prasādaṃ kimv anyad arpitabhayaṃ bhruva unnayais te
children.translated_text: They do not value even your final grace very highly, much less anything else, even the sovereignty free from fear that is granted by the lifting of your brows,

children.text: ye 'ṅga tvadaṅghriśaraṇā bhavataḥ kathāyāḥ kīrtanyatīrthayaśasaḥ kuśalā rasajñāḥ ||
children.translated_text: O dear Lord, they who have taken refuge at your feet and are skilled connoisseurs of your discourse, whose fame is a sacred ford worthy of praise.

children.text: kāmaṃ bhavaḥ svavṛjinair nirayeṣu naḥ stāc ceto 'livad yadi nu te padayo rameta
children.translated_text: Let worldly existence, if it must, be ours in hells through our own sins, provided our minds may delight at your feet like bees,

children.text: vācaś ca nas tulasīvad yadi te 'ṅghriśobhāḥ pūryeta te guṇagaṇair yadi karṇarandhraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and provided our speech, like <s>tulasī</s>, may be filled with the splendors of your feet, and the openings of our ears with the hosts of your virtues.

children.text: prāduścakartha yad idaṃ puruhūta rūpaṃ teneśa nirvṛtim avāpur alaṃ dṛśo naḥ
children.translated_text: O much-invoked one, you have manifested this form; by it, O Lord, our eyes have gained full satisfaction.

children.text: tasmā idaṃ bhagavate nama id vidhema yo 'nātmanāṃ durudayo bhagavān pratītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore we offer this homage to that Blessed Lord, who is hard for those without self-mastery to realize, yet has become manifest.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: iti tad gṛṇatāṃ teṣāṃ munīnāṃ yogadharmiṇām
children.translated_text: When those sages devoted to the discipline of yoga had praised him thus,
the all-pervading one, dwelling in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, approved and spoke these words.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: etau tau pārṣadau mahyaṃ jayo vijaya eva ca
children.translated_text: These two are my attendants, <s>Jaya</s> and indeed <s>Vijaya</s>.

children.text: kadarthīkṛtya māṃ yad vo bahv akrātām atikramam ||
children.translated_text: By showing contempt for you, they slighted me and committed a great transgression.

children.text: yas tv etayor dhṛto daṇḍo bhavadbhir mām anuvrataiḥ
children.translated_text: But the punishment imposed on these two by you, sages devoted to me,
is approved by us, because of their contempt toward divine beings.

children.text: tad vaḥ prasādayāmy adya brahma daivaṃ paraṃ hi me
children.translated_text: Therefore today I seek to conciliate you, O brahmins; the divine brahman is supreme for me.

children.text: tad dhīty ātmakṛtaṃ manye yat svapuṃbhir asatkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For I consider the dishonor you suffered from my own attendants to have been done by myself.

children.text: yan nāmāni ca gṛhṇāti loko bhṛtye kṛtāgasi
children.translated_text: When people mention the master by name because a servant has committed an offense,
that ill report destroys his fame, just as disease destroys the skin.

children.text: yasyāmṛtāmalayaśaḥśravaṇāvagāhaḥ sadyaḥ punāti jagad āśvapacād vikuṇṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: I am <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, whose deathless and stainless fame, when entered through hearing, at once purifies the world down to the dog-cooker.

children.text: so 'haṃ bhavadbhya upalabdhasutīrthakīrtiś chindyāṃ svabāhum api vaḥ pratikūlavṛttim ||
children.translated_text: Having gained through you the fame of a holy ford, I would cut off even my own arm if it acted contrary to you.
By serving me, <s>Śrī</s> has obtained the purifying dust of my lotus feet, which at once destroys every impurity and restores good character.

children.text: na śrīr viraktam api māṃ vijahāti yasyāḥ prekṣālavārtha itare niyamān vahanti ||
children.translated_text: She does not abandon me, though I am detached from her; for the sake of even a fraction of her glance, others undertake vows.

children.text: nāhaṃ tathādmi yajamānahavir vitāne ścyotadghṛtaplutam adan hutabhuṅmukhena
children.translated_text: I do not eat the sacrificer's oblation in the sacrificial enclosure, though soaked with dripping ghee, so much through the mouth of the fire-eater,

children.text: yad brāhmaṇasya mukhataś carato 'nughāsaṃ tuṣṭasya mayy avahitair nijakarmapākaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: as I eat the morsel from the mouth of a contented <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who moves about, when his own karmic fruits are offered by those whose minds are fixed on me.

children.text: yeṣāṃ bibharmy aham akhaṇḍavikuṇṭhayogamāyāvibhūtir amalāṅghrirajaḥ kirīṭaiḥ
children.translated_text: I, whose glory is the unbroken power of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>'s yogamāyā, bear on my crowns the spotless dust of the feet of those people.

children.text: viprāṃs tu ko na viṣaheta yadarhaṇāmbhaḥ sadyaḥ punāti sahacandralalāmalokān ||
children.translated_text: Who, then, would not tolerate and honor the learned brāhmaṇas, when the water of their worship at once purifies the worlds, together with the moon-crested lord?

children.text: ye me tanūr dvijavarān duhatīr madīyā bhūtāny alabdhaśaraṇāni ca bhedabuddhyā
children.translated_text: Those whose sight is wounded by sin, who with a notion of separateness will look upon the best twice-born, the milk-giving cows that are my own bodies, and upon beings that have found no refuge,

children.text: drakṣyanty aghakṣatadṛśo hy ahimanyavas tān gṛdhrā ruṣā mama kuṣanty adhidaṇḍanetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: those men, their anger like serpents, the vultures tear apart through the wrath of me, the wielder of punishment.

children.text: ye brāhmaṇān mayi dhiyā kṣipato 'rcayantas tuṣyaddhṛdaḥ smitasudhokṣitapadmavaktrāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who worship brāhmaṇas even when they revile me, seeing them as me, their hearts pleased and their lotus faces sprinkled with the nectar of smiles,

children.text: vāṇyānurāgakalayātmajavad gṛṇantaḥ saṃbodhayanty aham ivāham upāhṛtas taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who address them with words touched by affection, praising them as they would their own selves, by them I am won over as though I myself had been honored.

children.text: tan me svabhartur avasāyam alakṣamāṇau yuṣmadvyatikramagatiṃ pratipadya sadyaḥ
children.translated_text: These two servants of mine did not perceive the intention of their own master and have immediately incurred the consequence of offending you.

children.text: bhūyo mamāntikam itāṃ tad anugraho me yat kalpatām acirato bhṛtayor vivāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May they come again to my presence before long; let my favor to these servants be that their exile is made short.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Then, though they tasted that radiant goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the river of sages,
even the inner selves of those who had been bitten by anger were not satisfied.
Hearing that true speech with mouths opened, light yet cavernous with weighty meaning,
and plunging into it, unfathomable and deep, they did not know what he wished to do.
The brāhmaṇa sages, delighted, with hands folded and their skin trembling with joy,
spoke of his supreme lordly greatness, brought forth by yogamāyā.
The sages said:

children.text: na vayaṃ bhagavan vidmas tava deva cikīrṣitam
children.translated_text: Blessed Lord, O God, we do not know what you wish to do,

children.text: kṛto me 'nugrahaś ceti yad adhyakṣaḥ prabhāṣase ||
children.translated_text: when you, the overseer, say, 'A favor has been done to me.'

children.text: brahmaṇyasya paraṃ daivaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ kila te prabho
children.translated_text: O Lord, for you who are devoted to brāhmaṇas, the brāhmaṇas are indeed the supreme deity;
and for the brāhmaṇas, the gods of gods, the Blessed One is their own deity.

children.text: tvattaḥ sanātano dharmo rakṣyate tanubhis tava
children.translated_text: From you eternal <s>dharma</s> is protected by your bodies;

children.text: dharmasya paramo guhyo nirvikāro bhavān mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: you are held to be the supreme secret of <s>dharma</s>, changeless.

children.text: taranti hy añjasā mṛtyuṃ nivṛttā yadanugrahāt
children.translated_text: For yogins who have turned away from the world easily cross death by whose grace;

children.text: yoginaḥ sa bhavān kiṃ svid anugṛhyeta yat paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: since that one is you, how could you be favored by others?

children.text: yaṃ vai vibhūtir upayāty anuvelam anyair arthārthibhiḥ svaśirasā dhṛtapādareṇuḥ
children.translated_text: Prosperity attends you at every moment, though others who seek wealth bear the dust of your feet on their heads,
longing, like a lord of bees, for the abode fragrant with fresh <s>tulasī</s> garlands offered at your blessed feet.

children.text: yas tāṃ viviktacaritair anuvartamānāṃ nātyādriyat paramabhāgavataprasaṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: You, absorbed in the company of the supreme devotees, did not greatly value her, though she follows you by pure conduct;

children.text: sa tvaṃ dvijānupathapuṇyarajaḥpunītaḥ śrīvatsalakṣma kim agā bhagabhājanas tvam ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O bearer of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark, purified by the sacred dust on the path of the twice-born, what gain could you, the vessel of fortune, have obtained?

children.text: dharmasya te bhagavatas triyuga tribhiḥ svaiḥ padbhiś carācaram idaṃ dvijadevatārtham
children.translated_text: O Blessed <s>Triyuga</s>, surely this moving and unmoving world is sustained for the sake of the twice-born and the gods

children.text: nūnaṃ bhṛtaṃ tadabhighāti rajas tamaś ca sattvena no varadayā tanuvā nirasya ||
children.translated_text: by the three feet of your own <s>dharma</s>; for our good, bestower of boons, you drive away attacking rajas and tamas with your sattva body.

children.text: na tvaṃ dvijottamakulaṃ yadi hātmagopaṃ goptā vṛṣaḥ svarhaṇena sasūnṛtena
children.translated_text: If you, the protector, did not protect the family of the best twice-born, self-guarded by its own worship and truthful speech,

children.text: tarhy eva naṅkṣyati śivas tava deva panthā loko 'grahīṣyad ṛṣabhasya hi tat pramāṇam ||
children.translated_text: then surely, O auspicious God, your path would perish; for the world would take the conduct of the excellent one as its standard.

children.text: tat te 'nabhīṣṭam iva sattvanidher vidhitsoḥ kṣemaṃ janāya nijaśaktibhir uddhṛtāreḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, since you, a treasury of sattva, wish to establish welfare for people through your own powers after raising up your enemies,

children.text: naitāvatā tryadhipater bata viśvabhartus tejaḥ kṣataṃ tv avanatasya sa te vinodaḥ ||
children.translated_text: your splendor, O lord of the three worlds and supporter of the universe, is not diminished by this much when you bow down; that is your sport.

children.text: yaṃ vānayor damam adhīśa bhavān vidhatte vṛttiṃ nu vā tad anumanmahi nirvyalīkam
children.translated_text: O Lord, whatever punishment you impose on these two, or whatever state you assign them, we approve it without deceit;

children.text: asmāsu vā ya ucito dhriyatāṃ sa daṇḍo ye 'nāgasau vayam ayuṅkṣmahi kilbiṣeṇa ||
children.translated_text: or let whatever punishment is proper for us be applied, since we have joined these two guiltless ones with offense.
The Blessed Lord said:
These two, at once attaining a destiny among beings other than the gods, will be bound to yoga through concentration born of intense anger,

children.text: bhūyaḥ sakāśam upayāsyata āśu yo vaḥ śāpo mayaiva nimitas tad aveta viprāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and they will quickly come back again to my presence. Know, O brāhmaṇas, that this curse of yours was caused by me alone.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Then those sages saw <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, a delight to the eyes,
that abode, and <s>Vikuṇṭha</s> himself, self-luminous.
After circumambulating the Blessed One, bowing down, and taking their leave,
they returned, joyful, praising the splendor of the Vaiṣṇavas.

children.text: bhagavān anugāv āha yātaṃ mā bhaiṣṭam astu śam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said to the two attendants, 'Go; do not be afraid. Let there be peace.'

children.text: brahmatejaḥ samartho 'pi hantuṃ necche mataṃ tu me ||
children.translated_text: Though I am able to destroy the power of brahman, I do not wish to do so; this is my resolve.

children.text: etat puraiva nirdiṣṭaṃ ramayā kruddhayā yadā
children.translated_text: This was indicated long ago by <s>Ramā</s>, when she became angry,
having formerly been barred at the door as she was entering, while I was withdrawn.
By union with anger directed toward me, crossing beyond your slighting of the brāhmaṇas,
you shall return again to my vicinity after a very short time.
After instructing the two doorkeepers, the Blessed One entered his own abode,

children.text: sarvātiśayayā lakṣmyā juṣṭaṃ svaṃ dhiṣṇyam āviśat ||
children.translated_text: adorned with rows of aerial palaces and endowed with unsurpassed splendor of every kind.
But those two foremost among the divine ones, from the hard-to-cross world of <s>Hari</s>,
deprived of their splendor by the brāhmaṇas' curse, became free from pride.
At that time, as those two were falling from the seat of <s>Vikuṇṭha</s>,
a great cry of 'Alas, alas!' arose in the foremost aerial palaces, children.

children.text: tāv eva hy adhunā prāptau pārṣadapravarau hareḥ
children.translated_text: Those very two foremost attendants of <s>Hari</s> have now entered
the fierce energy of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, lodged in the womb of <s>Diti</s>.

children.text: tayor asurayor adya tejasā yamayor hi vaḥ
children.translated_text: For today, by the energy of those two Asuras, who are indeed a pair, your...

children.text: ākṣiptaṃ teja etarhi bhagavāṃs tad vidhitsati ||
children.translated_text: The radiance cast forth by you now is what the Blessed Lord intends to dispose of.

children.text: viśvasya yaḥ sthitilayodbhavahetur ādyo yogeśvarair api duratyayayogamāyaḥ
children.translated_text: He is the primal cause of the maintenance, dissolution, and arising of the universe; even for the lords of yoga his <s>yogamāyā</s> is hard to cross.

children.text: kṣemaṃ vidhāsyati sa no bhagavāṃs tryadhīśas tatrāsmadīyavimṛśena kiyān ihārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That Blessed Lord, ruler of the three, will bring about our welfare. What purpose is there here in deliberation by us?
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Hearing what was sung by the self-born one, and freed from doubt about the cause,
all the dwellers in heaven then turned back to the third heaven.
But <s>Diti</s>, in obedience to her husband's command and apprehensive about her offspring,

children.text: pūrṇe varṣaśate sādhvī putrau prasuṣuve yamau ||
children.translated_text: when a hundred years were complete, that virtuous woman gave birth to twin sons.
As they were being born, many portents fell there,
in heaven, on earth, and in the midspace, bringing great fear to the world.

children.text: sahācalā bhuvaś celur diśaḥ sarvāḥ prajajvaluḥ
children.translated_text: The earth shook together with its mountains, and all the directions blazed up;
meteors and thunderbolts fell, and comets appeared, causes of distress.

children.text: vavau vāyuḥ suduḥsparśaḥ phūtkārān īrayan muhuḥ
children.translated_text: A wind blew, harsh to the touch, repeatedly sending out blasts,
uprooting great trees, a troop of whirlwinds with dust as its banner.
When the stars had vanished amid a mass of clouds with upraised lightning,

children.text: vyomni praviṣṭatamasā na sma vyādṛśyate padam ||
children.translated_text: and darkness had entered the sky, not even a foot of ground could be seen.
The ocean, troubled in mind, cried out, with high waves and an agitated belly;
and the rivers, together with wells, were disturbed, their lotuses dried and covered with mud.
Again and again halos with <s>Rāhu</s> appeared around the moon and sun;
crashes like the rumbling of chariots arose from the hollows.
Within the villages, jackals, vomiting fierce fire from their mouths,
howled inauspiciously with the cries of jackals, owls, and shrieking birds.
Dogs, raising their necks, uttered various sounds here and there,

children.text: vyamuñcan vividhā vāco grāmasiṃhās tatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: as if singing and as if weeping.

children.text: kharāś ca karkaśaiḥ kṣattaḥ khurair ghnanto dharātalam
children.translated_text: Asses too, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, striking the ground with their hard hooves,
maddened by the force of their harsh braying, ran about in herds.
Crying out and frightened by the asses, birds flew up from their nests;
and cattle in the cow pens and in the forest passed dung and urine.
The cows became terrified and yielded blood for milk; the clouds rained pus;
the divine images wept, and trees fell though there was no wind.

children.text: grahān puṇyatamān anye bhagaṇāṃś cāpi dīpitāḥ
children.translated_text: Other blazing planets crossed the most auspicious planets and the constellations,
moving with retrograde motion, and they fought with one another.
Seeing these and other great portents, the people, who did not know the truth of things,
except for the sons of <s>Brahmā</s>, were frightened and thought the universe was being destroyed.
Those two first <s>daityas</s> (demonic sons of <s>Diti</s>), whose own prowess was suddenly manifesting,
grew, with bodies hard as stone, like two great mountains.
Touching the sky with the tips of their golden crowns, blocking the quarters, with arms flashing with armlets,

children.text: gāṃ kampayantau caraṇaiḥ pade pade kaṭyā sukāñcyārkam atītya tasthatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: shaking the earth with their feet at every step, and with their splendid waist-belts, they stood surpassing the sun.

children.text: prajāpatir nāma tayor akārṣīd yaḥ prāk svadehād yamayor ajāyata
children.translated_text: The lord of creatures, who had earlier been born from his own body, gave names to those twins:

children.text: taṃ vai hiraṇyakaśipuṃ viduḥ prajā yaṃ taṃ hiraṇyākṣam asūta sāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: people know that one as <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, and she first bore the other, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, by his arms and by the boon from <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: vaśe sapālān lokāṃs trīn akutomṛtyur uddhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: made the three worlds, together with their guardians, subject to his control, arrogant and free from fear of death from any quarter.
His younger brother <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, dear to him and pleasing him every day,

children.text: gadāpāṇir divaṃ yāto yuyutsur mṛgayan raṇam ||
children.translated_text: went to heaven with mace in hand, eager to fight and seeking battle.
Seeing him, whose speed was unbearable, whose golden anklets rang,
adorned with a <s>Vaijayantī</s> garland and with a great mace set upon his shoulder,
swollen with pride in the boon of mental power and strength, uncontrollable and fearless,
the frightened gods hid themselves, like snakes terrified of <s>Tārkṣya</s>.

children.text: sa vai tirohitān dṛṣṭvā mahasā svena daityarāṭ
children.translated_text: When that king of <s>daityas</s> saw that the hosts of gods with <s>Indra</s> had disappeared before his own brilliance,

children.text: sendrān devagaṇān kṣībān apaśyan vyanadad bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: and could not see them, as if they were drunk, he roared loudly.
Then, turning back and wishing to sport, the mighty being entered the ocean,

children.text: vijagāhe mahāsattvo vārdhiṃ matta iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: deep and terrible in sound, like a rutting elephant.

children.text: tasmin praviṣṭe varuṇasya sainikā yādogaṇāḥ sannadhiyaḥ sasādhvasāḥ
children.translated_text: When he had entered it, <s>Varuṇa</s>'s soldiers, the aquatic beings, their minds struck with alarm,

children.text: ahanyamānā api tasya varcasā pradharṣitā dūrataraṃ pradudruvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: though not beaten by him, were overpowered by his splendor and fled far away.

children.text: sa varṣapūgān udadhau mahābalaś caran mahormīñchvasaneritān muhuḥ
children.translated_text: For many years the mighty one wandered in the ocean, repeatedly striking the great waves driven by the wind with his mace,

children.text: maurvyābhijaghne gadayā vibhāvarīm āsedivāṃs tāta purīṃ pracetasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, O dear one, at night he reached the city of <s>Pracetas</s>.
There, finding the guardian of the asura-world, <s>Pracetas</s>, the foremost of the aquatic beings,

children.text: smayan pralabdhuṃ praṇipatya nīcavaj jagāda me dehy adhirāja saṃyugam ||
children.translated_text: he smiled, and in order to mock him bowed low like a humble man and said, 'Give me battle, O overlord.'
'You are a guardian of the world, a ruler of great fame, who robs proud heroes of their valor;

children.text: vijitya loke 'khiladaityadānavān yad rājasūyena purāyajat prabho ||
children.translated_text: for after conquering all <s>daityas</s> and <s>dānavas</s> in the world, you once performed a <s>rājasūya</s> sacrifice, O lord.'

children.text: sa evam utsiktamadena vidviṣā dṛḍhaṃ pralabdho bhagavān apāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus firmly mocked by his enemy, who was swollen with conceit, the blessed lord of the waters

children.text: roṣaṃ samutthaṃ śamayan svayā dhiyā vyavocad aṅgopaśamaṃ gatā vayam ||
children.translated_text: calmed the anger that had arisen and, by his own judgment, replied, 'My dear one, we have gone to peace.'

children.text: paśyāmi nānyaṃ puruṣāt purātanād yaḥ saṃyuge tvāṃ raṇamārgakovidam
children.translated_text: 'I see no one other than the ancient Person who will satisfy you in battle, you expert in the path of war.

children.text: ārādhayiṣyaty asurarṣabhehi taṃ manasvino yaṃ gṛṇate bhavādṛśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Go to him, O bull among asuras, whom spirited men like you praise.'

children.text: taṃ vīram ārād abhipadya vismayaḥ śayiṣyase vīraśaye śvabhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Approaching that hero nearby, your wonder gone, you will lie on the hero's bed, surrounded by dogs;

children.text: yas tvadvidhānām asatāṃ praśāntaye rūpāṇi dhatte sadanugrahecchayā ||
children.translated_text: for, wishing to favor the good, he assumes forms for the pacification of wicked men such as you.'
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: tad evam ākarṇya jaleśabhāṣitaṃ mahāmanās tad vigaṇayya durmadaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing in this way the speech of the lord of waters, the great-minded but very arrogant one disregarded it;

children.text: harer viditvā gatim aṅga nāradād rasātalaṃ nirviviśe tvarānvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, learning from <s>Nārada</s> the whereabouts of <s>Hari</s>, dear one, he hurriedly entered <s>Rasātala</s>.
There he saw the victorious bearer of the earth, lifting up the earth with the tip of his tusk,

children.text: muṣṇantam akṣṇā svaruco 'ruṇaśriyā jahāsa cāho vanagocaro mṛgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: stealing away with his eye the beauty of his own reddish splendor; and he laughed, saying, “Ah, a forest-ranging beast!”

children.text: āhainam ehy ajña mahīṃ vimuñca no rasaukasāṃ viśvasṛjeyam arpitā
children.translated_text: He said to him, “Come here, fool! Release the earth to us, the inhabitants of <s>Rasātala</s>; this was entrusted to us by the creator of the universe.

children.text: na svasti yāsyasy anayā mamekṣataḥ surādhamāsāditasūkarākṛte ||
children.translated_text: You will not go safely with her while I am watching, lowest of the gods, now that you have assumed the form of a boar.

children.text: tvaṃ naḥ sapatnair abhavāya kiṃ bhṛto yo māyayā hanty asurān parokṣajit
children.translated_text: Were you maintained by our enemies for our destruction, you who kill the asuras by <s>māyā</s>, conquering while unseen?

children.text: tvāṃ yogamāyābalam alpapauruṣaṃ saṃsthāpya mūḍha pramṛje suhṛcchucaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O fool, you whose strength is <s>yogamāyā</s> and whose manliness is slight, after laying you low I shall wipe away the grief of my kinsmen.

children.text: tvayi saṃsthite gadayā śīrṇaśīrṣaṇy asmadbhujacyutayā ye ca tubhyam
children.translated_text: When you stand with your head shattered by the mace fallen from our arm, then those who belong to you,

children.text: baliṃ haranty ṛṣayo ye ca devāḥ svayaṃ sarve na bhaviṣyanty amūlāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sages who bring offerings and the gods too, all of them, will themselves be without a root.”

children.text: sa tudyamāno 'riduruktatomarair daṃṣṭrāgragāṃ gām upalakṣya bhītām
children.translated_text: Pierced by the spears of his enemy's harsh words, he noticed the earth on the tip of his tusk, frightened,

children.text: todaṃ mṛṣan niragād ambumadhyād grāhāhataḥ sakareṇur yathebhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, enduring the goading, came out from the midst of the water like an elephant struck by a crocodile together with its cow-elephant.

children.text: taṃ niḥsarantaṃ salilād anudruto hiraṇyakeśo dviradaṃ yathā jhaṣaḥ
children.translated_text: As he emerged from the water, the golden-haired one pursued him like a crocodile pursuing an elephant;

children.text: karāladaṃṣṭro 'śaninisvano 'bravīd gatahriyāṃ kiṃ tv asatāṃ vigarhitam ||
children.translated_text: with terrible tusks and a thunderous roar he said, “What indeed is blameworthy among shameless wicked men?”

children.text: sa gām udastāt salilasya gocare vinyasya tasyām adadhāt svasattvam
children.translated_text: He lifted the earth out of the water into a visible place and placed his own sustaining power in her;

children.text: abhiṣṭuto viśvasṛjā prasūnair āpūryamāṇo vibudhaiḥ paśyato 'reḥ ||
children.translated_text: while the enemy looked on, he was praised by the creator of the universe and filled with flowers by the gods.
The enemy, clinging after him, bearing a great golden mace and armor ornamented with gold,

children.text: marmāṇy abhīkṣṇaṃ pratudantaṃ duruktaiḥ pracaṇḍamanyuḥ prahasaṃs taṃ babhāṣe ||
children.translated_text: continually piercing his vulnerable points with insults, was addressed by him as he laughed, his anger fierce.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: satyaṃ vayaṃ bho vanagocarā mṛgā yuṣmadvidhān mṛgaye grāmasiṃhān
children.translated_text: “True, sir, we are forest-ranging beasts, and we hunt village-lions such as you.

children.text: na mṛtyupāśaiḥ pratimuktasya vīrā vikatthanaṃ tava gṛhṇanty abhadra ||
children.translated_text: Heroes do not heed the boasting of you, O inauspicious one, caught in the nooses of death.

children.text: ete vayaṃ nyāsaharā rasaukasāṃ gatahriyo gadayā drāvitās te
children.translated_text: Here we are, thieves of the deposit of the dwellers in <s>Rasātala</s>, shameless, driven off by your mace;

children.text: tiṣṭhāmahe 'thāpi kathaṃcid ājau stheyaṃ kva yāmo balinotpādya vairam ||
children.translated_text: yet somehow we stand in battle. Where could we go, having provoked enmity with one so strong?

children.text: tvaṃ padrathānāṃ kila yūthapādhipo ghaṭasva no 'svastaya āśv anūhaḥ
children.translated_text: You are indeed the herd-chief of the foot-soldiers; quickly exert yourself for our misfortune without delay.

children.text: saṃsthāpya cāsmān pramṛjāśru svakānāṃ yaḥ svāṃ pratijñāṃ nātipiparty asabhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having laid us low, wipe away the tears of your own people; one who does not fulfill his own pledge is ignoble.”
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: so 'dhikṣipto bhagavatā pralabdhaś ca ruṣā bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Thus reproached and also mocked by the Blessed Lord, he became violently enraged,
and, being toyed with, he took on terrible wrath like a great serpent.
Indignant, sending forth breaths, his senses shaken by anger,
the daitya rushed upon him with force and struck <s>Hari</s> with his mace.
But the Blessed Lord avoided the rush of the mace hurled by the enemy at his chest,
turning sideways, as one mounted in yoga avoids death.

children.text: punar gadāṃ svām ādāya bhrāmayantam abhīkṣṇaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, taking up his own mace again and whirling it again and again,
<s>Hari</s>, angered and biting his lip in fury, charged at him.

children.text: tataś ca gadayārātiṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ bhruvi prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then with his mace the Lord struck his enemy on the right brow,

children.text: ājaghne sa tu tāṃ saumya gadayā kovido 'hanat ||
children.translated_text: but that skilled one, O gentle one, struck that mace with his own mace.

children.text: evaṃ gadābhyāṃ gurvībhyāṃ haryakṣo harir eva ca
children.translated_text: Thus, with their heavy maces, <s>Haryakṣa</s> and <s>Hari</s> too,
both greatly enraged in their desire for victory, struck one another.
As the two rivals, their limbs struck by sharp maces and their anger increased by the smell of blood from their wounds,

children.text: vicitramārgāṃś carator jigīṣayā vyabhād ilāyām iva śuṣmiṇor mṛdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: moved about in varied paths in desire for victory, their battle shone upon the earth like that of two powerful bulls.
O <s>Kauravya</s>, while the daitya, enemy of the great-souled Lord whose boar body had been assumed by <s>māyā</s> and whose limbs are sacrifice,

children.text: kauravya mahyāṃ dviṣator vimardanaṃ didṛkṣur āgād ṛṣibhir vṛtaḥ svarāṭ ||
children.translated_text: was grinding against him on the earth, <s>Svarāṭ</s>, desiring to see it, came surrounded by sages.
Seeing the daitya close at hand, bold, free from fear, making counterblows, and of irresistible valor,

children.text: vilakṣya daityaṃ bhagavān sahasraṇīr jagāda nārāyaṇam ādisūkaram ||
children.translated_text: the thousand-born Blessed One spoke to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the primeval Boar.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: eṣa te deva devānām aṅghrimūlam upeyuṣām
children.translated_text: “This asura, O God, is an offender against the gods who have come to the root of your feet,
against the brahmins, the cows, and even the innocent beings.
An offender, a maker of fear, an evil-doer, this asura has obtained a boon from me;
seeking opponents, he wanders through the worlds as a thorn, with no warrior able to withstand him.
Do not play like a child, O God, with this master of <s>māyā</s>, arrogant, unrestrained, and lowest of the wicked,
as one would with an awakened venomous serpent.

children.text: na yāvad eṣa vardheta svāṃ velāṃ prāpya dāruṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Before this terrible one should grow stronger, having reached his proper time,

children.text: svāṃ deva māyām āsthāya tāvaj jahy agham acyuta ||
children.translated_text: resort to your own <s>māyā</s>, O <s>Acyuta</s>, and kill the sinful one at once.
This most dreadful twilight, which confounds the worlds, O Lord,
is approaching; O self of all, bring victory to the gods.

children.text: adhunaiṣo 'bhijin nāma yogo mauhūrtiko hy agāt
children.translated_text: Now this momentary conjunction named <s>Abhijit</s> has arrived.

children.text: śivāya nas tvaṃ suhṛdām āśu nistara dustaram ||
children.translated_text: For the welfare of us, your friends, quickly cross over the hard-to-cross danger.

children.text: diṣṭyā tvāṃ vihitaṃ mṛtyum ayam āsāditaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: By fortune, this one has himself approached you, who have been ordained as his death.

children.text: vikramyainaṃ mṛdhe hatvā lokān ādhehi śarmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: Exert yourself, kill him in battle, and set the worlds in peace.”
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having understood <s>Viriñca</s>'s guileless, nectar-like words,
he smiled and accepted them with a sidelong glance filled with affection.
Then, as his rival moved fearlessly before him,
<s>Akṣaja</s> sprang up and struck the asura on the jaw with his mace.

children.text: sā hatā tena gadayā vihatā bhagavatkarāt
children.translated_text: That mace, struck by him with his mace, was knocked from the Blessed Lord's hand
Spinning as it fell, it shone, and the sight seemed wondrous.

children.text: sa tadā labdhatīrtho 'pi na babādhe nirāyudham
children.translated_text: Then, although he had gained his opening, he did not strike the unarmed one,

children.text: mānayan sa mṛdhe dharmaṃ viṣvaksenaṃ prakopayan ||
children.translated_text: honoring <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct) in battle and provoking <s>Viṣvaksena</s>.
When the mace had been cast away and cries of 'Ah! Ah!' arose,
the mighty one honored that <s>dharma</s> and remembered <s>Sunābha</s>.
As that lowest son of <s>Diti</s>, once chief among his own attendants, pressed upon him while his discus was engaged,

children.text: citrā vāco 'tadvidāṃ khecarāṇāṃ tatra smāsan svasti te 'muṃ jahīti ||
children.translated_text: various cries arose there from the sky-goers who did not know the truth: 'May it be well with you! Kill him!'

children.text: sa taṃ niśāmyāttarathāṅgam agrato vyavasthitaṃ padmapalāśalocanam
children.translated_text: Hearing him, and seeing him standing before him with the discus in hand, lotus-petal-eyed,

children.text: vilokya cāmarṣapariplutendriyo ruṣā svadantacchadam ādaśac chvasan ||
children.translated_text: he became flooded with impatience in all his senses and, breathing hard in anger, bit his own lip.
With terrible fangs, he stared with his eyes as though burning him up,
and, rushing forward with his mace, struck <s>Hari</s>, crying, 'You are slain!'

children.text: padā savyena tāṃ sādho bhagavān yajñasūkaraḥ
children.translated_text: But the Blessed Lord, the sacrificial boar, O good one, with his left foot
playfully struck that wind-swift mace while his enemy looked on.

children.text: āha cāyudham ādhatsva ghaṭasva tvaṃ jigīṣasi
children.translated_text: And he said, 'Take up your weapon. Exert yourself, if you wish to conquer.'

children.text: ity uktaḥ sa tadā bhūyas tāḍayan vyanadad bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, he then struck again and roared violently.

children.text: tāṃ sa āpatatīṃ vīkṣya bhagavān samavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing it coming down upon him, the Blessed Lord stood firm

children.text: jagrāha līlayā prāptāṃ garutmān iva pannagīm ||
children.translated_text: and caught it playfully as it arrived, like <s>Garutmān</s> catching a serpent.
When his own prowess had been checked, the great demon, his pride broken,
lost his splendor and did not wish to take the mace that <s>Hari</s> offered back to him.
He seized a three-pointed spear, blazing and eager like flickering fire,
as though practicing hostile magic against the sacrifice embodied as a brahmin.

children.text: tad ojasā daityamahābhaṭārpitaṃ cakāsad antaḥkha udīrṇadīdhiti
children.translated_text: That spear, hurled with force by the great Daitya warrior, flashed in the midair with heightened radiance,

children.text: cakreṇa cicheda niśātaneminā harir yathā tārkṣyapatatram ujjhitam ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Hari</s> cut it apart with his sharp-rimmed discus, as though it were a cast-off wing-feather of <s>Tārkṣya</s>.

children.text: vṛkṇe svaśūle bahudhāriṇā hareḥ pratyetya vistīrṇam uro vibhūtimat
children.translated_text: When his own spear had been cut down by <s>Hari</s>'s many-edged weapon, the demon came back to his broad, majestic chest,
and, his anger increased, roared, struck him with a hard fist, and vanished.
Struck in this way by him, O <s>Kṣattar</s>, the Blessed Lord, the primeval boar,

children.text: nākampata manāk kvāpi srajā hata iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: did not tremble even slightly anywhere, like an elephant struck with a garland.
Then, against <s>Hari</s>, lord of <s>yogamāyā</s> (divine illusion), he produced many powerful illusions,
and seeing them the creatures, terrified, thought the dissolution of this world had come.

children.text: pravavur vāyavaś caṇḍās tamaḥ pāṃsavam airayan
children.translated_text: Fierce winds blew, raising dusty darkness,

children.text: digbhyo nipetur grāvāṇaḥ kṣepaṇaiḥ prahitā iva ||
children.translated_text: and stones fell from the directions as though hurled by engines.
The sky, its stars lost, was filled with masses of clouds with lightning and thunder,
raining down again and again pus, hair, blood, feces, urine, and bones.
Mountains appeared, O sinless one, releasing many kinds of weapons,
and naked demonesses, armed with spears, with their hair unbound.
With many <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, with infantry, horses, chariots, and elephants,
violent and exceedingly cruel cries were released by murderous assailants.
To destroy those demonic illusions that had been manifested,
the Blessed Lord, the three-striding one, employed his beloved <s>Sudarśana</s> weapon.

children.text: tadā diteḥ samabhavat sahasā hṛdi vepathuḥ
children.translated_text: Then, suddenly, a trembling arose in <s>Diti</s>'s heart,

children.text: smarantyā bhartur ādeśaṃ stanāc cāsṛk prasusruve ||
children.translated_text: as she remembered her husband's instruction, and blood flowed from her breast.
When his own illusions had been destroyed, he again advanced upon <s>Keśava</s>,
embracing him in anger; but then he saw him standing outside.
As he beat him with fists hard as thunderbolts, <s>Adhokṣaja</s>
struck him with his hand at the root of the ear, as <s>Marutpati</s> struck <s>Tvāṣṭra</s>.

children.text: sa āhato viśvajitā hy avajñayā paribhramadgātra udastalocanaḥ
children.translated_text: Struck contemptuously by the conqueror of the universe, he staggered, his limbs whirling and his eyes bulging.
His arms, feet, and hair disheveled, he fell like a great mountain shaken by the wind.

children.text: kṣitau śayānaṃ tam akuṇṭhavarcasaṃ karāladaṃṣṭraṃ paridaṣṭadacchadam
children.translated_text: Seeing him lying on the ground, still of unbroken splendor, with terrible fangs and bitten lip,

children.text: ajādayo vīkṣya śaśaṃsur āgatā aho imaṃ ko nu labheta saṃsthitim ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aja</s> and the others who had come praised him: 'Ah! Who indeed could obtain such a death?'

children.text: yaṃ yogino yogasamādhinā raho dhyāyanti liṅgād asato mumukṣayā
children.translated_text: The one whom yogins meditate upon in solitude through yogic <s>samādhi</s>, seeking release from the unreal bodily mark,

children.text: tasyaiṣa daityaṛṣabhaḥ padāhato mukhaṃ prapaśyaṃs tanum utsasarja ha ||
children.translated_text: this bull among Daityas, struck by his foot, gave up his body while gazing upon his face.

children.text: etau tau pārṣadāv asya śāpād yātāv asadgatim
children.translated_text: These two are indeed his two attendants, who went to an unworthy state because of a curse;

children.text: punaḥ katipayaiḥ sthānaṃ prapatsyete ha janmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: after a few births they will again attain their proper place.
The gods said:
Homage, homage to you, the thread of all sacrifice, who for the world's preservation have assumed a body of stainless purity.

children.text: diṣṭyā hato 'yaṃ jagatām aruntudas tvatpādabhaktyā vayam īśa nirvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By good fortune this tormentor of the worlds has been killed; through devotion to your feet, O Lord, we are at peace.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ hiraṇyākṣam asahyavikramaṃ sa sādayitvā harir ādisūkaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus laid low <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> of unbearable valor, <s>Hari</s>, the primeval boar,

children.text: jagāma lokaṃ svam akhaṇḍitotsavaṃ samīḍitaḥ puṣkaraviṣṭarādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: went to his own world of unbroken festival, praised by <s>Puṣkaraviṣṭara</s> and the others.

children.text: mayā yathānūktam avādi te hareḥ kṛtāvatārasya sumitra ceṣṭitam
children.translated_text: As I have recounted it, O good friend, so has the deed of <s>Hari</s>, who took an incarnation, been told to you:

children.text: yathā hiraṇyākṣa udāravikramo mahāmṛdhe krīḍanavan nirākṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, of noble valor, was cast down in the great battle as if in play.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard this story of the Blessed Lord, narrated by <s>Kauṣārava</s>,
the great devotee <s>Kṣattar</s>, O brahmin, attained supreme joy.
When joy arises from hearing of other holy, famous, and noble persons,

children.text: upaśrutya bhaven modaḥ śrīvatsāṅkasya kiṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how much more from hearing of the one marked with <s>Śrīvatsa</s>?
He quickly freed <s>Gajendra</s>, who had been seized by a crocodile and was meditating on his lotus feet,
from his distress while the female elephants were crying out.
That one is easily worshiped by straightforward men who have no other refuge

children.text: kṛtajñaḥ ko na seveta durārādhyam asādhubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: What grateful person would not serve him, though he is hard for the wicked to propitiate?

children.text: yo vai hiraṇyākṣavadhaṃ mahādbhutaṃ vikrīḍitaṃ kāraṇasūkarātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: He who hears, sings, or readily approves the great marvel, the sportive act of the one whose self is the causal boar, the slaying of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>,

children.text: śṛṇoti gāyaty anumodate 'ñjasā vimucyate brahmavadhād api dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: is freed even from the killing of a brahmin, O twice-born ones.

children.text: etan mahāpuṇyam alaṃ pavitraṃ dhanyaṃ yaśasyaṃ padam āyurāśiṣām
children.translated_text: This is greatly meritorious, fully purifying, blessed, fame-giving, and a source of long life and blessings.

children.text: prāṇendriyāṇāṃ yudhi śauryavardhanaṃ nārāyaṇo 'nte gatir aṅga śṛṇvatām ||
children.translated_text: In battle it increases the valor of the vital powers and senses, and, dear one, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the final goal of those who hear it.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:

children.text: mahīṃ pratiṣṭhām adhyasya saute svāyambhuvo manuḥ
children.translated_text: Having taken his foundation upon the earth, O <s>Sauti</s>, what means did <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s> undertake
as a path for those born after him?
<s>Kṣattā</s>, the great devotee, the one-pointed friend of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: yas tatyājāgrajaṃ kṛṣṇe sāpatyam aghavān iti ||
children.translated_text: abandoned his elder brother along with his sons, because he was an offender against <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Born from the body of <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, he was not inferior to him in greatness.

children.text: sarvātmanā śritaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ tatparāṃś cāpy anuvrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: With his whole self he had taken refuge in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and he also followed those devoted to him.
What did that stainless one, purified by visiting sacred fords, ask <s>Maitreya</s>
after approaching him at <s>Kuśāvarta</s>, where he sat as the supreme knower of truth?

children.text: tayoḥ saṃvadatoḥ sūta pravṛttā hy amalāḥ kathāḥ
children.translated_text: When those two were conversing, O <s>Sūta</s>, pure stories surely began,
resting on the lotus feet of <s>Hari</s> and, like the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, destroying sin.

children.text: tā naḥ kīrtaya bhadraṃ te kīrtanyodārakarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Recount them to us; good fortune to you. They are stories of one whose deeds are noble and worthy of praise.

children.text: rasajñaḥ ko nu tṛpyeta harilīlāmṛtaṃ piban ||
children.translated_text: What connoisseur, drinking the nectar of <s>Hari</s>'s play, could ever be satisfied?
Thus questioned by the sages dwelling in <s>Naimiṣa</s>, <s>Ugraśravas</s>,

children.text: bhagavaty arpitādhyātmas tān āha śrūyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: whose inner self was offered to the Blessed Lord, said to them, "Listen."
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: harer dhṛtakroḍatanoḥ svamāyayā niśamya gor uddharaṇaṃ rasātalāt
children.translated_text: Hearing of <s>Hari</s>'s playful raising of the earth from <s>Rasātala</s> by his own māyā, when he had assumed the body of a boar,

children.text: līlāṃ hiraṇyākṣam avajñayā hataṃ saṃjātaharṣo munim āha bhārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> killed contemptuously in that play, the descendant of <s>Bharata</s>, filled with joy, spoke to the sage.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
After creating the <s>Prajāpatis</s> for the creation of beings, what did the lord of the <s>Prajāpatis</s> begin?

children.text: kim ārabhata me brahman prabrūhy avyaktamārgavit ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, O brahman, knower of the path of the unmanifest.

children.text: ye marīcyādayo viprā yas tu svāyambhuvo manuḥ
children.translated_text: Those brahmins beginning with <s>Marīci</s>, and also <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>:

children.text: te vai brahmaṇa ādeśāt katham etad abhāvayan ||
children.translated_text: by <s>Brahmā</s>'s command, how did they bring this forth?

children.text: sadvitīyāḥ kim asṛjan svatantrā uta karmasu
children.translated_text: Did they create with their wives, or independently in their works?

children.text: āhosvit saṃhatāḥ sarva idaṃ sma samakalpayan ||
children.translated_text: Or did all of them, united together, fashion this world?
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Through inscrutable divine power, supreme and unwinking,
when agitation arose from the Blessed Lord, the great principle came into being from the three guṇas.
From that great principle, predominated by rajas, marked in three ways, and impelled by fate,
arose <s>bhūtādi</s> (the elemental ego), which produced space and the others in fivefold form.
Those elements, each one unable by itself to create the material world,
came together through divine conjunction and brought forth the golden egg.
That egg-shell lay in the waters of the ocean, without a self,

children.text: sāgraṃ vai varṣasāhasram anvavātsīt tam īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the Lord dwelt within it for more than a thousand years.
From his navel arose a lotus, radiant like a thousand suns,
the abode of all communities of living beings, where the self-ruling one himself came into being.
Entered by the Blessed Lord who lies in the watery resting place,

children.text: lokasaṃsthāṃ yathā pūrvaṃ nirmame saṃsthayā svayā ||
children.translated_text: he formed the arrangement of the worlds as before, by his own ordering power.
First he created ignorance from his shadow, with five divisions:
<s>tāmisra</s>, <s>andhatāmisra</s>, <s>tamas</s>, <s>moha</s>, and <s>mahātamas</s>.
Not delighting in that darkness-made body, he cast it off from himself.
The <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s> seized it as night, born from hunger and thirst.

children.text: kṣuttṛḍbhyām upasṛṣṭās te taṃ jagdhum abhidudruvuḥ
children.translated_text: Overcome by hunger and thirst, they ran at him to eat him.

children.text: mā rakṣatainaṃ jakṣadhvam ity ūcuḥ kṣuttṛḍarditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tormented by hunger and thirst, they said, "Do not protect him; eat him!"

children.text: devas tān āha saṃvigno mā māṃ jakṣata rakṣata
children.translated_text: Alarmed, the god said to them, "Do not eat me; protect me.

children.text: aho me yakṣarakṣāṃsi prajā yūyaṃ babhūvitha ||
children.translated_text: Ah, you have become my offspring, <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>."

children.text: devatāḥ prabhayā yā yā dīvyan pramukhato 'sṛjat
children.translated_text: The shining god then created deities from his front by means of radiance.

children.text: te ahārṣur devayanto visṛṣṭāṃ tāṃ prabhām ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Playing as gods, they took that cast-off radiance; it was day.
From his loins the god created non-gods, exceedingly greedy.
Because of their greed, they approached him for sexual union.

children.text: tato hasan sa bhagavān asurair nirapatrapaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed Lord laughed, but, pursued swiftly by the shameless Asuras,
he became angry and afraid, and fled away.
He approached <s>Hari</s>, the giver of boons, the remover of the distress of those who surrender,
who, out of favor for his devotees, shows himself in a form suited to them.

children.text: pāhi māṃ paramātmaṃs te preṣaṇenāsṛjaṃ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: "Protect me, O supreme Self. By your command I created beings.

children.text: tā imā yabhituṃ pāpā upākrāmanti māṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: These sinful ones are now beginning to violate me, O Lord.

children.text: tvam ekaḥ kila lokānāṃ kliṣṭānāṃ kleśanāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: You alone are the destroyer of distress for the worlds when they are afflicted.

children.text: tvam ekaḥ kleśadas teṣām anāsannapadāṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: You alone give distress to those who are not near your feet."
Perceiving his wretchedness, he whose vision of the inner self is clear

children.text: vimuñcātmatanuṃ ghorām ity ukto vimumoca ha ||
children.translated_text: said, "Release your terrible body." Instructed thus, he released it.
When the Asuras perceived that woman, whose lotus feet tinkled and whose eyes were unsteady with intoxication,
whose hips were covered by silk shining with the array of her girdle,
whose high, full breasts pressed closely against one another,
whose nose was beautiful, whose teeth were lovely, and whose playful glances were softened by a gentle smile,
who hid herself out of modesty and was surrounded by dark curls,
all of them, O <s>Dharma</s>, became utterly bewildered by the woman.

children.text: aho rūpam aho dhairyam aho asyā navaṃ vayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Ah, her beauty! Ah, her composure! Ah, her fresh youth!
Among us who desire her, she moves about as if without desire.
Thinking in many ways about that <s>Saṃdhyā</s>, who had the form of a young woman,
the foolish ones honored her with confidence and asked:

children.text: kāsi kasyāsi rambhoru ko vārthas te 'tra bhāmini
children.translated_text: "Who are you? Whose are you, lovely-thighed one? What purpose have you here, beautiful woman?
With the merchandise of the wealth of your beauty, you are tormenting us unfortunate men."

children.text: yā vā kācit tvam abale diṣṭyā saṃdarśanaṃ tava
children.translated_text: Whoever you may be, O helpless lady, by good fortune we have had sight of you;
with your game of ball you agitate the minds of us who are eagerly watching.

children.text: naikatra te jayati śālini pādapadmaṃ ghnantyā muhuḥ karatalena patatpataṃgam
children.translated_text: O graceful one, as you repeatedly strike the falling ball with your palm, your lotus feet do not remain in one place;

children.text: madhyaṃ viṣīdati bṛhatstanabhārabhītaṃ śānteva dṛṣṭir amalā suśikhāsamūhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: your waist droops, afraid of the burden of your large breasts; your clear glance is calm, and your mass of lovely hair is beautiful.
Thus the foolish-minded asuras, thinking the evening twilight, who was making them amorous
and enticing them, to be a woman, seized her.
Laughing, with deep feeling, enjoying himself by himself,
the Blessed Lord, through his radiance, created the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases.

children.text: visasarja tanuṃ tāṃ vai jyotsnāṃ kāntimatīṃ priyām
children.translated_text: Indeed he cast off that body, the beloved shining one called moonlight,
and those very beings, headed by <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, joyfully accepted it.
Having created the Bhūtas and Piśācas from his own lassitude, the Blessed Lord
saw them naked and with loosened hair, and closed his eyes.

children.text: jagṛhus tadvisṛṣṭāṃ tāṃ jṛmbhaṇākhyāṃ tanuṃ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: They took that body abandoned by the Lord, called yawning,
sleep, by which the slackening of the senses is seen among beings;
and that by which they attack those defiled by leftovers is called madness.
The unborn Blessed Lord, thinking himself full of vigor,
created the hosts of Sādhyas and the hosts of Pitṛs through what is unseen.

children.text: ta ātmasargaṃ taṃ kāyaṃ pitaraḥ pratipedire
children.translated_text: The Pitṛs accepted that body, his own emanation,

children.text: sādhyebhyaś ca pitṛbhyaś ca kavayo yad vitanvate ||
children.translated_text: from which the wise extend offerings to the Sādhyas and the Pitṛs.
He created the Siddhas and Vidyādharas by invisibility,
and to them he gave that wondrous body of his called disappearance.
The Lord created Kinnaras and Kimpuruṣas by self-reflection,
honoring himself by himself as he looked upon his own semblance.

children.text: te tu taj jagṛhū rūpaṃ tyaktaṃ yat parameṣṭhinā
children.translated_text: They accepted that form which had been abandoned by <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
and, becoming couples, they sing of him alone at dawn through their rites.
Lying with a body meant for enjoyment, troubled by much thought,

children.text: sarge 'nupacite krodhād utsasarja ha tad vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: he angrily cast off that body because creation had not advanced.
The hairs that fell from that body, dear one, became snakes;
as they crawled away they became cruel serpents, Nāgas with broad hooded necks.
Then <s>Ātmabhū</s>, considering himself as if his task were accomplished,
created at the end the Manus by his mind, sustainers of the worlds.

children.text: tebhyaḥ so 'sṛjat svīyaṃ puraṃ puruṣam ātmavān
children.translated_text: To them the self-possessed one created his own city, the human person;

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā ye purā sṛṣṭāḥ praśaśaṃsuḥ prajāpatim ||
children.translated_text: seeing them, those who had been created before praised <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: aho etaj jagatsraṣṭaḥ sukṛtaṃ bata te kṛtam
children.translated_text: Ah, O creator of the world, well indeed has this been done by you;

children.text: pratiṣṭhitāḥ kriyā yasmin sākam annam adāma he ||
children.translated_text: in him the rites are established, and together with food we partake.
Endowed with austerity, knowledge, and yoga through excellent concentration,
the seer, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, created the seers, his desired progeny.

children.text: tebhyaś caikaikaśaḥ svasya dehasyāṃśam adād ajaḥ
children.translated_text: And to each of them, one by one, the unborn one gave a portion of his own body,
that which possessed samādhi, yoga, power, austerity, knowledge, and detachment.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
And tell of the portion of <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>, supremely esteemed,
O Blessed one, in which offspring increased by sexual union.
<s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s>, the two sons of <s>Svāyambhuva</s>,
protected, according to dharma, the earth with its seven islands.

children.text: tasya vai duhitā brahman devahūtīti viśrutā
children.translated_text: His daughter, O brahman, renowned as <s>Devahūti</s>,
was said by you, sinless one, to be the wife of Prajāpati <s>Kardama</s>.

children.text: tasyāṃ sa vai mahāyogī yuktāyāṃ yogalakṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: In her, who was endowed with the marks of yoga, that great yogin

children.text: sasarja katidhā vīryaṃ tan me śuśrūṣave vada ||
children.translated_text: produced his seed in how many ways? Tell that to me, who wish to hear.

children.text: rucir yo bhagavān brahman dakṣo vā brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: And how, O brahman, did the Blessed <s>Ruci</s>, or <s>Dakṣa</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: yathā sasarja bhūtāni labdhvā bhāryāṃ ca mānavīm ||
children.translated_text: create beings after obtaining a daughter of <s>Manu</s> as wife?
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Commanded by <s>Brahmā</s>, 'Create offspring,' the blessed <s>Kardama</s>

children.text: sarasvatyāṃ tapas tepe sahasrāṇāṃ samā daśa ||
children.translated_text: performed austerity on the <s>Sarasvatī</s> for ten thousand years.
Then <s>Kardama</s>, with his mind joined in samādhi, by kriyāyoga (disciplined ritual practice),
approached <s>Hari</s> with devotion, the swift giver of boons to those who take refuge.

children.text: tāvat prasanno bhagavān puṣkarākṣaḥ kṛte yuge
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed Lord, the lotus-eyed one, was pleased in the Kṛta age,

children.text: darśayāmāsa taṃ kṣattaḥ śābdaṃ brahma dadhad vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and showed himself to him, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, bearing a body that was the verbal <s>brahman</s>.
He saw him stainless, shining like the sun, wearing a garland of white lotuses and blue lotuses,
with a lotus-face framed by masses of soft dark curls, and clad in spotless garments,
wearing a crown and earrings, holding conch, discus, and mace,
with a white lotus as his plaything, with smiling glances that touched the mind,
his lotus feet placed on the shoulder-region of <s>Garuḍa</s>,
standing in the sky, bearing <s>Śrī</s> on his chest and the <s>Kaustubha</s> on his neck.
Filled with joy, having obtained his heart's desire, he fell with his head to the ground,
and, with joined palms, praised him with words, his self by nature filled with affection.
The sage said:

children.text: juṣṭaṃ batādyākhilasattvarāśeḥ sāṃsiddhyam akṣṇos tava darśanān naḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, today the perfection of our eyes has been attained through sight of you, O mass of all beings;

children.text: yad darśanaṃ janmabhir īḍya sadbhir āśāsate yogino rūḍhayogāḥ ||
children.translated_text: O worshipful one, yogins firmly established in yoga hope for that sight through many births among the good.

children.text: ye māyayā te hatamedhasas tvatpādāravindaṃ bhavasindhupotam
children.translated_text: Those whose understanding has been struck down by your māyā worship your lotus feet, the boat across the ocean of becoming,

children.text: upāsate kāmalavāya teṣāṃ rāsīśa kāmān niraye 'pi ye syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of a mere fragment of desire; to them, O Lord, you grant desires, even those that would exist in hell.

children.text: tathā sa cāhaṃ parivoḍhukāmaḥ samānaśīlāṃ gṛhamedhadhenum
children.translated_text: So I too, desiring to marry a household cow of similar character,
though of poor intention, have approached the root, the root of all, whose foot-tree yields desires.

children.text: prajāpates te vacasādhīśa tantyā lokaḥ kilāyaṃ kāmahato 'nubaddhaḥ
children.translated_text: By your word, O lord of progenitors, O ruler, this world, struck by desire, is indeed bound as by a cord.

children.text: ahaṃ ca lokānugato vahāmi baliṃ ca śuklānimiṣāya tubhyam ||
children.translated_text: And I too, following the ways of the world, bring an offering to you, O white, unwinking Lord.

children.text: lokāṃś ca lokānugatān paśūṃś ca hitvā śritās te caraṇātapatram
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the worlds, those who follow the world, and their cattle, they have taken refuge in the parasol of your feet,
their bodily conditions carried away by the nectar-wine of mutual speech about your qualities.

children.text: na te 'jarākṣabhramir āyur eṣāṃ trayodaśāraṃ triśataṃ ṣaṣṭiparva
children.translated_text: For them this span of life is not the whirling of your undecaying axle, with thirteen spokes, three hundred and sixty joints,

children.text: ṣaṇnemy anantacchadi yat trinābhi karālasroto jagad ācchidya dhāvat ||
children.translated_text: six rims, endless leaves, and three hubs, whose terrible current runs on, cutting down the world.

children.text: ekaḥ svayaṃ san jagataḥ sisṛkṣayādvitīyayātmann adhiyogamāyayā
children.translated_text: Being one yourself, yet wishing to create the universe, by your yoga-māyā you enter a second form of yourself;

children.text: sṛjasy adaḥ pāsi punar grasiṣyase yathorṇanābhir bhagavan svaśaktibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: you create this, you protect it, and again you will swallow it up, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, like a spider by its own powers.

children.text: naitad batādhīśa padaṃ tavepsitaṃ yan māyayā nas tanuṣe bhūtasūkṣmam
children.translated_text: Surely this, O supreme lord, is not the state desired by you, that through māyā you spread out for us the subtle elements.

children.text: anugrahāyāstv api yarhi māyayā lasattulasyā bhagavān vilakṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yet it is for grace, whenever the <s>Bhagavān</s>, marked by shining tulasī, becomes distinct through that māyā.
I repeatedly bow to you, who, when realized, bring the aim of action to rest, and who by your own māyā keep the order of the worlds turning;
your lotus feet are worthy of reverence and rain down desires even upon the very small.
The sage said:

children.text: ity avyalīkaṃ praṇuto 'bjanābhas tam ābabhāṣe vacasāmṛtena
children.translated_text: Thus praised without deceit, the lotus-naveled Lord addressed him with nectar-like words,
shining upon the back of <s>Suparṇa</s>, his brows moving with the play of a loving smile and sidelong glance.
<s>Śrībhagavān</s> said:

children.text: viditvā tava caityaṃ me puraiva samayoji tat
children.translated_text: Your intention has already been known by me, and that was arranged beforehand:
the purpose for which you yourself worshiped me with disciplines of self-restraint.

children.text: na vai jātu mṛṣaiva syāt prajādhyakṣa madarhaṇam
children.translated_text: Worship offered to me is never in vain, O lord of creatures,
especially among people like you, whose selves are firmly gathered into me.
The emperor <s>Manu</s>, son of the lord of creatures, famed for auspiciousness,
dwells in <s>Brahmāvarta</s> and rules the earth encircled by seven oceans.

children.text: sa ceha vipra rājarṣir mahiṣyā śatarūpayā
children.translated_text: That royal sage, O brahmin, together with his queen <s>Śatarūpā</s>,
will come here the day after tomorrow, wishing to see you, learned in <s>dharma</s>.
He will give his daughter, dark at the corners of her eyes and endowed with age, conduct, and virtues,

children.text: mṛgayantīṃ patiṃ dāsyaty anurūpāya te prabho ||
children.translated_text: who is seeking a husband, to you, O lord, who are suited to her.
She upon whom your heart has been fixed for these many years

children.text: sā tvāṃ brahman nṛpavadhūḥ kāmam āśu bhajiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will quickly serve you according to your desire, O brahmin, though she is a king's daughter.

children.text: yā ta ātmabhṛtaṃ vīryaṃ navadhā prasaviṣyati
children.translated_text: She will give birth in ninefold form to the seed that you have borne in yourself;
and in your seed the sages will readily establish themselves.

children.text: tvaṃ ca samyag anuṣṭhāya nideśaṃ ma uśattamaḥ
children.translated_text: And you, O most excellent and pure one, after properly carrying out my command,
will dedicate the purpose of all rites to me as a tīrtha and will resort to me.

children.text: kṛtvā dayāṃ ca jīveṣu dattvā cābhayam ātmavān
children.translated_text: Showing compassion to living beings, granting fearlessness, and self-possessed,

children.text: mayy ātmānaṃ saha jagad drakṣyasy ātmani cāpi mām ||
children.translated_text: you will see the self together with the world in me, and me also in the self.
I myself, with a portion of my own part, through your seed, O great sage,
will propound the compendium of principles in your field, in <s>Devahūti</s>.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having thus spoken to him in reply, the <s>Bhagavān</s> beyond the senses
went away from <s>Bindusaras</s>, which was surrounded by the <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
As he watched, the Lord went along the perfected path praised by all the lords of accomplished beings,
listening to the lofty Sāman-chant uttered by the wings of the king of birds.

children.text: atha samprasthite śukle kardamo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when the bright Lord had departed, the blessed sage <s>Kardama</s>

children.text: āste sma bindusarasi taṃ kālaṃ pratipālayan ||
children.translated_text: remained at <s>Bindusaras</s>, awaiting that time.
<s>Manu</s>, mounting a chariot covered with gold,

children.text: āropya svāṃ duhitaraṃ sabhāryaḥ paryaṭan mahīm ||
children.translated_text: placed his own daughter upon it and, with his wife, traveled over the earth.

children.text: tasmin sudhanvann ahani bhagavān yat samādiśat
children.translated_text: On that day, O <s>Sudhanvan</s>, as the <s>Bhagavān</s> had instructed,
he approached the hermitage of that sage of peaceful vows.
There drops of tears had fallen from the eyes of the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
when he was deeply overcome with compassion directed toward the surrendered one.

children.text: tad vai bindusaro nāma sarasvatyā pariplutam
children.translated_text: That place, named <s>Bindusaras</s>, flooded by the <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
was holy, with auspicious nectar-like water, and was frequented by hosts of great seers.
It was filled with networks of holy trees and creepers, and with holy beasts and birds calling out;
rich in fruits and flowers of every season, it possessed the beauty of rows of forest growth.
It resounded with flocks of excited birds and had the movement of intoxicated bees;
it was splendid with dancing peacocks in rut and with calling cuckoos intoxicated with song.
It was adorned with kadamba, campaka, aśoka, karañja, bakula, and āsana trees,
with kunda, mandāra, and kuṭaja, and with young mango shoots.
It was sweetly sounded by kāraṇḍava ducks, plavas, swans, ospreys, waterfowl,

children.text: sārasaiś cakravākaiś ca cakorair valgu kūjitam ||
children.translated_text: cranes, cakravākas, and cakora birds.
Likewise it was surrounded by deer, boars, porcupines, wild oxen, elephants,

children.text: gopucchair haribhir markair nakulair nābhibhir vṛtam ||
children.translated_text: gopucchas, monkeys, apes, mongooses, and nābhis.
Entering that foremost tīrtha, the first king, together with his daughter,
saw the sage seated there, after he had offered oblations into the fire.
He was radiant in body, yoked for a long time to fierce austerity,
yet not too emaciated, because of the affectionate sidelong glance of the <s>Bhagavān</s>
and because he had heard the nectar-stream of his spoken words.
He was tall, lotus-petal-eyed, matted-haired, and clothed in bark garments;
approaching him, the king saw that he was soiled and not adorned as would befit him.
Then, when the human lord had come to the hut and bowed before him,
the sage received him with hospitality, honoring him in a fitting way.
When the king had accepted the offering and was seated, restrained and composed, the sage, pleasing him,

children.text: smaran bhagavadādeśam ity āha ślakṣṇayā girā ||
children.translated_text: remembering the command of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus in a gentle voice:

children.text: nūnaṃ caṅkramaṇaṃ deva satāṃ saṃrakṣaṇāya te
children.translated_text: Surely, O lord, your roaming is for the protection of the good,

children.text: vadhāya cāsatāṃ yas tvaṃ hareḥ śaktir hi pālinī ||
children.translated_text: and for the destruction of the wicked, for you are indeed the protecting power of <s>Hari</s>.
You assume the forms and stations of the sun, moon, fire, Indra, wind, Yama, Dharma, and Pracetas;

children.text: rūpāṇi sthāna ādhatse tasmai śuklāya te namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: obeisance to that pure one of yours.

children.text: na yadā ratham āsthāya jaitraṃ maṇigaṇārpitam
children.translated_text: If you did not mount your victorious chariot, set with clusters of jewels,
with its fierce bow flashing, and terrify the wicked by your chariot,
shaking the circle of the earth, crushed by the feet of your own army,

children.text: vikarṣan bṛhatīṃ senāṃ paryaṭasy aṃśumān iva ||
children.translated_text: and drawing along a great army as you roamed like the sun,
then, O king, all the boundaries bound up with <s>varṇāśrama</s>
and made by the Blessed Lord would at once be broken by robbers.

children.text: adharmaś ca samedheta lolupair vyaṅkuśair nṛbhiḥ
children.translated_text: Unrighteousness would increase through greedy kings without restraint;
while you slept, this world, seized by robbers, would perish.

children.text: athāpi pṛcche tvāṃ vīra yadarthaṃ tvam ihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Even so, O hero, I ask you the purpose for which you have come here;
we shall accept it with an unfeigned heart.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
When all the rise of his qualities and deeds had thus been made manifest,

children.text: savrīḍa iva taṃ samrāḍ upāratam uvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: the emperor, as if bashful, addressed the sage when he had ceased speaking.
<s>Manu</s> said:
<s>Brahmā</s>, seeking to protect himself, created you from his own mouth:
made of sacred hymns, joined with austerity, knowledge, and yoga, and free from greed.
For their protection he created us from his thousand arms, O thousand-footed one;

children.text: hṛdayaṃ tasya hi brahma kṣatram aṅgaṃ pracakṣate ||
children.translated_text: for <s>brahman</s> is called his heart, and <s>kṣatra</s> his limb.

children.text: ato hy anyonyam ātmānaṃ brahma kṣatraṃ ca rakṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>brahman</s> and <s>kṣatra</s> protect one another as their own self;

children.text: rakṣati smāvyayo devaḥ sa yaḥ sadasadātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that imperishable god, whose nature is being and non-being, protects them.

children.text: tava saṃdarśanād eva chinnā me sarvasaṃśayāḥ
children.translated_text: By the mere sight of you all my doubts have been cut off,

children.text: yat svayaṃ bhagavān prītyā dharmam āha rirakṣiṣoḥ ||
children.translated_text: since the Blessed Lord himself, out of affection, has spoken <s>dharma</s> for one wishing to protect it.

children.text: diṣṭyā me bhagavān dṛṣṭo durdarśo yo 'kṛtātmanām
