children.translated_text: By good fortune I have seen you, Blessed One, who are hard to see for those whose selves are uncultivated;

children.text: diṣṭyā pādarajaḥ spṛṣṭaṃ śīrṣṇā me bhavataḥ śivam ||
children.translated_text: by good fortune the auspicious dust of your feet has been touched by my head.
By good fortune I have been instructed by you, and a great favor has been done for me;
by good fortune, through opened ear-passages, I have enjoyed your shining words.
Therefore, being such a one, please hear what I, whose heart is afflicted by affection for my daughter,

children.text: śrotum arhasi dīnasya śrāvitaṃ kṛpayā mune ||
children.translated_text: poor as I am, have said to you in appeal, O sage, out of compassion.
This daughter of mine, the sister of <s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s>,
seeks a husband suited to her in age, character, virtues, and the like.
When she heard from <s>Nārada</s> of your character, learning, beauty, age, and virtues,

children.text: aśṛṇon nāradād eṣā tvayy āsīt kṛtaniścayā ||
children.translated_text: she fixed her decision upon you.
Therefore accept her, best of twice-born men, offered by me with faith,
entirely suited to you in the duties of householders.

children.text: udyatasya hi kāmasya prativādo na śasyate
children.translated_text: For the refusal of desire that has arisen is not praised,
even in one freed from attachment; how much less in one colored by desire.
The man who disregards what is offered and goes to beg from a wretched giver

children.text: kṣīyate tadyaśaḥ sphītaṃ mānaś cāvajñayā hataḥ ||
children.translated_text: sees his abundant fame decline, and his honor is destroyed by contempt.
But I have heard, learned one, that you are prepared for marriage;

children.text: atas tvam upakurvāṇaḥ prattāṃ pratigṛhāṇa me ||
children.translated_text: therefore, doing me a favor, accept her whom I give.
The sage said:
Certainly, I desire to marry, and your daughter has not yet been given away;
this first rite of marriage is fitting for us both.

children.text: kāmaḥ sa bhūyān naradeva te 'syāḥ putryāḥ samāmnāyavidhau pratītaḥ
children.translated_text: May that desire for this daughter of yours be fulfilled, O king, as it is recognized in the Vedic ordinance;

children.text: ka eva te tanayāṃ nādriyeta svayaiva kāntyā kṣipatīm iva śriyam ||
children.translated_text: for who indeed would not honor your daughter, who by her own beauty seems to cast aside <s>Śrī</s>?
Seeing her on the palace roof, lovely with anklets ringing on her feet, playing, her eyes bewildered by the ball,

children.text: viśvāvasur nyapatat svād vimānād vilokya sammohavimūḍhacetāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāvasu</s> fell from his own aerial car, his mind deluded with bewilderment.
She is seeking me: the crest-jewel of women, unseen by those whose feet splendor has not served;

children.text: vatsāṃ manor uccapadaḥ svasāraṃ ko nānumanyeta budho 'bhiyātām ||
children.translated_text: what wise man would not approve her, the beloved daughter of <s>Manu</s> and sister of <s>Uttānapāda</s>, when she has come to him?

children.text: ato bhajiṣye samayena sādhvīṃ yāvat tejo bibhṛyād ātmano me
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall take this virtuous woman by agreement, so long as she bears my own seed;

children.text: ato dharmān pāramahaṃsyamukhyān śuklaproktān bahu manye 'vihiṃsrān ||
children.translated_text: after that, I shall highly honor the foremost <s>pāramahaṃsya</s> dharmas, taught in purity and free from harm.

children.text: yato 'bhavad viśvam idaṃ vicitraṃ saṃsthāsyate yatra ca vāvatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: From him this variegated universe has arisen, in him it will be dissolved, and in him it abides;

children.text: prajāpatīnāṃ patir eṣa mahyaṃ paraṃ pramāṇaṃ bhagavān anantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that Blessed <s>Ananta</s>, lord of the lords of creatures, is the supreme authority for me.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: sa ugradhanvann iyad evābabhāṣe āsīc ca tūṣṇīm aravindanābham
children.translated_text: O mighty archer, he spoke only this much and then became silent, holding the lotus-naveled Lord in his thought;

children.text: dhiyopagṛhṇan smitaśobhitena mukhena ceto lulubhe devahūtyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with his smile-bright face he captured the heart of <s>Devahūti</s>.

children.text: so 'nu jñātvā vyavasitaṃ mahiṣyā duhituḥ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: Then, clearly understanding the settled intention of his queen and daughter,
he joyfully gave her, a fitting match, to that man rich in hosts of virtues.
The great queen <s>Śatarūpā</s>, with affection, bestowed great bridal wealth
upon the couple: ornaments, garments, and household furnishings.
Having given his daughter to a suitable man, the emperor, freed from anxiety,
embraced her with his arms, his heart churned by longing.
Unable to bear separation from her, shedding drops of tears again and again,

children.text: āsiñcad amba vatseti netrodair duhituḥ śikhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: he wetted his daughter’s hair with the water of his eyes, saying, “Mother, dear child.”
Taking leave of that best of sages, and permitted by him, together with his retinue,

children.text: pratasthe ratham āruhya sabhāryaḥ svapuraṃ nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king mounted his chariot with his wife and set out for his own city.
On both lovely banks of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the stream of the sages,
he saw the hermitage-wealth of tranquil seers.

children.text: tam āyāntam abhipretya brahmāvartāt prajāḥ patim
children.translated_text: Perceiving their lord coming from <s>Brahmāvarta</s>,
the subjects joyfully came out to meet him with songs, praises, and instruments.
There was a city named <s>Barhiṣmatī</s>, endowed with every prosperity,
where the hairs of <s>Yajña</s> had fallen as he shook his body.
The kuśa grasses and kāśa reeds were those very ones, ever green in appearance,

children.text: ṛṣayo yaiḥ parābhāvya yajñaghnān yajñam ījire ||
children.translated_text: with which the sages, having overcome the destroyers of sacrifice, performed the sacrifice.
Spreading a barhis made of kuśa and kāśa, the blessed <s>Manu</s>

children.text: ayajad yajñapuruṣaṃ labdhā sthānaṃ yato bhuvam ||
children.translated_text: sacrificed to the <s>Yajñapuruṣa</s>, from whom he had obtained the earth as his place.

children.text: barhiṣmatīṃ nāma vibhur yāṃ nirviśya samāvasat
children.translated_text: The mighty one entered and dwelt in that city named <s>Barhiṣmatī</s>;
having entered a dwelling there, he found it a destroyer of the threefold suffering.
Together with his wife and children, he enjoyed his desires without opposition to the other aims.
His true fame was sung by women and by divine singers,

children.text: pratyūṣeṣv anubaddhena hṛdā śṛṇvan hareḥ kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and at daybreak, with attentive heart, he continually listened to stories of <s>Hari</s>.
<s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s> was a sage deeply immersed in yogamāyā,

children.text: yad ābhraṃśayituṃ bhogā na śekur bhagavatparam ||
children.translated_text: whom pleasures could not make fall away, since he was wholly devoted to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
His watches of time were not spent in vain; they passed in sustaining his inner self,

children.text: śṛṇvato dhyāyato viṣṇoḥ kurvato bruvataḥ kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as he listened to, meditated on, performed, and spoke the stories of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: sa evaṃ svāntaraṃ ninye yugānām ekasaptatim
children.translated_text: Thus he passed the span of his own manvantara, seventy-one yugas,
through association with <s>Vāsudeva</s>, having overcome the threefold course of worldly existence.

children.text: śārīrā mānasā divyā vaiyāse ye ca mānuṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Bodily, mental, divine, and human afflictions, O <s>Vaiyāsa</s>,

children.text: bhautikāś ca kathaṃ kleśā bādhante harisaṃśrayam ||
children.translated_text: and material sufferings as well: how can they oppress one who has taken refuge in <s>Hari</s>?

children.text: yaḥ pṛṣṭo munibhiḥ prāha dharmān nānāvidhān śubhān
children.translated_text: When asked by the sages, he taught many kinds of auspicious <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty),
the duties of men and of the varṇas and āśramas, always seeking the welfare of all beings.

children.text: etat ta ādirājasya manoś caritam adbhutam
children.translated_text: This wondrous career of the primal king <s>Manu</s>, who is worthy of description,
has been described to you; now hear of the rise of his offspring.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
When her parents had departed, the virtuous woman, skilled in understanding her husband's signs,

children.text: nityaṃ paryacarat prītyā bhavānīva bhavaṃ prabhum ||
children.translated_text: constantly attended her husband with love, as <s>Bhavānī</s> attends the lord <s>Bhava</s>.
With confidence, purity of self, respect, and self-restraint,

children.text: śuśrūṣayā sauhṛdena vācā madhurayā ca bhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: with service, affection, and sweet speech, O sir,

children.text: visṛjya kāmaṃ dambhaṃ ca dveṣaṃ lobham aghaṃ madam
children.translated_text: discarding desire, hypocrisy, hatred, greed, sin, and pride,
always vigilant and diligent, she satisfied the more powerful one.

children.text: sa vai devarṣivaryas tāṃ mānavīṃ samanuvratām
children.translated_text: That foremost divine sage saw that daughter of <s>Manu</s> following his vow,
as she hoped for great blessings from a husband greater by divine allotment.
After a long time she had grown thin, wasted by the practice of vows,
and, pained by compassion, he spoke in a voice choked with love.
<s>Kardama</s> said:

children.text: tuṣṭo 'ham adya tava mānavi mānadāyāḥ śuśrūṣayā paramayā parayā ca bhaktyā
children.translated_text: I am pleased today, O daughter of <s>Manu</s>, giver of honor, by your supreme service and highest devotion.

children.text: yo dehinām ayam atīva suhṛt sa deho nāvekṣitaḥ samucitaḥ kṣapituṃ madarthe ||
children.translated_text: For my sake you have not cared for this body, though it is very dear to embodied beings and fit to be preserved.
The blessings of the <s>Bhagavān</s> that I have won by austerity, concentration, knowledge, self-discipline, and yoga while devoted to my own <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: tān eva te madanusevanayāvaruddhān dṛṣṭiṃ prapaśya vitarāmy abhayān aśokān ||
children.translated_text: those very powers, secured by your attendance on me, behold with divine sight; I bestow them on you, free from fear and sorrow.

children.text: anye punar bhagavato bhruva udvijṛmbhavibhraṃśitārtharacanāḥ kim urukramasya
children.translated_text: Other attainments have their arrangements of value ruined by the mere playful expansion of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s brow; what are they before <s>Urukrama</s>?

children.text: siddhāsi bhuṅkṣva vibhavān nijadharmadohān divyān narair duradhigān nṛpavikriyābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: You have attained perfection; enjoy divine splendors, milked from your own <s>dharma</s>, difficult for men to obtain even through the transformations of kingship.

children.text: evaṃ bruvāṇam abalākhilayogamāyāvidyāvicakṣaṇam avekṣya gatādhir āsīt
children.translated_text: Seeing him speak thus, the helpless woman looked upon him, expert in all yogamāyā and knowledge, and her anxiety departed.
With a voice overwhelmed by reverence and love, her face shining with a bashful glance and slight smile, she said:
<s>Devahūti</s> said:

children.text: rāddhaṃ bata dvijavṛṣaitad amoghayogamāyādhipe tvayi vibho tad avaimi bhartaḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed this has been accomplished, O bull among twice-born men; in you, O powerful husband, lord of unfailing yogamāyā, I know it to be so.

children.text: yas te 'bhyadhāyi samayaḥ sakṛd aṅgasaṅgo bhūyād garīyasi guṇaḥ prasavaḥ satīnām ||
children.translated_text: But the condition you once declared to me, that bodily union should occur and that offspring is the greater virtue for chaste women, remains.

children.text: tatretikṛtyam upaśikṣa yathopadeśaṃ yenaiṣa me karśito 'tiriraṃsayātmā
children.translated_text: Therefore teach me what is to be done in this matter, according to your instruction, by which this body of mine, emaciated through excessive longing,

children.text: sidhyeta te kṛtamanobhavadharṣitāyā dīnas tad īśa bhavanaṃ sadṛśaṃ vicakṣva ||
children.translated_text: may succeed for you, O lord; for I am wretched and overcome by the passion you have stirred. Consider a dwelling suitable for that.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: priyāyāḥ priyam anvicchan kardamo yogam āsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Desiring to do what was dear to his beloved, <s>Kardama</s> resorted to yoga,
and just then, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, he created an aerial palace that moved at will.
It was divine, yielding every desire and furnished with every jewel,
promising the growth of every prosperity and equipped with jewel pillars.
It was provided with divine appliances and brought comfort in every season,
adorned with colorful hangings and banners.
It was decorated with garlands and varied flower wreaths, with bees sweetly humming,
and it shone with fine cloth, linen, silk, and many kinds of garments.
In dwellings set one above another, each arranged separately,
it was lovely with cushions laid out, with couches, fans, and seats.
Here and there it was adorned with various works of art placed about,
served by a great emerald floor and coral platforms.
At the doors it shone with coral thresholds and diamond doors,
and golden jars were set upon its sapphire peaks.
It was fitted with foremost rubies like seeing eyes, set in diamond walls,
and adorned with variegated canopies and costly golden gateways.
Here and there it resounded with flocks of swans and pigeons,
which, thinking the artificial birds to be their own, repeatedly perched upon them.
With pleasure grounds, resting places, sleeping chambers, courtyards, and inner courts,
arranged according to every enjoyment, it seemed to astonish even itself.

children.text: īdṛg gṛhaṃ tat paśyantīṃ nātiprītena cetasā
children.translated_text: As she looked at such a house, with a mind not overly pleased,
<s>Kardama</s> himself, who knew the hearts of all beings, spoke to her:

children.text: nimajyāsmin hrade bhīru vimānam idam āruha
children.translated_text: Immerse yourself in this lake, timid one, and then mount this aerial palace.

children.text: idaṃ śuklakṛtaṃ tīrtham āśiṣāṃ yāpakaṃ nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: This pure tīrtha (holy ford) is the fulfiller of blessings for men.

children.text: sā tad bhartuḥ samādāya vacaḥ kuvalayekṣaṇā
children.translated_text: She, lotus-eyed, accepted that word of her husband,

children.text: sarajaṃ bibhratī vāso veṇībhūtāṃś ca mūrdhajān ||
children.translated_text: wearing a garment covered with dust and her hair matted into a braid.
Her body was covered with a layer of dirt and her breasts were discolored;
she entered the lake of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, a reservoir of auspicious water.

children.text: sāntaḥ sarasi veśmasthāḥ śatāni daśa kanyakāḥ
children.translated_text: Inside the lake she saw ten hundreds of maidens stationed in a palace,
all of youthful age and fragrant like blue lotuses.

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya procuḥ prāñjalayaḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing her, those women rose up at once and, with joined palms, said,

children.text: vayaṃ karmakarīs tubhyaṃ śādhi naḥ karavāma kim ||
children.translated_text: "We are your servants. Command us; what shall we do?"
After bathing the high-minded woman with a very costly bath,

children.text: dukūle nirmale nūtane dadur asyai ca mānadāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the respectful maidens gave her clean, new silk garments.
They gave ornaments of the highest value, superior and radiant,
food furnished with every excellence, and drink like nectar-wine.
Then, in a mirror, she saw herself garlanded and clothed in spotless garments,
free from impurity, blessed by auspicious rites, and greatly honored by the maidens.
She had bathed, washed her hair, and was adorned with every ornament;
she had a niṣka at her neck, bracelets on her arms, and jingling golden anklets.
On her hips rested a golden girdle set with many jewels,

children.text: hāreṇa ca mahārheṇa rucakena ca bhūṣitam ||
children.translated_text: and she was adorned with a very costly necklace and with a rucaka ornament.
With fine teeth, beautiful brows, and eyes whose sidelong glances were smooth and moist,
her face shone, framed by dark curls that rivaled lotus buds.

children.text: yadā sasmāra ṛṣabham ṛṣīṇāṃ dayitaṃ patim
children.translated_text: When she remembered her husband, the best of sages and her beloved lord,

children.text: tatra cāste saha strībhir yatrāste sa prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: she was there together with the women, where that <s>Prajāpati</s> was staying.
Then, seeing herself before her husband, surrounded by a thousand women,
she became uncertain about that course of his yogic power.
He saw her, cleansed by a bath that removed her dirt, shining as never before,
displaying her own beauty, with her lovely breasts covered by garments.
She was well dressed and attended by a thousand <s>Vidyādharī</s> women;
feeling love arise, he made her ascend that vimāna, O destroyer of enemies.

children.text: tasminn aluptamahimā priyayānurakto vidyādharībhir upacīrṇavapur vimāne
children.translated_text: In that vimāna, his greatness undiminished, attached to his beloved, and his body served by <s>Vidyādharī</s> women,

children.text: babhrāja utkacakumudgaṇavān apīcyas tārābhir āvṛta ivoḍupatir nabhaḥsthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he shone like the moon in the sky, beautiful among clusters of blossoming kumudas and surrounded by stars.
With that aircraft he traveled in the valleys of the chief encircling mountains of the eight world-regions, lovely with breezes that are companions of Kāma,

children.text: siddhair nuto dyudhunipātaśivasvanāsu reme ciraṃ dhanadavallalanāvarūthī ||
children.translated_text: and, praised by siddhas amid the auspicious sounds of falling heavenly streams, he enjoyed for a long time, surrounded by women like the beloveds of <s>Dhanada</s>.
In <s>Vaiśrambhaka</s>, in the divine forest <s>Nandana</s>, in <s>Puṣpabhadraka</s>,

children.text: mānase caitrarathye ca sa reme rāmayā rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: at <s>Mānasa</s> and <s>Caitrarathya</s>, he enjoyed himself, delighted with his beloved wife.
With the brilliant, mighty vimāna that went wherever he wished,
he surpassed the aerial travelers as he moved through the worlds like the wind.
What is hard to obtain for those men of unbounded mind,
by whom the foot of <s>Tīrthapada</s>, the end of distress, has been taken as refuge?

children.text: prekṣayitvā bhuvo golaṃ patnyai yāvān svasaṃsthayā
children.translated_text: After showing his wife the globe of the earth, as extensive as it was in its own arrangement,
the great yogin returned to his own hermitage, filled with many wonders.
Dividing himself ninefold, he delighted <s>Mānavī</s>, who was eager for love,
and enjoyed with his beautiful wife for many years as though they were a moment.

children.text: tasmin vimāna utkṛṣṭāṃ śayyāṃ ratikarīṃ śritā
children.translated_text: Resting on an excellent bed in that vimāna, a bed that aroused love,

children.text: na cābudhyata taṃ kālaṃ patyāpīcyena saṃgatā ||
children.translated_text: she did not notice that time while united with her handsome husband.
Thus, by the power of yoga, while the couple enjoyed each other,
a hundred autumns passed for those two, who were still somewhat eager for desire.

children.text: tasyām ādhatta retas tāṃ bhāvayann ātmanātmavit
children.translated_text: The self-knower placed his seed in her, causing her to conceive by his own self,

children.text: nodhā vidhāya rūpaṃ svaṃ sarvasaṃkalpavid vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: after dividing his own form ninefold, the all-powerful one who knew every intention.

children.text: ataḥ sā suṣuve sadyo devahūtiḥ striyaḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Thereafter <s>Devahūti</s> at once gave birth to female children,
all of them lovely in every limb and fragrant like red lotuses.
Then she perceived that her husband was about to go forth, and, though smiling outwardly,
she was agitated, her heart aching and distressed.
With downcast face she traced the ground with her foot, bright with the jewels of her nails,
and slowly spoke graceful words, holding back drops of tears.
<s>Devahūti</s> said:

children.text: sarvaṃ tad bhagavān mahyam upovāha pratiśrutam
children.translated_text: The blessed lord has fulfilled for me everything that was promised,

children.text: athāpi me prapannāyā abhayaṃ dātum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: yet you ought to grant fearlessness to me, who have taken refuge.

children.text: brahman duhitṛbhis tubhyaṃ vimṛgyāḥ patayaḥ samāḥ
children.translated_text: O brahmin, suitable husbands must be sought for these daughters of yours;

children.text: kaścit syān me viśokāya tvayi pravrajite vanam ||
children.translated_text: and when you have gone forth to the forest, may there be someone to remove my sorrow.
Enough of this time that has passed for me, O lord,
in attachment to sense objects, while I had abandoned the supreme self.

children.text: indriyārtheṣu sajantyā prasaṅgas tvayi me kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Though I attached myself to the objects of the senses, my attachment was fixed on you;

children.text: ajānantyā paraṃ bhāvaṃ tathāpy astv abhayāya me ||
children.translated_text: not knowing your supreme nature, may even that become a source of fearlessness for me.

children.text: saṅgo yaḥ saṃsṛter hetur asatsu vihito 'dhiyā
children.translated_text: Attachment, when directed by ignorance toward the unreal, is the cause of transmigration;

children.text: sa eva sādhuṣu kṛto niḥsaṅgatvāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: that very same attachment, when directed toward the good, is fit to bring about freedom from attachment.

children.text: neha yat karma dharmāya na virāgāya kalpate
children.translated_text: A deed here that does not serve <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), does not lead to detachment,

children.text: na tīrthapadasevāyai jīvann api mṛto hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and does not serve <s>Tīrthapada</s> is death itself; though living, such a person is dead.

children.text: sāhaṃ bhagavato nūnaṃ vañcitā māyayā dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Surely I have been deeply deceived by the māyā of the <s>Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: yat tvāṃ vimuktidaṃ prāpya na mumukṣeya bandhanāt ||
children.translated_text: for, having obtained you, the giver of liberation, I did not seek release from bondage.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
As the daughter of <s>Manu</s> spoke in this way, voicing disenchantment, the compassionate sage
addressed that virtuous woman, remembering the pure declaration that had been spoken.
The sage said:

children.text: mā khido rājaputrīttham ātmānaṃ praty anindite
children.translated_text: Do not grieve about yourself in this way, O blameless princess;
the imperishable <s>Bhagavān</s> will very soon enter your womb.

children.text: dhṛtavratāsi bhadraṃ te damena niyamena ca
children.translated_text: You have kept your vows. Blessing be upon you. With restraint and observance,
and with austerity, gifts of wealth, and faith, worship <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: sa tvayārādhitaḥ śuklo vitanvan māmakaṃ yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: He, the white one worshiped by you, extending my fame,
will cut the knot of your heart, being generous and devoted to brahman.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
<s>Devahūti</s> too, with reverence for the command of the lord of creatures,

children.text: samyak śraddhāya puruṣaṃ kūṭastham abhajad gurum ||
children.translated_text: properly accepted it with faith and worshiped the changeless <s>Puruṣa</s> as her teacher.
After a long time, in her the Blessed <s>Madhusūdana</s>,

children.text: kārdamaṃ vīryam āpanno jajñe 'gnir iva dāruṇi ||
children.translated_text: having entered the seed of <s>Kardama</s>, was born like fire in wood.
Then in the sky the thick clouds sounded musical instruments;

children.text: gāyanti taṃ sma gandharvā nṛtyanty apsaraso mudā ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Gandharvas</s> sang of him, and the <s>Apsarases</s> danced with joy.
Divine flowers fell, dropped by the sky-roamers,

children.text: praseduś ca diśaḥ sarvā ambhāṃsi ca manāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: and all the quarters, the waters, and minds became clear and serene.
To that hermitage-place of <s>Kardama</s>, surrounded by the <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Svayambhū</s>, together with sages beginning with <s>Marīci</s>, came.
Knowing, O slayer of foes, that the Blessed One, the supreme brahman, had been born through an aṃśa of sattva,
to declare the knowledge of the enumeration of principles, the unborn self-ruling one came.
Honoring with a purified mind what he wished to do,
and with his life-breaths rejoicing, he addressed <s>Kardama</s> as follows.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
My worship has been rendered by you, dear son, without deceit,

children.text: yan me saṃjagṛhe vākyaṃ bhavān mānada mānayan ||
children.translated_text: since you, giver of honor, honored and accepted my word.

children.text: etāvaty eva śuśrūṣā kāryā pitari putrakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Only so much service is to be performed by sons toward a father:

children.text: bāḍham ity anumanyeta gauraveṇa guror vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with reverence one should assent firmly to the word of the guru.

children.text: imā duhitaraḥ satyas tava vatsa sumadhyamāḥ
children.translated_text: These truthful, slender-waisted daughters of yours, dear child,

children.text: sargam etaṃ prabhāvaiḥ svair bṛṃhayiṣyanty anekadhā ||
children.translated_text: will increase this creation in many ways through their own powers.
Therefore today give your daughters to the foremost sages according to their character and according to their liking,

children.text: ātmajāḥ paridehy adya vistṛṇīhi yaśo bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: and spread your fame upon the earth.
I know the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, descended by his own māyā,

children.text: bhūtānāṃ śevadhiṃ dehaṃ bibhrāṇaṃ kapilaṃ mune ||
children.translated_text: bearing the body named <s>Kapila</s>, the treasury of beings, O sage.
With the yoga of knowledge and discriminative realization, unraveling the tangles of actions,
he is golden-haired, lotus-eyed, and his lotus-feet bear the marks of lotuses.

children.text: eṣa mānavi te garbhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ kaiṭabhārdanaḥ
children.translated_text: This destroyer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, O daughter of <s>Manu</s>, has entered your womb;
cutting the knot of ignorance and doubt, he will wander over the earth.
This lord of hosts of perfected beings, highly approved by the teachers of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>,

children.text: loke kapila ity ākhyāṃ gantā te kīrtivardhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will obtain in the world the name <s>Kapila</s>, increasing your fame.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having reassured those two, the creator of the world, together with the <s>Kumāras</s> and <s>Nārada</s>,
went, as a swan, by his swan vehicle to the supreme threefold abode.

children.text: gate śatadhṛtau kṣattaḥ kardamas tena coditaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Śatadhṛti</s> had gone, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, <s>Kardama</s>, urged by him,
then gave his daughters to the creators of the universe as instructed.
He gave <s>Kalā</s> to <s>Marīci</s>, then <s>Anasūyā</s> to <s>Atri</s>;
he gave <s>Śraddhā</s> to <s>Aṅgiras</s> and <s>Havirbhū</s> to <s>Pulastya</s>.

children.text: pulahāya gatiṃ yuktāṃ kratave ca kriyāṃ satīm
children.translated_text: To <s>Pulaha</s> he gave the worthy <s>Gati</s>, and to <s>Kratu</s> the virtuous <s>Kriyā</s>;
he gave <s>Khyāti</s> to <s>Bhṛgu</s> and also <s>Arundhatī</s> to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
To <s>Atharvan</s> he gave <s>Śānti</s>, through whom sacrifice is extended;
and he duly honored those bull-like Brahmin sages, married and accompanied by their wives.

children.text: tatas ta ṛṣayaḥ kṣattaḥ kṛtadārā nimantrya tam
children.translated_text: Then those sages, O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, having taken wives and having taken leave of him,

children.text: prātiṣṭhan nandim āpannāḥ svaṃ svam āśramamaṇḍalam ||
children.translated_text: departed joyfully to their own respective circles of hermitages.
And he, recognizing that the best of gods, <s>Triyuga</s>, had descended,
approached him in solitude, bowed down, and spoke.
Ah, surely after a long time the deities become gracious here
to those being cooked in hell by their own inauspicious deeds.
By fully matured merit from many births and by perfect yoga-concentration,
ascetics strive in empty houses to see that state of his.

children.text: sa eva bhagavān adya helanaṃ na gaṇayya naḥ
children.translated_text: That very Blessed One, today, not counting our disrespect,

children.text: gṛheṣu jāto grāmyāṇāṃ yaḥ svānāṃ pakṣapoṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been born in the homes of us village-dwellers, he who nourishes the side of his own people.

children.text: svīyaṃ vākyam ṛtaṃ kartum avatīrṇo 'si me gṛhe
children.translated_text: You have descended into my house to make your own word true,
the Blessed One desiring to bring about knowledge and to increase the honor of his devotees.

children.text: tāny eva te 'bhirūpāṇi rūpāṇi bhagavaṃs tava
children.translated_text: Those forms of yours, Blessed One, are indeed fitting forms of you,

children.text: yāni yāni ca rocante svajanānām arūpiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whichever ones please your own people, though you are without form.
I take refuge in you, whose footstool is always worthy of homage from the wise who desire truth,
filled with sovereignty, detachment, fame, understanding, power, and splendor.

children.text: paraṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntaṃ kālaṃ kaviṃ trivṛtaṃ lokapālam
children.translated_text: I take refuge in <s>Kapila</s>, the supreme, the pradhāna, the puruṣa, the great principle, time, the seer, the threefold one, and protector of the world,
whose manifested universe is followed by self-experience, and whose power is independent.

children.text: a smābhipṛcche 'dya patiṃ prajānāṃ tvayāvatīrṇarṇa utāptakāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Today I ask permission from you, lord of creatures; because you have descended, I am freed from debt and have attained my desire.

children.text: parivrajatpadavīm āsthito 'haṃ cariṣye tvāṃ hṛdi yuñjan viśokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having entered the path of wandering renunciation, I shall move about free from sorrow, joining you in my heart.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: mayā proktaṃ hi lokasya pramāṇaṃ satyalaukike
children.translated_text: What has been spoken by me is indeed authoritative for the world, both in the true and in ordinary sphere;

children.text: athājani mayā tubhyaṃ yad avocam ṛtaṃ mune ||
children.translated_text: therefore I have been born to you, O sage, so that what I said might be true.

children.text: etan me janma loke 'smin mumukṣūṇāṃ durāśayāt
children.translated_text: This birth of mine in this world is for those seeking liberation from evil intention,
for the full enumeration of the principles, approved in the vision of the self.
This path of the self, unmanifest and lost through a long time,

children.text: taṃ pravartayituṃ deham imaṃ viddhi mayā bhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: know that this body has been borne by me in order to set it in motion.
Go as you wish, having been permitted by me, with your actions renounced in me;

children.text: jitvā sudurjayaṃ mṛtyum amṛtatvāya māṃ bhaja ||
children.translated_text: having conquered death, so hard to conquer, worship me for immortality.
Seeing me, the self, self-luminous and dwelling in the cave of all beings,
within the self by the self, you will reach sorrowlessness and fearlessness.
To his mother he will impart spiritual knowledge, the pacifier of all actions,
and by it she too will wholly pass beyond fear.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
When he had been thus addressed by that <s>Kapila</s>, the lord of creatures,

children.text: dakṣiṇīkṛtya taṃ prīto vanam eva jagāma ha ||
children.translated_text: pleased, honored him with due reverence and then went straight to the forest.

children.text: vrataṃ sa āsthito maunam ātmaikaśaraṇo muniḥ
children.translated_text: That sage undertook a vow of silence, taking the Self alone as his refuge;
free from attachment, without fire and without a dwelling, he wandered over the earth.

children.text: mano brahmaṇi yuñjāno yat tat sadasataḥ param
children.translated_text: He fixed his mind on <s>Brahman</s>, that which is beyond both being and non-being,
which appears through the guṇas yet is without guṇas, and is realized through single-minded devotion.

children.text: nirahaṃkṛtir nirmamaś ca nirdvaṃdvaḥ samadṛk svadṛk
children.translated_text: Free from ego, free from possessiveness, beyond dualities, seeing equally and seeing the Self,
with his inward intellect pacified, steadfast, he was like an ocean whose waves are stilled.
In the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the all-knowing inner Self,
through supreme loving devotion he attained the Self and was freed from bondage.
He saw the Blessed Lord established as the Self in all beings,
and all beings also in the Blessed Lord and in the Self.
With desire and hatred gone, with an equal mind everywhere,
joined to devotion to the Blessed Lord, he attained the bhāgavata state.
<s>Śaunaka</s> said:
<s>Kapila</s>, the enumerator of principles, the Blessed Lord, by his own māyā,

children.text: jātaḥ svayam ajaḥ sākṣād ātmaprajñaptaye nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: though unborn, was himself born directly for making the Self known to human beings.

children.text: na hy asya varṣmaṇaḥ puṃsāṃ varimṇaḥ sarvayoginām
children.translated_text: My vital breaths are not greatly satisfied with hearing of this form of his,
whose greatness is celebrated among men, the greatest of all yogins and the god praised in scripture.
Whatever the Blessed Lord, whose self is free, performs by his own māyā,
please recount those deeds, worthy of praise, for me, who listens with faith.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: dvaipāyanasakhas tv evaṃ maitreyo bhagavāṃs tathā
children.translated_text: Thus the blessed <s>Maitreya</s>, friend of <s>Dvaipāyana</s>,
pleased, spoke this to <s>Vidura</s>, being prompted in inquiry into ultimate truth.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
When his father had departed to the forest, out of a wish to please his mother,
the Blessed <s>Kapila</s> indeed remained there at <s>Bindusara</s>.
Seeing him sitting inactive, foremost in the vision of the path of truth,

children.text: svasutaṃ devahūty āha dhātuḥ saṃsmaratī vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Devahūti</s> addressed her own son, remembering the words of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Devahūti</s> said:
I am utterly weary, O abundant one, from the craving of unreal senses,
by the cultivation of which I have entered blind darkness, O Lord.
Today, through your favor, you have been obtained by me as the one who reaches the far shore

children.text: saccakṣur janmanām ante labdhaṃ me tvadanugrahāt ||
children.translated_text: of that blind darkness, hard to cross, as the true eye at the end of many births.

children.text: ya ādyo bhagavān puṃsām īśvaro vai bhavān kila
children.translated_text: For you are that primeval Blessed Lord, the ruler of beings,
risen like the sun as the eye of the world blinded by darkness.

children.text: atha me deva sammoham apākraṣṭuṃ tvam arhasi
children.translated_text: Therefore, O god, you should remove my delusion,
the false grasping of 'I' and 'mine' into which you have placed me.

children.text: taṃ tvā gatāhaṃ śaraṇaṃ śaraṇyaṃ svabhṛtyasaṃsārataroḥ kuṭhāram
children.translated_text: I have come to you for refuge, the refuge, the axe for cutting down the tree of saṃsāra of your servant;

children.text: jijñāsayāhaṃ prakṛteḥ pūruṣasya namāmi saddharmavidāṃ variṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: desiring to know prakṛti and puruṣa, I bow to you, foremost of those who know true <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: iti svamātur niravadyam īpsitaṃ niśamya puṃsām apavargavardhanam
children.translated_text: Having heard this faultless desire of his mother, which increases liberation for human beings,
he, the goal of the self-possessed and good, approved it in his mind and spoke, his face beautified by a slight smile.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: yoga ādhyātmikaḥ puṃsāṃ mato niḥśreyasāya me
children.translated_text: The inner yoga of human beings, I hold, is for the highest good,

children.text: atyantoparatir yatra duḥkhasya ca sukhasya ca ||
children.translated_text: where there is complete cessation of both pain and pleasure.

children.text: tam imaṃ te pravakṣyāmi yam avocaṃ purānaghe
children.translated_text: I shall teach you this yoga, O blameless one, which I formerly told
to the sages who wished to hear, a yoga skilled in all its limbs.

children.text: cetaḥ khalv asya bandhāya muktaye cātmano matam
children.translated_text: The mind of this self is indeed regarded as the cause of bondage and also of liberation:

children.text: guṇeṣu saktaṃ bandhāya rataṃ vā puṃsi muktaye ||
children.translated_text: attached to the guṇas, it leads to bondage; devoted to the Person, to liberation.
When the mind is free from the impurities born of the notions 'I' and 'mine', such as desire and greed,

children.text: vītaṃ yadā manaḥ śuddham aduḥkham asukhaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: it is pure, without pain, without pleasure, and even.

children.text: tadā puruṣa ātmānaṃ kevalaṃ prakṛteḥ param
children.translated_text: Then the person sees the Self as solitary, beyond prakṛti,
uninterrupted, self-luminous, subtle, and undivided.
With a self joined to knowledge and detachment and joined also to devotion,
he thoroughly sees prakṛti as indifferent and with its power destroyed.
For yogins seeking the perfection of <s>Brahman</s>, there is no auspicious path comparable
to devotion applied to the Blessed Lord, the Self of all.

children.text: prasaṅgam ajaraṃ pāśam ātmanaḥ kavayo viduḥ
children.translated_text: The wise know attachment to be an imperishable noose of the self;

children.text: sa eva sādhuṣu kṛto mokṣadvāram apāvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: that same attachment, when directed toward the sādhus, is an opened door to liberation.
They are forbearing, compassionate, friends to all embodied beings,
without born enemies, peaceful; the sādhus are adorned by the virtues of sādhus.

children.text: mayy ananyena bhāvena bhaktiṃ kurvanti ye dṛḍhām
children.translated_text: Those who practice firm devotion to me with an undivided disposition,
who for my sake have abandoned works and abandoned their own kin and relatives,

children.text: madāśrayāḥ kathā mṛṣṭāḥ śṛṇvanti kathayanti ca
children.translated_text: who, taking refuge in me, hear and tell delightful stories about me,
various afflictions do not torment these people whose minds are fixed on me.
These are the sādhus, O virtuous woman, completely free from every attachment;

children.text: saṅgas teṣv atha te prārthyaḥ saṅgadoṣaharā hi te ||
children.translated_text: therefore attachment to them is to be sought by you, for they remove the fault of attachment.

children.text: satāṃ prasaṅgān mama vīryasaṃvido bhavanti hṛtkarṇarasāyanāḥ kathāḥ
children.translated_text: From close association with the good, discussions of my heroic power become stories that are an elixir for the heart and ear;

children.text: tajjoṣaṇād āśv apavargavartmani śraddhā ratir bhaktir anukramiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: by enjoying them, faith, delight, and devotion will quickly follow in succession on the path of liberation.

children.text: bhaktyā pumān jātavirāga aindriyād dṛṣṭaśrutān madracanānucintayā
children.translated_text: Through devotion, a person born into detachment from sensory things, by contemplating what is seen and heard as my creation,

children.text: cittasya yatto grahaṇe yogayukto yatiṣyate ṛjubhir yogamārgaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: intent on grasping the mind and joined with yoga, will strive by straightforward paths of yoga.
By not serving the guṇas of prakṛti, and by knowledge expanded through detachment,

children.text: yogena mayy arpitayā ca bhaktyā māṃ pratyagātmānam ihāvarundhe ||
children.translated_text: and by <s>yoga</s> and devotion offered up to me, he realizes me here as the inner self.
<s>Devahūti</s> said:

children.text: kācit tvayy ucitā bhaktiḥ kīdṛśī mama gocarā
children.translated_text: What sort of devotion, fittingly directed to you, lies within my reach,

children.text: yayā padaṃ te nirvāṇam añjasānvāśnavā aham ||
children.translated_text: by which I may easily attain your state, <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation)?
What is that <s>yoga</s> connected with the Lord's teaching, O you whose nature is liberation, which you have described?
What is it like, and how many limbs does it have, from which there comes understanding of reality?

children.text: tad etan me vijānīhi yathāhaṃ mandadhīr hare
children.translated_text: Make this known to me, O <s>Hari</s>, so that I, dull-minded as I am,
a woman, may easily understand what is hard to grasp, through your favor.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: viditvārthaṃ kapilo mātur itthaṃ jātasneho yatra tanvābhijātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing his mother's meaning in this way, <s>Kapila</s>, in whom affection had arisen for the body from which he was born,

children.text: tattvāmnāyaṃ yat pravadanti sāṃkhyaṃ provāca vai bhaktivitānayogam ||
children.translated_text: taught the doctrine of reality which they call <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, and the yoga that unfolds devotion.
The Blessed Lord said:
Among the gods, whose marks are the <s>guṇas</s> and whose rites are known from sacred tradition,

children.text: sattva evaikamanaso vṛttiḥ svābhāvikī tu yā ||
children.translated_text: that natural movement of one whose mind is fixed solely in <s>sattva</s>,
causeless and directed to the Blessed Lord, is devotion; it is greater than perfection.

children.text: jarayaty āśu yā kośaṃ nigīrṇam analo yathā ||
children.translated_text: It quickly burns away the sheath, as fire consumes what has been swallowed.

children.text: naikātmatāṃ me spṛhayanti kecin matpādasevābhiratā madīhāḥ
children.translated_text: Some, devoted to service of my feet and intent on my purposes, do not long for unity with me,

children.text: ye 'nyonyato bhāgavatāḥ prasajya sabhājayante mama pauruṣāṇi ||
children.translated_text: those devotees who, joined with one another, honor my heroic deeds.

children.text: paśyanti te me rucirāṇy amba santaḥ prasannavaktrāruṇalocanāni
children.translated_text: Those holy ones see my lovely divine forms, O mother, with serene faces and reddish eyes,

children.text: rūpāṇi divyāni varapradāni sākaṃ vācaṃ spṛhaṇīyāṃ vadanti ||
children.translated_text: forms that grant boons; and together with them they speak words worthy of desire.
By those visible limbs, by noble playfulness, smiles, glances, and charming sayings,

children.text: hṛtātmano hṛtaprāṇāṃś ca bhaktir anicchato me gatim aṇvīṃ prayuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: their selves and life-breaths are seized; and devotion, even though they do not wish it, applies my subtle goal to them.

children.text: atho vibhūtiṃ mama māyāvinas tām aiśvaryam aṣṭāṅgam anupravṛttam
children.translated_text: Nor do they desire that splendor of mine, the magical power, the eightfold lordly power that follows upon it,

children.text: śriyaṃ bhāgavatīṃ vāspṛhayanti bhadrāṃ parasya me te 'śnuvate tu loke ||
children.translated_text: or the auspicious divine prosperity; yet they enjoy it in my supreme world.

children.text: na karhicin matparāḥ śāntarūpe naṅkṣyanti no me 'nimiṣo leḍhi hetiḥ
children.translated_text: Those who have me as their highest object will never perish in that peaceful state, nor does my unblinking weapon lick them,

children.text: yeṣām ahaṃ priya ātmā sutaś ca sakhā guruḥ suhṛdo daivam iṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: for I am their beloved self, their son, friend, teacher, well-wisher, deity, and chosen object.
This world, and likewise the next, and the self that passes through both,

children.text: ātmānam anu ye ceha ye rāyaḥ paśavo gṛhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and what follows the self here, wealth, cattle, and houses,

children.text: visṛjya sarvān anyāṃś ca mām evaṃ viśvatomukham
children.translated_text: having abandoned all these and all other things, they worship only me, whose face is turned everywhere,

children.text: bhajanty ananyayā bhaktyā tān mṛtyor atipāraye ||
children.translated_text: with undivided devotion; I carry them beyond death.
Apart from me, the Blessed Lord, the ruler of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>,
the intense fear of all beings is not turned away from the self.

children.text: madbhayād vāti vāto 'yaṃ sūryas tapati madbhayāt
children.translated_text: From fear of me this wind blows; from fear of me the sun gives heat;

children.text: varṣatīndro dahaty agnir mṛtyuś carati madbhayāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> rains, fire burns, and death goes about, from fear of me.
With <s>bhakti-yoga</s> joined to knowledge and detachment,
yogins enter the fearless root of my feet for their welfare.
Just this is the full arising of the highest good for people in this world:

children.text: tīvreṇa bhaktiyogena mano mayy arpitaṃ sthiram ||
children.translated_text: the mind, steady and offered to me through intense <s>bhakti-yoga</s>.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: atha te sampravakṣyāmi tattvānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthak
children.translated_text: Now I shall tell you separately the marks of the principles,

children.text: yad viditvā vimucyeta puruṣaḥ prākṛtair guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: knowing which a person is freed from the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>prakṛti</s>.
I shall describe to you that knowledge, vision of the self for the sake of a person's highest good,

children.text: yad āhur varṇaye tat te hṛdayagranthibhedanam ||
children.translated_text: which they call the cutting of the knot of the heart.

children.text: anādir ātmā puruṣo nirguṇaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: The beginningless self, the <s>puruṣa</s>, is without <s>guṇas</s>, beyond <s>prakṛti</s>,
having inward radiance, self-luminous, by whom the universe is pervaded.

children.text: sa eṣa prakṛtiṃ sūkṣmāṃ daivīṃ guṇamayīṃ vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: This all-pervading one, in play, approached subtle divine <s>prakṛti</s>,
composed of the <s>guṇas</s>, which had come to him simply by chance.

children.text: guṇair vicitrāḥ sṛjatīṃ sarūpāḥ prakṛtiṃ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>prakṛti</s>, through the <s>guṇas</s>, creating various offspring resembling herself,

children.text: vilokya mumuhe sadyaḥ sa iha jñānagūhayā ||
children.translated_text: he at once became bewildered here by the concealment of knowledge.
Thus, through meditation on what is other, the <s>puruṣa</s> thinks the agency of <s>prakṛti</s>,
in actions being performed by the <s>guṇas</s>, to belong to himself.

children.text: tad asya saṃsṛtir bandhaḥ pāratantryaṃ ca tatkṛtam
children.translated_text: That becomes his wandering in transmigration, his bondage, and the dependence produced by it,
though he is a non-agent, lord, witness, and one whose self is at rest.
They know <s>prakṛti</s> to be the cause in the state of effect, cause, and agency,
and the <s>puruṣa</s>, beyond <s>prakṛti</s>, to be the cause in the experience of pleasure and pain.
<s>Devahūti</s> said:
Tell me, O highest <s>puruṣa</s>, the mark of <s>prakṛti</s> and also of <s>puruṣa</s>,

children.text: brūhi kāraṇayor asya sadasac ca yadātmakam ||
children.translated_text: the two causes of this, and that whose nature is both existent and nonexistent.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: yat tat triguṇam avyaktaṃ nityaṃ sadasadātmakam
children.translated_text: That unmanifest, consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>, eternal, whose nature is both existent and nonexistent,
they call <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>prakṛti</s>, undifferentiated yet containing differentiation.

children.text: pañcabhiḥ pañcabhir brahma caturbhir daśabhis tathā
children.translated_text: With five and five, with four, and likewise with ten,
this twenty-fourfold aggregate is known as belonging to <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: mahābhūtāni pañcaiva bhūr āpo 'gnir marun nabhaḥ
children.translated_text: The five great elements are earth, water, fire, wind, and space,

children.text: tanmātrāṇi ca tāvanti gandhādīni matāni me ||
children.translated_text: and the subtle elements are just as many, beginning with smell; so they are understood by me.

children.text: indriyāṇi daśa śrotraṃ tvag dṛg rasananāsikāḥ
children.translated_text: The ten senses are hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell,

children.text: vāk karau caraṇau meḍhraṃ pāyur daśama ucyate ||
children.translated_text: speech, the hands, the feet, the generative organ, and the anus, which is called the tenth.

children.text: mano buddhir ahaṃkāraś cittam ity antarātmakam
children.translated_text: Mind, intellect, ego, and consciousness: this is what pertains to the inner self.
Its fourfold division is marked by function, which is the form of its defining characteristic.

children.text: etāvān eva saṃkhyāto brahmaṇaḥ saguṇasya ha
children.translated_text: So much, indeed, has been enumerated as the arrangement

children.text: saṃniveśo mayā prokto yaḥ kālaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of qualified brahman, as spoken by me; and time is the twenty-fifth.

children.text: prabhāvaṃ pauruṣaṃ prāhuḥ kālam eke yato bhayam
children.translated_text: Some call <s>kāla</s> (time) the power of <s>puruṣa</s>, from which fear arises
for the agent who, bewildered by ego, has entered into <s>prakṛti</s>.
That from which there is activity in <s>prakṛti</s>, whose <s>guṇas</s> are in equilibrium and which is without distinction, O daughter of <s>Manu</s>,

children.text: ceṣṭā yataḥ sa bhagavān kāla ity upalakṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that Blessed Lord is indicated by the name <s>kāla</s>.
As the form of <s>puruṣa</s> within, and as the form of time without,
this Blessed Lord attends upon beings through his own <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: daivāt kṣubhitadharmiṇyāṃ svasyāṃ yonau paraḥ pumān
children.translated_text: When, by fate, his own womb, whose nature had been stirred, was agitated, the supreme Male
placed his seed there; she gave birth to the golden <s>mahat-tattva</s> (great principle).
Manifesting the universe contained within himself, the immutable one, the seed of the world,
by his own radiance drank up the intense darkness that made the self sleep.

children.text: yat tat sattvaguṇaṃ svacchaṃ śāntaṃ bhagavataḥ padam
children.translated_text: That clear and tranquil <s>sattva-guṇa</s> (quality of lucidity), the abode of the Blessed Lord,

children.text: yad āhur vāsudevākhyaṃ cittaṃ tan mahadātmakam ||
children.translated_text: which they call by the name <s>Vāsudeva</s>, is consciousness having the nature of <s>mahat</s>.
Clarity, changelessness, and tranquility are said to be the marks of the mind

children.text: vṛttibhir lakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ yathāpāṃ prakṛtiḥ parā ||
children.translated_text: through its modes, just as purity is the higher natural state of waters.
From the transforming <s>mahat-tattva</s>, produced from the potency of the Blessed Lord,
<s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), the power of action, came into being as threefold.

children.text: vaikārikas taijasaś ca tāmasaś ca yato bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: It was <s>vaikārika</s>, <s>taijasa</s>, and <s>tāmasa</s>; from it came the origin

children.text: manasaś cendriyāṇāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ mahatām api ||
children.translated_text: of the mind, of the senses, and also of the great elements.
The very thousand-headed one whom they call <s>Ananta</s>
is the <s>puruṣa</s> named <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, consisting of elements, senses, and mind.

children.text: kartṛtvaṃ karaṇatvaṃ ca kāryatvaṃ ceti lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Agency, instrumentality, and being an effect are its marks;
or, for <s>ahaṃkṛti</s> (ego-formation), there may be peacefulness, fierceness, and delusion.
From the transforming <s>vaikārika</s> arose the mind-principle,
which operates through resolve and doubt, and from which desire arises.

children.text: yad vidur hy aniruddhākhyaṃ hṛṣīkāṇām adhīśvaram
children.translated_text: They know it as the one called <s>Aniruddha</s>, lord of the senses,
dark like an autumn blue lotus, to be worshiped steadily by yogins.

children.text: taijasāt tu vikurvāṇād buddhitattvam abhūt sati
children.translated_text: But from the transforming <s>taijasa</s>, O virtuous woman, the intellect-principle came into being:
the discernment of the manifestation of objects, and the support of the senses.

children.text: saṃśayo 'tha viparyāso niścayaḥ smṛtir eva ca
children.translated_text: Doubt, then misapprehension, certainty, memory,

children.text: svāpa ity ucyate buddher lakṣaṇaṃ vṛttitaḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and sleep are separately called the marks of intellect according to its modes.
The senses themselves are from <s>taijasa</s>, divided into action and knowledge;
for the power of action belongs to <s>prāṇa</s>, and the power of cognition belongs to intellect.
And from the transforming <s>tāmasa</s>, impelled by the potency of the Blessed Lord,

children.text: śabdamātram abhūt tasmān nabhaḥ śrotraṃ tu śabdagam ||
children.translated_text: there arose the mere sound; from that came space, and the ear, which goes to sound.

children.text: arthāśrayatvaṃ śabdasya draṣṭur liṅgatvam eva ca
children.translated_text: The sages know the support of meaning in sound, its being a sign for the seer,

children.text: tanmātratvaṃ ca nabhaso lakṣaṇaṃ kavayo viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: and its being a subtle element as the marks of space.

children.text: bhūtānāṃ chidradātṛtvaṃ bahir antaram eva ca
children.translated_text: Providing openings for beings, being outside and inside,
and being the seat of breath, senses, and self are the functional marks of space.
From space, whose subtle element is sound, as it transformed through the movement of time,

children.text: sparśo 'bhavat tato vāyus tvak sparśasya ca saṃgrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: touch arose; from that came wind, and the skin, which grasps touch.

children.text: mṛdutvaṃ kaṭhinatvaṃ ca śaityam uṣṇatvam eva ca
children.translated_text: Softness and hardness, coldness and heat:
this is the tactility of touch and the subtle-elementhood of wind.
Movement, arrangement, reaching, and guidance of substance and sound,
and being the animating principle of all the senses are the defining actions of wind.

children.text: vāyoś ca sparśatanmātrād rūpaṃ daiveritād abhūt
children.translated_text: And from the wind, whose subtle element is touch, form arose when stirred by divine impulse;
from that fire arose, along with the eye and the apprehension of form.
Having the shape of a substance, being a quality, and being manifest in an individual configuration:
O gentle one, these are the functions of mere form belonging to fire.
Illumining, cooking, drinking, eating, crushing cold,

children.text: tejaso vṛttayas tv etāḥ śoṣaṇaṃ kṣut tṛḍ eva ca ||
children.translated_text: drying, hunger, and thirst: these indeed are the functions of fire.
From mere form, as fire transformed under divine impulse,

children.text: rasamātram abhūt tasmād ambho jihvā rasagrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: mere taste arose; from that came water, and the tongue, which receives taste.

children.text: kaṣāyo madhuras tiktaḥ kaṭv amla iti naikadhā
children.translated_text: Astringent, sweet, bitter, pungent, and sour: in many forms,
one taste is divided through the transformations of material things.
Moistening, coagulating, satisfaction, enlivening, refreshing, and swelling,

children.text: tāpāpanodo bhūyastvam ambhaso vṛttayas tv imāḥ ||
children.translated_text: removal of heat, and abundance: these indeed are the functions of water.
From the transforming subtle element of taste in water, stirred by divine impulse,

children.text: gandhamātram abhūt tasmāt pṛthvī ghrāṇas tu gandhagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: mere odor arose; from that came earth, and the nose, which goes to odor.
As mixed, fetid, fragrant, mild, sharp, sour, and the like, separately,
one odor is divided because of the unevenness of the parts of substances.
Bringing into being, serving as the place of <s>Brahman</s>, supporting, particularizing what exists,
and manifesting the qualities of all beings are the functional marks of earth.
That whose object is the special quality of space is called the ear;

children.text: vāyor guṇaviśeṣo 'rtho yasya tat sparśanaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: that whose object is the special quality of wind is known as the organ of touch.
That whose object is the special quality of fire is called the eye;
that whose object is the special quality of water is known as the tongue;

children.text: bhūmer guṇaviśeṣo 'rtho yasya sa ghrāṇa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: that whose object is the special quality of earth is called the nose.

children.text: parasya dṛśyate dharmo hy aparasmin samanvayāt
children.translated_text: The property of an earlier element is seen in a later one because of inherence;
therefore the distinctness of beings is observed in earth alone.

children.text: etāny asaṃhatya yadā mahadādīni sapta vai
children.translated_text: When these seven beginning with <s>mahat</s> had not yet combined,
the origin of the world, endowed with time, karma, and the guṇas, entered them.
Then, from those things joined together and penetrated by him, an unconscious egg

children.text: utthitaṃ puruṣo yasmād udatiṣṭhad asau virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: arose, from which that <s>Virāṭ Puruṣa</s> came forth.
This egg, called <s>viśeṣa</s> (the differentiated), was surrounded by coverings beginning with water,
each increasing tenfold in succession, and outside by <s>pradhāna</s> enveloping them;
within it is this spread of worlds, the form of the Blessed <s>Hari</s>.
Rising from the golden shell of the egg that lay in the waters,

children.text: tam āviśya mahādevo bahudhā nirbibheda kham ||
children.translated_text: the Great God entered it and divided the space within in many ways.
First his mouth was opened, and from it speech came into being;

children.text: vāṇyā vahnir atho nāse prāṇoto ghrāṇa etayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: from speech came fire. Then, in the two nostrils, from breath came the sense of smell in them.

children.text: ghrāṇād vāyur abhidyetām akṣiṇī cakṣur etayoḥ
children.translated_text: From smell came air. The two eyes were opened, and sight was in them;

children.text: tasmāt sūryo nyabhidyetāṃ karṇau śrotraṃ tato diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: from that came the sun. The two ears were opened, and from hearing came the directions.
The skin of <s>Virāj</s> burst open, and from it came hair, moustache, beard, and the rest;

children.text: tata oṣadhayaś cāsan śiśnaṃ nirbibhide tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: from these the plants came into being. Then the penis was opened.

children.text: retas tasmād āpa āsan nirabhidyata vai gudam
children.translated_text: From that came semen, and the waters came into being. The anus too was opened;
from the anus came the downward breath, and from the downward breath came Death, terrifying the worlds.

children.text: hastau ca nirabhidyetāṃ balaṃ tābhyāṃ tataḥ svarāṭ
children.translated_text: The two hands were opened, and from them came strength; after that came the sovereign <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: pādau ca nirabhidyetāṃ gatis tābhyāṃ tato hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: The two feet were opened, and from them came movement; after that came <s>Hari</s>.
His channels were opened, and from them blood was brought forth;
from that the rivers came into being. The belly was opened;

children.text: kṣutpipāse tataḥ syātāṃ samudras tv etayor abhūt
children.translated_text: from it hunger and thirst arose, and the ocean came to be connected with these two.

children.text: athāsya hṛdayaṃ bhinnaṃ hṛdayān mana utthitam ||
children.translated_text: Then his heart was split open, and from the heart the mind arose.

children.text: manasaś candramā jāto buddhir buddher girāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: From the mind the moon was born; intellect arose, and from intellect came <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of speech.

children.text: ahaṃkāras tato rudraś cittaṃ caityas tato 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: From ego came <s>Rudra</s>, and from consciousness came the indwelling knower.
Although these deities had arisen, they were not able to make him rise.

children.text: punar āviviśuḥ khāni tam utthāpayituṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: In order to make him rise, they again entered his openings one after another.

children.text: vahnir vācā mukhaṃ bheje nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ
children.translated_text: Fire occupied the mouth with speech, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: ghrāṇena nāsike vāyur nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: Air occupied the two nostrils with smell, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.
The sun occupied the two eyes with sight, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: śrotreṇa karṇau ca diśo nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: The directions occupied the two ears with hearing, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: tvacaṃ romabhir oṣadhyo nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ
children.translated_text: The plants occupied the skin with hairs, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: retasā śiśnam āpas tu nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: The waters occupied the penis with semen, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: gudaṃ mṛtyur apānena nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ
children.translated_text: Death occupied the anus with the downward breath, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: hastāv indro balenaiva nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> occupied the two hands with strength alone, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: viṣṇur gatyaiva caraṇau nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> occupied the feet with movement alone, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: nāḍīr nadyo lohitena nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: The rivers occupied the channels with blood, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: kṣuttṛḍbhyām udaraṃ sindhur nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ
children.translated_text: The ocean occupied the belly with hunger and thirst, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ manasā candro nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: The moon occupied the heart with mind, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: buddhyā brahmāpi hṛdayaṃ nodatiṣṭhat tadā virāṭ
children.translated_text: Even <s>Brahmā</s> occupied the heart with intellect, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.
<s>Rudra</s> occupied the heart with self-conception, but then the <s>Virāṭ</s> did not stand up.

children.text: cittena hṛdayaṃ caityaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ prāviśad yadā
children.translated_text: But when the indwelling knower, the kṣetrajña, entered the heart with consciousness,
then at that very moment the <s>Virāṭ</s>, the puruṣa, rose up from the waters.
Just as breath, senses, mind, and intellect cannot by their power
rouse a man who is sleeping, apart from the one on whom they depend,
so one should discern this inward self within oneself with an intellect set in motion by yoga,
and contemplate him by means of devotion, detachment, and knowledge.
The Blessed Lord said:
Even while situated in prakṛti, the puruṣa is not stained by the guṇas of prakṛti,
because he is changeless, without agency, and free from guṇas, like the sun reflected in water.

children.text: sa eṣa yarhi prakṛter guṇeṣv abhiviṣajjate
children.translated_text: But when this puruṣa becomes attached to the guṇas of prakṛti,
his self is bewildered by ego-making, and he thinks, 'I am the doer.'
Because of that, helpless and unsatisfied, he enters the path of saṃsāra,
through incidental faults of karma, among wombs mixed of good and bad.

children.text: arthe hy avidyamāne 'pi saṃsṛtir na nivartate
children.translated_text: For even when the object is not real, saṃsāra does not cease
for one who meditates on sense-objects, just as misfortune comes in a dream.

children.text: ata eva śanaiś cittaṃ prasaktam asatāṃ pathi
children.translated_text: Therefore, by intense bhakti-yoga and by detachment,

children.text: bhaktiyogena tīvreṇa viraktyā ca nayed vaśam ||
children.translated_text: one should gradually bring under control the mind attached to the path of the unreal.
Practicing the paths of yoga beginning with yama, and endowed with faith,
with true feeling toward me and by hearing stories of me,
through equal regard for all beings, through absence of hostility, and through non-attachment,
through celibacy, silence, and one's own strong dharma,
content with what comes of its own accord, eating moderately, a sage,
taking refuge in solitude, peaceful, friendly, compassionate, and self-possessed,
not forming a false clinging to this body with all its attachments,
and by knowledge that has seen the truth of prakṛti and puruṣa,
with the resting-place of intellect withdrawn and the perception of anything other set far away,
the seer of the self perceives the self by the self, as one sees the sun with the eye.
He apprehends the self as free from the subtle mark, ever manifest as reality within the unreal,
the ally of the real, the eye of the unreal, threaded through all, and nondual.
Just as a reflection standing in water is seen by one standing on land,

children.text: svābhāsena tathā sūryo jalasthena divi sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and just as the sun situated in the sky is seen by its own reflection standing in water,
so the threefold ego, composed of elements, senses, and mind,
is recognized by this seer of truth through its own reflections and through the ever-manifest real.
When the subtle elements, senses, mind, intellect, and the rest here are dissolved by sleep

children.text: līneṣv asati yas tatra vinidro nirahaṃkriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: into the unreal, the one who remains awake there is without ego-making.
Then, falsely thinking that self to be lost, though it has not been destroyed, he seems as if lost;
when ego-making is lost, the seer is distressed like a man whose wealth is lost.
Reflecting in this way, that person attains the self,
who is the abiding ground and support of the substance endowed with ego.
<s>Devahūti</s> said:

children.text: puruṣaṃ prakṛtir brahman na vimuñcati karhicit
children.translated_text: O <s>Brahman</s>, prakṛti never releases the puruṣa,
because these two, O lord, depend on one another and are eternal.

children.text: yathā gandhasya bhūmeś ca na bhāvo vyatirekataḥ
children.translated_text: Just as smell and earth have no existence apart from each other,

children.text: apāṃ rasasya ca yathā tathā buddheḥ parasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and just as taste and water do not, so it is with intellect and the transcendent one.
This bondage by karma belongs to the purusha, who is not the agent, because it rests on that:

children.text: guṇeṣu satsu prakṛteḥ kaivalyaṃ teṣv ataḥ katham ||
children.translated_text: when the gunas of prakriti remain present, how then can there be kaivalya with regard to them?
At times, through insight into reality, a terrible fear has ceased;
but because its cause has not ceased, it arises again.
The Blessed Lord said:
By one's own dharma, without ulterior motive, with a stainless self,

children.text: tīvrayā mayi bhaktyā ca śrutasaṃbhṛtayā ciram ||
children.translated_text: and by intense devotion to me, accumulated over a long time through hearing,
by knowledge that has seen reality, and by very strong detachment,
by yoga joined with austerity, intense and marked by concentration on the self,
prakriti, belonging here to the purusha, being burned day and night,
will gradually disappear, like the fire's source, the arani wood.
Once its enjoyments have been experienced, it is abandoned, and its faults are constantly seen;

children.text: neśvarasyāśubhaṃ dhatte sve mahimni sthitasya ca ||
children.translated_text: it does not bring misfortune to the sovereign one established in his own greatness.
For just as sleep, for one who has not awakened, bears many evils,

children.text: sa eva pratibuddhasya na vai mohāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: that very same sleep, for one who has awakened, does not indeed become a source of delusion.
So, for one who knows reality, prakriti, while he fixes his mind on me,
never injures him, since he delights in the self.
When, in this way, the sage has become devoted to the inner self over the course of many births,
and has become detached everywhere, even up to the world of <s>Brahma</s>,
then, as my devotee whose purpose has awakened, through my abundant grace,
he reaches the highest good, his own state, called kaivalya, resting in me.
The steadfast one attains it here easily, his doubt cut off by his own vision;

children.text: yad gatvā na nivarteta yogī liṅgād vinirgame ||
children.translated_text: having gone there, the yogin does not return when he departs from the subtle body.

children.text: yadā na yogopacitāsu ceto māyāsu siddhasya viṣajjate 'ṅga
children.translated_text: When the mind of the perfected yogin does not cling to the powers amassed by yoga, O dear one,

children.text: ananyahetuṣv atha me gatiḥ syād ātyantikī yatra na mṛtyuhāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then my ultimate goal, dependent on no other cause, becomes his, where death has no mockery.
The Blessed Lord said:
I shall describe the mark of yoga with seed, O daughter of the king,

children.text: mano yenaiva vidhinā prasannaṃ yāti satpatham ||
children.translated_text: by just what method the mind, becoming serene, goes to the good path.
There is the practice of one's own dharma according to one's ability, and turning away from contrary dharma;
contentment with what is obtained by providence, and worship of the feet of those who know the self;
withdrawal from worldly dharma, and delight in the dharma of liberation;
constant eating of measured and pure food, and resorting to secluded, secure places;
nonviolence, truthfulness, non-stealing, and possession only to the extent needed;
celibacy, austerity, purity, study of sacred texts, and worship of the <s>Purusha</s>;
silence, constant mastery of posture, steadiness, and gradual mastery of the breath;
and withdrawal of the senses from their objects into the heart by means of the mind;
fixing the breath with the mind in one place among its own seats;
meditation on the play of <s>Vaikuntha</s>, and likewise concentration of the self.

children.text: etair anyaiś ca pathibhir mano duṣṭam asatpatham
children.translated_text: By these and other paths, the corrupted mind that has gone onto a false path

children.text: buddhyā yuñjīta śanakair jitaprāṇo hy atandritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should gradually be yoked by intelligence, once the breath is conquered, with no negligence.
Having set up his seat in a pure place, and having mastered the posture,
seated there comfortably and upright in body, he should practice.
He should purify the path of the breath through inhalation, retention, and exhalation,

children.text: pratikūlena vā cittaṃ yathā sthiram acañcalam ||
children.translated_text: or by the reverse order, so that the mind becomes steady and unmoving.
The mind of a yogin whose breath is conquered soon becomes free from impurity,

children.text: vāyvagnibhyāṃ yathā lohaṃ dhmātaṃ tyajati vai malam ||
children.translated_text: just as iron, blown upon by wind and fire, gives up its dross.

children.text: prāṇāyāmair dahed doṣān dhāraṇābhiś ca kilbiṣān
children.translated_text: By pranayamas he should burn away faults, and by dharanas, sins;
by pratyahara, contacts with objects, and by meditation, the gunas that are not of the Lord.

children.text: yadā manaḥ svaṃ virajaṃ yogena susamāhitam
children.translated_text: When his own mind has become stainless and well concentrated by yoga,
he should meditate on the form of the Blessed Lord, gazing at the tip of his own nose.
His lotus face is serene, and his eyes are reddish like the heart of a lotus;
he is dark like the petal of a blue lotus, holding conch, discus, and mace.
He wears yellow silk, shining like the filaments of a radiant lotus;
he bears the <s>Shrivatsa</s> on his chest, and the brilliant <s>Kaustubha</s> gem hangs at his neck.
He is encircled by a forest garland accompanied by the humming of intoxicated bees;
he has splendid necklaces, bracelets, crown, armlets, and anklets.
His hips shine with belt and girdle, and he is spread out within the lotus of the heart;
he is most beautiful to behold, peaceful, and increases the joy of mind and eyes.
His appearance is always lovely, and he is bowed to by all the worlds;
he remains in youthful age and is eager to show grace to his servants.
His fame is a sacred ford worthy of praise, and it makes the fame of the meritorious celebrated;

children.text: dhyāyed devaṃ samagrāṅgaṃ yāvan na cyavate manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should meditate on the god with all his limbs complete, until the mind does not fall away.

children.text: sthitaṃ vrajantam āsīnaṃ śayānaṃ vā guhāśayam
children.translated_text: Whether he is standing, walking, sitting, lying down, or dwelling in the cave of the heart,
one should meditate on his beautiful actions with a mind of pure devotion.
When the mind has found a footing in him and is settled on all his limbs,
the sage should observe them and then join the mind to one limb of the Blessed Lord.
He should contemplate the lotus feet of the Blessed Lord, rich with the marks of thunderbolt, goad, banner, and lotus,
which strike away the great darkness of the heart with the moonlight of their high, red, gleaming nails.

children.text: yacchaucaniḥsṛtasaritpravarodakena tīrthena mūrdhny adhikṛtena śivaḥ śivo 'bhūt
children.translated_text: By the excellent river water issuing from their washing, by that sacred ford placed upon his head, <s>Shiva</s> became auspicious;

children.text: dhyātur manaḥśamalaśailanisṛṣṭavajraṃ dhyāyec ciraṃ bhagavataś caraṇāravindam ||
children.translated_text: one should long meditate on the Blessed Lord's lotus feet, like a thunderbolt released against the mountain of impurity in the meditator's mind.

children.text: jānudvayaṃ jalajalocanayā jananyā lakṣmyākhilasya suravanditayā vidhātuḥ
children.translated_text: One should place in the heart the two knees of the mighty unborn Lord, which by the lotus-eyed <s>Lakshmi</s>, mother of all and worshiped by the gods,

children.text: ūrvor nidhāya karapallavarociṣā yat saṃlālitaṃ hṛdi vibhor abhavasya kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: were set upon her thighs and fondled with the radiance of her sprout-like hands.

children.text: ūrū suparṇabhujayor adhi śobhamānāv ojonidhī atasikākusumāvabhāsau
children.translated_text: One should meditate on his two thighs, shining above the arms of <s>Suparṇa</s>, reservoirs of strength and gleaming like atasī flowers,
and on the curve of his hips, clothed in excellent yellow garments hanging down and embraced by rows of girdle-bells.
One should meditate on the lake of his navel, situated in the abdominal cave of the world's enclosure, where the lotus of all worlds, the seat of the self-born <s>Brahmā</s>, is spread out,

children.text: vyūḍhaṃ harinmaṇivṛṣastanayor amuṣya dhyāyed dvayaṃ viśadahāramayūkhagauram ||
children.translated_text: and on his pair of breasts, like emerald peaks, made pale by the rays of a clear necklace.

children.text: vakṣo 'dhivāsam ṛṣabhasya mahāvibhūteḥ puṃsāṃ manonayananirvṛtim ādadhānam
children.translated_text: He should place in his mind the chest, the dwelling of <s>Śrī</s>, of the Lord of great majesty, which gives satisfaction to the minds and eyes of men,

children.text: kaṇṭhaṃ ca kaustubhamaṇer adhibhūṣaṇārthaṃ kuryān manasy akhilalokanamaskṛtasya ||
children.translated_text: and the neck of him who is bowed to by all worlds, as the support for the adornment of the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel.

children.text: bāhūṃś ca mandaragireḥ parivartanena nirṇiktabāhuvalayān adhilokapālān
children.translated_text: He should contemplate his arms, whose armlets were polished by the turning of Mount <s>Mandara</s>, presiding over the guardians of the worlds,

children.text: saṃcintayed daśaśatāram asahyatejaḥ śaṅkhaṃ ca tatkarasaroruharājahaṃsam ||
children.translated_text: and his discus with a thousand spokes, unbearable in splendor, and the conch, the royal swan in the lotus of his hand.

children.text: kaumodakīṃ bhagavato dayitāṃ smareta digdhām arātibhaṭaśoṇitakardamena
children.translated_text: He should remember <s>Kaumodakī</s>, the beloved mace of the Blessed Lord, smeared with the muddy blood of enemy warriors,

children.text: mālāṃ madhuvratavarūthagiropaghuṣṭāṃ caityasya tattvam amalaṃ maṇim asya kaṇṭhe ||
children.translated_text: the garland loudly hummed about by swarms of bees, and the pure reality of the caitya, the jewel on his neck.
He should contemplate the lotus face of the Blessed Lord, who has assumed a form here with a mind compassionate toward his servants,
whose spotless cheeks and noble nose are illuminated by the play of flashing makara earrings.

children.text: yac chrīniketam alibhiḥ parisevyamānaṃ bhūtyā svayā kuṭilakuntalavṛndajuṣṭam
children.translated_text: With tireless mind he should meditate on that abode of <s>Śrī</s>, served by bees, attended by its own splendor and by clusters of curling locks,

children.text: mīnadvayāśrayam adhikṣipad abjanetraṃ dhyāyen manomayam atandrita ullasadbhru ||
children.translated_text: on the lotus-eyed one, with shining brows, whose two eyes rest like a pair of fish and outshine the lotus.
He should meditate for a long time in the cave of the heart on that glance of his, sent forth from his eyes with surpassing compassion to pacify the three terrible torments,

children.text: snigdhasmitānuguṇitaṃ vipulaprasādaṃ dhyāyec ciraṃ vipulabhāvanayā guhāyām ||
children.translated_text: made still more gracious by a gentle smile and filled with broad favor, with expansive contemplation.
He should meditate on the very generous smile of <s>Hari</s>, which dries up the ocean of hot tears of grief of all the worlds bowed down,

children.text: sammohanāya racitaṃ nijamāyayāsya bhrūmaṇḍalaṃ munikṛte makaradhvajasya ||
children.translated_text: and on the circle of his brows, fashioned by his own <s>māyā</s> to bewilder <s>Makara-dhvaja</s>, it seems, for the sake of the sage.
As a support for meditation, he should contemplate his laughter, in which the row of small jasmine-bud teeth is reddened by the glow of the full lower lip,

children.text: dhyāyet svadehakuhare 'vasitasya viṣṇor bhaktyārdrayārpitamanā na pṛthag didṛkṣet ||
children.translated_text: and, with his mind offered in devotion and softened by bhakti, he should meditate on <s>Viṣṇu</s> settled in the cavity of his own body, not wishing to see him as separate.

children.text: evaṃ harau bhagavati pratilabdhabhāvo bhaktyā dravaddhṛdaya utpulakaḥ pramodāt
children.translated_text: Thus, when he has regained feeling toward the Blessed <s>Hari</s>, his heart melting through devotion and his hair bristling with joy,

children.text: autkaṇṭhyabāṣpakalayā muhur ardyamānas tac cāpi cittabaḍiśaṃ śanakair viyuṅkte ||
