children.translated_text: again and again afflicted by tears of longing, he slowly loosens even that fishhook of the mind.

children.text: muktāśrayaṃ yarhi nirviṣayaṃ viraktaṃ nirvāṇam ṛcchati manaḥ sahasā yathārciḥ
children.translated_text: When the mind, freed from support, without objects and detached, suddenly reaches nirvāṇa like a flame,

children.text: ātmānam atra puruṣo 'vyavadhānam ekam anvīkṣate pratinivṛttaguṇapravāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the person, the current of the guṇas having turned back, sees the self here as one, without any interval.

children.text: so 'py etayā caramayā manaso nivṛttyā tasmin mahimny avasitaḥ sukhaduḥkhabāhye
children.translated_text: By this final cessation of the mind, he too, established in that greatness beyond pleasure and pain,

children.text: hetutvam apy asati kartari duḥkhayor yat svātman vidhatta upalabdhaparātmakāṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having realized the supreme limit of the self, no longer imposes on himself even the causality of those pains when there is in truth no agent.

children.text: dehaṃ ca taṃ na caramaḥ sthitam utthitaṃ vā siddho vipaśyati yato 'dhyagamat svarūpam
children.translated_text: The perfected person at the final stage no longer regards that body, whether standing or risen, because he has attained his own true form,

children.text: daivād upetam atha daivavaśād apetaṃ vāso yathā parikṛtaṃ madirāmadāndhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether it has come by fate or gone by the force of fate, just as a man blinded by drunkenness does not notice a garment put on him.

children.text: deho 'pi daivavaśagaḥ khalu karma yāvat svārambhakaṃ pratisamīkṣata eva sāsuḥ
children.translated_text: The body too, governed by fate, along with its life-breath, waits only so long as the karma that began it remains,

children.text: taṃ saprapañcam adhirūḍhasamādhiyogaḥ svāpnaṃ punar na bhajate pratibuddhavastuḥ ||
children.translated_text: but one who has mounted the yoga of samādhi and awakened to reality does not again take up that body with its whole display, as one does not take up a dream.

children.text: yathā putrāc ca vittāc ca pṛthaṅ martyaḥ pratīyate
children.translated_text: Just as a mortal is understood as distinct from a son and from wealth,
so too the puruṣa is distinct from the body and the rest, even though they are regarded as the self.
Just as fire is distinct from a firebrand, from sparks, or from smoke, though these arise from itself,
so fire is distinct from the firebrand, even though the firebrand may be regarded as its very self.
From the elements, senses, inner organ, pradhāna, and that which is called jīva,

children.text: ātmā tathā pṛthag draṣṭā bhagavān brahmasaṃjñitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the self is likewise distinct: the seer, the Blessed Lord, known as <s>Brahman</s>.
One should behold the self in all beings and all beings in the self,
with a sense of non-difference, seeing in beings that very selfhood.

children.text: svayoniṣu yathā jyotir ekaṃ nānā pratīyate
children.translated_text: As one light appears as many in its several sources,
because of the inequality of the qualities of those sources, so the self appears in prakṛti.

children.text: tasmād imāṃ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ daivīṃ sadasadātmikām
children.translated_text: Therefore, having overcome this divine prakṛti of his own, consisting of being and non-being
and hard to discern, he abides in his own essential form.
<s>Devahūti</s> said:
Tell me the defining mark of the great principle and the others, and of prakṛti and puruṣa,
by which the ultimate true nature of these may be known.

children.text: yathā sāṃkhyeṣu kathitaṃ yanmūlaṃ tat pracakṣate
children.translated_text: As it has been taught in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrines, whose root they explain,

children.text: bhaktiyogasya me mārgaṃ brūhi vistaraśaḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: tell me in detail, O Lord, the path of bhaktiyoga.

children.text: virāgo yena puruṣo bhagavan sarvato bhavet
children.translated_text: By which a person may become detached from everything, O Blessed One,
explain to me the various courses of saṃsṛti for the world of living beings.
And tell me the nature of Time, the form of the Lord, of you who are beyond the higher ones and supreme,

children.text: svarūpaṃ bata kurvanti yaddhetoḥ kuśalaṃ janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of which skillful people pursue what is good.

children.text: lokasya mithyābhimater acakṣuṣaś ciraṃ prasuptasya tamasy anāśraye
children.translated_text: For the world, falsely self-conceiving, sightless, long asleep in unsupported darkness,

children.text: śrāntasya karmasv anuviddhayā dhiyā tvam āvirāsīḥ kila yogabhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and weary in actions with an intellect pierced by them, you have appeared, indeed, as the sun of yoga.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: iti mātur vacaḥ ślakṣṇaṃ pratinandya mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Having approved these gentle words of his mother, the great sage,
pleased and moved by compassion, addressed her, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>.
The Blessed Lord said:
O beautiful woman, <s>bhakti-yoga</s> is conceived in many forms and by many paths;
according to the path of one's own nature and <s>guṇa</s>, the disposition of people is differentiated.

children.text: abhisaṃdhāya yo hiṃsāṃ dambhaṃ mātsaryam eva vā
children.translated_text: One who, intending violence, hypocrisy, or envy,

children.text: saṃrambhī bhinnadṛg bhāvaṃ mayi kuryāt sa tāmasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: being enraged and seeing separately, directs a disposition toward me: he is <s>tāmasa</s>.

children.text: viṣayān abhisaṃdhāya yaśa aiśvaryam eva vā
children.translated_text: One who, aiming at sense-objects, fame, or lordly power,

children.text: arcādāv arcayed yo māṃ pṛthagbhāvaḥ sa rājasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: worships me in an image and the like, while holding a separate notion: he is <s>rājasa</s>.
One who worships with the aim of removing karma, or of offering it to the Supreme,

children.text: yajed yaṣṭavyam iti vā pṛthagbhāvaḥ sa sāttvikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or thinking, 'This ought to be sacrificed': holding a separate notion, he is <s>sāttvika</s>.
By the mere hearing of my qualities, toward me who dwell in every hidden heart,
there is an unbroken movement of the mind, like the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> toward the ocean.
This is indeed declared to be the mark of <s>bhakti-yoga</s> that is free from the <s>guṇa</s>s:
the devotion to <s>Puruṣottama</s> that is causeless and uninterrupted.
Even <s>sālokya</s>, <s>sārṣṭi</s>, <s>sāmīpya</s>, <s>sārūpya</s>, and oneness,

children.text: dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇanti vinā matsevanaṃ janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when they are offered, people do not accept without service to me.
That very state is called <s>bhakti-yoga</s> and is declared to be ultimate,
by which, passing beyond the three <s>guṇa</s>s, one becomes fit for my state.
By excellently practicing one's own <s>svadharma</s>, without ulterior cause,
by approved <s>kriyā-yoga</s>, performed constantly and not excessively violent,
by seeing, touching, worshiping, praising, and bowing to my abodes,
by regarding me among beings, by purity, and by nonattachment,
by great respect for the great and by compassion for the poor,
by friendship toward those equal to oneself, and by <s>yama</s> and <s>niyama</s>,
by hearing spiritual instruction and by the chanting of my names,
by straightforwardness, noble association, and likewise freedom from ego,
through these qualities of my <s>dharma</s>, the heart of a person, completely purified,
easily comes to me, whose qualities are apprehended by mere hearing.

children.text: yathā vātaratho ghrāṇam āvṛṅkte gandha āśayāt
children.translated_text: Just as scent, riding on the wind, takes hold of the sense of smell from its seat,

children.text: evaṃ yogarataṃ ceta ātmānam avikāri yat ||
children.translated_text: so the mind devoted to yoga takes hold of the self, which is changeless.
I am always established in all beings as the self of beings;
having disregarded me there, a mortal performs only a mockery of image-worship.

children.text: yo māṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu santam ātmānam īśvaram
children.translated_text: One who abandons me, the self and Lord present in all beings,

children.text: hitvārcāṃ bhajate mauḍhyād bhasmany eva juhoti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and worships an image out of delusion, sacrifices only into ashes.
For one who hates me in another's body, who is proud and sees distinctions,

children.text: bhūteṣu baddhavairasya na manaḥ śāntim ṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: and whose hostility toward beings is fixed, the mind does not attain peace.
O sinless one, with materials high and low and with ritual that produces its result,
I am not at all pleased when worshiped in an image by one who scorns the community of beings.

children.text: arcādāv arcayet tāvad īśvaraṃ māṃ svakarmakṛt
children.translated_text: So long may one who performs his own duties worship me, the Lord, in an image and the like,

children.text: yāvan na veda svahṛdi sarvabhūteṣv avasthitam ||
children.translated_text: until he knows me as established in his own heart and in all beings.

children.text: ātmanaś ca parasyāpi yaḥ karoty antarodaram
children.translated_text: One who makes a separation between himself and another

children.text: tasya bhinnadṛśo mṛtyur vidadhe bhayam ulbaṇam ||
children.translated_text: for that person of divided vision, death creates terrible fear.
Therefore one should honor me, the self of beings, who has made a dwelling in all beings,
with gifts and respect, and with friendship, through an undivided eye.

children.text: jīvāḥ śreṣṭhā hy ajīvānāṃ tataḥ prāṇabhṛtaḥ śubhe
children.translated_text: Living beings are superior to nonliving things; among them, bearers of breath, O auspicious one,
then conscious beings are higher, and then those with sensory activity.
Among these too, those aware of touch are higher; higher are those aware of taste.

children.text: tebhyo gandhavidaḥ śreṣṭhās tataḥ śabdavido varāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Superior to them are those who know smell; then excellent are those who know sound.
Among them are those who know distinctions of form; then those with teeth on both sides.

children.text: teṣāṃ bahupadāḥ śreṣṭhāś catuṣpādas tato dvipāt ||
children.translated_text: Of these, many-footed creatures are superior, then quadrupeds, and then bipeds.

children.text: tato varṇāś ca catvāras teṣāṃ brāhmaṇa uttamaḥ
children.translated_text: Then there are the four <s>varṇa</s>s; among them the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is highest.

children.text: brāhmaṇeṣv api vedajño hy arthajño 'bhyadhikas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even among <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, one who knows the Veda is higher, and one who knows its meaning is higher than that.
Higher than one who knows the meaning is the resolver of doubts; better than that is one who performs his own duty.

children.text: muktasaṅgas tato bhūyān adogdhā dharmam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Greater still is one free from attachment, one who does not milk his <s>dharma</s> for himself.
Therefore, one whose self, aims, and all actions are offered entirely to me without interruption,
a person whose self is offered to me and whose karma is renounced in me,

children.text: na paśyāmi paraṃ bhūtam akartuḥ samadarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: I do not see any being higher than him, because he is without doership and sees equally.
With the mind one should bow to these beings, honoring them,
thinking, 'The Blessed Lord, the Lord, has entered them by a portion as the <s>jīva</s>.'

children.text: bhaktiyogaś ca yogaś ca mayā mānavy udīritaḥ
children.translated_text: O daughter of <s>Manu</s>, <s>bhakti-yoga</s> and yoga have been declared by me,
by either one of which a person may reach the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
This is the form of the Blessed Lord, of Brahman, of the supreme self:
supreme, as <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, the divine impeller of the movements of karma.
The divine basis of distinctions of form is called <s>kāla</s> (Time),
from which there is fear for beings beginning with the <s>mahat</s>, for those who see separately.

children.text: yo 'ntaḥ praviśya bhūtāni bhūtair atty akhilāśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: He who, entering beings inwardly, devours them through beings, the support of all,
that one, called <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the <s>adhiyajña</s>, is Time, the lord of those who calculate.

children.text: na cāsya kaścid dayito na dveṣyo na ca bāndhavaḥ
children.translated_text: No one is dear to him, nor hateful, nor a kinsman;
that vigilant end-maker enters the negligent person.

children.text: yadbhayād vāti vāto 'yaṃ sūryas tapati yadbhayāt
children.translated_text: From fear of him this wind blows, and from fear of him the sun gives heat;

children.text: yadbhayād varṣate devo bhagaṇo bhāti yadbhayāt ||
children.translated_text: from fear of him the god rains, and from fear of him the host of stars shines.

children.text: yad vanaspatayo bhītā latāś cauṣadhibhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Afraid, the forest trees, creepers, and plants together with the herbs,

children.text: sve sve kāle 'bhigṛhṇanti puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: in their own seasons take on flowers and fruits.

children.text: sravanti sarito bhītā notsarpaty udadhir yataḥ
children.translated_text: Afraid, the rivers flow; because of him the ocean does not overflow.

children.text: agnir indhe sagiribhir bhūr na majjati yadbhayāt ||
children.translated_text: From fear of him, fire burns and the earth with its mountains does not sink.

children.text: nabho dadāti śvasatāṃ padaṃ yanniyamād adaḥ
children.translated_text: By whose regulation the sky gives space to breathing beings,

children.text: lokaṃ svadehaṃ tanute mahān saptabhir āvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and the great one expands this world, his own body, enclosed by seven coverings,
the gods who identify with the <s>guṇa</s>s, out of fear of him, in creation and so forth...
under whose control this moving and unmoving world exists age after age.
He is endless, the end-maker: Time, beginningless, the maker of beginnings, undecaying,
bringing forth one person from another and killing even the killer by death.
<s>Kapila</s> said:
A person surely does not know the vast stride of this one,
though he is being driven by the powerful one, like a mass of clouds by the wind.

children.text: yaṃ yam artham upādatte duḥkhena sukhahetave
children.translated_text: Whatever object he takes up with difficulty as a cause of happiness,

children.text: taṃ taṃ dhunoti bhagavān pumān śocati yatkṛte ||
children.translated_text: the Blessed Lord shakes each one away, and the man grieves for the sake of which he acted.
The foolish man, through delusion, regards as permanent the possessions of an impermanent body,
together with its attachments: house, field, wealth, and the rest.

children.text: jantur vai bhava etasmin yāṃ yāṃ yonim anuvrajet
children.translated_text: Whatever womb a creature enters in this existence,

children.text: tasyāṃ tasyāṃ sa labhate nirvṛtiṃ na virajyate ||
children.translated_text: in each one he finds satisfaction and does not become detached.

children.text: narakastho 'pi dehaṃ vai na pumāṃs tyaktum icchati
children.translated_text: Even when dwelling in hell, a man does not wish to abandon the body,
for there is satisfaction even in a hellish state, while he is deluded by divine <s>māyā</s>.
With his heart deeply rooted in self, wife, sons, house, cattle, wealth, and relatives,
he thinks very highly of himself.
Burning in every limb from the anxiety of carrying these burdens,
the fool, evil in intention, constantly commits evil deeds.
His self and senses are seized by the <s>māyā</s> of faithless women,
by private, contrived conversations and by the sweet prattle of children.
In houses where <s>dharma</s> is false and the whole apparatus is suffering,
the householder, tirelessly counteracting pain, thinks himself happy.

children.text: arthair āpāditair gurvyā hiṃsayetastataś ca tān
children.translated_text: With wealth obtained here and there through grave violence, he supports them,

children.text: puṣṇāti yeṣāṃ poṣeṇa śeṣabhug yāty adhaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: and by feeding those whose leftovers he eats, he himself goes downward.
When his livelihood is being lost, though he starts it again and again,
overcome by greed and devoid of strength, he longs for another's goods.
Unable to support his family, ill-fortuned, striving in vain,

children.text: śriyā vihīnaḥ kṛpaṇo dhyāyan śvasiti mūḍhadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: deprived of prosperity and miserable, the fool-minded man broods and sighs.
And when he is thus unable to support even himself, his wife and the others
do not respect him as before, like farmers an old ox.
Even then, not having developed disgust, he is maintained by those whom he once maintained,
made ugly by old age and facing death in the house.
He remains there, eating what is set down with contempt, like a house dog,
sick, his digestive fire unkindled, eating little and moving little.
With his eyes turned upward by the departing vital wind and his channels blocked by phlegm,
exhausted by cough and labored breathing, he rattles in his throat.
Lying there, surrounded by his own relatives as they lament,
even when addressed he does not speak, having come under the power of Time's noose.
Thus, with his self absorbed in supporting his family and his senses unconquered,
he dies while his own people weep, his mind ruined by great pain.
Then two messengers of <s>Yama</s> arrive, terrifying, with fierce eyes;
seeing them, his heart terrified, he releases feces and urine.

children.text: yātanādeha āvṛtya pāśair baddhvā gale balāt
children.translated_text: Enclosing him in a body of torment and binding him by force with nooses around the neck,

children.text: nayato dīrgham adhvānaṃ daṇḍyaṃ rājabhaṭā yathā ||
children.translated_text: the two lead him along a long road, like royal guards leading a punishable criminal.
His heart is pierced by their threats, and trembling arises in him;

children.text: pathi śvabhir bhakṣyamāṇa ārto 'ghaṃ svam anusmaran ||
children.translated_text: on the road, being eaten by dogs, he is afflicted and remembers his own sin.
Overcome by hunger and thirst, scorched on the road of hot sand by sun, forest fire, and winds,

children.text: kṛcchreṇa pṛṣṭhe kaśayā ca tāḍitaś calaty aśakto 'pi nirāśramodake ||
children.translated_text: and struck on the back with a whip, he moves with difficulty though powerless, with no shelter or water.

children.text: tatra tatra patan śrānto mūrchitaḥ punar utthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Falling here and there, exhausted, fainting and then rising again,
he is led swiftly along the most sinful path to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Having been taken over ninety-nine thousand <s>yojanas</s> of road

children.text: tribhir muhūrtair dvābhyāṃ vā nītaḥ prāpnoti yātanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: in three or two <s>muhūrtas</s>, he reaches the torments.
There is the burning of his own limbs, after they have been wrapped with firebrands and the like,
and in some place the eating of his own flesh, cut by himself or by others.
While he is alive, his entrails are pulled out by dogs and vultures in the abode of <s>Yama</s>,
and there is self-torment by snakes, scorpions, bites, and other biting things.
There is cutting limb by limb, splitting apart by elephants and the like,
hurling down from mountain peaks, and confinement in water-pits.
The torments called <s>Tāmisra</s>, <s>Andhatāmisra</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, and the rest,

children.text: bhuṅkte naro vā nārī vā mithaḥ saṅgena nirmitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: which are produced by mutual attachment, a man or a woman undergoes.

children.text: atraiva narakaḥ svarga iti mātaḥ pracakṣate
children.translated_text: Here itself, O mother, they declare hell and heaven to exist;

children.text: yā yātanā vai nārakyas tā ihāpy upalakṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever hellish torments there are, those are observed here as well.

children.text: evaṃ kuṭumbaṃ bibhrāṇa udaram bhara eva vā
children.translated_text: Thus, while supporting a family or merely filling his belly,
after abandoning both here, he experiences after death such a fruit of that.
Alone, having left this own body, he enters darkness,
with evil as his provision, from what was maintained by hostility toward beings.
By divine ordering, in hell a man undergoes the impurity
incurred by him for supporting his family, distressed like one whose wealth has been taken.
For the jīva, eager to support his family by adharma alone,
goes to <s>Andhatāmisra</s>, the last station of darkness.
After passing in order through as many torments and the like
as lie below the human world, he returns here again, purified.
The Blessed Lord said:
By karma, under divine supervision, a creature, for the arising of a body,
enters a woman's belly, lodged in a particle of a man's semen.
In one night it becomes <s>kalala</s>; in five nights, a bubble;

children.text: daśāhena tu karkandhūḥ peśy aṇḍaṃ vā tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: in ten days, a <s>karkandhū</s>; after that, a lump of flesh or an egg.
In one month the head forms; in two months the bodily form, with arms, legs, and the other limbs, appears,
and by three months nails, hair, bones, skin, the generative organ, and the bodily openings arise.
By four months the seven <s>dhātus</s> (bodily constituents) appear, and by five hunger and thirst arise;

children.text: ṣaḍbhir jarāyuṇā vītaḥ kukṣau bhrāmyati dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: by six, enveloped in the fetal membrane, he turns about on the right side in the womb.
His bodily constituents grow from the food, drink, and other things eaten by his mother, in that undesirable place;

children.text: śete viṇmūtrayor garte sa jantur jantusambhave ||
children.translated_text: there the creature lies in a pit of feces and urine, in the place where creatures are born.
With all his limbs wounded by worms, because of his delicacy, at every moment

children.text: mūrchām āpnoty urukleśas tatratyaiḥ kṣudhitair muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: he falls into faintness, suffering great pain again and again from those hungry creatures there.
By the bitter, sharp, hot, salty, dry, sour, and other overpowering foods
eaten by his mother and touching him, pain rises throughout all his limbs.

children.text: ulbena saṃvṛtas tasminn antraiś ca bahir āvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Covered by the fetal membrane there and enclosed outside by the intestines,
he remains with his head drawn into his belly, his back, head, and neck bent.
Unable to move his own limbs, like a bird in a cage,
there, by fate, he obtains memory and recalls the karma produced through hundreds of births;

children.text: smaran dīrgham anucchvāsaṃ śarma kiṃ nāma vindate ||
children.translated_text: remembering it, and long unable even to breathe freely, what happiness can he possibly find?
Beginning with the seventh month, though he has gained awareness, he is shaken
and cannot stay in one place because of the birth-winds, like a worm born from filth in the same womb.
Supplicating, frightened, bound in seven coverings, the sage-like fetus, with joined hands,
would praise, in a faltering voice, him by whom he has been placed in the womb.
The creature said:

children.text: tasyopasannam avituṃ jagad icchayāttanānātanor bhuvi calaccaraṇāravindam
children.translated_text: To protect the world that has approached him, he has assumed manifold bodies by his own will, and his lotus feet move upon the earth.

children.text: so 'haṃ vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ hy akutobhayaṃ me yenedṛśī gatir adarśy asato 'nurūpā ||
children.translated_text: I take refuge in him; for me he is fearlessness from every side, by whom this state, fit for the unreal, has been shown.

children.text: yas tv atra baddha iva karmabhir āvṛtātmā bhūtendriyāśayamayīm avalambya māyām
children.translated_text: He who, though as if bound here by karmas and covered in selfhood, rests upon <s>māyā</s> made of the elements, senses, and inner dispositions,

children.text: āste viśuddham avikāram akhaṇḍabodham ātapyamānahṛdaye 'vasitaṃ namāmi ||
children.translated_text: yet remains pure, changeless, and undivided awareness, settled in the heart that is being scorched: to him I bow.
I, hidden in a body fashioned from the five elements and seemingly identified with the senses, qualities, objects, and consciousness, am in truth apart from it;

children.text: tena vikuṇṭhamahimānam ṛṣiṃ tam enaṃ vande paraṃ prakṛtipūruṣayoḥ pumāṃsam ||
children.translated_text: therefore I venerate that sage of unimpeded majesty, that supreme Person beyond prakṛti and puruṣa.
By whose <s>māyā</s>, on this saṃsāric road bound by powerful qualities and actions, this being wanders, exhausted by that very toil;

children.text: naṣṭasmṛtiḥ punar ayaṃ pravṛṇīta lokaṃ yuktyā kayā mahadanugraham antareṇa ||
children.translated_text: with memory lost, by what means could he again choose the world, without the favor of the great one?

children.text: jñānaṃ yad etad adadhāt katamaḥ sa devas traikālikaṃ sthiracareṣv anuvartitāṃśaḥ
children.translated_text: What god placed in me this knowledge, extending through the three times, whose portion follows through moving and unmoving beings?

children.text: taṃ jīvakarmapadavīm anuvartamānās tāpatrayopaśamanāya vayaṃ bhajema ||
children.translated_text: Let us worship him, who follows the path of <s>jīva</s> and karma, for the calming of the threefold suffering.
The embodied one, in the cavity of another body, fallen into a well of blood, feces, and urine, his body intensely scorched by the digestive fire,

children.text: icchann ito vivasituṃ gaṇayan svamāsān nirvāsyate kṛpaṇadhīr bhagavan kadā nu ||
children.translated_text: desires to go out from here and counts his own months: when, O Blessed Lord, will this wretched-minded one be expelled?

children.text: yenedṛśīṃ gatim asau daśamāsya īśa saṃgrāhitaḥ purudayena bhavādṛśena
children.translated_text: O Lord, since this ten-month-old one has been made to understand such a condition by the abundant compassion of one like you,

children.text: svenaiva tuṣyatu kṛtena sa dīnanāthaḥ ko nāma tatprati vināñjalim asya kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: may that lord of the helpless be satisfied with his own deed; who indeed would do anything in return for him except fold his hands?

children.text: paśyaty ayaṃ dhiṣaṇayā nanu saptavadhriḥ śārīrake damaśarīry aparaḥ svadehe
children.translated_text: This being bound in seven coverings truly sees, by intelligence, the other indwelling ruler in his own bodily self;

children.text: yat sṛṣṭayāsaṃ tam ahaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ paśye bahir hṛdi ca caityam iva pratītam ||
children.translated_text: because of the creation by which I exist, I see that ancient <s>puruṣa</s> outside and in the heart, manifest like the caitya within.

children.text: so 'haṃ vasann api vibho bahuduḥkhavāsaṃ garbhān na nirjigamiṣe bahir andhakūpe
children.translated_text: Therefore, O Lord, though I dwell in the womb, an abode of much suffering, I do not wish to emerge into the dark well outside,

children.text: yatropayātam upasarpati devamāyā mithyā matir yadanu saṃsṛticakram etat ||
children.translated_text: where, when one has arrived, divine <s>māyā</s> approaches, and the false notion from which this wheel of saṃsāra follows.

children.text: tasmād ahaṃ vigataviklava uddhariṣya ātmānam āśu tamasaḥ suhṛdātmanaiva
children.translated_text: Therefore, free from agitation, I shall quickly lift myself out of darkness by my own self as my friend,

children.text: bhūyo yathā vyasanam etad anekarandhraṃ mā me bhaviṣyad upasāditaviṣṇupādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that, having attained the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, this misery of many openings may not befall me again.
<s>Kapila</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ kṛtamatir garbhe daśamāsyaḥ stuvann ṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus resolved in the womb, the ten-month-old sage-like fetus praises him,
but at once the birth-wind casts him downward for delivery.
Released by that wind suddenly, distressed and turning his head downward,
he comes out with difficulty, breathless and with memory destroyed.

children.text: patito bhuvy asṛṅmiśraḥ viṣṭhābhūr iva ceṣṭate
children.translated_text: Fallen on the ground, mixed with blood, he moves about like a worm born from filth;

children.text: rorūyati gate jñāne viparītāṃ gatiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he cries loudly, his knowledge gone, having come into an opposite condition.

children.text: paracchandaṃ na viduṣā puṣyamāṇo janena saḥ
children.translated_text: He is nourished by people, though he does not know another's intention,
and, fallen into what he does not desire, he has no power to reject it.
The creature is laid on an impure bed, soiled by sweat-born filth,
unable to scratch his limbs or to move in sitting and rising.
Gnats, mosquitoes, bedbugs, and the like bite his tender, unripe skin;
as worms bite a worm, they bite him while he cries, his knowledge lost.

children.text: ity evaṃ śaiśavaṃ bhuktvā duḥkhaṃ paugaṇḍam eva ca
children.translated_text: Having thus experienced the suffering of infancy and also of childhood,
he does not obtain what he longs for because of ignorance; his anger is inflamed, and he is given over to grief.
Along with the body, and with pride and anger growing,

children.text: karoti vigrahaṃ kāmī kāmiṣv antāya cātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the desire-driven man quarrels with those who are desire-driven, to the ruin of his own self.

children.text: bhūtaiḥ pañcabhir ārabdhe dehe dehy abudho 'sakṛt
children.translated_text: In a body begun from the five elements, the foolish embodied being again and again

children.text: ahaṃ mamety asadgrāhaḥ karoti kumatir matim ||
children.translated_text: forms the false grasping, 'I' and 'mine'; with bad understanding he makes this his thought.

children.text: tadarthaṃ kurute karma yadbaddho yāti saṃsṛtim
children.translated_text: For that purpose he performs action, by which, bound, he goes into saṃsṛti,
and the bondage of ignorance and karma follows him, bringing affliction.
If again he takes to the path of the unworthy, whose exertions are for the penis and the belly,

children.text: āsthito ramate jantus tamo viśati pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: the creature delights there and enters darkness just as before.

children.text: satyaṃ śaucaṃ dayā maunaṃ buddhiḥ śrīr hrīr yaśaḥ kṣamā
children.translated_text: Truthfulness, purity, compassion, silence, intelligence, prosperity, modesty, fame, and forbearance,

children.text: śamo damo bhagaś ceti yatsaṅgād yāti saṅkṣayam ||
children.translated_text: tranquillity, self-control, and fortune: through association with them, all these go to destruction.
One should not associate with those who are unpeaceful, foolish, inwardly broken, and unvirtuous,

children.text: saṅgaṃ na kuryāc chocyeṣu yoṣitkrīḍāmṛgeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: nor with pitiable men who have become play-animals for women.

children.text: na tathāsya bhaven moho bandhaś cānyaprasaṅgataḥ
children.translated_text: A man's delusion and bondage do not arise so much from any other attachment
as from association with women, and from association with those attached to them.
<s>Prajāpati</s>, seeing his own daughter, was overpowered by her beauty;
when she had become a doe, he, shameless, pursued her in the form of a stag.
Among the beings in the successive creation produced by him, what man could have unbroken understanding here,
except the sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, before <s>māyā</s> (illusion) made of woman?

children.text: balaṃ me paśya māyāyāḥ strīmayyā jayino diśām
children.translated_text: See the power of my <s>māyā</s> (illusion), female in form, conquering the conquerors of the directions;
by the mere expansion of her brow she makes them fall beneath her feet.

children.text: saṅgaṃ na kuryāt pramadāsu jātu yogasya pāraṃ param ārurukṣuḥ
children.translated_text: One who has gained the self through service to me and wishes to ascend to the farthest shore of yoga

children.text: matsevayā pratilabdhātmalābho vadanti yā nirayadvāram asya ||
children.translated_text: should never associate with women, for people say that such association is the gate of hell for him.
A woman, <s>māyā</s> (illusion) fashioned by the gods, approaches gradually;

children.text: tām īkṣetātmano mṛtyuṃ tṛṇaiḥ kūpam ivāvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: he should look upon her as his own death, like a well covered over with grass.

children.text: yāṃ manyate patiṃ mohān manmāyām ṛṣabhāyatīm
children.translated_text: One who, through attachment to women, has attained womanhood regards, from delusion, as her husband
my <s>māyā</s> (illusion) appearing as a male, bestowing wealth, children, and a house.
One should know that same power, taking the form of husband, children, and household,
as one's own death brought by fate, like a song for deer.
With the body that has become a living being, a person follows from world to world,

children.text: bhuñjāna eva karmāṇi karoty avirataṃ pumān ||
children.translated_text: and while experiencing karmas he continually performs them.
For this living being the body, made of elements, senses, and mind, is his follower;
its cessation is his death, while its manifestation is birth.
When the seat for apprehending objects becomes unfit to perceive objects,
that is called becoming the five elements; from self-conceit, birth is the seeing of objects.
Just as, when the eyes are unable to see the parts of an object,
at that very time both the eye and the seer are unfit for the act of seeing.

children.text: tasmān na kāryaḥ santrāso na kārpaṇyaṃ na sambhramaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore terror should not be produced, nor wretchedness, nor bewilderment;

children.text: buddhvā jīvagatiṃ dhīro muktasaṅgaś cared iha ||
children.translated_text: having understood the course of the living being, a steady person should move here free from attachment.
With an intellect of right vision, joined with yoga and detachment,
one should move in this world fashioned by <s>māyā</s> (illusion), laying aside the body.
<s>Kapila</s> said:

children.text: atha yo gṛhamedhīyān dharmān evāvasan gṛhe
children.translated_text: Now the man who, while living at home, dwells only in household <s>dharma</s> (duty)

children.text: kāmam arthaṃ ca dharmān svān dogdhi bhūyaḥ piparti tān ||
children.translated_text: milks desire, wealth, and his own duties, and again nourishes them.
He too, turned away from the <s>dharma</s> (way) of the Blessed Lord and deluded by desire,

children.text: yajate kratubhir devān pitṝṃś ca śraddhayānvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: worships the gods with sacrifices and the ancestors with faith.
A man whose mind is seized by that faith, devoted to ancestors and gods,

children.text: gatvā cāndramasaṃ lokaṃ somapāḥ punar eṣyati ||
children.translated_text: goes to the lunar world, drinks soma, and then returns again.
When <s>Hari</s>, whose seat is <s>Ananta</s>, lies upon the bed of the serpent-king,

children.text: tadā lokā layaṃ yānti ta ete gṛhamedhinām ||
children.translated_text: then these worlds of the householders pass into dissolution.

children.text: ye svadharmān na duhyanti dhīrāḥ kāmārthahetave
children.translated_text: But those steady ones who do not milk their own duties for the sake of desire and wealth,
who are unattached, have laid down their actions, are peaceful, and have pure minds,
who are devoted to the <s>dharma</s> (way) of cessation, free from possessiveness and ego,
with a mind purified by the sattva obtained through their own duty,
go by the gate of the sun to the puruṣa facing every direction,
the lord of higher and lower, who is the origin, end, and sustainer of this prakṛti.

children.text: dviparārdhāvasāne yaḥ pralayo brahmaṇas tu te
children.translated_text: At the end of the two parārdhas, when the dissolution of <s>Brahmā</s> occurs,
until then those who contemplate the Supreme dwell in the world of the higher one.
When the self-born one, wishing to withdraw the unmanifest, is surrounded by earth, water, fire, wind, ether, mind, senses, sense-objects, elements, and the rest,

children.text: avyākṛtaṃ viśati yarhi guṇatrayātmā kālaṃ parākhyam anubhūya paraḥ svayambhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, having experienced Time called supreme, he whose nature is the three guṇas enters the unmanifest.

children.text: evaṃ paretya bhagavantam anupraviṣṭāye yogino jitamarunmanaso virāgāḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus departed and entered the Blessed Lord, those yogins whose breath and mind are conquered, detached,

children.text: tenaiva sākam amṛtaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ brahma pradhānam upayānty agatābhimānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and free from self-conceit attain, together with him, the immortal ancient puruṣa, <s>Brahman</s> and pradhāna.
Therefore go for refuge, O lovely woman, to him who has made his abode
in the heart-lotuses of all beings, whose majesty is known from sacred hearing.
The first-born among the moving and unmoving, the womb of the Veda, together with the seers,
with lords of yoga beginning with the <s>Kumāras</s>, and with perfected beings who set yoga in motion,
because of the pride of seeing difference, even through action performed without attachment,
and because of doership, reaches only qualified <s>Brahman</s>, the puruṣa, the bull among persons.
Having passed through saṃsāra, when in time, through Time as the form of the Lord,
a disturbance of the guṇas arises, he is born again as before.
Even they, having enjoyed the sovereignty and supremacy made by <s>dharma</s> (merit),
come back again when a disturbance of the guṇas occurs.
But those whose minds are attached here to works, and who are endowed with faith,

children.text: kurvanty apratiṣiddhāni nityāny api ca kṛtsnaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: perform all actions that are not forbidden, and also the obligatory ones.
With minds blunted by rajas, made of desire, and with senses unconquered,
they worship the ancestors day after day, their hearts delighting in their homes.
Those men pursue the three aims of life and are turned away from <s>Hari</s>,
from the story of <s>Madhudviṣa</s>, whose mighty deeds are worthy to be told.
Surely struck down by fate are those who, abandoning the nectar of stories of <s>Acyuta</s>,

children.text: hitvā śṛṇvanty asadgāthāḥ purīṣam iva viḍbhujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: listen to false tales, like eaters of filth consuming excrement.
They go by the southern path of <s>Aryaman</s> to the world of the ancestors;
performing rites that end at the cremation ground, they are born again in succession among offspring.

children.text: tatas te kṣīṇasukṛtāḥ punar lokam imaṃ sati
children.translated_text: Then, O virtuous woman, when their merit has been exhausted, they return to this world,
falling helpless, their rise at once cast down by the gods.
Therefore worship the supreme Lord with your whole being,
with devotion resting on his qualities, whose lotus feet are worthy of worship.
Bhaktiyoga directed toward the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>

children.text: janayaty āśu vairāgyaṃ jñānaṃ yad brahmadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: quickly produces detachment and knowledge, which is vision of <s>Brahman</s>.
When his mind, toward objects made equal through the activities of the senses,

children.text: na vigṛhṇāti vaiṣamyaṃ priyam apriyam ity uta ||
children.translated_text: does not grasp a difference as 'dear' or 'not dear',
then at that very time, by the self, he sees the self as unattached and equal-seeing,
free from what is to be rejected or accepted, and mounted upon its proper state.
The supreme <s>Brahman</s>, pure knowledge alone, the supreme self, the Lord, the Person,

children.text: dṛśyādibhiḥ pṛthag bhāvair bhagavān eka īyate ||
children.translated_text: is called the one Blessed Lord under distinct states such as the visible and the rest.
For yogins here, through complete yoga, only this much

children.text: yujyate 'bhimato hy artho yad asaṅgas tu kṛtsnaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is joined with the desired goal: that there should be total nonattachment.

children.text: jñānam ekaṃ parācīnair indriyair brahma nirguṇam
children.translated_text: The single knowledge, <s>Brahman</s> without qualities, through the outward-turned senses
appears, by delusion, in the form of objects possessing qualities such as sound.

children.text: yathā mahān ahaṃrūpas trivṛt pañcavidhaḥ svarāṭ
children.translated_text: Just as the great principle, in the form of ego, is threefold, fivefold, self-ruling,

children.text: ekādaśavidhas tasya vapur aṇḍaṃ jagad yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and elevenfold, its body is the cosmic egg from which the world arises.

children.text: etad vai śraddhayā bhaktyā yogābhyāsena nityaśaḥ
children.translated_text: This, indeed, through faith, devotion, and constant practice of yoga,
one whose self is concentrated, unattached, and dispassionate clearly sees.

children.text: ity etat kathitaṃ gurvi jñānaṃ tad brahmadarśanam
children.translated_text: Thus, O venerable lady, I have told you that knowledge which is vision of <s>Brahman</s>,
by which the truth of prakṛti and puruṣa is understood.
Jñānayoga fixed on me, beyond the guṇas and characterized by bhakti,
has one and the same object in both cases, defined by the word 'Blessed Lord'.
Just as one object, the support of many qualities, is apprehended through the senses with their separate gates,
so the Blessed Lord is understood in many ways through the paths of scripture.
By ritual action, sacrifices, gifts, austerity, recitation, and reflection,
and also by conquest of the self and the senses, and by renunciation of actions,
by yoga with its various limbs, and indeed by bhaktiyoga,
by <s>dharma</s> marked by both courses, having both engagement and withdrawal,
by understanding the truth of the self and by firm detachment,

children.text: īyate bhagavān ebhiḥ saguṇo nirguṇaḥ svadṛk ||
children.translated_text: the Blessed Lord is reached through these, both with qualities and without qualities, self-seeing.
I have explained to you the fourfold nature of bhaktiyoga,
and of Time, whose unseen course runs hidden among living beings.
I have told the many wanderings of the jīva, produced by ignorance and karma,

children.text: yāsv aṅga praviśann ātmā na veda gatim ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: into which, dear one, the self enters and does not know its own path.
One should never teach this to a wicked person or to one who is undisciplined,

children.text: na stabdhāya na bhinnāya naiva dharmadhvajāya ca ||
children.translated_text: nor to the arrogant, nor to the divided in spirit, nor to one who displays <s>dharma</s> as a banner.
One should not teach it to the greedy, nor to one whose mind is fixed on household life,

children.text: nābhaktāya ca me jātu na madbhaktadviṣām api ||
children.translated_text: nor ever to one without devotion to me, nor to those who hate my devotees.
It should be given to one who has faith, who is devoted, humble, and free from envy,
who has formed friendship toward beings and is intent on hearing and service,
to one whose detachment from external things has arisen and whose mind is peaceful,
to one free from jealousy and pure, for whom I am dearer than what is dear.

children.text: ya idaṃ śṛṇuyād amba śraddhayā puruṣaḥ sakṛt
children.translated_text: O mother, the person who hears this once with faith,

children.text: yo vābhidhatte maccittaḥ sa hy eti padavīṃ ca me ||
children.translated_text: or who recites it with his mind fixed on me, surely reaches my path.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ niśamya kapilasya vaco janitrī sā kardamasya dayitā kila devahūtiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus heard the words of <s>Kapila</s>, his mother, beloved <s>Devahūti</s> of <s>Kardama</s>,
with the veil of delusion fallen away, bowed to him and joyfully praised him, the ground of perfection marked by the realm of truth.
<s>Devahūti</s> said:

children.text: athāpy ajo 'ntaḥsalile śayānaṃ bhūtendriyārthātmamayaṃ vapus te
children.translated_text: Yet the unborn one, born from the lotus of your belly, meditated on your body lying in the inner waters,

children.text: guṇapravāhaṃ sadaśeṣabījaṃ dadhyau svayaṃ yaj jaṭharābjajātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: made of beings, senses, objects, and self, the stream of the guṇas, the seed of all that remains.

children.text: sa eva viśvasya bhavān vidhatte guṇapravāheṇa vibhaktavīryaḥ
children.translated_text: You yourself fashion this universe by the stream of the guṇas, your power divided within it,
the source of creation and the rest, though free from desire, with unfailing intention, Lord of the self, possessing a thousand inconceivable powers.

children.text: sa tvaṃ bhṛto me jaṭhareṇa nātha kathaṃ nu yasyodara etad āsīt
children.translated_text: O Lord, you have been carried in my womb; how can this be, since this universe was in your belly,

children.text: viśvaṃ yugānte vaṭapattra ekaḥ śete sma māyāśiśur aṅghripānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and at the end of the age you alone lay on a banyan leaf, a wondrous infant sucking your foot?

children.text: tvaṃ dehatantraḥ praśamāya pāpmanāṃ nideśabhājāṃ ca vibho vibhūtaye
children.translated_text: O mighty one, you are dependent on bodies for the pacification of sins and for the prosperity of those who accept your command.

children.text: yathāvatārās tava sūkarādayas tathāyam apy ātmapathopalabdhaye ||
children.translated_text: Just as your descents as the Boar and the others occurred, so too this one is for the realization of the path of the self.

children.text: yan nāmadheyaśravaṇānukīrtanād yatprahvaṇād yatsmaraṇād api kvacit
children.translated_text: From hearing and chanting your name, from bowing to it, and even at times from remembering it,

children.text: śvādo 'pi sadyaḥ savanāya kalpate kutaḥ punas te bhagavan nu darśanāt ||
children.translated_text: even a dog-eater at once becomes fit for the soma-pressing; how much more, O Blessed Lord, from seeing you.

children.text: aho bata śvapaco 'to garīyān yaj jihvāgre vartate nāma tubhyam
children.translated_text: Ah, indeed, even a dog-cooker is greater, if your name is present on the tip of his tongue.

children.text: tepus tapas te juhuvuḥ sasnur āryā brahmānūcur nāma gṛṇanti ye te ||
children.translated_text: Those who utter your name have performed austerity, sacrificed, bathed, become noble, and recited the Veda.

children.text: taṃ tvām ahaṃ brahma paraṃ pumāṃsaṃ pratyaksrotasy ātmani saṃvibhāvyam
children.translated_text: I worship you, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme Person, to be contemplated in the inward-flowing self,

children.text: svatejasā dhvastaguṇapravāhaṃ vande viṣṇuṃ kapilaṃ vedagarbham ||
children.translated_text: whose own splendor has destroyed the stream of the guṇas: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, womb of the Veda.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: īḍito bhagavān evaṃ kapilākhyaḥ paraḥ pumān
children.translated_text: Thus praised, the Blessed Lord, the supreme Person known as <s>Kapila</s>,
spoke to his mother, affectionate toward his mother, in a voice overcome with emotion.
<s>Kapila</s> said:
By this path, mother, easy to serve and taught by me to you,
if you follow it, you will soon attain the supreme limit.

children.text: śraddhatsvaitan mataṃ mahyaṃ juṣṭaṃ yad brahmavādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Put faith in this doctrine of mine, honored by those who speak of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: yena mām abhayaṃ yāyā mṛtyum ṛcchanty atadvidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by which you may come to me, to fearlessness; those who do not know it meet death.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: iti pradarśya bhagavān satīṃ tām ātmano gatim
children.translated_text: Having thus shown that virtuous woman the path of his own state,
the Blessed Lord <s>Kapila</s>, with his mother, the speaker of brahman, having consented, went away.
And she too, joined to yoga by the instruction on yoga spoken by her son,
remained concentrated in that āśrama, the crest-jewel of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
Her matted locks and curling hair were tawny from constant bathing,
and by fierce austerity she bore her body thin and clad in bark garments.
The household splendor of <s>Kardama</s>, lord of creatures, had expanded through austerity and yoga,
and was incomparable, desired even by those who travel in celestial aerial cars.
There were beds like the foam of milk, ivory couches with golden fittings,
golden seats, and coverings pleasant to the touch.
Within clear crystal walls and great emerald chambers,
jewel-lamps shone, and women were adorned with jewels.
The garden of the house was lovely with many flowering trees of the gods,
with pairs of birds calling and intoxicated bees singing.
There, when she entered, attendants of the gods sang of her,
in the lotus-scented pool where she had been fondly served by <s>Kardama</s>.
Though that place was most desired even by the women of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>, she abandoned it,
and, distressed by separation from her son, gave only slight care to her appearance.
When her husband had gone forth to the forest, she was afflicted by the absence of her child;

children.text: jñātatattvāpy abhūn naṣṭe vatse gaur iva vatsalā ||
children.translated_text: though she knew the truth, when her calf was gone she became tender like a cow loving its calf.

children.text: tam eva dhyāyatī devam apatyaṃ kapilaṃ harim
children.translated_text: Meditating on that very divine son, <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Hari</s>,
O child, she soon became free from desire for such a house.
She meditated on the form of the Blessed Lord, which her son had described as an object of meditation,
his face gracious, through contemplation both collective and detailed.
By the yoga of an outpouring of devotion and by powerful detachment,
by knowledge born from properly joined practice and having brahman as its cause,
and with purity, she realized that self by her own self, facing every direction,
whose distinctions made by <s>māyā</s> and the guṇas had disappeared through direct experience.
Her mind was established in brahman, in the Blessed Lord, the refuge of the self;
because the condition of the individual soul had ceased, her afflictions were exhausted and she attained bliss.
Because she was constantly established in samādhi, the delusion caused by the guṇas had turned back,

children.text: na sasmāra tadātmānaṃ svapne dṛṣṭam ivotthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and she no longer remembered her own body, like one awakened from something seen in a dream.
Her body, though nourished by others, was not emaciated, because of its inner sustaining power;

children.text: babhau malair avacchannaḥ sadhūma iva pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: covered with dirt, it shone like a fire enveloped in smoke.
She did not notice her own body, made of austerity and yoga, with loosened hair and without garments,
protected by divine power, because her mind had entered <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Thus, by the path taught by <s>Kapila</s>, she quickly attained the supreme self,
the Blessed Lord, the nirvāṇa of brahman.
That place, O hero, became a most holy field, famed throughout the three worlds,

children.text: nāmnā siddhapadaṃ yatra sā saṃsiddhim upeyuṣī ||
children.translated_text: known by the name <s>Siddhapada</s>, where she reached complete perfection.

children.text: tasyās tad yogavidhutamārtyaṃ martyam abhūt sarit
children.translated_text: Her mortal body, with mortality washed away by that yoga, became a river,
O gentle one, the foremost of streams, giver of accomplishment and served by the perfected ones.
And <s>Kapila</s>, the great yogin and Blessed Lord, from his father's āśrama,
having taken leave of his mother, went toward the northeast.
Praised by siddhas, cāraṇas, gandharvas, sages, and hosts of apsarases,
and given a dwelling and respectful offerings by the ocean,
he remains there, established in yoga, praised by the teachers of Sāṃkhya,
concentrated for the pacification of all three worlds.

children.text: etan nigaditaṃ tāta yat pṛṣṭo 'haṃ tavānagha
children.translated_text: This has been told, dear one, in response to what you asked me, O sinless man:

children.text: kapilasya ca saṃvādo devahūtyāś ca pāvanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the purifying dialogue between <s>Kapila</s> and <s>Devahūti</s>.

children.text: ya idam anuśṛṇoti yo 'bhidhatte kapilamuner matam ātmayogaguhyam
children.translated_text: Whoever listens to this, or recites the secret doctrine of self-yoga taught by the sage <s>Kapila</s>,
with mind fixed on the Blessed Lord whose banner bears <s>Suparṇa</s>, obtains the lotus feet of the Blessed Lord.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: manos tu śatarūpāyāṃ tisraḥ kanyāś ca jajñire
children.translated_text: From <s>Manu</s> and <s>Śatarūpā</s> three daughters were born,

children.text: ākūtir devahūtiś ca prasūtir iti viśrutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: famed as <s>Ākūti</s>, <s>Devahūti</s>, and <s>Prasūti</s>.

children.text: ākūtiṃ rucaye prādād api bhrātṛmatīṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: The king gave <s>Ākūti</s> to <s>Ruci</s>, even though she had brothers,
resorting to the putrikā-dharma, with <s>Śatarūpā</s>'s approval.

children.text: prajāpatiḥ sa bhagavān rucis tasyām ajījanat
children.translated_text: The blessed lord of creatures, <s>Ruci</s>, begot in her
a pair of twins, radiant with brahmanical splendor, through supreme concentration.

children.text: yas tayoḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣād viṣṇur yajñasvarūpadhṛk
children.translated_text: The male of those two was directly <s>Viṣṇu</s>, bearing the form of <s>Yajña</s>,

children.text: yā strī sā dakṣiṇā bhūter aṃśabhūtānapāyinī ||
children.translated_text: and the female was <s>Dakṣiṇā</s>, an inseparable portion of prosperity.
<s>Svāyambhuva</s>, full of joy, brought to his own house the son of his daughter, blazing with widespread radiance;

children.text: svāyambhuvo mudā yukto rucir jagrāha dakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Ruci</s> accepted <s>Dakṣiṇā</s>.

children.text: tāṃ kāmayānāṃ bhagavān uvāha yajuṣāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord, master of the yajus-formulas, married her, who desired him;
delighted in her when she was pleased, he begot twelve sons.

children.text: toṣaḥ pratoṣaḥ santoṣo bhadraḥ śāntir iḍaspatiḥ
children.translated_text: They were <s>Toṣa</s>, <s>Pratoṣa</s>, <s>Santoṣa</s>, <s>Bhadra</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, and <s>Iḍaspati</s>,

children.text: idhmaḥ kavir vibhuḥ svahnaḥ sudevo rocano dviṣaṭ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Idhma</s>, <s>Kavi</s>, <s>Vibhu</s>, <s>Svahna</s>, <s>Sudeva</s>, and <s>Rocana</s>: twelve in all.

children.text: tuṣitā nāma te devā āsan svāyambhuvāntare
children.translated_text: They were the gods called <s>Tuṣitas</s> in the age of <s>Svāyambhuva</s> <s>Manu</s>;
<s>Marīci</s> and others were the sages, and <s>Yajña</s> was lord of the hosts of gods.
<s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s> were the two mighty sons of <s>Manu</s>;
after that came the account of their sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons.
O dear one, <s>Manu</s> gave his daughter <s>Devahūti</s> to <s>Kardama</s>;
what concerns her you have mostly heard from me as I spoke.
The Blessed <s>Manu</s> gave <s>Prasūti</s> to <s>Dakṣa</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: prāyacchad yatkṛtaḥ sargas trilokyāṃ vitato mahān ||
children.translated_text: from whom a great creation spread throughout the three worlds.
The daughters of <s>Kardama</s>, already mentioned, were nine wives of brahmarṣis;
now hear from me as their offspring and progeny are being described.

children.text: patnī marīces tu kalā suṣuve kardamātmajā
children.translated_text: The wife of <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Kalā</s>, daughter of <s>Kardama</s>, gave birth

children.text: kaśyapaṃ pūrṇimānaṃ ca yayor āpūritaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Pūrṇiman</s>, by whom the world was filled.
<s>Pūrṇiman</s> begot <s>Viraja</s> and <s>Viśvaga</s>, O subduer of foes,

children.text: devakulyāṃ hareḥ pādaśaucād yābhūt sarid divaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Devakulyā</s>, who, from the washing of <s>Hari</s>'s feet, became the river of heaven.

children.text: atreḥ patny anasūyā trīñ jajñe suyaśasaḥ sutān
children.translated_text: <s>Anasūyā</s>, wife of <s>Atri</s>, bore three sons of excellent fame:
<s>Datta</s>, <s>Durvāsas</s>, and <s>Soma</s>, born from the Self, <s>Īśa</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
In the house of <s>Atri</s>, the foremost gods, causes of preservation, creation, and dissolution,

children.text: kiṃciccikīrṣavo jātā etad ākhyāhi me guro ||
children.translated_text: were born, intending to accomplish something. Tell me this, my teacher.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: brahmaṇā coditaḥ sṛṣṭāv atrir brahmavidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Urged by <s>Brahmā</s> toward creation, <s>Atri</s>, best of the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: saha patnyā yayāv ṛkṣaṃ kulādriṃ tapasi sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went with his wife to <s>Ṛkṣa</s>, the family mountain, resolved on austerity.
There, in a forest of flower-clusters, palāśa, and aśoka trees,
which resounded on every side with waters flowing from the <s>Nirvindhyā</s>,
the sage restrained his mind by <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) for a hundred years
and stood on one foot, beyond the pairs of opposites, feeding on air.

children.text: śaraṇaṃ taṃ prapadye 'haṃ ya eva jagadīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: He thought, "I take refuge in him who alone is the Lord of the universe;

children.text: prajām ātmasamāṃ mahyaṃ prayacchatv iti cintayan ||
children.translated_text: may he grant me offspring equal to myself."
Seeing the three worlds being scorched by the fire kindled with the fuel of his <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,

children.text: nirgatena muner mūrdhnaḥ samīkṣya prabhavas trayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which issued from the sage's head, the three mighty lords
with Apsarases, sages, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, and serpents,
went to his hermitage, their fame being spread abroad.
His mind illumined by the conjunction of their manifestation, the sage,
rising while still on one foot, saw the bulls among the gods.
Bowing down like a staff upon the ground, he stood before them with hands joined in reverence,

children.text: vṛṣahaṃsasuparṇasthān svaiḥ svaiś cihnaiś ca cihnitān ||
children.translated_text: as they were seated on the bull, the swan, and <s>Suparṇa</s>, and marked with their own emblems.
They acknowledged him with compassionate glances and smiling faces;
then, his eyes closed because they were overwhelmed by their radiance,
he fixed his mind upon them and praised them with joined hands,
addressing the most venerable beings in all the worlds with smooth and hymnic speech.
<s>Atri</s> said:
You assume bodies age after age through the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of māyā, divided for the creation, preservation, and dissolution of the universe.

children.text: te brahmaviṣṇugiriśāḥ praṇato 'smy ahaṃ vastebhyaḥ ka eva bhavatāṃ ma ihopahūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Giriśa</s>; I bow to you. Which one among you has been summoned here by me?

children.text: eko mayeha bhagavān vividhapradhānaiścittīkṛtaḥ prajananāya kathaṃ nu yūyam
children.translated_text: For begetting offspring I fixed my thought here on the one Blessed Lord in his various chief forms. How, then, have all of you

children.text: atrāgatās tanubhṛtāṃ manaso 'pi dūrādbrūta prasīdata mahān iha vismayo me ||
children.translated_text: come here from beyond even the mind of embodied beings? Speak, be gracious; great wonder has arisen in me.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā trayas te vibudharṣabhāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing his words, those three bulls among the gods

children.text: pratyāhuḥ ślakṣṇayā vācā prahasya tam ṛṣiṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: laughed and answered that seer with gentle speech, O lord.
The gods said:

children.text: yathā kṛtas te saṅkalpo bhāvyaṃ tenaiva nānyathā
children.translated_text: As your resolve has been made, so it must come to pass, and not otherwise.

children.text: satsaṅkalpasya te brahman yad vai dhyāyati te vayam ||
children.translated_text: Since your resolve is true, O <s>brahman</s>, what you have meditated upon is indeed us.
Therefore sons of yours, born as portions of us and famous throughout the worlds,

children.text: bhavitāro 'ṅga bhadraṃ te visrapsyanti ca te yaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will come into being, dear one. Blessing be upon you; they will also spread your fame.
Having thus granted the boon he desired, the lords of the gods returned,

children.text: sabhājitās tayoḥ samyag dampatyor miṣatos tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: after being duly honored by the two spouses as they looked on.

children.text: somo 'bhūd brahmaṇo 'ṃśena datto viṣṇos tu yogavit
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> was born as a portion of <s>Brahmā</s>, while <s>Datta</s>, the knower of yoga, was born as a portion of <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
<s>Durvāsas</s> was a portion of <s>Śaṅkara</s>. Now learn the descendants of <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.text: śraddhā tv aṅgirasaḥ patnī catasro 'sūta kanyakāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śraddhā</s>, wife of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, bore four daughters:

children.text: sinīvālī kuhū rākā caturthy anumatis tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sinīvālī</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>, <s>Rākā</s>, and, as the fourth, <s>Anumati</s>.
Her two other sons were renowned in the <s>Svārociṣa</s> interval:

children.text: utathyo bhagavān sākṣād brahmiṣṭhaś ca bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the venerable <s>Utathya</s> himself, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, most firmly established in <s>Brahman</s>.
<s>Pulastya</s> begot in his wife <s>Havirbhu</s> both <s>Agastya</s>,
who in another birth was <s>Dahrāgni</s>, and <s>Viśravas</s>, the great ascetic.

children.text: tasya yakṣapatir devaḥ kuberas tv iḍaviḍāsutaḥ
children.translated_text: His son by <s>Iḍaviḍā</s> was the divine <s>Kubera</s>, lord of the Yakṣas;
and by another wife were <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, and likewise <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: pulahasya gatir bhāryā trīn asūta satī sutān
children.translated_text: <s>Gati</s>, the faithful wife of <s>Pulaha</s>, bore three sons:
<s>Karmaśreṣṭha</s>, <s>Varīyāṃs</s>, and <s>Sahiṣṇu</s>, O greatly wise one.

children.text: krator api kriyā bhāryā vālakhilyān asūyata
children.translated_text: <s>Kriyā</s>, wife of <s>Kratu</s>, bore the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>,
sixty thousand seers blazing with the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.
In <s>Ūrjā</s> were born the sons of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, O subduer of foes,
the seven stainless <s>brahmarṣis</s> (Brahman-sages), headed by <s>Citraketu</s>.

children.text: citraketuḥ surociś ca virajā mitra eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Citraketu</s>, <s>Suroci</s>, <s>Virajā</s>, <s>Mitra</s>,
<s>Ulbaṇa</s>, <s>Vasubhṛdyāna</s>, <s>Dyumān</s>, and others headed by <s>Śakti</s>.

children.text: cittis tv atharvaṇaḥ patnī lebhe putraṃ dhṛtavratam
children.translated_text: <s>Citti</s>, wife of <s>Atharvan</s>, obtained a son firm in vows,

children.text: dadhyañcam aśvaśirasaṃ bhṛgor vaṃśaṃ nibodha me ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dadhyañc</s>, the horse-headed one. Now hear from me the lineage of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: bhṛguḥ khyātyāṃ mahābhāgaḥ patnyāṃ putrān ajījanat
children.translated_text: The greatly fortunate <s>Bhṛgu</s> begot sons in his wife <s>Khyāti</s>:

children.text: dhātāraṃ ca vidhātāraṃ śriyaṃ ca bhagavatparām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, and <s>Śrī</s>, who was devoted to the Blessed Lord.

children.text: āyatiṃ niyatiṃ caiva sute merus tayor adāt
children.translated_text: <s>Meru</s> gave his daughters <s>Āyati</s> and <s>Niyati</s> to those two;

children.text: tābhyāṃ tayor abhavatāṃ mṛkaṇḍaḥ prāṇa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: from those two women, to those two men, were born <s>Mṛkaṇḍa</s> and <s>Prāṇa</s>.
From <s>Mṛkaṇḍa</s> came <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, and from <s>Prāṇa</s> the sage <s>Vedaśirā</s>;

children.text: kaviś ca bhārgavo yasya bhagavān uśanā sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and there was <s>Kavi</s> of the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, whose son was the blessed <s>Uśanas</s>.

children.text: ta ete munayaḥ kṣattar lokān sargair abhāvayan
children.translated_text: These sages, O <s>Kṣattar</s>, brought the worlds into being through their creations.
This lineage of <s>Kardama</s>'s daughter has been related to you;
for one who hears it with faith, it at once removes sin and is supreme.

children.text: prasūtiṃ mānavīṃ dakṣa upayeme hy ajātmajaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dakṣa</s>, son of the unborn one, married <s>Prasūti</s>, daughter of <s>Manu</s>;
in her he begot sixteen daughters with spotless eyes.
The powerful one gave thirteen daughters to <s>Dharma</s>, and likewise one to <s>Agni</s>,
one to the <s>Pitṛs</s>, who were devoted, and one to <s>Bhava</s>, the cutter off of becoming.

children.text: śraddhā maitrī dayā śāntis tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiḥ kriyonnatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Maitrī</s>, <s>Dayā</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, <s>Unnati</s>,

children.text: buddhir medhā titikṣā hrīr mūrtir dharmasya patnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Titikṣā</s>, <s>Hrī</s>, and <s>Mūrti</s> were the wives of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: śraddhāsūta śubhaṃ maitrī prasādam abhayaṃ dayā
children.translated_text: <s>Śraddhā</s> bore <s>Śubha</s>; <s>Maitrī</s> bore <s>Prasāda</s>; <s>Dayā</s> bore <s>Abhaya</s>;

children.text: śāntiḥ sukhaṃ mudaṃ tuṣṭiḥ smayaṃ puṣṭir asūyata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śānti</s> bore <s>Sukha</s>; <s>Tuṣṭi</s> bore <s>Muda</s>; <s>Puṣṭi</s> bore <s>Smaya</s>.

children.text: yogaṃ kriyonnatir darpam arthaṃ buddhir asūyata
children.translated_text: <s>Kriyā</s> bore <s>Yoga</s>; <s>Unnati</s> bore <s>Darpa</s>; <s>Buddhi</s> bore <s>Artha</s>;

children.text: medhā smṛtiṃ titikṣā tu kṣemaṃ hrīḥ praśrayaṃ sutam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Medhā</s> bore <s>Smṛti</s>; <s>Titikṣā</s> bore <s>Kṣema</s>; and <s>Hrī</s> bore <s>Praśraya</s> as her son.
<s>Mūrti</s>, the source of all virtues, bore the two sages <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: yayor janmany ado viśvam abhyanandat sunirvṛtam
children.translated_text: At their birth this whole world rejoiced, deeply fulfilled.
Minds, the quarters, the winds, rivers, and mountains became serene.
In heaven drums and instruments sounded, and showers of flowers fell.
The satisfied sages praised them, and the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Kinnaras</s> sang.

children.text: nṛtyanti sma striyo devya āsīt paramamaṅgalam
children.translated_text: Divine women danced, and there was supreme auspiciousness.
All the gods, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, approached them with hymns of praise.
The gods said:

children.text: yo māyayā viracitaṃ nijayātmanīdaṃ khe rūpabhedam iva tatpraticakṣaṇāya
children.translated_text: Obeisance to that supreme Person who, by his own <s>māyā</s> (power of manifestation), fashioned this differentiated form within his own self, as if in space, so that it might be perceived,

children.text: etena dharmasadane ṛṣimūrtinādya prāduścakāra puruṣāya namaḥ parasmai ||
children.translated_text: and today has manifested it in this sage-form in the house of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: so 'yaṃ sthitivyatikaropaśamāya sṛṣṭānsattvena naḥ suragaṇān anumeyatattvaḥ
children.translated_text: May he, whose reality is inferred, look upon us hosts of gods, created from <s>sattva</s> for the pacification of disturbances in preservation,

children.text: dṛśyād adabhrakaruṇena vilokanena yacchrīniketam amalaṃ kṣipatāravindam ||
children.translated_text: with his abundant compassion, casting toward us his stainless lotus eye, the abode of <s>Śrī</s>.
Thus, dear one, the two Blessed Lords were praised by the hosts of gods.
Having granted them their sight and been worshiped, they went to <s>Gandhamādana</s>.

children.text: tāv imau vai bhagavato harer aṃśāv ihāgatau
children.translated_text: These two are indeed portions of the Blessed <s>Hari</s>, come here
as the two <s>Kṛṣṇas</s>, foremost among the <s>Yadus</s> and <s>Kurus</s>, to lighten the burden of the earth.
<s>Svāhā</s>, identifying herself with <s>Agni</s>, bore three sons:

children.text: pāvakaṃ pavamānaṃ ca śuciṃ ca hutabhojanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pāvaka</s>, <s>Pavamāna</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>, consumers of oblations.
From them arose forty-five fires,
and these, together with their fathers and grandfather, are the forty-nine fires.
In Vedic ritual, with the names by which speakers of <s>Brahman</s> designate them,

children.text: āgneyya iṣṭayo yajñe nirūpyante 'gnayas tu te ||
children.translated_text: these are the fires assigned in the <s>Āgneyī</s> offerings within the sacrifice.
The <s>Pitṛs</s> are the <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>, the <s>Barhiṣads</s>, the <s>Saumyas</s>, and the <s>Ājyapas</s>,
some with sacred fires and some without; their wife was <s>Svadhā</s>, daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>.

children.text: tebhyo dadhāra kanye dve vayunāṃ dhāriṇīṃ svadhā
children.translated_text: From them <s>Svadhā</s> bore two daughters, <s>Vayunā</s> and <s>Dhāriṇī</s>.
Both were speakers of <s>Brahman</s>, who had crossed to the far shore of knowledge and realization.

children.text: bhavasya patnī tu satī bhavaṃ devam anuvratā
children.translated_text: <s>Satī</s>, the wife of <s>Bhava</s>, was devoted to the god <s>Bhava</s>;

children.text: ātmanaḥ sadṛśaṃ putraṃ na lebhe guṇaśīlataḥ ||
children.translated_text: but she did not obtain a son equal to herself in virtue and character.
When her own father acted in an unfitting way, angered against innocent <s>Bhava</s>,
she, though still young, abandoned herself by herself, joined to <s>yoga</s>.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
Why did <s>Dakṣa</s>, affectionate toward his daughter, show hatred toward <s>Bhava</s>, the best of the well-conducted,
disregarding his own daughter <s>Satī</s>?
Who could hate that lord of moving and unmoving beings, free from enmity and peaceful in form,

children.text: ātmārāmaṃ kathaṃ dveṣṭi jagato daivataṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: self-delighting, the great deity of the world?

children.text: etad ākhyāhi me brahman jāmātuḥ śvaśurasya ca
children.translated_text: Tell me this, O <s>brahman</s>: between son-in-law and father-in-law,

children.text: vidveṣas tu yataḥ prāṇāṃs tatyaje dustyajān satī ||
children.translated_text: what was the hatred because of which <s>Satī</s> gave up her breaths, so hard to abandon?
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Long ago, at a sacrificial session of the creators of the universe, the great seers had assembled,
and so too all the hosts of immortals, with their attendants, the sages, and the fires.

children.text: tatra praviṣṭam ṛṣayo dṛṣṭvārkam iva rociṣā
children.translated_text: There the seers saw <s>Dakṣa</s> enter, shining like the sun,

children.text: bhrājamānaṃ vitimiraṃ kurvantaṃ tan mahat sadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: blazing and dispelling the darkness of that great assembly.
The members of the assembly rose from their seats, together with the fires,
except for <s>Viriñca</s> and <s>Śarva</s>, their minds seized by his brilliance.
The blessed <s>Dakṣa</s> was duly honored by the lords of the assembly;
having bowed to the unborn lord, teacher of the worlds, he sat down at his command.
Seeing <s>Mṛḍa</s> already seated, he could not bear that disrespect.

children.text: uvāca vāmaṃ cakṣurbhyām abhivīkṣya dahann iva ||
children.translated_text: Glaring at him with his eyes as if burning him, he spoke hostile words.
Hear me, O <s>brahmarṣis</s>, together with the gods and the fires.

children.text: sādhūnāṃ bruvato vṛttaṃ nājñānān na ca matsarāt ||
children.translated_text: I speak of the conduct of good people, not from ignorance and not from jealousy.
But this shameless one, destroyer of the fame of the guardians of the worlds,

children.text: sadbhir ācaritaḥ panthā yena stabdhena dūṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has defiled the path followed by the good, being stubborn.

children.text: eṣa me śiṣyatāṃ prāpto yan me duhitur agrahīt
children.translated_text: He has come under my discipleship, for he took my daughter's hand,
properly, before the <s>vipras</s> and the fire, as one would take <s>Sāvitrī</s>.
After taking the hand of my fawn-eyed girl, he, monkey-eyed as he is,
did not perform what was proper even by speech for one worthy of rising and salutation.
To this man of abandoned rites, impure, conceited, and breaker of boundaries,

children.text: anicchann apy adāṃ bālāṃ śūdrāyevośatīṃ giram ||
children.translated_text: I gave my young daughter unwillingly, like pure speech given to a <s>Śūdra</s>.
He wanders in terrible cremation grounds, surrounded by corpses and hosts of spirits,

children.text: aṭaty unmattavan nagno vyuptakeśo hasan rudan ||
children.translated_text: like a madman, naked, with disheveled hair, laughing and weeping.
He bathes in funeral-pyre ashes, wears garlands of corpses and ornaments of bones.
Though called <s>Śiva</s>, he is inauspicious, intoxicated, dear to the intoxicated,
lord of the <s>Pramathas</s>, whose selves consist solely of darkness.
To that lord of madness, devoid of purity and evil-hearted,

children.text: dattā bata mayā sādhvī codite parameṣṭhinā ||
children.translated_text: alas, I gave my virtuous daughter, urged on by <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having reviled <s>Giriśa</s> in this way while he remained unopposed,
<s>Dakṣa</s> then sipped water and, angry, began to curse him.
But at this sacrifice of the gods, this <s>Bhava</s>, together with <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and the rest,

children.text: saha bhāgaṃ na labhatāṃ devair devagaṇādhamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: must not receive a share along with the gods, this lowest one among the hosts of gods.

children.text: niṣidhyamānaḥ sa sadasyamukhyair dakṣo giritrāya visṛjya śāpam
children.translated_text: Though the chief members of the assembly forbade him, <s>Dakṣa</s> cast a curse upon <s>Giritra</s>.

children.text: tasmād viniṣkramya vivṛddhamanyur jagāma kauravya nijaṃ niketanam ||
children.translated_text: Then, leaving that place, his anger grown great, he went, O <s>Kauravya</s>, to his own dwelling.
When <s>Nandīśvara</s>, foremost among the followers of <s>Giriśa</s>, learned of the curse, he was tainted red with anger,

children.text: dakṣāya śāpaṃ visasarja dāruṇaṃ ye cānvamodaṃs tadavācyatāṃ dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he hurled a terrible curse at <s>Dakṣa</s> and at those brahmins who had approved his unspeakable words.

children.text: ya etan martyam uddiśya bhagavaty apratidruhi
children.translated_text: Whoever, with reference to this mortal body, acts hostilely toward the Blessed Lord, who is never hostile,

children.text: druhyaty ajñaḥ pṛthagdṛṣṭis tattvato vimukho bhavet ||
children.translated_text: that ignorant man, seeing things as separate, shall be turned away from reality.
Attached to houses full of false <s>dharma</s>, from desire for village pleasures,
with his understanding ruined by Vedic literalism, he elaborates a system of ritual action.
With an intellect bent on what is other than the supreme, forgetting the soul's true course, he is an animal.
May that <s>Dakṣa</s>, lusting after women, very soon become goat-faced.
This dull man has his notion of knowledge fixed in ignorance, made of ritual action.
And may those here who follow this reviler of <s>Śarva</s> continue wandering in saṃsāra.
By the flowery speech of the Veda, with its abundant scent of honey,
may the enemies of <s>Hara</s>, their selves churned and agitated, fall into delusion.
May the twice-born, wearing learning, austerity, and vows only for a livelihood, become eaters of everything.
Delighting in wealth, body, and senses, may they wander here as beggars.

children.text: tasyaivaṃ vadataḥ śāpaṃ śrutvā dvijakulāya vai
children.translated_text: Hearing him thus pronounce a curse upon the family of twice-borns,
<s>Bhṛgu</s> cast back a curse, an irresistible brahminical rod of punishment.

children.text: bhavavratadharā ye ca ye ca tān samanuvratāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who maintain the vows of <s>Bhava</s>, and those who follow them in those vows,
let them become heretics, opponents of true scripture.
Having lost purity, with deluded minds, wearing matted hair, ashes, and bones,
let them enter initiation to <s>Śiva</s>, where liquor is treated as divine.

children.text: brahma ca brāhmaṇāṃś caiva yad yūyaṃ parinindatha
children.translated_text: Since you revile <s>Brahman</s> and the brahmins themselves,

children.text: setuṃ vidhāraṇaṃ puṃsām ataḥ pāṣaṇḍam āśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the restraining bridge for human beings, therefore you have taken refuge in heresy.

children.text: eṣa eva hi lokānāṃ śivaḥ panthāḥ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: This alone is the auspicious eternal path for the worlds,
which the ancients followed, and for which <s>Janārdana</s> is the authority.

children.text: tad brahma paramaṃ śuddhaṃ satāṃ vartma sanātanam
children.translated_text: That supreme, pure <s>Brahman</s> is the eternal path of the good.

children.text: vigarhya yāta pāṣaṇḍaṃ daivaṃ vo yatra bhūtarāṭ ||
children.translated_text: Reviling it, go to heresy, where the lord of beings is your deity.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: tasyaivaṃ vadataḥ śāpaṃ bhṛgoḥ sa bhagavān bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Bhṛgu</s> was speaking this curse, that Blessed Lord <s>Bhava</s>

children.text: niścakrāma tataḥ kiṃcid vimanā iva sānugaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then went away somewhat downcast, together with his followers.
Those creators of the universe also performed the sacrificial session for a thousand years,
O mighty archer, where <s>Hari</s>, the lord of sacrifice, was worshiped.
Having bathed in the avabhṛtha bath where the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is joined by the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: virajenātmanā sarve svaṃ svaṃ dhāma yayus tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: all of them, with purified selves, then went each to his own abode.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: sadā vidviṣator evaṃ kālo vai dhriyamāṇayoḥ
children.translated_text: As the son-in-law and the father-in-law thus held fast to mutual hatred,
a very long time indeed passed by between them.
But when <s>Dakṣa</s> had been consecrated by <s>Brahmā</s>, the supreme lord,
to rulership over all the Prajāpatis, pride arose in him.

children.text: iṣṭvā sa vājapeyena brahmiṣṭhān abhibhūya ca
children.translated_text: Having sacrificed with the <s>Vājapeya</s>, and having surpassed the most brahminical ones,
he undertook the supreme sacrifice called the <s>Bṛhaspatisava</s>.
At it were all the brahmin-sages, divine sages, ancestors, and deities,
with auspicious rites performed, and their wives together with their husbands.
Hearing in the sky the talk of the sky-goers,
the goddess <s>Satī</s> <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> learned of the great festival of her father's sacrifice.
Then she saw the excellent wives of the lesser gods going from all directions,
traveling in aerial cars with their beloveds, with golden necklaces and fine garments,
near her own dwelling, their eyes restless and their earrings polished.
Out of eagerness she addressed her husband, the god, the lord of beings.
<s>Satī</s> said:

children.text: prajāpates te śvaśurasya sāmprataṃ niryāpito yajñamahotsavaḥ kila
children.translated_text: The great sacrificial festival of your father-in-law, the Prajāpati, has now been set in motion, it is said.
