children.text: vayaṃ ca tatrābhisarāma vāma te yady arthitāmī vibudhā vrajanti hi ||
children.translated_text: Let us also go there, O fair one, if these gods are indeed going as invited guests.

children.text: tasmin bhaginyo mama bhartṛbhiḥ svakair dhruvaṃ gamiṣyanti suhṛddidṛkṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: There my sisters, with their own husbands, will surely go, wishing to see their relatives.

children.text: ahaṃ ca tasmin bhavatābhikāmaye sahopanītaṃ paribarham arhitum ||
children.translated_text: And I too desire to accept there, together with you, the honor and gifts that have been brought.

children.text: tatra svasṝr me nanu bhartṛsaṃmitā mātṛṣvasṝḥ klinnadhiyaṃ ca mātaram
children.translated_text: There I shall see my sisters with their husbands, my mother's sisters, and my mother whose heart is tender,

children.text: drakṣye cirotkaṇṭhamanā maharṣibhir unnīyamānaṃ ca mṛḍādhvaradhvajam ||
children.translated_text: while my mind longs after so long a time, and, O <s>Mṛḍa</s>, the sacrificial banner being raised by the great sages.

children.text: tvayy etad āścaryam ajātmamāyayā vinirmitaṃ bhāti guṇatrayātmakam
children.translated_text: In you, this wondrous universe, fashioned by unborn self-power, appears as consisting of the three guṇas.

children.text: tathāpy ahaṃ yoṣid atattvavic ca te dīnā didṛkṣe bhava me bhavakṣitim ||
children.translated_text: Yet I am a woman and do not know the truth; poor as I am, O <s>Bhava</s>, I wish to see the place of my birth.

children.text: paśya prayāntīr abhavānyayoṣito 'py alaṃkṛtāḥ kāntasakhā varūthaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Look, O <s>Bhava</s>, even other women are going, adorned, with their beloved companions, in groups.

children.text: yāsāṃ vrajadbhiḥ śitikaṇṭha maṇḍitaṃ nabho vimānaiḥ kalahaṃsapāṇḍubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: As they travel, O blue-throated one, the sky is adorned with aerial cars white as royal swans.

children.text: kathaṃ sutāyāḥ pitṛgehakautukaṃ niśamya dehaḥ suravarya neṅgate
children.translated_text: Hearing of the excitement at her father's house, how could a daughter's body not stir, O best of gods?

children.text: anāhutā apy abhiyanti sauhṛdaṃ bhartur guror dehakṛtaś ca ketanam ||
children.translated_text: Even uninvited, people go to the home of a friend, a husband, a teacher, or the father who gave them the body.

children.text: tan me prasīdedam amartya vāñchitaṃ kartuṃ bhavān kāruṇiko batārhati
children.translated_text: Therefore, immortal one, please grant this wish of mine; surely you, being compassionate, ought to do it.
You, whose vision is vast, have assigned me as half of your own self; favor me when I ask.
The sage said:

children.text: evaṃ giritraḥ priyayābhibhāṣitaḥ pratyabhyadhatta prahasan suhṛtpriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by his beloved, <s>Giritra</s>, smiling and dear to his friends, replied.

children.text: saṃsmārito marmabhidaḥ kuvāgiṣūn yān āha ko viśvasṛjāṃ samakṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: She was reminded of the arrows of wicked speech that pierce the vitals, which he had spoken before the creators of the universe.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: tvayoditaṃ śobhanam eva śobhane anāhutā apy abhiyanti bandhuṣu
children.translated_text: What you have said is indeed proper, fair one; even uninvited, people do go to relatives,
provided that their vision has not been made fault-finding by the stronger pride of bodily identity and by anger.
Learning, austerity, wealth, beauty, age, and lineage are the six qualities of the good, but in others who are very bad,

children.text: smṛtau hatāyāṃ bhṛtamānadurdṛśaḥ stabdhā na paśyanti hi dhāma bhūyasām ||
children.translated_text: when memory is destroyed, those whose sight is spoiled by cherished pride become stiff and do not see the greatness of the greater.
Out of regard for kinship one should not go to the houses of such people, whose selves are unsteady,
who look upon guests with crooked minds, raised eyebrows, and eyes full of intolerance.

children.text: tathāribhir na vyathate śilīmukhaiḥ śete 'rditāṅgo hṛdayena dūyatā
children.translated_text: A person does not suffer so much from enemies, though his body is pierced by arrows and he lies afflicted, grieving in heart,

children.text: svānāṃ yathā vakradhiyāṃ duruktibhir divāniśaṃ tapyati marmatāḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as he burns day and night, struck in the vitals by the harsh words of his own crooked-minded people.

children.text: vyaktaṃ tvam utkṛṣṭagateḥ prajāpateḥ priyātmajānām asi subhru me matā
children.translated_text: Clearly, fine-browed one, I know that you are among the beloved daughters of the <s>Prajāpati</s> whose course is exalted;

children.text: tathāpi mānaṃ na pituḥ prapatsyase madāśrayāt kaḥ paritapyate yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless you will not receive honor from your father, because of your connection with me, over which he is distressed.
With his heart burning and his senses afflicted by the excellences of those whose understanding witnesses the Person,

children.text: akalpa eṣām adhiroḍhum añjasā paraṃ padaṃ dveṣṭi yathāsurā harim ||
children.translated_text: he is unable readily to ascend their supreme state; he hates it, as the demons hate <s>Hari</s>.
Rising to meet, showing deference, and offering salutations to one another are rightly prescribed, gentle-waisted one,

children.text: prājñaiḥ parasmai puruṣāya cetasā guhāśayāyaiva na dehamānine ||
children.translated_text: by the wise, for the supreme Person who abides in the cave of the heart, not for one who is proud of the body.

children.text: sattvaṃ viśuddhaṃ vasudevaśabditaṃ yad īyate tatra pumān apāvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Pure sattva is called <s>Vasudeva</s>; when it is illumined, the Person is uncovered there,

children.text: sattve ca tasmin bhagavān vāsudevo hy adhokṣajo me namasā vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and in that sattva the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, is worshiped by me with reverence.

children.text: tat te nirīkṣyo na pitāpi dehakṛd dakṣo mama dviṭ tadanuvratāś ca ye
children.translated_text: Therefore you should regard <s>Dakṣa</s> not even as your father, though he produced your body; he hates me, and so do those who follow him,

children.text: yo viśvasṛgyajñagataṃ varoru mām anāgasaṃ durvacasākarot tiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: he who, at the sacrifice before the creators of the universe, fair-thighed one, covered me, though innocent, with evil speech.

children.text: yadi vrajiṣyasy atihāya madvaco bhadraṃ bhavatyā na tato bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: If you go, disregarding my word, no good will come to you from that;

children.text: saṃbhāvitasya svajanāt parābhavo yadā sa sadyo maraṇāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: for humiliation from one's own people, when one has been honored, at once becomes fit to bring about death.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: etāvad uktvā virarāma śaṅkaraḥ patnyaṅganāśaṃ hy ubhayatra cintayan
children.translated_text: Having said only this, <s>Śaṅkara</s> fell silent, thinking on both sides about the destruction of his wife's body.

children.text: suhṛddidṛkṣuḥ pariśaṅkitā bhavān niṣkrāmatī nirviśatī dvidhāsa sā ||
children.translated_text: Longing to see her relatives yet afraid, sir, as she went out and came back, she was divided in two.
Her mind pained because her wish to see her kin was obstructed, weeping from affection and overwhelmed by tears,

children.text: bhavaṃ bhavāny apratipūruṣaṃ ruṣā pradhakṣyatīvaikṣata jātavepathuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhavānī</s>, trembling, looked angrily at <s>Bhava</s>, her unequalled husband, as if she would burn him up.

children.text: tato viniḥśvasya satī vihāya taṃ śokena roṣeṇa ca dūyatā hṛdā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Satī</s>, sighing, left him, her heart tormented by grief and anger,

children.text: pitror agāt straiṇavimūḍhadhīr gṛhān premṇātmano yo 'rdham adāt satāṃ priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, her woman's understanding bewildered, went to her parents' house, leaving the beloved of the good who had given her half of his own body out of love.

children.text: tām anvagacchan drutavikramāṃ satīm ekāṃ trinetrānucarāḥ sahasraśaḥ
children.translated_text: The followers of the three-eyed lord, thousands of them, followed <s>Satī</s> as she strode swiftly and alone,
together with attendants and Yakṣas such as <s>Maṇimān</s> and <s>Mada</s>, placing the lordly bull in front and hurrying without anxiety.
With a mynah bird, ball, mirror, lotus, white parasol, fan, garlands, and other things,

children.text: gītāyanair dundubhiśaṅkhaveṇubhir vṛṣendram āropya viṭaṅkitā yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with songs, chants, kettledrums, conches, and flutes, they set her on the lordly bull and went in ornamented splendor.
She entered the sacrificial ground, filled with the loud sound of Vedic recitation and the vigorous bustle of the sacrifice, attended everywhere by Brahmin seers and by gods,
where vessels had been set out, made of clay, wood, iron, gold, darbha grass, and hide.

children.text: tām āgatāṃ tatra na kaścanādriyad vimānitāṃ yajñakṛto bhayājjanaḥ
children.translated_text: When she arrived there, no one among the people showed honor to her, who had been slighted, out of fear of the sacrificer,

children.text: ṛte svasṝr vai jananīṃ ca sādarāḥ premāśrukaṇṭhyaḥ pariṣasvajur mudā ||
children.translated_text: except that her sisters and mother, respectful and with throats choked by tears of love, joyfully embraced her.

children.text: saudaryasampraśnasamarthavārtayā mātrā ca mātṛṣvasṛbhiś ca sādaram
children.translated_text: With questions from her sisters about one another's welfare and suitable conversation, and respectfully by her mother and maternal aunts,

children.text: dattāṃ saparyāṃ varam āsanaṃ ca sā nādatta pitrāpratinanditā satī ||
children.translated_text: although worship, an excellent seat, and welcome had been offered, <s>Satī</s> did not accept them, because she had not been greeted by her father.

children.text: arudrabhāgaṃ tam avekṣya cādhvaraṃ pitrā ca deve kṛtahelanaṃ vibhau
children.translated_text: Seeing that sacrifice without a share for <s>Rudra</s>, and seeing that her father had shown contempt toward the god, the all-powerful lord,

children.text: anādṛtā yajñasadasy adhīśvarī cukopa lokān iva dhakṣyatī ruṣā ||
children.translated_text: the sovereign lady, disregarded in the sacrificial assembly, grew angry, as if in wrath she would burn the worlds.
With speech spoiled by indignation, the goddess rebuked the hater of <s>Śiva</s>, proud from the labor of the smoky path,

children.text: svatejasā bhūtagaṇān samutthitān nigṛhya devī jagato 'bhiśṛṇvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: after restraining by her own splendor the hosts of beings who had risen up, while the world listened.
The goddess said:

children.text: na yasya loke 'sty atiśāyanaḥ priyas tathāpriyo dehabhṛtāṃ priyātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: In this world there is no one especially dear, nor likewise anyone hateful, to him who is the dear Self of embodied beings;

children.text: tasmin samastātmani muktavairake ṛte bhavantaṃ katamaḥ pratīpayet ||
children.translated_text: toward him, the self of all and free from enmity, who except you would act with hostility?

children.text: doṣān pareṣāṃ hi guṇeṣu sādhavo gṛhṇanti kecin na bhavādṛśo dvija
children.translated_text: Some good people indeed take even others' faults as virtues, but not a twice-born person like you;

children.text: guṇāṃś ca phalgūn bahulīkariṣṇavo mahattamās teṣv avidad bhavān agham ||
children.translated_text: the greatest magnify even slight virtues, yet you have discovered evil in them.

children.text: nāścaryam etad yad asatsu sarvadā mahadvinindā kuṇapātmavādiṣu
children.translated_text: It is no wonder that among the wicked, who always speak of the corpse-like body as the self, there is censure of the great;

children.text: serṣyaṃ mahāpūruṣapādapāṃsubhir nirastatejaḥsu tad eva śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: for in those whose splendor has been destroyed by envy at the dust of great persons' feet, that very conduct is fitting.

children.text: yad dvyakṣaraṃ nāma gireritaṃ nṛṇāṃ sakṛt prasaṅgād agham āśu hanti tat
children.translated_text: That two-syllabled name, uttered by the tongue of men even once by chance, quickly destroys sin;

children.text: pavitrakīrtiṃ tam alaṅghyaśāsanaṃ bhavān aho dveṣṭi śivaṃ śivetaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Śiva</s>, of purifying fame and untransgressable command, you, inauspicious one, astonishingly hate.
His lotus feet are served by the bee-like minds of the great, who seek the honey-wine of the rasa of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: lokasya yad varṣati cāśiṣo 'rthinas tasmai bhavān druhyati viśvabandhave ||
children.translated_text: and he showers blessings on the world and on those who seek their aims; you bear malice toward him, the friend of the universe.

children.text: kiṃvā śivākhyam aśivaṃ na vidus tvad anye brahmādayas tam avakīrya jaṭāḥ śmaśāne
children.translated_text: Or do others than you, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, not know that the one called <s>Śiva</s> is not inauspicious, though he scatters his matted locks in the cremation ground?

children.text: tanmālyabhasmanṛkapāly avasat piśācair ye mūrdhabhir dadhati taccaraṇāvasṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: They bear upon their heads what has been cast off from his feet, with his garland, ashes, human skull, and the spirits among whom he dwells.

children.text: karṇau pidhāya nirayād yad akalpa īśe dharmāvitary asṛṇibhir nṛbhir asyamāne
children.translated_text: When the lord, the giver of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), is being reviled by harsh men, one who is powerless should cover his ears and leave, to avoid hell.

children.text: chindyāt prasahya ruśatīm asatīṃ prabhuś cejjihvām asūn api tato visṛjet sa dharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if he is capable, he should forcibly cut out the slanderous, false tongue, and then even give up his own life; that is <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: atas tavotpannam idaṃ kalevaraṃ na dhārayiṣye śitikaṇṭhagarhiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore I will not bear this body, born from you, the reviler of <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s>.

children.text: jagdhasya mohāddhi viśuddhim andhaso jugupsitasyoddharaṇaṃ pracakṣate ||
children.translated_text: For people prescribe the vomiting up of impure food that has been eaten in delusion and has become detestable.

children.text: na vedavādān anuvartate matiḥ sva eva loke ramato mahāmuneḥ
children.translated_text: The mind of the great sage, delighting in his own world, does not merely follow the declarations of the Veda.

children.text: yathā gatir devamanuṣyayoḥ pṛthak sva eva dharme na paraṃ kṣipet sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as the courses of gods and humans are distinct, one established in his own <s>dharma</s> should not disparage another.

children.text: karma pravṛttaṃ ca nivṛttam apy ṛtaṃ vede vivicyobhayaliṅgam āśritam
children.translated_text: The Veda distinguishes action that is engaged in and action that is renounced, both true, taking each as marked by its own signs.

children.text: virodhi tad yaugapadaikakartari dvayaṃ tathā brahmaṇi karma narcchati ||
children.translated_text: Since the two are opposed, they cannot belong simultaneously to one agent; so too, ritual action does not reach <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: mā vaḥ padavyaḥ pitar asmadāsthitā yā yajñaśālāsu na dhūmavartmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Father, may the paths followed by us not become yours, those paths that are not reached in sacrificial halls by the ways of smoke,
praised by enemies satisfied with that food, whose marks are hidden, and which are served by avadhūtas.

children.text: naitena dehena hare kṛtāgaso dehodbhavenālam alaṃ kujanmanā
children.translated_text: Enough of this body of mine, born from the body of one who has offended <s>Hara</s>; enough of this low birth.

children.text: vrīḍā mamābhūt kujanaprasaṅgatas tajjanma dhig yo mahatām avadyakṛt ||
children.translated_text: Shame has come upon me from association with a low person; fie on that birth which brings reproach upon the great.

children.text: gotraṃ tvadīyaṃ bhagavān vṛṣadhvajo dākṣāyaṇīty āha yadā sudurmanāḥ
children.translated_text: When the Blessed <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>, deeply distressed, calls me <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>, as belonging to your lineage,

children.text: vyapetanarmasmitam āśu tadāhaṃ vyutsrakṣya etat kuṇapaṃ tvadaṅgajam ||
children.translated_text: then at once, bereft of playful smiles, I shall cast off this corpse produced from your limb.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: ity adhvare dakṣam anūdya śatruhan kṣitāv udīcīṃ niṣasāda śāntavāk
children.translated_text: Having thus denounced <s>Dakṣa</s> at the sacrifice, O slayer of foes, she sat down on the ground facing north, with speech stilled.

children.text: spṛṣṭvā jalaṃ pītadukūlasaṃvṛtā nimīlya dṛgyogapathaṃ samāviśat ||
children.translated_text: Touching water, covered with a yellow garment, she closed her eyes and entered the path of yoga.

children.text: kṛtvā samānāv anilau jitāsanā sodānam utthāpya ca nābhicakrataḥ
children.translated_text: Having made the two breaths equal, mastered her seat, and raised the udāna breath from the navel wheel,

children.text: śanair hṛdi sthāpya dhiyorasi sthitaṃ kaṇṭhād bhruvor madhyam aninditānayat ||
children.translated_text: she slowly placed it in the heart; then, by her mind, she brought what was set in the chest from the throat to the space between the brows.

children.text: evaṃ svadehaṃ mahatāṃ mahīyasā muhuḥ samāropitam aṅkam ādarāt
children.translated_text: Thus the high-minded <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>, wishing to abandon her own body, which had often been placed with honor on the lap

children.text: jihāsatī dakṣaruṣā manasvinī dadhāra gātreṣv anilāgnidhāraṇām ||
children.translated_text: by the greatest of the great, because of anger toward <s>Dakṣa</s>, held within her limbs the concentration on wind and fire.

children.text: tataḥ svabhartuś caraṇāmbujāsavaṃ jagadguroś cintayatī na cāparam
children.translated_text: Then, thinking of the nectar of the lotus feet of her husband, the teacher of the world, and of nothing else,

children.text: dadarśa deho hatakalmaṣaḥ satī sadyaḥ prajajvāla samādhijāgninā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Satī</s>, her body freed from sin, saw inwardly, and at once her body blazed up with the fire born of samādhi.

children.text: tat paśyatāṃ khe bhuvi cādbhutaṃ mahaddhā heti vādaḥ sumahān ajāyata
children.translated_text: As those in the sky and on earth watched that great wonder, a very great cry of 'alas, alas' arose:

children.text: hanta priyā daivatamasya devī jahāv asūn kena satī prakopitā ||
children.translated_text: Alas! How was <s>Satī</s> provoked, that the beloved goddess of the most divine god gave up her life?

children.text: aho anātmyaṃ mahad asya paśyata prajāpater yasya carācaraṃ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, behold the great soullessness of this <s>Prajāpati</s>, whose offspring are all moving and unmoving beings.

children.text: jahāv asūn yadvimatātmajā satī manasvinī mānam abhīkṣṇam arhati ||
children.translated_text: Because of his contempt, his own daughter <s>Satī</s>, high-minded and always worthy of honor, gave up her life.

children.text: so 'yaṃ durmarṣahṛdayo brahmadhruk ca loke 'pakīrtiṃ mahatīm avāpsyati
children.translated_text: This man, intolerant at heart and hostile to <s>Brahman</s>, will obtain great infamy in the world,

children.text: yadaṅgajāṃ svāṃ puruṣadviḍ udyatāṃ na pratyaṣedhan mṛtaye 'parādhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: because, hating the Supreme Person, he did not restrain his own daughter, born from his body, when she rose to die though without offense.

children.text: vadaty evaṃ jane satyā dṛṣṭvāsutyāgam adbhutam
children.translated_text: As the people were speaking in this way after seeing <s>Satī</s>'s wondrous abandonment of life,
her attendants rose up with weapons raised to kill <s>Dakṣa</s>.

children.text: teṣām āpatatāṃ vegaṃ niśāmya bhagavān bhṛguḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the force of those rushing upon him, the blessed <s>Bhṛgu</s>
offered an oblation in the southern fire with a Yajus that destroys the destroyers of sacrifice.
As the adhvaryu priest was making the offering, gods sprang forth with power,

children.text: ṛbhavo nāma tapasā somaṃ prāptāḥ sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thousands of them, called <s>Ṛbhus</s>, who had attained Soma through austerity.
By them, armed with firebrands, all the <s>Pramathas</s>, together with the <s>Guhyakas</s>,
were struck down by blazing brahminical splendor and fled to the quarters.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: bhavo bhavānyā nidhanaṃ prajāpater asatkṛtāyā avagamya nāradāt
children.translated_text: When <s>Bhava</s> learned from <s>Nārada</s> of the death of <s>Bhavānī</s>, who had been dishonored by the <s>Prajāpati</s>,

children.text: svapārṣadasainyaṃ ca tadadhvararbhubhir vidrāvitaṃ krodham apāram ādadhe ||
children.translated_text: and that his own army of attendants had been routed at that sacrifice by the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, he took on boundless anger.

children.text: kruddhaḥ sudaṣṭauṣṭhapuṭaḥ sa dhūrjaṭir jaṭāṃ taḍidvahnisaṭograrociṣam
children.translated_text: Furious, biting hard upon his lips, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, with matted hair blazing fiercely like lightning and fire,

children.text: utkṛtya rudraḥ sahasotthito hasan gambhīranādo visasarja tāṃ bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: suddenly rose up laughing with a deep roar, tore out a lock of hair, and hurled it upon the ground.

children.text: tato 'tikāyas tanuvā spṛśan divaṃ sahasrabāhur ghanaruk trisūryadṛk
children.translated_text: Then there appeared one of vast body, touching heaven with his form, thousand-armed, dark as a cloud, with three sun-like eyes,
with terrible fangs, hair blazing like fire, garlanded with skulls, and holding many kinds of raised weapons.

children.text: taṃ kiṃ karomīti gṛṇantam āha baddhāñjaliṃ bhagavān bhūtanāthaḥ
children.translated_text: To him, who stood with folded hands and said, 'What shall I do?', the blessed <s>Bhūtanātha</s> said:

children.text: dakṣaṃ sayajñaṃ jahi madbhaṭānāṃ tvam agraṇī rudra bhaṭāṃśako me ||
children.translated_text: Kill <s>Dakṣa</s> together with the sacrifice. You are the foremost of my warriors, O <s>Rudra</s>, a portion of my own troop.

children.text: ājñapta evaṃ kupitena manyunā sa devadevaṃ paricakrame vibhum
children.translated_text: Thus commanded by the anger of the wrathful one, he circumambulated the mighty god of gods.

children.text: mene tadātmānam asaṅgaraṃhasā mahīyasāṃ tāta sahaḥ sahiṣṇum ||
children.translated_text: Then, by his irresistible speed, he considered himself able, dear one, to withstand even the power of the greatest.

children.text: anvīyamānaḥ sa tu rudrapārṣadair bhṛśaṃ nadadbhir vyanadat subhairavam
children.translated_text: Followed by <s>Rudra</s>'s attendants, who roared loudly, he gave a most terrifying roar.
Raising a trident deadly even to the ender of the world, he rushed forward, his feet adorned with resounding ornaments.

children.text: athartvijo yajamānaḥ sadasyāḥ kakubhyudīcyāṃ prasamīkṣya reṇum
children.translated_text: Then the priests, the sacrificer, and the assembly members saw dust in the northern quarter,

children.text: tamaḥ kimetatkuta etadrajo 'bhūditi dvijā dvijapatnyaśca dadhyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the twice-born men and their wives thought, 'What is this darkness? From where has this dust arisen?'

children.text: vātā na vānti na hi santi dasyavaḥ prācīnabarhir jīvati hogradaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: The winds are not blowing, nor indeed are there bandits; <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>, fierce in punishment, is still alive.

children.text: gāvo na kālyanta idaṃ kuto rajo loko 'dhunā kiṃ pralayāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: The cows are not moving about. Where has this dust come from? Is the world now being prepared for dissolution?

children.text: prasūtimiśrāḥ striya udvignacittā ūcur vipāko vṛjinasyaiva tasya
children.translated_text: Women, some pregnant and some with children, their minds disturbed, said, "This is indeed the ripening of that very sin:

children.text: yat paśyantīnāṃ duhitṝṇāṃ prajeśaḥ sutāṃ satīm avadadhyāvanāgām ||
children.translated_text: that before the eyes of his daughters, the lord of creatures disregarded his blameless daughter <s>Satī</s>."
He who at the time of the end has scattered his mass of matted hair, with the chief elephants of the quarters fixed on the points of his own trident,
stretches out and dances, raising arms like standards with weapons lifted, while his loud wild laughter splits the directions like thunder.

children.text: amarṣayitvā tam asahyatejasaṃ manyuplutaṃ durnirīkṣyaṃ bhrukuṭyā
children.translated_text: Having provoked him, of unbearable splendor, flooded with anger, hard to look upon because of his frown,

children.text: karāladaṃṣṭrābhir udastabhāgaṇaṃ syāt svasti kiṃ kopayato vidhātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: casting the hosts of heavenly bodies upward with his dreadful tusks, what welfare can there be when such an ordainer is angered?

children.text: bahv evam udvignadṛśocyamāne janena dakṣasya muhur mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: As the people, with anxious eyes, repeatedly spoke much in this way about great-souled <s>Dakṣa</s>,

children.text: utpetur utpātatamāḥ sahasraśo bhayāvahā divi bhūmau ca paryak ||
children.translated_text: thousands of most dreadful omens, fear-inspiring, arose on every side in heaven and on earth.

children.text: tāvat sa rudrānucarair mahāmakho nānāyudhair vāmanakair udāyudhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Just then that great sacrifice was surrounded by the attendants of <s>Rudra</s>, holding raised weapons, dwarfish, with many weapons,
tawny and yellow-brown, with bellies and faces like crocodiles, rushing all around, O <s>Vidura</s>.
Some broke the eastern structure, and others the wives' hall;
they broke the assembly hall, the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> hall, the sacrificial enclosure, and the kitchen.
Some smashed the sacrificial vessels, and others extinguished the fires;
some urinated in the pits, and some broke apart the girdles of the altar.

children.text: abādhanta munīn anye eke patnīr atarjayan
children.translated_text: Others harassed the sages; some threatened the wives;
others seized the gods who had come near and were fleeing.
<s>Maṇimān</s> bound <s>Bhṛgu</s>; <s>Vīrabhadra</s> bound the Prajāpati;
<s>Caṇḍeśa</s> seized the god <s>Pūṣan</s>, and <s>Nandīśvara</s> seized <s>Bhaga</s>.
Seeing this, all the priests, the assembly members, and the gods present in the assembly,
being violently beaten by them with stones, fled in many directions.
In the assembly Blessed <s>Bhava</s> plucked out the beard of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, who was pouring oblations with the ladle in his hand,
for <s>Bhṛgu</s> had laughed while showing his beard.

children.text: bhagasya netre bhagavān pātitasya ruṣā bhuvi
children.translated_text: In anger he tore out the eyes of <s>Bhaga</s>, who had been thrown to the ground,
because <s>Bhaga</s>, seated in the assembly, had signaled encouragement with his eyes to the one who was cursing.

children.text: pūṣṇo hy apātayad dantān kāliṅgasya yathā balaḥ
children.translated_text: He knocked out the teeth of <s>Pūṣan</s>, just as <s>Bala</s> had done to the king of <s>Kaliṅga</s>,
because, when the venerable one was being cursed, <s>Pūṣan</s> had laughed, showing his teeth.
Mounting the chest of <s>Dakṣa</s>, with a sharp-edged weapon,

children.text: chindann api tad uddhartuṃ nāśaknot tryambakas tadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tryambaka</s> tried to cut off his head, but at that time he could not lift it away.
Even with weapons furnished with missiles, <s>Hara</s> could not pierce his skin;

children.text: vismayaṃ param āpanno dadhyau paśupatiś ciram ||
children.translated_text: filled with supreme astonishment, <s>Paśupati</s> pondered for a long time.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā saṃjñapanaṃ yogaṃ paśūnāṃ sa patir makhe
children.translated_text: Seeing the sacrificial method of slaughter used for animals in the sacrifice,
that lord removed the head from the body of the sacrificer, the sacrificial animal, by that very method.

children.text: sādhuvādas tadā teṣāṃ karma tat tasya paśyatām
children.translated_text: Then praise arose among those who were watching that deed of his,
among the <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and others; among the rest, the opposite.
In anger he offered that head into that southern fire,
and, having burned that sacrificial ground, he departed for the abode of the <s>Guhyakas</s>.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Then all the hosts of gods, defeated by the armies of <s>Rudra</s>,
by tridents, spears, swords, clubs, iron bars, and mallets,
their whole bodies cut and split, together with the priests and assembly members, overcome with fear,
bowed to <s>Svayambhū</s> and reported all this in full.
Blessed <s>Abjasaṃbhava</s> had already learned of this beforehand,

children.text: nārāyaṇaś ca viśvātmā na kasyādhvaram īyatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the soul of the universe, likewise had not gone to that one's sacrifice.

children.text: tad ākarṇya vibhuḥ prāha tejīyasi kṛtāgasi
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the mighty one said, "When an offense has been committed against one stronger,

children.text: kṣemāya tatra sā bhūyān na prāyeṇa bubhūṣatām ||
children.translated_text: it is generally not for the welfare of those who wish to prosper.

children.text: athāpi yūyaṃ kṛtakilbiṣā bhavaṃ ye barhiṣo bhāgabhājaṃ parāduḥ
children.translated_text: Even so, you have committed an offense against <s>Bhava</s>, you who excluded him, the rightful sharer in the sacrificial portion, from the sacred grass.
With purified minds, therefore, propitiate him, quick to be gracious, whose lotus feet are accepted in refuge.

children.text: āśāsānā jīvitam adhvarasya lokaḥ sapālaḥ kupite na yasmin
children.translated_text: You and the world with its guardians hope for the life of the sacrifice; when he is angered, that life cannot remain.

children.text: tam āśu devaṃ priyayā vihīnaṃ kṣamāpayadhvaṃ hṛdi viddhaṃ duruktaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Quickly beg forgiveness from that god, deprived of his beloved, whose heart has been pierced by harsh words.

children.text: nāhaṃ na yajño na ca yūyam anye ye dehabhājo munayaś ca tattvam
children.translated_text: Neither I, nor the sacrifice, nor you, nor the other embodied beings, nor the sages know the truth,

children.text: viduḥ pramāṇaṃ balavīryayor vā yasyātmatantrasya ka upāyaṃ vidhitset ||
children.translated_text: or the measure of the strength and heroic power of that self-dependent one; who could wish to devise a remedy against him?"

children.text: sa ittham ādiśya surān ajas tu taiḥ samanvitaḥ pitṛbhiḥ saprajeśaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed the gods, the Unborn One, accompanied by them, by the ancestors, and by the lords of creatures,

children.text: yayau svadhiṣṇyān nilayaṃ puradviṣaḥ kailāsam adripravaraṃ priyaṃ prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: went from his own abode to <s>Kailāsa</s>, the dwelling of the enemy of the cities, the best of mountains, dear to the Lord.
It is frequented by beings perfected through birth, herbs, austerity, mantra, and yoga, and by nonhuman beings,
always attended by <s>kinnaras</s> and <s>gandharvas</s>, and surrounded by <s>apsarases</s>.
It has peaks made of many kinds of jewels, variegated with many minerals,
covered with many kinds of trees, creepers, shrubs, and herds of many animals.
With many pure streams, caves, and slopes,
it is a place of delight for perfected women sporting with their lovers.
It resounds with the cries of peacocks and is made dizzy, as it were, by bees blinded with intoxication;
it is flooded by the calls of red-throated birds and by the cooing of other birds.
With wish-fulfilling trees whose raised branches seem to invite the twice-born birds,

children.text: vrajantam iva mātaṅgair gṛṇantam iva nirjharaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it seems to move with elephants and to sing with waterfalls.
It is adorned with <s>mandāra</s> and <s>pārijāta</s> trees, and with <s>sarala</s> trees,
as well as <s>tamāla</s>, <s>śāla</s>, palm, <s>kovidāra</s>, <s>asana</s>, and <s>arjuna</s> trees,
with mangoes, <s>kadamba</s>, <s>nīpa</s>, <s>nāga</s>, <s>punnāga</s>, and <s>campaka</s> trees,
and also with <s>pāṭala</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>kunda</s>, and <s>kurabaka</s> trees.
with golden-colored hundred-petaled lotuses, and with choice reṇukā and jātī blossoms,

children.text: kubjakair mallikābhiś ca mādhavībhiś ca maṇḍitam ||
children.translated_text: adorned with kubjaka flowers, mallikās, and mādhavīs;
with jackfruit, udumbara, aśvattha, plakṣa, banyan, and hiṅgu trees,

children.text: bhūrjair oṣadhibhiḥ pūgai rājapūgaiś ca jambubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with birches, herbs, areca palms, royal arecas, and rose-apples,
with date-palms, āmrātaka and mango trees, priyāla, madhuka, and iṅguda,
and splendid with other kinds of trees, with bamboos and reed-like growths;
with groves flourishing with kumuda, utpala, kahlāra, and hundred-petaled lotuses,
and, in its lotus ponds, adorned by flocks of birds singing sweetly;
with deer, monkeys, boars, lions, bears, and porcupines,
with gavayas, śarabhas, tigers, ruru deer, buffaloes, and the like;
inhabited by <s>Karṇāntras</s>, <s>Ekapadas</s>, <s>Aśvāsyas</s>, and <s>Vṛkanābhis</s>,
its sandy banks and lotus ponds lovely, enclosed by clusters of plantain trees.
It was surrounded by the <s>Nandā</s>, whose waters had become still more sacred from <s>Satī</s>'s bathing;
seeing that mountain of <s>Bhūteśa</s>, the gods were filled with wonder.

children.text: dadṛśus tatra te ramyām alakāṃ nāma vai purīm
children.translated_text: There they saw the beautiful city named <s>Alakā</s>,

children.text: vanaṃ saugandhikaṃ cāpi yatra tannāma paṅkajam ||
children.translated_text: and also the <s>Saugandhika</s> forest, where the lotus of that name grows.

children.text: nandā cālakanandā ca saritau bāhyataḥ puraḥ
children.translated_text: The rivers <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Alakanandā</s> flowed outside, before the city,
made exceedingly purifying by the dust of the lotus feet of <s>Tīrthapāda</s>.
In those rivers, O <s>Kṣattar</s>, divine women, descending from their own abodes,
play by plunging in and sprinkling their men, wearied by love-sport.
Their water is stained yellow-red with fresh kuṅkuma washed off by that bathing;

children.text: vitṛṣo 'pi pibanty ambhaḥ pāyayanto gajā gajīḥ ||
children.translated_text: even elephants, though not thirsty, drink it while making their females drink.
The city was crowded with hundreds of aerial mansions made of star-bright gold and great jewels,
and was frequented by women of the <s>Puṇyajanas</s>, like the sky by clouds with lightning.

children.text: hitvā yakṣeśvarapurīṃ vanaṃ saugandhikaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: Passing beyond the city of the lord of the Yakṣas and that <s>Saugandhika</s> forest,
they reached a delightful grove with wish-fulfilling trees, whose leaves bore variegated garlands and fruits.
It had bees accompanied by the calls of flocks of red-throated birds,
was beloved of groups of melodious swans, and had ponds filled with hard reeds.
With the wind of yellow sandalwood stirred by herds of forest elephants,
it repeatedly stirred the minds of the women of the <s>Puṇyajanas</s> there.
After seeing stepwells with stairs made of vaidūrya and garlanded with blue lotuses,

children.text: prāptaṃ kimpuruṣair dṛṣṭvā ta ārād dadṛśur vaṭam ||
children.translated_text: attended by <s>Kimpuruṣas</s>, from afar they saw a banyan tree.
It rose a hundred yojanas high, with the spread of its branches three quarters of that,
casting shade over the mountain all around, without nests and free from heat.
There, in that place full of great yoga, a refuge for those seeking liberation, the gods
saw <s>Śiva</s> seated, as if Death itself had cast off anger.
He was attended by peaceful great siddhas beginning with <s>Sanandana</s>, their bodies stilled,
and also by his friend, the lord of the Guhyakas and Rākṣasas.
He, the supreme lord, had entered the path of knowledge, austerity, and yoga,
and moved for the welfare of the world, as the friend of the universe, out of affection.
He bore the ascetic marks dear to ascetics: ashes, a staff, matted locks, and a deerskin,
and on a body with the glow of evening clouds he wore the crescent moon.
He was seated on a seat made of darbha grass, the eternal <s>Brahman</s>,
speaking to <s>Nārada</s>, who had asked, while the good listened.

children.text: kṛtvorau dakṣiṇe savyaṃ pādapadmaṃ ca jānuni
children.translated_text: He had placed his left lotus foot upon his right thigh and upon his knee,
his hand on his forearm, holding a rosary, seated in the gesture of reasoning.

children.text: taṃ brahmanirvāṇasamādhim āśritaṃ vyupāśritaṃ giriśaṃ yogakakṣām
children.translated_text: Having approached <s>Giriśa</s>, who had taken refuge in the samādhi of brahmanirvāṇa and assumed the posture of yoga,

children.text: salokapālā munayo manūnām ādyaṃ manuṃ prāñjalayaḥ praṇemuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sages, together with the guardians of the worlds, bowed with joined palms to the primal teacher of the Manus.
But he, noticing that the self-born one had arrived, his feet bowed to by the lords of gods and asuras,

children.text: utthāya cakre śirasābhivandanam arhattamaḥ kasya yathaiva viṣṇuḥ ||
children.translated_text: rose and made obeisance with his head, as <s>Viṣṇu</s> would to one most worthy of honor.

children.text: tathāpare siddhagaṇā maharṣibhir ye vai samantād anu nīlalohitam
children.translated_text: Likewise the other hosts of siddhas, together with the great sages, who stood all around <s>Nīlalohita</s>, bowed.

children.text: namaskṛtaḥ prāha śaśāṅkaśekharaṃ kṛtapraṇāmaṃ prahasann ivātmabhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Ātmabhū</s>, smiling, addressed the moon-crested lord after he had made obeisance.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: āne tvām īśaṃ viśvasya jagato yonibījayoḥ
children.translated_text: I know you as the lord of the universe, of the world's womb and seed,

children.text: śakteḥ śivasya ca paraṃ yat tad brahmā nirantaram ||
children.translated_text: as that supreme, uninterrupted <s>Brahman</s> beyond <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śiva</s>.
You alone, Blessed Lord, from these two forms, <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>,

children.text: viśvaṃ sṛjasi pāsy atsi krīḍann ūrṇapaṭo yathā ||
children.translated_text: create, protect, and consume the universe in play, like a spider its web.

children.text: tvam eva dharmārthadughābhipattaye dakṣeṇa sūtreṇa sasarjithādhvaram
children.translated_text: You yourself, for the attainment of what yields <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, brought forth the sacrifice through <s>Dakṣa</s> as by a thread,

children.text: tvayaiva loke 'vasitāś ca setavo yān brāhmaṇāḥ śraddadhate dhṛtavratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by you alone have the boundaries been established in the world, in which vow-holding brahmins place their trust.

children.text: tvaṃ karmaṇāṃ maṅgala maṅgalānāṃ kartuḥ svalokaṃ tanuṣe svaḥ paraṃ vā
children.translated_text: O auspicious one, by rites you extend for the doer the world of auspicious deeds, heaven or what is beyond,

children.text: amaṅgalānāṃ ca tamisram ulbaṇaṃ viparyayaḥ kena tad eva kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: and for inauspicious deeds, dense darkness; for whom, and by what, does the contrary come about?

children.text: na vai satāṃ tvaccaraṇārpitātmanāṃ bhūteṣu sarveṣv abhipaśyatāṃ tava
children.translated_text: Anger usually does not overpower the good, whose selves are offered at your feet and who behold you in all beings,

children.text: bhūtāni cātmany apṛthagdidṛkṣatāṃ prāyeṇa roṣo 'bhibhaved yathā paśum ||
children.translated_text: and who wish to see beings within the self as not separate, as it overpowers a beast.
Those of separate understanding, seeing only ritual acts, evil-minded, with heart-wounds fixed on another's rise, constantly

children.text: parān duruktair vitudanty aruntudās tān māvadhīd daivavadhān bhavadvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: pierce others with harsh words, wounding like sores; one such as you should not slay them, already slain by fate.

children.text: yasmin yadā puṣkaranābhamāyayā durantayā spṛṣṭadhiyaḥ pṛthagdṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: When, in that condition, their minds are touched by the insurmountable <s>māyā</s> of the lotus-naveled Lord and they see separateness,

children.text: kurvanti tatra hy anukampayā kṛpāṃ na sādhavo daivabalāt kṛte kramam ||
children.translated_text: the holy act there with compassion and show mercy; they do not punish an act done by the force of fate.

children.text: bhavāṃs tu puṃsaḥ paramasya māyayā durantayāspṛṣṭamatiḥ samastadṛk
children.translated_text: But you, whose mind is untouched by the insurmountable <s>māyā</s> of the Supreme Person, seeing everything,

children.text: tayā hatātmasv anukarmacetaḥsv anugrahaṃ kartum ihārhasi prabho ||
children.translated_text: ought here, O Lord, to show favor to those whose selves are struck by that <s>māyā</s> and whose minds follow their karma.

children.text: kurv adhvarasyoddharaṇaṃ hatasya bhoḥ tvayāsamāptasya mano prajāpateḥ
children.translated_text: O lord, restore the sacrifice of the Prajāpati, which was slain by you and left unfinished.

children.text: na yatra bhāgaṃ tava bhāgino daduḥ kuyājino yena makho ninīyate ||
children.translated_text: There those bad sacrificers did not give you your share, by which the sacrifice is brought to completion.
Let this sacrificer live; let <s>Bhaga</s> receive his eyes.

children.text: bhṛgoḥ śmaśrūṇi rohantu pūṣṇo dantāś ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s beard grow again, and <s>Pūṣan</s>'s teeth as before.
Let the gods, whose limbs were broken by weapons and stones, and the priests too,
being favored by you, O wrathful one, quickly become free from injury.

children.text: eṣa te rudra bhāgo 'stu yaducchiṣṭo 'dhvarasya vai
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, let this be your portion, whatever remains of the sacrifice.

children.text: yajñas te rudra bhāgena kalpatām adya yajñahan ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, destroyer of sacrifice, by your share may your sacrifice today be made complete.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
When he had been thus entreated by the unborn lord, <s>Bhava</s>, being pleased,
laughed and said, O mighty-armed one, "Listen."
<s>Mahādeva</s> said:
O lord of creatures, I neither count nor brood over the offense of children,
who have been overcome by divine <s>māyā</s> (deluding power); the punishment there was applied by me.
Let the Prajāpati, whose head was burned, have the head of a goat.

children.text: mitrasya cakṣuṣekṣeta bhāgaṃ svaṃ barhiṣo bhagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Bhaga</s> see his own share on the sacred grass with <s>Mitra</s>'s eye.

children.text: pūṣā tu yajamānasya dadbhir jakṣatu piṣṭabhuk
children.translated_text: But let <s>Pūṣan</s>, who eats ground food, chew with the teeth of the sacrificer.

children.text: devāḥ prakṛtasarvāṅgā ye ma uccheṣaṇaṃ daduḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the gods who gave me the remnant offering have all their limbs restored to their natural state.
With the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s> and with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>,

children.text: bhavantv adhvaryavaś cānye bastaśmaśrur bhṛgur bhavet ||
children.translated_text: let the other <s>adhvaryus</s> (officiating priests) have arms made for them, and let <s>Bhṛgu</s> have a goat's beard.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Then all beings, hearing what the bountiful lord had said,

children.text: parituṣṭātmabhis tāta sādhu sādhv ity athābruvan ||
children.translated_text: with delighted hearts, dear one, cried out, "Good, good!"
Then, after honoring the bountiful lord, the gods together with the sages
went again to that sacrificial ground of the lord who shares oblations.

children.text: vidhāya kārtsnyena ca tad yad āha bhagavān bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: And when they had fully carried out what the Blessed <s>Bhava</s> had commanded,
they joined <s>Dakṣa</s>'s body with the head of the animal for the soma-pressing.
As the head was being attached, <s>Dakṣa</s>, looked upon by <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: sadyaḥ supta ivottasthau dadṛśe cāgrato mṛḍam ||
children.translated_text: at once rose up as if from sleep and saw <s>Mṛḍa</s> before him.
Then the Prajāpati, whose self had been muddied by hatred of the bull-bannered lord,
became stainless from <s>Śiva</s>'s glance, like a lake in autumn.
Resolving to praise <s>Bhava</s>, he could not do so, filled with affection,
because of longing and a film of tears, as he remembered his dead daughter.

children.text: kṛcchrāt saṃstabhya ca manaḥ premavihvalitaḥ sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: With difficulty he steadied his mind; wise though he was, he was overwhelmed by love.
With a sincere disposition the Prajāpati praised the Lord.
<s>Dakṣa</s> said:

children.text: bhūyān anugraha aho bhavatā kṛto me daṇḍas tvayā mayi bhṛto yad api pralabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, a great favor has been done for me by you, since punishment was borne by you against me, even though I had reviled you.

children.text: na brahmabandhuṣu ca vāṃ bhagavann avajñā tubhyaṃ hareś ca kuta eva dhṛtavrateṣu ||
children.translated_text: O Blessed Lord, there is no contempt in you two, in you and in <s>Hari</s>, even toward mere kinsmen of brahmins, much less toward those firm in vows.

children.text: vidyātapovratadharān mukhataḥ sma viprān brahmātmatattvam avituṃ prathamaṃ tvam asrāk
children.translated_text: You first created the brahmins from your mouth, bearers of knowledge, austerity, and vows, to protect the truth of <s>Brahman</s> and the self.

children.text: tad brāhmaṇān parama sarvavipatsu pāsi pālaḥ paśūn iva vibho pragṛhītadaṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, O supreme all-pervading lord, you protect the brahmins in every danger, like a herdsman protecting cattle, staff in hand.

children.text: yo 'sau mayāviditatattvadṛśā sabhāyāṃ kṣipto duruktiviśikhair vigaṇayya tan mām
children.translated_text: I, whose sight did not know the truth, reviled that lord in the assembly with arrows of harsh speech, having slighted him.

children.text: arvāk patantam arhattamanindayāpāddṛṣṭyārdrayā sa bhagavān svakṛtena tuṣyet ||
children.translated_text: May that Blessed Lord, who saved me as I was falling downward by his compassionate glance and by not blaming me, be pleased with his own act.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having thus begged pardon from the bountiful lord, and having been authorized by <s>Brahmā</s>,
he continued the rite together with his preceptors, priests, and the rest.
To continue the sacrifice for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O best of twice-born ones,
they offered a three-bowl <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) for purification from contact with <s>Vīrabhadra</s>.
When the oblation had been taken by the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest), the sacrificer, O lord of the people,
meditated with purified thought, and then <s>Hari</s> appeared.

children.text: tadā svaprabhayā teṣāṃ dyotayantyā diśo daśa
children.translated_text: Then, with his own radiance illuminating the ten directions for them,
he was brought by <s>Tārkṣya</s>, the hymn-winged one, stealing away all other brilliance.
Dark-hued, with a golden girdle and graced by a sunlike crown, his face adorned with earrings amid blue locks like swarms of bees,
with golden arms occupied with conch, lotus, discus, arrow, bow, mace, sword, and shield, he shone like a <s>karṇikāra</s> tree.

children.text: vakṣasy adhiśritavadhūr vanamāly udārahāsāvalokakalayā ramayaṃś ca viśvam
children.translated_text: On his chest rested his consort; wearing a forest garland, he delighted the universe with the beauty of his generous smile and glance.
Royal swans seemed to circle as fans and yak-tail whisks at his sides, while above him a white parasol shone like the moon.
Seeing him arrive, all the hosts of gods and others
rose suddenly and bowed down, with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the three-eyed lord at their head.
Their own radiance overcome by his splendor, their tongues silenced and themselves filled with awe,
they stood before <s>Adhokṣaja</s> with joined palms raised to their heads.

children.text: apy arvāgvṛttayo yasya mahi tv ātmabhuvādayaḥ
children.translated_text: Even <s>Ātmabhū</s> and the others, whose capacities move only below him,
praised his greatness according to their understanding, for he had assumed a form out of grace.

children.text: dakṣo gṛhītārhaṇasādanottamaṃ yajñeśvaraṃ viśvasṛjāṃ paraṃ gurum
children.translated_text: <s>Dakṣa</s>, purified and with joined palms, approached the Lord of sacrifice, the supreme guru of the creators of the universe, who had received the finest seat of honor,

children.text: sunandanandādyanugair vṛtaṃ mudā gṛṇan prapede prayataḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by attendants such as <s>Sunanda</s> and <s>Nanda</s>, and joyfully praised him.
<s>Dakṣa</s> said:

children.text: śuddhaṃ svadhāmny uparatākhilabuddhyavasthaṃ cinmātram ekam abhayaṃ pratiṣidhya māyām
children.translated_text: Pure, established in your own abode, with all states of intellect brought to rest, you are pure consciousness alone, one and fearless, having excluded <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: tiṣṭhaṃs tayaiva puruṣatvam upetya tasyām āste bhavān apariśuddha ivātmatantraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yet, through that very <s>māyā</s>, you assume personhood within it and remain as if impure, though self-governing.
The priests said:

children.text: tattvaṃ na te vayam anañjana rudraśāpātkarmaṇy avagrahadhiyo bhagavan vidāmaḥ
children.translated_text: O stainless Blessed Lord, because of <s>Rudra</s>'s curse our minds are obstructed in ritual action, and we do not know your reality.

children.text: dharmopalakṣaṇam idaṃ trivṛd adhvarākhyaṃ jñātaṃ yadartham adhidaivam ado vyavasthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: We know this threefold rite called sacrifice, marked by <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), for whose sake you have arranged that divine order.
The assembled members said:

On the path of birth, helpless, in the fortress of great affliction, pursued by the terrible serpent of death, chasing sense-objects like a deer after a mirage, and bearing the heavy burden of self and household,

children.text: dvandvaśvabhre khalamṛgabhaye śokadāve 'jñasārthaḥ pādaukas te śaraṇada kadā yāti kāmopasṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the abyss of opposites, afraid of wicked beasts, in the forest fire of grief, when will this ignorant caravan, assailed by desire, reach your feet, O giver of refuge?
<s>Rudra</s> said:

children.text: tava varada varāṅghrāv āśiṣehākhilārthe hy api munibhir asaktair ādareṇārhaṇīye
children.translated_text: O giver of boons, your excellent feet, sought here for every aim, are worthy of worship with reverence even by sages who are unattached.

children.text: yadi racitadhiyaṃ māvidyaloko 'paviddhaṃ japati na gaṇaye tat tvatparānugraheṇa ||
children.translated_text: If the ignorant world speaks of me as cast off, though my thought is fixed on them, I do not count that, through your favor toward those devoted to you.
<s>Bhṛgu</s> said:

children.text: yan māyayā gahanayāpahṛtātmabodhā brahmādayas tanubhṛtas tamasi svapantaḥ
children.translated_text: By whose deep māyā <s>Brahmā</s> and the other embodied beings, their self-knowledge stolen away, sleep in darkness,

children.text: nātmanśritaṃ tava vidanty adhunāpi tattvaṃ so 'yaṃ prasīdatu bhavān praṇatātmabandhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: they do not even now know your truth, O Self, lodged in the self. May that lord be gracious, the kinsman of those who bow before him.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: naitat svarūpaṃ bhavato 'sau padārthabhedagrahaiḥ puruṣo yāvad īkṣet
children.translated_text: This is not your own form, so long as a person sees it through graspings at distinctions among objects.

children.text: jñānasya cārthasya guṇasya cāśrayo māyāmayād vyatirikto matas tvam ||
children.translated_text: You are understood to be distinct from what is made of māyā, the support of knowledge, of object, and of quality.
<s>Indra</s> said:

children.text: idam apy acyuta viśvabhāvanaṃ vapur ānandakaraṃ manodṛśām
children.translated_text: This body of yours too, O <s>Acyuta</s>, maker of the universe, gives joy to the eyes of the mind,
and is furnished with eight club-like arms, bearing raised weapons for destroying the enemies of the gods.
The wives said:

children.text: yajño 'yaṃ tava yajanāya kena sṛṣṭo vidhvastaḥ paśupatinādya dakṣakopāt
children.translated_text: This sacrifice, created by someone for worshiping you, has now been destroyed by <s>Paśupati</s> because of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s anger.

children.text: taṃ nas tvaṃ śavaśayanābhaśāntamedhaṃ yajñātman nalinarucā dṛśā punīhi ||
children.translated_text: Purify it for us, O Self of sacrifice, lying like a corpse with its rite brought to rest, with your lotus-bright glance.
The seers said:

children.text: ananvitaṃ te bhagavan viceṣṭitaṃ yad ātmanā carasi hi karma nājyase
children.translated_text: O Blessed Lord, your activity is unattached, for when you act by yourself you are not smeared by action.

children.text: vibhūtaye yata upasedur īśvarīṃ na manyate svayam anuvartatīṃ bhavān ||
children.translated_text: People resort to sovereign power for prosperity, but you yourself do not regard it, though it follows after you.
The perfected beings said:
This elephant of our mind, burned by the forest fire of afflictions and tormented by thirst, has plunged into the river of nectar washed clean by stories of you.

children.text: tṛṣārto 'vagāḍho na sasmāra dāvaṃ na niṣkrāmati brahmasampannavan naḥ ||
children.translated_text: It did not remember the fire, and, like one who has attained <s>Brahman</s>, it does not come out.
The sacrificer's wife said:

children.text: svāgataṃ te prasīdeśa tubhyaṃ namaḥ śrīnivāsa śriyā kāntayā trāhi naḥ
children.translated_text: Welcome to you. Be gracious, Lord. Homage to you, O <s>Śrīnivāsa</s>; with <s>Śrī</s>, your beloved, protect us.

children.text: tvām ṛte 'dhīśa nāṅgair makhaḥ śobhate śīrṣahīnaḥ kabandho yathā puruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without you, O supreme lord, the sacrifice does not shine with its limbs, just as a man's headless torso does not shine.
The guardians of the worlds said:

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ kiṃ no dṛgbhir asadgrahais tvaṃ pratyagdraṣṭā dṛśyate yena viśvam
children.translated_text: Are you truly seen by our eyes, which grasp the unreal? You are the inner seer by whom the universe is seen.

children.text: māyā hy eṣā bhavadīyā hi bhūman yas tvaṃ ṣaṣṭhaḥ pañcabhir bhāsi bhūtaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is your māyā, O vast one: you, as the sixth, appear along with the five elements.
The lords of yoga said:

children.text: preyān na te 'nyo 'sty amutas tvayi prabho viśvātmanīkṣen na pṛthag ya ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: No one is dearer to you than the one who, O Lord, sees no self apart from you, the Self of the universe.
Even so, O Lord, affectionate one, favor those who approach you through that devotion, with undivided conduct.
In the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the world, by divine self-māyā whose qualities are divided in many ways,
homage to you, who are imagined as divided in yourself, yet whose own state has turned back the qualities of delusion from the self.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: namas te śritasattvāya dharmādīnāṃ ca sūtaye
children.translated_text: Homage to you, who have resorted to sattva and are the source of <s>dharma</s> (normative order) and the rest,

children.text: nirguṇāya ca yatkāṣṭhāṃ nāhaṃ vedāpare 'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: and who are without qualities; I do not know your limit, nor do the others.
<s>Agni</s> said:

children.text: yattejasāhaṃ susamiddhatejā havyaṃ vahe svadhvara ājyasiktam
children.translated_text: By your splendor I, with my splendor well kindled, carry the oblation sprinkled with ghee in a proper sacrifice.

children.text: taṃ yajñiyaṃ pañcavidhaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ sviṣṭaṃ yajurbhiḥ praṇato 'smi yajñam ||
children.translated_text: Bowing down, I honor that sacrifice, worthy of sacrifice, fivefold and well offered by the five yajus formulas.
The gods said:

children.text: purā kalpāpāye svakṛtam udarīkṛtya vikṛtaṃ tvam evādyas tasmin salila uragendrādhiśayane
children.translated_text: Formerly, at the dissolution of the kalpa, having drawn into your belly what you yourself had made and what had become transformed, you alone were the primal one in those waters, lying upon the lord of serpents.

children.text: pumān śeṣe siddhair hṛdi vimṛśitādhyātmapadaviḥ sa evādyākṣṇor yaḥ pathi carasi bhṛtyān avasi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: That same person, whose path of the inner self was pondered in the heart by perfected beings, now moves before our eyes and protects us, your servants.
The <s>Gandharvas</s> said:

children.text: aṃśāṃśās te deva marīcyādaya ete brahmendrādyā devagaṇā rudrapurogāḥ
children.translated_text: O god, these <s>Marīci</s> and the others, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the hosts of gods with <s>Rudra</s> at their head, are portions and portions of portions of you.

children.text: krīḍābhāṇḍaṃ viśvam idaṃ yasya vibhūman tasmai nityaṃ nātha namas te karavāma ||
children.translated_text: O vast lord, for him whose plaything this universe is, to that master, to you, we always make obeisance.
The <s>Vidyādharas</s> said:

children.text: tvanmāyayārtham abhipadya kalevare 'smin kṛtvā mamāham iti durmatir utpathaiḥ svaiḥ
children.translated_text: By your māyā, having taken this body as one's object and made the bad notion 'mine' and 'I' by one's own wrong paths,
even when cast down and longing for unreal sense-objects, one who partakes of the nectar of your stories would cast off self-delusion.
The Brahmins said:

children.text: tvaṃ kratus tvaṃ havis tvaṃ hutāśaḥ svayaṃ tvaṃ hi mantraḥ samiddarbhapātrāṇi ca
children.translated_text: You are the rite, you are the oblation, you are the fire itself; you are the mantra, the fuel, the darbha grass, and the vessels.

children.text: tvaṃ sadasyartvijo dampatī devatā agnihotraṃ svadhā soma ājyaṃ paśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are the officiants, the priests, the sacrificial couple, the deity, the agnihotra, the svadhā, the soma, the ghee, and the victim.

children.text: tvaṃ purā gāṃ rasāyā mahāsūkaro daṃṣṭrayā padminīṃ vāraṇendro yathā
children.translated_text: Formerly, as the great boar, you raised the earth from <s>Rasā</s> with your tusk, as the lord of elephants raises a lotus,

children.text: stūyamāno nadallīlayā yogibhir vyujjahartha trayīgātra yajñakratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: while yogins praised you and you roared in play, O body of the three Vedas, O sacrifice and rite.

children.text: sa prasīda tvam asmākam ākāṅkṣatāṃ darśanaṃ te paribhraṣṭasatkarmaṇām
children.translated_text: Be gracious to us, who desire the sight of you and whose good rites have fallen away.

children.text: kīrtyamāne nṛbhir nāmni yajñeśa te yajñavighnāḥ kṣayaṃ yānti tasmai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When your name is chanted by men, O lord of sacrifice, obstacles to sacrifice go to destruction. Homage to that one.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: iti dakṣaḥ kavir yajñaṃ bhadra rudrābhimarśitam
children.translated_text: Thus, fortunate one, the wise <s>Dakṣa</s> brought together the sacrifice that had been injured by <s>Rudra</s>,
while <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the source of the sacrificial state, was being praised.
The Blessed Lord, the Self of all and the enjoyer of every share, taking his own share,
addressed <s>Dakṣa</s>, speaking as if pleased, O sinless one.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: ahaṃ brahmā ca śarvaś ca jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ param
children.translated_text: I, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Śarva</s> are the supreme cause of the universe,
the self, the lord, the overseer, self-seeing and without distinctions.
Entering my own māyā, made of the guṇas, I, this same one, O twice-born,

children.text: sṛjan rakṣan haran viśvaṃ dadhre saṃjñāṃ kriyocitām ||
children.translated_text: while creating, protecting, and destroying the universe, assume names appropriate to each action.
In that nondual, solitary <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme self,
the ignorant person sees <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and living beings as distinct.

children.text: yathā pumān na svāṅgeṣu śiraḥpāṇyādiṣu kvacit
children.translated_text: Just as a man never regards his own limbs, such as head and hands,
with the thought that they belong to another, so one whose highest aim is me regards all beings.

children.text: trayāṇām ekabhāvānāṃ yo na paśyati vai bhidām
children.translated_text: O <s>Brahman</s>, whoever truly sees no difference among the three,
whose single nature is the self of all beings, attains peace.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Thus instructed by the Blessed Lord, the lord of the progenitors worshipped <s>Hari</s>,
and by his own sacrifice he honored the gods on both sides.

children.text: rudraṃ ca svena bhāgena hy upādhāvat samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: With collected mind he also approached <s>Rudra</s> with his own share,
and, at the conclusion of the rite, the other drinkers of soma as well.
Having completed the concluding rite together with the officiating priests, he then bathed in the avabhṛtha bath.
To him also, who by his own power had attained his object,

children.text: dharma eva matiṃ dattvā tridaśās te divaṃ yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: those gods gave a mind fixed on <s>dharma</s> and went to heaven.
Thus <s>Satī</s>, daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, abandoned her former body,

children.text: jajñe himavataḥ kṣetre menāyām iti śuśruma ||
children.translated_text: and we have heard that she was born in <s>Menā</s>, in the realm of <s>Himavat</s>.

children.text: tam eva dayitaṃ bhūya āvṛṅkte patim ambikā
children.translated_text: <s>Ambikā</s> again chose that very beloved one as her husband,
with no other disposition and with him as her sole goal, like power choosing the person though asleep.
This deed of the Blessed <s>Śambhu</s>, the foe of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice,
I heard from the devotee <s>Uddhava</s>, disciple of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: idaṃ pavitraṃ param īśaceṣṭitaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyam aghaughamarṣaṇam
children.translated_text: This supremely purifying deed of the Lord is glorious, lengthens life, and wipes away heaps of sin.

children.text: yo nityadākarṇya naro 'nukīrtayed dhunoty aghaṃ kaurava bhaktibhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man who always hears it and recounts it, O <s>Kaurava</s>, shakes off sin through the feeling of devotion.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: sanakādyā nāradaś ca ṛbhur haṃso 'ruṇir yatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sanaka</s> and the others, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Aruṇi</s>, and <s>Yati</s>,
these sons of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose seed was raised upward, did not dwell in households.

children.text: mṛṣādharmasya bhāryāsīd dambhaṃ māyāṃ ca śatruhan
children.translated_text: O destroyer of foes, the wife of false <s>dharma</s> was <s>Mṛṣā</s>, and she bore

children.text: asūta mithunaṃ tat tu nirṛtir jagṛhe 'prajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the twins <s>Dambha</s> and <s>Māyā</s>; childless <s>Nirṛti</s> took them.
O great-minded one, from those two were born <s>Lobha</s> and <s>Nikṛti</s>;

children.text: tābhyāṃ krodhaś ca hiṃsā ca yad duruktiḥ svasā kaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: from them came <s>Krodha</s> and <s>Hiṃsā</s>, and their sister was <s>Durukti</s>; from her came <s>Kali</s>.

children.text: duruktau kalir ādhatta bhayaṃ mṛtyuṃ ca sattama
children.translated_text: O best of the good, <s>Kali</s> begot <s>Bhaya</s> and <s>Mṛtyu</s> upon <s>Durukti</s>;

children.text: tayoś ca mithunaṃ jajñe yātanā nirayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: and from those two were born the pair <s>Yātanā</s> and <s>Niraya</s>.
I have briefly told you the secondary creation, O sinless one.

children.text: triḥ śrutvaitat pumān puṇyaṃ vidhunoty ātmano malam ||
children.translated_text: A man who hears this sacred account three times shakes off the impurity of his self.
Now then, O bearer of the Kurus, I shall recount the lineage of the famed-in-merit
<s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>, who was born as a partial portion of <s>Hari</s>.
<s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s> were the two sons of the husband of <s>Śatarūpā</s>;
they were established for the protection of the world through a portion of <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
The wives of <s>Uttānapāda</s> were <s>Sunīti</s> and <s>Suruci</s>.

children.text: suruciḥ preyasī patyur netarā yatsuto dhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Suruci</s> was dearer to her husband; the other was not, and her son was <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: ekadā suruceḥ putram aṅkam āropya lālayan
children.translated_text: One day the king, having lifted <s>Suruci</s>'s son
<s>Uttama</s> onto his lap and fondled him, did not welcome <s>Dhruva</s>, who wanted to climb up.

children.text: tathā cikīrṣamāṇaṃ taṃ sapatnyās tanayaṃ dhruvam
children.translated_text: As <s>Dhruva</s>, the son of her co-wife, wished to do the same,
<s>Suruci</s>, very proud and jealous, spoke while the king listened.

children.text: na vatsa nṛpater dhiṣṇyaṃ bhavān āroḍhum arhati
children.translated_text: "Child, you do not deserve to mount the king's seat,

children.text: na gṛhīto mayā yat tvaṃ kukṣāv api nṛpātmajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for, prince though you are, you were not taken by me even into my womb.
You are a child, alas; surely you do not know yourself

children.text: nūnaṃ veda bhavān yasya durlabhe 'rthe manorathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as one carried in the womb of another woman, though your desire is for an unattainable object.
If you wish for the royal throne, worship the <s>Puruṣa</s> through austerity,
and, by his favor, bring yourself into my womb."
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: mātuḥ sapatnyāḥ sa duruktividdhaḥ śvasan ruṣā daṇḍahato yathāhiḥ
children.translated_text: Pierced by the harsh words of his mother's co-wife, breathing in anger like a snake struck by a staff,

children.text: hitvā miṣantaṃ pitaraṃ sannavācaṃ jagāma mātuḥ prarudan sakāśam ||
children.translated_text: he left his father, who looked on silently, and went weeping to his mother.

children.text: taṃ niḥśvasantaṃ sphuritādharoṣṭhaṃ sunītir utsaṅga udūhya bālam
children.translated_text: <s>Sunīti</s> lifted the child, who was sighing and whose lips were trembling, onto her lap.

children.text: niśamya tatpauramukhān nitāntaṃ sā vivyathe yad gaditaṃ sapatnyā ||
children.translated_text: Hearing from the palace attendants what her co-wife had said, she was deeply distressed.

children.text: sotsṛjya dhairyaṃ vilalāpa śokadāvāgninā dāvalateva bālā
children.translated_text: Abandoning courage, the young woman lamented, like a forest creeper burned by a forest fire of grief.

children.text: vākyaṃ sapatnyāḥ smaratī sarojaśriyā dṛśā bāṣpakalām uvāha ||
children.translated_text: Remembering her co-wife's words, with lotus-lovely eyes she shed drops of tears.

children.text: dīrghaṃ śvasantī vṛjinasya pāram apaśyatī bālakam āha bālā
children.translated_text: Sighing deeply and seeing no limit to her misfortune, the woman spoke to the child:

children.text: māmaṅgalaṃ tāta pareṣu maṃsthā bhuṅkte jano yat paraduḥkhadas tat ||
children.translated_text: "My dear child, do not think ill of others; a person suffers the pain that he gives to another.

children.text: satyaṃ surucyābhihitaṃ bhavān me yad durbhagāyā udare gṛhītaḥ
children.translated_text: What <s>Suruci</s> said is true: you were taken into the womb of me, an unfortunate woman,

children.text: stanyena vṛddhaś ca vilajjate yāṃ bhāryeti vā voḍhum iḍaspatir mām ||
children.translated_text: and the lord of sacrifice is ashamed to bear me as a wife, though you grew from my milk.

children.text: ātiṣṭha tat tāta vimatsaras tvam uktaṃ samātrāpi yad avyalīkam
children.translated_text: Therefore, my child, free from envy, follow what your stepmother said, even though it was harsh.
If, like <s>Uttama</s>, you desire the throne, worship the lotus feet of <s>Adhokṣaja</s>.
By serving his lotus feet, <s>Aja</s>, having gained the qualities needed for creating the universe,
indeed occupied the supreme station, venerated by those whose self and breath are conquered.

children.text: tathā manur vo bhagavān pitāmaho yam ekamatyā purudakṣiṇair makhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise your grandfather, the Blessed <s>Manu</s>, with one-pointed mind

children.text: iṣṭvābhipede duravāpam anyato bhaumaṃ sukhaṃ divyam athāpavargyam ||
children.translated_text: worshipped him through sacrifices rich in gifts and attained earthly, heavenly, and liberating happiness, hard to gain from any other.

children.text: tam eva vatsāśraya bhṛtyavatsalaṃ mumukṣubhir mṛgyapadābjapaddhatim
children.translated_text: Take refuge in that very one, child, the lover of his servants, whose lotus-foot path is sought by those who desire liberation.

children.text: ananyabhāve nijadharmabhāvite manasy avasthāpya bhajasva pūruṣam ||
children.translated_text: Install the <s>Puruṣa</s> in your mind, fixed in your own <s>dharma</s> with undivided feeling, and worship him.

children.text: nānyaṃ tataḥ padmapalāśalocanād duḥkhacchidaṃ te mṛgayāmi kaṃcana
children.translated_text: Other than that lotus-petal-eyed one, I seek no one at all who can cut off your sorrow."

children.text: yo mṛgyate hastagṛhītapadmayā śriyetarair aṅga vimṛgyamāṇayā ||
children.translated_text: he whom <s>Śrī</s>, holding a lotus in her hand, seeks, while she herself is sought by others, O dear one.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Hearing this speech of his mother, which showed the way to obtain his aim,
he restrained himself by himself and went out from his father's city.

children.text: nāradas tad upākarṇya jñātvā tasya cikīrṣitam
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s>, hearing that and knowing what he intended to do,

children.text: spṛṣṭvā mūrdhany aghaghnena pāṇinā prāha vismitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: touched him on the head with his sin-destroying hand and, astonished, said:
Ah, the fiery spirit of kṣatriyas, who cannot bear the breaking of their honor!

children.text: bālo 'py ayaṃ hṛdā dhatte yat samātur asadvacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though only a child, this boy keeps in his heart the harsh words of his stepmother.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: nādhunāpy avamānaṃ te sammānaṃ vāpi putraka
children.translated_text: Even now, little son, we do not perceive any insult to you, or any honor either,
since you are a child attached to games and such things.
Even when distinctions exist, causes of dissatisfaction are not really separate

children.text: puṃso moham ṛte bhinnā yalloke nijakarmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for a man, apart from delusion, since in this world they arise through one's own deeds.
Therefore, dear child, a person should be content with just that much
as is supplied by fate, while the wise man observes the course of the Lord.
But if, by the yoga taught by your mother, you wish to ascend

children.text: yatprasādaṃ sa vai puṃsāṃ durārādhyo mato mama ||
children.translated_text: to his grace, he is, in my view, very difficult for men to worship successfully.
The sages, seeking his path with intense yogic concentration
and with detachment over many births, still do not know it.

children.text: ato nivartatām eṣa nirbandhas tava niṣphalaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore let this futile insistence of yours come to an end.
You will strive in due time, when the occasions for higher good have arrived.

children.text: yasya yad daivavihitaṃ sa tena sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever has been ordained by fate for someone, with that, in happiness and distress,

children.text: ātmānaṃ toṣayan dehī tamasaḥ pāram ṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: the embodied being, satisfying himself, reaches the far shore of darkness.
One should seek delight toward those superior in qualities, compassion toward those lower in qualities,

children.text: maitrīṃ samānād anvicchen na tāpair abhibhūyate ||
children.translated_text: and friendship toward equals; then one is not overcome by afflictions.
<s>Dhruva</s> said:
This tranquility has indeed been shown by the Blessed One, out of compassion, for people whose selves are struck by happiness and sorrow;

children.text: darśitaḥ kṛpayā puṃsāṃ durdarśo 'smadvidhais tu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but that is hard for such as us to perceive.
Even so, for me, undisciplined and seized by the terrible kṣatriya nature,

children.text: surucyā durvacobāṇair na bhinne śrayate hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: my heart, split by the arrow-like harsh words of <s>Suruci</s>, finds no rest.

children.text: padaṃ tribhuvanotkṛṣṭaṃ jigīṣoḥ sādhu vartma me
children.translated_text: O brahmin, tell me the good path for one wishing to win a station exalted above the three worlds,

children.text: brūhy asmatpitṛbhir brahmann anyair apy anadhiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: one not occupied by our forefathers or even by others.
Surely you are the son of the Blessed <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
and, plucking your vīṇā, you wander like the sun for the welfare of the world.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: ity udāhṛtam ākarṇya bhagavān nāradas tadā
children.translated_text: Hearing what had thus been spoken, the Blessed <s>Nārada</s> then

children.text: prītaḥ pratyāha taṃ bālaṃ sadvākyam anukampayā ||
children.translated_text: was pleased and, with compassion, replied to the boy with true words.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: jananyābhihitaḥ panthāḥ sa vai niḥśreyasasya te
children.translated_text: The path stated by your mother is indeed the path to your final good;

children.text: bhagavān vāsudevas taṃ bhaja taṃ pravaṇātmanā ||
children.translated_text: with a mind inclined toward him, worship Bhagavān <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Whoever desires his own good, called <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), <s>artha</s> (prosperity), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation),

children.text: ekaṃ hy eva hares tatra kāraṇaṃ pādasevanam ||
children.translated_text: for him service to the feet of <s>Hari</s> alone is the single cause.

children.text: tat tāta gaccha bhadraṃ te yamunāyās taṭaṃ śuci
children.translated_text: Therefore, dear child, go, may there be welfare for you, to the pure bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: puṇyaṃ madhuvanaṃ yatra sānnidhyaṃ nityadā hareḥ ||
children.translated_text: to holy <s>Madhuvana</s>, where <s>Hari</s>'s presence is always found.
Having bathed at the three junctures of the day in the auspicious water of the <s>Kālindī</s>,
and having performed the proper rites, dwell there, having prepared a seat for yourself.
By threefold <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control), slowly dispelling the impurity
of breath, senses, and mind, meditate with a firm mind on the supreme guru.
Always turned toward grace, with a serene face and glance,
with fine nose and brows, lovely cheeks, and beauty like that of the gods,
young, with charming limbs, reddish lips and eyes,
the refuge of those who bow down, majestic, a shelter, an ocean of compassion,
marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, dark as a rain cloud, the Person garlanded with forest flowers,
manifested as four-armed by conch, discus, mace, and lotus,
wearing a crown and earrings, adorned with armlets and bracelets,
with his neck ornamented by the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel and clothed in yellow silk,
girded with a jeweled belt and shining golden anklets,
most beautiful to behold, peaceful, increasing the delight of mind and eyes.
With his two feet shining with rows of jewel-like nails for those who worship him,
having stepped onto the pericarp of the lotus of the heart, he is established within the self.
One should meditate on him smiling and looking with affection,
with a controlled, single-pointed mind, as the best of boon-givers.

children.text: evaṃ bhagavato rūpaṃ subhadraṃ dhyāyato manaḥ
children.translated_text: For one who meditates thus on the very auspicious form of the Blessed Lord, the mind,

children.text: nirvṛtyā parayā tūrṇaṃ sampannaṃ na nivartate ||
children.translated_text: quickly endowed with supreme bliss, does not turn back.

children.text: japaś ca paramo guhyaḥ śrūyatāṃ me nṛpātmaja
children.translated_text: And hear from me, prince, the supreme secret <s>japa</s> (recitation),

children.text: yaṃ saptarātraṃ prapaṭhan pumān paśyati khecarān ||
children.translated_text: reciting which for seven nights a man sees the sky-roamers.
<s>Oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya</s>.
With this mantra, a wise person should perform material worship of the deity
with various substances, knowing the divisions of place and time.
With pure waters, garlands, forest products, roots, fruits, and the like,
and with approved sprouts and cloth, he should worship the Lord with beloved <s>Tulasī</s>.
Having obtained a material image, or else in earth, water, and the like, he should worship;
the sage should be self-collected, peaceful, controlled in speech, and moderate in eating forest fare.
Through the deeds of his chosen descents, performed by his inconceivable own <s>māyā</s> (power of manifestation),
the one praised in the finest verses will act; one should meditate on that which enters the heart.
Whatever services of the Blessed Lord have been prescribed and previously practiced,
he should apply those same services, by the heart of the mantra, to the mantra-embodied Lord.

children.text: evaṃ kāyena manasā vacasā ca manogatam
children.translated_text: Thus, by body, mind, and speech, the Blessed Lord who is present in the mind,
being served with devoted service,
increases the devotional feeling of men who worship properly and without deceit.

children.text: śreyo diśaty abhimataṃ yad dharmādiṣu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: which bestows upon embodied beings the desired good in <s>dharma</s> and the other aims.
And if one is detached from delight in the senses, then with abundant <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (devotional discipline)
one should worship him in an uninterrupted state of devotion, precisely for liberation.

children.text: ity uktas taṃ parikramya praṇamya ca nṛpārbhakaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus instructed, the royal child circumambulated him, bowed down,
and went to holy <s>Madhuvana</s>, marked by the feet of <s>Hari</s>.
When he had gone to the grove of austerity, the sage entered the inner apartments;
honored by the king with fitting honors, he sat comfortably and spoke to him.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: rājan kiṃ dhyāyase dīrghaṃ mukhena pariśuṣyatā
children.translated_text: O king, why are you reflecting for so long, with your face dried up?

children.text: kiṃvā na riṣyate kāmo dharmo vārthena saṃyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Has some desire been thwarted, or <s>dharma</s> together with prosperity?
The king said:
My little son, O brahman, by a woman of cruel heart,

children.text: nirvāsitaḥ pañcavarṣaḥ saha mātrā mahān kaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been banished together with his mother, though he is only five years old and wise beyond his years.

children.text: apy anāthaṃ vane brahman mā smādanty arbhakaṃ vṛkāḥ
children.translated_text: O brahman, may wolves not eat that helpless child in the forest,
weary, lying down, hungry, his lotus-face withered.
Ah, alas, consider my wickedness, conquered as I am by a woman:
I, the basest of men, did not welcome him when he lovingly wished to climb onto my lap.
