<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: mā mā śucaḥ svatanayaṃ devaguptaṃ viśāmpate
children.translated_text: Do not, do not grieve for your own son, protected by the gods, O lord of men.
Not knowing his power, the world will yet be enveloped by his fame.

children.text: suduṣkaraṃ karma kṛtvā lokapālair api prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Having performed a deed very hard to accomplish even for the guardians of the worlds, that lordly one

children.text: aiṣyaty acirato rājan yaśo vipulayaṃs tava ||
children.translated_text: will soon return, O king, enlarging your fame.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Hearing what had thus been said by the divine seer, the lord of the earth
disregarded royal fortune and thought only of his son.
There, after bathing, purified and having fasted through that night,
with mind composed he worshiped the <s>Puruṣa</s>, according to the sage's instruction.
At the end of every three nights, feeding on kapittha and badara fruits,
according to what sustained his body, he passed a month worshiping <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: dvitīyaṃ ca tathā māsaṃ ṣaṣṭhe ṣaṣṭhe 'rbhako dine
children.translated_text: Likewise in the second month, on every sixth day, the child
made food from withered grasses, leaves, and the like, while worshiping the Lord.
And passing the third month, on every ninth day
he lived on water and attended upon <s>Uttamaśloka</s> with concentration.

children.text: caturtham api vai māsaṃ dvādaśe dvādaśe 'hani
children.translated_text: In the fourth month too, on every twelfth day,
feeding on air, with breath conquered, he held himself firm while meditating on the god.
When the fifth month had arrived, the prince, with his breath conquered,

children.text: dhyāyan brahma padaikena tasthau sthāṇur ivācalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: stood on one foot, meditating on <s>Brahman</s>, unmoving like a post.
Drawing his mind back from every side into the heart, the seat of beings and senses,
and meditating on the form of the Blessed Lord, he saw nothing else at all.
As he held in meditation <s>Brahman</s>, the support of <s>mahat</s> and the rest, the Lord of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>,
the three worlds trembled.

children.text: yadaikapādena sa pārthivārbhakas tasthau tadaṅguṣṭhanipīḍitā mahī
children.translated_text: When that royal child stood on one foot, then the earth, pressed down by his toe,

children.text: nanāma tatrārdham ibhendradhiṣṭhitā tarīva savyetarataḥ pade pade ||
children.translated_text: bent on one side, like a boat occupied by a lordly elephant, shifting left and right at every step.

children.text: tasminnabhidhyāyati viśvam ātmano dvāraṃ nirudhyāsum ananyayā dhiyā
children.translated_text: As he meditated on him as the Self of the universe, blocking the gate of breath with undivided thought,

children.text: lokā nirucchvāsanipīḍitā bhṛśaṃ salokapālāḥ śaraṇaṃ yayur harim ||
children.translated_text: the worlds, together with their world-protectors, sorely oppressed by breathlessness, went to <s>Hari</s> for refuge.
The gods said:
O Blessed Lord, we do not understand such a stoppage of breath in the whole abode of beings, moving and unmoving.

children.text: vidhehi tan no vṛjinād vimokṣaṃ prāptā vayaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ śaraṇyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore grant us release from this distress; we have come to you, the refuge, for refuge.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: mā bhaiṣṭa bālaṃ tapaso duratyayān nivartayiṣye pratiyāta svadhāma
children.translated_text: Do not fear. I shall turn the boy back from his insurmountable austerity; return to your own abodes,

children.text: yato hi vaḥ prāṇanirodha āsīd auttānapādir mayi saṃgatātmā ||
children.translated_text: for your obstruction of breath arose because the son of <s>Uttānapāda</s> has fixed his self on me.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: ta evam utsannabhayā urukrame kṛtāvanāmāḥ prayayus triviṣṭapam
children.translated_text: Thus freed from fear, they bowed to <s>Urukrama</s> and went to heaven.

children.text: sahasraśīrṣāpi tato garutmatā madhor vanaṃ bhṛtyadidṛkṣayā gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the thousand-headed Lord, mounted on <s>Garutmān</s>, went to <s>Madhu</s>'s forest, wishing to see his servant.

children.text: sa vai dhiyā yogavipākatīvrayā hṛtpadmakośe sphuritaṃ taḍitprabham
children.translated_text: With the intense ripening of yoga in his thought, he had seen in the calyx of his heart-lotus a lightning-bright form flashing;
when it suddenly disappeared, he saw it standing outside in that same form.
At that sight, awe came upon him; bending his body like a staff, he bowed down on the ground,

children.text: dṛgbhyāṃ prapaśyan prapibann ivārbhakaś cumbann ivāsyena bhujair ivāśliṣan ||
children.translated_text: while the child gazed with his eyes as if drinking him, as if kissing him with his mouth, as if embracing him with his arms.

children.text: sa taṃ vivakṣantam atadvidaṃ harir jñātvāsya sarvasya ca hṛdy avasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, knowing that he wished to speak but did not know how, and being present in his heart and in the heart of all,

children.text: kṛtāñjaliṃ brahmamayena kambunā pasparśa bālaṃ kṛpayā kapole ||
children.translated_text: mercifully touched the boy's cheek with his conch, made of <s>Brahman</s>, as he stood with joined palms.

children.text: sa vai tadaiva pratipāditāṃ giraṃ daivīṃ parijñātaparātmanirṇayaḥ
children.translated_text: At that very moment he received divine speech and understood the certainty of the supreme self;
then <s>Dhruva</s>, filled with devotional feeling, calmly praised him whose great fame is widely heard.
<s>Dhruva</s> said:

children.text: yo 'ntaḥ praviśya mama vācam imāṃ prasuptāṃ saṃjīvayaty akhilaśaktidharaḥ svadhāmnā
children.translated_text: Entering within, the bearer of all powers revives by his own radiance this sleeping speech of mine,

children.text: anyāṃś ca hastacaraṇaśravaṇatvagādīnprāṇān namo bhagavate puruṣāya tubhyam ||
children.translated_text: and also the other faculties, hands, feet, hearing, skin, and the vital breaths. Homage to you, the Blessed <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: ekas tvam eva bhagavann idam ātmaśaktyā māyākhyayoruguṇayā mahadādyaśeṣam
children.translated_text: You alone are one, O Blessed Lord; by your own power, called <s>māyā</s> and endowed with vast <s>guṇas</s>, this whole universe beginning with <s>mahat</s>

children.text: sṛṣṭvānuviśya puruṣas tadasadguṇeṣu nāneva dāruṣu vibhāvasuvad vibhāsi ||
children.translated_text: you create and then enter as the <s>Puruṣa</s>; among those manifest and unmanifest qualities you appear as many, like fire in pieces of wood.

children.text: tvaddattayā vayunayedam acaṣṭa viśvaṃ suptaprabuddha iva nātha bhavatprapannaḥ
children.translated_text: By discernment given by you, one surrendered to you sees this universe, O Lord, like a sleeper awakened.

children.text: tasyāpavargyaśaraṇaṃ tava pādamūlaṃ vismaryate kṛtavidā katham ārtabandho ||
children.translated_text: How could one who knows your kindness forget the root of your feet, the refuge granting release, O friend of the distressed?

children.text: nūnaṃ vimuṣṭamatayas tava māyayā te ye tvāṃ bhavāpyayavimokṣaṇam anyahetoḥ
children.translated_text: Surely those who worship you, the one who releases beings from coming into existence and passing away, for some other purpose, have had their minds stolen by your <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: arcanti kalpakataruṃ kuṇapopabhogyam icchanti yat sparśajaṃ niraye 'pi nṝṇām ||
children.translated_text: They worship a wish-fulfilling tree, yet desire pleasures fit for a corpse-like body, pleasures born of touch which are available to human beings even in hell.

children.text: yā nirvṛtis tanubhṛtāṃ tava pādapadmadhyānād bhavajjanakathāśravaṇena vā syāt
children.translated_text: The satisfaction that embodied beings may have from meditation on your lotus feet, or from hearing the stories of those devoted to you,

children.text: sā brahmaṇi svamahimany api nātha mā bhūtkiṃtvantakāsilulitāt patatāṃ vimānāt ||
children.translated_text: may that not be mine even in <s>Brahman</s> in its own greatness, O Lord; how much less from a heavenly car that falls, shaken by the sword of Death.

children.text: bhaktiṃ muhuḥ pravahatāṃ tvayi me prasaṅgo bhūyād ananta mahatām amalāśayānām
children.translated_text: May I again and again have fellowship with the great ones of stainless hearts, whose devotion flows toward you, O <s>Ananta</s>.
Through that fellowship, intoxicated by drinking the nectar of the stories of your virtues, I shall easily cross the terrible, vast misery, the ocean of becoming.

children.text: te na smaranty atitarāṃ priyam īśa martyaṃ ye cānv adaḥ sutasuhṛdgṛhavittadārāḥ
children.translated_text: O Lord, those who have formed attachment among hearts greedy for the fragrance of your lotus feet, O <s>Abjanābha</s>,
do not at all remember the mortal body, so dear, nor what follows it: sons, friends, house, wealth, and wives.

O unborn one, I know this very gross form, manifold from <s>mahat</s> onward, marked by distinctions of existent and non-existent, and familiar through beasts, trees, twice-born beings, creeping things, gods, demons, mortals, and the rest.

children.text: rūpaṃ sthaviṣṭham aja te mahadādyanekaṃ nātaḥ paraṃ parama vedmi na yatra vādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beyond this, O supreme one, I know nothing higher, nor where argument may reach.

children.text: kalpānta etad akhilaṃ jaṭhareṇa gṛhṇan śete pumān svadṛg anantasakhas tadaṅke
children.translated_text: At the end of a <s>kalpa</s>, drawing all this into his belly, the Person lies down, seeing by himself, with <s>Ananta</s> as his companion, upon his lap.
In the golden world-lotus born from the ocean of his navel is the radiant one; to that Blessed Lord I bow.

children.text: tvaṃ nityamuktapariśuddhavibuddha ātmā kūṭastha ādipuruṣo bhagavāṃs tryadhīśaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the self, eternally liberated, perfectly pure, fully awakened, immutable, the primordial person, the Blessed Lord, master of the threefold realm.

children.text: yadbuddhyavasthitim akhaṇḍitayā svadṛṣṭyā draṣṭā sthitāv adhimakho vyatirikta āsse ||
children.translated_text: With your own unbroken vision you are the witness of the states of the intellect; in preservation you sit apart as the lord of the sacrifice.

children.text: yasmin viruddhagatayo hy aniśaṃ patanti vidyādayo vividhaśaktaya ānupūrvyāt
children.translated_text: In you, indeed, knowledge and the other manifold powers, though moving in opposed ways, ceaselessly enter in due order.

children.text: tad brahma viśvabhavam ekam anantam ādyamānandamātram avikāram ahaṃ prapadye ||
children.translated_text: I take refuge in that <s>Brahman</s>: the one source of the universe, infinite, primordial, mere bliss, and changeless.

children.text: satyāśiṣo hi bhagavaṃs tava pādapadmamāśīs tathānubhajataḥ puruṣārthamūrteḥ
children.translated_text: True indeed, O Blessed Lord, are the blessings for one who worships your lotus feet, for you are the embodiment of human ends.

children.text: apy evam arya bhagavān paripāti dīnānvāśreva vatsakam anugrahakātaro 'smān ||
children.translated_text: Even so, O noble one, may the Blessed Lord, eager to show favor, protect us poor ones like a cow protecting her calf.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Then, when he had been praised in this way by the wise one whose resolve was true,
the Blessed Lord, affectionate toward his servant, congratulated him and spoke these words.
The Blessed Lord said:
I know the resolve in your heart, royal boy.

children.text: tat prayacchāmi bhadraṃ te durāpam api suvrata ||
children.translated_text: I grant it to you, O good-vowed one, though it is difficult to obtain. May there be welfare for you.

children.text: nānyair adhiṣṭhitaṃ bhadra yad bhrājiṣṇu dhruvakṣiti
children.translated_text: O good one, that radiant station of <s>Dhruva</s>, not occupied by others,
where the wheel of lights, planets, asterisms, and stars is set, shall be yours.
Fixed at the pole like the wheel of oxen, it stands beyond those who dwell for a <s>kalpa</s>.

children.text: dharmo 'gniḥ kaśyapaḥ śukro munayo ye vanaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, and the sages who live in the forest,
moving with the stars, circle around it keeping it to their right.

children.text: prasthite tu vanaṃ pitrā dattvā gāṃ dharmasaṃśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: When your father has gone to the forest after giving the earth to you, you, resting on <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
will protect it for thirty-six thousand years, with your senses unimpaired.

children.text: tvadbhrātary uttame naṣṭe mṛgayāyāṃ tu tanmanāḥ
children.translated_text: When your brother <s>Uttama</s> has disappeared while hunting, your mother, intent on him,

children.text: anveṣantī vanaṃ mātā dāvāgniṃ sā pravekṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will enter the forest searching for him and will enter a forest fire.
Having worshiped me, the heart of sacrifice, with sacrifices rich in gifts,

children.text: bhuktvā cehāśiṣaḥ satyā ante māṃ saṃsmariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: and having enjoyed true blessings here, at the end you will remember me.
Then you will go to my station, honored by all worlds,

children.text: upariṣṭād ṛṣibhyas tvaṃ yato nāvartate gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: above the seers, from which one who has gone does not return.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: ity arcitaḥ sa bhagavān atidiśyātmanaḥ padam
children.translated_text: Thus worshiped, the Blessed Lord, the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>, assigned his own abode

children.text: bālasya paśyato dhāma svam agād garuḍadhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to the boy and went to his own realm while the boy looked on.
He too, having obtained the fulfillment of the resolve born in him through service to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s feet,
was not very pleased, and returned to the city.
<s>Vidura</s> said:

children.text: sudurlabhaṃ yat paramaṃ padaṃ harer māyāvinas taccaraṇārcanārjitam
children.translated_text: That supreme state of <s>Hari</s>, very hard to obtain, won by worship of the feet of the master of <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: labdhvāpy asiddhārtham ivaikajanmanā kathaṃ svam ātmānam amanyatārthavit ||
children.translated_text: though he had obtained it in a single birth, why did that knower of the goal think himself as if unsuccessful?
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: mātuḥ sapatnyā vāgbāṇair hṛdi viddhas tu tān smaran
children.translated_text: Pierced in the heart by the arrow-like words of his mother's co-wife, and remembering them,

children.text: naicchan muktipater muktiṃ tasmāt tāpam upeyivān ||
children.translated_text: he did not desire the liberation belonging to the Lord of liberation; therefore he came to grief.
<s>Dhruva</s> said:

children.text: samādhinā naikabhavena yat padaṃ viduḥ sanandādaya ūrdhvaretasaḥ
children.translated_text: That state which <s>Sananda</s> and the other celibate sages know through <s>samādhi</s> after many births,

children.text: māsair ahaṃ ṣaḍbhir amuṣya pādayoś chāyām upetyāpagataḥ pṛthaṅmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I reached the shade of his feet in six months, yet I came away with a mind set on difference.
Ah, look at the lack of true selfhood in me, unlucky as I am.

children.text: bhavacchidaḥ pādamūlaṃ gatvā yāce yad antavat ||
children.translated_text: Having gone to the root of the feet of the one who cuts off becoming, I asked for what has an end.
My understanding was polluted by the gods, who were falling and intolerant,
for I, worst of the unreal-minded, did not accept the true words of <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: daivīṃ māyām upāśritya prasupta iva bhinnadṛk
children.translated_text: Resorting to divine <s>māyā</s>, like one asleep and seeing division,
I burn with the heart-pain of brother and rival, though the second thing is also unreal.
This thing I prayed for was useless, like treatment for one whose life has gone.
Having propitiated the soul of the universe, hard to propitiate through austerity,
I, devoid of fortune, asked the cutter of becoming for becoming itself.

children.text: svārājyaṃ yacchato mauḍhyān māno me bhikṣito bata
children.translated_text: When he was granting sovereign rule, through folly I begged for honor from the Lord, alas,
like a poor man whose merit is exhausted asking for husks.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: na vai mukundasya padāravindayo rajojuṣas tāta bhavādṛśā janāḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed, dear one, people like you, who delight in the dust of <s>Mukunda</s>'s lotus feet...

children.text: vāñchanti taddāsyam ṛte 'rtham ātmano yadṛcchayā labdhamanaḥsamṛddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They seek servitude to him, and no advantage for themselves, their minds satisfied by what has come of its own accord.
Hearing that his son was coming, just as he had returned after passing away,

children.text: rājā na śraddadhe bhadram abhadrasya kuto mama ||
children.translated_text: the king did not believe it: "How could there be good fortune for me, who am unfortunate?"
Trusting the word of the divine seer, overwhelmed by a rush of joy,
and exceedingly pleased with the bringer of the news, he gave him a necklace of great value.
Mounting a chariot with fine horses, adorned with gold,
and surrounded by brāhmaṇas, elders of the family, ministers, and kinsmen,
with the sound of conches and kettledrums, with Vedic recitation and flutes,
he quickly went out from the city, eager to see his son.
<s>Sunīti</s> and <s>Suruci</s>, his two queens, adorned with golden ornaments,
mounted a palanquin and went together with <s>Uttama</s>.
Seeing him approaching near the grove, the king quickly descended
from his chariot and, coming near at once, was overcome with love.
Breathing hard with a heart long filled with longing, he embraced his son with both arms,
his child whose every bond of sin had been destroyed by contact with the feet of <s>Viṣvaksena</s>.
Then, smelling his head again and again, with cool waters from his eyes
he bathed his son, his intense desire now fulfilled.
After bowing to his father's feet and being blessed by him,
he bowed his head to his two mothers, honored as the foremost of the good.
<s>Suruci</s> raised up the little boy who had bowed at her feet,
embraced him, and said, "Live long," in a voice choked and faltering with tears.
When the Lord <s>Hari</s> is pleased with someone because of virtues such as friendliness,

children.text: tasmai namanti bhūtāni nimnam āpa iva svayam ||
children.translated_text: all beings bow to him of their own accord, as waters flow down to a low place.

children.text: uttamaś ca dhruvaś cobhāv anyonyaṃ premavihvalau
children.translated_text: <s>Uttama</s> and <s>Dhruva</s>, both overwhelmed with love for one another,
again and again shed streams of tears, thrilled with horripilation from bodily contact.

children.text: sunītir asya jananī prāṇebhyo 'pi priyaṃ sutam
children.translated_text: <s>Sunīti</s>, his mother, embraced her son, dearer to her than life itself,
and gave up her distress, delighted by the touch of his body.

children.text: payaḥ stanābhyāṃ susrāva netrajaiḥ salilaiḥ śivaiḥ
children.translated_text: Milk flowed from her breasts, and auspicious waters born from her eyes
repeatedly bathed him then, O hero, from that mother of a hero.

children.text: tāṃ śaśaṃsur janā rājñīṃ diṣṭyā te putra ārtihā
children.translated_text: The people praised that queen: "By good fortune, your son, remover of sorrow,

children.text: pratilabdhaś ciraṃ naṣṭo rakṣitā maṇḍalaṃ bhuvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been recovered after being lost for a long time; he will protect the circle of the earth.
Surely you have worshipped the Blessed Lord, remover of the distress of those who bow to him,
for steadfast people who meditate on him have conquered death, so very hard to conquer."

children.text: lālyamānaṃ janair evaṃ dhruvaṃ sabhrātaraṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: As the people thus fondled <s>Dhruva</s> and his brother, the king,
joyfully placing them on a female elephant and being praised, entered the city.
Here and there it was furnished with shining makara-arches,
with clusters of banana trunks and young areca palms of that kind.
At every gateway it was adorned with mango shoots, cloths, garlands, and hanging strings of pearls,
and with water jars accompanied by lamps.
With ramparts, gate towers, and palaces covered with gold,
it was splendidly adorned on every side, shining with the radiance of palace spires.
Its crossroads, streets, market roads, and highways were swept clean and smeared with sandalwood paste,
and strewn with parched grain, unbroken rice, flowers, fruits, rice grains, and offerings.

children.text: dhruvāya pathi dṛṣṭāya tatra tatra purastriyaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Dhruva</s> was seen on the road, the women of the city here and there
brought mustard seed, unbroken rice, curd, water, dūrvā grass, flowers, and fruits.
Out of affection they bestowed these on him, uttering true blessings,
and, listening to their sweet songs, he entered his father's palace.
In that finest palace, made of masses of great jewels,

children.text: lālito nitarāṃ pitrā nyavasad divi devavat ||
children.translated_text: he dwelt, fondled constantly by his father, like a god in heaven.
There the couches were like the foam of milk, made of ivory and covered with gold,
the seats were very costly, and the furnishings were golden.
There, on crystal walls and great emerald surfaces,
jewel lamps shone, accompanied by jewels among women.
There were lovely gardens with varied heavenly trees,
with pairs of birds calling and intoxicated bees singing.
There were ponds with steps of beryl, filled with lotuses, blue lotuses, and white water lilies,
frequented by flocks of swans, kāraṇḍava ducks, cakravākas, and cranes.
The royal sage <s>Uttānapāda</s>, having heard of and seen
that most wondrous power of his son, attained supreme amazement.

children.text: vīkṣyoḍhavayasaṃ taṃ ca prakṛtīnāṃ ca saṃmatam
children.translated_text: Seeing that he had reached mature age, that he was approved by the ministers,

children.text: anuraktaprajaṃ rājā dhruvaṃ cakre bhuvaḥ patim ||
children.translated_text: and that the subjects were attached to him, the king made <s>Dhruva</s> lord of the earth.
Recognizing himself to be advanced in age, the lord of the people,

children.text: vanaṃ viraktaḥ prātiṣṭhad vimṛśann ātmano gatim ||
children.translated_text: having become detached, set out for the forest, contemplating the goal of his self.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
<s>Dhruva</s> married <s>Bhrami</s>, the daughter of <s>Prajāpati Śiśumāra</s>;
her two sons were <s>Kalpa</s> and <s>Vatsara</s>.
By another wife, <s>Ilā</s>, daughter of <s>Vāyu</s>, the very mighty one
begot a son named <s>Utkala</s> and a jewel among women.
But <s>Uttama</s>, before he had married, was killed while hunting on a mountain
by a powerful Puṇyajana; his mother followed his path.
When <s>Dhruva</s> heard of his brother's killing, he was seized by anger, indignation, and grief.
Mounting his victorious chariot, he went to the dwelling place of the Puṇyajanas.
Going to the northern quarter, served by the attendants of <s>Rudra</s>, the king
saw, in a valley of the <s>Himavat</s>, a city crowded with Guhyakas.
The mighty-armed one blew his conch, making the sky and the directions resound,
and by that sound, O <s>Kṣattar</s>, the wives of the minor gods became greatly terrified, their eyes agitated.
Then the powerful great warriors among the upadevas came out,
and, unable to bear that roar, rushed against him with weapons raised.
That hero, the great chariot-warrior with the fierce bow, struck those who came rushing on,
all at once, each one separately, with three arrows apiece.

children.text: te vai lalāṭalagnaistairiṣubhiḥ sarva eva hi
children.translated_text: Indeed, with those arrows fixed in their foreheads, all of them
thought themselves defeated and praised that deed of his.
Yet they too, unable to endure him, like serpents unable to bear the touch of a foot,
pierced him all at once with arrows, wishing to repay him twofold.
Then with iron clubs, swords, spears, pikes, axes,
lances, missiles, bhuśuṇḍī weapons, brightly-feathered shafts, and arrows as well,
the enraged ones rained down blows upon him, together with his chariot and charioteer,
wanting to counter that attack, thirteen ayutas in number.
Then <s>Auttānapādi</s>, under that heavy shower of weapons,
was no longer visible, covered as a mountain is by a downpour.
At that very moment a cry of lament arose among the siddhas watching in heaven:
"This human sun has been slain, sunk in the ocean of the Puṇyajanas."
As the yātudhānas roared and shouted for victory in the battle,
his chariot rose up like the sun from mist.
Twanging his divine bow and bringing distress to his enemies,
he scattered the flood of missiles with arrows, as the wind scatters a mass of clouds.

children.text: tasya te cāpanirmuktā bhittvā varmāṇi rakṣasām
children.translated_text: Those arrows released from his bow pierced the armor of the rakṣasas
and entered their bodies, sharp as thunderbolts enter mountains.
With heads bearing lovely earrings cut off by crescent arrows,
with thighs like golden palm trunks, and with arms charming with bracelets,
with costly necklaces, armlets, crowns,
and turbans, those battlefields, strewn over, shone in a way that delighted heroes.
The other hosts of rakṣasas who remained alive in the arena of battle,
their limbs mostly severed by the arrows of the best of kṣatriyas, fled like herds of deer after a lion's play.

children.text: apaśyamānaḥ sa tadātatāyinaṃ mahāmṛdhe kaṃcana mānavottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that best of men, seeing no assailant at all in the great battle,

children.text: purīṃ didṛkṣannapi nāviśaddviṣāṃ na māyināṃ veda cikīrṣitaṃ janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: did not enter the enemies' city though he wished to see it, for people do not know what magicians intend to do.

children.text: iti bruvaṃścitrarathaḥ svasārathiṃ yattaḥ pareṣāṃ pratiyogaśaṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: Saying this to his charioteer, alert and suspicious of a counterstroke from the enemies,

children.text: śuśrāva śabdaṃ jaladheriveritaṃ nabhasvato dikṣu rajo 'nvadṛśyata ||
children.translated_text: he heard a sound like the ocean stirred up, and dust was seen in the directions, driven by the wind.
In a moment the sky was covered on every side by a mass of clouds,
with lightning flashing in the quarters and terrifying him with thunder.
They rained torrents of blood, gore, pus, feces, urine, and fat,
and headless trunks fell from the sky before him, O sinless one.
Then a mountain was seen in the sky, and from every direction there fell
maces, iron clubs, swords, and pestles, together with showers of stones.
Serpents breathing lightning and vomiting fire, with eyes enraged,
rushed at him, as did maddened elephants and troops of lions and tigers.
The ocean, terrible with waves and flooding the earth on every side,
approached with a great roar, fearful as at the end of an age.
The asuras, swift in their attacks, created many such terrors
by demonic magic, things that frighten the faint-hearted.
When the sages, having assembled, heard of that demonic magic, very hard to cross,
which the asuras had directed against <s>Dhruva</s>, they wished him well.
The sages said:

children.text: auttānapāda bhagavāṃstava śārṅgadhanvā devaḥ kṣiṇotvavanatārtiharo vipakṣān
children.translated_text: "O son of <s>Uttānapāda</s>, may the blessed god who bears the Śārṅga bow, the remover of the distress of those who bow down, destroy your enemies.

children.text: yannāmadheyamabhidhāya niśamya cāddhā loko 'ñjasā tarati dustaramaṅga mṛtyum ||
children.translated_text: By uttering and hearing his name directly, O dear one, people easily cross over death, which is so hard to cross."
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
When the blessed Lord of Wealth perceived that <s>Dhruva</s> had turned back from the slaughter and was free of anger,
he came there, praised by cāraṇas, yakṣas, and kinnaras, and addressed him as he stood with joined palms.
<s>Dhanada</s> said:
"O scion of kṣatriyas, O sinless one, I am pleased with you,
because, at your grandfather's command, you gave up an enmity difficult to abandon.
You did not kill the yakṣas, nor did the yakṣas kill your brother;
Time alone is the lord of the birth and dissolution of beings.
The thought, 'I am this and you are that,' is meaningless, for it arises from a person's ignorance.
It appears like something in a dream through meditation on what is not real, and through it bondage and its reversal arise.
Therefore go, <s>Dhruva</s>; welfare to you. Worship the Blessed <s>Adhokṣaja</s>,
whose form is the self of all beings, with the disposition that he is the self in every being.
Worship his feet, worthy of worship, for the sake of ending becoming; he cuts off worldly existence,
being both joined with and separate from his power, his own māyā made of the guṇas.
Choose the desire that is in your mind from me without hesitation, O king, O son of <s>Uttānapāda</s>.
You are worthy of a boon, dear one, for we have heard that you are ever near the lotus feet of the Lotus-naveled Lord."
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: sa rājarājena varāya codito dhruvo mahābhāgavato mahāmatiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus urged by the king of kings to choose a boon, <s>Dhruva</s>, the great devotee and great-minded one,

children.text: harau sa vavre 'calitāṃ smṛtiṃ yayā taratyayatnena duratyayaṃ tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: chose unwavering remembrance of <s>Hari</s>, by which one effortlessly crosses the darkness that is so hard to cross.
Then <s>Aiḍaviḍa</s>, pleased in mind, gave that to him,
and vanished while he watched; he too returned to his own city.
Then he worshipped the Lord of Sacrifice with rites rich in sacrificial gifts,
the giver of the fruit of action in the sphere of materials, ritual acts, and deities.
Bearing an intense flood of devotion toward <s>Acyuta</s>, the Self of all, who is beyond all,
he saw that same all-pervading one established in himself and in all beings.
The people regarded him, thus endowed with good conduct, devoted to brahmanical order, and affectionate to the poor,
as the protector of the bridges of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), and as their father.
For thirty-six thousand years he ruled the circle of the earth,
exhausting merit through enjoyments and exhausting evil through renunciations.
Thus the great-souled one, whose senses were unmoving, passed a long time rich in sacrifices,
and, having led a life suitable for the three aims of life, handed the royal throne to his son.
He regarded this whole universe, fashioned by <s>māyā</s> (cosmic illusion), as existing in the self,
like a dream or a city of Gandharvas fashioned by ignorance.
His self, wife, children, friends, army, wealth, treasury, inner apartments, and charming pleasure grounds,

children.text: bhūmaṇḍalaṃ jaladhimekhalamākalayya kālopasṛṣṭamiti sa prayayau viśālām ||
children.translated_text: and the earth encircled by the ocean as by a girdle, he understood to be seized by Time; then he set out for <s>Viśālā</s>.
There, with his faculties purified, after bathing in auspicious water, he fixed his seat, conquered his breath, and drew in his senses with his mind.
Meditating on this gross form that is a likeness of the Blessed Lord, with no separation from him, he cast off the body in <s>samādhi</s>.
While devotion to <s>Hari</s>, the Blessed Lord, flowed in him unceasingly, he was repeatedly overwhelmed by droplets of tears of bliss.
His heart melted, his limbs were covered with horripilation, and, freed from the sign of embodied existence, he no longer remembered himself.
<s>Dhruva</s> saw a supreme celestial vehicle descending from the sky,
making the ten directions shine like the full moon newly risen.
There, next to it, stood two foremost gods, four-armed, dark-blue, youthful, and with eyes like red lotuses.
They leaned upon their maces, wore fine garments, and were adorned with crowns, necklaces, armlets, and lovely earrings.
Recognizing them as servants of <s>Uttamagāya</s>, he rose up, his proper procedure forgotten through awe,
and, with joined palms, he bowed to those chief attendants while uttering the names of <s>Madhudviṣ</s>.
To him, whose mind was fixed on the feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose palms were joined and whose neck was bowed low in reverence,
<s>Sunanda</s> and <s>Nanda</s>, esteemed by the lotus-naveled Lord, came near and spoke with a smile.
<s>Sunanda</s> and <s>Nanda</s> said:

children.text: bho bho rājansubhadraṃ te vācaṃ no 'vahitaḥ śṛṇu
children.translated_text: O king, O king, may there be good fortune for you. Listen attentively to our words.
You are the one who, at five years old, satisfied the god by austerity.
We two are attendants of that god, the bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s>, the sustainer of the whole universe,
and we have come here to lead you to the Blessed Lord's abode.

children.text: sudurjayaṃ viṣṇupadaṃ jitaṃ tvayā yatsūrayo 'prāpya vicakṣate param
children.translated_text: You have won the very hard-to-conquer <s>Viṣṇupada</s>, which seers, unable to attain it, behold as supreme.
Take your place there; the moon, the sun, the planets, the lunar mansions, and the stars circle it to the right.
Never at any time has it been occupied by your fathers, O dear one, nor by others either.

children.text: ātiṣṭha jagatāṃ vandyaṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: Take your place in that highest station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, worshipped by the worlds.
This foremost celestial vehicle has been brought near by <s>Uttamaśloka</s>, the crowned Lord,
and you, long-lived one, are worthy to ascend it.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Hearing the honey-sweet speech of the two chief appointees of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the beloved of <s>Urukrama</s>
bathed, performed his daily auspicious rites, bowed to the sages, and respectfully received their blessings.
Having circumambulated and worshipped the foremost aerial abode, and having bowed to the attendants,
he wished to take his place upon it, bearing a golden form.
Then the son of <s>Uttānapāda</s> saw Death arrived before him.
Placing his foot on the head of Death, he mounted the wondrous abode.
Then kettledrums resounded, along with mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas, and other instruments.
The chief Gandharvas sang, and showers of flowers fell.
As <s>Dhruva</s> was about to ascend to heaven, he remembered <s>Sunīti</s>, his mother:
"How shall I go to <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>, leaving behind that helpless woman?"
When this was his settled resolve, the two excellent gods, understanding his determination,
showed him the goddess going ahead before him in a vehicle.

children.text: tatra tatra praśaṃsadbhiḥ pathi vaimānikaiḥ suraiḥ
children.translated_text: Along the path, by gods in aerial cars who praised him here and there,
he was showered with flowers, and he gradually saw the planets.
By the path of the gods he passed beyond the three worlds and even beyond the sages,
and then reached, beyond them, the station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the fixed course of <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: yadbhrājamānaṃ svarucaiva sarvato lokāstrayo hyanu vibhrājanta ete
children.translated_text: Shining everywhere by its own radiance, it is that after which these three worlds shine.

children.text: yannāvrajanjantuṣu ye 'nanugrahā vrajanti bhadrāṇi caranti ye 'niśam ||
children.translated_text: Those among creatures who are without divine favor do not go there; those who constantly perform blessed deeds do go there.
Peaceful, equal-sighted, pure, and pleasing to all beings,
the dear companions of <s>Acyuta</s> go easily to the abode of <s>Acyuta</s>.
Thus <s>Dhruva</s>, the son of <s>Uttānapāda</s>, devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
became like the spotless crest-jewel of the three worlds.
O <s>Kauravya</s>, in him the deep-rolling, unblinking wheel of the luminaries is fixed,
and it turns as a herd of cattle turns around a central post.
Seeing his greatness, the blessed sage <s>Nārada</s>
strummed his instrument and sang verses in the sacrificial session of the <s>Pracetas</s>.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: nūnaṃ sunīteḥ patidevatāyāstapaḥprabhāvasya sutasya tāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: Surely, seeing that destiny of the son of <s>Sunīti</s>, faithful to her husband, whose greatness came from austerity,

children.text: dṛṣṭvābhyupāyānapi vedavādino naivādhigantuṃ prabhavanti kiṃ nṛpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: even those who teach the Veda cannot attain it by ritual means; how then could kings?

children.text: yaḥ pañcavarṣo gurudāravākśarairbhinnena yāto hṛdayena dūyatā
children.translated_text: At five years old, wounded in his heart by the sharp words of his father's wife and deeply pained,

children.text: vanaṃ madādeśakaro 'jitaṃ prabhuṃ jigāya tadbhaktaguṇaiḥ parājitam ||
children.translated_text: he went to the forest, following my instruction, and conquered the unconquered Lord, who is conquered by the virtues of his devotees.
What mere kinsman of warriors on earth could climb, even over many years, to the height he ascended?
For at five or six years old, in only a few days, he propitiated <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and obtained that station.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
All this has been told to you here, everything about which I was asked by you,
the conduct of <s>Dhruva</s> of lofty fame, approved by the good.
It brings blessedness, fame, long life, merit, and great welfare;
it leads to heaven, firmness, gladness of mind, excellence, and the wiping away of sin.
By repeatedly hearing with faith this activity dear to <s>Acyuta</s>,
there would arise devotion to the Blessed Lord, by which affliction is destroyed.
For those who desire greatness, it is a tīrtha; in the hearer arise virtues such as good conduct;
in those who desire splendor, splendor arises, and in the high-minded, honor.
With self-control one should recite, in the morning in an assembly of twice-born men,

children.text: sāyaṃ ca puṇyaślokasya dhruvasya caritaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: and in the evening too, the great story of <s>Dhruva</s>, whose fame is holy.
On the full-moon day, on <s>Sinīvālī</s>, on the twelfth lunar day, or under <s>Śravaṇa</s>,
at the end of the day, at <s>Vyatīpāta</s>, at a solar transition, or even on Sunday,
one who has taken refuge at the feet of the Lord of tīrthas should cause faithful people to hear it;
not desiring anything there for himself, being satisfied within himself, he attains perfection.
The compassionate man who gives immortal knowledge on the true path to one who does not know reality,
to one who is poor and without a protector, is favored by the gods.

children.text: idaṃ mayā te 'bhihitaṃ kurūdvaha dhruvasya vikhyātaviśuddhakarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: This has been told by me to you, O best of the Kurus: the story of <s>Dhruva</s>, whose deeds are famed and pure,

children.text: hitvārbhakaḥ krīḍanakāni māturgṛhaṃ ca viṣṇuṃ śaraṇaṃ yo jagāma ||
children.translated_text: who, as a small child, abandoned his mother's toys and home and went to <s>Viṣṇu</s> for refuge.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Hearing from <s>Kauṣāravi</s> the account of <s>Dhruva</s>'s ascent to the station of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,

children.text: prarūḍhabhāvo bhagavatyadhokṣaje praṣṭuṃ punastaṃ viduraḥ pracakrame ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidura</s>, whose feeling for the Blessed <s>Adhokṣaja</s> had fully grown, began again to question him.
<s>Vidura</s> said:

children.text: ke te pracetaso nāma kasyāpatyāni suvrata
children.translated_text: Who were those named the <s>Pracetas</s>, O virtuous one? Whose offspring were they?
In whose lineage were they renowned, and where did they perform the sacrificial session?
I think the great devotee <s>Nārada</s>, seer of the gods,
was the one by whom <s>kriyāyoga</s> (ritual practice), the rule of service to <s>Hari</s>, was taught.
For the Blessed Lord, the Person of the sacrifice,
was indeed worshipped with devotion by men devoted to their own <s>svadharma</s> (proper duty), as instructed by <s>Nārada</s>.
Those stories of the Blessed Lord that were described there by the divine seer,
please tell them to me in full, O <s>brahman</s>, for I am eager to hear.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: dhruvasya cotkalaḥ putraḥ pitari prasthite vanam
children.translated_text: <s>Dhruva</s>'s son <s>Utkala</s>, when his father had departed to the forest,
did not desire universal royal fortune, his father's sovereign throne.
By birth he was one whose self was at peace, free from attachment, and equal in vision;
he saw the self spread out in the world and the world within the self.
He saw the self as <s>brahman</s>, nirvāṇa, with embodied form set aside,
as the unity whose essence is the relish of awakening, uninterrupted bliss.
By the unbroken fire of yoga his actions, impurities, and dispositions were burned away;
grasping his own true form, he then saw nothing other than the self.
He appeared like one dull, blind, deaf, mad, or mute, without apparent understanding,
noticed by boys on the road like a fire whose flame has grown calm.
Thinking him dull and mad, the elders of the family together with the ministers
made <s>Vatsara</s>, the younger son of <s>Bhrami</s>, king.
<s>Svarvīthi</s>, the beloved wife of <s>Vatsara</s>, bore six sons:

children.text: puṣpārṇaṃ tigmaketuṃ ca iṣamūrjaṃ vasuṃ jayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣpārṇa</s>, <s>Tigmaketu</s>, <s>Iṣa</s>, <s>Ūrja</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, and <s>Jaya</s>.

children.text: puṣpārṇasya prabhā bhāryā doṣā ca dve babhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣpārṇa</s> had two wives, <s>Prabhā</s> and <s>Doṣā</s>;
<s>Prātah</s>, <s>Madhyandina</s>, and <s>Sāyam</s> were the sons of <s>Prabhā</s>.
<s>Pradoṣa</s>, <s>Niśītha</s>, and <s>Vyuṣṭa</s> were the three sons of <s>Doṣā</s>;
<s>Vyuṣṭa</s> begot in <s>Puṣkariṇī</s> a son named <s>Sarvatejas</s>.

children.text: sa cakṣuḥ sutamākūtyāṃ patnyāṃ manumavāpa ha
children.translated_text: That <s>Sarvatejas</s>, by his wife <s>Ākūti</s>, obtained a son, <s>Cakṣus Manu</s>;
the queen of <s>Manu</s>, <s>Naḍvalā</s>, bore sons free from passion:

children.text: puruṃ kutsaṃ tritaṃ dyumnaṃ satyavantamṛtaṃ vratam
children.translated_text: <s>Puru</s>, <s>Kutsa</s>, <s>Trita</s>, <s>Dyumna</s>, <s>Satyavant</s>, <s>Ṛta</s>, <s>Vrata</s>,
<s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, <s>Atīrātra</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Śibi</s>, and <s>Ulmuka</s>.
<s>Ulmuka</s> begot in <s>Puṣkariṇī</s> six excellent sons:
<s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Sumanas</s>, <s>Khyāti</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and <s>Gaya</s>.
<s>Sunīthā</s>, the wife of <s>Aṅga</s>, gave birth to the fierce <s>Vena</s>;
because of his bad conduct that royal sage, becoming disheartened, left the city.

children.text: yamaṅga śepuḥ kupitā vāgvajrā munayaḥ kila
children.translated_text: Angry sages, it is said, cursed that <s>Vena</s> with thunderbolt-like words;
when his life had departed, they again churned his right hand.

children.text: arājake tadā loke dasyubhiḥ pīḍitāḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: At that time, when the world had no king and the subjects were oppressed by bandits,
<s>Pṛthu</s>, the first lord of the earth, was born with a portion of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
How did that righteous, great-souled king, a treasure-house of character and devoted to the brahmans,
come to have a wicked son, because of whom he went away with a troubled mind?
Or what sin did <s>Vena</s> commit, on account of which they applied the brahmanical punishment
against a king who bore the discipline of punishment, those sages learned in dharma?
A protector of subjects should not be slighted by his subjects, even if he is sinful,
because by his own splendor he bears the power of the world-protectors.
Tell me this, O <s>brahman</s>, the behavior of the son of <s>Sunīthā</s>;
I am faithful and devoted, and you are the best knower of higher and lower things.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
The royal sage <s>Aṅga</s> undertook an <s>aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice), a great rite;
the deities, though summoned there by the expounders of sacred speech, did not come.
Then the priests there, astonished, said to the sacrificer:

children.text: havīṃṣi hūyamānāni na te gṛhṇanti devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The deities do not accept the oblations that are being offered by you.
O king, your oblations are unspoiled and have been prepared with faith;
the Vedic hymns, not stale or ineffectual, have been employed by disciplined observers of vows.
We do not know here even the slightest offense against the gods
because of which these gods, witnesses of the rite, do not accept their own shares.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having heard the words of the twice-born, the sacrificer <s>Aṅga</s> was deeply downcast.
With the permission of the members of the sacrificial assembly, he uttered speech in order to question them about that.
The gods, though invited, do not come; here they do not accept the sacrificial portions.
O lords of the assembly, tell me: what fault has been committed by me?
The lords of the assembly said:
O king, here there is not yet the slightest sin present in you.
There is one sin from a former time, if in this life you are childless in this way.

children.text: tathā sādhaya bhadraṃ te ātmānaṃ suprajaṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: Therefore accomplish this, O king, and may there be welfare for you: make yourself possessed of good offspring.
When worshipped by you, who desire a son, the enjoyer of the sacrifice will give you a son.
Then the dwellers in heaven will accept their own shares
if <s>Hari</s> himself, the sacrificial Person, is chosen for the sake of offspring.
<s>Hari</s> gives to people each of those desires which they desire.
According as he is worshipped, so the fruit arises for human beings.
Thus resolved, the brahmins, for the birth of that king's offspring,
offered a sacrificial cake to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, called <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>.
From that arose a man, wearing a golden garland and spotless garments,
holding in a golden vessel cooked milk-rice.
With the brahmins' approval, the noble-minded king took the rice with joined palms,
smelled it, and, filled with joy, gave it to his wife.

children.text: sā tatpuṃsavanaṃ rājñī prāśya vai patyurādadhe
children.translated_text: The queen ate that means of producing a male child, and by her husband conceived
a pregnancy; when the proper time had come, though previously childless, she gave birth to a boy.
Even as a boy that person followed his maternal grandfather.
He had arisen from a portion of <s>Adharma</s> in the line of <s>Mṛtyu</s>; through that he became unrighteous.
Taking up his bow and moving through the forest as a hunter,
the wicked one killed helpless animals; the people cried, "This is <s>Vena</s>!"
When boys of his own age were playing in the playground, that very cruel one
forcibly and without pity killed them, as if killing beasts.
Seeing that wicked son, the king tried by many disciplines
to control him; when he was unable to control him, he became intensely downcast.
Generally, god is worshipped by those householders who have no children,

children.text: kadapatyabhṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ ye na vindanti durbharam ||
children.translated_text: because they do not experience the unbearable misery borne by a bad child.
For from that comes a most sinful reputation and a great unrighteousness among men;
from that comes conflict with everyone, and from that unending mental anguish.
What wise man would greatly value that mere name of offspring,

children.text: paṇḍito bahu manyeta yadarthāḥ kleśadā gṛhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: a bond of delusion for oneself, for whose sake homes become sources of distress?
I think a bad child is better than a good child, who is a seat of sorrows,
because a mortal may become detached from his home, since homes are masses of distress.

children.text: evaṃ sa nirviṇṇamanā nṛpo gṛhānniśītha utthāya mahodayodayāt
children.translated_text: Thus, with his mind disenchanted, the king rose from his home at midnight, from the rise of great distress.
Sleepless and unnoticed by his people, he went away, leaving <s>Vena</s>'s mother sleeping.

children.text: vijñāya nirvidya gataṃ patiṃ prajāḥ purohitāmātyasuhṛdgaṇādayaḥ
children.translated_text: When the subjects, the priests, ministers, groups of friends, and others learned that their lord had gone away in detachment,
they searched the earth, overwhelmed by excessive grief, like unskilled yogins searching for a hidden person.

children.text: alakṣayantaḥ padavīṃ prajāpaterhatodyamāḥ pratyupasṛtya te purīm
children.translated_text: Not seeing the path of the lord of the people, their efforts frustrated, they returned to the city.
With tears, after bowing to the assembled sages, they reported, O <s>Paurava</s>, the loss of their protector.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Those sages beginning with <s>Bhṛgu</s>, who saw to the welfare of the worlds,
observed that, when there was no protector, human beings became like beasts.
The speakers of sacred knowledge summoned <s>Sunīthā</s>, the mother of the hero,
and consecrated <s>Vena</s>, though disapproved by the subjects by nature, as lord of the earth.
Hearing that <s>Vena</s>, whose punishment was exceedingly fierce, had ascended the royal seat,
the bandits at once hid themselves, like mice terrified by a snake.
Having mounted the place of kingship, he became swollen with the eight royal powers.
Stiff with pride and self-conceit, he disrespected the greatly fortunate ones.

children.text: evaṃ madāndha utsikto niraṅkuśa iva dvipaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, blinded by pride and arrogant, like an elephant without a goad,
he roamed about, mounted on his chariot, as if shaking heaven and earth.

children.text: na yaṣṭavyaṃ na dātavyaṃ na hotavyaṃ dvijāḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: "No sacrifice is to be performed, no gift is to be given, no oblation is to be offered anywhere, O twice-borns";
with this proclamation by drumbeat he stopped <s>dharma</s> everywhere.
Seeing the conduct of ill-behaved <s>Vena</s>,
the sages engaged in sacrifice considered the people's calamity and spoke with compassion.

children.text: aho ubhayataḥ prāptaṃ lokasya vyasanaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Alas, a great calamity for the people has arrived from both sides,
as when a log is burning at both ends, from bandits and from the protector.
Because of the fear of anarchy, this man, though unworthy of it, was made king.
But now fear has arisen even from him; how can there be well-being for embodied beings?
Like nourishing a snake with milk, he brings harm even to the one who nourishes him.
<s>Vena</s> is wicked by nature, born from the womb of <s>Sunīthā</s>.

children.text: nirūpitaḥ prajāpālaḥ sa jighāṃsati vai prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Appointed as guardian of the subjects, he indeed seeks to kill the subjects.
Even so, let us pacify him, so that his sin may not touch us.
For <s>Vena</s>, though of evil conduct, was made king by us who know better.

children.text: sāntvito yadi no vācaṃ na grahīṣyatyadharmakṛt ||
children.translated_text: If, when conciliated, he does not accept our word, being a doer of unrighteousness,
we shall burn up, by our own fiery power, this man scorched already by the censure of the world.
Having resolved thus, the sages, their anger concealed,
approached <s>Vena</s> and addressed him after pacifying him with conciliatory words.
The sages said:
Best of kings, listen to this that we declare to you, sir.
It will increase your life, prosperity, strength, and fame, dear one.
<s>Dharma</s>, practiced by men through speech, mind, body, and intellect,
bestows sorrowless worlds and then endlessness upon those who are unattached.

children.text: sa te mā vinaśedvīra prajānāṃ kṣemalakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Let that <s>dharma</s>, O hero, whose mark is the welfare of the subjects, not perish for you.
When it is destroyed, the king falls down from sovereignty.
O king, a ruler protects his subjects from wicked ministers, thieves, and the like;

children.text: rakṣanyathā baliṃ gṛhṇanniha pretya ca modate ||
children.translated_text: taking tribute properly, he rejoices both here and after death.
In whose kingdom and city the Blessed Lord, the <s>Yajñapuruṣa</s> (person of sacrifice),
is worshipped by people endowed with the orders of class and life, each according to his own <s>dharma</s> (duty),
for that king, O greatly fortunate one, the Blessed Lord, source of all beings,
the soul of the universe, is pleased while he abides within his own ordinance.
When he is pleased, what is unattainable, since he is lord of the lords of the worlds?
The worlds, together with their guardians, respectfully bring tribute to him.
He gathers together all worlds, immortals, and sacrifices; he consists of the three Vedas, of sacrificial substances, and of austerity.
O king, for your prosperity you should allow your own lands to worship him with manifold sacrifices.

children.text: yajñena yuṣmadviṣaye dvijātibhirvitāyamānena surāḥ kalā hareḥ
children.translated_text: Through sacrifice being extended in your realm by the twice-born, the gods, who are portions of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: sviṣṭāḥ sutuṣṭāḥ pradiśanti vāñchitaṃ taddhelanaṃ nārhasi vīra ceṣṭitum ||
children.translated_text: well honored and fully satisfied, grant what is desired; you ought not, O hero, act in contempt of that.
<s>Vena</s> said:

children.text: bāliśā bata yūyaṃ vā adharme dharmamāninaḥ
children.translated_text: Foolish indeed are you, considering <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) to be <s>dharma</s> (righteousness),

children.text: ye vṛttidaṃ patiṃ hitvā jāraṃ patimupāsate ||
children.translated_text: you who abandon the husband who gives you livelihood and worship a paramour as husband.
These fools insult the Lord who has the form of a king;

children.text: nānuvindanti te bhadramiha loke paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: they obtain no welfare in this world or in the next.

children.text: ko yajñapuruṣo nāma yatra vo bhaktirīdṛśī
children.translated_text: What is this so-called person of sacrifice, for whom you have such devotion,
like that of bad women, far removed from love for their husbands, toward a paramour?
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Viriñca</s>, <s>Giriśa</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Ravi</s>,
<s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Kṣiti</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Apāmpati</s>,

children.text: ete cānye ca vibudhāḥ prabhavo varaśāpayoḥ
children.translated_text: these and other gods, powers over boons and curses,
exist in the body of the king; the king consists of all the gods.
Therefore, brahmins, worship me with rites, free from envy,

children.text: baliṃ ca mahyaṃ harata matto 'nyaḥ ko 'grabhuk pumān ||
children.translated_text: and bring tribute to me; what man other than I is the first enjoyer?
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Thus the very sinful one, whose understanding was reversed and who had gone onto a wrong path,
though being conciliated, did not carry out that request, for his auspiciousness had fallen away.
Thus those twice-borns, disrespected by him, who imagined himself learned,
became angry at him, O <s>Vidura</s>, when their wholesome request had been broken.
"Kill him, kill him! This sinner is fierce by nature;
if he lives, he will surely and quickly reduce the world to ashes.
This man of evil conduct does not deserve the excellent throne of a god among men,
for without shame he reviles <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord presiding over sacrifice.
Who indeed, except this one inauspicious <s>Vena</s>, would censure him,
having attained such sovereignty as a recipient of his favor?"
Having thus resolved to kill him, the sages, their anger grown strong,
slew <s>Vena</s> with their cries of huṃ, though he had already been slain by reviling <s>Acyuta</s>.
When the sages had gone to their own hermitage,
the grieving <s>Sunīthā</s> preserved her son's body by the power of knowledge.
One day those sages, bathed in the waters of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
offered into the fires and, seated on the riverbank, spoke sacred tales.
Seeing omens then arising, terrifying to the world,
they said, "May no misfortune come to the helpless earth from bandits."
As the sages were reflecting in this way,
a great dust cloud rose from thieves racing in every direction as they plundered.
Recognizing that disturbance among the people caused by men plundering wealth,
and by men intent on killing one another when that ruler had passed away,
they did not restrain the country, which had become mostly thieves, weak in spirit, and kingless,
though they were capable and saw the fault in that condition.
A brahmin who is impartial and peaceful, yet neglects the afflicted,
lets even his sacred power leak away, like milk from a cracked vessel.
"This lineage of the royal sage <s>Aṅga</s> ought not come to an end;
for kings in this lineage, sheltered by <s>Keśava</s>, have unfailing power."
Having decided thus, the sages forcefully churned the thigh
of the dead king; there appeared a man, <s>Bāhuka</s>.
He was black as a crow, with extremely short limbs, short arms, and a great jaw,
with short feet, the tip of his nose depressed, red eyes, and copper-colored hair.

children.text: taṃ tu te 'vanataṃ dīnaṃ kiṃ karomīti vādinam
children.translated_text: To him, bowed down and miserable, saying, "What shall I do?"
they said, "Sit down," O dear one; therefore he became <s>Niṣāda</s>.
His descendants are the <s>Naiṣādas</s>, moving through mountains and forests,
because, as he was born, the fierce impurity of <s>Vena</s> was carried away by him.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Then again, from the two arms being churned by the brahmins
of that sonless king, a male-and-female pair appeared.
Seeing that pair born, the sages, speakers of sacred truth,
recognized a portion of the Blessed Lord and spoke in great delight.
The sages said:
This is a portion of the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, protector of the worlds,
and this woman is a manifestation of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, inseparable from the <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ tu prathamo rājñāṃ pumānprathayitā yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: This man will be foremost among kings, a spreader of fame;
he will be a great king named <s>Pṛthu</s>, of wide renown.
And this fair-toothed goddess, adorned with the ornament of virtues,
named <s>Arci</s>, with beautiful hips, will choose <s>Pṛthu</s> alone.
This one is directly a portion of <s>Hari</s>, born for the protection of the world,
and this woman, devoted to him, is indeed <s>Śrī</s>, born as his inseparable companion.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: praśaṃsanti sma taṃ viprā gandharvapravarā jaguḥ
children.translated_text: The brahmins praised him, and the foremost <s>Gandharvas</s> sang;
the <s>Siddhas</s> released showers of flowers, and the women of heaven danced.
Conches, trumpets, mṛdaṅgas, and other instruments, and kettledrums sounded in heaven.
There all the hosts of the divine sages and the <s>Pitṛs</s> came together.
<s>Brahmā</s>, the teacher of the world, arrived there together with the gods and the lords of the gods.

children.text: vainyasya dakṣiṇe haste dṛṣṭvā cihnaṃ gadābhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing on <s>Vainya</s>'s right hand the mark of the mace-bearer,

children.text: pādayoraravindaṃ ca taṃ vai mene hareḥ kalām
children.translated_text: and a lotus on his feet, he indeed regarded him as a portion of <s>Hari</s>.
He whose wheel is unobstructed is a portion of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
His consecration was begun by brahmins who spoke of <s>Brahman</s>.
From every side the people brought him the materials for consecration.

children.text: saritsamudrā girayo nāgā gāvaḥ khagā mṛgāḥ
children.translated_text: Rivers, oceans, mountains, serpents, cows, birds, and beasts,
heaven, earth, and all beings brought offerings.
Consecrated, the great king, dressed in fine garments and well adorned,
shone with his ornamented wife <s>Arciṣ</s>, like another fire.

children.text: tasmai jahāra dhanado haimaṃ vīra varāsanam
children.translated_text: <s>Dhanada</s> brought him, O hero, a golden excellent throne,
and <s>Varuṇa</s> a moon-bright umbrella dripping water.
<s>Vāyu</s> brought yak-tail fans, <s>Dharma</s> a garland made of fame,
<s>Indra</s> an excellent crown, and <s>Yama</s> a restraining staff.
<s>Brahmā</s> brought armor made of <s>Brahman</s>, and <s>Bhāratī</s> an excellent necklace.
<s>Hari</s> brought the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus, and his wife unfailing prosperity.
<s>Rudra</s> brought a sword marked with ten moons, and <s>Ambikā</s> likewise a shield marked with a hundred moons.
<s>Soma</s> brought horses made of nectar, and <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> a chariot that was the seat of beauty.
<s>Agni</s> brought a bow of horn, and <s>Sūrya</s> arrows made of rays.
<s>Bhūḥ</s> brought yogic sandals, and <s>Dyauḥ</s> a garland of flowers every day.
The sky-goers brought drama, excellent song, instrumental music, and invisibility.
The sages brought true blessings, and the ocean a conch born from itself.
The seas, mountains, and rivers provided chariot roads for the great-souled one.
Then the <s>Sūta</s>, the <s>Māgadha</s>, and the panegyrist stood near to praise him.
Not welcoming those praisers, mighty <s>Pṛthu Vainya</s>,
smiling, spoke this in a voice like the rumbling of clouds.
<s>Pṛthu</s> said:

children.text: bhoḥ sūta he māgadha saumya vandinloke 'dhunāspaṣṭaguṇasya me syāt
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>, O <s>Māgadha</s>, gentle panegyrist, since my qualities are now not yet manifest in the world,

children.text: kimāśrayo me stava eṣa yojyatāṃ mā mayyabhūvanvitathā giro vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: on what basis should this praise of me be applied? Let your words about me not become false.
Therefore, later, when matters concerning us have been heard indirectly, you whose speech is fitting may make sufficient praise.
In proclaiming the qualities of one worthy of the highest verses, respectable people do not praise what is contemptible.
What man, able to make great qualities belong to himself, has flatterers praise him even for qualities that are not there?
A fool, deceived by the thought, 'They will arise in him,' does not realize that he is a laughingstock among people.
For powerful men, even when famous, are ashamed of praise of themselves,
being modest and exceedingly noble, and also of a censured display of manliness.
But we are still unknown in the world, O <s>Sūta</s> and the rest, through excellent deeds.
How shall we cause ourselves to be sung like a child?
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
As the king was speaking thus, the singers, urged by the sages,
praised him with delighted minds, having savored the nectar of his speech.

children.text: nālaṃ vayaṃ te mahimānuvarṇane yo devavaryo 'vatatāra māyayā
children.translated_text: We are not capable of describing your greatness, you best of gods, who descended through <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: venāṅgajātasya ca pauruṣāṇi te vācaspatīnāmapi babhramurdhiyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even the minds of masters of speech are bewildered by your heroic deeds, born from the body of <s>Vena</s>.
Nevertheless, honoring the nectar of the story of generous-famed <s>Pṛthu</s>, a partial descent of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: yathopadeśaṃ munibhiḥ pracoditāḥ ślāghyāni karmāṇi vayaṃ vitanmahi ||
children.translated_text: and prompted by the sages according to their instruction, we shall unfold his praiseworthy deeds.
This one is the best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>, causing the world to follow <s>dharma</s>.
He is the protector of the bridges of <s>dharma</s> and the chastiser of those who oppose them.
This one alone bears in his body the bodies of the guardians of the world,
at each proper time, according to each share, for the welfare of both worlds.

children.text: vasu kāla upādatte kāle cāyaṃ vimuñcati
children.translated_text: At the proper time he takes up wealth, and at the proper time he releases it.
Equal toward all beings, the mighty one shines like the sun.
<s>Vainya</s> will endure the offense even of those who tread upon him from above.
He is compassionate toward beings and always behaves like the earth toward the afflicted.
When the god does not rain, this god, <s>Hari</s> in the body of a king among men,
will easily protect the subjects whose lives are distressed, like <s>Indra</s>.
He refreshes the world with the nectar-like form of his face,
with his loving glance, clear smile, and beauty.
His path is unmanifest, his plans hidden, his insight deep, and his wealth well guarded.
<s>Pṛthu</s>, the sole abode of limitless greatness and virtue, is self-contained like <s>Pracetā</s>.
Hard to approach and hard to withstand, though near he is like one far away.
He cannot be overpowered at all, a fire arisen from the fire-sticks of <s>Vena</s>.
Through his agents he sees the actions of beings both within and without.
He is like an indifferent overseer, like the wind, like the self among embodied beings.
He does not punish one who is not punishable, even if he is the son of his enemies.
Standing on the path of <s>dharma</s>, he punishes even his own son if he deserves punishment.
This unobstructed wheel of <s>Pṛthu</s> will turn as far as Mount <s>Mānasa</s>,
as long as the blessed sun burns with its multitude of rays.
Because he will delight the world by his own deeds,
the subjects will call this one king for his acts that delight the mind.
Firm in vows, true to his promises, devoted to brahmins, and serving elders,
he will be a refuge for all beings, respectful, and affectionate toward the lowly.
Toward others' wives he will have the devotion due to mothers, and toward his wife he will be as toward half of his own self.
Toward his subjects he will be affectionately disposed like a father, and he will be a servant of those who speak of <s>Brahman</s>.
He will be dear to embodied beings like their own self and an increaser of the joy of his friends.
He is attached to the company of the unattached, and he bears the rod of punishment against the wicked.

children.text: ayaṃ tu sākṣādbhagavāṃstryadhīśaḥ kūṭastha ātmā kalayāvatīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But this one is directly the blessed Lord, the ruler of the threefold order, the unchanging self, descended with a portion of himself.
In him they see even the apparent diversity, fashioned by ignorance and without real purpose.

children.text: ayaṃ bhuvo maṇḍalam odayādrer goptaikavīro naradevanāthaḥ
children.translated_text: This lord of human rulers, the sole heroic protector of the circle of the earth from the eastern mountain onward,

children.text: āsthāya jaitraṃ rathamāttacāpaḥ paryasyate dakṣiṇato yathārkaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will move around it from the south like the sun, having mounted his victorious chariot and taken up his bow.

children.text: asmai nṛpālāḥ kila tatra tatra baliṃ hariṣyanti salokapālāḥ
children.translated_text: To him kings in each place, together with the guardians of their worlds, will surely bring tribute.

children.text: maṃsyanta eṣāṃ striya ādirājaṃ cakrāyudhaṃ tadyaśa uddharantyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their women, lifting up his fame, will regard him as the first king, bearing the discus as his weapon.

children.text: ayaṃ mahīṃ gāṃ duduhe 'dhirājaḥ prajāpatirvṛttikaraḥ prajānām
children.translated_text: This overlord, a <s>Prajāpati</s> who provides livelihood for his subjects, milked the earth as a cow.
Sportively splitting the mountains with the tip of his bow, he made the earth level, as <s>Indra</s> once did.
When he himself twanged the <s>Ājagava</s> bow and ranged over the earth, irresistible in battle,

children.text: tadā nililyurdiśi diśyasanto lāṅgūlamudyamya yathā mṛgendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the wicked hid themselves in every direction, like animals with tails raised before a lion.
He performed a hundred <s>aśvamedha</s> sacrifices at the place where the <s>Sarasvatī</s> appeared.
When the last was underway, <s>Purandara</s>, <s>Śatakratu</s>, stole his horse.
This king, meeting the blessed and peerless <s>Sanatkumāra</s> in the garden of his own palace,

children.text: ārādhya bhaktyālabhatāmalaṃ tajjñānaṃ yato brahma paraṃ vidanti ||
children.translated_text: worshiped him with devotion and obtained that stainless knowledge by which people know the supreme <s>brahman</s>.
Here and there, those very praises will be heard, for his valor is renowned.
<s>Pṛthu</s>, of vast prowess, will hear songs resting on himself.
Having conquered the quarters, his wheel unobstructed, and having uprooted the thorn of the world by his own brilliance,
praised by the lords of gods and asuras, that great-souled one will become the lord of the earth.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Thus the blessed <s>Vainya</s> had been proclaimed through his qualities and deeds.
After honoring and applauding them, he satisfied them with the gifts they desired.
He duly honored the social orders headed by the brahmins, and his servants, ministers, and priests,
as well as the townspeople, country people, guilds, and constituent bodies of the realm.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
Why did the many-formed earth take the form of a cow?

children.text: yāṃ dudoha pṛthustatra ko vatso dohanaṃ ca kim ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Pṛthu</s> milked her there, who was the calf, and what was the milking vessel?

children.text: prakṛtyā viṣamā devī kṛtā tena samā katham
children.translated_text: How was the goddess, uneven by nature, made level by him?

children.text: tasya medhyaṃ hayaṃ devaḥ kasya hetorapāharat ||
children.translated_text: For what reason did the god steal his consecrated horse?
After receiving knowledge together with realization from the blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, O brahman, the best knower of <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: labdhvā jñānaṃ savijñānaṃ rājarṣiḥ kāṃ gatiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: what goal did that royal sage attain?
And whatever else there is about <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the blessed Lord, the master,
the holy renown of the greatly renowned one, resting on the story of his former embodiment,
you should tell to me, devoted and attached to you and to <s>Adhokṣaja</s>.
He was the one who, in the form of <s>Vainya</s>, milked this earth.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus urged by <s>Vidura</s> concerning the story of <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
<s>Maitreya</s>, pleased at heart, praised him and replied.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
When <s>Pṛthu</s> had been consecrated, O <s>Aṅga</s>, and summoned by the brahmins as the protector of the people,

children.text: prajā niranne kṣitipṛṣṭha etya kṣutkṣāmadehāḥ patimabhyavocan ||
children.translated_text: his subjects, with bodies emaciated by hunger and without food on the surface of the earth, came and addressed their lord:

children.text: vayaṃ rājañ jāṭhareṇābhitaptā yathāgninā koṭarasthena vṛkṣāḥ
children.translated_text: O king, we are tormented by the belly's fire, like trees by a fire lodged in their hollows.

children.text: tvāmadya yātāḥ śaraṇaṃ śaraṇyaṃ yaḥ sādhito vṛttikaraḥ patirnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Today we have come to you for refuge, O shelter-giver, for you have been appointed as our lord who provides livelihood.
Therefore, O god of kings, let your honor strive here to give food to us, who are afflicted by hunger,

children.text: yāvanna naṅkṣyāmaha ujjhitorjā vārtāpatistvaṃ kila lokapālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: before we perish, drained of strength; for you are indeed the lord of livelihood and guardian of the world.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Hearing the pitiful lament of the subjects,
<s>Pṛthu</s> pondered long, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>, and he found the cause.
Having resolved thus by his understanding and taken up his bow,
he set an arrow against the earth, angry like <s>Tripurahā</s>.
The trembling earth, seeing him with his weapon raised,
became a cow and, truly terrified, ran away like a doe pursued by a hunter.
That son of <s>Vena</s>, enraged and with eyes very red, pursued her,

children.text: śaraṃ dhanuṣi saṃdhāya yatra yatra palāyate ||
children.translated_text: fixing an arrow on his bow wherever she fled.

children.text: sā diśo vidiśo devī rodasī cāntaraṃ tayoḥ
children.translated_text: The goddess ran through the directions and intermediate directions, through heaven and earth and the space between them,
and everywhere she saw him with his weapon still raised behind her.
Then, finding no protection in the world from <s>Vainya</s>, as subjects find none from death,
she turned back in terror, her heart in pain.
She said to the greatly fortunate one, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, O lover of the distressed:
Protect me also; you are established in the protection of beings.
Why, then, do you wish to kill me, who am helpless and have committed no offense?

children.text: ahaniṣyatkathaṃ yoṣāṃ dharmajña iti yo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: How could one who is considered a knower of <s>dharma</s> kill a woman?

children.text: praharanti na vai strīṣu kṛtāgaḥsvapi jantavaḥ
children.translated_text: Creatures do not strike women, even when they have committed an offense.
How much less should kings such as you, compassionate and loving toward the distressed, do so?

children.text: māṃ vipāṭyājarāṃ nāvaṃ yatra viśvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: If you split me open, the ageless boat on which the whole world is established,
how will you support yourself and these subjects upon the waters?
<s>Pṛthu</s> said:
O earth, I shall kill you, for you have turned away from my command.

children.text: bhāgaṃ barhiṣi yā vṛṅkte na tanoti ca no vasu ||
children.translated_text: You take your share on the sacrificial grass, but you do not extend wealth to us.
A cow that eats grass every day but does not yield milk from her udder

children.text: tasyāmevaṃ hi duṣṭāyāṃ daṇḍo nātra na śasyate ||
children.translated_text: is so wicked that punishment for her is certainly appropriate here.
The seeds of plants, formerly created by <s>Svayambhū</s>,
you do not release; you hold them within yourself, despising me, dull-witted one.
I shall quiet the lamentation of these people who are overcome by hunger and afflicted
with my arrows, and with your fat when you have been split open.
Whether a person is male, female, or neuter, if that base one is self-conceited
and without compassion for living beings, for kings the killing of such a one is no killing.

children.text: tvāṃ stabdhāṃ durmadāṃ nītvā māyāgāṃ tilaśaḥ śaraiḥ
children.translated_text: I will bring you, stubborn, greatly intoxicated with pride, a magical cow, to pieces with arrows,
and by the power of my own yoga I myself will sustain these subjects.
When he bore such an anger-filled form, like Death itself,
the Earth, bowing with joined palms and trembling, spoke.
<s>Dharā</s> said:

children.text: namaḥ parasmai puruṣāya māyayā vinyastanānātanave guṇātmane
children.translated_text: Obeisance to the supreme Person, whose many bodies are arranged by māyā and whose nature is the guṇas;
obeisance to him whose wave of bewilderment about substance, action, and agent is washed away by the experience of his own true form.
By whom I was fashioned as the abode of beings, by the creator from whom this aggregate of guṇa-born creation comes,

children.text: sa eva māṃ hantumudāyudhaḥ svarāḍ upasthito 'nyaṃ śaraṇaṃ kamāśraye ||
children.translated_text: that very self-ruler has approached, weapon raised, to kill me; what other refuge shall I seek?
He who in the beginning created this moving and unmoving world by his own māyā, resting on himself and beyond reasoning,

children.text: tayaiva so 'yaṃ kila goptumudyataḥ kathaṃ nu māṃ dharmaparo jighāṃsati ||
children.translated_text: by that same power is now intent on protecting it; how then does he, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, wish to kill me?
Surely, alas, the intention of the Lord is not perceived by people whose selves are untrained,

children.text: na lakṣyate yastvakarodakārayadyo 'neka ekaḥ parataśca īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of his unconquerable māyā: he who himself acted and caused action, who, though one, is many and is the Lord beyond all.
He who restrains this creation and the rest by his powers, whose forms are substance, action, instrument, and consciousness,

children.text: tasmai samunnaddhaniruddhaśaktaye namaḥ parasmai puruṣāya vedhase ||
children.translated_text: to him, whose powers are expanded and withdrawn, obeisance, to the supreme Person, the creator.
Indeed you, O mighty unborn lord, intending to establish the world made by yourself, consisting of beings, senses, and inner organ,
raised me up from <s>Rasātala</s> and the waters as the primeval Boar.

children.text: apāmupasthe mayi nāvyavasthitāḥ prajā bhavānadya rirakṣiṣuḥ kila
children.translated_text: When beings, not established upon me in the lap of the waters, were to be protected by you today,

children.text: sa vīramūrtiḥ samabhūddharādharo yo māṃ payasyugraśaro jighāṃsasi ||
children.translated_text: you became the heroic earth-bearer; yet now, with fierce arrows, you wish to kill me in the water.
Surely the intent of lords is not understood by people like us,
whose paths of thought are deluded by the māyā that creates their qualities; homage to those who make heroic fame.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having praised <s>Pṛthu</s> in this way, whose lip was quivering with anger,
the Earth, fearless, again spoke, steadying herself by herself.

children.text: saṃniyacchābhibho manyuṃ nibodha śrāvitaṃ ca me
children.translated_text: Restrain your anger, O lord, and understand what has been set forth by me;
a wise man takes the essence from every side, just as a honeybee does.
In this world and in the next, by sages who see reality,
methods have been seen and employed for the accomplishment of welfare for men.
The inferior man who properly follows those means shown by the ancients,
endowed with faith, readily attains the things to be attained.
But the ignorant man who disregards them and begins undertakings for his purposes on his own
has his purposes fail, though begun again and again.

children.text: purā sṛṣṭā hyoṣadhayo brahmaṇā yā viśāmpate
children.translated_text: The herbs that were created of old by <s>Brahmā</s>, O lord of the people,
I saw being consumed by wicked men who did not uphold their vows.
Since they were unprotected and disregarded by you guardians of the world,
and the world had become thievish, I swallowed the herbs meant for sacrifice.

children.text: nūnaṃ tā vīrudhaḥ kṣīṇā mayi kālena bhūyasā
children.translated_text: Surely those plants have wasted away within me over a very long time;
therefore you should take them by the method that has been seen.

children.text: vatsaṃ kalpaya me vīra yenāhaṃ vatsalā tava
children.translated_text: Arrange a calf for me, O hero, by which, loving my calf for your sake,
I shall milk out desired objects in the form of milk, along with a suitable milking arrangement.
And, mighty-armed one, arrange a milker for the beings, O nurturer of beings,
if Your Majesty desires nourishing food that is sought by all.

children.text: samāṃ ca kuru māṃ rājandevavṛṣṭaṃ yathā payaḥ
children.translated_text: Make me level, O king, so that rain sent by the gods, like milk,

children.text: apartāvapi bhadraṃ te upāvarteta me vibho ||
children.translated_text: may return to me even outside the proper season, O lord; welfare to you.

children.text: iti priyaṃ hitaṃ vākyaṃ bhuva ādāya bhūpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having accepted this dear and beneficial speech of the Earth, the king
made <s>Manu</s> the calf and milked all the herbs into his hand.
In the same way other wise beings everywhere took the essence;
after that, others milked her, made fruitful by <s>Pṛthu</s>, according to their desire.
Then the seers milked the goddess into the senses, O best one,
