making <s>Bṛhaspati</s> the calf, obtaining pure milk consisting of Vedic metres.
The hosts of gods made <s>Indra</s> the calf and milked soma,
with a golden vessel, as milk in the form of vigor, vitality, and strength.
The Daityas and Dānavas appointed <s>Prahlāda</s>, bull among asuras, as their calf
and milked liquor as milk into an iron vessel.
The Gandharvas and Apsarases milked milk into a lotus-made vessel,

children.text: vatsaṃ viśvāvasuṃ kṛtvā gāndharvaṃ madhu saubhagam ||
children.translated_text: making <s>Viśvāvasu</s> the calf: Gandharva sweetness and beauty.
With <s>Aryaman</s> as calf, the Fathers milked kavya, the ancestral oblation, as milk
into an unbaked earthen vessel, those greatly fortunate deities of the śrāddha, with faith.
Having appointed <s>Kapila</s> as calf, the Siddhas milked perfection made of intention,

children.text: siddhiṃ nabhasi vidyāṃ ca ye ca vidyādharādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the Vidyādharas and others milked knowledge moving in the sky.
Other magicians milked māyā, the power of disappearance and wondrous forms,
having appointed <s>Maya</s> as calf; they milked a product made of concentration.
The Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Piśācas, and flesh-eaters,
with <s>Bhūteśa</s> as calf, milked blood-liquor into a skull.
Likewise the snakes, the biting serpents, the sarpas, and the nāgas, making <s>Takṣaka</s>
their calf, milked poison as milk into a hole-vessel.

children.text: paśavo yavasaṃ kṣīraṃ vatsaṃ kṛtvā ca govṛṣam
children.translated_text: The animals milked grass as milk, making the bull of cows their calf,
and the fang-bearing beasts milked in a forest vessel, with the lion as their calf.

children.text: kravyādāḥ prāṇinaḥ kravyaṃ duduhuḥ sve kalevare
children.translated_text: The flesh-eating living beings milked flesh into their own bodies,
and the birds, with <s>Suparṇa</s> as their calf, milked both what moves and what does not move.
The trees, with the banyan as their calf, milked sap in different forms as their milk,
and the mountains, with <s>Himavat</s> as their calf, milked various minerals on their own slopes.

children.text: sarve svamukhyavatsena sve sve pātre pṛthak payaḥ
children.translated_text: All, each with its own chief as calf and in its own vessel, milked separate milk
from the earth, made by <s>Pṛthu</s> into a cow that yields every desire.
In this way, O lord of the <s>Kurus</s>, beginning with <s>Pṛthu</s>, the eaters of food on the earth
made distinctions of milk for themselves as food, according to differences of milking, calf, and the like.
Then the lord of the earth, <s>Pṛthu</s>, pleased with the earth that yielded every desire,
made her his daughter, with affection, for he was tender toward daughters.
Crushing the peaks of mountains with the tip of his bow, the king of kings,
the mighty son of <s>Vena</s>, made this circle of the earth mostly level.
Then, on this earth, the blessed son of <s>Vena</s>, father and giver of livelihood to his subjects,
arranged dwellings here and there for them, according to what was proper.
Villages, cities, market towns, and various forts,
cowherd hamlets, cattle stations, camps, mines, agricultural villages, and small fortified settlements he arranged.
Before <s>Pṛthu</s>, there had been no such arrangement here of cities, villages, and the like;
people lived wherever they pleased, here and there, without fear from any quarter.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Then that king undertook consecration for a hundred horse sacrifices

children.text: brahmāvarte manoḥ kṣetre yatra prācī sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: in <s>Brahmāvarta</s>, in the field of <s>Manu</s>, where the eastern-flowing <s>Sarasvatī</s> is.
Perceiving that extraordinary sacrificial action of his,
the blessed <s>Śatakratu</s> could not endure <s>Pṛthu</s>'s great sacrificial festival.
There the lord of sacrifice himself, the blessed <s>Hari</s>, the sovereign,
the self of all, the teacher of all worlds, the master, was directly experienced.
Accompanied by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śarva</s>, and by the guardians of the worlds together with their attendants,
he was praised by the <s>Gandharvas</s>, sages, and groups of <s>Apsarases</s>.
The <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Dānavas</s>, <s>Guhyakas</s>, and others,
and the foremost attendants of <s>Hari</s>, headed by <s>Sunanda</s> and <s>Nanda</s>, were there.
<s>Kapila</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Datta</s>, the lords of yoga such as the <s>Sanakas</s>,
and those devotees eager for his service followed him.
There the earth, yielding <s>dharma</s> and being a cow that yields every desire,
milked out the desired goods for the sacrificer, O <s>Bhārata</s>.
The rivers carried every kind of flavor: milk, curds, food, and juices from cows;
the trees, with massive bodies, brought forth streams of honey.
The oceans brought heaps of jewels, and the mountains brought the four kinds of food
as tribute; all the worlds, together with their guardians, offered gifts.
And so, envying the supreme rise of <s>Pṛthu</s>, lord of the lord <s>Adhokṣaja</s>,
the blessed <s>Indra</s> set about obstructing it.
When the son of <s>Vena</s> was sacrificing to the lord of sacrifice with the final horse sacrifice,
<s>Indra</s>, out of rivalry, stole away the sacrificial animal and disappeared.
The blessed <s>Atri</s> saw him hurrying through the sky,
as if wearing a heretical disguise, that confusion of <s>dharma</s> within <s>adharma</s>.
Urged by <s>Atri</s> to kill him, <s>Pṛthu</s>'s son, a great chariot-warrior,
pursued him in anger and cried, 'Stop! Stop!'

children.text: taṃ tādṛśākṛtiṃ vīkṣya mene dharmaṃ śarīriṇam
children.translated_text: But seeing him in such a form, he thought him to be <s>dharma</s> embodied,

children.text: jaṭilaṃ bhasmanācchannaṃ tasmai bāṇaṃ na muñcati ||
children.translated_text: matted-haired and covered with ash, and he did not release his arrow at him.
When he had turned back from killing him, <s>Atri</s> again urged him to kill:
'Strike down the destroyer of the sacrifice, dear boy, <s>Mahendra</s>, the lowest of the gods.'
Thus addressed, the son of <s>Vena</s>, furious,
pursued him as he hurried through the sky, like the king of vultures pursuing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: so 'śvaṃ rūpaṃ ca taddhitvā tasmā antarhitaḥ svarāṭ
children.translated_text: That sovereign abandoned both the horse and that form, and then vanished from him;
the hero took back his own sacrificial animal and came to his father's sacrifice.
Seeing that marvelous deed of his, the supreme sages,
O lord, gave him the name <s>Vijitāśva</s>, 'he by whom the horse was won.'
Again <s>Hari</s>, spreading dense darkness, stole the horse,
concealed from the sacrificial post with its golden girdle, the mighty one.
<s>Atri</s> pointed him out as he hurried through the sky,
carrying a skull and a skull-topped staff; but the hero did not attack him.
Urged by <s>Atri</s>, he angrily fitted an arrow against him.

children.text: so 'śvaṃ rūpaṃ ca taddhitvā tasthāvantarhitaḥ svarāṭ ||
children.translated_text: That sovereign abandoned both the horse and that form, and stood vanished from sight.
Then the hero took the horse and went to his father's sacrifice;
but men weak in knowledge adopted that blameworthy form of <s>Hari</s>.
The forms that <s>Indra</s> assumed out of desire to steal the horse,
those are fragments of sin; here a broken sign is called a khaṇḍa.
Thus, as <s>Indra</s> kept stealing the horse, wishing to destroy the sacrifice of the son of <s>Vena</s>,
people's minds became attached to the heretical forms that he had taken and cast off.
Through delusion they generally cling to secondary, false forms of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: prāyeṇa sajjate bhrāntyā peśaleṣu ca vāgmiṣu ||
children.translated_text: such as nakedness, red garments, and the like, and to those who are attractive and eloquent.
Knowing this, the blessed <s>Pṛthu</s>, of great valor,
angry at <s>Indra</s>, took up an arrow with his bow raised.
Seeing that he intended to kill <s>Śakra</s>, impossible to look upon and with irresistible force, the officiating priests restrained him:
'Ah, great-minded one, it is not proper here to kill anyone other than the one prescribed.'
'Here we shall summon the destroyer of your purpose, the lord of the <s>Maruts</s>, whose brilliance has been destroyed by your fame;
with unfailing invocations, O king, we shall forcibly offer your enemy into the fire.'
Having thus addressed the lord of the sacrifice, O <s>Vidura</s>, his priests, in anger,
approached with ladles in hand as they were making the oblation, but <s>Svayambhū</s> himself forbade them.
<s>Indra</s> is not to be killed by you, if <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice) is the body of the Lord,
for you seek to kill by sacrifice the one whose worshiped embodiments are the gods.
Therefore see this great transgression against <s>dharma</s>, O twice-born ones,
this deed done by <s>Indra</s>, who wished to obstruct the king's rite.
Let the fame of <s>Pṛthu</s>, son of <s>Pṛthu</s>, become that of one who has performed ninety-nine sacrifices;
enough for you are well-performed sacrifices, since Your Majesty knows the <s>dharma</s> that leads to liberation.
You should not bring anger upon yourself against great <s>Indra</s>;
for both of you, welfare to you, are embodiments of the One praised in highest verses.

children.text: māsminmahārāja kṛthāḥ sma cintāṃ niśāmayāsmadvaca ādṛtātmā
children.translated_text: Do not, O great king, make this anxiety; listen attentively to our words.

children.text: yaddhyāyato daivahataṃ nu kartuṃ mano 'tiruṣṭaṃ viśate tamo 'ndham ||
children.translated_text: For when a man's mind dwells on doing what fate has thwarted, deeply enraged, it enters blind darkness.
Let this sacrifice cease, for it is hard even for the gods to restrain,
since there is a disruption of <s>dharma</s> where the heresies created by <s>Indra</s> appear.
Look at this people being carried away by these heresies,
introduced by <s>Indra</s>, thieves of the mark, for he who harmed your sacrifice stole the horse.
Your Majesty has descended here to protect the <s>dharma</s> of the people, suited to the times;
today, because of <s>Vena</s>'s offense, that <s>dharma</s> had been lost, and you, O <s>Vainya</s>, are a portion of <s>Viṣṇu</s> from his body.

children.text: sa tvaṃ vimṛśyāsya bhavaṃ prajāpate saṃkalpanaṃ viśvasṛjāṃ pipīpṛhi
children.translated_text: Therefore, having considered the welfare of this world, O lord of creatures, fulfill the intention of the creators of the universe,

children.text: aindrīṃ ca māyāmupadharmamātaraṃ pracaṇḍapākhaṇḍapathaṃ prabho jahi ||
children.translated_text: and destroy the māyā of <s>Indra</s>, mother of pseudo-dharma, the violent path of heresy, O lord.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Thus instructed by the teacher of the world, the lord of the people

children.text: tathā ca kṛtvā vātsalyaṃ maghonāpi ca saṃdadhe ||
children.translated_text: did accordingly, and he also made friendship with <s>Maghavan</s> out of affection.
To <s>Pṛthu</s>, of abundant deeds, after he had performed the concluding avabhṛtha bath,
those boon-giving beings, satisfied at that sacrificial seat, gave boons.
The brāhmaṇas, true in their blessings, were pleased and had received their gifts with faith;
honored, they joined blessings to the first king, O <s>Kṣattar</s>.
All those summoned by you, mighty-armed one, have indeed assembled,
and the ancestors, gods, seers, and humans have been honored with gifts and respect.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
The blessed <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> himself, the mighty one, together with <s>Maghavan</s>,
the lord of sacrifice and enjoyer of sacrifice, pleased by the sacrifices, spoke to him.
The blessed Lord said:
This one has indeed caused an interruption to your hundred horse sacrifices;
as he asks forgiveness for himself, you should forgive him for this offense.
Wise, saintly men in the world, O god among men, O best of men,
do not harm living beings when they know that the self is not the body.
If persons such as you are bewildered by the māyā of the god,

children.text: śrama eva paraṃ jāto dīrghayā vṛddhasevayā ||
children.translated_text: then the long service of the elders has produced only weariness as its highest result.
Therefore the awakened man, knowing this body to have been begun by ignorance, desire, and action,
does not become attached to it at all.
Who, being wise, would make a sense of mine toward this body, this house produced by it,

children.text: apatye draviṇe vāpi kaḥ kuryānmamatāṃ budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or toward offspring or wealth, when he is unattached?
That self is one, pure, self-luminous, without qualities, though the support of qualities,
all-pervading, uncovered, witness, without a material self, the true self, beyond the self.
The person who knows the self as such, abiding in the self,

children.text: nājyate prakṛtistho 'pi tadguṇaiḥ sa mayi sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: though situated in prakṛti, is not smeared by its qualities; he is established in me.

children.text: yaḥ svadharmeṇa māṃ nityaṃ nirāśīḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: One who, by his own <s>dharma</s>, worships me constantly, without expectation and endowed with faith,
his mind, O king, gradually becomes clear and pleased.
Having abandoned the qualities, seeing rightly, and having a purified heart,
he obtains peace, firm abiding in me, <s>brahman</s>, and isolation.
He who knows this self as if indifferent, the overseer of substance, knowledge, and action,
unchanging, obtains the auspicious state.
When the flow of qualities belonging to the divided subtle body, whose nature is substance, action, agenthood, and consciousness,

children.text: dṛṣṭāsu saṃpatsu vipatsu sūrayo na vikriyante mayi baddhasauhṛdāḥ ||
children.translated_text: is seen in prosperity and adversity, the wise, whose friendship is bound to me, are not altered.

children.text: samaḥ samānottamamadhyamādhamaḥ sukhe ca duḥkhe ca jitendriyāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Equal toward equals, superiors, middling persons, and inferiors, in happiness and in suffering, with senses and mind conquered,
joined to all the worlds arranged by me, O hero, carry out the protection of all the worlds.
The welfare of a king is precisely the protection of his subjects, for in the next world he receives a sixth share of their merit;
otherwise, as a tax-taker who does not protect his people, robbed of merit, he consumes their sin.
Thus, with <s>dharma</s> approved by the foremost twice-born as your chief concern and followed by you, you will be an unparalleled protector of this earth;
in a short time, beloved by the people, you will see perfected beings who have come to your house.

children.text: varaṃ ca matkaṃcana mānavendra vṛṇīṣva te 'haṃ guṇaśīlayantritaḥ
children.translated_text: And choose from me some boon, O king of men; I am constrained by your qualities and conduct.
I am not easily attained by sacrifices, nor by austerities, nor by yoga, as I am by one who moves with an even mind.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Thus instructed by <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, teacher of the world, <s>Viśvajit</s>
accepted <s>Hari</s>'s command upon his head.

children.text: spṛśantaṃ pādayoḥ premṇā vrīḍitaṃ svena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Śatakratu</s> touching his feet with love, ashamed by his own deed,
he embraced him and cast away his hatred.
Then the blessed Lord, the Self of the universe, was offered worship by <s>Pṛthu</s>,
who, with devotion swelling up, had grasped his lotus feet.
Although he had turned toward departure, he was delayed by favor toward him;
the lotus-petal-eyed friend of the good, looking upon him, did not set out.
That first king, with folded hands, was unable to look upon <s>Hari</s> because his eyes were filled with tears;
overwhelmed with weeping, he said nothing, but embraced him in his heart and remained standing.
Then, wiping away the drops of tears and looking at the Person who was still not enough for the range of his sight, he spoke.
touching the earth with his foot, with the tips of his hands placed on the raised shoulder of the enemy of serpents, <s>Garuḍa</s>.
<s>Pṛthu</s> said:
O mighty Lord, how could a wise man choose boons from you, the lord of boon-giving lords, when they belong to those whose selves are transformations of the guṇas?

children.text: ye nārakāṇāmapi santi dehināṃ tānīśa kaivalyapate vṛṇe na ca ||
children.translated_text: Those boons are available even to embodied beings in hell; O Lord, master of <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation), I do not choose them.

children.text: na kāmaye nātha tadapyahaṃ kvacinna yatra yuṣmaccaraṇāmbujāsavaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor, O master, do I ever desire even that state in which there is no nectar from your lotus feet,
fallen from the inner hearts of the greatest souls through their mouths. Grant me ten thousand ears; this is my boon.
O <s>Uttamaśloka</s>, the breeze carrying drops of nectar from your lotus feet, fallen from the mouths of the great,

children.text: smṛtiṃ punarvismṛtatattvavartmanāṃ kuyogināṃ no vitaratyalaṃ varaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: restores memory to us poor yogins who have forgotten the path of truth. Enough, then, with other boons.

children.text: yaśaḥ śivaṃ suśrava āryasaṅgame yadṛcchayā copaśṛṇoti te sakṛt
children.translated_text: When someone, even by chance and even once in the company of the noble, hears your auspicious fame, so worthy of hearing,

children.text: kathaṃ guṇajño viramedvinā paśuṃ śrīryatpravavre guṇasaṅgrahecchayā ||
children.translated_text: how could one who knows its qualities turn away, unless he were a beast? <s>Śrī</s> herself chose it from the desire to gather up its qualities.
Therefore I worship you, the supreme person of all, the abode of all qualities, eager like the lotus-handed <s>Śrī</s> herself.
May no quarrel arise between us, though we compete for one husband, since both of us are wholly intent on your feet.

children.text: jagajjananyāṃ jagadīśa vaiśasaṃ syādeva yatkarmaṇi naḥ samīhitam
children.translated_text: O Lord of the world, conflict with the mother of the world may indeed arise in the action we desire,

children.text: karoṣi phalgvapyuru dīnavatsalaḥ sva eva dhiṣṇye 'bhiratasya kiṃ tayā ||
children.translated_text: yet, compassionate to the humble, you make even a slight thing great. Since you delight in your own abode, what need have you of her?
Therefore the good worship you, whose rise is free from the bewildering display of the qualities of māyā.
Apart from the remembrance of your feet, O Blessed One, we know no other motive for the virtuous.

children.text: manye giraṃ te jagatāṃ vimohinīṃ varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti bhajantamāttha yat
children.translated_text: I think your speech bewilders the worlds when you say to your worshipper, 'Choose a boon.'

children.text: vācā nu tantyā yadi te jano 'sitaḥ kathaṃ punaḥ karma karoti mohitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If a person is bound by that cord of your speech, how, deluded, could he again perform action?

children.text: tvanmāyayāddhā jana īśa khaṇḍito yadanyadāśāsta ṛtātmano 'budhaḥ
children.translated_text: O Lord, a person truly shattered by your māyā, being ignorant, seeks something other than the true self.

children.text: yathā caredbālahitaṃ pitā svayaṃ tathā tvamevārhasi naḥ samīhitum ||
children.translated_text: As a father himself should act for a child's welfare, so you alone ought to arrange what is desired for us.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: ityādirājena nutaḥ sa viśvadṛk tamāha rājanmayi bhaktirastu te
children.translated_text: Praised thus by the first king, the all-seeing Lord said to him, 'O king, may you have devotion toward me.

children.text: diṣṭyedṛśī dhīrmayi te kṛtā yayā māyāṃ madīyāṃ tarati sma dustyajām ||
children.translated_text: By good fortune such understanding has been formed in you toward me, by which one crosses my māyā, hard to abandon.
Therefore, O lord of creatures, carefully do what I have commanded.
One who carries out my command everywhere obtains what is auspicious.'
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having approved the meaningful speech of <s>Vainya</s>, the royal seer,
<s>Acyuta</s>, worshipped by him, blessed him and made up his mind to depart.
The divine seers, ancestors, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, serpents,
<s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, mortals, birds, and many kinds of beings,
honored by the king with speech, wealth, folded hands, and devotion, with the thought that he was the Lord of sacrifice,
all departed from there, following <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.
The Blessed <s>Acyuta</s> too, together with the royal seer's preceptor,
as though carrying away that king's mind, returned to his own abode.
Having bowed to him who was no longer visible, who had shown his true self,

children.text: avyaktāya ca devānāṃ devāya svapuraṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: to the unmanifest one, the god of the gods, the king went to his own city.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
There and there it was adorned with pearls, flower garlands, fine cloths, golden gateways,
and highly fragrant incenses.
Its streets, squares, and roads were damp with sandalwood and aloe-water,
and were honored with flowers, unbroken rice, fruits, sprouts, parched grain, and lamps.
It was embellished with clusters of banana trunks and young betel-nut trees,
and everywhere decorated with garlands of tree-shoots.
The subjects came toward him with lamps, offerings, and every auspicious article assembled,
and with well-adorned maidens ornamented with polished earrings.
To the sound of conches and kettledrums, and to the Vedic chanting of the officiating priests,
the hero entered his palace, praised by all and free from pride.
Honored, the greatly renowned king in turn honored, there and there,
the citizens and the people of the countryside, delighted and bestowing cherished boons.
Thus, performing many such irreproachable deeds, the great one, the greatest of the great,

children.text: kurvanśaśāsāvanimaṇḍalaṃ yaśaḥ sphītaṃ nidhāyāruruhe paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: ruled the circle of the earth; having established his abundant fame, he ascended to the supreme state.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then the fame of that first king, expanded by all virtues and honored by the virtuous,

children.text: kṣattā mahābhāgavataḥ sadaspate kauṣāraviṃ prāha gṛṇantamarcayan ||
children.translated_text: was being praised by <s>Kauṣāravi</s>; the great devotee <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, O lord of the assembly, honored him and spoke.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
He, <s>Pṛthu</s>, was consecrated by the brahmins and received every honor fit for the gods,

children.text: bibhratsa vaiṣṇavaṃ tejo bāhvoryābhyāṃ dudoha gām ||
children.translated_text: bearing the Vaiṣṇava splendor in those two arms with which he milked the earth.

children.text: ko nvasya kīrtiṃ na śṛṇotyabhijño yadvikramocchiṣṭamaśeṣabhūpāḥ
children.translated_text: What discerning person would not hear his fame, since all kings live upon what remained from his valor,

children.text: lokāḥ sapālā upajīvanti kāmamadyāpi tanme vada karma śuddham ||
children.translated_text: and the worlds, together with their guardians, still live upon it as they desire? Tell me of that pure deed of his.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Dwelling in the region between the rivers <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>,
he enjoyed only those pleasures that had already begun, out of a wish to cast off merit.
His command was unobstructed everywhere; he wielded the single rod of authority over the seven continents,
except over the families of brahmins and except over the lineage of <s>Acyuta</s>.
Once there was a great sacrificial session and consecration of the dwellers in heaven,

children.text: samājo brahmarṣīṇāṃ ca rājarṣīṇāṃ ca sattama ||
children.translated_text: and an assembly of brahmin seers and royal seers, O best one.
When all the worthy persons in that gathering had been duly honored by him according to their worth,
he rose in the middle of the assembly like the moon among the stars.
He was tall, with full and long arms, fair in complexion, and with eyes red like lotuses,
with a fine nose, handsome gentle face, broad shoulders, and a smile showing beautiful teeth.
His chest was broad, his hips large, and his belly was graceful with folds;
his navel was whorled, he was vigorous, with golden thighs and prominent feet.
His hair was fine, curling, dark, and glossy, and his neck was like a conch.
He put on and wore costly, excellent silk garments,
so that the beauty of all his limbs was manifest, though in observance he had set aside ornaments.
Wearing a black antelope skin, splendid, with kuśa grass in hand, he had performed what was proper.
With eyes cool, gentle, and star-bright, he looked all around,
and the lord of the earth spoke these words, as though delighting the assembly.
His speech was charming, varied in expression, smooth, polished, deep, and unconfused,
and for the benefit of all he then seemed to be expounding the matter.
The king said:

children.text: sabhyāḥ śṛṇuta bhadraṃ vaḥ sādhavo ya ihāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Members of the assembly, listen; may there be welfare for you, noble ones who have come here.
Among good people, those who desire to understand <s>dharma</s> should declare their own considered view.
I am a king bearing the rod of punishment, appointed here among the subjects

children.text: rakṣitā vṛttidaḥ sveṣu setuṣu sthāpitā pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: as their protector, giver of livelihood, and establisher of each in his proper bounds.
Through my carrying out of that duty, those worlds of mine which the expounders of brahman speak of

children.text: lokāḥ syuḥ kāmasaṃdohā yasya tuṣyati diṣṭadṛk ||
children.translated_text: would become heaps of desired rewards, for the one with destiny-seeing sight is pleased.
A king who takes tax while failing to instruct his subjects in the ways of <s>dharma</s>

children.text: prajānāṃ śamalaṃ bhuṅkte bhagaṃ ca svaṃ jahāti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: eats the impurity of his subjects, and he loses his own share.
Therefore, my subjects, free from envy, for the sake of supporting your lord and for your own good,
act with your minds fixed on <s>Adhokṣaja</s>; then favor will have been done to me.
You pure ancestors, gods, and sages, approve that act,
for after death the fruit is the same for the doer, the instructor, and the one who gives approval.
There is indeed, O best of the venerable, one called the lord of sacrifice for some;
both here and hereafter, bright worlds are perceived in certain cases.
For <s>Manu</s>, for <s>Uttānapāda</s>, and also for King <s>Dhruva</s>,
for the royal sage <s>Priyavrata</s>, and for <s>Aṅga</s>, my father's father,
and then for others such as these, and for <s>Aja</s> and <s>Bhava</s>,
and also for <s>Prahlāda</s> and <s>Bali</s>, there is a purpose to be fulfilled by the mace-bearer.
Except for the grandsons and others of <s>Mṛtyu</s>, pitiable and deluded from <s>dharma</s>,
he is generally the sole cause of worldly aims, heaven, and liberation.
A taste for service to his feet at once destroys the impurity of mind accumulated through all births by ascetics,

children.text: sadyaḥ kṣiṇotyanvahamedhatī satī yathā padāṅguṣṭhaviniḥsṛtā sarit ||
children.translated_text: and, being pure, it grows day by day, like the river that issued from his big toe.
A man whose whole impurity of mind has been shaken off, endowed with the special power of unattached knowledge,

children.text: yadaṅghrimūle kṛtaketanaḥ punarna saṃsṛtiṃ kleśavahāṃ prapadyate ||
children.translated_text: and who has made his dwelling at the root of his feet, does not again enter painful <s>saṃsṛti</s>.
Therefore worship him alone with your own ways of life, with the qualities of mind, speech, and body, and with your own actions,
sincere, so that the aims determined by your station may be accomplished at his lotus feet, which yield every desire.
Here this sacrifice, possessing many qualities yet itself beyond qualities,
is accomplished through various prescribed materials, qualities, actions, utterances, meanings, intentions, signs, and names, though in its own nature it is a solid mass of pure consciousness.
In this body, a collection of primordial matter, time, latent disposition, and <s>dharma</s>, when consciousness is assumed,
the all-pervading one is manifested as the fruit of action, just as fire appears in wood according to its qualities.

children.text: aho mamāmī vitarantyanugrahaṃ hariṃ guruṃ yajñabhujāmadhīśvaram
children.translated_text: Ah, these people of mine bestow favor on me, for they worship <s>Hari</s>, the guru and lord of those who enjoy sacrifice,

children.text: svadharmayogena yajanti māmakā nirantaraṃ kṣoṇitale dṛḍhavratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: constantly on the surface of the earth, firm in vows, through the discipline of their own <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: mā jātu tejaḥ prabhavenmaharddhibhistitikṣayā tapasā vidyayā ca
children.translated_text: May the splendor of the twice-born, blazing with forbearance, austerity, and knowledge,
never be overpowered by great royal prosperities, in the lineage of those whose deities are unconquered.
The ancient person <s>Hari</s>, the god favorable to brahman and Brahmins, by constant reverence to their feet

children.text: avāpa lakṣmīmanapāyinīṃ yaśo jagatpavitraṃ ca mahattamāgraṇīḥ ||
children.translated_text: obtained unfailing <s>Lakṣmī</s>, fame that purifies the world, and leadership among the greatest.
By service to them, the self-ruling lord who dwells in all hearts, dear to Brahmins, is pleased as one desires.
Therefore let that Brahmin lineage be served with one's whole self by those who are disciplined and devoted to that <s>dharma</s>.
When it is pleased, a person quickly obtains for himself supreme peace, naturally and of itself.

children.text: yannityasambandhaniṣevayā tataḥ paraṃ kimatrāsti mukhaṃ havirbhujām ||
children.translated_text: What more than that is there here? They are the mouth of those who eat the oblations.

children.text: aśnātyanantaḥ khalu tattvakovidaiḥ śraddhāhutaṃ yanmukha ijyanāmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: The infinite one truly eats what is offered with faith into their mouth, under the names used in worship, by those who know reality;

children.text: na vai tathā cetanayā bahiṣkṛte hutāśane pāramahaṃsyaparyaguḥ ||
children.translated_text: not in the same way in the external fire, which is devoid of consciousness, say those who have reached the supreme swan's path.
That eternal, stainless, ancient brahman they bear, through faith, austerity, auspicious practice, silence, and restraint,
and through samādhi, for the vision of reality; in it this world shines forth as in a mirror.
May I, O noble ones, carry on my crown for my lifetime the dust of their lotus feet,

children.text: yaṃ nityadā bibhrata āśu pāpaṃ naśyatyamuṃ sarvaguṇā bhajanti ||
children.translated_text: for when one bears it always, sin quickly perishes, and all virtues attend that person.

children.text: guṇāyanaṃ śīladhanaṃ kṛtajñaṃ vṛddhāśrayaṃ saṃvṛṇate 'nu sampadaḥ
children.translated_text: Prosperities follow and choose him: a treasury of virtues, rich in character, grateful, and dependent on elders.

children.text: prasīdatāṃ brahmakulaṃ gavāṃ ca janārdanaḥ sānucaraśca mahyam ||
children.translated_text: May the Brahmin lineage, the cows, and <s>Janārdana</s> together with his attendants be gracious to me.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
As the king was speaking thus, the ancestors, gods, and twice-born,
their minds delighted, praised him with cries of 'Well done!' as noble people do.
The sacred statement, 'By a son one conquers the worlds,' is true,
since the sinful <s>Vena</s>, struck down by the Brahmin's rod, crossed beyond darkness through his son.
And <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> too, because of reviling the Lord, was about to enter darkness,
but passed beyond it through the power of his son <s>Prahlāda</s>.

children.text: vīravarya pitaḥ pṛthvyāḥ samāḥ saṃjīva śāśvatīḥ
children.translated_text: O best of heroes, father of the earth, live for everlasting years,
you whose devotion to <s>Acyuta</s>, the one sustainer of all worlds, is such.

children.text: aho vayaṃ hyadya pavitrakīrte tvayaiva nāthena mukundanāthāḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, today indeed, O one of purifying fame, with you alone as lord we have <s>Mukunda</s> as lord,
for you make manifest the story of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the most excellent of those praised in noble verses, the god who loves the brahmins.
This instruction from you for the conduct of life, O lord, is not very astonishing;
affection for their subjects is the very nature of the great, whose selves are compassion.
Today, O master, the far shore of our darkness has been reached by us through you,
as we wander about, blind in vision, because of deeds that are called fate.
Homage to the greatly exalted <s>puruṣa</s> (cosmic person), whose <s>sattva</s> has increased,
who, entering <s>brahman</s> and royal power, upholds this world by his own splendor.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
While the people were praising <s>Pṛthu</s> in this way, the king of broad valor,
four sages, radiant like the sun, came there.
The king, together with his attendants, saw those lords of siddhas descending from the sky by their radiance,
recognized as they made the worlds free from sin.
As if wishing to take back his life-breaths that had gone out at the sight of them, he rose up,
<s>Vainya</s>, together with his assembly and attendants, like the lord of the senses going toward the qualities.
Held in check by reverence, and with his neck bowed low in humility before the assembly,
he worshiped them according to rule, after they had accepted the arghya and seats.
With his hair-knot moistened by the water that had washed their feet,
he there seemed to honor the conduct practiced by those of good character.
They sat on golden seats like fires in their own sacred places;
endowed with faith and restraint, pleased, he addressed the elder brothers of <s>Bhava</s>.
<s>Pṛthu</s> said:

children.text: aho ācaritaṃ kiṃ me maṅgalaṃ maṅgalāyanāḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, what auspicious deed has been performed by me, O abodes of auspiciousness,

children.text: yasya vo darśanaṃ hyāsīddurdarśānāṃ ca yogibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that the sight of you, who are difficult even for yogins to behold, has come about?

children.text: kiṃ tasya durlabhataramiha loke paratra ca
children.translated_text: What could be still harder to obtain, in this world or the next, for the man

children.text: yasya viprāḥ prasīdanti śivo viṣṇuśca sānugaḥ ||
children.translated_text: toward whom brahmins are gracious, and also <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> with their attendants?
The world does not perceive you, though you travel through the worlds,

children.text: yathā sarvadṛśaṃ sarva ātmānaṃ ye 'sya hetavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as all people do not perceive the all-seeing self, though these are its causes.

children.text: adhanā api te dhanyāḥ sādhavo gṛhamedhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Even without wealth, those virtuous householders are blessed
whose houses contain eminent worthy guests, water, grass, ground, and a master ready to serve.
But houses that lack all this wealth are truly dwellings of snakes and trees,
when they are deprived of the holy water from the feet of those whose feet are themselves tīrthas.
Welcome to you, best of twice-born men, whose vows are practiced by seekers of liberation,

children.text: caranti śraddhayā dhīrā bālā eva bṛhanti ca ||
children.translated_text: steadfast and faithful, who are boys and yet great.
Is there welfare for us, O lords, who know only the purposes of sense objects,
fallen by our own deeds into this pit of calamity?
Among you, who delight in the self, a question about welfare is not fitting,
for there no mental movements of welfare and ill-fare exist.
Therefore, having placed my trust in you as friends of those who practice austerity,
I ask: by what means, in this existence, may welfare quickly come about?
Clearly the self of those who possess the self, the blessed lord who brings the self into being,
the unborn one, moves about here in the form of siddhas for the favor of his own people.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having heard that good speech of <s>Pṛthu</s>, substantial, well measured, and sweet,

children.text: smayamāna iva prītyā kumāraḥ pratyuvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kumāra</s>, as if smiling with affection, replied.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Well asked, great king, by you whose self is devoted to the welfare of all beings,
and by you who are learned; such is the disposition of the good.
Indeed, the meeting of good people is approved for both parties,
since conversation and questioning among them spreads peace for everyone.
There is indeed in you, O king, a steadfast love, hard to obtain, for recounting the qualities of the lotus-feet of <s>Madhudviṣ</s>,

children.text: ratirdurāpā vidhunoti naiṣṭhikī kāmaṃ kaṣāyaṃ malamantarātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and it completely shakes off the astringent impurity of the inner self.

children.text: śāstreṣviyāneva suniścito nṛṇāṃ kṣemasya sadhryagvimṛśeṣu hetuḥ
children.translated_text: In the śāstras this much alone is well determined as the cause of human welfare by those who examine correctly:

children.text: asaṅga ātmavyatirikta ātmani dṛḍhā ratirbrahmaṇi nirguṇe ca yā ||
children.translated_text: detachment from what is other than the self, and firm love for the self and for qualityless <s>brahman</s>.
That arises through faith, through the practice of <s>bhagavad-dharma</s> (devotion-centered duty), through inquiry, and through steadiness in inner yoga,

children.text: yogeśvaropāsanayā ca nityaṃ puṇyaśravaḥkathayā puṇyayā ca ||
children.translated_text: and also through constant worship of the lords of yoga, and through the sacred and meritorious tale that is worthy to hear.
It arises through lack of thirst for gatherings devoted to wealth and sense pleasure, and through not accepting what is approved by such people,
through a taste for solitude, through contentment in the self, and through drinking the nectar of <s>Hari</s>'s qualities and no other delight.
It arises through <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-harm), through the conduct of the <s>paramahaṃsas</s>, and through memory made sweet by the finest liquor of <s>Mukunda</s>'s deeds,
through desireless restraints, through observances, through non-reproach, through freedom from restless striving, and through endurance of opposites.
Through devotion that expands by repeatedly proclaiming the qualities of <s>Hari</s>, which fill the ears of those intent on him,

children.text: bhaktyā hyasaṅgaḥ sadasatyanātmani syānnirguṇe brahmaṇi cāñjasā ratiḥ ||
children.translated_text: detachment from this unreal non-self, and love for qualityless <s>brahman</s>, easily arise.
When a man, possessing a teacher, has steadfast love for <s>brahman</s>, then by the force of knowledge and dispassion
he burns up the powerless heart, the living sheath made of five parts, like fire arising from its source.
With his inner seat burned and freed from all its qualities, he no longer sees anything outside or inside the self,
nor the former division between the supreme self and the individual self, just as a person does not see it when a dream has vanished.
A person sees the self, the objects of the senses, and what is beyond both
only when there is a limiting adjunct founded on reality; not at any other time.
When a cause is present, everywhere, even in water and the like, a person
sees a division between his own self and another's; not at any other time.
For those who meditate while their senses are drawn by their objects, the mind, being carried away,
takes away the consciousness of the intellect, like a clump drawing water from a lake.
Memory then falls away, and the mind also; when memory is lost, knowledge is ruined.
The wise call the obstruction of that the self's own denial of itself.
There is no greater violation of a person's own good in this world
than that by which, through transgressing one's own self, another is considered dearer than oneself.
Brooding over wealth and sense-objects is the denial of every human aim;
deprived by it of knowledge and realization, a person enters into gross materiality.
One who wishes to cross over the intense darkness should never form attachment to it,
for it is the utter obstruction of <s>dharma</s>, prosperity, pleasure, and liberation.
Among these, liberation alone is regarded as the true aim, because it is final;
for the threefold aim is always joined with fear of death.
Those conditions, high and low, which arise from the intermingling of the <s>guṇas</s>,
have no security, since their blessings are destroyed by the Lord.

children.text: tattvaṃ narendra jagatāmatha tasthūṣāṃ ca dehendriyāsudhiṣaṇātmabhir āvṛtānām
children.translated_text: O king of men, know the truth of moving beings and of those that stand still, covered by bodies, senses, life-breaths, intellects, and selves:

children.text: yaḥ kṣetravittapatayā hṛdi viśvag āviḥ pratyak cakāsti bhagavāṃstamavehi so 'smi ||
children.translated_text: he who, as the knower and lord of the field, appears everywhere in the heart and shines inwardly, the blessed Lord; know him: that am I.

children.text: yasminidaṃ sadasadātmatayā vibhāti māyā vivekavidhuti sraji vā hi buddhiḥ
children.translated_text: In him this world appears as having the nature of existence and non-existence, while the intellect, through <s>māyā</s> and lack of discrimination, sees as one might see in a garland.
I take refuge in him whose reality is eternally free, purified, and pure, and whose nature has cast off the mire of karma.
By playful devotion to the petals of his lotus feet, the saints unloosen the karmic disposition that has been knotted together;

children.text: tadvanna riktamatayo yatayo 'pi ruddhasrotogaṇāstamaraṇaṃ bhaja vāsudevam ||
children.translated_text: but ascetics of empty mind, though the streams of their senses are checked, do not do so in the same way. Worship <s>Vāsudeva</s>, that refuge.

children.text: kṛcchro mahāniha bhavārṇavam aplaveśāṃ ṣaḍvarganakramasukhena titīrṣanti
children.translated_text: Great and hard to cross here is the ocean of becoming for those without a boat, when they wish to cross it with difficulty, full of the crocodiles of the sixfold host.

children.text: tattvaṃ harerbhagavato bhajanīyamaṅghriṃ kṛtvoḍupaṃ vyasanamuttara dustarārṇam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore make the worshipful foot of the blessed <s>Hari</s> your raft and cross beyond the calamity, the ocean hard to cross.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Thus, by that son of <s>Brahmā</s>, the sage <s>Kumāra</s>, wise in the self,
the king was fully shown the path of the self; he praised him and spoke.
The king said:
A favor was formerly done to me by <s>Hari</s>, who has compassion for the distressed;
to bring that favor to fulfillment, O brahman, O blessed ones, you have come.
And it has been fully accomplished by you blessed and compassionate ones.

children.text: sādhūcchiṣṭaṃ hi me sarvamātmanā saha kiṃ dade ||
children.translated_text: All that I have is the leavings of the holy; along with my very self, what can I give?
My life-breaths, wives, sons, O brahman, houses with their furnishings,

children.text: rājyaṃ balaṃ mahī kośa iti sarvaṃ niveditam ||
children.translated_text: kingdom, army, earth, and treasury: all this has been offered.

children.text: saināpatyaṃ ca rājyaṃ ca daṇḍanetṛtvameva ca
children.translated_text: Generalship, kingship, leadership in punishment,
and sovereignty over all worlds belong properly to one learned in the <s>Veda</s> and <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: svameva brāhmaṇo bhuṅkte svaṃ vaste svaṃ dadāti ca
children.translated_text: A brahmin enjoys only his own property, wears his own, and gives his own;
by his favor the kṣatriyas and the others eat their food.

children.text: yairīdṛśī bhagavato gatirātmavāda ekāntato nigamibhiḥ pratipāditā naḥ
children.translated_text: May those of boundless compassion, by whom this path of the blessed Lord, the doctrine of the self, has been taught to us exclusively, though it was not so taught by the Vedic knowers,

children.text: tuṣyantvadabhrakaruṇāḥ svakṛtena nityaṃ ko nāma tatpratikaroti vinodapātram ||
children.translated_text: be ever satisfied with their own deed. Who indeed could repay that, except as an object of their gracious play?
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Those lords of the yoga of the self, honored by the first king,
praised his character and became present in the sky, while men looked on.
But <s>Vainya</s>, foremost among the great, through their instruction in spiritual steadiness,
considered himself as one whose desires were fulfilled, established in the self.
He performed actions according to time, according to place, according to strength,
as was fitting and according to his wealth, consecrating them to <s>Brahman</s>.
He offered the fruit to <s>Brahman</s>, was free from attachment and composed,

children.text: karmādhyakṣaṃ ca manvāna ātmānaṃ prakṛteḥ param ||
children.translated_text: and regarded the self as the overseer of action and as beyond <s>prakṛti</s>.
Though he lived in his houses and was endowed with imperial splendor,
he did not cling to the objects of the senses; his sense of 'I' was gone, like the sun.
Thus, practicing actions through the yoga of the self,
he begot five sons upon <s>Arci</s>, dear to his own self:
<s>Vijitāśva</s>, <s>Dhūmrakeśa</s>, <s>Haryakṣa</s>, <s>Draviṇa</s>, and <s>Vṛka</s>.
<s>Pṛthu</s> alone bore the qualities of all the guardians of the worlds.
For the protection of the created world, at each proper time, with his self fixed on <s>Acyuta</s>,
he delighted his subjects by gentle qualities, and by the activities of mind and speech.
He bore the title 'king,' like another moon-king,
releasing, taking in, and heating the wealth of the earth like the sun.
He was unassailable by his brilliance, like fire, and unconquerable like great <s>Indra</s>;
in forbearance he was like the earth, and like heaven he granted what men desired.

children.text: varṣati sma yathākāmaṃ parjanya iva tarpayan
children.translated_text: He rained as desired, satisfying like <s>Parjanya</s>;
he was hard to fathom like the ocean, and by firmness like the king of mountains.
In discipline he was like <s>Dharmarāja</s>, in wonder like <s>Himavān</s>,

children.text: kubera iva kośāḍhyo guptārtho varuṇo yathā ||
children.translated_text: rich in treasury like <s>Kubera</s>, and guarding secrets like <s>Varuṇa</s>.
Like <s>Mātariśvan</s>, he was the self of all; in strength, greatness, and vigor,
and in irresistibility he was like the divine blessed lord of beings.

children.text: kandarpa iva saundarye manasvī mṛgarāḍ iva
children.translated_text: In beauty he was like <s>Kandarpa</s>, and, being high-minded, like the king of beasts;
in affection for men he was like <s>Manu</s>, and in sovereignty like the blessed unborn one.
In discourse on <s>Brahman</s> he was <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; in self-possession, <s>Hari</s> himself.
Through devotion to cows, teachers, brahmins,
and those who followed <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, and through modesty, humility, and character, he was equal to himself in concern for others.
With fame sung high by men throughout the three worlds, here and there,
he entered the openings of women's ears like <s>Rāma</s>, and those of the good as well.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Once, when self-possessed <s>Vainya</s> saw himself advanced in age,
he, the lord of creatures, whose entire creation had been increased by himself,
the giver of livelihood to the moving world and also to what stands still, the bearer of <s>dharma</s> for the good,
having fulfilled the command of the Lord for the sake of which he had been born here...
Having placed his daughter among his sons, while she seemed to weep from separation,
and while his subjects were dispirited, he went alone with his wife to the forest of austerity.
Even there, with unfailing discipline approved by the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> ascetics,
he undertook fierce austerity, as he had formerly done for the conquest of himself.
He lived on bulbs, roots, and fruits, and at times ate dry leaves;
for some fortnights he consumed only water, and after that only air.
In summer the hero stood amid the five fires; in the rains the sage endured torrents of rain;
in winter he was immersed up to the neck in water, and he lay upon the bare ground.
Patient, restrained in speech, subdued, preserving his seed, and master of the breath,
he practiced the highest austerity, wishing to propitiate <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
By that discipline, perfected in due sequence, the impurity of karma in his heart was destroyed;
through breath-control the sixfold host was restrained, and his bonds were cut.
The blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s> had taught that supreme inner
yoga; by that very yoga the best of men worshiped the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
For the saint who followed the <s>bhagavaddharma</s> (the Lord's way) and always strove with faith,
devotion to the blessed <s>Brahman</s> arose, fixed on no other object.
Through this service to the Lord, through his self purified in sattva, and through the full sequence of repeated remembrance of him,

children.text: jñānaṃ viraktimadabhūnniśitena yena cicheda saṃśayapadaṃ nijajīvakośam ||
children.translated_text: knowledge endowed with detachment arose; with its sharp edge he cut his own sheath of living existence, the seat of doubt.
Having cut away other notions, attained the path of the self, and become free from desire, he abandoned that by whose discernment he had severed this bond;

children.text: tāvanna yogagatibhiryatirapramatto yāvadgadāgrajakathāsu ratiṃ na kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: for a vigilant ascetic does not reach the goal by yogic courses until he has formed delight in tales of <s>Gadāgraja</s>.
Thus that foremost hero joined the self in the self,

children.text: brahmabhūto dṛḍhaṃ kāle tatyāja svaṃ kalevaram ||
children.translated_text: became <s>brahman</s>, and in time firmly abandoned his own body.
Pressing the anus with his heels and slowly driving the breath upward,
he established it at the navel, in the belly, the heart, the chest, the throat, and the head.
Raising it upward and gradually setting it in the crown, desireless,
he joined the breath with air, the body with earth, and heat with heat.
He placed the cavities in space and the liquid in water, each in its proper place and division;
he dissolved earth into water, that water into fire, that fire into air, and that air into space.
He placed the mind in the senses, and those senses in the subtle elements according to their origin;
then, drawing these through the source of the elements, he set them in the great self.
That whole arrangement of the guṇas he placed in the living being made of māyā;
and that latent impression established in the self, that man who was himself the bearer of latent impressions,
the master, standing in his own true nature, abandoned by the power of manifold detachment.
<s>Arci</s>, the great queen, his wife, had followed her husband into the forest;
she was delicate and unfit even for the touch of earth upon her feet.
Through her intense firmness in her husband's vow and <s>dharma</s> (duty), through service, and through a sage-like bodily discipline,
she felt no distress, though emaciated, fulfilled by the touch of her beloved's hand and the joy of his face.

children.text: dehaṃ vipannākhilacetanādikaṃ patyuḥ pṛthivyā dayitasya cātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the body of her husband, the lord of the earth and dear to her own self, with all consciousness departed,

children.text: ālakṣya kiṃcicca vilapya sā satī citāmathāropayadadrisānuni ||
children.translated_text: that faithful woman lamented a little and then placed him on a funeral pyre on the mountain slope.
Having performed the rite, bathed in river water, and given the water-offering to her husband of noble deeds,

children.text: natvā divisthāṃstridaśāṃstriḥ parītya viveśa vahniṃ dhyāyatī bhartṛpādau ||
children.translated_text: she bowed to the gods standing in heaven, circumambulated three times, and entered the fire while meditating on her husband's feet.
Seeing the virtuous woman following her husband, the hero-best <s>Pṛthu</s>,
the wives of the gods, together with the gods, praised her by the thousands as givers of boons.
As they poured down showers of flowers on that slope of <s>Mandara</s>,
and as the instruments of the immortals sounded, they spoke to one another.
The goddesses said:

children.text: aho iyaṃ vadhūrdhanyā yā caivaṃ bhūbhujāṃ patim
children.translated_text: Ah, blessed is this bride, who in this way served as husband the lord of earth's rulers,
with her whole self, as the bride <s>Śrī</s> serves the Lord of Sacrifice.

children.text: saiṣā nūnaṃ vrajatyūrdhvamanu vainyaṃ patiṃ satī
children.translated_text: This faithful woman <s>Arci</s> is surely going upward, following her husband, <s>Vainya</s>;
look how, by an act hard to fathom, she passes beyond us.
What else, indeed, is difficult for such mortals to attain, beyond the Lord's feet,

children.text: bhuvi lolāyuṣo ye vai naiṣkarmyaṃ sādhayantyuta ||
children.translated_text: when, with flickering life on earth, they accomplish <s>naiṣkarmya</s> (freedom from binding action)?

children.text: sa vañcito batātmadhruk kṛcchreṇa mahatā bhuvi
children.translated_text: Alas, that person is cheated, betraying his own self, who, with great difficulty on earth,
has obtained a human birth fit for liberation, yet becomes attached to sense-objects.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
While the immortal women were praising her, the wife went to her husband's world,

children.text: yaṃ vā ātmavidāṃ dhuryo vainyaḥ prāpācyutāśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the world which <s>Vainya</s>, foremost among knowers of the self, reached by taking refuge in <s>Acyuta</s>.
Such was the power of this <s>Pṛthu</s>, that greatest devotee of the Lord;
the story of that man of lofty deeds has been recounted to you.
Whoever, with faith and attention, reads this very great and holy account,
or causes it to be recited, or hears it, will go to the station of <s>Pṛthu</s>.
A brāhmaṇa becomes radiant with brahman; a kṣatriya becomes lord of the earth;
a vaiśya, reading it, becomes lord of his people, and a śūdra reaches the state of the best.
A man or woman who hears this three times with reverence,
if childless, becomes richly blessed with children; if poor, becomes very wealthy.
One whose fame is unclear becomes renowned, and a fool becomes learned;
this brings welfare to people and wards off inauspiciousness.
It brings prosperity, fame, long life, heaven, and removes the stain of the Kali age.
Those who desire the full attainment of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, pleasure, and liberation
should have this recited with faith, for it is the supreme means for the four aims.
A king intent on victory, having heard this, goes forth on campaigns;

children.text: baliṃ tasmai harantyagre rājānaḥ pṛthave yathā ||
children.translated_text: kings bring tribute before him, just as they did before <s>Pṛthu</s>.
Liberated from attachment to anything else, bearing stainless devotion to the Lord,
One should hear, recite to others, or read the holy story of <s>Vainya</s>.
Spoken to <s>Vaicitravīrya</s>, it indicates his great majesty.
A mortal who fixes his mind on this would attain an exalted royal state.
A person who daily hears this with reverence and proclaims the story of <s>Pṛthu</s>, freed from attachment,

children.text: bhagavati bhavasindhupotapāde sa ca nipuṇāṃ labhate ratiṃ manuṣyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: obtains refined love for the Blessed Lord, whose feet are the boat across the ocean of becoming.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
<s>Vijitāśva</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s>'s son, famous through <s>Pṛthu</s>, became the overlord.
Loving his brothers, he gave the quarters to his younger brothers.
The mighty one assigned the eastern quarter to <s>Haryakṣa</s> and the southern to <s>Dhūmrakeśa</s>.
He gave the western quarter to the one named <s>Vṛka</s>, and the fourth to <s>Draviṇa</s>.
Having received from <s>Śakra</s> the power of moving unseen, he was called <s>Antardhāna</s>.
Upon <s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s> he begot three sons, highly esteemed.
They were the fires formerly known as <s>Pāvaka</s>, <s>Pavamāna</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>.
Born because of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s curse, they again reached the path of yoga.
<s>Antardhāna</s> obtained <s>Havirdhāna</s> from <s>Nabhasvatī</s>,
he who, though he knew <s>Indra</s> to be the horse-thief, did not kill him.
Regarding the livelihood of kings, with its taxes, punishments, tolls, and the like, as cruel,
he gave it up under the pretext of a long sacrificial session.
Even there, as a seer of the self, he sacrificed to the swan-like Person, the supreme Self,
and through skillful concentration he attained that same world.
From <s>Havirdhāna</s>, <s>Havirdhānī</s> bore six sons, O <s>Vidura</s>:

children.text: barhiṣadaṃ gayaṃ śuklaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ satyaṃ jitavratam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Barhiṣad</s>, <s>Gaya</s>, <s>Śukla</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Satya</s>, and <s>Jitavrata</s>.
<s>Barhiṣat</s>, the very fortunate son of <s>Havirdhāna</s>, was a lord of creatures.
He was deeply versed in ritual actions and also in yogas, O scion of <s>Kuru</s>.
As he kept extending sacrifice after sacrifice in this divine worship,
the surface of the earth became covered with kuśa grasses whose tips pointed east.
He married <s>Śatadruti</s>, daughter of the Ocean, spoken of by the god of gods.
Seeing her, a maiden charming in every limb and richly adorned,
as she circumambulated at the wedding, <s>Agni</s> desired her as he had <s>Śukī</s>.
Gods, asuras, gandharvas, sages, siddhas, men, and serpents
were captivated in all quarters as she, like <s>Sūryā</s>, merely made her anklets ring.
Ten sons were born to <s>Prācīnabarhiṣ</s> from <s>Śatadruti</s>.
All had the same name and vows; purified by <s>dharma</s>, they were the <s>Pracetases</s>.
Instructed by their father to create progeny, they entered the ocean for austerity.
For ten thousand years they worshiped the lord of austerity with austerity.
They meditated on, recited, and worshiped with restraint
that which had been spoken on the road by <s>Giriśa</s>, whom they had seen and who was gracious to them.
<s>Vidura</s> said:
How did the meeting of the <s>Pracetases</s> with <s>Giritra</s> occur on the road?
And what did pleased <s>Hara</s> say? Tell us that fully, O brahman.
Indeed, O brahmin sage, a meeting here with <s>Śiva</s> is rare for embodied beings.
Sages, through detachment, meditate upon him as the desired goal.
Even though he delights in the self, the blessed <s>Bhava</s>, for the prosperity of this world's order,
wanders joined with his terrible power.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
The virtuous <s>Pracetases</s> accepted their father's command upon their heads.
With minds intent on austerity, they set out toward the western quarter.
They saw a very great lake spread out near the ocean,
clear like the mind of a great soul, with an expanse of tranquil water.
It was a mass of blue and red lotuses, white lotuses, kahlāras, and indīvaras,
and it resounded with the calls of swans, cranes, cakravākas, and kāraṇḍava birds.
Its trees, with creepers as their feet and hairs thrilled by the sweet tones of intoxicated bees,
made a festival for the wind as lotus-cup pollen was scattered through the quarters.
There, hearing celestial gandharva music, delightful to the divine path,
those princes were amazed, with the sounds of mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas, and other instruments following it.
At that very moment, from that lake there emerged, together with his attendants,
the foremost of the immortals, being sung by the followers of the gods.
Seeing him shining like a mass of molten gold, blue-throated, three-eyed,
and gracious-faced, they bowed down, filled with wonder.
That blessed one, remover of the distress of those who take refuge, fond of <s>dharma</s>,
pleased with them as knowers of <s>dharma</s> and endowed with good character, spoke to them, who were themselves delighted.
<s>Śrī Rudra</s> said:
You are the sons of <s>Vediṣad</s>; what you wish to do is known to me.

children.text: anugrahāya bhadraṃ va evaṃ me darśanaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: For your favor, blessings to you, I have made this vision of me occur.
He who has taken refuge in the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, who is directly beyond the impetuous current,

children.text: bhagavantaṃ vāsudevaṃ prapannaḥ sa priyo hi me ||
children.translated_text: beyond the three guṇas and beyond what is called the individual soul, is indeed dear to me.

children.text: svadharmaniṣṭhaḥ śatajanmabhiḥ pumānviriñcatāmeti tataḥ paraṃ hi mām
children.translated_text: A man steadfast in his own <s>dharma</s> attains the state of <s>Viriñci</s> after a hundred births, and after that, beyond it, he reaches me.

children.text: avyākṛtaṃ bhāgavato 'tha vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ yathāhaṃ vibudhāḥ kalātyaye ||
children.translated_text: But the <s>Bhāgavata</s> reaches the unmanifest <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> state, as I and the gods do at the end of time.

children.text: atha bhāgavatā yūyaṃ priyāḥ stha bhagavānyathā
children.translated_text: Therefore you, being <s>Bhāgavatas</s>, are dear, just as the Blessed Lord is dear.
There is never anyone dearer to me than the Lord's <s>Bhāgavatas</s>.

children.text: idaṃ viviktaṃ japtavyaṃ pavitraṃ maṅgalaṃ param
children.translated_text: This secluded recitation is pure and supremely auspicious; it should be recited.
It brings the highest good as well. Listen to it; I shall tell it to you.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Thus the compassionate-hearted blessed <s>Śiva</s> spoke to those royal sons,
who stood with joined palms, a speech wholly devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Śrī Rudra</s> said:

children.text: jitaṃ ta ātmavidvarya svastaye svastirastu me
children.translated_text: Victory is yours, O best of knowers of the self; for welfare, may there be welfare for me.
By worshiping you, all is worshiped. Homage to you, the Self of all.
Homage to the lotus-naveled one, the self of the subtle elements and the senses,
to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, peaceful, immutable, and self-luminous.
Homage to <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, subtle, difficult to pass beyond, and the end-maker.
Obeisance to <s>Pradyumna</s>, the awakener of the universe, the inner self.
Again and again obeisance to <s>Aniruddha</s>, to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the self of the senses.
Obeisance to the supreme swan, the complete one whose self is withdrawn.
Constant obeisance to him who sits in purity, the door to heaven and liberation.
Obeisance to him of golden power, to the thread of the four priestly functions.

children.text: nama ūrja iṣe trayyāḥ pataye yajñaretase
children.translated_text: Obeisance to vigor and nourishment, to the lord of the threefold <s>Veda</s>, to the seed of sacrifice.
And obeisance to the giver of satisfaction to living beings, the self of every savor.
Obeisance to him whose body is the self of all beings, to the particular and to the gross.
Obeisance to the protector of the three worlds, and also to strength and force together.
Obeisance to the sky, the sign of meaning, to the self within and without.
Obeisance to the pure world, to that one there, of abundant splendor.
Obeisance to activity and withdrawal, to the rite for the ancestors and gods, and to action.
Obeisance to death, the fruition of unrighteousness, and the giver of suffering.
Obeisance to you, lord of blessings, to <s>Manu</s>, the self of causality.
Obeisance to vast <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of unfailing intelligence,
and to the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>, lord of <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>.
Obeisance to him joined with the three powers, the bounteous one whose self is the maker of I-ness.
Obeisance to him whose form is mind and intention, to the manifestation of speech.
Give to us, who long to see it, the vision worshiped by the devotees,
the form most dear to your own, an ointment for the qualities of all the senses.
Dark like a glossy rain-cloud, the collection of all beauty,
charming, broad, four-armed, with a well-formed lovely face,
with eyes like the petals of a lotus bud, beautiful brows, and a fine nose,
with handsome teeth, a fine-cheeked face, and equal ears adorned with ornaments,
made beautiful in form by loving, smiling side-glances and curling locks,
clothed in silk shining like lotus filaments, with polished earrings,
gleaming with crown, bracelets, necklace, anklets, and girdle,
made rich with conch, discus, mace, lotus, garland, and excellent jewels,
bearing on a lion-like shoulder a splendid neck with the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem,
flashing like gold on a touchstone, struck by inseparable <s>Śrī</s>,
with a belly lovely with folds moved by inhalation and exhalation,
drawing the universe inward by the deep whirl of his navel.
With dark hips made resplendent by silk and a golden girdle,
beautiful with even, charming feet, shanks, thighs, and low knees,
with a foot whose radiance is like autumn lotus petals and which, by the brightness of its nails, shakes off our inner sin,
show us your own fearless-giving foot, O teacher, highest guide of those who dwell in darkness.
This is the form to be meditated upon by those who desire purification of the self,
for devotion to it gives fearlessness to those who carry out their own <s>dharma</s>.
You are attainable by those who have devotion, but hard to attain for all embodied beings;
even for sovereignty over oneself, you are the desired goal, the destination of knowers of the self through single-mindedness.
Having worshiped him who is hard to worship and hard even for the good to obtain,
who would desire anything outside, apart from the root of his feet, through exclusive devotion?
There, where death is fully overcome, <s>Kṛtānta</s> does not presume to act,
though he destroys the universe with brows flashing with vigor and heroism.
I do not weigh heaven, nor non-return, as equal even for half a moment
to the company of those associated with the Blessed Lord; how much less, then, the blessings of mortals.
Therefore, may there be for us the meeting with those whose sins have been washed away by bathing inwardly and outwardly in the holy ford of your fame, O one of stainless feet,
with those whose nature is compassion for beings and true goodness; this meeting is your favor to us.

children.text: na yasya cittaṃ bahirarthavibhramaṃ tamoguhāyāṃ ca viśuddhamāviśat
children.translated_text: The mind of one purified by your devotion has not entered the bewilderment of external objects or the cave of darkness.

children.text: yadbhaktiyogānugṛhītamañjasā munirvicaṣṭe nanu tatra te gatim ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, by the favor of devotional yoga the sage immediately perceives your course there.
Where this universe is made manifest, and what shines forth in the universe,
that reality is supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the highest light, extended like space.
You, unchanged, created this by māyā of many forms, and again you sustain and destroy it.
O Blessed Lord, we understand you as self-dependent, though the notion of difference belongs to the self badly situated as if in the real.

children.text: kriyākalāpairidameva yoginaḥ śraddhānvitāḥ sādhu yajanti siddhaye
children.translated_text: With collections of rites, yogins endowed with faith rightly worship this very one for perfection,

children.text: bhūtendriyāntaḥkaraṇopalakṣitaṃ vede ca tantre ca ta eva kovidāḥ ||
children.translated_text: marked by beings, senses, and inner organ; in <s>Veda</s> and <s>tantra</s>, they alone are skilled.

children.text: tvameka ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ suptaśaktistayā rajaḥsattvatamo vibhidyate
children.translated_text: You alone are the primal <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose power lies dormant; by it rajas, sattva, and tamas are divided.

children.text: mahānahaṃ khaṃ marudagnivārdharāḥ surarṣayo bhūtagaṇā idaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: From you arise the great principle, egoity, ether, wind, fire, water, earth, the gods, seers, hosts of beings, and this world.
Created by your own power, this fourfold city has been entered by you with a portion of yourself.

children.text: atho vidustaṃ puruṣaṃ santamantarbhuṅkte hṛṣīkairmadhu sāraghaṃ yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then those who know recognize that <s>Puruṣa</s> dwelling within, who enjoys the honey through the senses like a bee taking the essence.

children.text: sa eṣa lokānaticaṇḍavego vikarṣasi tvaṃ khalu kālayānaḥ
children.translated_text: You indeed, moving as the vehicle of time, draw away these worlds with exceedingly fierce speed.
Your nature is inferred from beings through beings, irresistible like the wind sweeping away masses of clouds.
While a careless man cries, 'This is to be done,' absorbed in worry over tasks, swollen with greed and longing for sense objects,
you, never careless, suddenly come upon him, O ender, like a hungry snake licking up a mouse.
What wise man would abandon your lotus feet, when your dwelling is honored, undecaying, and free from humiliation,
which our teacher worshiped without doubt, and also the fourteen <s>Manus</s>, without interruption?
Therefore you are our <s>Brahman</s>, O <s>Paramātman</s>, for those who discern.
For the universe shattered by fear of <s>Rudra</s>, there is no refuge anywhere apart from you.

children.text: idaṃ japata bhadraṃ vo viśuddhā nṛpanandanāḥ
children.translated_text: Recite this; may there be welfare for you, O pure sons of the king,
while you carry out your own <s>dharma</s>, with your intentions offered to the Blessed Lord.
Him alone, the self abiding in the self and established in all beings,
Worship <s>Hari</s>, praise him, and meditate on him again and again.
Having received the instruction in <s>yoga</s>, and maintaining the vows of sages,
all of you, with concentrated minds, should practice this with reverence.
Long ago the Blessed Lord, the lord who creates the universe, spoke this to us
when he wished to create <s>Bhṛgu</s> and the others, his sons, who themselves wished to create.

children.text: te vayaṃ noditāḥ sarve prajāsarge prajeśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: Urged by him, we, all the lords of creatures, engaged in the creation of beings;
with our darkness destroyed by this teaching, we seek to create varied living beings.
Then a man who is always disciplined, reciting this with attentive mind,
and devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, quickly obtains the highest good.
Among all goods in this world, knowledge is the supreme and final good;
by the boat of knowledge he easily crosses the hard-to-cross ocean of misfortune.

children.text: ya imaṃ śraddhayā yukto madgītaṃ bhagavatstavam
children.translated_text: The man who, joined with faith, studies this hymn to the Blessed Lord sung by me
thereby worships <s>Hari</s>, who is difficult to propitiate.
A man obtains from him, without delay, whatever he desires,
from him who is well pleased by the song sung by me, the one beloved source of all blessings.

children.text: idaṃ yaḥ kalya utthāya prāñjaliḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: The mortal who rises early, with folded hands and endowed with faith,
and hears this or causes it to be heard, is released from the bonds of karma.

children.text: gītaṃ mayedaṃ naradevanandanāḥ parasya puṃsaḥ paramātmanaḥ stavam
children.translated_text: O princes, this hymn to the Supreme Person, the supreme self, has been sung by me.
Reciting it with one-pointed minds, practice great austerity; at the end you will obtain what you desire.
<s>Maitreya</s> said:
Having instructed them thus, the Blessed Lord <s>Hara</s>, worshipped by the sons of <s>Barhiṣad</s>,
disappeared then and there while the royal sons looked on.
All the <s>Pracetases</s>, reciting the Rudra-song, the hymn to the Blessed Lord,
performed austerity in the water for ten thousand years.
O <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>, whose mind was attached to ritual actions,
was awakened by compassionate <s>Nārada</s>, the knower of the truth of the self.
What good for yourself, O king, do you seek by action?
The good is the removal of suffering and the attainment of happiness; that is not achieved here by such action.
The king said:
I do not know the supreme good, O greatly fortunate one; my understanding has been thrown aside by ritual action.

children.text: brūhi me vimalaṃ jñānaṃ yena mucyeya karmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Teach me pure knowledge, by which I may be freed from karmic acts.
In households with their false duties, with his mind fixed on sons, wife, wealth, and property,
the deluded man does not find the supreme good, but wanders on the paths of saṃsāra.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
O, O king, lord of creatures, look at the animals in the sacrifice,
living beings by the thousands, slaughtered by you without compassion.

children.text: ete tvāṃ sampratīkṣante smaranto vaiśasaṃ tava
children.translated_text: They are now waiting for you, remembering your cruelty;
when you have passed away, they will cut you with iron-pointed weapons, their anger aroused.
In this connection I shall tell you an ancient narrative;
listen to the story of <s>Purañjana</s> as I relate it.
There was, O king, a famous king named <s>Purañjana</s>.
He had a friend named <s>Avijñāta</s>, whose activities were unknown.
That powerful king, searching for a refuge, wandered over the earth.
When he found nothing suitable, he became as if dejected.

children.text: na sādhu mene tāḥ sarvā bhūtale yāvatīḥ puraḥ
children.translated_text: He did not consider good all the cities that existed on the earth,
for he desired objects of enjoyment, seeking the fitting occasion for each of them.
Then one day, on the southern slopes of <s>Himavat</s>,
he saw a city marked by auspicious signs and having nine gates.
It had ramparts, parks, watchtowers, moats, gateways, and arches,
and it was crowded on every side with houses and with golden, silver, and iron turrets.
With blue sapphire, crystal, vaidūrya, pearls, emeralds, and red gems,
its mansion floors were laid out and it shone with splendor, like <s>Bhogavatī</s>.
It was furnished with assembly halls, squares, roads, pleasure grounds, and markets,
with shrines, banners, flags, and coral platforms.
Outside the city, in a park filled with divine trees and creepers,
there were reservoirs noisy with calling birds and swarms of bees.
The wind from the flower-filled spring was sprinkled by drops from snowy waterfalls,
and the banks, with moving red shoots, branches, and lotus ponds, were richly beautiful.
There, with herds of many forest animals and undisturbed ascetics,
a traveler thinks he is being summoned by the calls of cuckoos.
There by chance he saw an excellent young woman,
approaching with ten attendants, each one the leader of a hundred.
She was guarded on every side by a five-headed serpent as her gatekeeper,
searching for a husband, not yet mature, and able to assume forms at will.
She had a fine nose, good teeth, youthfulness, fine cheeks, and a lovely face,
and she bore the beauty of earrings set evenly upon her two ears.
Her lower garment was yellowish; she had beautiful hips, a dark complexion, and a golden girdle.
As she walked, her anklets rang at her feet, and she seemed like a goddess.
Her breasts, revealing her dawning youth, were round, even, and close together;
out of modesty she covered them with the edge of her garment, moving with the gait of an elephant.
The hero spoke sweetly to her, who was beautiful with a bashful smile,
having been touched by the smooth arrow of her sidelong glance, her brows restless with love.

children.text: kā tvaṃ kañjapalāśākṣi kasyāsīha kutaḥ sati
children.translated_text: Who are you, lotus-petal-eyed one? Whose are you here, and where have you come from, virtuous lady?

children.text: imāmupa purīṃ bhīru kiṃ cikīrṣasi śaṃsa me ||
children.translated_text: Coming near this city, timid one, what do you wish to do? Tell me.

children.text: ka ete 'nupathā ye ta ekādaśa mahābhaṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Who are these eleven great warriors of yours who follow your path?

children.text: etā vā lalanāḥ subhru ko 'yaṃ te 'hiḥ puraḥsaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And who are these women, fair-browed one? Who is this serpent going before you?

children.text: tvaṃ hrīrbhavānyasyatha vāgramā patiṃ vicinvatī kiṃ munivadraho vane
children.translated_text: Are you <s>Hrī</s>, or <s>Bhavānī</s>, or perhaps <s>Ramā</s>, seeking your husband here alone in the forest like a sage?
Where is the lotus bud that fell from your fingertips, the one that fulfills all desires for those who long for your feet?

children.text: nāsāṃ varorvanyatamā bhuvispṛk purīmimāṃ vīravareṇa sākam
children.translated_text: For none of these, O fair-thighed one, touches the earth; this city, together with a foremost hero...
You are fit, by abundant deeds, to adorn the supreme world, as <s>Śrī</s> adorns the sacrificial Person.
For, with your sidelong glance, your bashful mood, your smile, and your playful eyebrows,
this blessed <s>Manobhava</s>, sent toward me by you, torments me; therefore show me favor, O lovely one.
Your face, O fair-browed, starry-eyed one, is veiled by a cluster of hanging dark curls;

children.text: unnīya me darśaya valguvācakaṃ yadvrīḍayā nābhimukhaṃ śucismite ||
children.translated_text: lift it up and show it to me, charmingly speaking; from bashfulness, O bright-smiling one, it is not turned toward me.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
When the woman heard <s>Purañjana</s> begging in this way, like an impatient man,

children.text: abhyanandata taṃ vīraṃ hasantī vīra mohitā ||
children.translated_text: she welcomed that hero, smiling, O hero, herself captivated by him.

children.text: na vidāma vayaṃ samyak kartāraṃ puruṣarṣabha
children.translated_text: We do not know rightly the maker, O bull among men,

children.text: ātmanaśca parasyāpi gotraṃ nāma ca yatkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: nor the lineage and name that have been made for ourselves or for another.

children.text: ihādya santamātmānaṃ vidāma na tataḥ param
children.translated_text: We know ourselves existing here today, and nothing beyond that,
nor by whom this city, a refuge for the self, was fashioned, O hero.

children.text: ete sakhāyaḥ sakhyo me narā nāryaśca mānada
children.translated_text: These men and women are my male friends and female friends, O giver of honor;
while I sleep, this serpent stays awake, guarding the city.
By good fortune you have come; may it be well with you. You desire common sensual pleasures;
I shall procure them for you with my own kinsmen, O subduer of foes.
Take possession of this nine-gated city, O lord;
accept the enjoyments of desire brought by me for a hundred years.
For what man other than you should I delight, one unknowing in passion and unskilled,
turned away from the next world, ignorant of tomorrow, a mere beast?
Here, indeed, are <s>dharma</s> (normative order), wealth, and desire, the joy of offspring, immortality, and fame,

children.text: lokā viśokā virajā yānna kevalino viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: and worlds free from sorrow and stain, which the solitary ones do not know.
For ancestors, gods, seers, mortals, beings, and indeed for oneself,
they say that the householder stage is welfare and refuge in this existence.

children.text: kā nāma vīra vikhyātaṃ vadānyaṃ priyadarśanam
children.translated_text: What woman, O hero, would not choose as her beloved husband

children.text: na vṛṇīta priyaṃ prāptaṃ mādṛśī tvādṛśaṃ patim ||
children.translated_text: one famous, generous, pleasing to see, and arrived like you, a beloved man suited to one like me?

children.text: kasyā manaste bhuvi bhogibhogayoḥ striyā na sajedbhujayormahābhuja
