children.translated_text: What woman's mind on earth would not cling to your arms, O mighty-armed one, which are like the coils of serpents?
For with your compassionate, lifted, smiling glance you move about to remove the heavy misery of the unprotected.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: iti tau dampatī tatra samudya samayaṃ mithaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the two, husband and wife, having come to a mutual agreement there,

children.text: tāṃ praviśya purīṃ rājanmumudāte śataṃ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: entered that city, O king, and rejoiced for a hundred years.

children.text: upagīyamāno lalitaṃ tatra tatra ca gāyakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Being sung to sweetly here and there by singers,
and playing surrounded by women, he entered the lake in the hot season.

children.text: saptopari kṛtā dvāraḥ purastasyāstu dve adhaḥ
children.translated_text: Seven gates were made above and two below in that city,
for separate movement toward sense-objects by whoever was its lord.
There were five eastern gates, one southern, and likewise one northern;

children.text: paścime dve amūṣāṃ te nāmāni nṛpa varṇaye ||
children.translated_text: there were two in the west. I shall describe their names to you, O king.
<s>Khadyotā</s> and <s>Āvirmukhī</s> were two eastern gates, built in one place;
with <s>Dyumat</s> as his companion he goes through them to the region <s>Vibhrājita</s>.
<s>Nalinī</s> and <s>Nālinī</s> were two eastern gates, built in one place;
with <s>Avadhūta</s> as his companion he goes through them to the domain of fragrance, <s>Saurabha</s>.
In front was a gate named <s>Mukhyā</s>; through it, to <s>Āpaṇa</s> and <s>Bahūdana</s>,
the king of the city goes to those two regions, accompanied by <s>Rasajña</s> and <s>Vipaṇa</s>.
The gate of the city called <s>Pitṛhū</s>, O king, was on the south; through it <s>Purañjana</s>,
accompanied by <s>Śrutadhara</s>, goes to the country of <s>Dakṣiṇapañcāla</s>.
The gate of the city called <s>Devahū</s> was on the north; through it <s>Purañjana</s>,
accompanied by <s>Śrutadhara</s>, goes to the country of <s>Uttarapañcāla</s>.
There was a western gate called <s>Āsurī</s>; through it <s>Purañjana</s> goes
to the region called <s>Grāmaka</s>, accompanied by <s>Durmada</s>.
There was a western gate called <s>Nirṛti</s>; through it <s>Purañjana</s> goes
to the region called <s>Vaiśasa</s>, accompanied by <s>Lubdhaka</s>.
Among these citizens, the two named <s>Nirvāk</s> and <s>Peśaskṛt</s> were both blind;
the lord of those possessing eyes goes with them and acts.
Whenever he entered the inner apartment, accompanied by <s>Viṣūcīna</s>,

children.text: mohaṃ prasādaṃ harṣaṃ vā yāti jāyātmajodbhavam ||
children.translated_text: he experienced delusion, serenity, or joy born from wife and children.
Thus attached to activities, desire-centered, deceived and unknowing,
whatever the queen wished to do, that very thing he followed.
At times, when she drank wine, he drank too, staggered with intoxication;
at times, when she ate, he ate, and when she chewed, he chewed along with her.
At times he sang when she sang; at times he wept when she wept;
at times he laughed when she laughed, and he babbled after her when she babbled.
At times he ran when she ran; when she stood, he stood after her;
when she lay down, he lay down after her, and at times he sat when she sat.
At times he listened when she listened; when she saw, he saw after her;

children.text: kvacij jighrati jighrantyāṃ spṛśantyāṃ spṛśati kvacit ||
children.translated_text: at times he smelled when she smelled, and when she touched, he touched.
At times, when his wife grieved, he grieved after her like a wretched man;
when she rejoiced, he rejoiced after her, and when she was delighted, he delighted.
Thus deceived by his queen, cheated by all <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature),
the ignorant man, unwilling, imitated her out of weakness, like a tame play-animal.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
One day he, the great archer, mounted a swift chariot with five horses,
with two poles, two wheels, one axle, three bamboo staffs, and five joints,
with one rein, one bridle, one seat, and two yoke-pins,
with five weapons, seven coverings, and five modes of movement.
Mounting it, with golden fittings, wearing golden armor and an inexhaustible quiver,
the lord of eleven troops went to the forest called <s>Pañcaprastha</s>.
There, proud and having taken up arrows and bow, he pursued the hunt.
abandoning his wife, when it was not proper to do so, eager for the vice of hunting deer.
Taking on a demonic way of life, fierce in nature and without compassion,
he killed the forest-roaming creatures in the woods with sharp arrows.
For a king, when sacrificial places are in view, it is prescribed that in the forest
he may kill pure animals only as much as is necessary; so it is regulated.

children.text: ya evaṃ karma niyataṃ vidvānkurvīta mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: A man who, knowing this, performs such prescribed action,

children.text: karmaṇā tena rājendra jñānena na sa lipyate ||
children.translated_text: O king, is not tainted by that action, because of his knowledge.
But one who acts otherwise, mounted on pride, becomes bound;
fallen into the current of the guṇas, his wisdom destroyed, he goes downward.
There, among those whose bodies were pierced by the variegated, swift, arrow-headed shafts,
there arose an unbearable tumult of suffering for the compassionate-hearted animals.
Hares, boars, buffaloes, gavayas, rurus, porcupines,
and various other pure animals he killed; then he came to fatigue.
Then, exhausted by hunger, thirst, and weariness, he turned back and went home.
Having bathed and eaten suitable food, he lay down, his fatigue gone.
He honored himself with incense, ointments, garlands, and the like;
with all his limbs well adorned, he fixed his mind on his queen.
Satisfied, delighted, and very proud, his mind drawn by Kāma,
he did not see the fair-hipped lady, the housewife of the householder.
Distracted, as if pained, he asked the women of the inner apartments,

children.text: api vaḥ kuśalaṃ rāmāḥ seśvarīṇāṃ yathā purā ||
children.translated_text: "Are you well, ladies? Is it with your mistress as it was before?
The household possessions in the house do not please me now as they did before,

children.text: yadi na syādgṛhe mātā patnī vā patidevatā
children.translated_text: if in the house there is not a mother, or a wife devoted to her husband.

children.text: vyaṅge ratha iva prājñaḥ ko nāmāsīta dīnavat ||
children.translated_text: What wise man would sit there pitiably, like a chariot with a broken part?

children.text: kva vartate sā lalanā majjantaṃ vyasanārṇave
children.translated_text: Where is that woman who rescues me as I sink in the ocean of vice,

children.text: yā māmuddharate prajñāṃ dīpayantī pade pade ||
children.translated_text: kindling my understanding at every step?"
The women said:
"Lord of men, we do not know what your beloved intends.
Look, destroyer of foes: she is lying on the bare ground."
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Seeing his own queen cast down on the ground, <s>Purañjana</s>,
whose knowledge had been shaken by attachment to her, fell into the deepest distress.
Though he consoled her with gentle speech, his heart tormented,
he did not detect in himself the sign of the beloved's agitation born of affection.
Then, slowly, the hero, skilled in conciliation, coaxed her;
he touched her pair of feet and spoke to her as she was fondled on his lap.
<s>Purañjana</s> said:

children.text: nūnaṃ tvakṛtapuṇyāste bhṛtyā yeṣv īśvarāḥ śubhe
children.translated_text: "Surely those servants of yours are without accumulated merit, O auspicious one, whose masters,
having accepted their offense as their own, do not apply the rod of correction.
Punishment assigned by a master to his servants is the highest favor;
a child, slender lady, does not know that act of a kinsman when he is angry.
Therefore, O fine-toothed, fair-browed, high-minded one, show us your face, with its glance and smile shining slowly through the heavy shame of love,

children.text: nīlālakālibhirupaskṛtamunnasaṃ naḥ svānāṃ pradarśaya manasvini valguvākyam ||
children.translated_text: with its raised nose adorned by rows of dark curls; speak sweet words to your own people.

children.text: tasmindadhe damamahaṃ tava vīrapatni yo 'nyatra bhūsurakulātkṛtakilbiṣastam
children.translated_text: I shall bring him under your control, that man who, apart from the family of the earth-gods, has committed an offense against you, O hero's wife;

children.text: paśye na vītabhayamunmuditaṃ trilokyāmanyatra vai murariporitaratra dāsāt ||
children.translated_text: in the three worlds I see him nowhere fearless and joyful, except in relation to <s>Muraripu</s>, or otherwise as a servant.

children.text: vaktraṃ na te vitilakaṃ malinaṃ viharṣaṃ saṃrambhabhīmam avimṛṣṭamapetarāgam
children.translated_text: I do not see your face with its tilaka, unstained, cheerful, and loving; instead it is fearsome with anger, unwashed, and bereft of affection.

children.text: paśye stanāvapi śucopahatau sujātau bimbādharaṃ vigatakuṅkumapaṅkarāgam ||
children.translated_text: I see your well-formed breasts struck by grief, and your bimba-like lips with the red stain of saffron gone.

children.text: tanme prasīda suhṛdaḥ kṛtakilbiṣasya svairaṃ gatasya mṛgayāṃ vyasanāturasya
children.translated_text: So be gracious to me, your friend, who has committed an offense, who went off freely to the hunt, afflicted by vice.

children.text: kā devaraṃ vaśagataṃ kusumāstravegavisrastapauṃsnamuśatī na bhajeta kṛtye ||
children.translated_text: What woman, desiring what ought to be done, would not attend to a brother-in-law who is under her control, his manhood scattered by the force of the flower-weapon?"
<s>Nārada</s> said:
In this way, by her graceful charms, <s>Purañjanī</s> duly brought <s>Purañjana</s> under control,
O great king, and she took pleasure, causing her husband to take pleasure.
That king, O king, rejoiced over his queen when she came to him, well bathed, with a lovely face,
with auspicious rites performed and satisfied.
Embraced by her, his neck clasped, his consciousness drawn away by secret coaxing words,

children.text: na kālaraṃho bubudhe duratyayaṃ divā niśeti pramadāparigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he, possessed by women, did not perceive the irresistible speed of time, by day or by night.
Lying on a costly couch, puffed up with intoxication, high-minded, with the queen's arm as his pillow,

children.text: tāmeva vīro manute paraṃ yatastamo'bhibhūto na nijaṃ paraṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: the hero thought her alone to be supreme; overcome by darkness, he did not know what was his own or another's.
As he thus took pleasure with her, his mind stained by desire,
O king, his new youth passed away as if it were half a moment.
By <s>Purañjanī</s>, <s>Purañjana</s> begot sons,
eleven hundred of them, O <s>Virāṭ</s>, and then half his life had passed.
He also begot one hundred and ten daughters, bringers of honor to their father and mother,
the daughters of <s>Purañjana</s>, endowed with good conduct, generosity, and virtues, O lord of creatures.
He, the lord of <s>Pañcāla</s>, joined his sons, who increased their father's lineage,
with wives, and his daughters with suitable bridegrooms.
And the sons of his sons were born, one hundred for each one;
by them the lineage of <s>Purañjana</s> flourished among the <s>Pañcālas</s>.
Among them, the heirs of his estate, living on his house and treasury,
he became bound to the objects of sense through deeply rooted possessiveness.
Consecrated, he performed terrible sacrifices that killed animals,
worshiping the gods, the ancestors, and the lords of beings for various desires, as you have done.
While he was thus occupied and heedless, his mind attached to his family,

children.text: āsasāda sa vai kālo yo 'priyaḥ priyayoṣitām ||
children.translated_text: there approached that time which is unwelcome to those who love beloved women.
O king, there was one known as <s>Caṇḍavega</s>, the lord of the Gandharvas,
and his powerful Gandharvas numbered three hundred and sixty.
He had Gandharvī women of the same number, coupled as white and black,
and by turns they plunder the city fashioned out of every object of desire.
When those followers of <s>Caṇḍavega</s>
began to rob the city of <s>Purañjana</s>, there <s>Prajāgara</s> resisted them.

children.text: sa saptabhiḥ śataireko viṃśatyā ca śataṃ samāḥ
children.translated_text: He, though alone, with seven hundred and twenty, for a hundred years,
as the superintendent of <s>Purañjana</s>'s city, fought powerfully with the Gandharvas.
As his own connection was being worn away in battle by many against one,
he, distressed, fell into deep anxiety, together with his realm, city, and kinsmen.

children.text: sa eva puryāṃ madhubhuk pañcāleṣu svapārṣadaiḥ
children.translated_text: In that very city, among the <s>Pañcālas</s>, he enjoyed sweetness with his attendants,
receiving the tribute brought to him; conquered by women, he did not perceive the danger.
There was a certain daughter of Time who, desiring a husband throughout the three worlds,
wandered about, O <s>Barhiṣman</s>, but no one welcomed her.
Because of her own misfortune she was known in the world as <s>Durbhagā</s>, the unfortunate one;

children.text: yā tuṣṭā rājarṣaye tu vṛtādātpūrave varam ||
children.translated_text: yet when she was pleased with the royal seer <s>Pūru</s>, she gave him the boon he had chosen.
Once, while wandering, she saw me, firm in a great vow,

children.text: vavre bṛhadvrataṃ māṃ tu jānatī kāmamohitā ||
children.translated_text: as I had come from <s>Brahmaloka</s> to the earth, and, knowing me, chose me, being deluded by desire.
Angry with me, she gave a very hard-to-bear curse:
"You shall not be able to stay in one place, O sage, since you have turned away from my command."
Then, her intention frustrated, the maiden approached the lord of the Yavanas,
named <s>Bhaya</s>, whom I had pointed out, and chose him as her husband.

children.text: ṛṣabhaṃ yavanānāṃ tvāṃ vṛṇe vīrepsitaṃ patim
children.translated_text: "I choose you, the bull among the Yavanas, as the husband desired by a hero;

children.text: saṅkalpastvayi bhūtānāṃ kṛtaḥ kila na riṣyati ||
children.translated_text: for a resolve fixed on you by living beings, it is said, does not fail.
Two childish people, of false grasp, are to be pitied:
one who does not give what is sanctioned by the world and scripture, and one who does not desire it.

children.text: atho bhajasva māṃ bhadra bhajantīṃ me dayāṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Therefore accept me, good sir; I am devoted to you, so show me compassion.
This much is the <s>dharma</s> (duty) of manliness: that one has compassion for the distressed."
Hearing the words spoken by <s>Kālakanyā</s>, the lord of the Yavanas,
wishing to accomplish the secret purpose of the gods, smilingly spoke to her.
"A husband has been appointed for you by me through inward concentration.
This world does not approve of you, inauspicious and unwelcome as you are.
You, whose movement is unmanifest, enjoy the world fashioned by karma,

children.text: yā hi me pṛtanāyuktā prajānāśaṃ praṇeṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: for, joined with my army, you will lead living beings to destruction.

children.text: prajvāro 'yaṃ mama bhrātā tvaṃ ca me bhaginī bhava
children.translated_text: This <s>Prajvāra</s> is my brother; you shall be my sister.
With both of you I move in this world, unseen, with a fearsome army."
<s>Nārada</s> said:
The soldiers of the one named <s>Bhaya</s>, O <s>Barhiṣman</s>, agents of destiny,
roamed over this earth together with <s>Prajvāra</s> and <s>Kālakanyā</s>.

children.text: ta ekadā tu rabhasā purañjanapurīṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: Then one day, with violence, O king, they surrounded the city of <s>Purañjana</s>,
rich in earthly enjoyments and guarded by an aged serpent.
<s>Kālakanyā</s> too forcibly consumed the city of <s>Purañjana</s>;
overcome by her, a person at once comes to emptiness and loss of vigor.
As she was consuming it, the Yavanas entered through the gates
from every direction and oppressed the whole city exceedingly.
When that city was being tormented, the self-regarding <s>Purañjana</s>,
a householder confused by possessiveness, underwent many kinds of suffering.
Embraced by the maiden, bereft of splendor, pitiable, absorbed in objects of sense,
his understanding lost and his lordly power seized by the Gandharvas and Yavanas by force,
seeing his own city broken apart, and his sons, grandsons, followers, ministers,
and wife turned hostile, disregarded, and bereft of affection,
seeing himself seized by the maiden and the <s>Pañcālas</s> injured by enemies,
he was overtaken by endless anxiety and found no remedy for it.
Wretched, longing for pleasures already exhausted and worn out by the maiden,
his sense of self and affection gone, yet still cherishing his sons and wife,
the king began to leave that city, overrun by the Gandharvas and Yavanas
and crushed by <s>Kālakanyā</s>, though he did not wish to do so.
<s>Prajvāra</s>, the elder brother of the one named <s>Bhaya</s>, arrived,

children.text: dadāha tāṃ purīṃ kṛtsnāṃ bhrātuḥ priyacikīrṣayā ||
children.translated_text: and, wishing to do what was dear to his brother, burned that whole city.
As it was burning, together with its citizens and equipment,
the family man, along with his wife and lineage, was tormented.
When the city had been seized by <s>Kālakanyā</s>, its dwelling place obstructed by the Yavanas,
and joined with <s>Prajvāra</s>, the guardian of the city suffered distress.
There, in great hardship and trembling severely, he was unable to protect it,
and then wished to depart, like a serpent from a tree hollow that is on fire.
When his limbs had grown slack, his manly strength taken away by the Gandharvas,
and he was hemmed in by the enemy Yavanas, O king, he wept.
His daughters, sons and grandsons, sisters, sons-in-law, and attendants,
and whatever remained as his own property, house, treasury, and possessions,
the foolish householder had accepted in his homes as "I" and "mine";
wretched, with separation from his beloved woman at hand, he brooded.
"When I have gone to another world, how will this family woman, without a protector,
live, grieving over the children?

children.text: na mayyanāśite bhuṅkte nāsnāte snāti matparā
children.translated_text: When I have not eaten, she does not eat; when I have not bathed, she does not bathe, devoted to me.
When I am angry she is very frightened, and when rebuked she restrains her speech out of fear.
When I am away, worn thin by grief, she awakens me, who am unknowing.
Though she is the mother of brave sons, she will not be able to follow this path of a householder.
How indeed will the poor boys, or the girls with no other refuge,
live when I am gone, like people in a broken boat upon the ocean?"
Thus, with pitiable understanding, he was lamenting what did not deserve such lamentation,
A figure named <s>Bhaya</s>, resolved to seize him, approached him.
As he was being led like an animal by the <s>Yavanas</s> to his own destruction,
his followers ran after him along the road, grieving and deeply distressed.
When the serpent, blocked and departing, abandoned the city,

children.text: yadā tamevānu purī viśīrṇā prakṛtiṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: then that very city, following him, fell apart and returned to its original elements.
Being dragged away by force by the stronger <s>Yavana</s>,
and enveloped in darkness, he did not find before him his companion and well-wishing friend.
The sacrificial animals that had been slaughtered by this merciless man
cut him with axes in anger, remembering that injury done by him.
Sunk in boundless darkness, with his memory lost, for years
he experienced endless suffering, corrupted by attachment to women.
Holding that very woman in his mind, he became an excellent woman
next in the palace of <s>Vidarbha</s>, the lion among kings.
<s>Malayadhvaja</s>, the <s>Pāṇḍya</s> who conquered enemy cities, married
the <s>Vaidarbhī</s> princess whose bride-price was valor, after defeating the kings in battle.
In her he begot one dark-eyed daughter
and seven younger sons, the seven rulers of the <s>Draviḍa</s> land.
Each one of them, O king, had arbudas upon arbudas of descendants,
by whose lineage the earth will be enjoyed through the next manvantara.
<s>Agastya</s> first married his daughter, firm in vows,
in whom <s>Dṛḍhacyuta</s> was born, the sage whose son was <s>Idhmavāha</s>.
After dividing the earth among his sons, the royal sage <s>Malayadhvaja</s>,
wishing to worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, went to <s>Kulācala</s>.
Leaving home, sons, and enjoyments, <s>Vaidarbhī</s> of wine-dark eyes
followed the lord of the <s>Pāṇḍyas</s> as moonlight follows the moon.
There were sacred waters named <s>Candravasā</s>, <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, and <s>Vaṭodakā</s>;
with their holy waters he constantly cleansed himself inwardly and outwardly.
Subsisting on bulbs, seeds, roots, fruits, flowers, leaves, grass, and water,
he undertook austerity that gradually emaciated his body.
Cold and heat, wind and rain, hunger and thirst, pleasure and pain, pleasant and unpleasant things,
these pairs of opposites he conquered, being equal in vision.
With austerity and knowledge, his impurities ripened away through observances and restraints;
having conquered the senses, breath, and mind, he yoked himself to <s>brahman</s> (ultimate reality).
He remained fixed in one place like a post for a hundred divine years,
bearing love for blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> and knowing nothing else.
Knowing the self as all-pervading, and as distinct within the self,
as the witness, like one who has understood a dream, he came to rest.
By the lamp of pure knowledge, directly spoken by blessed <s>Hari</s> as guru, O king,
shining with its face turned everywhere,

children.text: pare brahmaṇi cātmānaṃ paraṃ brahma tathātmani
children.translated_text: he saw the self in the supreme <s>brahman</s>, and likewise the supreme <s>brahman</s> in the self;
abandoning separate seeing, he withdrew from this world.
<s>Vaidarbhī</s>, whose husband was her deity, served with love
her husband <s>Malayadhvaja</s>, the supreme knower of dharma, after giving up pleasures.
Clothed in bark, emaciated by vows, her hair become matted,
she shone quietly near her husband like a flame beside a fire at rest.
When the woman did not know that her dearest one had ceased to live,
she approached his firm seat and attended on him as before.
When, while worshipping him, she did not perceive warmth in her husband's feet,
her heart was shaken, like a doe separated from the herd.
Lamenting herself as wretched and without kin, with agitated tears
wetting her breasts, she cried out sweetly in the forest.
Rise, rise, O royal sage; this earth girdled by the ocean,
frightened by robbers who are mere kṣatriyas in name, deserves to be protected by you.
Thus lamenting, the young woman who had followed her husband in the forest
fell at her husband's feet and, weeping, shed tears.

children.text: citiṃ dārumayīṃ citvā tasyāṃ patyuḥ kalevaram
children.translated_text: Having built a wooden funeral pyre and placed her husband's body upon it,
she lit it and, while lamenting, set her mind on dying with him.
There a certain Brahmin, an earlier friend and self-possessed man,
consoled her with gentle words and spoke to her as she wept, O lord.
The Brahmin said:

children.text: kā tvaṃ kasyāsi ko vāyaṃ śayāno yasya śocasi
children.translated_text: Who are you? Whose are you? And who is this man lying here, for whom you grieve?

children.text: jānāsi kiṃ sakhāyaṃ māṃ yenāgre vicacartha ha ||
children.translated_text: Do you know me, the friend with whom you formerly wandered?
Do you remember yourself, O friend, and me, your unknown friend?
Leaving me, you went away, seeking a place and delighting in earthly enjoyments.

children.text: haṃsāvahaṃ ca tvaṃ cārya sakhāyau mānasāyanau
children.translated_text: I and you, O noble one, were two swans, friends
dwelling in <s>Mānasa</s> for a thousand years.

children.text: sa tvaṃ vihāya māṃ bandho gato grāmyamatirmahīm
children.translated_text: You, my companion, left me and went to the earth with a worldly mind;
as you wandered, you saw a place constructed by some woman.
It had five gardens, nine gates, one guardian, three chambers,
six families, five markets, five material constituents, and a woman as its master.

children.text: pañcendriyārthā ārāmā dvāraḥ prāṇā nava prabho
children.translated_text: The five sense-objects are the gardens; the nine life-openings are the gates, O lord;
fire, water, and food are the chambers; the family is the collection of senses.
The market is the power of action, and the imperishable material cause is made of the elements;
the person, lord of power, having entered here, is not understood.
In that city, touched by <s>Rāmā</s> and delighting, with sacred learning and memory lost,
through association with her you have reached such a most wretched condition, O lord.

children.text: na tvaṃ vidarbhaduhitā nāyaṃ vīraḥ suhṛttava
children.translated_text: You are not the daughter of <s>Vidarbha</s>, and this hero is not your friend;

children.text: na patistvaṃ purañjanyā ruddho navamukhe yayā ||
children.translated_text: nor are you the husband of <s>Purañjanī</s>, by whom you were confined in the nine-mouthed city.

children.text: māyā hyeṣā mayā sṛṣṭā yatpumāṃsaṃ striyaṃ satīm
children.translated_text: For this is indeed <s>māyā</s> (illusion), created by me, by which a person is taken as a man, a woman, or a faithful wife...
If you think, indeed, that there is no fear for us both, then, as two <s>haṃsas</s>, look at the course of us two.

children.text: ahaṃ bhavānna cānyastvaṃ tvamevāhaṃ vicakṣva bhoḥ
children.translated_text: I am you, and you are no other; you yourself are I. Consider this, sir.

children.text: na nau paśyanti kavayaśchidraṃ jātu manāgapi ||
children.translated_text: The wise never see even the slightest division between us two.
Just as a person might behold his own single self as made double
in a mirror and in the eye, so indeed is the difference between us two.

children.text: evaṃ sa mānaso haṃso haṃsena pratibodhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus that mental <s>haṃsa</s>, awakened by the <s>haṃsa</s>,
became himself again and, when that deviation ceased, regained the memory that had been lost.
O <s>Barhiṣman</s>, this teaching concerning the self has been shown indirectly,
because the blessed Lord, the maker of the universe, delights in indirect expression.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Thus praised by the hosts of gods, the blessed <s>Hari</s>, the Lord,
appeared to them, O king, with the brilliance of the rising of a thousand suns.
By that very sudden radiance all the gods had their sight checked;

children.text: nāpaśyan khaṃ diśaḥ kṣauṇīmātmānaṃ ca kuto vibhum ||
children.translated_text: they did not see the sky, the quarters, the earth, or themselves, much less the all-pervading Lord.

children.text: viriñco bhagavān dṛṣṭvā saha śarveṇa tāṃ tanum
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Viriñca</s>, seeing that form together with <s>Śarva</s>,
clear, emerald-dark, with eyes red like the heart of a lotus,
with shining silk garments bright like refined gold,
with every limb gracious and lovely, with a beautiful face and handsome brows,
adorned with a great jeweled crown and with armlets,
with cheeks and lotus-like face radiant from earrings,
beautiful with girdle, belt, bracelets, necklace, and anklets,
bearing the <s>Kaustubha</s> ornament, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, and a forest garland,
attended by his own weapons, such as the <s>Sudarśana</s>, embodied in visible forms,
the chief of the gods, together with <s>Śarva</s>, praised the supreme Person,
along with all the hosts of immortals, all their limbs bowed down to the ground.
<s>Śrī Brahmā</s> said:
Obeisance, obeisance to you, whose birth, continuance, and restraint are unborn, whose nature is an ocean of the happiness of liberation,
subtler than the subtle, of immeasurable abode, of mighty majesty.
This form of yours, O best of persons, worthy of worship by those seeking blessedness, by Vedic and Tantric

children.text: yogena dhātaḥ saha nas trilokān paśyāmy amuṣminnu ha viśvamūrtau ||
children.translated_text: yoga, O creator, I see before us here as the form of the universe together with the three worlds.

children.text: tvayy agra āsīt tvayi madhya āsīt tvayy anta āsīd idam ātmatantre
children.translated_text: In you this was at the beginning, in you it was in the middle, in you it was at the end, self-dependent one.

children.text: tvamādiranto jagato 'sya madhyaṃ ghaṭasya mṛtsneva paraḥ parasmāt ||
children.translated_text: You are the beginning, the end, and the middle of this world, beyond what is beyond, like clay in relation to a pot.

children.text: tvaṃ māyayātmāśrayayā svayedaṃ nirmāya viśvaṃ tadanupraviṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: By your own self-supported <s>māyā</s> you yourself fashioned this universe and then entered into it.

children.text: paśyanti yuktā manasā manīṣiṇo guṇavyavāye 'py aguṇaṃ vipaścitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise, disciplined in mind, behold you as qualityless even amid the differentiation of the qualities.

children.text: yathāgnimedhasy amṛtaṃ ca goṣu bhuvy annamambūdyamane ca vṛttim
children.translated_text: Just as fire is in wood, nectar in cows, food on the earth, and livelihood in rising waters,

children.text: yogairmanuṣyā adhiyanti hi tvāṃ guṇeṣu buddhyā kavayo vadanti ||
children.translated_text: so by yogic disciplines human beings perceive you within the qualities; the sages declare this through understanding.

children.text: taṃ tvāṃ vayaṃ nātha samujjihānaṃ sarojanābhāticirepsitārtham
children.translated_text: Seeing you, Lord, rising up from the lotus-naveled one for the long-desired purpose,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā gatā nirvṛtamadya sarve gajā davārtā iva gāṅgamambhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: we all have today attained satisfaction, like elephants distressed by a forest fire reaching the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: sa tvaṃ vidhatsvākhilalokapālā vayaṃ yadarthāstava pādamūlam
children.translated_text: Therefore you, guardian of all worlds, ordain that purpose for which we
have come to the root of your feet, O inner and outer self; what else need be made known to the witness of everything?

children.text: ahaṃ giritraśca surādayo ye dakṣādayo 'gneriva ketavaste
children.translated_text: I, <s>Giritra</s>, and the other gods, such as <s>Dakṣa</s>, are like sparks of your fire.

children.text: kiṃ vā vidāmeśa pṛthagvibhātā vidhatsva śaṃ no dvijadevamantram ||
children.translated_text: What can we separately know, O Lord who shines forth distinctly? Grant us welfare, O mantra of the twice-born and the gods.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ viriñcādibhirīḍitastad vijñāya teṣāṃ hṛdayaṃ yathaiva
children.translated_text: Thus praised by <s>Viriñca</s> and the others, he understood their heart exactly as it was,
and spoke with a voice deep as a rain-cloud to them, who stood with joined palms and with all their faculties restrained.
The one Lord alone, the lord of the gods, in that divine undertaking,
desiring to sport, addressed them about such means as the churning of the ocean.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: hanta brahmannaho śambho he devā mama bhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Well then, O <s>Brahmā</s>, ah, O <s>Śambhu</s>, O gods, all of you

children.text: śṛṇutāvahitāḥ sarve śreyo vaḥ syādyathā surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: listen attentively to my words, so that there may be welfare for you, O gods.
Go; for the time being an alliance should be made with the <s>Dānavas</s> and <s>Daityas</s>,
who are favored by time, until prosperity comes to you yourselves.
Even enemies should be allied with when the importance of the task is real,
O gods, like the snake and the mouse when they have entered upon the path of gain.
Effort should be made without delay for the production of <s>amṛta</s>,
by drinking which a creature seized by death would become immortal.
After casting all creepers, grasses, vines, and herbs into the milk ocean,

children.text: manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā netraṃ kṛtvā tu vāsukim ||
children.translated_text: making <s>Mandara</s> the churning-stick and making <s>Vāsuki</s> the rope,
with me as your helper, O gods, churn it without weariness.
The <s>Daityas</s> will become sharers in the toil, while you will be takers of the fruit.
O gods, approve whatever the Asuras desire in that matter.

children.text: na saṃrambheṇa sidhyanti sarvārthāḥ sāntvayā yathā ||
children.translated_text: All aims are not accomplished by wrath as they are by conciliation.
You must not fear the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison arising from the ocean,

children.text: lobhaḥ kāryo na vo jātu roṣaḥ kāmastu vastuṣu ||
children.translated_text: and you must never feel greed, anger, or desire toward the objects there.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Having thus instructed the gods, the blessed <s>Puruṣottama</s>,
the Lord whose movement is free, disappeared from them, O king.
Then, bowing to that blessed Lord, the grandsire

children.text: bhavaśca jagmatuḥ svaṃ svaṃ dhāmopeyurbaliṃ surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Bhava</s> went each to his own abode, while the gods approached <s>Bali</s>.
Seeing his enemies, though unarmed, agitated and without their own leaders composed,
the praiseworthy king of the <s>Daityas</s>, who knew the proper times for alliance and war, restrained them.
They approached the son of <s>Virocana</s>, seated there, protected by chiefs of Asura troops,
endowed with supreme splendor and having conquered all directions.
Great-minded <s>Mahendra</s>, having conciliated him with smooth speech,
He related all that he had been taught by <s>Puruṣottama</s>.
That pleased the Daitya, and also the other lords of the asuras who were there,
<s>Śambara</s>, <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, and those who dwelt in <s>Tripura</s>.
Then the gods and asuras made an agreement and formed a friendship,
and they undertook a supreme effort for the sake of amṛta (immortal nectar), O <s>Parantapa</s>.
Then those arrogant ones, uprooting Mount Mandara with force,
roared and carried it to the ocean, strong as they were, with arms like iron bars.
<s>Śakra</s>, <s>Vairocana</s>, and the others, exhausted from carrying that distant heavy load,
were unable to bear it and, helpless, left it on the road.
As it fell there, that golden mountain
crushed many gods and dānavas with its great weight.
Seeing them thus, their spirits broken and their arms, thighs, and necks shattered,
the Blessed Lord, whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>, appeared there.
Looking upon the gods and dānavas crushed by the mountain's fall,
with a glance he brought the immortals back to life and made them woundless as before.
And, playfully placing the mountain on <s>Garuḍa</s> with one hand,
he mounted and went to the ocean, surrounded by hosts of gods and asuras.

children.text: avaropya giriṃ skandhāt suparṇaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Having set the mountain down from his shoulder, <s>Suparṇa</s>, best of birds,

children.text: yayau jalānta utsṛjya hariṇā sa visarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: departed after leaving it at the water's edge, dismissed by <s>Hari</s>.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
They invited <s>Vāsuki</s>, king of serpents, with a share in the reward,
and joyfully wrapped him around that mountain as the churning rope.
The gods, exerting themselves for the sake of amṛta, began to churn the ocean, O <s>Kurūdvaha</s>.
<s>Hari</s> first took hold at the front, and then the gods stood there.
The Daitya chiefs did not approve that act of the Great Person:
"We will not grasp the tail of the serpent, an inauspicious limb."
"We are endowed with recitation and sacred learning, renowned for our birth and deeds."

children.text: iti tūṣṇīṃ sthitān daityān vilokya puruṣottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the Daityas standing silent in this way, <s>Puruṣottama</s>,
smiling, let go of the front and, together with the immortals, took hold of the tail.
Thus those sons of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, with their positions assigned,
churned the ocean with utmost effort for the sake of amṛta.
While the ocean was being churned, that mountain, having no support, sank into the waters,
though it was being held by the strong ones, because of its weight, O <s>Pāṇḍunandana</s>.
They became deeply despondent, the beauty of their faces withered,
when their own manly power had been overcome by fate, which was far stronger.
Seeing the obstruction so ordained, the Lord of that all, of irresistible power and unfailing purpose,

children.text: kṛtvā vapuḥ kacchapamadbhutaṃ mahat praviśya toyaṃ girimujjahāra ||
children.translated_text: assumed an amazing, great tortoise body, entered the water, and lifted up the mountain.

children.text: tamutthitaṃ vīkṣya kulācalaṃ punaḥ samudyatā nirmathituṃ surāsurāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that chief mountain raised up again, the gods and asuras again set themselves to churn,

children.text: dadhāra pṛṣṭhena sa lakṣayojanaprastāriṇā dvīpa ivāparo mahān ||
children.translated_text: and he supported it on his back, which extended for a hundred thousand yojanas, like another great island.
Bearing the mountain as it whirled upon his back, shaken by the arm-strength of the lords of gods and asuras,
the immeasurable primal Tortoise regarded its turning as a scratching of his limbs.
Likewise, in an asuric form he entered the asuras, stirring up their strength and vigor,
and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in a divine form, energized the hosts of gods and, as a form of sleep, entered the serpent king.

children.text: upary agendraṃ girirāḍ ivānya ākramya hastena sahasrabāhuḥ
children.translated_text: Above, like another king of mountains upon the lord of mountains, the thousand-armed one pressed down on it with his hand,
and stood in the sky, praised by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the chief gods, and showered with flowers.

children.text: upary adhaścātmani gotranetrayoḥ pareṇa te prāviśatā samedhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Strengthened by him, who had entered above, below, themselves, the mountain, and the rope,
they, wild with pride, churned the ocean rapidly with the great mountain, agitating its circles of sea-creatures.
The asuras, their luster struck by the fire and smoke from the thousand hard eyes, mouths, and breaths of the serpent king,
<s>Pauloma</s>, <s>Kāleya</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Ilvala</s>, and the rest, became like sarala trees burned by a forest fire.
And the gods, their brilliance struck by the flames of his breath, with smoke-darkened garments, garlands, armor, and faces,
were rained upon by clouds under the Lord's control, while winds embraced by ocean waves blew.
When, from the ocean being churned by the leaders of gods and asuras,

children.text: yadā sudhā na jāyeta nirmamanthājitaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: no nectar arose, <s>Ajita</s> himself churned it.

children.text: meghaśyāmaḥ kanakaparidhiḥ karṇavidyotavidyun mūrdhni bhrājadvilulitakacaḥ sragdharo raktanetraḥ
children.translated_text: Dark as a cloud, with a golden girdle, lightning flashing from his earrings, loose hair shining on his head, garlanded, and red-eyed,

children.text: jaitrair dorbhir jagadabhayadair dandaśūkaṃ gṛhītvā mathnan mathnā pratigiririvāśobhatātho dhṛtādriḥ ||
children.translated_text: taking the serpent in victorious arms that grant fearlessness to the world, and himself holding the mountain, he shone as he churned, like a second mountain set against the mountain.
From the ocean being churned there first arose a very terrible poison called <s>Hālahala</s>,
from waters crowded with panicked fish, makaras, serpents, tortoises, timis, dvipas, grahas, and timiṅgilas.

children.text: tadugravegaṃ diśi diśy upary adho visarpadutsarpadasahyamaprati
children.translated_text: Its fierce, unbearable, irresistible force spread and surged in every direction, above and below,

children.text: bhītāḥ prajā dudruvuraṅga seśvarā arakṣyamāṇāḥ śaraṇaṃ sadāśivam ||
children.translated_text: and the frightened beings, O dear one, together with their lords, fled unprotected for refuge to <s>Sadāśiva</s>.

children.text: vilokya taṃ devavaraṃ trilokyā bhavāya devyābhimataṃ munīnām
children.translated_text: Seeing that best of gods, desired by the goddess, the benefactor of the three worlds and of the sages,
seated on the mountain and practicing austerity for the sake of liberation, they bowed to him with hymns.
The <s>Prajāpatis</s> said:
O God of gods, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, soul of beings, source of beings,
protect us, who have taken refuge, from the poison that burns the three worlds.
You alone are the Lord of the whole universe, of bondage and liberation,
and the wise worship you as the teacher who removes the distress of those who surrender.
O mighty one, when, by your own power made of the guṇas (qualities), you take up this world's creation, preservation, and dissolution,
then, seeing through yourself, you bear the names <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>.
You are the supreme hidden <s>brahman</s>, causing the states of being and non-being to arise.
Appearing through many powers, you are the self, O lord of the universe.

children.text: tvaṃ śabdayonir jagadādir ātmā prāṇendriyadravyaguṇaḥ svabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the source of sound, the beginning of the world, the self, breath, senses, substances, qualities, and inherent nature.

children.text: kālaḥ kratuḥ satyamṛtaṃ ca dharmas tvayy akṣaraṃ yat trivṛdāmananti ||
children.translated_text: You are time, the sacrificial rite, truth, <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), and <s>dharma</s>; they call the imperishable in you the threefold syllable.
Fire is your mouth, since you are the self of all the gods; they know the earth to be your lotus feet, from which the worlds arise.

children.text: kālaṃ gatiṃ te 'khiladevatātmano diśaśca karṇau rasanaṃ jaleśam ||
children.translated_text: They know time as your movement, O self of all the gods, the directions as your ears, and the lord of waters as your tongue.

children.text: nābhirnabhaste śvasanaṃ nabhasvān sūryaśca cakṣūṃṣi jalaṃ sma retaḥ
children.translated_text: The sky is your navel, the wind your breath, the sun your eyes, and water indeed your seed.

children.text: parāvarātmāśrayaṇaṃ tavātmā somo mano dyaurbhagavan śiraste ||
children.translated_text: Your own self is the refuge of higher and lower beings; the moon is your mind and heaven is your head, O blessed lord.
The oceans are your belly, the mountains your mass of bones, and all herbs and plants your hairs.

children.text: chandāṃsi sākṣāt tava sapta dhātavas trayīmayātman hṛdayaṃ sarvadharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The metres themselves are your seven bodily elements; O you whose self consists of the three Vedas, all <s>dharma</s> is your heart.
The five <s>Upaniṣads</s> are your faces, O lord, by which there is the class of thirty-eight mantras.

children.text: yat tac chivākhyaṃ paramātmatattvaṃ deva svayaṃjyotiravasthitiste ||
children.translated_text: That supreme principle of the self called <s>Śiva</s>, O god, is your self-luminous state.
Your shadow is <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), from whose waves creation proceeds; your three eyes are <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: sāṃkhyātmanaḥ śāstrakṛtastavekṣā chandomayo deva ṛṣiḥ purāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your vision, as the scripture-maker whose nature is <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, is the ancient seer made of sacred metre, O god.
O <s>Giritra</s>, protector of all the worlds, your supreme light is not accessible to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, or the lord of the gods.

children.text: jyotiḥ paraṃ yatra rajastamaśca sattvaṃ na yadbrahma nirastabhedam ||
children.translated_text: There neither <s>rajas</s> nor <s>tamas</s>, nor even <s>sattva</s>, exists; it is <s>brahman</s>, free from all division.
That is not enough for the praise of you who destroy the many enemies of beings, such as desire, the sacrifice, <s>Tripura</s>, time, and poison.

children.text: yastvantakāla idamātmakṛtaṃ svanetravahnisphuliṅgaśikhayā bhasitaṃ na veda ||
children.translated_text: At the time of the end, one does not know this world, made by yourself, as it is reduced to ashes by flames from the sparks of fire of your own eyes.
Yet some boast about you, whose pair of feet is contemplated in the heart by teachers delighting in the self, and who moves with <s>Umā</s>, scorched by austerity.

children.text: katthanta ugraparuṣaṃ nirataṃ śmaśāne te nūnamūtimavidaṃstava hātalajjāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They call you fierce, harsh, and fixed in the cremation ground; surely they are shameless and do not know your majesty.

children.text: tat tasya te sadasatoḥ parataḥ parasya nāñjaḥ svarūpagamane prabhavanti bhūmnaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Brahmā</s> and the others cannot easily attain the true form of you, the infinite one, who are beyond being and non-being.

children.text: brahmādayaḥ kimuta saṃstavane vayaṃ tu tatsargasargaviṣayā api śaktimātram ||
children.translated_text: How much less can we praise you, whose sphere is only your creation and what is created from it, and who are but a mere portion of your power?

children.text: etat paraṃ prapaśyāmo na paraṃ te maheśvara
children.translated_text: We perceive this as your supreme form, O <s>Maheśvara</s>, not what lies beyond you.
For your manifestation, whose acts are unmanifest, exists for the gracious protection of the world.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Seeing their calamity, and deeply afflicted with compassion,
the god, friend of all beings, said this to his beloved <s>Satī</s>.
<s>Śrī Śiva</s> said:

children.text: aho bata bhavāny etat prajānāṃ paśya vaiśasam
children.translated_text: Ah, <s>Bhavānī</s>, see this distress of the creatures,
which has arisen from the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison produced by the churning of the milk ocean.
For these beings who long to preserve their lives, fearlessness must indeed be granted by me.
This much is the purpose of a lord: the protection of the afflicted.

children.text: prāṇaiḥ svaiḥ prāṇinaḥ pānti sādhavaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅguraiḥ
children.translated_text: Good people protect living beings with their own lives, though those lives last only a moment,
among beings bound in enmity and bewildered by their own <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: puṃsaḥ kṛpayato bhadre sarvātmā prīyate hariḥ
children.translated_text: When a man shows compassion, O fair one, <s>Hari</s>, the self of all, is pleased.
When blessed <s>Hari</s> is pleased, I too am pleased, along with all that moves and does not move.

children.text: tasmādidaṃ garaṃ bhuñje prajānāṃ svastirastu me ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall consume this poison; may there be welfare for the creatures through me.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Having thus addressed <s>Bhavānī</s>, the blessed lord, creator of the universe,
began to eat that poison, and she, knowing his power, approved.
Then, taking into his palm the all-pervading hālāhala poison,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, the nurturer of beings, swallowed it out of compassion.
Even that impurity of the waters displayed its own power:

children.text: yac cakāra gale nīlaṃ tacca sādhor vibhūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: it made his throat blue, and that became an ornament of the holy one.
Holy people are usually tormented by the suffering of the world.
That indeed is the highest worship of the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the self of all.
Hearing that deed of <s>Śambhu</s>, the god of gods and the bountiful one,
the creatures, <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> praised him.

children.text: praskannaṃ pibataḥ pāṇeryat kiṃcij jagṛhuḥ sma tat
children.translated_text: Whatever small amount spilled from his hand as he drank, they took up:
scorpions, snakes, poisonous herbs, biting serpents, and others of that kind.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
When the poison had been drunk by the bull-marked <s>Śiva</s>, those gods and demons were pleased.
They churned the ocean vigorously, and then <s>Havirdhānī</s> appeared.
The sages who spoke of <s>brahman</s> accepted her as an <s>agnihotrī</s> cow,
for the pure oblation of the sacrifice that leads to the gods, O king.
Then a horse named <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>, pale as the moon, came into being.

children.text: tasmin baliḥ spṛhāṃ cakre nendra īśvaraśikṣayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bali</s> desired him, while <s>Indra</s> did not, because of the Lord's instruction.
Then the lordly elephant named <s>Airāvata</s> emerged,
stealing the majesty of a white mountain with his four tusks.
Then the eight elephants of the quarters, beginning with <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, came into being,
and eight female elephants too, beginning with <s>Abhramu</s>, came into being, O king.
A jewel called <s>Kaustubha</s>, a great padmarāga, arose from the great ocean.

children.text: tasmin maṇau spṛhāṃ cakre vakṣo'laṃkaraṇe hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> desired that jewel as an ornament for his chest.
Then the <s>Pārijāta</s> appeared, the adornment of the world of the gods.

children.text: pūrayaty arthino yo 'rthaiḥ śaśvadbhuvi yathā bhavān ||
children.translated_text: It always fulfils supplicants with desired objects on earth, just as you do.
Then the apsarases were born, wearing golden necklaces and fine garments,
charming to the heavenly beings with their lovely gait, play, and glances.
Then <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Ramā</s> herself, devoted to the blessed Lord, manifested,

children.text: rañjayantī diśaḥ kāntyā vidyut saudāmanī yathā ||
children.translated_text: delighting the directions with her radiance like a flash of lightning.
All beings, including gods, asuras, and humans, felt longing for her,
their minds captivated by the majesty of her beauty, generosity, youth, and complexion.
For her <s>Indra</s> brought a great and marvelous seat,
and the best rivers, embodied in person, brought pure water in golden pitchers.
The earth, fit for the consecration, brought all herbs,
the cows brought the five pure products, and spring brought the months Madhu and Mādhava.
The seers performed the consecration according to rule,
the gandharvas sang auspicious songs, and the dancers danced and sang.
The clouds made resound mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas, murajas, ānakas, and gomukhas,
along with conches, flutes, and vīṇās, producing a tumultuous sound.
Then the elephants of the quarters consecrated the goddess <s>Śrī</s>, the chaste lotus-handed one,
with full pitchers, while sacred formulae were uttered by the twice-born.
The ocean offered two yellow silk garments,
and <s>Varuṇa</s> offered the <s>Vaijayantī</s> garland, whose bees were intoxicated with honey.
<s>Viśvakarmā</s>, lord of creatures, offered many varied ornaments,
<s>Sarasvatī</s> a necklace, <s>Aja</s> a lotus, and the nāgas earrings.
Then, taking in her hand a garland of lotuses, prepared with auspicious rites and humming with bees,

children.text: cacāla vaktraṃ sukapolakuṇḍalaṃ savrīḍahāsaṃ dadhatī suśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: she moved about, bearing a beautiful face with fine cheeks and earrings, brightened by a bashful smile.
Her pair of breasts, together with her very slender waist, was unbrokenly sprinkled with sandal and saffron,

children.text: tatastato nūpuravalguśiñjitair visarpatī hemalateva sā babhau ||
children.translated_text: and as she moved here and there with the sweet tinkling of anklets, she shone like a golden creeper.
Looking for an unblemished, fixed, and unfailing seat for herself, endowed with good qualities,
she did not find it among gandharvas, siddhas, asuras, yakṣas, cāraṇas, the dwellers in heaven, and the rest.

children.text: nūnaṃ tapo yasya na manyunirjayo jñānaṃ kvacit tac ca na saṅgavarjitam
children.translated_text: "Surely one has austerity, but not conquest of anger; another has knowledge, but that too is not free from attachment.

children.text: kaścin mahāṃstasya na kāmanirjayaḥ sa īśvaraḥ kiṃ parato vyapāśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Someone may be great, but he has not conquered desire; if one is lordly, what dependence does he have on another?

children.text: dharmaḥ kvacit tatra na bhūtasauhṛdaṃ tyāgaḥ kvacit tatra na muktikāraṇam
children.translated_text: Somewhere there is <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), but there is no kindness toward beings; somewhere there is renunciation, but it is not a cause of liberation.

children.text: vīryaṃ na puṃso 'sty ajaveganiṣkṛtaṃ na hi dvitīyo guṇasaṅgavarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man's vigor is not free from the force of birth, and there is no second one free from contact with the guṇas.

children.text: kvacic cirāyurna hi śīlamaṅgalaṃ kvacit tadapy asti na vedyamāyuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Somewhere there is long life, but no auspicious character; elsewhere even that exists, but the span of life is not knowable.

children.text: yatrobhayaṃ kutra ca so 'py amaṅgalaḥ sumaṅgalaḥ kaśca na kāṅkṣate hi mām ||
children.translated_text: Where both are present, somewhere that person too is inauspicious; and what truly auspicious one does not desire me?"
Thus reflecting, <s>Ramā</s> chose as her bridegroom the one whose good qualities do not fail,

children.text: vavre varaṃ sarvaguṇairapekṣitaṃ ramā mukundaṃ nirapekṣamīpsitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mukunda</s>, desired by all virtues, without dependence, wished for as her own sole refuge and the abode beyond the guṇas.
In that assembly she placed upon him a fresh lotus garland, splendid and proclaimed by the humming of swarms of intoxicated bees,

children.text: tasthau nidhāya nikaṭe taduraḥ svadhāma savrīḍahāsavikasannayanena yātā ||
children.translated_text: and then, with eyes blooming in a bashful smile, she went and stood nearby, at his chest, her own abode.

children.text: tasyāḥ śriyastrijagato janako jananyā vakṣo nivāsamakarot paramaṃ vibhūteḥ
children.translated_text: The father of the three worlds made the breast that was the dwelling of their mother, <s>Śrī</s>, the supreme seat of splendor.

children.text: śrīḥ svāḥ prajāḥ sakaruṇena nirīkṣaṇena yatra sthitaidhayata sādhipatīṃstrilokān ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Śrī</s>, established with a compassionate glance, caused his offspring, together with their lords, to flourish throughout the three worlds.
There arose a broad sound from conches, trumpets, mṛdaṅgas,
and other instruments, while the attendants of the gods, together with their women, danced and sang.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and the other chief creators of the universe praised the Lord,
with unfailing mantras appropriate to him, while they showered flowers.
The gods, the Prajāpatis, and their peoples, looked upon by <s>Śrī</s>,
became endowed with virtues beginning with good conduct and attained supreme contentment.
But when they were disregarded by <s>Lakṣmī</s>, O king, the daityas and dānavas
became devoid of strength, greedy, inactive, and shameless.
Then the goddess <s>Vāruṇī</s>, a lotus-eyed maiden, appeared,
and the asuras took her, with <s>Hari</s>'s permission.
Then, from the ocean being churned by the descendants of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, who desired amṛta,
there arose, O great king, a supremely marvelous man.
His arms were long, stout shafts; his neck was conch-like; his eyes were ruddy.
He was dark, young, garlanded, and adorned with every ornament.
He wore yellow garments, had a broad chest, and had well-polished jeweled earrings.
He was handsome with the ends of his glossy curling hair, and had the stride of a lion.
He bore a pitcher filled with <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality), and was adorned with bracelets.
He was indeed born directly from a portion of a portion of the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
He is renowned as <s>Dhanvantari</s>, the revealer of <s>Āyurveda</s>, and a receiver of sacrificial shares.
Seeing him, all the asuras saw also the pitcher filled with amṛta.
Desiring all its contents, they quickly seized the pitcher,
and when that pitcher, the vessel containing amṛta, was being carried away by the asuras,
the gods, dejected in mind, went to <s>Hari</s> for refuge.
Seeing that misery of theirs, the Blessed Lord, who fulfills the wishes of his servants, said,

children.text: mā khidyata mitho 'rthaṃ vaḥ sādhayiṣye svamāyayā ||
children.translated_text: "Do not be distressed; by my own māyā I shall accomplish your purpose among them."
Then, with their minds thirsting for it, a quarrel arose among them over that object:

children.text: ahaṃ pūrvamahaṃ pūrvaṃ na tvaṃ na tvamiti prabho ||
children.translated_text: "I first, I first! Not you, not you!" so they cried, O lord.
"The gods deserve their own share, since they are equally the cause of the effort.
As in a sattra-sacrifice, this is the eternal <s>dharma</s> (rule) in this matter."

children.text: iti svān pratyaṣedhan vai daiteyā jātamatsarāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the envious sons of <s>Diti</s> repeatedly forbade their own weaker companions,
O king, while the stronger ones held the pitcher.
At that moment <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord who knows every expedient,
assumed an indescribable female form, supremely marvelous.
It was lovely to behold, dark like a blue lotus, beautiful in every limb,
with matching ear ornaments, fine cheeks, and an elevated nose and face.
with her belly slender from the weight of breasts fully formed in fresh youth,
her eyes restless at the humming of bees drawn by the fragrance of her face;
bearing, in her mass of beautiful hair, a garland of fully blossomed jasmine,
adorned with a lovely necklace on her neck and armlets upon her graceful arms;
with the beauty of island-like hips wrapped in spotless garments,
with a girdle shining brightly and anklets charmingly moving on her feet;
with glances marked by bashful smiles and playful movements of her brows,
again and again arousing desire in the hearts of the leaders of the <s>Daityas</s>.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Those Asuras, stealing the vessel from one another and abandoning friendship,
throwing it about in the manner of robbers, saw a woman approaching.

children.text: aho rūpamaho dhāma aho asyā navaṃ vayaḥ
children.translated_text: "Ah, what beauty! Ah, what radiance! Ah, what fresh youth she has!"
So saying, they ran up to her and questioned her, their hearts filled with passion.

children.text: kā tvaṃ kañjapalāśākṣi kuto vā kiṃ cikīrṣasi
children.translated_text: "Who are you, lotus-petal-eyed one? From where have you come, and what do you wish to do?

children.text: kasyāsi vada vāmoru mathnatīva manāṃsi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whose are you? Tell us, fair-thighed one, for you are churning our minds.
We do not know that you have ever before been touched by the immortals, the <s>Daityas</s>, the <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, or <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
nor by the lords of the world, much less by human beings.

children.text: nūnaṃ tvaṃ vidhinā subhrūḥ preṣitāsi śarīriṇām
children.translated_text: Surely, fair-browed one, you have been sent by compassionate <s>Vidhi</s>
to bring delight to the minds and all the senses of embodied beings.
Therefore, proud lady, since we are rivals over a single object,
kinsmen bound in enmity, bring welfare to us, slender-waisted one.
We are descendants of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, brothers who have shown our valor.

children.text: vibhajasva yathānyāyaṃ naiva bhedo yathā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Divide it according to justice, so that no division among us may arise."
Thus invited by the <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Hari</s>, wearing the form of an illusory woman,
laughed, and, looking at them with charming sidelong glances, said this.
The Blessed Lord said:
"How can you descendants of <s>Kaśyapa</s> put trust in me, a wanton woman, when you have met me?

children.text: viśvāsaṃ paṇḍito jātu kāminīṣu na yāti hi ||
children.translated_text: For a wise man never places trust in passionate women.
They say that the friendships of jackals and of independent women, O enemies of the gods,
are impermanent, for they are always seeking something new and new."
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Thus the Asuras, their minds reassured by her playful words,
laughed deeply with feeling and gave her the vessel of nectar.

children.text: tato gṛhītvāmṛtabhājanaṃ harir babhāṣa īṣatsmitaśobhayā girā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s>, taking the vessel of nectar, spoke with words made beautiful by a slight smile:

children.text: yady abhyupetaṃ kva ca sādhvasādhu vā kṛtaṃ mayā vo vibhaje sudhāmimām ||
children.translated_text: "If what I do, whether proper or improper in some way, is accepted by you, I shall distribute this nectar among you."
Hearing what she had said, the foremost Asuras,
not knowing her true measure, agreed: "So be it, just as you say."
Then, having fasted, bathed, and offered oblations with clarified butter into the fire,
and having given gifts to cows, brahmins, and other beings, they had auspicious rites performed by the twice-born.
Putting on, according to their liking, fresh garments that had not been worn before,
they all entered upon seats of kuśa grass with their tips facing east, adorned with ornaments.
When the gods and the sons of <s>Diti</s> had sat down facing east,
in a hall fragrant with incense and furnished with garlands and lamps,
there, O lord of men, with thighs like an elephant's trunk, wearing shining silk, moving with the gait of an intoxicated elephant along the slope of her hips, her eyes bewildered with passion,
she then entered, jingling with the sound of golden anklets, full-breasted and carrying the pitcher in her hand.
Seeing her, the companion of <s>Śrī</s>, with ears beautiful with golden earrings, with lovely nose, cheeks, and face, famed as the supreme goddess,
the gods and Asuras became utterly bewildered by her smiling glance, as the end of the cloth over her breasts had slipped down.
Considering the giving of nectar to the Asuras to be bad policy, like giving milk to snakes,
<s>Acyuta</s> did not distribute it to those naturally cruel beings.
The lord of the world arranged separate rows for both groups
and seated them in their own respective rows.
Holding the pitcher, he went about deceiving the <s>Daityas</s>,
and made the gods, seated at a distance, drink the nectar that removes old age and death.
The Asuras, O king, keeping the agreement they themselves had made,
sat silent, bound by affection and shrinking from a quarrel with a woman.
Because they had formed excessive attachment to her and feared the loss of her affection,
and because they were bound by great respect, they said nothing unpleasant.
<s>Svarbhānu</s>, disguised in the appearance of a god, entered the assembly of the gods
and drank the soma; he was pointed out by <s>Candra</s> and <s>Arka</s>.
With his discus, sharp as a razor's edge,
<s>Hari</s> cut off his head as he was drinking, but his headless trunk, drenched by the nectar, fell down.
His head, however, having been brought to immortality, unborn <s>Brahmā</s> made into a planet;
that hostile-minded one attacks <s>Candra</s> and <s>Arka</s> at the lunar nodes.
When the nectar had mostly been drunk by the gods, the blessed <s>Hari</s>, creator of the worlds,
assumed his own form while the lords of the Asuras looked on.

children.text: evaṃ surāsuragaṇāḥ samadeśakāla hetvarthakarmamatayo 'pi phale vikalpāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the hosts of gods and Asuras were alike in place, time, cause, purpose, action, and intention, yet their results differed.

children.text: tatrāmṛtaṃ suragaṇāḥ phalamañjasāpur yatpādapaṅkajarajaḥśrayaṇān na daityāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the hosts of gods quickly obtained the fruit, the nectar, because they had taken shelter in the dust of his lotus feet, while the <s>Daityas</s> did not.
Whatever is applied by human beings with life-breath, wealth, action, mind, and speech to the body, the self, and the like is unreal because of separateness;

children.text: tair eva sadbhavati yat kriyate 'pṛthaktvāt sarvasya tadbhavati mūlaniṣecanaṃ yat ||
children.translated_text: but by those very means, whatever is done for the real becomes real because it is not separate from him, just as watering the root benefits the whole.
<s>Śrī Rājā</s> said:
You have described the extensive lineages of <s>Soma</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>,
and the supremely wondrous deeds of the kings belonging to both lineages.
And especially, O best of sages, tell us of the mighty deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
who descended with a portion of himself there in the line of righteous <s>Yadu</s>.
Having descended in the lineage of <s>Yadu</s>, the Blessed Lord, creator of beings,

children.text: kṛtavānyāni viśvātmā tāni no vada vistarāt ||
children.translated_text: Tell us at length of those deeds which the soul of the universe performed.
From what is sung by those whose thirst has ceased, from the medicine for worldly existence, delightful to ear and mind,
what man would turn away from the recounting of <s>Uttamaśloka</s>'s qualities, except a killer of animals?
In battle my grandfathers, with great warriors such as <s>Devavrata</s>, conquerors of the immortals and like timingila sea-monsters,
crossed the hard-to-cross ocean of the <s>Kaurava</s> army, making it like a calf's hoofprint, because he was their boat.
This body of mine, the seed of the lineage of the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, was scorched by the weapon of <s>Drauṇi</s>;

children.text: jugopa kukṣiṃ gata āttacakro mātuśca me yaḥ śaraṇaṃ gatāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: he protected it, having entered my mother's womb with discus in hand, and protected my mother too, who had gone to him for refuge.
Tell, O learned one, the heroic deeds of him who, as the <s>puruṣa</s> (cosmic person) and as Time, within and without all embodied beings,

children.text: prayacchato mṛtyumutāmṛtaṃ ca māyāmanuṣyasya vadasva vidvan ||
children.translated_text: grants death and also immortality, though he appears as a human being through <s>māyā</s> (divine illusion).
You have said that <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, was the son of <s>Rohiṇī</s>;
how could there have been a connection with <s>Devakī</s>'s womb without his taking another body?
Why did the Blessed <s>Mukunda</s> go from his father's house to <s>Vraja</s>?

children.text: kva vāsaṃ jñātibhiḥ sārdhaṃ kṛtavānsātvatāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And where did the lord of the <s>Sātvatas</s> live together with his kinsmen?
What did <s>Keśava</s> do while living in <s>Vraja</s>, and what did he do in <s>Madhupurī</s>?
And why did he kill his mother's brother <s>Kaṃsa</s>, who was utterly unworthy of honor?
Having assumed a human body, for how many years did he dwell with the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>
in the city of the <s>Yadus</s>, and how many wives did the Lord have?
All this, and everything else concerning <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s activities, O sage,
you should tell in detail to me, who have faith, O all-knowing one.
This exceedingly unbearable hunger does not trouble me, though I have given up water,
while I drink the nectar of <s>Hari</s>'s stories flowing from the lotus of your mouth.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ niśamya bhṛgunandana sādhuvādaṃ vaiyāsakiḥ sa bhagavānatha viṣṇurātam
children.translated_text: O descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, when the blessed son of <s>Vyāsa</s> heard this excellent speech of <s>Viṣṇurāta</s>,
he honored him in return and, foremost among devotees of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>, began to recount <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s deeds, which destroy the stain of the Kali age.
<s>Śrīśuka</s> said:
Your understanding is rightly resolved, O best of royal sages,

children.text: vāsudevakathāyāṃ te yaj jātā naiṣṭhikī ratiḥ ||
children.translated_text: since steadfast love for the story of <s>Vāsudeva</s> has arisen in you.
A question about the story of <s>Vāsudeva</s> purifies three persons:
the speaker, the questioner, and the hearers, just as the water from his feet does.
The Earth, oppressed by a great burden of hundreds of thousands of armies of arrogant kings who were hosts of daityas in disguise,
went to <s>Brahmā</s> for refuge.
Having become a cow, tear-faced, distressed, and crying piteously,
she came near the Lord and told him of her distress.
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, having understood that, together with the gods and with her,
went with the three-eyed <s>Śiva</s> to the shore of the Ocean of Milk.
Having gone there, with concentrated mind he worshiped the Lord of the universe, the God of gods, <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>,
the <s>Puruṣa</s> (cosmic person), by means of the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>.

children.text: giraṃ samādhau gagane samīritāṃ niśamya vedhāstridaśānuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Hearing, in samādhi, a voice uttered in the sky, the creator spoke to the gods:

children.text: gāṃ pauruṣīṃ me śṛṇutāmarāḥ punarvidhīyatāmāśu tathaiva mā ciram ||
children.translated_text: "Hear from me again the divine command, O immortals; let it be carried out quickly, just so, without delay.
The fever of the Earth has already been perceived by the <s>Puruṣa</s>; be born among the <s>Yadus</s> with your portions,
while the Lord of lords moves upon the earth, reducing its burden by the power of his own time.
The Blessed Lord, the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, will be born directly in the house of <s>Vasudeva</s>;
for the sake of his pleasure, let the women of the gods also take birth.
<s>Ananta</s>, a portion of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, thousand-faced and self-ruling,
will appear before the Lord, desiring to do what is dear to <s>Hari</s>.
The blessed <s>māyā</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by whom the world is bewildered,
being commanded by the Lord, will be born by a portion for the sake of the task."
<s>Śrīśuka</s> said:
Having thus instructed the hosts of the immortals, the powerful lord of the Prajāpatis

children.text: āśvāsya ca mahīṃ gīrbhiḥ svadhāma paramaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: reassured the Earth with words and went to his own supreme abode.
<s>Śūrasena</s>, lord of the <s>Yadus</s>, dwelling in the city of <s>Mathurā</s>,
formerly ruled the districts of the <s>Māthuras</s> and the <s>Śūrasenas</s>.
For that reason <s>Mathurā</s> became the capital of all the <s>Yādava</s> kings,
for there the Blessed <s>Hari</s> is always present.
In that city, at a certain time, <s>Śauri</s>, <s>Vasudeva</s>, newly married,
mounted a chariot for the journey together with the noble <s>Devakī</s>.
<s>Kaṃsa</s>, son of <s>Ugrasena</s>, wishing to please his sister,
took the reins of the horses, surrounded by hundreds of golden chariots.
As a wedding gift there were four hundred elephants adorned with golden garlands,
ten thousand horses, and eighteen hundred chariots.
There were also two hundred well-adorned, delicate maidservants;
<s>Devaka</s>, loving his daughter, gave them to his daughter at her departure.
Conches, trumpets, mṛdaṅgas, and kettledrums
sounded together at the start of the journey, auspiciously for the bride and bridegroom, dear one.
On the road, a bodiless voice addressed <s>Kaṃsa</s>, who held the reins:
"Fool, the eighth embryo of this woman whom you are carrying will kill you."

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa khalaḥ pāpo bhojānāṃ kulapāṃsanaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that wicked sinner, the disgrace of the <s>Bhojas</s>,
sword in hand, seized his sister by the hair and began to kill her.
To him, whose act was loathsome, cruel, and shameless,
the greatly fortunate <s>Vasudeva</s> spoke, calming him.
<s>Śrīvasudeva</s> said:
You are one whose virtues are praised by heroes, a bringer of fame to the <s>Bhojas</s>;
how could you kill your sister, a woman, on the occasion of her marriage?
O hero, for beings who have taken birth, death is born together with the body.

children.text: adya vābdaśatānte vā mṛtyurvai prāṇināṃ dhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether today or at the end of a hundred years, death is certain for living beings.
When the body has gone back to the five elements, the embodied self, following its karma and powerless,
obtains another body and abandons the former frame.
Just as a person walking and standing on one foot goes forward with the other,
so the embodied self, like a grass-leech, moves on along the course of karma.
Just as in a dream one sees such a body, with consciousness absorbed in mental imagining,
pondering with the mind what has been seen and heard, one enters that state, which is indeed a kind of forgetfulness.

children.text: yato yato dhāvati daivacoditaṃ mano vikārātmakamāpa pañcasu
children.translated_text: Wherever the mind, driven by fate and made of transformations, runs among the five

children.text: guṇeṣu māyārociteṣu dehyasau prapadyamānaḥ saha tena jāyate ||
children.translated_text: qualities fashioned by <s>Māyā</s>, this embodied being, identifying with that, is born together with it.
Just as light in water or on earth is perceived as following the force of the wind,

children.text: evaṃ svamāyāraciteṣvasau pumān guṇeṣu rāgānugato vimuhyati ||
children.translated_text: so this person, among the qualities fashioned by his own <s>māyā</s>, becomes deluded through attachment.
Therefore a person of such understanding should not practice hostility toward anyone,
seeking his own welfare; for fear from another surely comes to the one who acts with hostility.
This young woman is your younger sister, pitiable and like a daughter.
You, compassionate toward the wretched, ought not to kill this auspicious woman.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Though he was being instructed in this way by conciliatory words and distinctions, that cruel man
did not turn back, O <s>Kauravya</s>, being devoted to the conduct of man-eaters.
Knowing that firm resolve of his, and considering it, <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>
then reached this conclusion, since the time had come to ward him off.
Death should be averted by an intelligent man as far as the rise of his intelligence and strength permits.
If this man should not turn back, there is no fault in the embodied person.
By handing over my sons to Death, I shall free this pitiable woman,

children.text: sutā me yadi jāyeranmṛtyurvā na mriyeta cet ||
children.translated_text: if sons are born to me, and if Death himself does not die.
Or might not the opposite occur? The course of the Creator is hard to overcome.
One who has arrived may turn back, and one who has turned back may come again.
Just as, in the separation and conjunction of fire and wood, there is no cause other than the unseen,
so too for a living being the cause of union with and separation from the body is hard to discern.
Having reflected in this way about that sinner while he remained before his eyes,
<s>Śauri</s> honored him with great respect.
With his lotus-face cheerful, before the cruel and shameless man,
and with his mind in pain, he smiled and said this:
<s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> said:

children.text: na hyasyāste bhayaṃ saumya yadvai sāhāśarīravāk
children.translated_text: Gentle one, there is no fear for you from her, since that bodiless voice spoke so.
I shall hand over her sons, from whom your fear has arisen.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
<s>Kaṃsa</s>, understanding the essence of that speech, desisted from killing his sister.
<s>Vasudeva</s> too, pleased, praised him and entered his house.
Then, when time had come, <s>Devakī</s>, endowed with all divinities,
gave birth to eight sons and also to a daughter, year after year.
<s>Ānakadundubhi</s>, with difficulty, handed over his firstborn <s>Kīrtimān</s> to <s>Kaṃsa</s>;
he was exceedingly distraught at the thought of falsehood.

children.text: kiṃ duḥsahaṃ nu sādhūnāṃ viduṣāṃ kimapekṣitam
children.translated_text: What is unbearable for good men? What is there to be expected by the wise?
What is not to be done by the mean? What is hard to give up for the self-controlled?

children.text: dṛṣṭvā samatvaṃ tacchaureḥ satye caiva vyavasthitim
children.translated_text: Seeing that impartiality of <s>Śauri</s> and his firmness in truth,
<s>Kaṃsa</s>, pleased in mind, O king, laughed and said this:

children.text: pratiyātu kumāro 'yaṃ na hyasmādasti me bhayam
children.translated_text: Let this boy go back; for from him there is no fear for me.
It is said that my death has been appointed from the eighth embryo of you two.
Saying, "So be it," <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> took his son and went away.
He did not rejoice in that statement of the false, self-uncontrolled man.

children.text: nandādyā ye vraje gopā yāścāmīṣāṃ ca yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: The cowherds in <s>Vraja</s>, beginning with <s>Nanda</s>, and these wives of theirs,
the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> beginning with <s>Vasudeva</s>, and the women of <s>Yadu</s> beginning with <s>Devakī</s>,
all were indeed almost gods on both sides, O <s>Bhārata</s>,
as were the relatives, kinsmen, friends, and those who followed <s>Kaṃsa</s>.
The blessed <s>Nārada</s> came to <s>Kaṃsa</s> and told him this:
the undertaking to kill the <s>Daityas</s> who had become a burden on the earth.
After the sage departed, <s>Kaṃsa</s>, thinking that the <s>Yadus</s> were gods,

children.text: devakyā garbhasambhūtaṃ viṣṇuṃ ca svavadhaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: and that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, born from <s>Devakī</s>'s womb, was his own death,
confined <s>Devakī</s> and <s>Vasudeva</s> with fetters in the house,
and killed each son born to them, fearing the unborn one.
Mothers, fathers, brothers, and all friends as well

children.text: ghnanti hyasutṛpo lubdhā rājānaḥ prāyaśo bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: kings on earth, greedy and intent on their own lives, often kill.
Knowing himself here to have been born as the great Asura <s>Kālanemi</s>, formerly slain by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
he became hostile toward the <s>Yadus</s>.
His father <s>Ugrasena</s>, lord of the <s>Yadus</s>, <s>Bhojas</s>, and <s>Andhakas</s>,
the mighty man himself imprisoned, and then ruled the <s>Śūrasenas</s>.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Together with <s>Pralamba</s>, <s>Baka</s>, <s>Cāṇūra</s>, <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>, and <s>Mahāśana</s>,
with <s>Muṣṭika</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Keśī</s>, and <s>Dhenuka</s>,
and with other Asura kings, beginning with <s>Bāṇa</s> and <s>Bhauma</s>,
the powerful one, relying on the king of <s>Magadha</s>, brought ruin upon the <s>Yadus</s>.
Oppressed, they settled among the <s>Kurus</s>, <s>Pañcālas</s>, and <s>Kekayas</s>,
and also among the <s>Śālvas</s>, <s>Vidarbhas</s>, <s>Niṣadhas</s>, <s>Videhas</s>, and <s>Kośalas</s>.
Some relatives, following him, attended upon him.
When the six infants of <s>Devakī</s> had been killed by the son of <s>Ugrasena</s>,
the seventh embryo, whom they call <s>Ananta</s>, the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
came to be in <s>Devakī</s>, increasing both joy and sorrow.
The Blessed Lord too, the Self of the universe, knowing the fear produced by <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
he commanded <s>Yogamāyā</s> on behalf of the <s>Yadus</s>, whose own lord he was.
"Go, O goddess, auspicious one, to <s>Vraja</s>, adorned with cowherds and cows.
<s>Rohiṇī</s>, the wife of <s>Vasudeva</s>, lives in <s>Nanda</s>'s cowherd settlement,
and other wives, too, terrified by <s>Kaṃsa</s>, are living in hidden places.

children.text: devakyā jaṭhare garbhaṃ śeṣākhyaṃ dhāma māmakam
children.translated_text: In <s>Devakī</s>'s womb is an embryo called <s>Śeṣa</s>, my own luminous power;
draw that away and place it in <s>Rohiṇī</s>'s womb.
Then, O blessed one, I shall become <s>Devakī</s>'s son by a portion of myself,
and you will be born from <s>Yaśodā</s>, the wife of <s>Nanda</s>.
Human beings will worship you as the mistress who grants every desired boon,
with incense, offerings, and oblations, as the giver of every desired boon.

children.text: nāmadheyāni kurvanti sthānāni ca narā bhuvi
children.translated_text: People on earth will establish names and sacred places for you:
<s>Durgā</s>, <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>,
