children.text: kumudā caṇḍikā kṛṣṇā mādhavī kanyaketi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kumudā</s>, <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Mādhavī</s>, and <s>Kanyakā</s>,
<s>Māyā</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>, <s>Īśānī</s>, <s>Śāradā</s>, and <s>Ambikā</s>.
Because of being drawn from the womb, people on earth will call him <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>;
because he delights the world, <s>Rāma</s>; because of his eminent strength, <s>Balabhadra</s>."
Thus instructed by the Blessed Lord, she accepted his command, saying, "So be it. Oṃ."
After circumambulating him, she went to the earth and carried that out just so.
When the embryo had been transferred from <s>Devakī</s> to <s>Rohiṇī</s> by <s>Yoganidrā</s>,

children.text: aho visraṃsito garbha iti paurā vicukruśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the townspeople cried out, "Alas, the embryo has miscarried!"
The Blessed Lord too, the Self of the universe and remover of fear for his devotees,
entered, by a portion of himself, the mind of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>.

children.text: sa bibhratpauruṣaṃ dhāma bhrājamāno yathā raviḥ
children.translated_text: Bearing that masculine radiance, blazing like the sun,
he became unapproachable and exceedingly hard for beings to assail.
Then the goddess bore the world-auspicious portion of <s>Acyuta</s>, deposited in her by the son of <s>Śūra</s>,

children.text: dadhāra sarvātmakam ātmabhūtaṃ kāṣṭhā yathānandakaraṃ manastaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Self of all, present as her own self, as the eastern quarter bears the joy-giving moon.

children.text: sā devakī sarvajagannivāsanivāsabhūtā nitarāṃ na reje
children.translated_text: That <s>Devakī</s>, who had become the dwelling of the indweller of the whole universe, did not shine forth fully,

children.text: bhojendragehe 'gniśikheva ruddhā sarasvatī jñānakhale yathā satī ||
children.translated_text: like a flame shut up in the house of the <s>Bhoja</s> king, or like true learning in an ignorant rogue.

children.text: tāṃ vīkṣya kaṃsaḥ prabhayājitāntarāṃ virocayantīṃ bhavanaṃ śucismitām
children.translated_text: Seeing her, radiant with beauty within and lighting up the house with her pure smile, <s>Kaṃsa</s> said:

children.text: āhaiṣa me prāṇaharo harirguhāṃ dhruvaṃ śrito yanna pureyamīdṛśī ||
children.translated_text: "This <s>Hari</s>, the taker of my life, has surely taken refuge in the cave of her womb, since she was not like this before.

children.text: kimadya tasminkaraṇīyamāśu me yadarthatantro na vihanti vikramam
children.translated_text: What should I do quickly today about him? My prowess, bound by its purpose, must not strike her down.

children.text: striyāḥ svasurgurumatyā vadho 'yaṃ yaśaḥ śriyaṃ hantyanukālamāyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The killing of a woman, of my own sister, and of one heavy with child, would destroy fame, prosperity, life span, and good fortune.

children.text: sa eṣa jīvankhalu saṃpareto varteta yo 'tyantanṛśaṃsitena
children.translated_text: A man who lives by extreme cruelty is indeed already dead while living;

children.text: dehe mṛte taṃ manujāḥ śapanti gantā tamo 'ndhaṃ tanumānino dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: when his body is dead, people curse him, and one who identifies with the body surely goes to blind darkness."
Thus the lord himself turned back from that most dreadful intention,
and remained waiting for the birth of <s>Hari</s>, maintaining his bond of enmity.
Sitting, lying down, standing, eating, and wandering over the earth,
as he thought of <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, he saw the world filled with him.
<s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Bhava</s> came there, together with sages such as <s>Nārada</s>,
and, along with the gods and their attendants, praised the mighty Lord with hymns.

children.text: satyavrataṃ satyaparaṃ trisatyaṃ satyasya yoniṃ nihitaṃ ca satye
children.translated_text: "You are true in vow, devoted to truth, true in the three times, the source of truth, and hidden in truth;

children.text: satyasya satyamṛtasatyanetraṃ satyātmakaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: you are the truth of truth, the eye of truth and immortality; we have taken refuge in you, whose nature is truth.
This primordial tree has one support, two fruits, three roots, four tastes, five kinds, and sixfold nature;
it has seven barks, eight branches, nine openings, ten leaves, and two birds.

children.text: tvameka evāsya sataḥ prasūtistvaṃ sannidhānaṃ tvamanugrahaśca
children.translated_text: You alone are the origin of this existent world; you are its abiding presence and its grace.

children.text: tvanmāyayā saṃvṛtacetasastvāṃ paśyanti nānā na vipaścito ye ||
children.translated_text: Those whose minds are covered by your <s>māyā</s> see you as many; the truly wise do not.

children.text: bibharṣi rūpāṇyavabodha ātmā kṣemāya lokasya carācarasya
children.translated_text: You, the conscious Self, assume forms endowed with <s>sattva</s> for the welfare of the moving and unmoving world;
they bring happiness to the good and, again and again, misfortune to the wicked.
Some, O lotus-eyed one, fix their minds in <s>samādhi</s> on you, the abode of all <s>sattva</s>;
by the great boat of your feet they make the ocean of becoming like the water in a calf's hoofprint.

children.text: svayaṃ samuttīrya sudustaraṃ dyuman bhavārṇavaṃ bhīmamadabhrasauhṛdāḥ
children.translated_text: Having themselves crossed the fearful, very difficult ocean of becoming, O radiant one, out of boundless friendship,

children.text: bhavatpadāmbhoruhanāvamatra te nidhāya yātāḥ sadanugraho bhavān ||
children.translated_text: they leave here the boat of your lotus feet and depart; you are gracious to the good.
Others, O lotus-eyed one, who think themselves liberated, have impure understanding because their feeling is not fixed in you;

children.text: āruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṃ padaṃ tataḥ patantyadho 'nādṛtayuṣmadaṅghrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having climbed with difficulty to the highest state, they then fall down, neglecting your feet.

children.text: tathā na te mādhava tāvakāḥ kvacidbhraśyanti mārgāttvayi baddhasauhṛdāḥ
children.translated_text: But your own people, O <s>Mādhava</s>, never fall from the path, for their friendship is bound to you;
protected by you, O Lord, they move fearlessly over the heads of hosts of obstacle-makers.

children.text: sattvaṃ viśuddhaṃ śrayate bhavān sthitau śarīriṇāṃ śreyaupāyanaṃ vapuḥ
children.translated_text: In sustaining embodied beings, you take refuge in pure <s>sattva</s>, a body that is the means to their highest good;
through it people seek to worship you by Vedic rites, yoga, austerity, and <s>samādhi</s>.
If this pure <s>sattva</s>, your own form, did not exist, O creator, there would be no knowledge that wipes away the split of ignorance.

children.text: guṇaprakāśairanumīyate bhavānprakāśate yasya ca yena vā guṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are inferred by the manifestations of the qualities, and a quality is revealed by that in which and through which it appears.

children.text: na nāmarūpe guṇajanmakarmabhir nirūpitavye tava tasya sākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Your name and form cannot be defined by qualities, birth, or actions, for you are the witness of them;
your course is only inferred by mind and speech, O god, though people still approach you through sacred action.

children.text: śṛṇvangṛṇansaṃsmarayaṃśca cintayan nāmāni rūpāṇi ca maṅgalāni te
children.translated_text: Hearing, reciting, remembering, causing others to remember, and contemplating your auspicious names and forms...
But one whose mind is absorbed in the rites connected with your lotus feet is not fit for worldly becoming.

children.text: diṣṭyā hare 'syā bhavataḥ pado bhuvo bhāro 'panītastava janmaneśituḥ
children.translated_text: By good fortune, O <s>Hari</s>, through this birth of you, the Lord, the burden of the earth has been removed.

children.text: diṣṭyāṅkitāṃ tvatpadakaiḥ suśobhanairdrakṣyāma gāṃ dyāṃ ca tavānukampitām ||
children.translated_text: By good fortune we shall see the earth and heaven, graced by you, marked and made splendid with your auspicious footprints.

children.text: na te 'bhavasyeśa bhavasya kāraṇaṃ vinā vinodaṃ bata tarkayāmahe
children.translated_text: O Lord, we cannot reason that there is any cause for your birth, though you are birthless and the cause of becoming, except mere play.
For birth, dissolution, and continuance are produced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) in you, the self who are the fearless refuge.
You have taken avatāras among fish, horse, tortoise, man-lion, boar, swan, kings, brahmins, and gods.

children.text: tvaṃ pāsi nastribhuvanaṃ ca yathādhuneśa bhāraṃ bhuvo hara yadūttama vandanaṃ te ||
children.translated_text: So now too, O Lord, protect us and the three worlds; remove the burden of the earth, O best of the <s>Yadus</s>. Reverence to you.

children.text: diṣṭyāmba te kukṣigataḥ paraḥ pumān aṃśena sākṣādbhagavānbhavāya naḥ
children.translated_text: By good fortune, O mother, the supreme person, the Blessed Lord himself, is in your womb by a portion of himself for our welfare.
Let there be no fear from the <s>Bhoja</s> king who is doomed to die; your son will become the protector of the <s>Yadus</s>.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Having thus praised the <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose form is not like this world, as best they could,
the gods, placing <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Īśāna</s> in front, returned to heaven.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Then the time came, endowed with every virtue and supremely beautiful,
when the constellation of the unborn one's birth arose, and the constellations, planets, and stars were peaceful.
The quarters became clear, and the sky was pure with the rising of hosts of stars.
The earth, with its cities, villages, cowherd settlements, and mines, was full of auspiciousness.
The rivers had clear water, and the lakes possessed the beauty of lotuses.
The forest groves were filled with clusters of flowers and the calls of flocks of birds and bees.
A wind blew, pleasant to the touch, pure, and carrying holy fragrance.
And the fires of the twice-born, peaceful there, blazed up.
The minds of the good, the enemies of the Asuras, became serene.
As the unborn one was being born, kettledrums sounded together.
Kinnaras and Gandharvas sang, and Siddhas and Cāraṇas offered praises.
The Vidyādhara women danced joyfully together with the Apsarases.
Sages and gods, filled with joy, released showers of flowers.
Clouds gently, gently thundered, following the sound of the ocean.
At midnight, when darkness had arisen and <s>Janārdana</s> was being born,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, who dwells in every hidden heart, appeared in the godlike <s>Devakī</s>,
like the full moon appearing in the eastern quarter.
<s>Vasudeva</s> saw that wondrous child, lotus-eyed, four-armed, holding up weapons such as the conch and mace,
bearing the mark of <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, with the <s>Kaustubha</s> shining on his neck, wearing yellow garments, and beautiful like a dense raincloud.
The splendor of his costly sapphire crown and earrings embraced his thousand locks of hair,
and he shone with a resplendent girdle, armlets, bracelets, and other ornaments.
Then <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>, his eyes opened wide with wonder, saw <s>Hari</s> as his son.
Overwhelmed with the festival joy of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s avatāra, he mentally gave ten thousand cows to the twice-born.

children.text: athainamastaudavadhārya pūruṣaṃ paraṃ natāṅgaḥ kṛtadhīḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Then, recognizing him as the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, with his body bowed, his mind composed, and his hands joined, he praised him,

children.text: svarociṣā bhārata sūtikāgṛhaṃ virocayantaṃ gatabhīḥ prabhāvavit ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhārata</s>, as he illumined the birth-chamber with his own radiance; <s>Vasudeva</s>, knowing his majesty, was free from fear.
<s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> said:
I know that you are directly the <s>Puruṣa</s>, beyond <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature),
whose own form is the bliss of pure experience alone, the seer of all intellects.
You yourself, having first created this universe by your own <s>prakṛti</s>, composed of the three <s>guṇas</s>,

children.text: tadanu tvaṃ hyapraviṣṭaḥ praviṣṭa iva bhāvyase ||
children.translated_text: after that, though not entered into it, are conceived as if entered into it.
Just as these unmodified elements, together with their modifications,
having different powers and becoming separate, indeed produce the cosmic body,
and, after coming together and producing it, are seen as if they had entered into it,
yet because they existed beforehand, they have no real arising here.
In the same way, though you exist among the graspable <s>guṇas</s>, whose marks are inferred by the intellect, you are not grasped by those <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: anāvṛtatvādbahirantaraṃ na te sarvasya sarvātmana ātmavastunaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because you are unobstructed, there is no outside or inside for you, the self-substance that is the self of all and everything.

children.text: ya ātmano dṛśyaguṇeṣu sanniti vyavasyate svavyatirekato 'budhaḥ
children.translated_text: An ignorant person who determines that the self exists among visible qualities apart from his own true distinction

children.text: vinānuvādaṃ na ca tanmanīṣitaṃ samyagyatastyaktam upādadat pumān ||
children.translated_text: has not thought correctly, since a person who takes up what has been rejected does so without proper instruction.
O mighty Lord, they say that the birth, continuance, and restraint of this world come from you, though you are inactive, without <s>guṇas</s>, and changeless.

children.text: tvayīśvare brahmaṇi no virudhyate tvadāśrayatvādupacaryate guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is not contradictory in you, the Lord, the brahman, because it is conventionally expressed through qualities, since those qualities depend on you.

children.text: sa tvaṃ trilokasthitaye svamāyayā bibharṣi śuklaṃ khalu varṇamātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: You, for the maintenance of the three worlds, bear by your own <s>māyā</s> the white color of yourself;

children.text: sargāya raktaṃ rajasopabṛṃhitaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca varṇaṃ tamasā janātyaye ||
children.translated_text: for creation you bear the red color strengthened by <s>rajas</s>, and for the destruction of creatures the black color with <s>tamas</s>.
O mighty lord, wishing to protect this world, you have descended in my house, O Lord of all.
You will destroy the armies being deployed by troop-leaders, crores of Asuras known as kings.

children.text: ayaṃ tvasabhyastava janma nau gṛhe śrutvāgrajāṃste nyavadhītsureśvara
children.translated_text: But this uncivilized man, O lord of the gods, having heard of your birth in our house, killed your elder brothers.
Now, hearing of your avatāra as reported by his men, he is coming this very moment with weapon raised.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Then, seeing this son of hers marked with the signs of the great person,
<s>Devakī</s>, frightened of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and greatly astonished, addressed him.
<s>Śrī Devakī</s> said:
That form which they call unmanifest, primal, brahman, light, without <s>guṇas</s>, changeless,

children.text: sattāmātraṃ nirviśeṣaṃ nirīhaṃ sa tvaṃ sākṣādviṣṇuradhyātmadīpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: mere being, without distinctions, inactive: you are directly that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lamp of the inner self.
When the world has perished at the end of two parārdhas, and the great elements have gone into the primal element,
When the manifest has gone into the unmanifest through the force of time, you alone remain, known as that which is without remainder.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ kālastasya te 'vyaktabandho ceṣṭāmāhuśceṣṭate yena viśvam
children.translated_text: This time, which belongs to you, O source of the unmanifest, is called your activity, by which the universe acts;
from the blink of an eye up to the year, it is vast. I take refuge in you, the Lord, the abode of well-being.
A mortal, fleeing in fear of the serpent of death, has not found any fearless place in all the worlds.

children.text: tvatpādābjaṃ prāpya yadṛcchayādya susthaḥ śete mṛtyurasmādapaiti ||
children.translated_text: But having reached your lotus feet today by chance, he lies at ease; death turns away from him.
Therefore rescue us, frightened as we are, from the terrible son of <s>Ugrasena</s>; you remove the fears of your servants.

children.text: rūpaṃ cedaṃ pauruṣaṃ dhyānadhiṣṇyaṃ mā pratyakṣaṃ māṃsadṛśāṃ kṛṣīṣṭhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And do not make this human-like form, the seat of meditation, directly visible to eyes of flesh.

children.text: janma te mayyasau pāpo mā vidyānmadhusūdana
children.translated_text: May that sinful one not learn of your birth from me, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>.
Because of you I tremble before <s>Kaṃsa</s>, my mind unsteady with fear.
Withdraw, O self of the universe, this supernatural form,
four-armed and adorned with the splendor of conch, discus, mace, and lotus.

children.text: viśvaṃ yadetatsvatanau niśānte yathāvakāśaṃ puruṣaḥ paro bhavān
children.translated_text: At the end of the cosmic night, you, the supreme Person, bear this whole universe within your own body, each thing in its proper place.

children.text: bibharti so 'yaṃ mama garbhago 'bhūdaho nṛlokasya viḍambanaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: That very one has entered my womb: indeed, this is a wondrous mockery of the human world.
The Blessed Lord said:
You yourself, in a former creation, were <s>Pṛśni</s> in the age of <s>Svāyambhuva</s>, O virtuous woman;
and this one was then an unblemished <s>Prajāpati</s> named <s>Sutapā</s>.

children.text: yuvāṃ vai brahmaṇādiṣṭau prajāsarge yadā tataḥ
children.translated_text: When you two were commanded by <s>Brahmā</s> to create offspring,
you restrained the whole group of the senses and performed supreme austerity.
Enduring rain, wind, sun, cold, heat, and the seasonal qualities of time,
with the impurities of the mind shaken off by restraint of the breath,
feeding on withered leaves and air, and with tranquil minds,
you two sought to worship me, desiring boons from me.
While you two, whose minds were fixed on me, practiced in this way a fierce austerity, supremely difficult to perform,
twelve thousand divine years passed.
Then, O sinless one, I was satisfied with you two and appeared in this form,

children.text: tapasā śraddhayā nityaṃ bhaktyā ca hṛdi bhāvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: brought into your hearts by your austerity, faith, constant devotion, and love.
I appeared before you as the king of boon-givers, wishing to grant your desire;

children.text: vriyatāṃ vara ityukte mādṛśo vāṃ vṛtaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when I said, 'Choose a boon,' you chose a son like me.
Since you had not yet enjoyed worldly sense-objects and were a childless couple,
you did not choose liberation from me, being deluded by divine <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: gate mayi yuvāṃ labdhvā varaṃ matsadṛśaṃ sutam
children.translated_text: When I had gone, you two obtained the boon of a son like me;
with your wish fulfilled, you enjoyed worldly pleasures.
Seeing no one else in the world equal in character, generosity, and qualities,

children.text: ahaṃ suto vāmabhavaṃ pṛśnigarbha iti śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I became your son, famed as <s>Pṛśnigarbha</s>.
Again, for those same two of you, I was born from <s>Kaśyapa</s> in <s>Aditi</s>;
I was renowned as <s>Upendra</s>, and because of my dwarfish form, as <s>Vāmana</s>.
Now, in this third birth, with that very form, I have indeed been born again to you two.

children.text: jāto bhūyastayoreva satyaṃ me vyāhṛtaṃ sati ||
children.translated_text: My statement is true, O virtuous woman.
This form has been shown to you so that you may remember my previous births;
otherwise knowledge of my divine birth would not arise from a mortal appearance.
Thinking of me repeatedly both with the feeling for a son and with awareness of <s>brahman</s>,
you two, full of affection, will attain my supreme state.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Having spoken thus, the Blessed <s>Hari</s> became silent, and by his own <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: pitroḥ sampaśyatoḥ sadyo babhūva prākṛtaḥ śiśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: at once, while his parents looked on, he became an ordinary infant.

children.text: tataśca śaurirbhagavatpracoditaḥ sutaṃ samādāya sa sūtikāgṛhāt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śauri</s>, impelled by the Blessed Lord, took his son from the birth-chamber;

children.text: yadā bahirgantumiyeṣa tarhyajā yā yogamāyājani nandajāyayā ||
children.translated_text: and when he wished to go outside, just then the unborn <s>Yogamāyā</s> was born from <s>Nanda</s>'s wife.
By her, the awareness and all the functions of the gatekeepers and even of the townspeople were taken away, and they lay asleep.
All the gates, hard to pass, were closed with great doors, iron bolts, and chains.

children.text: tāḥ kṛṣṇavāhe vasudeva āgate svayaṃ vyavaryanta yathā tamo raveḥ
children.translated_text: But when <s>Vasudeva</s>, carrying <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, came to them, they opened by themselves, as darkness gives way before the sun.
<s>Parjanya</s> rained with low thunder, and <s>Śeṣa</s> followed behind, warding off the water with his hoods.
As <s>Maghavan</s> poured rain again and again, the river <s>Yamunā</s>, with deep floods, swift waves, and foam,

children.text: bhayānakāvartaśatākulā nadī mārgaṃ dadau sindhuriva śriyaḥ pateḥ ||
children.translated_text: crowded with hundreds of frightening whirlpools, gave him a path, like the ocean for the lord of <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: nandavrajaṃ śaurirupetya tatra tān gopānprasuptānupalabhya nidrayā
children.translated_text: <s>Śauri</s> reached <s>Nanda</s>'s cowherd settlement, and there found the cowherds sunk in sleep.
Placing his son on <s>Yaśodā</s>'s bed and taking up her daughter, he returned again to his own house.
Then <s>Vasudeva</s> placed the girl on <s>Devakī</s>'s bed,
fastened the iron shackles back onto his feet, and remained confined as before.
<s>Yaśodā</s>, <s>Nanda</s>'s wife, did not fully understand that a child had been born,
nor its sex, for she was exhausted and her memory had been carried away by sleep.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
The doors outside and inside the women's quarters were all shut as before.
Then, hearing the sound of a child, the guards of the house rose up.

children.text: te tu tūrṇamupavrajya devakyā garbhajanma tat
children.translated_text: They quickly approached and reported to the king of the <s>Bhojas</s>
that birth from <s>Devakī</s>'s womb for which he waited in anxiety.
He sprang quickly from his bed, distraught and thinking, 'This is my death.'
With loosened hair, stumbling as he went, he quickly entered the birth-chamber.

children.text: tamāha bhrātaraṃ devī kṛpaṇā karuṇaṃ satī
children.translated_text: The wretched, virtuous goddess spoke piteously to her brother:

children.text: snuṣeyaṃ tava kalyāṇa striyaṃ mā hantumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: 'O auspicious one, this girl is your daughter-in-law; you should not kill a woman.
Many children, bright as fire, have been slain by you, brother,
impelled by fate. Let this one little daughter be granted to me.

children.text: nanvahaṃ te hyavarajā dīnā hatasutā prabho
children.translated_text: Am I not your younger sister, O lord, wretched and bereft of sons?
Dear brother, you ought to give this last child to miserable me.'
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Though she embraced her daughter in this way and wept most piteously,
the wicked man, when she begged him, rebuked her and tore the child from her hands.
Taking that daughter of his sister by the feet as soon as she was born,
he, whose affection had been uprooted by self-interest, dashed her against the surface of a stone.
But she sprang up from his hands at once and went into the divine sky;
she was seen as <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s younger sister, armed and eight-armed in majestic form.
She was adorned with divine garlands, garments, unguents, jewels, and ornaments,
bearing bow, trident, arrows, shield, sword, conch, discus, and mace.
As Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, Apsarases, Kinnaras, and serpents
praised her with abundant offerings brought before her, she spoke these words:

children.text: kiṃ mayā hatayā manda jātaḥ khalu tavāntakṛt
children.translated_text: "What is gained by killing me, fool? The one who will end you has indeed been born.

children.text: yatra kva vā pūrvaśatrurmā hiṃsīḥ kṛpaṇānvṛthā ||
children.translated_text: Your former enemy is somewhere else. Do not kill pitiable children in vain."

children.text: iti prabhāṣya taṃ devī māyā bhagavatī bhuvi
children.translated_text: Having addressed him thus, the goddess, the blessed <s>Māyā</s>,
became known on earth by many names in many abodes.
Hearing what she had said, <s>Kaṃsa</s> was utterly astonished;
releasing <s>Devakī</s> and <s>Vasudeva</s>, he spoke submissively:

children.text: aho bhaginyaho bhāma mayā vāṃ bata pāpmanā
children.translated_text: "Ah, my sister! Ah, noble lady! Alas, by me, a sinful man,
many sons of yours have been killed like children by a man-eater.
As for me, cruel, without compassion, and having abandoned kinsmen and friends,
to what worlds shall I go, like a killer of Brahmins, dead while still breathing?

children.text: daivamapyanṛtaṃ vakti na martyā eva kevalam
children.translated_text: Even fate speaks falsely, not only mortals,
for trusting in it, I, a sinner, killed my sister's infants.
Do not grieve, most fortunate ones, for your own sons who were killed by me; experience what was wrought by your own acts.
Living beings, dependent on fate, do not always remain together in one place.

children.text: bhuvi bhaumāni bhūtāni yathā yāntyapayānti ca
children.translated_text: Just as earthly beings on earth come and go,
so the self does not change among these bodies, just as the earth itself does not.
For one who does not know this, there is division, because of the misapprehension of the self;
and while there is union and separation with the body, transmigration does not cease.
Therefore, good lady, do not grieve for your sons, even though they were slain by me,
since everyone helplessly receives the fruit of his own action.
So long as a person of false vision thinks of himself, 'I have been killed' or 'I am the killer,'
so long, ignorant and attached to that conception, he reaches the condition of being harmed and harming.
Forgive my wickedness, you righteous ones, compassionate to the wretched."
Having said this, his face wet with tears, the brother-in-law then grasped his sister's and her husband's feet.
Trusting in the words of the girl, he released <s>Devakī</s> and <s>Vasudeva</s>
from their shackles, displaying his own affection for them.
<s>Devakī</s>, her anger calmed toward her repentant brother, forgave him,
and <s>Vasudeva</s> too, smiling, let him go and spoke to him:
"It is indeed so, most fortunate one, just as you say of embodied beings:
the notion of 'I' arises from ignorance, and from it comes the division, 'mine' and 'another's.'
Filled with grief, joy, fear, hatred, greed, delusion, and pride,

children.text: mitho ghnantaṃ na paśyanti bhāvairbhāvaṃ pṛthagdṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: people of separate vision do not see that one state kills another state among themselves."
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Thus answered with pure words by <s>Devakī</s> and <s>Vasudeva</s>, who were reconciled with him,
<s>Kaṃsa</s>, having received their permission, entered his house.

children.text: tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ kaṃsa āhūya mantriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: When that night had passed, <s>Kaṃsa</s> summoned his ministers
and told them everything that had been said by <s>Yoganidrā</s>.
Hearing their master's speech, the Daiteyas, enemies of the gods,
who were angry toward the gods and not very wise, said to him:
"If this is so, then, O king of the Bhojas, in cities, villages, cowherd settlements, and elsewhere,
we shall today kill infants younger than ten days and those older than ten days.
What will the gods, afraid of battle, do by their efforts,
their minds always agitated by the twang of your bowstring?
When you release volleys of arrows, and they are struck down on every side,
they, wanting to live, abandon the fight and go intent on flight.
Some gods, wretched with joined palms and weapons laid down,
and some, with loosened garments and hair-tufts, say, 'We are afraid.'
You do not kill those who have forgotten their weapons and missiles, who are without chariots and enveloped in fear,
who are unattached, turned away, with bows broken, and not fighting.
What use are the gods, brave only when secure and boasting outside battle?

children.text: rahojuṣā kiṃ hariṇā śambhunā vā vanaukasā
children.translated_text: What use is <s>Hari</s>, fond of secret places, or <s>Śambhu</s>, a forest-dweller?
What use is <s>Indra</s> of little valor, or <s>Brahmā</s>, who is engaged in austerity?
Nevertheless, we think the gods, as our rivals, should not be ignored;
therefore appoint us, your followers, to dig up their root.
Just as a disease in the body, when neglected by men, cannot be cured once it has taken firm root,
and just as the troop of senses, when neglected, becomes so strong that it cannot be moved, so too a great enemy with established strength cannot be displaced.

children.text: mūlaṃ hi viṣṇurdevānāṃ yatra dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: For <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the root of the gods, and wherever there is eternal <s>dharma</s>,
his roots are Brahmins, cows, priests learned in brahman, austerity, and sacrifices with proper gifts.
Therefore, O king, with every effort let us kill the Brahmins who speak of brahman,
the ascetics, those devoted to sacrifice, and the cows that yield oblations.

children.text: viprā gāvaśca vedāśca tapaḥ satyaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ
children.translated_text: Brahmins, cows, the Vedas, austerity, truth, restraint, tranquility,

children.text: śraddhā dayā titikṣā ca kratavaśca harestanūḥ ||
children.translated_text: faith, compassion, endurance, and sacrificial rites are the bodies of <s>Hari</s>.
He is indeed the overseer of all the gods, the hater of Asuras, dwelling in the hidden heart;
all the deities, together with <s>Īśvara</s> and the four-faced one, have him as their root.
This indeed is the means of killing him: violence against the seers."
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ durmantribhiḥ kaṃsaḥ saha saṃmantrya durmatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated with his evil ministers, the wicked-minded <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
an Asura bound by the noose of Time, considered violence against Brahmins to be beneficial.
Having instructed those demons, lovers of slaughter who could assume any form at will, to go into the quarters for the destruction of the righteous people,
he entered his house.
They, indeed, were of a passionate nature, their minds deluded by darkness,
and, with death already near at hand, they practiced hatred against the good from afar.

children.text: āyuḥ śriyaṃ yaśo dharmaṃ lokānāśiṣa eva ca
children.translated_text: A transgression against the great destroys a man's life, prosperity, fame, <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), worlds, and blessings,
and all his highest goods.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
But <s>Nanda</s>, rejoicing at the birth of his son and high-minded,
summoned Brahmins learned in the Veda; bathed, purified, and adorned,
he had auspicious benedictions recited and duly performed the birth-rite for his son,
as well as worship of the ancestors and gods.
He gave to the Brahmins two million cows, adorned,
and seven hills of sesame covered with masses of jewels, gold-woven cloth, and garments.
By time, by bathing and purification, by sacraments, austerity, and worship,
things are purified; by gifts and contentment, and the self by knowledge of the self.
The Brahmins uttered words of blessing; the bards, genealogists, and panegyrists,
and the singers sang, while kettledrums and war-drums sounded again and again.
<s>Vraja</s> had its doorways, courtyards, and interiors swept and sprinkled,
and was adorned with variegated banners, flags, garlands, cloths, leafy shoots, and arches.
The cows, bulls, and young calves were smeared with turmeric and oil,
and were garlanded with various minerals, peacock feathers, wreaths, cloths, and gold ornaments.
The cowherds, adorned with costly garments, ornaments, jackets, and turbans,
came together, O king, with many kinds of gifts in their hands.
And the cowherd women, hearing with joy of the birth of <s>Yaśodā</s>'s son,
adorned themselves with garments, ornaments, collyrium, and the like.
Their lotus faces were bright with fresh saffron pollen;
with offerings they went quickly, broad-hipped, their breasts swaying.
The cowherd women, with polished jeweled earrings and gold necklaces, wearing bright garments, showering garlands that slipped from their hair along the road,
shone as they went with bangles to <s>Nanda</s>'s house, splendid with swinging earrings, breasts, and necklaces.
Offering blessings to the child, saying, 'May you protect us long,'
they sprinkled the people with turmeric powder, oil, and water, and sang aloud.
Many kinds of musical instruments were played at the great festival,
when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, lord of the universe, the infinite one, had come to <s>Nanda</s>'s <s>Vraja</s>.
The cowherds, delighted with one another, with curds, milk, ghee, and water,
sprinkled and smeared one another, and pelted one another with fresh butter.
High-minded <s>Nanda</s> honored them with garments, ornaments, and wealth in cows,
and also the bards, genealogists, panegyrists, and others who lived by learning,
with those various desired gifts, as was proper, his heart not mean,
for the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and for the prosperity of his own son.
And greatly fortunate <s>Rohiṇī</s>, congratulated by <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd,
moved about adorned with divine garments, garlands, necklace, and ornaments.
From then on, O king, <s>Nanda</s>'s <s>Vraja</s> became endowed with every prosperity,
and, because of the inherent qualities of <s>Hari</s>'s residence, became a playground of <s>Ramā</s>.
After assigning the cowherds to guard <s>Gokula</s>, <s>Nanda</s> went to <s>Mathurā</s>,

children.text: nandaḥ kaṃsasya vārṣikyaṃ karaṃ dātuṃ kurūdvaha ||
children.translated_text: O descendant of <s>Kuru</s>, to give the annual tax to <s>Kaṃsa</s>.
<s>Vasudeva</s>, hearing that his brother <s>Nanda</s> had arrived,
and knowing that he had given the tax to the king, went to the place where he was staying.
Seeing him, he rose suddenly, as if his life had returned to his body,
and, delighted and overwhelmed with love, embraced his dearest friend with both arms.
After <s>Nanda</s> had been honored, was comfortably seated, and had respectfully asked after his welfare,
<s>Vasudeva</s>, his mind fixed on his two sons, spoke these words, O ruler of men:
'By good fortune, brother, though you were advanced in age and until now without offspring,
and had given up hope for children, a child has been born to you.
By good fortune, while you move in this wheel of saṃsāra, you have today been encountered again,
for the sight of a dear one is hard to obtain.
Dear friends whose karmic courses are varied do not dwell together in one place,
just as boats being driven along by a current do not remain together in a stream.
Is that great forest where you live among your friends now suitable for cattle, free from disease,
and rich in water, grass, and plants?
Brother, is my son there in your <s>Vraja</s> with his mother,
thinking of you as his father and cherished by you both?
For a man, the three aims of life are enjoined when his friends too have been benefited;
when they are suffering, the three aims do not serve their purpose.'
<s>Śrī Nanda</s> said:

children.text: aho te devakīputrāḥ kaṃsena bahavo hatāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Ah, many sons of your <s>Devakī</s> have been killed by <s>Kaṃsa</s>.
One younger daughter alone remained, and she too has gone to heaven.
Surely this human being has the unseen as his basis and the unseen as his highest end;

children.text: adṛṣṭamātmanastattvaṃ yo veda na sa muhyati ||
children.translated_text: he who knows the truth that the unseen is his own does not become deluded.'
<s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> said:

children.text: karo vai vārṣiko datto rājñe dṛṣṭā vayaṃ ca vaḥ
children.translated_text: 'The annual tax has indeed been paid to the king, and we have seen you.
You should not remain here for many days; there are disturbances in <s>Gokula</s>.'
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: iti nandādayo gopāḥ proktāste śauriṇā yayuḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Śauri</s>, <s>Nanda</s> and the other cowherds,
having taken leave of him, went to <s>Gokula</s> in carts yoked with oxen.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: kṛtvā daityavadhaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ sarāmo yadubhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Having accomplished the slaughter of the demons, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with <s>Rāma</s> and surrounded by the <s>Yadus</s>,
removed the burden of the earth, swiftly bringing about strife.

children.text: ye kopitāḥ subahu pāṇḍusutāḥ sapatnair durdyūtahelanakacagrahaṇādibhis tān
children.translated_text: Those sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, greatly angered by their enemies through wicked gambling, insult, seizure of the hair, and the like,

children.text: kṛtvā nimittam itaretarataḥ sametān hatvā nṛpān niraharat kṣitibhāram īśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he made them the occasion; when they had assembled against one another, the Lord slew the kings and removed the burden of the earth.

children.text: bhūbhārarājapṛtanā yadubhir nirasya guptaiḥ svabāhubhir acintayad aprameyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having removed the burden of the earth, the armies of kings, by means of the <s>Yadus</s> protected by his own arms, the immeasurable Lord reflected:

children.text: manye 'vaner nanu gato 'py agataṃ hi bhāraṃ yad yādavaṃ kulam aho aviṣahyam āste ||
children.translated_text: 'I think the earth's burden has not in fact gone, although it has been removed, since the <s>Yādava</s> clan remains here, unbearable indeed.

children.text: naivānyataḥ paribhavo 'sya bhavet kathaṃcin matsaṃśrayasya vibhavonnahanasya nityam
children.translated_text: There could never be defeat for this clan from any other source, since it is under my protection and is always swollen with prosperity.

children.text: antaḥ kaliṃ yadukulasya vidhāya veṇustambasya vahnim iva śāntim upaimi dhāma ||
children.translated_text: By creating internal strife within the <s>Yadu</s> clan, like fire within a bamboo grove, I shall go peacefully to my abode.'
Resolved in this way, O king, the Lord, whose resolve is true,
the all-powerful one, destroyed his own clan through the pretext of the Brahmins' curse.
By his own form, which embodied the beauty of the world, he captured the eyes of men;

children.text: gīrbhis tāḥ smaratāṃ cittaṃ padais tān īkṣatāṃ kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: by his words, the minds of those who remembered them; and by his footsteps, the actions of those who saw them.

children.text: ācchidya kīrtiṃ suślokāṃ vitatya hy añjasā nu kau
children.translated_text: Having spread his splendid fame, celebrated in noble verses, by which people would easily

children.text: tamo 'nayā tariṣyantīty agāt svaṃ padam īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: cross over darkness, the Lord went to his own state.
The king said:
How did a Brahmin's curse fall upon the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, who were devoted to Brahmins, generous, always serving their elders,
and whose minds were fixed on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?

children.text: yannimittaḥ sa vai śāpo yādṛśo dvijasattama
children.translated_text: Tell me all this, O best of twice-born men: what was the cause of that curse, what kind of curse was it,

children.text: katham ekātmanāṃ bheda etat sarvaṃ vadasva me ||
children.translated_text: and how did division arise among those who were of one mind?
<s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> said:

children.text: bibhrad vapuḥ sakalasundarasaṃniveśaṃ karmācaran bhuvi sumaṅgalam āptakāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Bearing a body composed of every kind of beauty, performing supremely auspicious deeds on earth, and having all desires fulfilled,

children.text: āsthāya dhāma ramamāṇa udārakīrtiḥ saṃhartum aicchata kulaṃ sthitakṛtyaśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he remained in his abode, sporting there, famous and noble, and wished to withdraw his clan, with only this task left to be done.
After he had performed meritorious and supremely auspicious deeds, deeds sung by the world and removing the stain of the age of <s>Kali</s>,

children.text: kālātmanā nivasatā yadudevagehe piṇḍārakaṃ samagaman munayo nisṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sages, impelled by him who dwelt as Time in the house of the lord of the <s>Yadus</s>, went to <s>Piṇḍāraka</s>.
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Asita</s>, <s>Kaṇva</s>, <s>Durvāsas</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
<s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and others were there.
The young <s>Yādava</s> princes, sons of the <s>Yadus</s>, approached them in sport,
grasped their feet, and, though undisciplined, questioned them as if they were humble.
They dressed <s>Sāmba</s>, the son of <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, in women's clothing and said:

children.text: eṣā pṛcchati vo viprā antarvatny asitekṣaṇā ||
children.translated_text: 'O Brahmins, this dark-eyed pregnant woman asks you.
She is ashamed to ask directly; therefore tell us, O you whose vision never fails:
desiring a son and about to give birth, what will she produce?'

children.text: evaṃ pralabdhā munayas tān ūcuḥ kupitā nṛpa
children.translated_text: Thus deceived, the sages became angry and said to them, O king:
'Fools, she will produce for you an iron pestle that will destroy your clan.'
Hearing this, they were greatly terrified, and at once they uncovered his belly.

children.text: sāmbasya dadṛśus tasmin musalaṃ khalv ayasmayam ||
children.translated_text: There, on <s>Sāmba</s>, they indeed saw an iron pestle.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtaṃ mandabhāgyair naḥ kiṃ vadiṣyanti no janāḥ
children.translated_text: 'What have we, ill-fated fools, done? What will people say of us?'

children.text: iti vihvalitā gehān ādāya musalaṃ yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Distraught in this way, they took the pestle and went home.
Bringing it into the assembly, their faces withered in beauty,
they reported it to the king in the presence of all the <s>Yādavas</s>.

children.text: śrutvāmoghaṃ vipraśāpaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca musalaṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: Hearing the unfailing Brahmin's curse and seeing the pestle, O king,
the inhabitants of <s>Dvārakā</s> were astonished and stricken with fear.

children.text: tac cūrṇayitvā musalaṃ yadurājaḥ sa āhukaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Yadu</s> king, <s>Āhuka</s>, had that pestle ground to powder,
and he cast it into the water of the ocean, together with the piece of iron that remained from it.

children.text: kaścin matsyo 'grasīl lohaṃ cūrṇāni taralais tataḥ
children.translated_text: A certain fish swallowed the iron piece, and then the powders, carried by the waves,
came to rest on the shore and became, it is said, reeds of eraka grass.
The fish was caught in the ocean by fishermen, along with other fish, in a net.
A hunter made the iron found in its belly into an arrowhead.
Although the Blessed Lord, the sovereign, knew the meaning of everything, he did not wish
to make the Brahmin's curse otherwise; taking the form of Time, he approved it.
<s>Śuka</s> said:
In <s>Dvāravatī</s>, protected by the arms of <s>Govinda</s>, O scion of <s>Kuru</s>,
<s>Nārada</s> often stayed, eager to worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
What self-controlled person, O king, would not worship the lotus feet of <s>Mukunda</s>,
which are worthy of worship by the best of immortals and before whom death comes from every side?

children.text: tam ekadā tu devarṣiṃ vasudevo gṛhāgatam
children.translated_text: Once <s>Vasudeva</s> bowed to that divine seer, who had come to his house,
had been honored, and was seated comfortably, and then he spoke these words:
<s>Vasudeva</s> said:
Blessed one, your journey is for the welfare of all embodied beings,
like that of parents for the helpless, and like that of those who follow the path of <s>Uttamaśloka</s>.

children.text: bhūtānāṃ devacaritaṃ duḥkhāya ca sukhāya ca
children.translated_text: The conduct of the gods toward beings brings both sorrow and happiness;
but that of holy ones like you, whose self is fixed in <s>Acyuta</s>, is only for happiness.

children.text: bhajanti ye yathā devān devā api tathaiva tān
children.translated_text: As people worship the gods, so the gods also respond to them;
they are like shadows, attendants of karma, whereas holy men are compassionate toward the poor.

children.text: brahmaṃs tathāpi pṛcchāmo dharmān bhāgavatāṃs tava
children.translated_text: O Brahmin, nevertheless we ask you about the dharmas of the devotees of the Blessed Lord,

children.text: yān śrutvā śraddhayā martyo mucyate sarvato bhayāt ||
children.translated_text: hearing which with faith a mortal is freed from fear on every side.

children.text: ahaṃ kila purānantaṃ prajārtho bhuvi muktidam
children.translated_text: Formerly, indeed, desiring offspring, I worshiped <s>Ananta</s> on earth, the giver of liberation,
but not for liberation, for I was deluded by divine <s>māyā</s>.
Teach us, O virtuous one, how through you we may directly and easily be freed

children.text: mucyema hy añjasaivāddhā tathā naḥ śādhi suvrata ||
children.translated_text: from varied calamity and from fear on every side.
<s>Śuka</s> said:
O king, when the wise <s>Vasudeva</s> had asked this question,

children.text: prītas tam āha devarṣir hareḥ saṃsmārito guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the divine seer, pleased and reminded of <s>Hari</s> by his virtues, said to him:
<s>Nārada</s> said:
This has been rightly resolved by you, O bull among the <s>Sātvatas</s>,

children.text: yat pṛcchase bhāgavatān dharmāṃs tvaṃ viśvabhāvanān ||
children.translated_text: in that you ask about the bhāgavata dharmas, which sustain the universe.
This true dharma, whether heard, recited, meditated upon, honored,
or simply approved, at once purifies even one who has harmed the gods and the world.
By you, the supremely auspicious one, whose hearing and chanting are meritorious,

children.text: smārito bhagavān adya devo nārāyaṇo mama ||
children.translated_text: Today the Blessed Lord, the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, has been brought to my remembrance.
In this connection they also cite this ancient history,
the dialogue of the sages descended from <s>Ṛṣabha</s> with the great-souled king of <s>Videha</s>.

children.text: priyavrato nāma suto manoḥ svāyambhuvasya yaḥ
children.translated_text: There was a son of <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s> named <s>Priyavrata</s>;

children.text: tasyāgnīdhras tato nābhir ṛṣabhas tatsutaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his son was <s>Agnīdhra</s>, then <s>Nābhi</s>, and <s>Ṛṣabha</s> is remembered as his son.
They say that he was a portion of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, descended with the wish to teach the dharma of liberation;
he had one hundred sons, who had mastered the Veda and brahman.
Of them <s>Bharata</s>, the eldest, was devoted wholly to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: vikhyātaṃ varṣam etad yan nāmnā bhāratam adbhutam ||
children.translated_text: this wondrous land is famed by his name as <s>Bhārata</s>.

children.text: sa bhuktabhogāṃ tyaktvemāṃ nirgatas tapasā harim
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed pleasures, he abandoned this earth and went forth; through austerity, worshiping <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: upāsīnas tatpadavīṃ lebhe vai janṛnabhis tribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he attained the Lord's path through three births, O men.
Of the others, nine became lords of the nine island-continents around this land,
and eighty-one, twice-born, were promulgators of the ritual system.
Nine became greatly blessed sages, proclaimers of the true good,
renunciants, clothed with the wind, expert in knowledge of the self.
They were <s>Kavi</s>, <s>Havi</s>, <s>Antarīkṣa</s>, <s>Prabuddha</s>, <s>Pippalāyana</s>,
<s>Āvirhotra</s>, then <s>Drumila</s>, <s>Camasa</s>, and <s>Karabhājana</s>.
Seeing this universe, composed of being and non-being, as the form of the Blessed Lord,
and as not separate from the self, they wandered over the earth.
Their chosen movements were unobstructed through the worlds of gods, siddhas, sādhyas, gandharvas, yakṣas, men, kinnaras, and nāgas;
liberated, they move at will through the realms of sages, cāraṇas, bhūtanāthas, vidyādharas, twice-borns, and cows.

children.text: ta ekadā nimeḥ sattram upajagmur yadṛcchayā
children.translated_text: One day they came by chance to <s>Nimi</s>'s sacrificial session,
which was being extended by the seers of the great-souled descendant of <s>Ajanābha</s>.
Seeing those great devotees, shining like the sun, O king,
the sacrificer, the fires, the brahmins, all of them, rose up in attendance.
Recognizing them as devoted wholly to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the king of <s>Videha</s>,
delighted, worshiped them according to their worth after they had taken their seats.
Those nine, radiant with their own splendor and like sons of <s>Brahmā</s>,
he questioned with supreme joy, O king, bowing low in humility.
<s>Śrī Videha</s> said:

children.text: manye bhagavataḥ sākṣāt pārṣadān vo madhudviṣaḥ
children.translated_text: I think you are direct attendants of the Blessed Lord, the foe of <s>Madhu</s>;

children.text: viṣṇor bhūtāni lokānāṃ pāvanāya caranti hi ||
children.translated_text: for beings belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s> wander for the purification of the worlds.
A human body is hard for embodied beings to obtain and perishes in a moment;
even there, I consider the sight of those dear to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> hard to obtain.
Therefore, O sinless ones, we ask you about the ultimate welfare,
for in this saṃsāra even half a moment of association with the good is a treasure for human beings.

children.text: dharmān bhāgavatān brūta yadi naḥ śrutaye kṣamam
children.translated_text: Tell us the bhāgavata-dharmas, if it is fit for us to hear,

children.text: yaiḥ prasannaḥ prapannāya dāsyaty ātmānam apy ajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by which the unborn Lord, pleased with one who has taken refuge, will grant even himself.
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ te niminā pṛṣṭā vasudeva mahattamāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus questioned by <s>Nimi</s>, O <s>Vasudeva</s>, those greatest ones,
having been duly worshiped, spoke with affection to the king together with his assembly and priests.
<s>Śrī Kavi</s> said:
I consider constant worship here of <s>Acyuta</s>'s lotus feet to be freedom from fear from every side,

children.text: udvignabuddher asadātmabhāvād viśvātmanā yatra nivartate bhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: for there fear ceases for the anxious mind that arises from identifying the self with the unreal, by seeing the Self as the universe.

children.text: ye vai bhagavatā proktā upāyā hy ātmalabdhaye
children.translated_text: Those means taught by the Blessed Lord for the attainment of the self,

children.text: añjaḥ puṃsām aviduṣāṃ viddhi bhāgavatān hi tān ||
children.translated_text: know them indeed to be the bhāgavata ways, easy for ignorant people.

children.text: yān āsthāya naro rājan na pramādyeta karhicit
children.translated_text: Adopting them, O king, a person would never become heedless at any time;

children.text: dhāvan nimīlya vā netre na skhalen na pated iha ||
children.translated_text: even running with his eyes closed, he would not stumble or fall here.

children.text: kāyena vācā manasendriyair vā buddhyātmanā vānusṛtasvabhāvāt
children.translated_text: Whatever one does with body, speech, mind, senses,

children.text: karoti yad yat sakalaṃ parasmai nārāyaṇāyeti samarpayet tat ||
children.translated_text: intellect, or self, according to one's own nature, all of that one should offer, saying, 'It is for the supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.'

children.text: bhayaṃ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād īśād apetasya viparyayo 'smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Fear arises from absorption in a second thing, for one who has turned away from the Lord; there is inversion and forgetfulness,

children.text: tanmāyayāto budha ābhajet taṃ bhaktyaikayeśaṃ gurudevatātmā ||
children.translated_text: because of his māyā. Therefore the wise person should worship that Lord alone with devotion, regarding the guru as deity and self.

children.text: avidyamāno 'py avabhāti hi dvayo dhyātur dhiyā svapnamanorathau yathā
children.translated_text: Though not really existent, duality appears to the meditator's mind, just like dream and fantasy;

children.text: tat karmasaṃkalpavikalpakaṃ mano budho nirundhyād abhayaṃ tataḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: therefore the wise person should restrain the mind that makes schemes and alternatives about action; from that fearlessness will arise.

children.text: śṛṇvan subhadrāṇi rathāṅgapāṇer janmāni karmāṇi ca yāni loke
children.translated_text: Hearing the auspicious births and deeds of the wielder of the discus as they are sung in the world,

children.text: gītāni nāmāni tadarthakāni gāyan vilajjo vicared asaṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and singing his names, which express those meanings, one should wander without shame and unattached.
Keeping such a vow, attached by singing the names of his beloved Lord, his heart melted, aloud

children.text: hasaty atho roditi rauti gāyaty unmādavan nṛtyati lokabāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he laughs, then weeps, cries out, sings, and, like a madman, dances, outside worldly convention.

children.text: khaṃ vāyum agniṃ salilaṃ mahīṃ ca jyotīṃṣi sattvāni diśo drumādīn
children.translated_text: Sky, wind, fire, water, earth, the heavenly lights, living beings, directions, trees and the rest,

children.text: saritsamudrāṃś ca hareḥ śarīraṃ yat kiṃ ca bhūtaṃ praṇamed ananyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: rivers and oceans, and whatever being there is, he should bow to as <s>Hari</s>'s body, with no sense of otherness.

children.text: bhaktiḥ pareśānubhavo viraktir anyatra caiṣa trika ekakālaḥ
children.translated_text: Devotion, direct experience of the supreme Lord, and detachment from other things: this triad arises at the same time

children.text: prapadyamānasya yathāśnataḥ syus tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiḥ kṣudapāyo 'nughāsam ||
children.translated_text: for one who is taking refuge, just as satisfaction, nourishment, and the cessation of hunger arise at each mouthful for one who eats.

children.text: ity acyutāṅghriṃ bhajato 'nuvṛttyā bhaktir viraktir bhagavatprabodhaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, for the devotee who worships <s>Acyuta</s>'s feet by continual service, devotion, detachment, and awakening to the Blessed Lord

children.text: bhavanti vai bhāgavatasya rājaṃs tataḥ parāṃ śāntim upaiti sākṣāt ||
children.translated_text: surely arise, O king; then he directly attains supreme peace.
The king said:

children.text: atha bhāgavataṃ brūta yaddharmo yādṛśo nṛṇām
children.translated_text: Now tell us about the bhāgavata, what his dharma is and of what sort it is among men,

children.text: yathācarati yad brūte yair liṅgair bhagavatpriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how the Lord's beloved one behaves, what he says, and by what signs he is known.
<s>Śrī Havi</s> said:
He who sees the state of the Blessed Lord, as his own self, in all beings,
and sees all beings in the Blessed Lord, the Self: he is the highest bhāgavata.
With respect to the Lord, to those dependent on him, to the childish, and to those who hate him...
One who shows love, friendship, compassion, and indifference is an intermediate devotee.

children.text: arcāyām eva haraye pūjāṃ yaḥ śraddhayehate
children.translated_text: One who, with faith, undertakes worship of <s>Hari</s> only in the image,

children.text: na tadbhakteṣu cānyeṣu sa bhaktaḥ prākṛtaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but not toward his devotees or toward others, is remembered as a material, ordinary devotee.

children.text: gṛhītvāpīndriyair arthān yo na dveṣṭi na hṛṣyati
children.translated_text: Even while receiving objects through the senses, one who neither hates nor rejoices,

children.text: viṣṇor māyām idaṃ paśyan sa vai bhāgavatottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing this as the <s>māyā</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, that one indeed is the best of the <s>bhāgavatas</s>.
One who is not bewildered by birth, death, hunger, fear, thirst, and hardships belonging to body, senses, life-breath, mind, and intellect,
by the conditions of saṃsāra, because of remembrance of <s>Hari</s>, is foremost among the <s>bhāgavatas</s>.
In whose mind no arising of the seeds of desire and action occurs,
whose sole abode is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, that one indeed is the best of the <s>bhāgavatas</s>.
In whom, because of birth or actions, or because of class, life-stage, or caste,

children.text: sajjate 'sminn ahambhāvo dehe vai sa hareḥ priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: no sense of 'I' attaches to this body, that one indeed is dear to <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: na yasya svaḥ para iti vitteṣv ātmani vā bhidā
children.translated_text: For whom there is no division, 'mine' and 'another's,' either in possessions or in the self,
who is equal toward all beings and peaceful, that one indeed is the best of the <s>bhāgavatas</s>.
One who, even for the prosperity of the three worlds, does not move from the lotus feet of the Blessed Lord, sought by the gods and others whose selves are unconquered, his memory unimpeded,

children.text: na calati bhagavatpadāravindāl lavanimiṣārdham api yaḥ sa vaiṣṇavāgryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: not even for half the blink of an eye, is the foremost <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.
For one in whose heart the heat has been removed by the moonlight of the jewel-like nails on the branches of the Blessed Lord's feet of mighty stride,

children.text: hṛdi katham upasīdatāṃ punaḥ sa prabhavati candra ivodite 'rkatāpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how can burning pain again settle there? How can the sun's heat prevail when the moon has risen?

children.text: visṛjati hṛdayaṃ na yasya sākṣāddharir avaśābhihito 'py aghaughanāśaḥ
children.translated_text: One whose heart <s>Hari</s> does not leave, though directly named even involuntarily, he who destroys the mass of sins,

children.text: praṇayaraśanayā dhṛtāṅghripadmaḥ sa bhavati bhāgavatapradhāna uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose lotus feet are held by the cord of affection, is said to be foremost among the <s>bhāgavatas</s>.
The revered king said:

children.text: parasya viṣṇor īśasya māyinām api mohinīm
children.translated_text: We wish to know the <s>māyā</s> of the supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord,

children.text: māyāṃ veditum icchāmo bhagavanto bruvantu naḥ ||
children.translated_text: which bewilders even the possessors of <s>māyā</s>; venerable ones, please tell us.
I am not satisfied while enjoying your words, the nectar of stories of <s>Hari</s>;
a mortal, scorched by the heat of saṃsāra, finds in them the medicine for that burning.
The revered <s>Antarikṣa</s> said:
With these great elements, O mighty-armed one, the primordial soul of beings
created beings, high and low, for the manifestation of himself through his own measures.
Having entered the beings thus created with the five elements,
he enjoys the qualities, dividing himself as one and as ten.

children.text: guṇair guṇān sa bhuñjāna ātmapradyotitaiḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: That Lord, enjoying the qualities through the qualities illuminated by himself,

children.text: manyamāna idaṃ sṛṣṭam ātmānam iha sajjate ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'This created thing is myself,' becomes attached here.
The embodied being, performing actions by means of actions together with their causes,

children.text: tat tat karmaphalaṃ gṛhṇan bhramatīha sukhetaram ||
children.translated_text: receives the particular fruit of each action and wanders here through pleasure and what is other than pleasure.
Thus, going along paths of karma that bring much misfortune, a person,
helplessly experiences creation and dissolution until the destruction of beings.
When the disturbance of the elements is near, manifest reality, consisting of substance and qualities,
is drawn back into the unmanifest by time, which has no beginning or end.

children.text: śatavarṣā hy anāvṛṣṭir bhaviṣyaty ulbaṇā bhuvi
children.translated_text: There will be a terrible drought on earth for a hundred years;
the sun, grown hot by that time, will scorch the three worlds.
Beginning from the surface of <s>Pātāla</s>, the fire from the mouth of <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>
burns upward with its flame and grows in every direction, driven by the wind.

children.text: saṃvartako meghagaṇo varṣati sma śataṃ samāḥ
children.translated_text: The host of clouds of dissolution rains for a hundred years,
with streams like elephant trunks, and the cosmic body is dissolved in the water.

children.text: tato virājam utsṛjya vairājaḥ puruṣo nṛpa
children.translated_text: Then, abandoning the cosmic body, O king, the <s>Vairāja</s> person
enters the subtle unmanifest, like fire without fuel.
The earth, with its smell removed by wind, is prepared to become water;
that water, with its taste removed, is prepared to become fire.

children.text: hṛtarūpaṃ tu tamasā vāyau jyotiḥ pralīyate
children.translated_text: Fire, with its form removed by darkness, is dissolved into wind;
wind, with its touch removed by space, is dissolved into the sky;
and the sky, with its qualities removed by time as the self, is dissolved into the self.

children.text: indriyāṇi mano buddhiḥ saha vaikārikair nṛpa
children.translated_text: The senses, mind, and intellect, together with the modifications born of the vaikārika principle, O king,

children.text: praviśanti hy ahaṃkāraṃ svaguṇair aham ātmani ||
children.translated_text: enter into ahaṃkāra along with their qualities, and ahaṃkāra enters the self.
This is the <s>māyā</s> of the Blessed Lord, which brings about creation, maintenance, and end;

children.text: trivarṇā varṇitāsmābhiḥ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: we have described it as three-colored. What more do you wish to hear?
The revered king said:
How do even gross-minded people easily cross this divine <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: taranty añjaḥ sthūladhiyo maharṣa idam ucyatām ||
children.translated_text: so hard to cross for those whose selves are unprepared? O great seer, please tell this.
The revered <s>Prabuddha</s> said:
One should see, among people joined in sexual life, the reversal of the result
of actions begun for the destruction of suffering and for happiness.
With wealth, which constantly gives pain, is hard to obtain, and is death to the self,
what delight is there in houses, children, relatives, and cattle, which are gained only with effort and are unstable?

children.text: evaṃ lokaṃ param vidyān naśvaraṃ karmanirmitam
children.translated_text: Thus one should know the higher world too to be perishable, made by karma,
subject to equality, superiority, and destruction, just like the worlds of those who dwell within the cosmic sphere.

children.text: tasmād guruṃ prapadyeta jijñāsuḥ śreya uttamam
children.translated_text: Therefore one who desires to know the highest good should take refuge in a guru,

children.text: śābde pare ca niṣṇātaṃ brahmaṇy upaśamāśrayam ||
children.translated_text: one deeply versed in scripture and in the supreme, grounded in quietude in <s>brahman</s>.
There one should learn the <s>Bhāgavata</s> dharmas from the guru, regarding him as self and deity,
with sincere service, by which <s>Hari</s>, the self and giver of the self, is pleased.

children.text: sarvato manaso 'saṅgam ādau saṅgaṃ ca sādhuṣu
children.translated_text: First, detachment of the mind from everything, and attachment to the good;

children.text: dayāṃ maitrīṃ praśrayaṃ ca bhūteṣv addhā yathocitam ||
children.translated_text: compassion, friendship, and humility toward beings, truly and as is appropriate;

children.text: śaucaṃ tapas titikṣāṃ ca maunaṃ svādhyāyam ārjavam
children.translated_text: purity, austerity, forbearance, silence, recitation of sacred texts, straightforwardness,
celibacy, non-violence, and evenness toward what are called the pairs of opposites;
seeing the self and the Lord everywhere, solitude, homelessness,
wearing simple garments in a secluded place, and contentment with whatever comes;

children.text: śraddhāṃ bhāgavate śāstre 'nindām anyatra cāpi hi
children.translated_text: faith in the <s>Bhāgavata</s> scripture, and also non-censure elsewhere
restraint of mind, speech, and action, truthfulness, tranquility, and self-control as well;
hearing, chanting, and meditation on <s>Hari</s>, whose deeds are wondrous,
and on his births, deeds, and qualities, and every undertaking for his sake;

children.text: iṣṭaṃ dattaṃ tapo japtaṃ vṛttaṃ yac cātmanaḥ priyam
children.translated_text: whatever has been sacrificed, given, practiced as austerity, or recited, whatever conduct and whatever is dear to oneself,

children.text: dārān sutān gṛhān prāṇān yat parasmai nivedanam ||
children.translated_text: one's wife, sons, homes, and very life: offering all that to the Supreme;
in this way, friendship toward those for whom <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is self and lord, and also toward human beings,
and service in both cases, toward the great, toward men, and toward the good;
mutual narration among themselves of the purifying fame of the Blessed One,

children.text: mitho ratir mithas tuṣṭir nivṛttir mitha ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: mutual delight, mutual satisfaction, and mutual release of the self;
remembering and reminding one another of <s>Hari</s>, who destroys the mass of sins,

children.text: bhaktyā saṃjātayā bhaktyā bibhraty utpulakāṃ tanum ||
children.translated_text: by devotion born from devotion they bear bodies with hair standing on end.

children.text: kvacid rudanty acyutacintayā kvaciddhasanti nandanti vadanty alaukikāḥ
children.translated_text: At times they weep from thought of <s>Acyuta</s>; at times, being otherworldly, they laugh, rejoice, and speak;

children.text: nṛtyanti gāyanty anuśīlayanty ajaṃ bhavanti tūṣṇīṃ param etya nirvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they dance, sing, and continually contemplate the unborn one; then, attaining the supreme, they become silent and fulfilled.

children.text: iti bhāgavatān dharmān śikṣan bhaktyā tadutthayā
children.translated_text: Thus, learning the <s>dharmas</s> (ways of conduct) of the devotees with the devotion that arises from them,
one who is devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> easily crosses over <s>māyā</s>, which is hard to cross.
The revered king said:
You are worthy to tell us the fixed nature of the supreme self, brahman,

children.text: niṣṭhām arhatha no vaktuṃ yūyaṃ hi brahmavittamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: which bears the name <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, for you are the foremost knowers of brahman.
The revered <s>Pippalāyana</s> said:
Know that, O lord of men, to be the supreme: the cause of the continuance, arising, and dissolution of this world, yet itself without cause;
that which exists in dream, waking, and deep sleep, and outside them as well;
that by which bodies, senses, vital breaths, and hearts,
being brought to life, move.

children.text: naitan mano viśati vāg uta cakṣur ātmā
children.translated_text: The mind does not enter this, nor speech, nor even the eye, the self,
nor the vital breath and the senses, just as sparks do not enter their own fire.
Even sacred sound speaks of the root of self through indication and negation;
it states the intended meaning, for without that, negation could not be established.

children.text: sattvaṃ rajas tama iti trivṛd ekam ādau
children.translated_text: Sattva, rajas, and tamas: this threefold principle is one in the beginning;

children.text: sūtraṃ mahān aham iti pravadanti jīvam
children.translated_text: as <s>sūtra</s>, the great principle, and ego, they describe the living being.
Because it has the forms of knowledge, action, objects, and their results, and possesses vast power,

children.text: brahmaiva bhāti sad asac ca tayoḥ paraṃ yat ||
children.translated_text: brahman alone appears as both being and non-being, while that which is beyond them is higher.

children.text: nātmā jajāna na mariṣyati naidhate 'sau na kṣīyate savanavid vyabhicāriṇāṃ hi
children.translated_text: The self was not born, will not die, does not grow, and does not decay; it is the knower of the changing states.

children.text: sarvatra śaśvad anapāyy upalabdhimātraṃ prāṇo yathendriyabalena vikalpitaṃ sat ||
children.translated_text: Everywhere, always, undecaying, it is mere awareness, though designated as the vital breath through the power of the senses.

children.text: aṇḍeṣu peśīṣu taruṣv aviniściteṣu prāṇo hi jīvam upadhāvati tatra tatra
children.translated_text: In eggs, embryos, trees, and indistinct forms, the vital principle pursues the living being here and there.

children.text: sanne yad indriyagaṇe 'hami ca prasupte kūṭastha āśayam ṛte tadanusmṛtir naḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the group of senses is stilled and the 'I' is asleep, the changeless one remains; without that abiding basis there would be no later memory for us.
When, through intense devotion in the quest for the lotus-naveled Lord's feet, one shakes off the impurities of the mind born of qualities and actions,

children.text: tasmin viśuddha upalabhyata ātmatattvaṃ sākṣād yathāmaladṛśoḥ savitṛprakāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, when the mind is purified, the truth of the self is directly perceived, just as the light of the sun is seen by stainless eyes.
The revered king said:

children.text: karmayogaṃ vadata naḥ puruṣo yena saṃskṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Tell us of <s>karmayoga</s> (the discipline of action), by which a person, refined,
quickly casts off actions here and attains the supreme state beyond action.

children.text: evaṃ praśnam ṛṣīn pūrvam apṛcchaṃ pitur antike
children.translated_text: I formerly asked the seers this question in my father's presence,

children.text: nābruvan brahmaṇaḥ putrās tatra kāraṇam ucyatām ||
children.translated_text: but the sons of <s>Brahmā</s> did not answer; please tell the reason for that.
The revered <s>Āvirhotra</s> said:
Action, non-action, and wrong action are matters of Vedic teaching, not of ordinary worldly discourse.
Because the Veda has the Lord as its self, even wise men are bewildered in this matter.
This Veda speaks indirectly, an instruction for the immature;

children.text: karmamokṣāya karmāṇi vidhatte hy agadaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of release from action it enjoins actions, just as one uses a medicine.

children.text: nācared yas tu vedoktaṃ svayam ajño 'jitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: But one who is himself ignorant and has not conquered his senses, and does not perform what is stated in the Veda,

children.text: vikarmaṇā hy adharmeṇa mṛtyor mṛtyum upaiti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: goes, through wrong action and unrighteousness, from death to death.
Doing only what is stated in the Veda, without attachment and offering it to the Lord,
one attains perfection beyond action; statements of reward are for making it attractive.
One who wishes quickly to cut out the knot of the heart belonging to the supreme self
should, according to rule and according to the teaching of the tantra, worship the god <s>Keśava</s>.
Having received grace from the teacher and being shown the sacred procedure by him,
one should worship the Great Person in an image agreeable to oneself.
Pure, seated facing the image, by breath-control and the other practices,
having purified the body and made protection by renunciation, one should worship.
In the image and also in the heart, with such means of service as have been obtained,
having prepared the substances, the ground, and the personal emblems, and having sprinkled the seat,
then, having arranged water for washing the feet and the other offerings, and having established the deity's presence with concentration,
having performed the placements beginning with the heart, one should worship with the root mantra.

children.text: sāṅgopāṅgāṃ sapārṣadāṃ tāṃ tāṃ mūrtiṃ svamantrataḥ
children.translated_text: Each chosen form, together with its major and minor limbs and with its attendants, by its own mantra,
with water for the feet, arghya, water for sipping, and so on, with bathing, garments, and ornaments,
with sandal paste, garlands, unbroken grains, wreaths, incense, lamps, and offerings,

children.text: sāṅgam sampūjya vidhivat stavaiḥ stutvā nameddharim ||
children.translated_text: having worshiped it fully and according to rule, one should praise <s>Hari</s> with hymns and bow down.
Meditating on oneself as made of him, one should thoroughly worship the image of <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: śeṣam ādhāya śirasā svadhāmny udvāsya satkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: placing the remainder upon one's head, one should respectfully dismiss him to his own abode.

children.text: evam agnyarkatoyādāv atithau hṛdaye ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in fire, the sun, water, and the like, in a guest, and in the heart,

children.text: yajatīśvaram ātmānam acirān mucyate hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever worships the Lord as the self is indeed liberated before long.
The revered king said:

children.text: yāni yānīha karmāṇi yair yaiḥ svacchandajanmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever deeds here, by whatever spontaneous births,

children.text: cakre karoti kartā vā haris tāni bruvantu naḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> has done, does, or will do as agent, please tell those to us.
The revered <s>Drumila</s> said:

children.text: yo vā anantasya guṇān anantān anukramiṣyan sa tu bālabuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever intends to recount in order the endless qualities of the endless one has the understanding of a child.

children.text: rajāṃsi bhūmer gaṇayet kathaṃcit kālena naivākhilaśaktidhāmnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Somehow, in time, one might count the particles of dust of the earth, but not the qualities of him who is the abode of all powers.
When, with the five elements created by himself,
Having fashioned the city-body called <s>Virāj</s>,
and having entered it with his own portion, under the designation <s>Puruṣa</s>,
the primal god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> attained that name.

children.text: yatkāya eṣa bhuvanatrayasaṃniveśo yasyendriyais tanubhṛtām ubhayendriyāṇi
children.translated_text: In whose body this arrangement of the three worlds exists, and by whose senses the two kinds of senses of embodied beings exist,

children.text: jñānaṃ svataḥ śvasanato balam oja īhā sattvādibhiḥ sthitilayodbhava ādikartā ||
children.translated_text: from whom knowledge arises of itself, and from whose breathing come strength, vigor, and activity; through sattva and the other qualities he is the first agent of maintenance, dissolution, and origination.

children.text: ādāv abhūc chatadhṛtī rajasāsya sarge viṣṇuḥ sthitau kratupatir dvijadharmasetuḥ
children.translated_text: At the beginning <s>Śatadhṛti</s> came into being through rajas for his creation; in maintenance he is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of sacrifice and bridge of the dharma of twice-born people;

children.text: rudro 'pyayāya tamasā puruṣaḥ sa ādya ity udbhavasthitilayāḥ satataṃ prajāsu ||
children.translated_text: and for dissolution he is <s>Rudra</s> through tamas. He is that primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>; thus arising, maintenance, and dissolution continually occur among creatures.

children.text: dharmasya dakṣaduhitary ajaniṣṭa mūrtyāṃ nārāyaṇo nara ṛṣipravaraḥ praśāntaḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Dharma</s>, in <s>Mūrti</s>, the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, were born <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Nara</s>, the foremost seers, peaceful in nature.

children.text: naiṣkarmyalakṣaṇam uvāca cacāra karma yo 'dyāpi cāsta ṛṣivaryaniṣevitāṅghriḥ ||
children.translated_text: He taught action whose mark is freedom from action, and he practiced action; even today he remains, his feet served by the best of seers.
<s>Indra</s>, suspecting, 'He wishes to seize my domain,'
appointed <s>Kāma</s> with his retinue to go to the place called <s>Badarī</s>.
Going there with hosts of apsarases, springtime, and gentle winds,
he pierced him with the arrows of women's glances, not knowing his greatness.
Recognizing the improper act done by <s>Śakra</s>, the primal god
laughed and spoke to them, trembling and freed from their pride:

children.text: mā bhair vibho madana māruta devavadhvo gṛhṇīta no balim aśūnyam imaṃ kurudhvam ||
children.translated_text: 'Do not be afraid, mighty <s>Madana</s>, <s>Māruta</s>, and heavenly women. Accept our offering and make this place not empty.'

children.text: itthaṃ bruvaty abhayade naradeva devāḥ savrīḍanamraśirasaḥ saghṛṇaṃ tam ūcuḥ
children.translated_text: When the divine <s>Nara</s>, giver of fearlessness, spoke thus, the gods bowed their heads in bashful humility and spoke to him with remorse:

children.text: naitad vibho tvayi pare 'vikṛte vicitraṃ svārāmadhīranikarānatapādapadme ||
children.translated_text: 'This is not astonishing in you, mighty lord, supreme and unchanging, at whose lotus feet multitudes of self-delighting sages bow.
For those who serve you there are many obstacles made by the gods,

children.text: svauko vilaṅghya paramaṃ vrajatāṃ padaṃ te
children.translated_text: as they pass beyond the gods' own abodes and go to your supreme station.
But for another, who offers bali-obligations on the sacred grass and gives them their own shares,

children.text: dhatte padaṃ tvam avitā yadi vighnamūrdhni ||
children.translated_text: no obstacle gains a foothold, if you, the protector, set your foot on the head of obstruction.
Some cross over us, boundless oceans born of hunger, thirst, the three times, the qualities, wind, tongue, and genitals,
crossing those immeasurable seas;

children.text: krodhasya yānti viphalasya vaśaṃ pade gor majjanti duścaratapaś ca vṛthotsṛjanti ||
children.translated_text: yet they fall under the power of fruitless anger in a cow's hoofprint, sink there, and abandon difficult austerity in vain.'
While they praised him in this way, the Lord showed women of utterly wondrous appearance,
self-created women who were performing service.

children.text: te devānucarā dṛṣṭvā striyaḥ śrīr iva rūpiṇīḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing those women, like embodied <s>Śrī</s>, the attendants of the gods
became bewildered by their fragrance, their own splendor humbled by those women's beauty and nobility.

children.text: tān āha devadeveśaḥ praṇatān prahasann iva
children.translated_text: The lord of the lords of gods said to them, as they bowed, smiling as it were:
'Choose one of these, one of your own kind, an ornament of heaven.'

children.text: oṃ ity ādeśam ādāya natvā taṃ suravandinaḥ
children.translated_text: Saying 'Om,' accepting his command, and bowing to him, the divine attendants
went to heaven, placing <s>Urvaśī</s>, the best of apsarases, in front.
Bowing to <s>Indra</s> in his assembly, while the inhabitants of heaven listened,
they told of the power of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; <s>Śakra</s> was frightened and amazed.

children.text: haṃsasvarūpy avadad acyuta ātmayogaṃ dattaḥ kumāra ṛṣabho bhagavān pitā naḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s> taught the yoga of the self; as <s>Datta</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, and <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, the Blessed Lord, our father, appeared.

children.text: viṣṇuḥ śivāya jagatāṃ kalayāvatīrṇas tenāhṛtā madhubhidā śrutayo hayāsye ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> descended by a portion for the welfare of the worlds; as <s>Hayāsya</s>, the slayer of <s>Madhu</s> recovered the Vedas.

children.text: gupto 'pyaye manur ilauṣadhayaś ca mātsye krauḍe hato ditija uddharatāmbhasaḥ kṣmām
