children.translated_text: As the fish, he protected <s>Manu</s>, the earth, and the herbs at the dissolution; as the boar, lifting the earth from the waters, he slew the son of <s>Diti</s>.

children.text: kaurme dhṛto 'drir amṛtonmathane svapṛṣṭhe grāhāt prapannam ibharājam amuñcad ārtam ||
children.translated_text: As the tortoise, he held the mountain on his back during the churning for nectar; he released the distressed elephant king from the crocodile when it sought refuge.

children.text: saṃstunvato nipatitān śramaṇān ṛṣīṃś ca śakraṃ ca vṛtravadhatas tamasi praviṣṭam
children.translated_text: He protected the fallen ascetics and seers who praised him, and <s>Śakra</s>, who after killing <s>Vṛtra</s> had entered darkness.

children.text: devastriyo 'suragṛhe pihitā anāthā jaghne 'surendram abhayāya satāṃ nṛsiṃhe ||
children.translated_text: He rescued the helpless wives of the gods shut in the asura's house; as <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> he slew the lord of asuras for the fearlessness of the good.

children.text: devāsure yudhi ca daityapatīn surārthe hatvāntareṣu bhuvanāny adadhāt kalābhiḥ
children.translated_text: In the war between gods and asuras, he killed the lords of the daityas for the gods' sake, and in the intervals between Manus he upheld the worlds by his portions.

children.text: bhūtvātha vāmana imām aharad baleḥ kṣmāṃ yācñāc chalena samadād aditeḥ sutebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, becoming <s>Vāmana</s>, he took this earth from <s>Bali</s> by the device of begging and gave it to the sons of <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: niḥkṣatriyām akṛta gāṃ ca triḥsaptakṛtvo rāmas tu haihayakulāpyayabhārgavāgniḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, the Bhārgava fire that consumed the <s>Haihaya</s> line, made the earth devoid of kṣatriyas twenty-one times.

children.text: so 'bdhiṃ babandha daśavaktram ahan salaṅkaṃ sītāpatir jayati lokamalaghnakīrtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He bridged the ocean and slew the ten-faced one together with <s>Laṅkā</s>; the husband of <s>Sītā</s> is victorious, his fame removing the world's impurity.

children.text: bhūmer bharāvataraṇāya yaduṣv ajanmā jātaḥ kariṣyati surair api duṣkarāṇi
children.translated_text: For the removal of earth's burden, the unborn one, born among the <s>Yadus</s>, will perform deeds difficult even for the gods.

children.text: vādair vimohayati yajñakṛto 'tadarhān śūdrān kalau kṣitibhujo nyahaniṣyad ante ||
children.translated_text: By doctrines he will bewilder unworthy sacrificers; at the end, in the Kali age, he will kill śūdra rulers.
Such births and deeds of the lord of the world,
many indeed, of him of abundant fame, have been described, O mighty-armed one.
The revered king said:

children.text: bhagavantaṃ hariṃ prāyo na bhajanty ātmavittamāḥ
children.translated_text: O best knowers of the self, why do people generally not worship the Blessed <s>Hari</s>?
What is the end of those whose desires are unpacified and whose selves are unconquered?
The revered <s>Camasa</s> said:
From the mouth, arms, thighs, and feet of the <s>Puruṣa</s>, together with the āśramas,

children.text: catvāro jajñire varṇā guṇair viprādayaḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: the four varṇas were born, the brāhmaṇas and the others distinguished separately by their qualities.

children.text: ya eṣāṃ puruṣaṃ sākṣād ātmaprabhavam īśvaram
children.translated_text: Those among them who do not worship the <s>Puruṣa</s> directly, the Lord born from the self,

children.text: na bhajanty avajānanti sthānād bhraṣṭāḥ patanty adhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who treat him with contempt, fall down from their station and descend below.
Some are far from stories of <s>Hari</s> and far from the singing of <s>Acyuta</s>'s glory;
women, śūdras, and the like are therefore to be shown compassion by people such as you.

children.text: vipro rājanyavaiśyau vā hareḥ prāptāḥ padāntikam
children.translated_text: A brāhmaṇa, a rājanya, or a vaiśya, though brought near the feet of <s>Hari</s>
by birth sanctioned by śruti, nevertheless becomes deluded as a mere proclaimer of sacred tradition.
Unskilled in action, proud, foolish, and thinking themselves learned,

children.text: vadanti cāṭukān mūḍhā yayā mādhvyā girotsukāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those fools speak flattering words, eager for honeyed speech.
Driven by rajas, with terrible designs, lustful, and wrathful like serpents,
The hypocritical, arrogant, sinful men laugh at those dear to <s>Acyuta</s>.

children.text: vadanti te 'nyonyam upāsitastriyo gṛheṣu maithunyapareṣu cāśiṣaḥ
children.translated_text: They speak among one another, with women courted in houses devoted to sexual union, and they offer blessings.

children.text: yajanty asṛṣṭānnavidhānadakṣiṇaṃ vṛttyai paraṃ ghnanti paśūn atadvidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ignorant of the real meaning, they sacrifice only for livelihood, killing animals in rites where the provisions of food and gifts are not properly ordained.

children.text: śriyā vibhūtyābhijanena vidyayā tyāgena rūpeṇa balena karmaṇā
children.translated_text: By fortune, power, birth, learning, renunciation, beauty, strength, and action,
the wicked, blinded in mind by pride at birth, despise the good who are dear to <s>Hari</s>, together with the Lord.

children.text: sarveṣu śaśvat tanubhṛtsv avasthitaṃ yathā kham ātmānam abhīṣṭam īśvaram
children.translated_text: The fools do not listen to the self, the desired Lord, who is eternally present in all embodied beings like space,

children.text: vedopagītaṃ ca na śṛṇvate 'budhā manorathānāṃ pravadanti vārttayā ||
children.translated_text: and who is sung by the Vedas; instead, in ordinary talk they proclaim the objects of their own fantasies.

children.text: loke vyavāyāmiṣamadyasevā nityā hi jantor na hi tatra codanā
children.translated_text: In the world, sexual intercourse, meat, and liquor are natural for living beings; there is no need for an injunction there.

children.text: vyavasthitis teṣu vivāhayajña surāgrahair āsu nivṛttir iṣṭā ||
children.translated_text: Regulation concerning them is made through marriage, sacrifice, and the taking of liquor; in these matters cessation is what is desired.

children.text: dhanaṃ ca dharmaikaphalaṃ yato vai jñānaṃ savijñānam anupraśānti
children.translated_text: Wealth, indeed, has <s>dharma</s> as its sole fruit, and from that come knowledge, realized knowledge, and subsequent peace.

children.text: gṛheṣu yuñjanti kalevarasya mṛtyuṃ na paśyanti durantavīryam ||
children.translated_text: But they apply it to households and the body, and they do not see death, whose power is hard to overcome.

children.text: yad ghrāṇabhakṣo vihitaḥ surāyās tathā paśor ālabhanaṃ na hiṃsā
children.translated_text: What is prescribed for liquor is smelling it, and likewise the ritual touching of an animal is not violence.

children.text: evaṃ vyavāyaḥ prajayā na ratyā imaṃ viśuddhaṃ na viduḥ svadharmam ||
children.translated_text: So too sexual union is for offspring, not for pleasure; they do not know this pure <s>svadharma</s>.
But those who do not understand in this way, the unreal, obstinate men who think themselves good,

children.text: paśūn druhyanti viśrabdhāḥ pretya khādanti te ca tān ||
children.translated_text: harm animals without fear; after death those animals eat them in turn.
Hating <s>Hari</s>, the Lord, their own self, in the bodies of others,
and bound by affection for this dead body and what is connected with it, they fall downward.

children.text: ye kaivalyam asaṃprāptā ye cātītāś ca mūḍhatām
children.translated_text: Those who have not attained <s>kaivalya</s>, and those who have gone beyond mere foolishness,

children.text: traivargikā hy akṣaṇikā ātmānaṃ ghātayanti te ||
children.translated_text: but are devoted to the three aims, being inattentive, destroy themselves.
These self-slayers, unpeaceful and ignorant while thinking themselves wise,
sink down, having failed to do what was to be done, their hopes shattered by time.
Abandoning houses, children, friends, and wives fashioned by the māyā of the self,
those turned away from <s>Vāsudeva</s> enter darkness against their will.
The revered king said:

children.text: kasmin kāle sa bhagavān kiṃ varṇaḥ kīdṛśo nṛbhiḥ
children.translated_text: At what time is that Blessed Lord worshiped by men, of what color and what form,

children.text: nāmnā vā kena vidhinā pūjyate tad ihocyatām ||
children.translated_text: by what name, and by what method? Please tell that here.
The revered <s>Karabhājana</s> said:

children.text: kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kalir ity eṣu keśavaḥ
children.translated_text: In these ages called <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s>, <s>Keśava</s>
has various colors, names, and forms, and is worshiped by various methods.
In the <s>Kṛta</s> age he is white, four-armed, with matted hair and clothed in bark garments,
bearing a black-antelope skin, sacred thread, rosary beads, staff, and water pot.

children.text: manuṣyās tu tadā śāntā nirvairāḥ suhṛdaḥ samāḥ
children.translated_text: People then are peaceful, free from enmity, friendly, and equal-minded;

children.text: yajanti tapasā devaṃ śamena ca damena ca ||
children.translated_text: they worship the god through austerity, tranquility, and self-restraint.
He is sung as <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Suparṇa</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Yogeśvara</s>, <s>Amala</s>,
<s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Avyakta</s>, and <s>Paramātman</s>.
In the <s>Tretā</s> age he is red in color, four-armed, with three girdles,
golden-haired, the embodiment of the three Vedas, and recognizable by ladles such as the sruk and sruva.

children.text: taṃ tadā manujā devaṃ sarvadevamayaṃ harim
children.translated_text: At that time righteous men, speakers of <s>brahman</s>,
worship him, the god <s>Hari</s> who contains all the gods, by the knowledge of the three Vedas.
He is called <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Yajña</s>, <s>Pṛśnigarbha</s>, <s>Sarvadeva</s>, <s>Urukrama</s>,
<s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, and <s>Urugāya</s>.
In <s>Dvāpara</s> the Blessed Lord is dark, wearing yellow garments and bearing his own weapons,
marked by emblems such as the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and by other distinguishing marks.
At that time, O king, mortals who seek to know the supreme
worship him, the Person bearing the marks of a great king, by both Veda and Tantra.

children.text: namas te vāsudevāya namaḥ saṃkarṣaṇāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to you, <s>Vāsudeva</s>; homage also to <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>;
homage to <s>Pradyumna</s> and <s>Aniruddha</s>; homage to you, the Blessed Lord.
Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the seer, the Person, the great-souled one,
to the Lord of the universe, the universe itself, the self of all beings.
Thus, O lord of the earth, in <s>Dvāpara</s> they praise the Lord of the world;
now hear how, in the same way, he is worshiped in <s>Kali</s> by the ordinances of many tantras.
Those of good understanding worship him who is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> by designation but not dark in luster, accompanied by his limbs, subsidiary limbs, weapons, and attendants,
through sacrifices chiefly consisting of <s>saṃkīrtana</s>.

children.text: dhyeyaṃ sadā paribhavaghnam abhīṣṭadohaṃ tīrthāspadaṃ śivaviriñcinutaṃ śaraṇyam
children.translated_text: Always to be meditated upon, destroyer of humiliation, fulfiller of desires, abode of sacred places, praised by <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Viriñci</s>, refuge,

children.text: bhṛtyārtihaṃ praṇatapāla bhavābdhipotaṃ vande mahāpuruṣa te caraṇāravindam ||
children.translated_text: remover of servants' distress, protector of the surrendered, boat across the ocean of becoming: O <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>, I worship your lotus feet.

children.text: tyaktvā sudustyajasurepsitarājyalakṣmīṃ dharmiṣṭha āryavacasā yad agād araṇyam
children.translated_text: You abandoned royal fortune, desired by the gods and very hard to abandon, and, most righteous, went to the forest because of the word of a noble one;

children.text: māyāmṛgaṃ dayitayepsitam anvadhāvad vande mahāpuruṣa te caraṇāravindam ||
children.translated_text: you pursued the illusory deer desired by your beloved. O <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>, I worship your lotus feet.
Thus, in forms appropriate to each age, the Blessed Lord,

children.text: manujair ijyate rājan śreyasām īśvaro hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: the master of all blessings, <s>Hari</s>, is worshiped by men living in each age, O king.
Noble people, knowers of qualities and graspers of the essence, honor <s>Kali</s>,
for in it every purpose of the self is obtained by <s>saṃkīrtana</s> alone.

children.text: na hy ataḥ paramo lābho dehināṃ bhrāmyatām iha
children.translated_text: There is no higher gain than this for embodied beings wandering here:

children.text: yato vindeta paramāṃ śāntiṃ naśyati saṃsṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: from it one obtains supreme peace, and worldly transmigration comes to an end.

children.text: kṛtādiṣu prajā rājan kalāv icchanti sambhavam
children.translated_text: O king, people in the ages beginning with <s>Kṛta</s> desire birth in <s>Kali</s>;
indeed, in <s>Kali</s> there will be people wholly devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: kvacit kvacin mahārāja draviḍeṣu ca bhūriśaḥ
children.translated_text: Here and there, O great king, and especially among the <s>Draviḍas</s>,
where the rivers <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, <s>Kṛtamālā</s>, and <s>Payasvinī</s> flow,

children.text: kāverī ca mahāpuṇyā pratīcī ca mahānadī
children.translated_text: and the very holy <s>Kāverī</s> and the great river <s>Pratīcī</s>,

children.text: ye pibanti jalaṃ tāsāṃ manujā manujeśvara
children.translated_text: the people who drink their waters, O lord of men,
are mostly devotees of the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, pure in intention.

children.text: devarṣibhūtāptanṛṇāṃ pitṝṇāṃ na kiṃkaro nāyam ṛṇī ca rājan
children.translated_text: O king, one who has gone with his whole being to <s>Mukunda</s>, the refuge-giving refuge, is not the servant of the gods, seers, beings, kinsmen, men, or ancestors, nor is he in their debt,

children.text: sarvātmanā yaḥ śaraṇaṃ śaraṇyaṃ gato mukundaṃ parihṛtya kartam ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned what is to be done.

children.text: svapādamūlam bhajataḥ priyasya tyaktānyabhāvasya hariḥ pareśaḥ
children.translated_text: For his dear devotee who worships the root of his feet and has abandoned all other dispositions, <s>Hari</s>, the supreme Lord,

children.text: vikarma yac cotpatitaṃ kathaṃcid dhunoti sarvaṃ hṛdi saṃniviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: dwelling within the heart, washes away whatever improper action has somehow arisen.
Revered <s>Nārada</s> said:
After hearing the <s>Bhāgavata</s> dharmas in this way, the lord of <s>Mithilā</s>,

children.text: jāyanteyān munīn prītaḥ sopādhyāyo hy apūjayat ||
children.translated_text: delighted, honored the sages born of <s>Jayantī</s>, together with his priests.
Then those perfected ones disappeared while the whole world looked on,

children.text: rājā dharmān upātiṣṭhann avāpa paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: and the king, practicing those dharmas, attained the supreme goal.

children.text: tvam apy etān mahābhāga dharmān bhāgavatān śrutān
children.translated_text: You too, O greatly fortunate one, having heard these <s>Bhāgavata</s> dharmas,

children.text: āsthitaḥ śraddhayā yukto niḥsaṅgo yāsyase param ||
children.translated_text: if you remain established in them, joined with faith and free from attachment, will go to the supreme.

children.text: yuvayoḥ khalu dampatyor yaśasā pūritaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Indeed, the world is filled with the fame of you two as a married pair,

children.text: putratām agamad yad vāṃ bhagavān īśvaro hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: because the Blessed Lord, the sovereign <s>Hari</s>, became your son.
Through seeing him, embracing him, speaking with him, lying down, sitting, and eating with him,

children.text: ātmā vāṃ pāvitaḥ kṛṣṇe putrasnehaṃ prakurvatoḥ ||
children.translated_text: your selves have been purified as you showed parental affection toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Kings such as <s>Śiśupāla</s>, <s>Pauṇḍra</s>, and <s>Śālva</s>, meditating on him through hostility, with minds fixed on his gait, play, glances, and the like,

children.text: dhyāyanta ākṛtadhiyaḥ śayanāsanādau tatsāmyam āpur anuraktadhiyāṃ punaḥ kim ||
children.translated_text: attained likeness to him while lying down, sitting, and so on; what, then, of those whose minds are lovingly attached?
Do not form the notion of offspring toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Lord who is the self of all,
the supreme imperishable one whose majesty is hidden by his appearance as a human through <s>māyā</s>.
The fame of him who descended to kill the asura-like kings burdening the earth and to protect the good,
and for the delight of all, is spread throughout the world.
Revered <s>Śuka</s> said:
Hearing this, the greatly fortunate <s>Vasudeva</s> was exceedingly amazed,

children.text: devakī ca mahābhāgā jahatur moham ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the greatly fortunate <s>Devakī</s> too cast off her own delusion.

children.text: itihāsam imaṃ puṇyaṃ dhārayed yaḥ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever, with concentrated mind, holds this sacred history,
after shaking off impurity here, becomes fit for the state of <s>brahman</s>.
Revered <s>Śuka</s> said:
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, surrounded by his sons, by the gods, and by the lords of creatures, approached,

children.text: bhavaś ca bhūtabhavyeśo yayau bhūtagaṇair vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Bhava</s>, lord of beings past and future, went surrounded by hosts of spirits.
Lord <s>Indra</s> came with the <s>Maruts</s>, as did the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>,

children.text: ṛbhavo 'ṅgiraso rudrā viśve sādhyāś ca devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and the <s>Viśve</s> and <s>Sādhya</s> deities.
The <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, and <s>Guhyakas</s>,
the seers and ancestors as well, together with the <s>Vidyādharas</s> and <s>Kiṃnaras</s>,
all went to <s>Dvārakā</s>, desiring to see <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
the Blessed Lord whose body was delightful to the world of men,
and whose fame he spread through the worlds, removing the impurity of every world.
In that city, shining and prosperous with great splendors,
they saw <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, wonderful to behold, with eyes that were not satisfied.
Covering the best of the <s>Yadus</s> with garlands brought from the gardens of heaven,
they praised the Lord of the universe with words rich in varied meanings.
The revered gods said:

children.text: natāḥ sma te nātha padāravindaṃ buddhīndriyaprāṇamanovacobhiḥ
children.translated_text: O Lord, we bow to your lotus feet with intellect, senses, life-breath, mind, and speech,

children.text: yac cintyate 'ntar hṛdi bhāvayuktair mumukṣubhiḥ karmamayorupāśāt ||
children.translated_text: which are contemplated within the heart by those filled with devotion and seeking liberation from the vast bond made of karma.

children.text: tvaṃ māyayā triguṇayātmani durvibhāvyaṃ vyaktaṃ sṛjasy avasi lumpasi tadguṇasthaḥ
children.translated_text: By your <s>māyā</s> consisting of the three guṇas, while standing within those qualities, you create, protect, and dissolve the manifest world that is hard to conceive within yourself;

children.text: naitair bhavān ajita karmabhir ajyate vai yat sve sukhe 'vyavahite 'bhirato 'navadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet you, O <s>Ajita</s>, are not stained at all by these actions, since you are absorbed in your own unobstructed bliss, O blameless one.

children.text: śuddhir nṛṇāṃ na tu tatheḍya durāśayānāṃ vidyāśrutādhyayanadānatapaḥkriyābhiḥ
children.translated_text: For men of corrupt intention, O praiseworthy one, purification does not come in that way through learning, sacred hearing, study, giving, austerity, and ritual acts,

children.text: sattvātmanām ṛṣabha te yaśasi pravṛddhasacchraddhayā śravaṇasambhṛtayā yathā syāt ||
children.translated_text: as it may for those whose self is sattva, O best one, through true faith that grows strong from hearing your fame.

children.text: syān nas tavāṅghrir aśubhāśayadhūmaketuḥ kṣemāya yo munibhir ārdrahṛdohyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: May your foot, the fire-banner that burns away inauspicious intention, be for our welfare, that foot which is borne by sages with softened hearts,

children.text: yaḥ sātvataiḥ samavibhūtaya ātmavadbhir vyūhe 'rcitaḥ savanaśaḥ svaratikramāya ||
children.translated_text: and which is worshiped at every pressing in the <s>vyūha</s> by the <s>Sātvatas</s>, who share equal splendor and regard all as themselves, for surpassing heaven.

children.text: yaś cintyate prayatapāṇibhir adhvarāgnau trayyā niruktavidhineśa havir gṛhītvā
children.translated_text: It is contemplated in the sacrificial fire by those with purified hands, following the rule of the three Vedas and the <s>Nirukta</s>, after they have received the oblation, O Lord;

children.text: adhyātmayoga uta yogibhir ātmamāyāṃ jijñāsubhiḥ paramabhāgavataiḥ parīṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, in the yoga of the self, it is supremely worshiped by yogins, the highest <s>Bhāgavatas</s>, who seek to know your self-<s>māyā</s>.

children.text: paryuṣṭayā tava vibho vanamālayeyaṃ saṃspardhinī bhagavatī pratipatnīvac chrīḥ
children.translated_text: O all-pervading Lord, this forest garland of yours, made fragrant by long wearing, rivals blessed <s>Śrī</s> like a co-wife;

children.text: yaḥ supraṇītam amuyārhaṇam ādadan no bhūyāt sadāṅghrir aśubhāśayadhūmaketuḥ ||
children.translated_text: may that foot, which accepted from us the worship well offered with it, always be the fire-banner that burns away inauspicious intention.

children.text: ketus trivikramayutas tripatatpatāko yas te bhayābhayakaro 'suradevacamvoḥ
children.translated_text: Your foot, whose emblem, joined with <s>Trivikrama</s>, became a banner flying over the three worlds, brings fear and fearlessness to the armies of asuras and gods;

children.text: svargāya sādhuṣu khaleṣv itarāya bhūman padaḥ punātu bhagavan bhajatām aghaṃ naḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the good it leads to heaven, for the wicked to the opposite; O Blessed Vast One, may that foot purify the sin of us who worship.

children.text: nasy otagāva iva yasya vaśe bhavanti brahmādayas tanubhṛto mithur ardyamānāḥ
children.translated_text: Embodied beings, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, are under your control like cattle with ropes through their noses, mutually tormented;

children.text: kālasya te prakṛtipūruṣayoḥ parasya śaṃ nas tanotu caraṇaḥ puruṣottamasya ||
children.translated_text: may the foot of you as Time, beyond <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, the foot of the Supreme Person, bring us welfare.

children.text: asyāsi hetur udayasthitisaṃyamānām avyaktajīvamahatām api kālam āhuḥ
children.translated_text: You are the cause of the arising, continuance, and restraint of this world, even of the unmanifest, the individual soul, and the great principle; they call you Time.

children.text: so 'yaṃ triṇābhir akhilāpacaye pravṛttaḥ kālo gabhīraraya uttamapūruṣas tvam ||
children.translated_text: This Time, with three hubs, engaged in the dissolution of all, moving with profound speed, is you, the Supreme Person.

children.text: tvattaḥ pumān samadhigamya yayāsya vīryaṃ dhatte mahāntam iva garbham amoghavīryaḥ
children.translated_text: From you the <s>puruṣa</s>, obtaining that power by which he, of unfailing seed, deposits the great principle as though an embryo,

children.text: so 'yaṃ tayānugata ātmana āṇḍakośaṃ haimaṃ sasarja bahir āvaraṇair upetam ||
children.translated_text: accompanied by her, created for himself this golden egg-shell, furnished outside with coverings.

children.text: tat tasthūṣaś ca jagataś ca bhavān adhīśo yan māyayotthaguṇavikriyayopanītān
children.translated_text: You are the overlord of what stands and what moves, of the world, whose forms are brought forth by transformations of the guṇas arisen from your <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: arthāñ juṣann api hṛṣīkapate na lipto ye 'nye svataḥ parihṛtād api bibhyati sma ||
children.translated_text: Though you enjoy objects, O <s>Hṛṣīkapati</s>, you are not tainted; others fear them even after they have themselves renounced them.
With sidelong glances and playful looks that displayed captivating emotions, and with eyebrows skilled in sending erotic spells,

children.text: patnyas tu ṣoḍaśasahasram anaṅgabāṇair yasyendriyaṃ vimathituṃ karaṇair na vibhvyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even the sixteen thousand wives, with the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> and their feminine charms, were unable to agitate his senses.

children.text: vibhvyas tavāmṛtakathodavahās trilokyāḥ pādāvanejasaritaḥ śamalāni hantum
children.translated_text: Powerful, O Lord, are the streams that bear the nectar of your stories, and the river that has washed your feet, for destroying the impurities of the three worlds.

children.text: ānuśravaṃ śrutibhir aṅghrijam aṅgasaṅgais tīrthadvayaṃ śuciṣadas ta upaspṛśanti ||
children.translated_text: The pure-hearted touch those two holy streams: the one born from your feet through bodily contact, and the one received through the ears from sacred tradition.
The venerable <s>Bādarāyaṇi</s> said:

children.text: ity abhiṣṭūya vibudhaiḥ seśaḥ śatadhṛtir harim
children.translated_text: Having thus praised <s>Hari</s> together with the gods, <s>Śatadhṛti</s>, accompanied by <s>Īśa</s>,
bowed to <s>Govinda</s> and, remaining in the sky, addressed him.
The venerable <s>Brahmā</s> said:
Long ago, O Lord, we appealed to you for the removal of the earth's burden;
O soul of all, that has been accomplished exactly so by you.

children.text: dharmaś ca sthāpitaḥ satsu satyasaṃdheṣu vai tvayā
children.translated_text: You have established <s>dharma</s> among the good, who are faithful to truth,
and your fame, which removes the stains of all worlds, has been spread through the directions.

children.text: avatīrya yador vaṃśe bibhrad rūpam anuttamam
children.translated_text: Descending into the lineage of <s>Yadu</s> and bearing an unsurpassed form,
you performed deeds of vast scope for the welfare of the world.

children.text: yāni te caritānīśa manuṣyāḥ sādhavaḥ kalau
children.translated_text: Those deeds of yours, O Lord, which virtuous people in the Kali age

children.text: śṛṇvantaḥ kīrtayantaś ca tariṣyanty añjasā tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will hear and proclaim, will easily carry them across darkness.
Since you descended in the <s>Yadu</s> lineage, O supreme person,
one hundred and twenty-five autumns have passed, O Lord.
Now, O foundation of all, no work of the gods remains unfinished for you,

children.text: kulaṃ ca vipraśāpena naṣṭaprāyam abhūd idam ||
children.translated_text: and this clan has become almost destroyed through the curse of the Brahmins.

children.text: tataḥ svadhāma paramaṃ viśasva yadi manyase
children.translated_text: Therefore enter your supreme abode, if you think it right,
and protect us, the guardians of the worlds together with our realms, as servants of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: avadhāritam etan me yad āttha vibudheśvara
children.translated_text: I have understood this that you say, O lord of the gods;

children.text: kṛtaṃ vaḥ kāryam akhilaṃ bhūmer bhāro 'vatāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all your work has been done, and the burden of the earth has been removed.
But this <s>Yādava</s> clan, swollen with strength, valor, and splendor,

children.text: lokaṃ jighṛkṣad ruddhaṃ me velayeva mahārṇavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: would seize the world; I have held it back like the shore restraining the great ocean.

children.text: yady asaṃhṛtya dṛptānāṃ yadūnāṃ vipulaṃ kulam
children.translated_text: If I go without destroying the vast clan of the arrogant <s>Yadus</s>,
this world will perish through that overflowing flood.
Now the destruction of the clan, born from the Brahmins' curse, has begun;
after this, O <s>Brahmā</s>, O blameless one, I shall go to my abode.
<s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: ity ukto lokanāthena svayambhūḥ praṇipatya tam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the Lord of the worlds, the self-born god bowed down to him,
and with the hosts of gods he went to his own abode.
Then the Blessed Lord saw great portents arising in <s>Dvāravatī</s>,
and spoke to the assembled elders of the <s>Yadus</s>.
The Blessed Lord said:
These very great portents are arising here on every side,

children.text: śāpaś ca naḥ kulasyāsīd brāhmaṇebhyo duratyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and there is the inescapable curse upon our clan from the Brahmins.
We must not remain here, noble ones, if we wish to live;
let us go this very day, without delay, to the highly sacred <s>Prabhāsa</s>.
There, after bathing, the moon, king of the stars, who had been seized by consumption because of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s curse,

children.text: vimuktaḥ kilbiṣāt sadyo bheje bhūyaḥ kalodayam ||
children.translated_text: was immediately freed from sin and again attained the waxing of his digits.

children.text: vayaṃ ca tasminn āplutya tarpayitvā pitṝn surān
children.translated_text: We too, having bathed there and satisfied the ancestors and the gods,
and having fed the Brahmin priests with food of many excellent qualities,

children.text: teṣu dānāni pātreṣu śraddhayoptvā mahānti vai
children.translated_text: will sow great gifts, with faith, among those worthy recipients,
and by gifts we shall cross over our sins as if crossing the ocean with boats.
<s>Śuka</s> said:
Thus instructed by the Blessed Lord, O delight of the <s>Kurus</s>, the <s>Yādavas</s>,
having resolved to go to the holy place, yoked their chariots.
Seeing this, O king, and hearing what the Blessed Lord had said, <s>Uddhava</s>,
who constantly followed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, saw the dreadful omens.
Approaching in private the Lord of lords of the worlds,

children.text: praṇamya śirasā pādau prāñjalis tam abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: he bowed his head to his feet and, with joined palms, spoke to him.
The venerable <s>Uddhava</s> said:
O Lord of the lords of gods, O master of yoga, whose hearing and chanting are purifying,

children.text: saṃhṛtyaitat kulaṃ nūnaṃ lokaṃ saṃtyakṣyate bhavān
children.translated_text: surely, after destroying this clan, you will abandon the world,

children.text: vipraśāpaṃ samartho 'pi pratyahan na yad īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: since, though able, O Lord, you have not counteracted the Brahmins' curse.
I cannot bear to leave your lotus feet even for half a moment, O <s>Keśava</s>;

children.text: tyaktuṃ samutsahe nātha svadhāma naya mām api ||
children.translated_text: O Lord, take me too to your own abode.
Your divine play, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, is the supreme blessing for human beings;
people who have obtained that nectar for the ears abandon every other desire.
In lying down, sitting, walking, standing, bathing, playing, eating, and the like,

children.text: kathaṃ tvāṃ priyam ātmānaṃ vayaṃ bhaktās tyajema hi ||
children.translated_text: how could we devotees ever abandon you, our beloved very self?
Adorned with the garlands, fragrances, garments, and ornaments enjoyed by you,

children.text: ucchiṣṭabhojino dāsās tava māyāṃ jayema hi ||
children.translated_text: and eating your remnants, we servants indeed overcome your <s>māyā</s>.
Those sages who are clothed in the wind, ascetics with their vital power drawn upward,

children.text: brahmākhyaṃ dhāma te yānti śāntāḥ saṃnyāsino 'malāḥ ||
children.translated_text: peaceful, spotless renunciants, attain your abode called <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: vayaṃ tv iha mahāyogin bhramantaḥ karmavartmasu
children.translated_text: But we, O great yogin, wandering here on the paths of action,
will cross the hard-to-cross darkness by talk of you among your own people.

children.text: smarantaḥ kīrtayantas te kṛtāni gaditāni ca
children.translated_text: We will remember and proclaim the things you have done and spoken,
your gait, smiles, glances, and playful words, by which you imitate human life.
<s>Śuka</s> said:
Thus appealed to, O king, the Blessed Lord, son of <s>Devakī</s>,
addressed <s>Uddhava</s>, his beloved servant, wholly devoted to him.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: yad āttha māṃ mahābhāga taccikīrṣitam eva me
children.translated_text: What you have said to me, O greatly fortunate one, is exactly what I wish to do.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, and the guardians of the worlds, desiring my dwelling in heaven,

children.text: mayā niṣpāditaṃ hy atra devakāryam aśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: for here the work of the gods has been completely accomplished by me,
for the sake of which I descended in a portion, after being entreated by <s>Brahmā</s>.
The clan, burned by the curse, will perish through mutual conflict,

children.text: samudraḥ saptame hy enāṃ purīṃ ca plāvayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and on the seventh day the ocean will flood this city.

children.text: yarhy evāyaṃ mayā tyakto loko 'yaṃ naṣṭamaṅgalaḥ
children.translated_text: As soon as this world has been abandoned by me, it will have lost its auspiciousness,
and before long, O good one, it will also be overrun by <s>Kali</s>.

children.text: na vastavyaṃ tvayaiveha mayā tyakte mahītale
children.translated_text: You must not live here when the surface of the earth has been abandoned by me;
in the age of <s>Kali</s>, O auspicious one, people will delight in what is inauspicious.

children.text: tvaṃ tu sarvaṃ parityajya snehaṃ svajanabandhuṣu
children.translated_text: But you, abandoning all attachment to your own people and kinsmen,

children.text: mayy āveśya manaḥ samyak samadṛg vicarasva gām ||
children.translated_text: fix your mind fully on me and wander the earth with equal vision.

children.text: yad idaṃ manasā vācā cakṣurbhyāṃ śravaṇādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever this is, grasped by mind, speech, the eyes, the ears, and the other senses,
know it to be perishable and formed by the mind under <s>māyā</s> (illusion).
For a man who is not disciplined, the manifold object is a delusion, partaking of qualities and faults;
the distinction of action, non-action, and wrong action belongs to an intellect that thinks in terms of qualities and faults.
Therefore, with the group of your senses disciplined and your mind disciplined,
behold this world as spread out in the self, and behold the self in me, the supreme Lord.
Joined with knowledge and realized knowledge, having become the self of embodied beings,
with your self satisfied by experience of the self, you will not be obstructed by impediments.
One who has gone beyond both notions of fault and merit does not turn back because of prohibitions,

children.text: guṇabuddhyā ca vihitaṃ na karoti yathārbhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor, through the notion of merit, does he perform what is prescribed, just like a child.
A friend to all beings, peaceful, and firm in knowledge and realized knowledge,

children.text: paśyan madātmakaṃ viśvaṃ na vipadyeta vai punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing the universe as consisting of me, he truly does not fall into misfortune again.
Śrī <s>Śuka</s> said:
Thus instructed by the Blessed Lord, O king,
the great devotee <s>Uddhava</s>, wishing to know the truth, bowed down and spoke to <s>Acyuta</s>.
Śrī <s>Uddhava</s> said:
O lord of yoga, arranger of yoga, self of yoga, source of yoga,
you have taught me, for the highest good, renunciation marked by <s>saṃnyāsa</s>.
This renunciation of desires is difficult, O great one, for those whose selves are absorbed in sense-objects;

children.text: sutarāṃ tvayi sarvātmann abhaktair iti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the more so, I think, for those without devotion to you, O self of all.

children.text: so 'haṃ mamāham iti mūḍhamatir vigāḍhas tvanmāyayā viracitātmani sānubandhe
children.translated_text: I am one whose mind is foolish, deeply sunk in the notion 'I' and 'mine' toward the self fabricated by your <s>māyā</s> together with its attachments.

children.text: tat tv añjasā nigaditaṃ bhavatā yathāhaṃ saṃsādhayāmi bhagavann anuśādhi bhṛtyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore instruct your servant, O Blessed Lord, so that I may easily carry out what has been clearly stated by you.

children.text: satyasya te svadṛśa ātmana ātmano 'nyaṃ vaktāram īśa vibudheṣv api nānucakṣe
children.translated_text: O Lord, among the gods I do not see any speaker of truth for me other than you, the self, who see by your own vision.

children.text: sarve vimohitadhiyas tava māyayeme brahmādayas tanubhṛto bahirarthabhāvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All these embodied beings, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, have their intellects deluded by your <s>māyā</s> and take external objects to be real.

children.text: tasmād bhavantam anavadyam anantapāraṃ sarvajñam īśvaram akuṇṭhavikuṇṭhadhiṣṇyam
children.translated_text: Therefore, with my mind wearied and scorched by distress, I take refuge in you, the faultless one, whose far shore is endless,

children.text: nirviṇṇadhīr aham u he vṛjinābhitapto nārāyaṇaṃ narasakhaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye ||
children.translated_text: the all-knowing Lord, whose abode in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is unobstructed, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the friend of man.
The Blessed Lord said:
For the most part, people in the world who are skilled in discerning the truth of the world
raise themselves up from an inauspicious disposition by themselves alone.
The self itself is the teacher of a person, especially of a human being,
because he finds his highest good by direct perception and inference.
And in human form, the wise, skilled in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and yoga,
see me most clearly, strengthened by all powers.
Creatures with one foot, two feet, three feet, and four feet, many-footed and footless,

children.text: bahvyaḥ santi puraḥ sṛṣṭās tāsāṃ me pauruṣī priyā ||
children.translated_text: many kinds have been created before; among them the human form is dear to me.

children.text: atra māṃ mṛgayanty addhā yuktā hetubhir īśvaram
children.translated_text: Here disciplined people seek me directly, the Lord, by reasons,
inferring the ungraspable from graspable qualities and signs.
On this point too they tell this ancient history:
the dialogue of the <s>Avadhūta</s> with <s>Yadu</s> of immeasurable splendor.
Seeing a certain twice-born <s>Avadhūta</s>, a sage, young and wandering fearless of anything,

children.text: kaviṃ nirīkṣya taruṇaṃ yaduḥ papraccha dharmavit ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yadu</s>, who knew <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), questioned him.
Śrī <s>Yadu</s> said:

children.text: kuto buddhir iyaṃ brahmann akartuḥ suviśāradā
children.translated_text: Whence comes this very expert intelligence of yours, O <s>brahman</s>, though you do not act,

children.text: yām āsādya bhavāl lokaṃ vidvāṃś carati bālavat ||
children.translated_text: by which, being learned, you move about the world like a child?
Generally, in regard to <s>dharma</s>, wealth, pleasure, and the wish to know, human beings
strive with a motive for long life, fame, and prosperity.

children.text: tvaṃ tu kalpaḥ kavir dakṣaḥ subhago 'mṛtabhāṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: But you are capable, wise, skillful, fortunate, and speaking nectar-like words;
yet you do nothing here and desire nothing, like one inert, mad, or possessed.
When people are burning in the forest fire of desire and greed,

children.text: na tapyase 'gninā mukto gaṅgāmbhaḥstha iva dvipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you are not burned by that fire, like an elephant standing free in the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ hi naḥ pṛcchatāṃ brahmann ātmany ānandakāraṇam
children.translated_text: For us who ask, O <s>brahman</s>, tell the cause of joy in the self
for you, who are untouched by sense-contact and are the self alone.
The Blessed Lord said:
Thus questioned and honored by <s>Yadu</s>, the greatly fortunate, wise, and devoted to <s>brahman</s>,
the twice-born one spoke to him as he bowed down respectfully.
The Śrī <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said:

children.text: santi me guravo rājan bahavo buddhyupaśritāḥ
children.translated_text: I have many teachers, O king, upon whom my understanding has relied;

children.text: yato buddhim upādāya mukto 'ṭāmīha tān śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: having taken understanding from them, I wander here liberated. Hear of them.

children.text: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo 'gniś candramā raviḥ
children.translated_text: Earth, wind, space, water, fire, the moon, the sun,
the pigeon, the python, the ocean, the moth, the honey-maker, and the elephant;
the honey-gatherer, the deer, the fish, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, the osprey, the child,
the maiden, the arrow-maker, the serpent, the spider, and the wasp:

children.text: ete me guravo rājan caturviṃśatir āśritāḥ
children.translated_text: these, O king, are the twenty-four teachers whom I have taken as refuge.
From the conduct of these, I have learned instruction here for myself.

children.text: yato yad anuśikṣāmi yathā vā nāhuṣātmaja
children.translated_text: What I have learned from each one, and how, O son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>,

children.text: tat tathā puruṣavyāghra nibodha kathayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: That being so, O tiger among men, understand it; I shall tell it to you.
Even while being overrun by beings acting under the control of fate, the steadfast man,

children.text: tad vidvān na calen mārgād anvaśikṣaṃ kṣiter vratam ||
children.translated_text: knowing this, should not swerve from the path; I learned this observance from the earth.
Whose every constant effort is for the sake of others, whose very existence is wholly for others,
a holy man should learn other-centeredness from the mountain and the tree, as their pupil.
A sage should be content with just what sustains life, not with things dear to the senses,

children.text: jñānaṃ yathā na naśyeta nāvakīryeta vāṅmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that knowledge may not perish and speech and mind may not be scattered.
Moving among sense objects and among many kinds of conditions everywhere, the <s>yogī</s>,
whose self is free from merit and fault, should not become attached, like the wind.
Having entered earthly bodies here, and resting in their qualities,

children.text: guṇair na yujyate yogī gandhair vāyur ivātmadṛk ||
children.translated_text: the self-seeing <s>yogī</s> is not joined to those qualities, just as the wind is not joined to odors.
Hidden within things that stand and move, through the integrated awareness that <s>brahman</s> is the self,

children.text: vyāptyāvyavacchedam asaṅgam ātmano munir nabhastvaṃ vitatasya bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: the sage should contemplate the sky-like nature of the extended self, unbounded in its pervasion and unattached.
The sky is not touched by forms made of fire, water, and food, nor by clouds and the like driven by the wind;

children.text: na spṛśyate nabhas tadvat kālasṛṣṭair guṇaiḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: likewise a person is not touched by the qualities created by time.

children.text: svacchaḥ prakṛtitaḥ snigdho mādhuryas tīrthabhūr nṛṇām
children.translated_text: Pure by nature, gentle, sweet, and a sacred ford for human beings,
a sage, like friendly water, purifies by being seen, touched, and praised.
Radiant, blazing with austerity, hard to assail, and having the belly as his vessel,
though eating everything, one whose self is disciplined does not take on impurity, like fire.

children.text: kvacic channaḥ kvacit spaṣṭa upāsyaḥ śreya icchatām
children.translated_text: Sometimes hidden and sometimes manifest, worthy of worship for those who seek blessedness,
he consumes food everywhere from donors, burning away their earlier and later evil.
The all-pervading Lord, entering this world, created by his own <s>māyā</s> and marked as real and unreal,
is perceived as having this or that form, like fire in pieces of fuel.
States beginning with birth and ending at the cremation ground belong to the body, not to the self,
like the phases of the moon produced by time, whose course is unseen.
By time, with the force of a flood-current, the coming forth and passing away of beings,

children.text: nityāv api na dṛśyete ātmano 'gner yathārciṣām ||
children.translated_text: though continual, are not seen in the self, just as those of flames are not seen in fire.
Through the qualities he takes up the qualities at the proper time and releases them,

children.text: na teṣu yujyate yogī gobhir gā iva gopatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet the <s>yogī</s> is not joined to them, just as the sun, lord of rays, is not joined to the waters it draws up.

children.text: budhyate sve na bhedena vyaktistha iva tadgataḥ
children.translated_text: The self is known in itself without division, though it seems to abide in separate individuals;
by those of coarse understanding it is perceived as situated there, like the sun reflected in different places.

children.text: nātisnehaḥ prasaṅgo vā kartavyaḥ kvāpi kenacit
children.translated_text: Excessive affection or close attachment should never be formed anywhere with anyone;

children.text: kurvan vindeta saṃtāpaṃ kapota iva dīnadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: forming it, one would undergo suffering, like the pigeon of wretched understanding.
A certain pigeon, having made a nest in a tree in the forest,

children.text: kapotyā bhāryayā sārdham uvāsa katicit samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: lived there for some years together with his wife, the hen pigeon.
The two pigeons, householders whose hearts were multiplied by affection,

children.text: dṛṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭyāṅgam aṅgena buddhiṃ buddhyā babandhatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: bound sight to sight, limb to limb, and mind to mind.
Their lying down, sitting, wandering, standing, conversation, play, eating, and the rest,
they performed together as a pair, trustingly, among the rows of trees.

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ vāñchati sā rājan tarpayanty anukampitā
children.translated_text: Whatever she desired, O king, he, moved by compassion and wishing to satisfy her,

children.text: taṃ taṃ samanayat kāmaṃ kṛcchreṇāpy ajitendriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: brought that desired thing, even with difficulty, for his senses were unconquered.

children.text: kapotī prathamaṃ garbhaṃ gṛhṇantī kāla āgate
children.translated_text: In due time the hen pigeon, becoming pregnant for the first time,

children.text: aṇḍāni suṣuve nīḍe sthapatyuḥ saṃnidhau satī ||
children.translated_text: laid eggs in the nest, the faithful wife in the presence of her husband.
In due time there were born in them, by the hard-to-fathom powers of <s>Hari</s>,
young ones with formed limbs and soft down upon their bodies.
The delighted couple, affectionate toward their children, nourished their offspring,
hearing their cooing and taking joy in their childish sounds.
By their wings pleasant to touch, their cooings, their charming movements,
and their confident approaches, the parents attained delight.
Their hearts bound by affection, deluded toward one another by the <s>māyā</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
the two of poor understanding nourished the children, their offspring.

children.text: ekadā jagmatus tāsām annārthaṃ tau kuṭumbinau
children.translated_text: One day those two householders went out for the sake of food for them,

children.text: paritaḥ kānane tasminn arthinau ceratuś ciram ||
children.translated_text: and, seeking it, wandered for a long time all around in that forest.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tān lubdhakaḥ kaścid yadṛcchāto vanecaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing those young ones by chance, a certain hunter, a forest-roamer,
spread out a net and seized them as they moved about near their own dwelling.

children.text: kapotaś ca kapotī ca prajāpoṣe sadotsukau
children.translated_text: The pigeon and the hen pigeon, always eager for the nourishment of their offspring,
having gone and obtained food, approached their own nest.
The hen pigeon, seeing her own children, the little ones, enclosed in the net,
ran toward them crying out, while they cried out, greatly afflicted with grief.
She, repeatedly bound tight by affection, of pitiable mind, by the unborn Lord's <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: svayaṃ cābadhyata śicā baddhān paśyanty apasmṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: herself too was caught in the snare, losing awareness as she watched the bound ones.

children.text: kapotaḥ svātmajān baddhān ātmano 'py adhikān priyān
children.translated_text: The pigeon, seeing his own children bound, dearer to him even than himself,
and his wife, equal to his own self, lamented in misery, exceedingly afflicted with grief:
'Ah, see the ruin of me, a man of little merit and foolish mind,
unsatisfied and unfulfilled; my household, aimed at the three goals of life, has been destroyed.
She who was devoted to her husband, well-matched and favorable to me,

children.text: śūnye gṛhe māṃ saṃtyajya putraiḥ svar yāti sādhubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: abandoning me in an empty house, is going to heaven with her good sons.

children.text: so 'haṃ śūnye gṛhe dīno mṛtadāro mṛtaprajaḥ
children.translated_text: I, then, wretched in an empty house, with wife dead and children dead,

children.text: jijīviṣe kim arthaṃ vā vidhuro duḥkhajīvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: bereft and living a life of sorrow, for what purpose would I wish to live?'
Seeing them just so enclosed in snares, seized by death and struggling,

children.text: svayaṃ ca kṛpaṇaḥ śikṣu paśyann apy abudho 'patat ||
children.translated_text: and being himself miserable, the foolish one fell into the snares even as he looked on.

children.text: taṃ labdhvā lubdhakaḥ krūraḥ kapotaṃ gṛhamedhinam
children.translated_text: Having obtained that pigeon, the cruel hunter,

children.text: kapotakān kapotīṃ ca siddhārthaḥ prayayau gṛham ||
children.translated_text: his aim accomplished, went home with the householder pigeon, the young pigeons, and the hen pigeon.
Thus a family man, whose self is unpeaceful and who delights in paired attachments, like the bird,
The poor man, maintaining his family together with its dependents, sinks down.

children.text: yaḥ prāpya mānuṣaṃ lokaṃ muktidvāram apāvṛtam
children.translated_text: One who, having attained the human world, whose door to liberation stands open,

children.text: gṛheṣu khagavat saktas tam ārūḍhacyutaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: remains attached to houses like a bird: they know him as one who has climbed up and then fallen away.
The revered brāhmaṇa said:

children.text: sukham aindriyakaṃ rājan svarge naraka eva ca
children.translated_text: Sensory pleasure, O king, exists in heaven and in hell alike,

children.text: dehināṃ yad yathā duḥkhaṃ tasmān neccheta tadbudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as suffering comes to embodied beings unbidden; therefore the wise man should not desire it.

children.text: grāsaṃ sumṛṣṭaṃ virasaṃ mahāntaṃ stokam eva vā
children.translated_text: A morsel, whether very well prepared or tasteless, large or only small,
fallen to him purely by chance, the inactive python-like sage should swallow.
He should lie for many days without food and without undertaking effort,

children.text: yadi nopanayed grāso mahāhir iva diṣṭabhuk ||
children.translated_text: if no morsel comes to him, like a great serpent eating what destiny gives.
Bearing a body endowed with vigor, endurance, and strength, yet inactive,
lying awake and possessing the senses, he should still make no effort.
The sage should be clear, deep, hard to fathom, hard to cross,
boundless in extent and unshakable, like an ocean with still waters.
Whether his desires are abundantly fulfilled or he is deprived, the sage devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

children.text: notsarpeta na śuṣyeta saridbhir iva sāgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: should neither swell nor dry up, like the ocean with its rivers.
Seeing a woman, the <s>māyā</s> of the god, an uncontrolled man is drawn by her moods;

children.text: pralobhitaḥ pataty andhe tamasy agnau pataṃgavat ||
children.translated_text: deluded, he falls into blind darkness, like a moth into fire.
A fool, whose self is tempted by the thought of enjoyment toward things fashioned by <s>māyā</s>, such as women, gold, ornaments, garments, and the like,

children.text: pralobhitātmā hy upabhogabuddhyā pataṃgavan naśyati naṣṭadṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: perishes like a moth, his vision lost.

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ grased grāsaṃ deho varteta yāvatā
children.translated_text: He should take morsel after morsel only in small measure, just enough for the body to continue,

children.text: gṛhān ahiṃsann ātiṣṭhed vṛttiṃ mādhukarīṃ muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the sage should adopt the bee-like way of life, without injuring households.

children.text: aṇubhyaś ca mahadbhyaś ca śāstrebhyaḥ kuśalo naraḥ
children.translated_text: A skillful man should take the essence from scriptures small and great,

children.text: sarvataḥ sāram ādadyāt puṣpebhya iva ṣaṭpadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: from every side, like a bee from flowers.

children.text: sāyantanaṃ śvastanaṃ vā na saṃgṛhṇīta bhikṣitam
children.translated_text: He should not collect alms for the evening or for tomorrow,
being one whose hands are his bowl and whose belly is his measure, not a hoarder like a bee.

children.text: sāyantanaṃ śvastanaṃ vā na saṃgṛhṇīta bhikṣukaḥ
children.translated_text: A mendicant should not collect alms for the evening or for tomorrow;

children.text: makṣikā iva saṃgṛhṇan saha tena vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: collecting like bees, he perishes along with what he has collected.

children.text: padāpi yuvatīṃ bhikṣur na spṛśed dāravīm api
children.translated_text: A mendicant should not touch a young woman even with his foot, not even one made of wood;
touching her, he would be bound like a male elephant through contact with a female elephant's body.

children.text: nādhigacchet striyaṃ prājñaḥ karhicin mṛtyum ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should never approach a woman, his own death;

children.text: balādhikaiḥ sa hanyeta gajair anyair gajo yathā ||
children.translated_text: he would be killed by stronger men, as one elephant is killed by other elephants.

children.text: na deyaṃ nopabhogyaṃ ca lubdhair yad duḥkhasaṃcitam
children.translated_text: What greedy men painfully accumulate is neither given away nor enjoyed;

children.text: bhuṅkte tad api tac cānyo madhuhevārthavin madhu ||
children.translated_text: another person consumes that very thing, like the knower of honey taking honey from the bee.
With wealth acquired through great suffering, householders hope for household blessings;
yet a <s>yati</s> (renunciant), like a honey-gatherer, enjoys it before them.

children.text: grāmyagītaṃ na śṛṇuyād yatir vanacaraḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: A forest-dwelling <s>yati</s> should never listen to village songs;
he should learn from the deer, which are captured by the hunter when bewildered by song.
Enjoying the vulgar dancing, instrumental music, and songs of women,
<s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, son of a doe, became their plaything and subject to their control.
A person deluded by taste, through the tongue that is most violently agitating,

children.text: mṛtyum ṛcchaty asadbuddhir mīnas tu baḍiśair yathā ||
children.translated_text: meets death through bad judgment, like a fish by hooks.
Wise men quickly conquer the senses by fasting,

children.text: varjayitvā tu rasanaṃ tan nirannasya vardhate ||
children.translated_text: except for the tongue; in one without food, it grows stronger.

children.text: tāvaj jitendriyo na syād vijitānyendriyaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: A man may have conquered the other senses, but he is not yet self-controlled

children.text: na jayed rasanaṃ yāvaj jitaṃ sarvaṃ jite rase ||
children.translated_text: so long as he has not conquered the tongue; when taste is conquered, all is conquered.
There was once a courtesan named <s>Piṅgalā</s> in the city of <s>Videha</s>;

children.text: tasyā me śikṣitaṃ kiṃcin nibodha nṛpanandana ||
children.translated_text: learn from me, O delight of kings, something I learned from her.

children.text: sā svairiṇy ekadā kāntaṃ saṃketa upaneṣyatī
children.translated_text: That wanton woman, intending one day to bring a lover to a rendezvous,

children.text: abhūt kāle bahir dvāre bibhratī rūpam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: stood at the doorway outside at the proper time, displaying excellent beauty.
Watching men coming along the road, O bull among men,
she, desiring wealth, thought those wealthy fee-paying men were lovers.
As they came and went, she who lived by appointments thought,

children.text: apy anyo vittavān ko 'pi mām upaiṣyati bhūridaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Perhaps some other wealthy man, a generous giver, will come to me.'
Thus, with sleep ruined by vain hope, leaning on the doorway,
going out and coming in, she reached midnight.
As her face dried up from hope for money and her mind became wretched,
a supreme <s>nirveda</s> (disillusionment), a cause of thought and a bringer of happiness, arose in her.

children.text: tasyā nirviṇṇacittāyā gītaṃ śṛṇu yathā mama
children.translated_text: Hear from me the song of her whose mind had become disenchanted;

children.text: nirveda āśāpāśānāṃ puruṣasya yathā hy asiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for <s>nirveda</s> is like a sword cutting the bonds of hope for a person.
For one in whom <s>nirveda</s> has not arisen, O king, does not wish to abandon the bondage of the body,
just as a man without true knowledge does not abandon possessiveness.
<s>Piṅgalā</s> said:
Ah, behold the extent of my delusion, since I am one who has not mastered herself,

children.text: yā kāntād asataḥ kāmaṃ kāmaye yena bāliśā ||
children.translated_text: that foolish as I am, I desire pleasure from an unreal lover.

children.text: santaṃ samīpe ramaṇaṃ ratipradaṃ vittapradaṃ nityam imaṃ vihāya
children.translated_text: Abandoning this true lover near at hand, who gives delight, pleasure, and wealth always,
I, ignorant woman, serve a trifling one who gives no desire, but gives suffering, fear, anxiety, grief, and delusion.
Ah, I have tormented myself in vain by this rendezvous trade, a most blameworthy livelihood,

children.text: straiṇān narād yārthatṛṣo 'nuśocyāt krītena vittaṃ ratim ātmanecchatī ||
children.translated_text: seeking wealth and pleasure for myself from pitiable, lustful men ruled by women.

children.text: yad asthibhir nirmitavaṃśavaṃsyasthūṇaṃ tvacā romanakhaiḥ pinaddham
children.translated_text: This house is built with bones as its rafters, ribs, and posts, bound with skin, hair, and nails,

children.text: kṣarannavadvāram agāram etad viṇmūtrapūrṇaṃ mad upaiti kānyā ||
children.translated_text: oozing through nine doors and full of feces and urine; what other woman would approach it?

children.text: videhānāṃ pure hy asminn aham ekaiva mūḍhadhīḥ
children.translated_text: In this city of the <s>Videhas</s>, I alone am foolish-minded,

children.text: yānyam icchanty asaty asmād ātmadāt kāmam acyutāt ||
children.translated_text: for I desire another, false and apart from him who grants the self and desire, <s>Acyuta</s>.

children.text: suhṛt preṣṭhatamo nātha ātmā cāyaṃ śarīriṇām
children.translated_text: This very one is the friend, the dearest beloved, the lord, and the self of embodied beings.
Having gained him by giving myself alone, I shall delight in him as <s>Ramā</s> does.

children.text: kiyat priyaṃ te vyabhajan kāmā ye kāmadā narāḥ
children.translated_text: How much pleasure did those men, givers of desire, bestow on you, when they divided their desires?
They, or even the gods, are subject to beginning and end and are driven away by Time from a wife.

children.text: nūnaṃ me bhagavān prīto viṣṇuḥ kenāpi karmaṇā
children.translated_text: Surely the Blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been pleased with me because of some deed,

children.text: nirvedo 'yaṃ durāśāyā yan me jātaḥ sukhāvahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since this disillusionment with vain hope, bringing happiness, has arisen in me.
Let these afflictions of a woman of poor fortune not be otherwise; they are causes of disillusionment,
by which a person, removing attachment, comes to peace.
Accepting that help with my head, I abandon worldly associations

children.text: tyaktvā durāśāḥ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi tam adhīśvaram ||
children.translated_text: and vain hopes, and I go for refuge to that supreme Lord.
Contented, trusting in this, and living on whatever comes by chance,
I shall sport with this very self as my lover.
When the self has fallen into the well of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), its sight stolen by sense objects,
and it is seized by the serpent of Time, who other than the supreme Lord can save it?

children.text: ātmaiva hy ātmano goptā nirvidyeta yadākhilāt
children.translated_text: The self alone is indeed the protector of the self, when one becomes disillusioned with everything

children.text: apramatta idaṃ paśyed grastaṃ kālāhinā jagat ||
children.translated_text: and, vigilant, sees this world swallowed by the serpent of Time.
The revered brāhmaṇa said:
Thus her mind resolved, she cut off the vain hope born from thirst for lovers,
adopted peace, and lay down on her bed.

children.text: āśā hi paramaṃ duḥkhaṃ nairāśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham
children.translated_text: Hope is the highest misery; hopelessness is the highest happiness.

children.text: yathā saṃchidya kāntāśāṃ sukhaṃ suṣvāpa piṅgalā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having cut off her hope for lovers, <s>Piṅgalā</s> slept happily.
The revered brāhmaṇa said:

children.text: parigraho hi duḥkhāya yad yat priyatamaṃ nṝṇām
children.translated_text: Possession is indeed for suffering, whatever is most dear to human beings.

children.text: anantaṃ sukham āpnoti tad vidvān yas tv akiñcanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise person who owns nothing attains endless happiness.
Other strong birds without meat attacked a hawk that had meat;
then, abandoning that meat, it found happiness.

children.text: na me mānāpamānau sto na cintā gehaputriṇām
children.translated_text: For me there is neither honor nor dishonor, nor the anxieties of householders with children.
Delighting in the self and taking pleasure in the self, I wander here like a child.

children.text: dvāv eva cintayā muktau paramānanda āplutau
children.translated_text: Only two are free from care and immersed in supreme bliss:

children.text: yo vimugdho jaḍo bālo yo guṇebhyaḥ paraṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the utterly deluded, dull child, and the one who has gone beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature).

children.text: kvacit kumārī tv ātmānaṃ vṛṇānān gṛham āgatān
children.translated_text: Once, when suitors came to the house to choose a maiden,

children.text: svayaṃ tān arhayāmāsa kvāpi yāteṣu bandhuṣu ||
children.translated_text: she herself honored them while her relatives had gone somewhere.
For their meal, O king, she was secretly pounding rice,

children.text: avaghnantyāḥ prakoṣṭhasthāś cakruḥ śaṅkhāḥ svanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: and the shell bracelets on her wrists made a great noise.

children.text: sā taj jugupsitaṃ matvā mahatī vrīḍitā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking that disgraceful, she became very ashamed,

children.text: babhañjaikaikaśaḥ śaṅkhān dvau dvau pāṇyor aśeṣayat ||
children.translated_text: and she broke the shell bracelets one by one, leaving two on each hand.

children.text: ubhayor apy abhūd ghoṣo hy avaghnantyāḥ svaśaṅkhayoḥ
children.translated_text: While she was pounding with her own shell bracelets, there was noise even from both of them;

children.text: tatrāpy ekaṃ nirabhidad ekasmān nābhavad dhvaniḥ ||
children.translated_text: there too she broke one, and from a single bracelet there was no sound.
As I wandered among these worlds, wishing to know the truth of the world,
I learned this instruction from her, O subduer of enemies.

children.text: vāse bahūnāṃ kalaho bhaved vārttā dvayor api
children.translated_text: Where many live together there will be quarrel, and conversation even between two.

children.text: eka eva vaset tasmāt kumāryā iva kaṅkaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should live alone, like the single bracelet of the maiden.
One should fix the mind on one point, with breath mastered and posture mastered,
holding it carefully through the yoga of dispassion and practice.

children.text: yasmin mano labdhapadaṃ yad etac chanaiḥ śanair muñcati karmareṇūn
children.translated_text: When the mind has gained its footing in that, it gradually casts off the dust of karma,

children.text: sattvena vṛddhena rajas tamaś ca vidhūya nirvāṇam upaity anindhanam ||
children.translated_text: and, with <s>sattva</s> increased, shaking off <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, it reaches extinguishment without fuel.

children.text: tadaivam ātmany avaruddhacitto na veda kiṃcid bahir antaraṃ vā
children.translated_text: When the mind is thus confined within the self, one knows nothing outside or inside,

children.text: yatheṣukāro nṛpatiṃ vrajantam iṣau gatātmā na dadarśa pārśve ||
children.translated_text: just as an arrow-maker, absorbed in his arrow, did not see the king passing beside him.
A sage should move alone, be without a fixed dwelling, vigilant, dwelling in a cave,
unnoticed by his conduct, solitary, and sparing in speech.
The undertaking of a house is indeed misery and fruitless for one whose self is impermanent.

children.text: sarpaḥ parakṛtaṃ veśma praviśya sukham edhate ||
children.translated_text: A snake prospers happily by entering a dwelling made by another.
The one god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Lord, having withdrawn by his own <s>māyā</s>
this world that had been created before, through the measure of Time at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>,
became alone, without a second, self-supported and the support of all.
When, by Time and his own power, the energies beginning with <s>sattva</s>
have been brought to equilibrium, the primal Person, lord of <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit),
the supreme one among higher and lower beings, abides in what is called <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation),
a mass of the bliss of pure experience, free from limiting conditions.
By the experience of the pure self, he agitates his own <s>māyā</s>, made of the three <s>guṇas</s>,

children.text: saṃkṣobhayan sṛjaty ādau tayā sūtram ariṃdama ||
children.translated_text: and at the beginning, through her, he creates the <s>sūtra</s> (cosmic thread), O subduer of enemies.
They call her the manifestation of the three <s>guṇas</s>, creating in every direction,

children.text: yasmin protam idaṃ viśvaṃ yena saṃsarate pumān ||
children.translated_text: in whom this universe is strung and by whom a person transmigrates.
As a spider extends thread from its heart through its mouth,

children.text: tayā vihṛtya bhūyas tāṃ grasaty evaṃ maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: plays with it, and then swallows it again, so does the great Lord.

children.text: yatra yatra mano dehī dhārayet sakalaṃ dhiyā
children.translated_text: Whatever form an embodied being fixes the whole mind upon with its intellect,

children.text: snehād dveṣād bhayād vāpi yāti tattatsvarūpatām ||
children.translated_text: whether from affection, hatred, or fear, it goes to the nature of that very thing.

children.text: kīṭaḥ peśaskṛtaṃ dhyāyan kuḍyāṃ tena praveśitaḥ
children.translated_text: A worm, placed by a wasp in a wall and meditating on that wasp,
comes to sameness with it, O king, without abandoning its former form.

children.text: evaṃ gurubhya etebhya eṣā me śikṣitā matiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus from these teachers I have learned this understanding;

children.text: svātmopaśikṣitāṃ buddhiṃ śṛṇu me vadataḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: now hear me, O lord, as I speak the wisdom taught by my own self.

children.text: deho gurur mama viraktivivekahetur bibhrat sma sattvanidhanaṃ satatārtyudarkam
children.translated_text: The body is my teacher, because it causes detachment and discrimination, bearing destruction of its elements and always ending in pain.

children.text: tattvāny anena vimṛśāmi yathā tathāpi pārakyam ity avasito vicarāmy asaṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through it I examine the principles; nevertheless, convinced that it belongs to another, I wander unattached.
It nourishes wife, offspring, wealth, animals, servants, houses, and circles of relatives, expanding them in the wish to do what is pleasing to them...

children.text: svānte sakṛcchram avaruddhadhanaḥ sa dehaḥ sṛṣṭvāsya bījam avasīdati vṛkṣadharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At his own end, the body, which has confined wealth with great hardship, sinks down after producing its seed, following the nature of a tree.

children.text: jihvaikato 'mum apakarṣati karhi tarṣā śiśno 'nyatas tvag udaraṃ śravaṇaṃ kutaścit
children.translated_text: The tongue pulls him in one direction, thirst in another; the penis elsewhere, the skin, the belly, and the ear from another side.

children.text: ghrāṇo 'nyataś capaladṛk kva ca karmaśaktir bahvyaḥ sapatnya iva gehapatiṃ lunanti ||
children.translated_text: The nose pulls him elsewhere, the restless eye somewhere else, and the power of action in yet another direction; many rivals plunder the householder like co-wives.

children.text: sṛṣṭvā purāṇi vividhāny ajayātmaśaktyā vṛkṣān sarīsṛpapaśūn khagadandaśūkān
children.translated_text: Having formerly created various bodies by his own unborn power: trees, reptiles, beasts, birds, and fanged creatures,

children.text: tais tair atuṣṭahṛdayaḥ puruṣaṃ vidhāya brahmāvalokadhiṣaṇaṃ mudam āpa devaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the god <s>Brahmā</s>, his heart unsatisfied with each of those, fashioned the human being, endowed with intelligence for beholding <s>brahman</s> (ultimate reality), and attained joy.

children.text: labdhvā sudurlabham idaṃ bahusambhavānte mānuṣyam arthadam anityam apīha dhīraḥ
children.translated_text: Having obtained this human state, exceedingly hard to obtain after many births, useful for the goal though impermanent here, the wise person

children.text: tūrṇaṃ yateta na pated anumṛtyu yāvan niḥśreyasāya viṣayaḥ khalu sarvataḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: should quickly strive for the highest good before he falls, so long as death has not overtaken him; for sense-objects are indeed available everywhere.
Thus, with detachment arisen and the light of knowledge present in the self,
I wander over this earth, freed from attachment and without ego.

children.text: na hy ekasmād guror jñānaṃ susthiraṃ syāt supuṣkalam
children.translated_text: For knowledge from a single teacher alone would not be very firm or abundant;
this non-dual <s>brahman</s> is indeed sung in many ways by the seers.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: ity uktvā sa yaduṃ vipras tam āmantrya gabhīradhīḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that deeply wise <s>brāhmaṇa</s> took leave of <s>Yadu</s>;

children.text: vanditaḥ svarcito rājñā yayau prīto yathāgatam ||
children.translated_text: honored and duly worshiped by the king, he departed happily, just as he had come.

children.text: avadhūtavacaḥ śrutvā pūrveṣāṃ naḥ sa pūrvajaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of the <s>Avadhūta</s>, that ancestor and forefather of ours
became free from every attachment and equal-minded.
The Blessed Lord said:
Attentive to the <s>svadharmas</s> (one's own duties) taught by me, and taking refuge in me,
one whose self is free from desire should practice the custom of <s>varṇa</s>, <s>āśrama</s>, and family.
With purified self, he should examine, among embodied beings whose selves are given to sense-objects,
the complete reversal of all undertakings in the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), through meditation on reality.
The appearance of objects to one asleep, or the fancy of one who is imagining,
is fruitless because of its manifold nature; so too is an understanding of difference produced by the <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: nivṛttaṃ karma seveta pravṛttaṃ matparas tyajet
children.translated_text: He should practice action that has turned back from worldly pursuit, and, devoted to me, abandon action that is outwardly directed;
having set out upon inquiry, he should not pay regard to injunctions to ritual action.

children.text: yamān abhīkṣṇaṃ seveta niyamān matparaḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: Being devoted to me, he should constantly practice the <s>yamas</s> (restraints), and the <s>niyamas</s> (observances) when appropriate;
he should attend upon a peaceful <s>guru</s>, one who knows me and whose self is fixed in me.
He should be free from vanity and envy, capable, without possessiveness, firm in friendship,
not hasty, desirous of knowing the truth, not fault-finding, and of unfailing speech.
Toward wife, children, house, fields, kinsmen, wealth, and the like,

children.text: udāsīnaḥ samaṃ paśyan sarveṣv artham ivātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should be indifferent, seeing equally in all things what is like the purpose of his own self.
The self, the seer and self-luminous, is distinct from the gross and subtle body,
just as fire, present in wood, is other than the combustible wood: it burns and gives light.
Cessation, arising, smallness, greatness, and diversity are qualities produced by that;

children.text: antaḥ praviṣṭa ādhatta evaṃ dehaguṇān paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: having entered within, the supreme one takes on the body's qualities in just this way.

children.text: yo 'sau guṇair viracito deho 'yaṃ puruṣasya hi
children.translated_text: This body of the person, fashioned by the <s>guṇas</s>, is indeed <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly wandering);
and this bondage of the conscious self is ignorance.
Therefore, through inquiry, approaching the self that abides in the self, the sole and supreme one,
one should gradually dispel this notion of substantial reality in objects.
The teacher should be the first fire-stick, and the student the upper fire-stick;
instruction is their joining, and knowledge is the kindling at the junction, bringing happiness.
That highly purified, expert intelligence shakes off <s>māyā</s> (illusion), which has arisen from the <s>guṇas</s>;

children.text: guṇāṃś ca saṃdahya yadātmam etat svayaṃ ca śāmyaty asamid yathāgniḥ ||
children.translated_text: and after burning the <s>guṇas</s> and this self-related superimposition, it itself becomes calm, like a fire without fuel.
Now, if you think that these agents of action and enjoyers of pleasure and pain
and the worlds, time, revealed tradition, and selves are diverse and eternal,

children.text: manyase sarvabhāvānāṃ saṃsthā hy autpattikī yathā
children.translated_text: and that the condition of all beings is innate in this way,
then thought arises and is divided according to each difference of form.

children.text: evam apy aṅga sarveṣāṃ dehināṃ dehayogataḥ
children.translated_text: Even so, dear one, for all embodied beings, because of their connection with a body,
states such as birth occur repeatedly through the divisions of time.

children.text: tatrāpi karmaṇāṃ kartur asvātantryaṃ ca lakṣyate
children.translated_text: Even in that case, the lack of independence of the doer of actions is observed,

children.text: bhoktuś ca duḥkhasukhayoḥ ko nv artho vivaśaṃ bhajet ||
children.translated_text: and also of the enjoyer of pain and pleasure; what purpose would anyone gain by resorting to what is helpless?

children.text: na dehināṃ sukhaṃ kiṃcid vidyate viduṣām api
children.translated_text: There is no happiness at all for embodied beings, even for the learned;

children.text: tathā ca duḥkhaṃ mūḍhānāṃ vṛthāhaṃkaraṇaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: and likewise there is suffering for the deluded: in the highest sense, making an 'I' is futile.

children.text: yadi prāptiṃ vighātaṃ ca jānanti sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
children.translated_text: If they know the attainment and obstruction of pleasure and pain,

children.text: te 'py addhā na vidur yogaṃ mṛtyur na prabhaved yathā ||
children.translated_text: even they certainly do not know the <s>yoga</s> by which death would not prevail.

children.text: ko 'nv arthaḥ sukhayaty enaṃ kāmo vā mṛtyur antike
children.translated_text: What object, or what desire, can give this person happiness when death is near?
For one being led to execution, like a condemned man, it does not give satisfaction.
What is heard of is flawed, like what is seen, by rivalry, envy, decay, and loss;
because desires have many obstacles, it is fruitless, like agriculture too.
If <s>dharma</s> (righteous practice), well performed, is not obstructed by impediments,

children.text: tenāpi nirjitaṃ sthānaṃ yathā gacchati tac chṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: then hear how one goes to the place conquered by that.

children.text: iṣṭveha devatā yajñaiḥ svarlokaṃ yāti yājñikaḥ
children.translated_text: Having worshiped the deities here with sacrifices, the sacrificer goes to heaven;

children.text: bhuñjīta devavat tatra bhogān divyān nijārjitān ||
children.translated_text: there he enjoys divine pleasures, earned by himself, like a god.
In a radiant aerial car heaped up by his own merit, he is sung by <s>Gandharvas</s>
as he sports among goddesses, wearing dress delightful to the heart.
Playing with women amid pleasure-songs and a garlanded net of tinkling bells,
he does not know his own fall while delighted in the divine pleasure-groves.

children.text: tāvat sa modate svarge yāvat puṇyaṃ samāpyate
children.translated_text: He rejoices in heaven only so long as his merit lasts;
when his merit is exhausted, moved by time, he falls downward against his will.
If, through association with the wicked, he is devoted to <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), or has not conquered his senses...
A man whose nature is desire, pitiable, greedy, addicted to women, and injurious to beings,
taking animals improperly and worshiping hosts of ghosts and spirits,

children.text: narakān avaśo jantur gatvā yāty ulbaṇaṃ tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: goes helplessly to hells, and the creature enters terrible darkness.

children.text: karmāṇi duḥkhodarkāṇi kurvan dehena taiḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Doing deeds with the body whose outcome is suffering, by those deeds again

children.text: deham ābhajate tatra kiṃ sukhaṃ martyadharmiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he obtains a body there. What happiness is there for one subject to mortality?
The worlds and the guardians of the worlds, though they live for a kalpa, are afraid of me;
even <s>Brahmā</s>, whose highest lifespan is two parārdhas, is afraid of me.
The guṇas produce actions, and a guṇa gives rise to further guṇas;

children.text: jīvas tu guṇasaṃyukto bhuṅkte karmaphalāny asau ||
children.translated_text: but the living being, joined with the guṇas, experiences the fruits of those actions.

children.text: yāvat syād guṇavaiṣamyaṃ tāvan nānātvam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as there is imbalance among the guṇas, so long there is multiplicity of the self;

children.text: nānātvam ātmano yāvat pāratantryaṃ tadaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: and as long as there is multiplicity of the self, precisely so long there is dependence.
As long as this being lacks independence, so long there is fear from the Lord;

children.text: ya etat samupāsīraṃs te muhyanti śucārpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who worship this condition become deluded, afflicted by grief.

children.text: kāla ātmāgamo lokaḥ svabhāvo dharma eva ca
children.translated_text: Time, the self, scripture, the world, inherent nature, and <s>dharma</s> itself:

children.text: iti māṃ bahudhā prāhur guṇavyatikare sati ||
children.translated_text: when there is disturbance among the guṇas, people speak of me in many ways as these.
<s>Śrī-Uddhava</s> said:
