Though the embodied one remains among the guṇas born of the body and is not separated from them,

children.text: guṇair na badhyate dehī badhyate vā kathaṃ vibho ||
children.translated_text: how is he not bound by the guṇas, or how is he bound, O lord?

children.text: kathaṃ varteta viharet kair vā jñāyeta lakṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: How should he live and move about, and by what marks should he be known?

children.text: kiṃ bhuñjītota visṛjec chayītāsīta yāti vā ||
children.translated_text: What should he eat, what should he discard, how should he sleep, sit, or go?

children.text: etad acyuta me brūhi praśnaṃ praśnavidāṃ vara
children.translated_text: Tell me this question, O <s>Acyuta</s>, best of those who know questions;

children.text: nityabaddho nityamukta eka eveti me bhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am confused, thinking that the same one is eternally bound and eternally free.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: baddho mukta iti vyākhyā guṇato me na vastutaḥ
children.translated_text: The explanation 'bound' and 'free' is, for me, based on the guṇas, not on reality;

children.text: guṇasya māyāmūlatvān na me mokṣo na bandhanam ||
children.translated_text: because the guṇa has māyā as its root, there is for me neither liberation nor bondage.

children.text: śokamohau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ dehāpattiś ca māyayā
children.translated_text: Grief and delusion, happiness and suffering, and the taking on of a body are through māyā;

children.text: svapno yathātmanaḥ khyātiḥ saṃsṛtir na tu vāstavī ||
children.translated_text: as a dream is a manifestation to the self, transmigration is not truly real.

children.text: vidyāvidye mama tanū viddhy uddhava śarīriṇām
children.translated_text: Know knowledge and ignorance, O <s>Uddhava</s>, to be two forms of mine for embodied beings;
these first two, which cause liberation and bondage, were fashioned by my māyā.
For the living being, who is a portion of me alone, O great-minded one,
his bondage through ignorance is beginningless, and the other state is likewise through knowledge.

children.text: atha baddhasya muktasya vailakṣaṇyaṃ vadāmi te
children.translated_text: Now I shall tell you the distinction between the bound and the liberated,
dear one, although they have opposed properties while abiding in one and the same substratum.

children.text: suparṇāv etau sadṛśau sakhāyau yadṛcchayaitau kṛtanīḍau ca vṛkṣe
children.translated_text: These two birds, alike and companions, by chance have made a nest in a tree;

children.text: ekas tayoḥ khādati pippalānnam anyo niranno 'pi balena bhūyān ||
children.translated_text: one of them eats the food of the pippala fruit, while the other, though not eating, is greater in strength.

children.text: ātmānam anyaṃ ca sa veda vidvān apippalādo na tu pippalādaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise one, the non-eater of pippala, knows himself and the other; but the pippala-eater does not.

children.text: yo 'vidyayā yuk sa tu nityabaddho vidyāmayo yaḥ sa tu nityamuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who is joined with ignorance is eternally bound; he who consists of knowledge is eternally free.

children.text: dehastho 'pi na dehastho vidvān svapnād yathotthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Though dwelling in the body, the wise man is not body-bound, like one awakened from a dream;
though not established in the body, the foolish-minded man is body-bound, like one who sees a dream.

children.text: indriyair indriyārtheṣu guṇair api guṇeṣu ca
children.translated_text: When, by the senses, sense-objects are being grasped, and by the guṇas, the guṇas,

children.text: gṛhyamāṇeṣv ahaṃ kuryān na vidvān yas tv avikriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise man, being unchanged, should not think, 'I am doing this.'
In this body, which is dependent on fate, while action proceeds through what is produced by the guṇas,
the ignorant man there becomes bound by thinking, 'I am the doer.'
Thus detached, in lying down, sitting, wandering, and bathing,
and in seeing, touching, smelling, eating, hearing, and the rest,

children.text: na tathā badhyate vidvān tatra tatrādayan guṇān ||
children.translated_text: the wise man is not bound in the same way, perceiving the guṇas in each case.
Though situated in prakṛti, he is unattached, like space, the sun, or the wind;
his doubt has been cut off by the sharpness of clear vision sharpened by detachment,
and, like one awakened from dreams, he turns away from multiplicity.
One whose activities of vital breaths, senses, mind, and intellect are free from self-willed intention

children.text: vṛttayaḥ sa vinirmukto dehastho 'pi hi tadguṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: is fully liberated, even though dwelling in the body, from the qualities belonging to it.

children.text: yasyātmā hiṃsyate hiṃsrair yena kiṃcid yadṛcchayā
children.translated_text: When his self is injured by violent men, or when by chance he is somehow

children.text: arcyate vā kvacit tatra na vyatikriyate budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: honored somewhere, the wise man is not altered by it.

children.text: na stuvīta na nindeta kurvataḥ sādhv asādhu vā
children.translated_text: The sage, seeing equally and free from judgments of merit and fault,
should neither praise nor blame those who do good or bad actions, or those who speak.

children.text: na kuryān na vadet kiṃcin na dhyāyet sādhv asādhu vā
children.translated_text: He should do nothing, say nothing, and meditate on nothing as good or bad;
delighting in the self, the sage should move about with this way of life like an insensible man.

children.text: śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇāto na niṣṇāyāt pare yadi
children.translated_text: If one deeply versed in the verbal Brahman is not deeply immersed in the supreme,

children.text: śramas tasya śramaphalo hy adhenum iva rakṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: his labor has labor as its fruit, like that of one guarding a cow that gives no milk.

children.text: gāṃ dugdhadohām asatīṃ ca bhāryāṃ dehaṃ parādhīnam asatprajāṃ ca
children.translated_text: A cow whose milk has been milked out, an unfaithful wife, a body dependent on another, bad offspring,

children.text: vittaṃ tv atīrthīkṛtam aṅga vācaṃ hīnāṃ mayā rakṣati duḥkhaduḥkhī ||
children.translated_text: wealth not made sacred by offerings, O dear one, and speech devoid of me: one who guards these is miserable with suffering.

children.text: yasyāṃ na me pāvanam aṅga karma sthityudbhavaprāṇanirodham asya
children.translated_text: Speech in which there is no purifying deed of mine, O dear one, concerning the maintenance, arising, and cessation of this world,

children.text: līlāvatārepsitajanma vā syād vandhyāṃ giraṃ tāṃ bibhṛyān na dhīraḥ ||
children.translated_text: or my playful avatāra and desired birth, should not be sustained by a wise man; such speech is barren.
Thus, by inquiry, having removed the delusion of multiplicity in the self,

children.text: upārameta virajaṃ mano mayy arpya sarvage ||
children.translated_text: one should become tranquil, offering the stainless mind to me, who am all-pervading.

children.text: yady anīśo dhārayituṃ mano brahmaṇi niścalam
children.translated_text: If you are unable to hold the mind unmoving in Brahman,
then perform all actions in me, free from expectation.
Faithful, hearing my stories, which are very auspicious and purify the worlds,

children.text: gāyann anusmaran karma janma cābhinayan muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: singing and repeatedly remembering my deeds and birth, and enacting them,
practicing <s>dharma</s>, pleasure, and wealth for my sake, taking refuge in me,

children.text: labhate niścalāṃ bhaktiṃ mayy uddhava sanātane ||
children.translated_text: one obtains steady devotion to me, O <s>Uddhava</s>, the eternal one.

children.text: satsaṅgalabdhayā bhaktyā mayi māṃ sa upāsitā
children.translated_text: By devotion obtained through association with the good, he worships me in me;

children.text: sa vai me darśitaṃ sadbhir añjasā vindate padam ||
children.translated_text: indeed he easily attains the state shown by the good, which is mine.
<s>Śrī-Uddhava</s> said:
O Lord, O <s>Uttamaśloka</s>, what kind of person is regarded by you as a sādhu?

children.text: bhaktis tvayy upayujyeta kīdṛśī sadbhir ādṛtā ||
children.translated_text: And what kind of devotion to you is practiced and honored by the good?
Tell this to me, O overseer of persons, overseer of the worlds, lord of the universe,
to one who has bowed down, who is devoted to you, and who has taken refuge.

children.text: tvaṃ brahma paramaṃ vyoma puruṣaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: You are the supreme <s>brahman</s>, the highest heaven, the person beyond prakṛti;
O blessed Lord, you have descended, assuming distinct bodies by your own will.
The blessed Lord said:
Compassionate, harming none, forbearing toward all embodied beings,
firm in truth, blameless in self, even-minded, and beneficent to all,

children.text: kāmair ahatadhīr dānto mṛduḥ śucir akiñcanaḥ
children.translated_text: with his understanding unstruck by desires, self-controlled, gentle, pure, without possessions,

children.text: anīho mitabhuk śāntaḥ sthiro maccharaṇo muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: inactive in worldly striving, moderate in food, peaceful, steady, taking refuge in me, and a sage;
vigilant, deep in self, resolute, having conquered the six qualities,

children.text: amānī mānadaḥ kalyo maitraḥ kāruṇikaḥ kaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: not self-important, giving honor, skillful, friendly, compassionate, and wise;

children.text: ājñāyaivaṃ guṇān doṣān mayādiṣṭān api svakān
children.translated_text: having thus understood virtues and faults, even his own dharmas ordained by me,

children.text: dharmān saṃtyajya yaḥ sarvān māṃ bhajeta sa tu sattamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the one who abandons all dharmas and worships me is indeed the best of the good.

children.text: jñātvājñātvātha ye vai māṃ yāvān yaś cāsmi yādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who, whether knowing or not knowing how great I am, who I am, and what I am like,

children.text: bhajanty ananyabhāvena te me bhaktatamā matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: worship me with undivided feeling are considered by me the most devoted of my devotees.
Seeing, touching, and worshiping my emblem and my devotees,
service, praise, bowing down, and recounting my qualities and deeds,
faith in hearing my stories, meditation upon me, O <s>Uddhava</s>,
offering all gains to me and self-surrender in the role of a servant,
telling of my births and deeds, and approving my festival days,
festival worship in my house with assemblies for singing, dancing, and instrumental music,
pilgrimage and the arrangement of offerings at all annual festivals,
Vedic and Tantric initiation, and the taking up of vows belonging to me,
faith in installing my image, and effort undertaken either by oneself or together with others
in the work of gardens, groves, playgrounds, cities, and temples;
service to my house with sweeping and smearing, sprinkling water, and drawing maṇḍalas,
done for me like a servant, without deceit;
freedom from pride, freedom from hypocrisy, and not proclaiming what one has done;
one should not use even the light of a lamp offered to me for oneself.

children.text: yad yad iṣṭatamaṃ loke yac cātipriyam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever is most desired in the world, and whatever is especially dear to oneself,

children.text: tat tan nivedayen mahyaṃ tad ānantyāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: that very thing one should offer to me; that is fit for endless reward.

children.text: sūryo 'gnir brāhmaṇā gāvo vaiṣṇavaḥ khaṃ maruj jalam
children.translated_text: The sun, fire, brahmins, cows, a Vaiṣṇava, the sky, wind, water,

children.text: bhūr ātmā sarvabhūtāni bhadra pūjāpadāni me ||
children.translated_text: the earth, the self, and all beings, O good one, are places for my worship.

children.text: sūrye tu vidyayā trayyā haviṣāgnau yajeta mām
children.translated_text: In the sun one should worship me with the threefold knowledge, and in fire with oblation;

children.text: ātithyena tu viprāgrye goṣv aṅga yavasādinā ||
children.translated_text: in an excellent brahmin, with hospitality; among cows, dear one, with grass and the like;
in a Vaiṣṇava, with the respectful treatment of a kinsman; in the heart and sky, through firmness in meditation;
in wind, with the understanding of it as chief; in water, with substances preceded by water;
on the altar-ground, with the heart of mantras; in the self, with enjoyments offered within the self;
and in all beings one should worship me, the knower of the field, with equal regard.
In these seats one should meditate on my form, furnished with conch, discus, mace, and lotus,

children.text: yuktaṃ caturbhujaṃ śāntaṃ dhyāyann arcet samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: four-armed and peaceful, and worship it with collected mind.

children.text: iṣṭāpūrtena mām evaṃ yo yajeta samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever worships me thus with works of sacrifice and public benefaction, with collected mind,
obtains true devotion to me; remembrance of me comes through service to the good.
For the most part, O <s>Uddhava</s>, apart from the yoga of devotion and association with the good,

children.text: nopāyo vidyate samyak prāyaṇaṃ hi satām aham ||
children.translated_text: there is no proper means; for I am the final refuge of the good.
Now, O delight of the <s>Yadus</s>, I shall tell this supreme secret,

children.text: sugopyam api vakṣyāmi tvaṃ me bhṛtyaḥ suhṛt sakhā ||
children.translated_text: though it is very hidden, to you as you listen, for you are my servant, well-wisher, and friend.
The blessed Lord said:

children.text: na rodhayati māṃ yogo na sāṃkhyaṃ dharma eva ca
children.translated_text: Yoga does not hold me fast, nor Sāṃkhya, nor dharma itself,

children.text: na svādhyāyas tapas tyāgo neṣṭāpūrtaṃ na dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: nor recitation, austerity, renunciation, works of sacrifice and public benefaction, nor gifts.

children.text: vratāni yajñaś chandāṃsi tīrthāni niyamā yamāḥ
children.translated_text: Vows, sacrifices, Vedic meters, sacred places, observances, and restraints
do not hold me as association with the good does, for it removes every attachment.

children.text: satsaṅgena hi daiteyā yātudhānā mṛgāḥ khagāḥ
children.translated_text: Through association with the good, indeed, Daityas, sorcerous beings, animals, birds,
Gandharvas, Apsarases, Nāgas, Siddhas, Cāraṇas, and Guhyakas,
Vidyādharas, and among humans Vaiśyas, Śūdras, women, and outcastes,
those whose natures are made of passion and darkness, in each and every age,
many have attained my abode, such as <s>Tvāṣṭra</s>, <s>Kāyādhava</s>, and others,

children.text: vṛṣaparvā balir bāṇo mayaś cātha vibhīṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, <s>Maya</s>, and also <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: sugrīvo hanumān ṛkṣo gajo gṛdhro vaṇikpathaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>, the bear, the elephant, the vulture, the merchant,

children.text: vyādhaḥ kubjā vraje gopyo yajñapatnyas tathāpare ||
children.translated_text: the hunter, <s>Kubjā</s>, the cowherd women of <s>Vraja</s>, the wives of the sacrificers, and others.
They had not studied the collections of revelation, nor had they served the greatest ones;
without vows and without heated austerities, they reached me through association with me.

children.text: kevalena hi bhāvena gopyo gāvo nagā mṛgāḥ
children.translated_text: By feeling alone, the cowherd women, the cows, trees, and deer,

children.text: ye 'nye mūḍhadhiyo nāgāḥ siddhā mām īyur añjasā ||
children.translated_text: and others of dull understanding, including Nāgas and Siddhas, reached me easily.
That which even a strenuous person could not attain through yoga, Sāṃkhya, gifts, vows, austerities, or sacrifices,
nor through exposition, recitation, or renunciation,

children.text: rāmeṇa sārdhaṃ mathurāṃ praṇīte śvāphalkinā mayy anuraktacittāḥ
children.translated_text: when I was brought to <s>Mathurā</s> together with <s>Rāma</s> by <s>Śvāphalki</s>, their minds fixed in love on me,

children.text: vigāḍhabhāvena na me viyogatīvrādhayo 'nyaṃ dadṛśuḥ sukhāya ||
children.translated_text: those women, with deep feeling, saw nothing else as happiness because of the intense anguish of separation from me.

children.text: tās tāḥ kṣapāḥ preṣṭhatamena nītā mayaiva vṛndāvanagocareṇa
children.translated_text: Those nights that they had spent with their dearest beloved, with me roaming in the pasture-land of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,

children.text: kṣaṇārdhavat tāḥ punar aṅga tāsāṃ hīnā mayā kalpasamā babhūvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: passed for them like half a moment; but then, dear one, deprived of me, they became equal to an aeon.

children.text: tā nāvidan mayy anuṣaṅgabaddhadhiyaḥ svam ātmānam adas tathedam
children.translated_text: Their minds bound by attachment to me, they did not know their own self, nor this body and this world,

children.text: yathā samādhau munayo 'bdhitoye nadyaḥ praviṣṭā iva nāmarūpe ||
children.translated_text: just as sages in samādhi do not know name and form, like rivers entered into the water of the ocean.
Desiring me as a lover and an illicit paramour, those women, not knowing my true nature,

children.text: brahma māṃ paramaṃ prāpuḥ saṅgāc chatasahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they attained me, the supreme Brahman, by association, in hundreds of thousands.
Therefore, O <s>Uddhava</s>, abandon injunction and counter-injunction,

children.text: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca śrotavyaṃ śrutam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: both engagement and withdrawal, and what is to be heard and what has already been heard.

children.text: mām ekam eva śaraṇam ātmānaṃ sarvadehinām
children.translated_text: Go to me alone as refuge, the self of all embodied beings,

children.text: yāhi sarvātmabhāvena mayā syā hy akutobhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the disposition that I am the self of all; through me you will be fearless from every side.
<s>Śrī Uddhava</s> said:
As I hear your speech, O Lord of the lords of yoga,

children.text: na nivartata ātmastho yena bhrāmyati me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the doubt lodged in my self does not depart, by which my mind is bewildered.
<s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: sa eṣa jīvo vivaraprasūtiḥ prāṇena ghoṣeṇa guhāṃ praviṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: This very <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), born from the aperture, has entered the cave with breath and with sound;

children.text: manomayaṃ sūkṣmam upetya rūpaṃ mātrā svaro varṇa iti sthaviṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having assumed a subtle form made of mind, it becomes gross as measure, tone, and syllable.

children.text: yathānalaḥ khe 'nilabandhur uṣmā balena dāruṇy adhimathyamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as fire, whose ally is wind in space, is heat, and, when churned forcefully in wood,

children.text: aṇuḥ prajāto haviṣā samedhate tathaiva me vyaktir iyaṃ hi vāṇī ||
children.translated_text: is born minute and grows with oblation, so indeed is this manifestation of mine as speech.

children.text: evaṃ gadiḥ karma gatir visargo ghrāṇo raso dṛk sparśaḥ śrutiś ca
children.translated_text: Thus speech, action, motion, emission, smell, taste, sight, touch, and hearing,
intention, understanding, then self-conceit, the <s>sūtra</s> (cosmic thread), and the transformations of <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>tamas</s> arise.

children.text: ayaṃ hi jīvas trivṛd abjayonir avyakta eko vayasā sa ādyaḥ
children.translated_text: For this <s>jīva</s>, threefold and lotus-born, is the one unmanifest, ancient by age, and primordial;

children.text: viśliṣṭaśaktir bahudheva bhāti bījāni yoniṃ pratipadya yadvat ||
children.translated_text: with its powers divided, it appears as if manifold, just as seeds appear various when they enter a womb.

children.text: yasminn idaṃ protam aśeṣam otaṃ paṭo yathā tantuvitānasaṃsthaḥ
children.translated_text: In it all this is woven lengthwise and crosswise, as cloth is set in an expanse of threads;

children.text: ya eṣa saṃsārataruḥ purāṇaḥ karmātmakaḥ puṣpaphale prasūte ||
children.translated_text: this ancient tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), made of karma, brings forth flowers and fruits.

children.text: dve asya bīje śatamūlas trinālaḥ pañcaskandhaḥ pañcarasaprasūtiḥ
children.translated_text: It has two seeds, a hundred roots, three trunks, five stems, and produces five tastes;
it has eleven branches, a nest for two birds, three barks, two fruits, and it reaches the sun.

children.text: adanti caikaṃ phalam asya gṛdhrā grāmecarā ekam araṇyavāsāḥ
children.translated_text: The vultures, moving in the village, eat one fruit of it, and the forest-dwelling swans eat the other;

children.text: haṃsā ya ekaṃ bahurūpam ijyair māyāmayaṃ veda sa veda vedam ||
children.translated_text: whoever knows, through acts of worship, the one that is many-formed and made of <s>māyā</s>, he knows the <s>Veda</s>.
Thus, by serving the guru and by single-minded devotion, the wise man, with the sharpened axe of knowledge,

children.text: vivṛścya jīvāśayam apramattaḥ sampadya cātmānam atha tyajāstram ||
children.translated_text: should carefully cut through the abode of the <s>jīva</s>; then, having attained the self, he should cast away the weapon.
<s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: sattvaṃ rajas tama iti guṇā buddher na cātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are qualities of the intellect, not of the self.

children.text: sattvenānyatamau hanyāt sattvaṃ sattvena caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: By <s>sattva</s> one should destroy the other two, and then <s>sattva</s> itself by <s>sattva</s> alone.

children.text: sattvād dharmo bhaved vṛddhāt puṃso madbhaktilakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: From increased <s>sattva</s> there arises for a person <s>dharma</s> marked by devotion to me;
through a <s>sāttvika</s> mode of worship <s>sattva</s> grows, and from that <s>dharma</s> proceeds.

children.text: dharmo rajas tamo hanyāt sattvavṛddhir anuttamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> destroys <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>; the growth of <s>sattva</s> is unsurpassed.

children.text: āśu naśyati tanmūlo hy adharma ubhaye hate ||
children.translated_text: When both have been destroyed, <s>adharma</s>, whose root is in them, quickly perishes.

children.text: āgamo 'paḥ prajā deśaḥ kālaḥ karma ca janma ca
children.translated_text: Scripture, water, people, place, time, action, birth,
meditation, mantra, and purification: these ten are causes of the qualities.

children.text: tat tat sāttvikam evaiṣāṃ yad yad vṛddhāḥ pracakṣate
children.translated_text: Whatever among these the elders declare to be <s>sāttvika</s>, that is precisely <s>sāttvika</s>;

children.text: nindanti tāmasaṃ tat tad rājasaṃ tadupekṣitam ||
children.translated_text: whatever they condemn is <s>tāmasa</s>, and what they disregard is <s>rājasa</s>.
A person should resort only to <s>sāttvika</s> things for the increase of <s>sattva</s>;

children.text: tato dharmas tato jñānaṃ yāvat smṛtir apohanam ||
children.translated_text: from that comes <s>dharma</s>, from that knowledge, until memory and forgetfulness are overcome.
Fire born from the friction of bamboo burns that forest and then becomes quiet;
so the body, born from the alteration of the qualities, becomes quiet when its activity ceases.
<s>Śrī Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: vidanti martyāḥ prāyeṇa viṣayān padam āpadām
children.translated_text: Mortals generally know that sense-objects are the abode of calamities,

children.text: tathāpi bhuñjate kṛṣṇa tat kathaṃ śvakharājavat ||
children.translated_text: yet they still enjoy them, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; how is that, like dogs, donkeys, and goats?
<s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: aham ity anyathābuddhiḥ pramattasya yathā hṛdi
children.translated_text: For a heedless person, the mistaken understanding 'I am this' rises in the heart;

children.text: utsarpati rajo ghoraṃ tato vaikārikaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then terrible <s>rajas</s> surges upward, and from that comes the mutable mind.
For the mind joined with <s>rajas</s>, intention becomes full of alternatives;

children.text: tataḥ kāmo guṇadhyānād duḥsahaḥ syāddhi durmateḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, from meditation on the qualities, unbearable desire arises in one of poor judgment.
Subdued by desire and with unconquered senses, he performs actions,
though he sees that they end in suffering, because he is deluded by the force of <s>rajas</s>.

children.text: rajastamobhyāṃ yad api vidvān vikṣiptadhīḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Even if a wise man is again distracted in mind by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>,

children.text: atandrito mano yuñjan doṣadṛṣṭir na sajjate ||
children.translated_text: being diligent, fixing the mind, and seeing the fault, he does not become attached.
He should steadily practice, without negligence, gradually offering the mind to me,
not despondent, at the proper times, with breath mastered and posture mastered.
This much yoga was taught by my disciples, beginning with <s>Sanaka</s>:

children.text: sarvato mana ākṛṣya mayy addhāveśyate yathā ||
children.translated_text: how the mind, drawn back from every side, is placed directly in me.
<s>Śrī Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: yadā tvaṃ sanakādibhyo yena rūpeṇa keśava
children.translated_text: When you taught yoga to <s>Sanaka</s> and the others, O <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: yogam ādiṣṭavān etad rūpam icchāmi veditum ||
children.translated_text: in what form did you do so? I wish to know that form.
<s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> said:
<s>Sanaka</s> and the others, the mind-born sons of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>,
asked their father about the subtle and final goal of yoga.
<s>Sanaka</s> and the others said:

children.text: guṇeṣv āviśate ceto guṇāś cetasi ca prabho
children.translated_text: The mind enters into the qualities, and the qualities enter into the mind, O lord;
how can one seeking liberation and wishing to cross beyond abandon them mutually?
<s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> said:
Thus questioned, the great god <s>Svayambhū</s>, creator of beings,
though he contemplated the root of the question, did not arrive at an answer, for his intellect was occupied with creation.
That god thought of me, wishing to cross beyond the question;
then I went into his presence in the form of a <s>haṃsa</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā mām ta upavrajya kṛtvā pādābhivandanam
children.translated_text: Seeing me, they approached, made obeisance at my feet,

children.text: brahmāṇam agrataḥ kṛtvā papracchuḥ ko bhavān iti ||
children.translated_text: and, placing <s>Brahmā</s> in front, asked, 'Who are you?'

children.text: ity ahaṃ munibhiḥ pṛṣṭas tattvajijñāsubhis tadā
children.translated_text: Thus, when I was questioned at that time by the sages who wished to know reality,

children.text: yad avocam ahaṃ tebhyas tad uddhava nibodha me ||
children.translated_text: hear from me, O <s>Uddhava</s>, what I said to them.

children.text: vastuno yady anānātva ātmanaḥ praśna īdṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: If there is no manifoldness of the real, then such a question about the self

children.text: kathaṃ ghaṭeta vo viprā vaktur vā me ka āśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How could it apply to you, O brahmins, or what support would there be for me as speaker?
When the fivefold elements are in reality the same,

children.text: ko bhavān iti vaḥ praśno vācārambho hy anarthakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: your question, 'Who are you?', is merely a beginning made with words and is meaningless.
What is grasped by the mind, by speech, by sight, and also by the other senses

children.text: aham eva na matto 'nyad iti budhyadhvam añjasā ||
children.translated_text: is I alone; there is nothing apart from me. Understand this directly.

children.text: guṇeṣv āviśate ceto guṇāś cetasi ca prajāḥ
children.translated_text: The mind enters into the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature), O people, and the <s>guṇas</s> enter into the mind.

children.text: jīvasya deha ubhayaṃ guṇāś ceto madātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the living being whose self is me, the body consists of both: the <s>guṇas</s> and the mind.
Through constant service of the <s>guṇas</s>, the mind repeatedly enters into the <s>guṇas</s>,

children.text: guṇāś ca cittaprabhavā madrūpa ubhayaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>guṇas</s> arise from the mind; one should abandon both, which have me as their form.

children.text: jāgrat svapnaḥ suṣuptaṃ ca guṇato buddhivṛttayaḥ
children.translated_text: Waking, dream, and deep sleep are functions of the intellect caused by the <s>guṇas</s>;
the living being is determined to be distinct from them by being their witness.
When this bondage of transmigration, which gives rise to the functions of the <s>guṇas</s> for the self, is present,

children.text: mayi turye sthito jahyāt tyāgas tad guṇacetasām ||
children.translated_text: one established in me as the fourth state should abandon it; that is the renunciation of the <s>guṇas</s> and the mind.
The wise person, becoming disenchanted with the bondage made by ego,

children.text: vidvān nirvidya saṃsāracintāṃ turye sthitas tyajet ||
children.translated_text: which is a mistaken inversion of the self's true good, should abandon concern for saṃsāra while established in the fourth state.

children.text: yāvan nānārthadhīḥ puṃso na nivarteta yuktibhiḥ
children.translated_text: As long as a person's cognition of many objects is not turned back by reasoning,

children.text: jāgarty api svapann ajñaḥ svapne jāgaraṇaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: he is ignorant and dreaming even while awake, just as in dream there is an appearance of waking.
Because things other than the self are unreal, the distinctions produced by them,

children.text: gatayo hetavaś cāsya mṛṣā svapnadṛśo yathā ||
children.translated_text: and this one's courses and causes, are false, like those of a dreamer.

children.text: yo jāgare bahir anukṣaṇadharmiṇo 'rthān bhuṅkte samastakaraṇair hṛdi tatsadṛkṣān
children.translated_text: The one who, in waking, enjoys external objects that change at every moment with all the senses, and in the heart enjoys things resembling them,

children.text: svapne suṣupta upasaṃharate sa ekaḥ smṛtyanvayāt triguṇavṛttidṛg indriyeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who in dream and deep sleep withdraws them, is one, because memory continues; he is the seer of the functions of the three <s>guṇas</s> and the lord of the senses.

children.text: evaṃ vimṛśya guṇato manasas tryavasthā manmāyayā mayi kṛtā iti niścitārthāḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus examined the mind's three states as arising from the <s>guṇas</s>, and having determined that they have been made in me by my <s>māyā</s>,
cut away the heart's disease of all doubt with the sharp sword of knowledge, whetted by inference and true teaching, and worship me.

children.text: īkṣeta vibhramam idaṃ manaso vilāsaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vinaṣṭam atilolam alātacakram
children.translated_text: One should see this delusion as a play of the mind: seen and then destroyed, extremely unstable, like the circle of a whirling firebrand.

children.text: vijñānam ekam urudheva vibhāti māyā svapnas tridhā guṇavisargakṛto vikalpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The one consciousness appears as if manifold through <s>māyā</s>; dream is a threefold construction produced by the manifestation of the <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭim tataḥ pratinivartya nivṛttatṛṣṇas tūṣṇīṃ bhaven nijasukhānubhavo nirīhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, withdrawing one's sight from it, free from thirst, one should be silent, experiencing one's own happiness and without desire.

children.text: saṃdṛśyate kva ca yadīdam avastubuddhyā tyaktaṃ bhramāya na bhavet smṛtir ānipātāt ||
children.translated_text: If this is sometimes perceived through the notion of an unreal thing, then, once abandoned, it should not become delusion; only memory remains until the fall of the body.

children.text: dehaṃ ca naśvaram avasthitam utthitaṃ vā siddho na paśyati yato 'dhyagamat svarūpam
children.translated_text: A perfected one does not regard the perishable body, whether it is sitting or standing, because he has attained his own true form,

children.text: daivād apetam atha daivavaśād upetaṃ vāso yathā parikṛtaṃ madirāmadāndhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as a man blinded by the intoxication of liquor does not notice a garment put off by chance or put on under the power of chance.

children.text: deho 'pi daivavaśagaḥ khalu karma yāvat svārambhakaṃ pratisamīkṣata eva sāsuḥ
children.translated_text: The body too, indeed subject to fate, remains with the life-breaths as long as the karma that set it in motion lasts,

children.text: taṃ saprapañcam adhirūḍhasamādhiyogaḥ svāpnaṃ punar na bhajate pratibuddhavastuḥ ||
children.translated_text: but one who has mounted the yoga of samādhi and awakened to reality does not again resort to it with its whole display, as one does not return to a dream.

children.text: mayaitad uktaṃ vo viprā guhyaṃ yat sāṃkhyayogayoḥ
children.translated_text: This secret of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and yoga has been spoken by me to you, O brahmins.
Know that I, <s>Yajña</s>, have come because I wished to explain your dharma.
I am the supreme goal of yoga, of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, of truth, of cosmic order, and of splendor,

children.text: parāyaṇaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ śriyaḥ kīrter damasya ca ||
children.translated_text: O best of twice-born men, and also of fortune, fame, and self-restraint.

children.text: māṃ bhajanti guṇāḥ sarve nirguṇaṃ nirapekṣakam
children.translated_text: All qualities worship me, who am without <s>guṇas</s> and without dependence,
the friend, the beloved, the self; equanimity, nonattachment, and the rest are qualities beyond the <s>guṇas</s>.
Thus the sages, <s>Sanaka</s> and the others, had their doubts cut away by me,
and after honoring me with supreme devotion, they praised me with hymns.

children.text: tair ahaṃ pūjitaḥ samyak saṃstutaḥ paramarṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Properly worshiped by them and praised by those supreme seers,
I returned to my own abode while <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> looked on.
<s>Śrī Uddhava</s> said:
O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the expounders of brahman speak of many highest goods.
Among these, is there predominance of many alternatives, or is there one that is chief?
O master, you have declared a self-sufficient yoga of devotion,

children.text: nirasya sarvataḥ saṅgaṃ yena tvayy āviśen manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by which, casting off attachment from every side, the mind may enter into you.
The blessed Lord said:
In the dissolution, this speech known as the Veda was destroyed by time;

children.text: mayādau brahmaṇe proktā dharmo yasyāṃ madātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the beginning it was taught by me to <s>Brahmā</s>, and in it dharma has me as its self.

children.text: tena proktā svaputrāya manave pūrvajāya sā
children.translated_text: That speech was taught by him to his son, the first-born <s>Manu</s>;
then <s>Bhṛgu</s> and the others, the seven great brahmin seers, received it.
From those fathers, their sons received it: gods, demons, and <s>Guhyakas</s>,
human beings, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
<s>Kiṃdevas</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, serpents, <s>Rakṣases</s>, <s>Kiṃpuruṣas</s>, and others.
Their natures are many, born from <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: yābhir bhūtāni bhidyante bhūtānāṃ patayas tathā
children.translated_text: By these, beings are distinguished, and so too are the lords of beings;

children.text: yathāprakṛti sarveṣāṃ citrā vācaḥ sravanti hi ||
children.translated_text: according to each nature, varied teachings flow forth from all of them.
Thus, because of the diversity of natures, the opinions of men are divided.
Some are handed down by tradition, while others are doctrines of heresy.
Men whose minds are deluded by my <s>māyā</s>, O bull among men,
declare the highest good to be many-sided, according to their karma and according to their liking.

children.text: dharmam eke yaśaś cānye kāmaṃ satyaṃ damaṃ śamam
children.translated_text: Some declare it to be dharma, others fame, desire, truth, self-control, or tranquility;

children.text: anye vadanti svārthaṃ vā aiśvaryaṃ tyāgabhojanam
children.translated_text: others declare it to be self-interest, sovereignty, renunciation, or enjoyment.

children.text: kecid yajñaṃ tapo dānaṃ vratāni niyamān yamān ||
children.translated_text: Some declare sacrifice, austerity, giving, vows, observances, and restraints to be the highest good.
The worlds of these people, produced by karma, all have beginning and end.
They end in suffering, are fixed in darkness, petty and slow, and are consigned to grief.
For one whose self is offered to me, O noble one, and who is independent of everything,

children.text: mayātmanā sukhaṃ yat tat kutaḥ syād viṣayātmanām ||
children.translated_text: how could that happiness which comes through me, the self, belong to those whose selves are set on sense objects?
For one who owns nothing, who is controlled, peaceful, and equal-minded,
whose mind is satisfied through me, all directions are full of happiness.

children.text: na pārameṣṭhyaṃ na mahendradhiṣṇyaṃ na sārvabhaumaṃ na rasādhipatyam
children.translated_text: Neither the station of <s>Pārameṣṭhin</s>, nor the seat of great <s>Indra</s>, nor universal sovereignty, nor lordship over the nether realm,

children.text: na yogasiddhīr apunarbhavaṃ vā mayy arpitātmecchati mad vinānyat ||
children.translated_text: nor yogic powers, nor freedom from rebirth, does one whose self is offered to me desire as anything apart from me.

children.text: na tathā me priyatama ātmayonir na śaṃkaraḥ
children.translated_text: Neither <s>Ātmayoni</s> is so dear to me, nor <s>Śaṃkara</s>,

children.text: na ca saṃkarṣaṇo na śrīr naivātmā ca yathā bhavān ||
children.translated_text: nor <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, nor <s>Śrī</s>, nor even my own self, as you are.
I always follow the sage who is free from dependence, peaceful, without enmity, and equal in vision,
thinking, 'May I be purified by the dust of his feet.'
Those who own nothing, whose minds are attached to me, peaceful, great-souled, and affectionate toward all beings,

children.text: kāmair anālabdhadhiyo juṣanti te yan nairapekṣyaṃ na viduḥ sukhaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: enjoy in me that happiness of freedom from dependence which those whose minds are seized by desires do not know.
Even when troubled by sense-objects, my devotee, though his senses are unconquered,
is generally not overpowered by those objects because of his vigorous devotion.
As fire, when its flame is well kindled, turns fuel to ashes,
so devotion directed toward me, O <s>Uddhava</s>, burns sins completely.

children.text: na sādhayati māṃ yogo na sāṃkhyaṃ dharma uddhava
children.translated_text: Yoga does not attain me, nor Sāṃkhya, nor <s>dharma</s>, O <s>Uddhava</s>,

children.text: na svādhyāyas tapas tyāgo yathā bhaktir mamorjitā ||
children.translated_text: nor recitation, austerity, or renunciation, as does my powerful <s>bhakti</s> (devotion).

children.text: bhaktyāham ekayā grāhyaḥ śraddhayātmā priyaḥ satām
children.translated_text: I, the self dear to the good, am to be grasped by devotion alone, with faith;

children.text: bhaktiḥ punāti manniṣṭhā śvapākān api sambhavāt ||
children.translated_text: devotion fixed on me purifies even dog-cookers from birth.
<s>Dharma</s>, joined with truth and compassion, or knowledge accompanied by austerity,

children.text: madbhaktyāpetam ātmānaṃ na samyak prapunāti hi ||
children.translated_text: does not fully purify the self when it is deprived of devotion to me.

children.text: kathaṃ vinā romaharṣaṃ dravatā cetasā vinā
children.translated_text: How could the heart be purified without the hair standing on end, without the mind melting,
without a stream of tears of joy, and without devotion?

children.text: vāg gadgadā dravate yasya cittaṃ rudaty abhīkṣṇaṃ hasati kvacic ca
children.translated_text: He whose speech falters, whose mind melts, who weeps repeatedly and sometimes laughs,

children.text: vilajja udgāyati nṛtyate ca madbhaktiyukto bhuvanaṃ punāti ||
children.translated_text: who sings aloud without shame and dances too, being joined with devotion to me, purifies the world.

children.text: yathāgninā hema malaṃ jahāti dhmātaṃ punaḥ svaṃ bhajate ca rūpam
children.translated_text: As gold, heated by fire, abandons its impurity and again assumes its own form,

children.text: ātmā ca karmānuśayaṃ vidhūya madbhaktiyogena bhajaty atho mām ||
children.translated_text: so the self, shaking off the residue of karma through the yoga of devotion to me, then attains me.
As this self is more and more cleansed by hearing and reciting my meritorious stories,

children.text: tathā tathā paśyati vastu sūkṣmaṃ cakṣur yathaivāñjanasamprayuktam ||
children.translated_text: so it sees subtle reality, just as the eye does when treated with collyrium.
The mind of one who meditates on sense-objects becomes attached to sense-objects;

children.text: mām anusmarataś cittaṃ mayy eva pravilīyate ||
children.translated_text: the mind of one who remembers me dissolves into me alone.
Therefore, abandoning meditation on the unreal, like a dream or a fantasy,
fix your mind on me, made intent on my state.

children.text: strīṇāṃ strīsaṅgināṃ saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dūrata ātmavān
children.translated_text: Having abandoned from afar the company of women and of men attached to women, self-possessed,

children.text: kṣeme vivikta āsīnaś cintayen mām atandritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should sit in a secure, secluded place and meditate on me without sloth.

children.text: na tathāsya bhavet kleśo bandhaś cānyaprasaṅgataḥ
children.translated_text: For a man there is not such distress and bondage from attachment to anything else
as there is from association with women and from association with those attached to them.
<s>Śrī Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: yathā tvām aravindākṣa yādṛśaṃ vā yadātmakam
children.translated_text: O lotus-eyed one, in what way, in what form, and as being of what nature

children.text: dhyāyen mumukṣur etan me dhyānaṃ tvaṃ vaktum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: should one who desires liberation meditate on you? You ought to tell me this meditation.
The blessed Lord said:
Seated on an even seat, with the body held even, as comfortably as possible,
placing the two hands in the lap, with the gaze fixed on the tip of one's own nose,
one should purify the path of the breath by inhalation, retention, and exhalation;
also in the reverse order, one who has conquered the senses should practice gradually.
In the heart, one should raise by the breath the uninterrupted <s>oṃkāra</s> (syllable oṃ), sounding like a bell and fine like a lotus-fiber,
and then, there, cause the sound to enter again.
In this way one should repeatedly practice the breath joined with the <s>praṇava</s> (sacred syllable oṃ),
ten times at the three junctions of the day; within a month one becomes master of the breath.
One should meditate on the heart-lotus within, with its stalk upward and its face downward,
then as facing upward, opened, eight-petalled, and with a pericarp.
In the pericarp one should place sun, moon, and fire, each above the preceding one;
in the midst of the fire one should remember this form of mine, auspicious for meditation.
It is balanced, tranquil, gracious-faced, with four long and beautiful arms,
with a very lovely and handsome neck, fine cheeks, and a pure smile,
with glittering makara-earrings set evenly at the ears,
clad in golden garments, dark like a rain-cloud, bearing <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and as the abode of <s>Śrī</s>,
adorned with conch, discus, mace, lotus, and forest garland,
with feet shining with anklets and endowed with the radiance of the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem,
possessed of a brilliant crown, bracelets, girdle, and armlets,
beautiful in every limb, pleasing, with a gracious and pleasant gaze.
One should meditate on him as delicate, placing the mind on all his limbs.
Drawing the senses away from their objects by means of the mind,

children.text: buddhyā sārathinā dhīraḥ praṇayen mayi sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the steadfast one, with intellect as charioteer, should guide that mind wholly into me.
Drawing in that mind which ranges everywhere, one should hold it in a single place;

children.text: nānyāni cintayed bhūyaḥ susmitaṃ bhāvayen mukham ||
children.translated_text: one should not think of other things any more, but contemplate the smiling face.

children.text: tatra labdhapadaṃ cittam ākṛṣya vyomni dhārayet
children.translated_text: When the mind has gained a foothold there, one should draw it away and hold it in the sky;

children.text: tac ca tyaktvā madāroho na kiṃcid api cintayet ||
children.translated_text: and abandoning that too, having ascended to me, one should think of nothing at all.
Thus, with concentrated understanding, the yogin sees me alone, the self, within the self,

children.text: vicaṣṭe mayi sarvātman jyotir jyotiṣi saṃyutam ||
children.translated_text: in me, the Self of all, like light joined with light.
For the yogin who yokes the mind by such very intense meditation,
the delusion of substance, knowledge, and action will quickly pass into cessation.
The blessed Lord said:
For the yogin who has conquered the senses, is disciplined, and has conquered the breath,
As one fixes the mind on me, the siddhis (yogic powers) present themselves.
<s>Śrī Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: kayā dhāraṇayā kā svit kathaṃ vā siddhir acyuta
children.translated_text: By what dhāraṇā (concentration), O <s>Acyuta</s>, does which siddhi arise, and how?

children.text: kati vā siddhayo brūhi yogināṃ siddhido bhavān ||
children.translated_text: How many siddhis are there? Tell me, for you are the giver of siddhis to yogins.
The blessed Lord said:
Eighteen siddhis are taught by those who have gone to the far shore of yoga and dhāraṇā.
Of them, eight have me as their chief basis, and ten are caused by the guṇas (constituents of nature).

children.text: aṇimā mahimā mūrter laghimā prāptir indriyaiḥ
children.translated_text: Aṇimā (becoming minute), mahimā (becoming great) with respect to the body, laghimā (becoming light), and prāpti (reach) through the senses,
prākāmya (unhindered enjoyment) among things heard and seen, and īśitā, the power of impelling powers;

children.text: guṇeṣv asaṅgo vaśitā yatkāmas tad avasyati
children.translated_text: vaśitā (control), non-attachment among the guṇas, and the fulfillment of whatever one desires:

children.text: etā me siddhayaḥ saumya aṣṭāv autpattikā matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these, O gentle one, are considered my eight innate siddhis.
Freedom from the bodily waves, distant hearing and distant sight,
speed like the mind, taking any desired form, entering another body,
death at will, seeing and joining the play of the gods,
success according to one's resolve, and movement unobstructed by command,
knowledge of the three times, freedom from dualities, knowledge of others' minds and the like,
checking fire, sun, water, poison, and similar things, and invincibility:
these siddhis of yogic dhāraṇā have been stated in summary.

children.text: yayā dhāraṇayā yā syād yathā vā syān nibodha me ||
children.translated_text: Now learn from me by which dhāraṇā each one arises, and how it arises.
One should fix the mind on the tanmātra (subtle element) in me, the self of the subtle elements;
as a worshiper of my tanmātra, one obtains aṇimā.
Placing the mind, according to its true state, on me as the self of the great principle,

children.text: mahimānam avāpnoti bhūtānāṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: one obtains mahimā, and also the greatness of the elements one by one.
Suffusing the mind with me as the atomic form of the elements,
the yogin obtains subtlety with respect to the minuteness of time, and obtains laghimā.
Holding the whole mind on me in the vaikārika principle of egoity,
one whose mind is on me obtains prāpti, identity with all the senses.

children.text: mahaty ātmani yaḥ sūtre dhārayen mayi mānasam
children.translated_text: He who fixes his mind on me as the sūtra, the great self,
attains my supreme prākāmya, belonging to the one whose birth is the unmanifest.
One should fix the mind on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of the three, whose form is time;
he obtains īśitva, the power that impels the knower of the field and the field.
Setting the mind on me as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, called the fourth and denoted by the word 'blessed Lord',

children.text: mano mayy ādadhad yogī maddharmā vaśitām iyāt ||
children.translated_text: the yogin, having my nature, attains vaśitā.

children.text: nirguṇe brahmaṇi mayi dhārayan viśadaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: Fixing a clear mind on me, the qualityless Brahman,
one obtains supreme bliss, where desire comes to an end.
Fixing the mind on me, the lord of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, pure and made of dharma,
a man becomes white and pure, free from the six bodily waves.

children.text: mayy ākāśātmani prāṇe manasā ghoṣam udvahan
children.translated_text: Lifting sound with the mind in me, as the sky-self within prāṇa,

children.text: tatropalabdhā bhūtānāṃ haṃso vācaḥ śṛṇoty asau ||
children.translated_text: that haṃsa, perceiving it there, hears the speech of beings.

children.text: cakṣus tvaṣṭari saṃyojya tvaṣṭāram api cakṣuṣi
children.translated_text: Joining the eye to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> and <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> also to the eye,

children.text: māṃ tatra manasā dhyāyan viśvaṃ paśyati dūrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and meditating on me there with the mind, one sees the universe from afar.
Having well joined the mind to me, and the body to the wind that follows it,
by the power of concentration on me, the self is there wherever the mind is.

children.text: yadā mana upādāya yad yad rūpaṃ bubhūṣati
children.translated_text: When, taking up the mind, he wishes to become whatever form,

children.text: tat tad bhaven manorūpaṃ madyogabalam āśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he becomes that very mind-made form, relying on the strength of my yoga.

children.text: parakāyaṃ viśan siddha ātmānaṃ tatra bhāvayet
children.translated_text: Entering another body, the siddha should imagine himself there;

children.text: piṇḍaṃ hitvā viśet prāṇo vāyubhūtaḥ ṣaḍaṅghrivat ||
children.translated_text: leaving his own bodily mass, the breath, having become wind, enters like a bee.
Pressing the anus with the heel, he should raise the prāṇa through the heart, chest, throat, and head;
then, leading it through the aperture of Brahman to Brahman, he should abandon the body.
If he wishes to roam in the playground of the gods, he should contemplate sattva established in me;
then divine women whose activity is sattva attend him with an aerial car.

children.text: yathā saṃkalpayed buddhyā yadā vā matparaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: Whatever and whenever a man intent on me resolves with his intellect,

children.text: mayi satye mano yuñjaṃs tathā tat samupāśnute ||
children.translated_text: joining his mind to me, the true one, he obtains that accordingly.

children.text: yo vai madbhāvam āpanna īśitur vaśituḥ pumān
children.translated_text: A man who has attained my state, the state of the lord and controller,

children.text: kutaścin na vihanyeta tasya cājñā yathā mama ||
children.translated_text: is not obstructed from anywhere; his command is like mine.
For the yogin of pure sattva, purified by devotion to me and skilled in dhāraṇā,
his intelligence becomes threefold in time, embracing birth and death.

children.text: agnyādibhir na hanyeta muner yogamayaṃ vapuḥ
children.translated_text: Fire and the like do not injure the yoga-made body of the sage
whose mind has been pacified by my yoga, just as water does not injure aquatic beings.
Meditating on my manifestations, adorned with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and weapons,
with banners, parasols, and fans, he becomes unconquered.
For the sage who worships me in this way through yogic dhāraṇā,
the siddhis described before present themselves without remainder.
For the sage who has conquered the senses, is restrained, and has mastered breath and self,

children.text: maddhāraṇāṃ dhārayataḥ kā sā siddhiḥ sudurlabhā ||
children.translated_text: while he holds concentration on me, what siddhi is very difficult to obtain?

children.text: antarāyān vadanty etā yuñjato yogam uttamam
children.translated_text: These are said to be obstacles for one practicing the supreme yoga;
for one being perfected by me, they are causes for the wasting of time.
As many siddhis as there are here through birth, herbs, austerity, and mantras,

children.text: yogenāpnoti tāḥ sarvā nānyair yogagatiṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: one obtains all of them through yoga; by no other means does one reach the course of yoga.

children.text: sarvāsām api siddhīnāṃ hetuḥ patir ahaṃ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: I am the cause, the lord, the master of all siddhis.
I am the lord of yoga, Sāṃkhya, dharma, and of those who speak of Brahman.
I am the self of all embodied beings, within and without, uncovered.

children.text: yathā bhūtāni bhūteṣu bahir antaḥ svayaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: As the elements are in beings, outside and inside, so am I myself.
<s>Śrī Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: tvaṃ brahma paramaṃ sākṣād anādyantam apāvṛtam
children.translated_text: You are the supreme Brahman directly, without beginning or end, unobscured,
the source of the protection, continuance, dissolution, and arising of all beings.
Among beings high and low, you are hard to know by those whose selves are unrefined;
but brahmins worship you, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, according to reality.

children.text: yeṣu yeṣu ca bhūteṣu bhaktyā tvāṃ paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Tell me among which beings the supreme seers, worshipping you with devotion,

children.text: upāsīnāḥ prapadyante saṃsiddhiṃ tad vadasva me ||
children.translated_text: take refuge in you and attain complete perfection.
Hidden, you move as the self of beings, O soul of beings, O maker of beings;

children.text: na tvāṃ paśyanti bhūtāni paśyantaṃ mohitāni te ||
children.translated_text: beings, deluded by you, do not see you, though you see them.

children.text: yāḥ kāś ca bhūmau divi vai rasāyāṃ vibhūtayo dikṣu mahāvibhūte
children.translated_text: Whatever manifestations there are on earth, in heaven, in the nether realm, and in the directions, O greatly manifest one,

children.text: tā mahyam ākhyāhy anubhāvitās te namāmi te tīrthapadāṅghripadmam ||
children.translated_text: tell them to me as powers set in motion by you. I bow to the lotus of your feet, whose steps are sacred fords.
The blessed Lord said:

children.text: evam etad ahaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ praśnaṃ praśnavidāṃ vara
children.translated_text: Thus I was asked this question, O best of those who know how to ask,
by <s>Arjuna</s>, who wished to fight at the time of destruction against his rivals.
Having understood that killing his kinsmen for the sake of kingship was blameworthy <s>adharma</s>,

children.text: tato nivṛtto hantāhaṃ hato 'yam iti laukikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he then drew back, thinking in worldly terms, 'I am the killer, and this one is killed.'

children.text: sa tadā puruṣavyāghro yuktyā me pratibodhitaḥ
children.translated_text: That tiger among men was then awakened by me through reasoning,

children.text: abhyabhāṣata mām evaṃ yathā tvaṃ raṇamūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: and he addressed me just as you do now, on the field of battle.
I am the self, O <s>Uddhava</s>, the friend and lord of these beings;
I am all beings, and their continuance, arising, and passing away.

children.text: ahaṃ gatir gatimatāṃ kālaḥ kalayatām aham
children.translated_text: I am the goal of those who move; I am time among those who reckon.

children.text: guṇāṇāṃ cāpy ahaṃ sāmyaṃ guṇiny autpattiko guṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among the <s>guṇa</s>s (constituent qualities) I am equilibrium, and in what possesses qualities I am the innate quality.

children.text: guṇinām apy ahaṃ sūtraṃ mahatāṃ ca mahān aham
children.translated_text: Among things possessing qualities I am the thread-principle, and among great principles I am the great one.

children.text: sūkṣmāṇām apy ahaṃ jīvo durjayānām ahaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among subtle things I am the <s>jīva</s> (living self); among the hard to conquer I am the mind.
Among the Vedas I am <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>; among mantras I am the threefold <s>praṇava</s>.
Among syllables I am the letter a; among meters I am their metrical feet.
I am <s>Indra</s> among all gods; among the <s>Vasu</s>s I am <s>Havyavāṭ</s>.
Among the <s>Āditya</s>s I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>; among the <s>Rudra</s>s I am <s>Nīlalohita</s>.

children.text: brahmarṣīṇāṃ bhṛgur ahaṃ rājarṣīṇām ahaṃ manuḥ
children.translated_text: Among brahmin seers I am <s>Bhṛgu</s>; among royal seers I am <s>Manu</s>.
Among divine seers I am <s>Nārada</s>; among cows I am the one rich in oblation.
Among lords of the perfected I am <s>Kapila</s>; among birds I am <s>Suparṇa</s>.
Among progenitors I am <s>Dakṣa</s>; among the fathers I am <s>Aryaman</s>.

children.text: māṃ viddhy uddhava daityānāṃ prahlādam asureśvaram
children.translated_text: Know me, O <s>Uddhava</s>, among the Daityas as <s>Prahlāda</s>, lord of the Asuras;
as <s>Soma</s> among constellations and herbs, and as the Lord of Wealth among Yakṣas and Rākṣasas.
Among lordly elephants I am <s>Airāvata</s>; among aquatic beings I am <s>Varuṇa</s>, the lord.

children.text: tapatāṃ dyumatāṃ sūryaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ca bhūpatim ||
children.translated_text: Among things that heat and shine I am the sun, and among human beings the king.
Among horses I am <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>; among metals I am gold.

children.text: yamaḥ saṃyamatāṃ cāham sarpāṇām asmi vāsukiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among those who restrain I am <s>Yama</s>, and among serpents I am <s>Vāsuki</s>.
Among chief Nāgas I am <s>Ananta</s>; among horned and fanged beasts I am the lion.
Among life-stages I am the fourth, and among social classes the first, O sinless one.

children.text: tīrthānāṃ srotasāṃ gaṅgā samudraḥ sarasām aham
children.translated_text: Among sacred fords and rivers I am the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; among waters I am the ocean.
Among weapons I am the bow; among bowmen I am <s>Tripuraghna</s>.

children.text: dhiṣṇyānām asmy ahaṃ merur gahanānāṃ himālayaḥ
children.translated_text: Among fixed abodes I am <s>Meru</s>; among rugged regions I am the <s>Himālaya</s>.
Among forest trees I am the <s>aśvattha</s>; among cultivated plants I am barley.
Among household priests I am <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; among those most devoted to sacred knowledge I am <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Among all commanders I am <s>Skanda</s>; among foremost leaders I am the blessed <s>Aja</s>.
Among sacrifices I am the <s>brahmayajña</s> (sacrifice of sacred recitation); among vows I am non-injury.
Among purifying things I am the purifier whose self is wind, fire, sun, water, and speech.
Among yogas I am restraint of the self; among those who wish to conquer I am counsel.
Among disciplines of skill I am <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (critical inquiry); among theorists I am discriminating analysis.

children.text: strīṇāṃ tu śatarūpāhaṃ puṃsāṃ svāyambhuvo manuḥ
children.translated_text: Among women I am <s>Śatarūpā</s>, and among men I am <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>.
Among sages I am <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and among celibates I am <s>Kumāra</s>.
Among forms of <s>dharma</s> I am <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation); among safeguards I am a mind not turned outward.

children.text: guhyānāṃ sūnṛtaṃ maunaṃ mithunānām ajas tv aham ||
children.translated_text: Among secrets I am truthful pleasant speech and silence; among pairs I am the unborn one.
Among the unwinking gods I am the year; among seasons I am <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>.
Among months I am <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, and among constellations likewise <s>Abhijit</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ yugānāṃ ca kṛtaṃ dhīrāṇāṃ devalo 'sitaḥ
children.translated_text: Among ages I am the <s>Kṛta</s>; among the steadfast I am <s>Devala</s> and <s>Asita</s>.
Among the Vyāsas I am <s>Dvaipāyana</s>; among poets I am self-possessed <s>Kāvya</s>.

children.text: vāsudevo bhagavatāṃ tvaṃ tu bhāgavateṣv aham
children.translated_text: Among the blessed I am <s>Vāsudeva</s>; but among the Bhāgavatas, you are I.
Among the Kimpuruṣas I am <s>Hanumān</s>; among the Vidyādharas I am <s>Sudarśana</s>.
Among jewels I am the ruby; among beautiful things I am the lotus bud.

children.text: kuśo 'smi darbhajātīnāṃ gavyam ājyaṃ haviḥṣv aham ||
children.translated_text: Among kinds of darbha grass I am <s>kuśa</s>; among oblations I am ghee from the cow.
Among the enterprising I am <s>Lakṣmī</s>; among gamblers I am seizure by deceit.
Among the forbearing I am forbearance; among those rich in <s>sattva</s> I am <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: ojaḥ saho balavatāṃ karmāhaṃ viddhi sātvatām
children.translated_text: Know me as the vigor, endurance, and strength of the strong, and as the action of the Sātvatas.
Among the nine forms of the Sātvatas, I am the first and supreme form.
Among Gandharvas and Apsarases I am <s>Viśvāvasu</s> and <s>Pūrvacitti</s>.

children.text: bhūdharāṇām ahaṃ sthairyaṃ gandhamātram ahaṃ bhuvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among mountains I am stability; I am the mere scent of the earth.

children.text: apāṃ rasaś ca paramas tejiṣṭhānāṃ vibhāvasuḥ
children.translated_text: I am the supreme taste of waters; among the most brilliant I am fire.
I am the light of sun, moon, and stars; I am the supreme sound of the sky.

children.text: brahmaṇyānāṃ balir ahaṃ vīrāṇām aham arjunaḥ
children.translated_text: Among those devoted to brahman I am <s>Bali</s>; among heroes I am <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: bhūtānāṃ sthitir utpattir ahaṃ vai pratisaṃkramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am the continuance, arising, and reabsorption of beings.
Going, speaking, excretion, grasping, pleasure, and touch as their marks,
taste, hearing, and smell: I am the faculty of every sense.

children.text: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśa āpo jyotir ahaṃ mahān
children.translated_text: Earth, wind, sky, waters, and light: I am the great principle.

children.text: vikāraḥ puruṣo 'vyaktaṃ rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaḥ param
children.translated_text: I am modification, <s>puruṣa</s>, the unmanifest, <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, <s>tamas</s>, and the supreme.
I am this enumeration, knowledge, and ascertainment of reality.
Apart from me as lord, as the <s>jīva</s>, as quality and as possessor of qualities,

children.text: sarvātmanāpi sarveṇa na bhāvo vidyate kvacit ||
children.translated_text: there is no entity anywhere at all, in any form whatsoever.
The counting of atoms is done by me in time,

children.text: na tathā me vibhūtīnāṃ sṛjato 'ṇḍāni koṭiśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but not so the counting of my manifestations, as I create cosmic eggs by the tens of millions.

children.text: tejaḥ śrīḥ kīrtir aiśvaryaṃ hrīs tyāgaḥ saubhagaṃ bhagaḥ
children.translated_text: Brilliance, prosperity, fame, sovereignty, modesty, renunciation, good fortune, lordly power,

children.text: vīryaṃ titikṣā vijñānaṃ yatra yatra sa me 'ṃśakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: heroic strength, endurance, and knowledge: wherever these are found, that is a portion of me.

children.text: etās te kīrtitāḥ sarvāḥ saṃkṣepeṇa vibhūtayaḥ
children.translated_text: All these manifestations have been described to you briefly.
They are only modifications of the mind, insofar as they are denoted by speech.

children.text: vācaṃ yaccha mano yaccha prāṇān yacchendriyāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Restrain speech; restrain the mind; restrain the life-breaths and the senses.

children.text: ātmānam ātmanā yaccha na bhūyaḥ kalpase 'dhvane ||
children.translated_text: Restrain the self by the self; then you will no longer be destined for the road of transmigration.

children.text: yo vai vāṅmanasī samyag asaṃyacchan dhiyā yatiḥ
children.translated_text: The ascetic who does not properly restrain speech and mind with his understanding

children.text: tasya vrataṃ tapo dānaṃ sravaty āmaghaṭāmbuvat ||
children.translated_text: has his vow, austerity, and gift leak away like water from an unbaked pot.

children.text: tasmād vaco manaḥ prāṇān niyacchen matparāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore one devoted to me should restrain speech, mind, and life-breaths
with an understanding joined to devotion to me; then he reaches completion.
<s>Śrī Uddhava</s> said:
The <s>dharma</s> you previously described as marked by devotion to you,
for all human beings who observe the conduct of the <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>,
by practicing which people would come to have devotion to you,
through their own <s>dharma</s>, O lotus-eyed one: please explain that to me.

children.text: purā kila mahābāho dharmaṃ paramakaṃ prabho
children.translated_text: Formerly, O mighty-armed lord, O master,
that supreme <s>dharma</s> which, in your form as the swan, you taught to <s>Brahmā</s>, O <s>Mādhava</s>,
now, after a very long time, O scorcher of enemies,

children.text: na prāyo bhavitā martyaloke prāg anuśāsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will mostly not remain in the mortal world as it was instructed before.

children.text: vaktā kartāvitā nānyo dharmasyācyuta te bhuvi
children.translated_text: There is no other speaker, performer, or protector of <s>dharma</s> than you on earth, O <s>Acyuta</s>,

children.text: sabhāyām api vairiñcyāṃ yatra mūrtidharāḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor even in the assembly of <s>Vairiñca</s>, where your embodied portions are present.
When you, its maker, protector, and teacher, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>,

children.text: tyakte mahītale deva vinaṣṭaṃ kaḥ pravakṣyati ||
children.translated_text: have abandoned the earth, O god, who will teach it when it is lost?

children.text: tat tvaṃ naḥ sarvadharmajña dharmas tvadbhaktilakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, you who know all <s>dharmas</s>, tell us the <s>dharma</s> marked by devotion to you,

children.text: yathā yasya vidhīyeta tathā varṇaya me prabho ||
children.translated_text: describing how it should be prescribed for each person, O lord.
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: itthaṃ svabhṛtyamukhyena pṛṣṭaḥ sa bhagavān hariḥ
children.translated_text: Thus questioned by the foremost of his servants, that blessed <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: prītaḥ kṣemāya martyānāṃ dharmān āha sanātanān ||
children.translated_text: pleased, spoke the eternal <s>dharmas</s> for the welfare of mortals.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: dharmya eṣa tava praśno naiḥśreyasakaro nṛṇām
children.translated_text: This question of yours is righteous and brings the highest good to human beings;
O <s>Uddhava</s>, hear from me that teaching for those who observe the conduct of the <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>.

children.text: ādau kṛtayuge varṇo nṛṇāṃ haṃsa iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: At the beginning, in the Kṛta age, the single <s>varṇa</s> of human beings was remembered as <s>Haṃsa</s>.

children.text: kṛtakṛtyāḥ prajā jātyā tasmāt kṛtayugaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: People were accomplished in their duties by birth; therefore they know it as the Kṛta age.
In the beginning the Veda was only the praṇava; <s>dharma</s> was I, bearing the form of a bull.
Those devoted to austerity, freed from sin, worshiped me, the <s>Haṃsa</s>.

children.text: tretāmukhe mahābhāga prāṇān me hṛdayāt trayī
children.translated_text: At the opening of the Tretā age, O very fortunate one, from my life-breath and heart

children.text: vidyā prādurabhūt tasyā aham āsaṃ trivṛn makhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the threefold knowledge appeared; from it I became the threefold sacrifice.
Brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras were born from the mouth, arms, thighs, and feet
of the cosmic <s>Puruṣa</s>, the <s>Virāj</s>, each marked by its own conduct.
The householder's <s>āśrama</s> arose from my loins, brahmacarya from my heart,
forest dwelling from my chest, and renunciation stood in my head.
The dispositions of men followed the birthplaces
of the <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>: lower in the lower, and higher in the higher.

children.text: śamo damas tapaḥ śaucaṃ saṃtoṣaḥ kṣāntir ārjavam
children.translated_text: Tranquility, restraint, austerity, purity, contentment, forbearance, straightforwardness,

children.text: madbhaktiś ca dayā satyaṃ brahmaprakṛtayas tv imāḥ ||
children.translated_text: devotion to me, compassion, and truth: these are the brahmin dispositions.

children.text: tejo balaṃ dhṛtiḥ śauryaṃ titikṣaudāryam udyamaḥ
children.translated_text: Splendor, strength, firmness, valor, endurance, generosity, enterprise,

children.text: sthairyaṃ brahmaṇyam aiśvaryaṃ kṣatraprakṛtayas tv imāḥ ||
children.translated_text: steadfastness, reverence for the sacred, and lordship: these are the kṣatriya dispositions.
Belief in sacred authority, devotion to giving, absence of hypocrisy, service to brahmins,
and dissatisfaction with the mere accumulation of wealth: these are the vaiśya dispositions.
Sincere service to twice-born men, cows, and gods, without deceit,

children.text: tatra labdhena saṃtoṣaḥ śūdraprakṛtayas tv imāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and contentment with what is obtained thereby: these are the śūdra dispositions.
Impurity, falsehood, theft, disbelief, barren quarrelsomeness,

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhaś ca tarṣaś ca sa bhāvo 'ntyāvasāyinām ||
children.translated_text: desire, anger, and craving: this is the nature of those who dwell at the lowest end.
Nonviolence, truth, nonstealing, freedom from desire, anger, and greed,
and effort for what is dear and beneficial to beings: this <s>dharma</s> belongs to all <s>varṇas</s>.
After receiving, in due order, a second birth through initiation, a twice-born man
should live controlled in the guru's household and study the Veda when summoned.
He should carry a girdle, deerskin, staff, rosary, sacred thread, and water-pot,
with matted hair, unwashed teeth and clothing, no dyed seat, and kuśa grass.
In bathing, eating, fire-offerings, recitation, and uttering japa, he should keep speech restrained.
He should not cut his nails or hair, even those in the armpits and private parts.
A keeper of the vow of brahmacarya should never spill semen intentionally.
If it has been spilled, he should bathe in water, restrain his breath, and recite the three-footed verse.
Pure and collected, he should worship fire, the sun, the teacher, cows, brahmins, the guru, elders, and gods

children.text: samāhita upāsīta saṃdhye dve yatavāg japan ||
children.translated_text: at the two twilights, with speech restrained, while reciting japa.
He should know the teacher to be me and should never disrespect him.
He should not resent him with the thought that he is mortal, for the guru contains all the gods.

children.text: sāyaṃ prātar upānīya bhaikṣyaṃ tasmai nivedayet
children.translated_text: In the evening and morning he should bring alms and present them to him.

children.text: yac cānyad apy anujñātam upayuñjīta saṃyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And whatever else is permitted, he should use with restraint.
Intent on serving the teacher, he should always attend upon him like a lowly servant,
standing with joined hands, not too far away, when he is traveling, lying down, sitting, or standing.
Conducting himself in this way, he should live in the guru's household, free from enjoyment,

children.text: vidyā samāpyate yāvad bibhrad vratam akhaṇḍitam ||
children.translated_text: bearing his vow unbroken until his learning is completed.

children.text: yady asau chandasāṃ lokam ārokṣyan brahmaviṣṭapam
children.translated_text: If he wishes to ascend to the world of the Vedas, the abode of brahman,
then, keeping the great vow, he should dedicate his body to the guru for the sake of sacred study.

children.text: agnau gurāv ātmani ca sarvabhūteṣu māṃ param
children.translated_text: In fire, in the teacher, in oneself, and in all beings, one should worship me as supreme,
with understanding that does not divide me from them, endowed with brahmanical radiance and free from stain.
Looking at women, touching them, conversing with them, joking with them, and the like,
and living beings paired for mating, one who is not a householder should avoid from before him.
Purity, sipping water, bathing, worship at the twilights, and worship of me,
service at sacred fords, recitation, and avoidance of the untouchable, the uneatable, and those with whom one should not converse:
this rule is prescribed for all the <s>āśramas</s>, O joy of the family,
namely, seeing my presence in all beings and restraining mind, speech, and body.
Thus the brāhmaṇa who keeps the great vow, blazing like fire,
my devotee, pure through intense austerity, burns up the latent store of karma.
Then afterward, having studied the sacred tradition as he wished to know it,
having given a fee to the teacher, he should bathe, with the teacher's approval.

children.text: gṛhaṃ vanaṃ vopaviśet pravrajed vā dvijottamaḥ
children.translated_text: O best of the twice-born, he may enter the house, the forest, or renunciation,
or he may pass from one <s>āśrama</s> to another; devoted to me, he should not act otherwise.
If he desires the household life, he should marry a suitable wife who is not objectionable,

children.text: yavīyasīṃ tu vayasā yaṃ savarṇām anu kramāt ||
children.translated_text: younger than himself in age and of the same varṇa, in due order.
Sacrifice, study, and giving are for all the twice-born,
but receiving gifts, teaching, and officiating at sacrifice belong to the brāhmaṇa alone.
If he regards receiving gifts as taking away austerity, brilliance, and fame,

children.text: anyābhyām eva jīveta śilair vā doṣadṛk tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should live by the other two; if he sees fault in those as well, then by gleaning grains.
For this body of a brāhmaṇa is not intended for petty desire,
but for hardship and austerity here, and for endless happiness after death.

children.text: śiloñchavṛttyā parituṣṭacitto dharmaṃ mahāntaṃ virajaṃ juṣāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Content in the livelihood of gleaning, embracing the great stainless <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),

children.text: mayy arpitātmā gṛha eva tiṣṭhan nātiprasaktaḥ samupaiti śāntim ||
children.translated_text: with his self offered to me, remaining at home and not overly attached, he attains peace.
Those who rescue a brāhmaṇa who is sinking and is devoted to me,

children.text: tān uddhariṣye na cirād āpadbhyo naur ivārṇavāt ||
children.translated_text: I will rescue them before long from calamities, like a boat from the ocean.

children.text: sarvāḥ samuddhared rājā piteva vyasanāt prajāḥ
children.translated_text: The king should rescue all his subjects from distress, like a father,

children.text: ātmānam ātmanā dhīro yathā gajapatir gajān ||
children.translated_text: and the wise man should rescue himself by himself, as the lord of elephants rescues elephants.
A king of this kind, in an aerial car shining like the sun,
shaking off all evil here, rejoices together with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: sīdan vipro vaṇigvṛttyā paṇyair evāpadaṃ taret
children.translated_text: A brāhmaṇa in distress may cross over calamity by a merchant's livelihood, with goods,
or, when overwhelmed by danger, by the sword, but never in any way by a servile livelihood.
A ruler may live by a vaiśya's livelihood, or by hunting, in time of distress,

children.text: cared vā viprarūpeṇa na śvavṛttyā kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: or he may conduct himself in the manner of a brāhmaṇa, but never in any way by a servile livelihood.
A vaiśya may resort to a śūdra's livelihood, and a śūdra to the work of artisanship;

children.text: kṛcchrān mukto na garhyeṇa vṛttiṃ lipseta karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: when freed from difficulty, one should not seek a livelihood through blameworthy action.
With Vedic recitation, offerings of <s>svadhā</s> and <s>svāhā</s>, bali-offerings, food, and the like, as they arise,
one should daily worship the gods, seers, ancestors, and beings as forms of me.
With wealth that has come by chance, or that has been acquired by pure means,
without oppressing one's dependents, one should properly perform sacrifices according to rule.

children.text: kuṭumbeṣu na sajjeta na pramādyet kuṭumby api
children.translated_text: One should not cling to family, and even while having a family one should not be negligent;

children.text: vipaścin naśvaraṃ paśyed adṛṣṭam api dṛṣṭavat ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should see what is unseen as perishable, just like what is seen.
The meeting of sons, wives, close friends, and kinsmen is a meeting of travelers;

children.text: anudehaṃ viyanty ete svapno nidrānugo yathā ||
children.translated_text: with each body these go apart, as a dream follows upon sleep.

children.text: itthaṃ parimṛśan mukto gṛheṣv atithivad vasan
children.translated_text: Reflecting in this way, liberated, dwelling in houses like a guest,
one should not be bound by houses, being free from possessiveness and egoism.

children.text: karmabhir gṛhamedhīyair iṣṭvā mām eva bhaktimān
children.translated_text: Having worshipped me alone through the rites of a householder, full of devotion,

children.text: tiṣṭhed vanaṃ vopaviśet prajāvān vā parivrajet ||
children.translated_text: he should remain, or enter the forest; or, having offspring, he may become a wandering renunciant.
But he whose mind is attached to the house, tormented by longing for sons and wealth,

children.text: straiṇaḥ kṛpaṇadhīr mūḍho mamāham iti badhyate ||
children.translated_text: subservient to women, poor-minded, and deluded, is bound by the thought 'mine' and 'I.'

children.text: aho me pitarau vṛddhau bhāryā bālātmajātmajāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Alas, my parents are old, my wife, my young children and grandchildren

children.text: anāthā mām ṛte dīnāḥ kathaṃ jīvanti duḥkhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are helpless, wretched, and miserable without me; how will they live?'
Thus, this foolish-minded man, whose heart is seized by attachment to the house,

children.text: atṛptas tān anudhyāyan mṛto 'ndhaṃ viśate tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: dies unsatisfied while brooding on them, and enters blind darkness.
The blessed Lord said:

children.text: vanaṃ vivikṣuḥ putreṣu bhāryāṃ nyasya sahaiva vā
children.translated_text: Wishing to enter the forest, having entrusted his wife to his sons, or taking her along with him,

children.text: vana eva vasec chāntas tṛtīyaṃ bhāgam āyuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should dwell in the forest, peaceful, during the third part of his life.
He should arrange his livelihood from pure forest roots, bulbs, and fruits,
and should wear bark garments, or grass, leaves, or deerskins.
He should bear his hair, body hair, nails, beard, and dirt, self-controlled;

children.text: na dhāved apsu majjeta trikālaṃ sthaṇḍileśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should not groom himself, should plunge into water three times a day, and should sleep on the bare ground.

children.text: grīṣme tapyeta pañcāgnīn varṣāsv āsāraṣāḍ jale
children.translated_text: In summer he should heat himself among the five fires; in the rains he should endure the downpour;

children.text: ākaṇṭhamagnaḥ śiśira evaṃ vṛttas tapaś caret ||
children.translated_text: in winter he should remain sunk in water up to the neck. Living in this way, he should practice austerity.
He may eat what is cooked by fire, or else what is ripened by time,
or what is pounded with mortar and stone, or even using his teeth as the mortar.
