He should gather everything himself for the sake of his own livelihood,
knowing place, time, and strength; he should not accept what has been brought by another.
With forest-grown <s>caru</s> and <s>puroḍāśa</s> offerings he should make the oblations prescribed for the proper times,

children.text: na tu śrautena paśunā māṃ yajeta vanāśramī ||
children.translated_text: but the forest-dweller should not worship me with a Vedic animal sacrifice.

children.text: agnihotraṃ ca darśaś ca paurṇamāsaś ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: The <s>agnihotra</s>, the new-moon sacrifice, and the full-moon sacrifice are as before,

children.text: cāturmāsyāni ca muner āmnātāni ca naigamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the <s>cāturmāsya</s> rites, prescribed for the sage by the Vedic texts.
By austerity practiced in this way, the sage, reduced to a network of veins,

children.text: māṃ tapomayam ārādhya ṛṣilokād upaiti mām ||
children.translated_text: having worshipped me as consisting of austerity, passes from the world of seers to me.

children.text: yas tv etat kṛcchrataś cīrṇaṃ tapo niḥśreyasaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: But whoever would apply this austerity, difficult to perform and great as a means to final good,
to some petty desire: what fool could be worse than he?
When, in that observance, he is no longer capable and has begun to tremble from old age,
Having installed the sacred fires within himself, with his mind fixed on me, he should enter into the fire.
When true dispassion arises toward the worlds that are the results of action

children.text: virāgo jāyate samyaṅ nyastāgniḥ pravrajet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and are hellish in nature, then, having laid down the fires, he should renounce.

children.text: iṣṭvā yathopadeśaṃ māṃ dattvā sarvasvam ṛtvije
children.translated_text: Having worshiped me according to instruction and given all his possessions to the officiating priest,
he should place the fires in his own breath and wander forth without dependence.
When a brahmin is renouncing, the gods, taking the form of wife and the like,

children.text: vighnān kurvanty ayaṃ hy asmān ākramya samiyāt param ||
children.translated_text: create obstacles, thinking, 'This man will pass beyond us and go to the supreme.'

children.text: bibhṛyāc cen munir vāsaḥ kaupīnācchādanaṃ param
children.translated_text: If the sage wears clothing, it should be no more than a loincloth and a covering;

children.text: tyaktaṃ na daṇḍapātrābhyām anyat kiṃcid anāpadi ||
children.translated_text: apart from staff and bowl, he should keep nothing else except in distress.

children.text: dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyaset pādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ pibej jalam
children.translated_text: He should set down his foot purified by sight, and drink water purified through a cloth.
He should speak words purified by truth, and act with a mind made pure.
Silence, non-activity, and control of breath are the staffs of speech, body, and mind.

children.text: na hy ete yasya santy aṅga veṇubhir na bhaved yatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who does not have these, dear one, does not become a <s>yati</s> merely by bamboo staffs.

children.text: bhikṣāṃ caturṣu varṇeṣu vigarhyān varjayaṃś caret
children.translated_text: He should go for alms among the four <s>varṇas</s>, avoiding censured households,
and should be content with just what is obtained from seven houses not prearranged.
Going outside to a reservoir, touching water there, and keeping his speech restrained,
he should divide and purify the food, then eat all the remaining alms that have been brought.

children.text: ekaś caren mahīm etāṃ niḥsaṅgaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: He should wander this earth alone, unattached and with his senses restrained,
sporting in the self, delighting in the self, self-possessed, and seeing equally.
Taking refuge in a solitary and secure place, with his heart purified by devotion to me,

children.text: ātmānaṃ cintayed ekam abhedena mayā muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sage should contemplate the one self as non-different from me.
With steadfastness in knowledge he should examine the bondage and liberation of the self:

children.text: bandha indriyavikṣepo mokṣa eṣāṃ ca saṃyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: bondage is the scattering of the senses, and liberation is their restraint.

children.text: tasmān niyamya ṣaḍvargaṃ madbhāvena caren muniḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, having restrained the group of six, the sage should live in a state of devotion to me,
dispassionate toward petty desires and having found great happiness in the self.
He should move about entering cities, villages, cowherd settlements, and caravans for the sake of alms,
wandering over the earth with its sacred places, rivers, mountains, forests, and hermitages.
He should frequently seek alms in the dwelling places of the forest-dweller's <s>āśrama</s>.
By food obtained through gleaning, his purified mind quickly becomes perfected and free from delusion.
He should not regard this visible world as substantially real, for what is seen perishes.
With an unattached mind he should cease from intentions concerning this world and the next.
This whole universe, gathered in the self as a compound of mind, speech, and breath,

children.text: sarvaṃ māyeti tarkeṇa svasthas tyaktvā na tat smaret ||
children.translated_text: he should reason to be entirely <s>māyā</s> (appearance); established in himself, having abandoned it, he should not dwell on it.
One who is steadfast in knowledge, or detached, or a devotee of mine without expectation,
should abandon the <s>āśramas</s> with their external marks and wander beyond the range of formal rule.

children.text: budho bālakavat krīḍet kuśalo jaḍavac caret
children.translated_text: Though wise, he should play like a child; though skillful, he should behave like a dullard.

children.text: vaded unmattavad vidvān gocaryāṃ naigamaś caret ||
children.translated_text: Though learned, he should speak like a madman; in his movements for alms he should conduct himself according to sacred custom.

children.text: vedavādarato na syān na pāṣaṇḍī na haitukaḥ
children.translated_text: He should not be attached to Vedic disputation, nor be a heretic, nor a mere rationalist.
In barren doctrinal quarrels he should not take up any side.

children.text: nodvijeta janād dhīro janaṃ codvejayen na tu
children.translated_text: The steadfast man should not be disturbed by people, nor should he disturb people.
He should endure harsh words and should not despise anyone.

children.text: deham uddiśya paśuvad vairaṃ kuryān na kenacit ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of the body, he should not make enmity with anyone like a beast.

children.text: eka eva paro hy ātmā bhūteṣv ātmany avasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: There is indeed one supreme self, present in beings and in oneself,
just as the moon is reflected in vessels of water; beings too share one self.

children.text: alabdhvā na viṣīdeta kāle kāle 'śanaṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: If at some time he does not obtain food, he should not be dejected.

children.text: labdhvā na hṛṣyed dhṛtimān ubhayaṃ daivatantritam ||
children.translated_text: If he obtains it, he should not rejoice; the resolute man should know both to be governed by fate.
He should make proper effort for food, since it sustains the life-breaths.

children.text: tattvaṃ vimṛśyate tena tad vijñāya vimucyate ||
children.translated_text: Through that, reality is investigated; knowing that, one is liberated.
The sage should eat food that comes by chance, whether excellent or inferior.

children.text: tathā vāsas tathā śayyāṃ prāptaṃ prāptaṃ bhajen muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too with clothing and bedding: whatever comes to him, he should make use of it.

children.text: śaucam ācamanaṃ snānaṃ na tu codanayā caret
children.translated_text: The knower should perform purity, sipping water, bathing,

children.text: anyāṃś ca niyamāñ jñānī yathāhaṃ līlayeśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and other observances not under compulsion, just as I, the Lord, do them playfully.

children.text: na hi tasya vikalpākhyā yā ca madvīkṣayā hatā
children.translated_text: For him there is no notion called difference, since it has been destroyed by seeing me.

children.text: ādehāntāt kvacit khyātis tataḥ sampadyate mayā ||
children.translated_text: Until the end of the body some appearance may remain; after that he attains union with me.
A self-possessed person who has become disillusioned with desires that end in suffering
and who longs to know my <s>dharma</s> should approach a sage as guru.
As a devoted, faithful, and non-envious disciple, he should serve him

children.text: yāvad brahma vijānīyān mām eva gurum ādṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: until he knows <s>brahman</s>, honoring the guru as none other than me.
But one whose group of six is uncontrolled and whose fierce senses are the charioteers,
who lacks knowledge and detachment and merely lives off the triple staff,

children.text: surān ātmānam ātmasthaṃ nihnute māṃ ca dharmahā
children.translated_text: destroys the gods, himself, the self within, and me; he is a destroyer of <s>dharma</s>.
With his impurities not yet matured away, he loses both this world and the next.

children.text: bhikṣor dharmaḥ śamo 'hiṃsā tapa īkṣā vanaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> of the mendicant is tranquility and nonviolence; that of the forest-dweller is austerity and discernment.
The householder's is protection of beings and sacrifice; the twice-born student's is service to the teacher.
Celibacy, austerity, purity, contentment, and friendliness toward beings
belong also to the householder who approaches his wife only in season; worship of me belongs to all.

children.text: iti māṃ yaḥ svadharmeṇa bhajen nityam ananyabhāk
children.translated_text: Thus whoever worships me constantly through his own <s>dharma</s>, with undivided devotion,
seeing my presence in all beings, obtains firm devotion to me.
By unfailing devotion, O <s>Uddhava</s>, he reaches me,
the great Lord of all worlds, <s>brahman</s>, the cause of the arising and passing away of all.
Thus, with his being purified by his own <s>dharma</s> and my course understood,
endowed with knowledge and realization, he comes to me before long.
This is the <s>dharma</s>, marked by proper conduct, for those who possess <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>.
That very <s>dharma</s>, joined with devotion to me, is the supreme maker of final blessedness.

children.text: etat te 'bhihitaṃ sādho bhavān pṛcchati yac ca mām
children.translated_text: This has been explained to you, O good man, as well as what you ask me.

children.text: yathā svadharmasaṃyukto bhakto māṃ samiyāt param ||
children.translated_text: so that a devotee, joined with his own <s>dharma</s>, may fully reach me, the supreme.
The Blessed Lord said:
One who is endowed with learning and sacred instruction, self-possessed, and not a mere reasoner,

children.text: māyāmātram idaṃ jñātvā jñānaṃ ca mayi saṃnyaset ||
children.translated_text: having known this to be only <s>māyā</s>, should also renounce knowledge in me.

children.text: jñāninas tv aham eveṣṭaḥ svārtho hetuś ca saṃmataḥ
children.translated_text: For those who know, I alone am beloved, accepted as their own good and as the cause,

children.text: svargaś caivāpavargaś ca nānyo 'rtho madṛte priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as heaven and as liberation too; apart from me there is no other dear goal.
Those perfected in knowledge and realization know my highest state;

children.text: jñānī priyatamo 'to me jñānenāsau bibharti mām ||
children.translated_text: therefore the knower is dearest to me, for by knowledge he bears me.

children.text: tapas tīrthaṃ japo dānaṃ pavitrāṇītarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Austerity, pilgrimage, recitation, giving, and other purifying acts

children.text: nālaṃ kurvanti tāṃ siddhiṃ yā jñānakalayā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: cannot accomplish the perfection that is produced by even a fraction of knowledge.

children.text: tasmāj jñānena sahitaṃ jñātvā svātmānam uddhava
children.translated_text: Therefore, having known your own self together with knowledge, O <s>Uddhava</s>,
endowed with knowledge and realization, worship me with the disposition of <s>bhakti</s>.
By the sacrifice of knowledge and realization, worshiping me, the Self within the self,
the sages reached perfection, for I indeed am the lord of all sacrifices.

children.text: tvayy uddhavāśrayati yas trividho vikāro māyāntarāpatati nādyapavargayor yat
children.translated_text: O <s>Uddhava</s>, the threefold transformation that takes refuge in you falls within <s>māyā</s>; it is not there at the beginning or at liberation.

children.text: janmādayo 'sya yad amī tava tasya kiṃ syur ādyantayor yad asato 'sti tad eva madhye ||
children.translated_text: Since birth and the rest belong to this body, what could they be to you? What is unreal at the beginning and end is just that in the middle also.
Śrī <s>Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: jñānaṃ viśuddhaṃ vipulaṃ yathaitad vairāgyavijñānayutaṃ purāṇam
children.translated_text: Tell me this pure, vast, ancient knowledge, joined with detachment and realization,

children.text: ākhyāhi viśveśvara viśvamūrte tvadbhaktiyogaṃ ca mahadvimṛgyam ||
children.translated_text: O lord of the universe, O whose form is the universe, and also the yoga of <s>bhakti</s>, sought by the great.
For one struck by the three sufferings, burning on the terrible road of becoming, O Lord,
I see no refuge other than the twin parasol of your feet, which pours down nectar.

children.text: daṣṭaṃ janaṃ saṃpatitaṃ bile 'smin kālāhinā kṣudrasukhorutarṣam
children.translated_text: This person has been bitten by the serpent of Time, has fallen into this pit, and is intensely thirsty for petty pleasure.
Lift him up; with liberating words sprinkle him, out of compassion, O great-souled one.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: ittham etat purā rājā bhīṣmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam
children.translated_text: In former times, in this very way, King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> asked <s>Bhīṣma</s>, the best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>,
while all of us were listening.
When the Bhārata war had ended, he was overwhelmed by the death of his friends;

children.text: śrutvā dharmān bahūn paścān mokṣadharmān apṛcchata ||
children.translated_text: after hearing many <s>dharmas</s>, he then asked about the <s>mokṣa-dharmas</s>.
I shall tell you those teachings heard from the mouth of <s>Devavrata</s>,
strengthened by knowledge, detachment, realization, faith, and <s>bhakti</s>.

children.text: navaikādaśa pañca trīn bhāvān bhūteṣu yena vai
children.translated_text: That by which one sees the nine, the eleven, the five, and the three principles among beings,

children.text: īkṣetāthāikam apy eṣu taj jñānaṃ mama niścitam ||
children.translated_text: and then also the one in these: that is knowledge, in my judgment.

children.text: etad eva hi vijñānaṃ na tathaikena yena yat
children.translated_text: This indeed is realization: that by which, through the one, one sees
the continuance, origination, and dissolution of entities whose nature is the three <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: ādāv ante ca madhye ca sṛjyāt sṛjyaṃ yad anviyāt
children.translated_text: At the beginning, at the end, and in the middle, that from which the created thing arises and which accompanies what is created,

children.text: punas tatpratisaṃkrāme yac chiṣyeta tad eva sat ||
children.translated_text: and which remains again at its reabsorption: that alone is real.
Revelation, direct perception, tradition, and inference are the four
means of knowledge; because they do not reach a final resting place and because of alternatives, one becomes detached.
Because actions have changing results, they are inauspicious all the way up to <s>Viriñci</s>'s world;

children.text: vipaścin naśvaraṃ paśyed adṛṣṭam api dṛṣṭavat ||
children.translated_text: the wise person should see even the unseen as perishable, just like what is seen.
The yoga of <s>bhakti</s> was already taught earlier to you, O sinless one, since you are dear to me;

children.text: punaś ca kathayiṣyāmi madbhakteḥ kāraṇaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: and again I shall tell the supreme cause of devotion to me.
Faith in my nectar-like stories, constant singing of me,

children.text: pariniṣṭhā ca pūjāyāṃ stutibhiḥ stavanaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: firm dedication to worship, and praising me with hymns,
respect for service, bowing down with all the limbs,
greater honor for the worship of my devotees, and the thought of me in all beings,
movement of the limbs for my purposes, and with speech the proclamation of my qualities,
the offering of the mind to me, and the abandonment of all desires,
the giving up of wealth for my sake, and also of enjoyment and pleasure,

children.text: iṣṭaṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ madarthaṃ yad vrataṃ tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sacrifice, gifts, oblations, recitation, vows, and austerity done for my sake:
by such <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Uddhava</s>, for human beings who dedicate themselves to me,
<s>bhakti</s> arises toward me; what other goal remains for such a person?
When the mind is offered to the Self, peaceful and strengthened by <s>sattva</s>,

children.text: dharmaṃ jñānaṃ sa vairāgyam aiśvaryaṃ cābhipadyate ||
children.translated_text: one attains <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, detachment, and lordly power.

children.text: yad arpitaṃ tad vikalpe indriyaiḥ paridhāvati
children.translated_text: When, turned toward distinctions, it runs about through the senses,
know that mind to be stained by <s>rajas</s>, fixed on the unreal, and the very opposite.
<s>Dharma</s> is declared to be what produces my <s>bhakti</s>; knowledge is the vision of oneness;
detachment is nonattachment to the <s>guṇas</s>, and lordly power is the powers beginning with minuteness.
Śrī <s>Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: yamaḥ katividhaḥ prokto niyamo vārikarṣaṇa kaḥ śamaḥ ko damaḥ kṛṣṇa ||
children.translated_text: How many kinds of restraint are taught, and what is observance, O subduer of foes? What is tranquility, what is self-control, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?

children.text: kā titikṣā dhṛtiḥ prabho kiṃ dānaṃ kiṃ tapaḥ śauryam
children.translated_text: What is forbearance? What is firmness, O Lord? What is giving, what is austerity, what is heroism?

children.text: kim satyam ṛtam ucyate kas tyāgaḥ kiṃ dhanaṃ ceṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: What is truth, and what is called rightness? What is renunciation, and what wealth is desirable?

children.text: ko yajñaḥ kā ca dakṣiṇā puṃsaḥ kiṃ svid balaṃ śrīman
children.translated_text: What is sacrifice, and what is the priestly gift? What indeed is a man's strength, O glorious one?

children.text: bhago lābhaś ca keśava kā vidyā hrīḥ parā kā śrīḥ ||
children.translated_text: What are fortune and gain, O <s>Keśava</s>? What is learning, what is modesty, and what is highest beauty?

children.text: kiṃ sukhaṃ duḥkham eva ca kaḥ paṇḍitaḥ kaś ca mūrkhaḥ
children.translated_text: What are happiness and suffering? Who is a learned person, and who is a fool?

children.text: kaḥ panthā utpathaś ca kaḥ kaḥ svargo narakaḥ kaḥ svit ||
children.translated_text: What is the path, and what is the wrong path? What is heaven, and what is hell?

children.text: ko bandhur uta kiṃ gṛham ka āḍhyaḥ ko daridro vā
children.translated_text: Who is a friend, and what is a home? Who is rich, and who is poor?

children.text: kṛpaṇaḥ kaḥ ka īśvaraḥ etān praśnān mama brūhi
children.translated_text: Who is wretched, and who is lord? Tell me these questions,
and their opposites as well, O lord of the good. The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: ahiṃsā satyam asteyam asaṅgo hrīr asaṃcayaḥ
children.translated_text: Nonviolence, truth, nonstealing, nonattachment, modesty, nonaccumulation,

children.text: āstikyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ ca maunaṃ sthairyaṃ kṣamābhayam ||
children.translated_text: faith in sacred authority, celibate discipline, silence, steadiness, forgiveness, and fearlessness.

children.text: śaucaṃ japas tapo homaḥ śraddhātithyaṃ madarcanam
children.translated_text: Purity, japa, austerity, oblation, faith, hospitality, and worship of me,
pilgrimage to sacred places, effort for the sake of others, contentment, and service to the teacher.

children.text: ete yamāḥ saniyamā ubhayor dvādaśa smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: These are remembered as the yamas together with the niyamas, twelve in each of the two groups;

children.text: puṃsām upāsitās tāta yathākāmaṃ duhanti hi ||
children.translated_text: when practiced by men, dear one, they indeed yield whatever is desired.
Calm is the intellect's fixed devotion to me; restraint is control of the senses.
Forbearance is endurance of suffering; firmness is mastery over the tongue and the genitals.

children.text: daṇḍanyāsaḥ paraṃ dānaṃ kāmatyāgas tapaḥ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Laying down the rod is the highest gift; abandonment of desire is remembered as austerity.
Conquest of one's own nature is valor, and truth is equal vision.

children.text: anyac ca sūnṛtā vāṇī kavibhiḥ parikīrtitā
children.translated_text: And, further, truthful and pleasing speech is praised by the poets.

children.text: karmasv asaṃgamaḥ śaucaṃ tyāgaḥ saṃnyāsa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Nonattachment in actions is purity; abandonment is called renunciation.

children.text: dharma iṣṭaṃ dhanaṃ nṝṇāṃ yajño 'haṃ bhagavattamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is the desired wealth of human beings; sacrifice is I, O best of the blessed.
The sacrificial gift is the communication of knowledge; breath-control is the highest strength.

children.text: bhago ma aiśvaro bhāvo lābho madbhaktir uttamaḥ
children.translated_text: My divine fortune is lordly being; the highest gain is devotion to me.
Knowledge is the negation of difference in the self; disgust is shame at wrongful acts.
Splendor consists in qualities such as independence; happiness is the passing beyond happiness and pain.
Pain is dependence on the pleasures of desire; the learned man is one who knows bondage and release.
A fool is one whose ego-notion rests on the body and the like; the path is remembered as my revealed teaching.
The wrong path is distraction of the mind; heaven is the rise of the quality of sattva.

children.text: narakas tamaunnāho bandhur gurur ahaṃ sakhe
children.translated_text: Hell is the swelling of tamas; the friend and teacher am I, O friend.

children.text: gṛhaṃ śarīraṃ mānuṣyaṃ guṇāḍhyo hy āḍhya ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The human body is the house; one rich in qualities is indeed called rich.

children.text: daridro yas tv asaṃtuṣṭaḥ kṛpaṇo yo 'jitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: But one who is discontent is poor, and one whose senses are unconquered is pitiable.
The master is one whose thought is unattached to the guṇas; attachment to the guṇas is the opposite.

children.text: eta uddhava te praśnāḥ sarve sādhu nirūpitāḥ
children.translated_text: These questions of yours, O <s>Uddhava</s>, have all been well explained.
What is the use of describing at length the mark of virtue and fault?
The seeing of virtue and fault is itself fault; virtue is what is free from both.
<s>Śrī Uddhava</s> said:

children.text: vidhiś ca pratiṣedhaś ca nigamo hīśvarasya te
children.translated_text: Your Veda, O Lord, is made of injunction and prohibition,
and it considers the virtue and fault of actions, O lotus-eyed one.
It also considers the distinctions of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, arising from mixed and regular lineage,
as well as substance, place, age, time, heaven, and hell.
Without a vision that distinguishes virtue from fault, your word
marked by prohibition and injunction, how could it be the highest good for human beings?
The Veda is the eye of ancestors, gods, and humans, O Lord;
it reveals the good in a matter not otherwise perceived, and also the means and the goal.

children.text: guṇadoṣabhidādṛṣṭir nigamāt te na hi svataḥ
children.translated_text: The vision of distinction between virtue and fault comes from your scripture, not by itself;

children.text: nigamenāpavādaś ca bhidāyā iti ha bhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and yet scripture also teaches the negation of distinction. Surely this is a perplexity.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: yogās trayo mayā proktā nṝṇāṃ śreyovidhitsayā
children.translated_text: Three yogas have been taught by me for human beings who wish to accomplish the highest good:

children.text: jñānaṃ karma ca bhaktiś ca nopāyo 'nyo 'sti kutracit ||
children.translated_text: knowledge, action, and devotion; there is no other means anywhere.
For those who are disillusioned and have renounced actions here, there is the yoga of knowledge;
but for those whose minds are not disillusioned with them, and who still desire, there is the yoga of action.

children.text: yadṛcchayā matkathādau jātaśraddhas tu yaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: But a person in whom faith in my stories and the like has arisen by chance,
being neither disillusioned nor overly attached, has the yoga of devotion as the giver of success.

children.text: tāvat karmāṇi kurvīta na nirvidyeta yāvatā
children.translated_text: One should perform actions only so long as one does not become disillusioned,

children.text: matkathāśravaṇādau vā śraddhā yāvan na jāyate ||
children.translated_text: or so long as faith in hearing my stories and the like has not arisen.
Established in his own <s>dharma</s>, worshiping with sacrifices and without desire for reward, O <s>Uddhava</s>,

children.text: na yāti svarganarakau yady anyan na samācaret ||
children.translated_text: he goes neither to heaven nor to hell, provided he does not practice anything else.
Living in this world, established in his own <s>dharma</s>, sinless and pure,

children.text: jñānaṃ viśuddham āpnoti madbhaktiṃ vā yadṛcchayā ||
children.translated_text: he obtains pure knowledge, or else devotion to me by chance.

children.text: svargiṇo 'py etam icchanti lokaṃ nirayiṇas tathā
children.translated_text: Even those in heaven desire this world, and so also do those in hell;
it is effective for knowledge and devotion, while both of those other states are ineffective for them.

children.text: na naraḥ svargatiṃ kāṅkṣen nārakīṃ vā vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: A discerning person should not long for a heavenly state, nor for a hellish one,

children.text: nemaṃ lokaṃ ca kāṅkṣeta dehāveśāt pramādyati ||
children.translated_text: nor should he long for this world; through absorption in the body he becomes heedless.

children.text: etad vidvān purā mṛtyor abhavāya ghaṭeta saḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing this, before death he should strive for non-becoming,

children.text: apramatta idaṃ jñātvā martyam apy arthasiddhidam ||
children.translated_text: being vigilant, having understood this mortal body, though mortal, to accomplish the goal.
As a bird, when the tree in which it has made its nest is being cut down by these cutters,

children.text: khagaḥ svaketam utsṛjya kṣemaṃ yāti hy alampaṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: abandons its own dwelling and, free from clinging, goes to safety,
so, knowing that life is being cut down by days and nights, trembling with fear,
one becomes free of attachment, knows the supreme, and, desireless, grows peaceful.

children.text: nṛdeham ādyaṃ sulabhaṃ sudurlabhaṃ plavaṃ sukalpaṃ gurukarṇadhāram
children.translated_text: The human body, the primal one, easy to obtain yet very hard to obtain, is a well-made boat with the guru as helmsman,

children.text: mayānukūlena nabhasvateritaṃ pumān bhavābdhiṃ na taret sa ātmahā ||
children.translated_text: driven by the favorable wind sent by me; the person who does not cross the ocean of becoming is a killer of himself.
When a yogin is disillusioned with undertakings, detached, and restrained in senses,
by practice he should hold the mind steady in the self.

children.text: dhāryamāṇaṃ mano yarhi bhrāmyad āśv anavasthitam
children.translated_text: When the mind being held quickly wanders and becomes unsteady,
he should, untiring, bring it under the self's control by a conciliatory path.
Having conquered breath and senses, he should not let the movement of the mind go free;
with an intellect endowed with sattva, he should bring the mind under the self's control.

children.text: eṣa vai paramo yogo manasaḥ saṃgrahaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: This indeed is remembered as the highest yoga: the gathering-in of the mind,
as one repeatedly seeks to know its disposition, like that of a horse to be tamed.
By <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, in reverse and forward order, of all states,
one should contemplate their arising and disappearance until the mind becomes clear.
For a person who is disillusioned, detached, and knows the teaching as stated,
the mind gives up its wickedness through repeated reflection on what has been contemplated.
By yogic paths such as yama, and by the science of inquiry,

children.text: mamārcopāsanābhir vā nānyair yogyaṃ smaren manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or by worshipful services to my image, one should regard the mind as fit for me, not by other means.

children.text: yadi kuryāt pramādena yogī karma vigarhitam
children.translated_text: If, through negligence, a yogin should perform a censured action...

children.text: yogenaiva dahed aṃho nānyat tatra kadācana ||
children.translated_text: By yoga alone should one burn away sin; there is never any other means for that.

children.text: sve sve 'dhikāre yā niṣṭhā sa guṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: Steadfastness in one's own proper sphere is declared a virtue.
By this, a rule has been made for actions that are impure by their very class,
through the prescription of merits and faults, with the wish that attachments be abandoned.
One in whom faith has arisen in my stories, and who is disenchanted with all actions,
knows desires to be made of suffering, yet is powerless to renounce them.

children.text: tato bhajeta māṃ prītaḥ śraddhālur dṛḍhaniścayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, being pleased, faithful, and firm in resolve, he should worship me,

children.text: juṣamāṇaś ca tān kāmān duḥkhodarkāṃś ca garhayan ||
children.translated_text: while still experiencing those desires, yet condemning them as ending in suffering.
For the sage who worships me constantly by the taught <s>bhakti-yoga</s> (discipline of devotion),

children.text: kāmā hṛdayyā naśyanti sarve mayi hṛdi sthite ||
children.translated_text: all desires lodged in the heart perish, when I stand in the heart.
The knot of the heart is split; all doubts are cut away.
His karmic acts are exhausted when I am seen as the Self of all.
Therefore, for the yogin endowed with devotion to me, whose self is fixed in me,

children.text: na jñānaṃ na ca vairāgyaṃ prāyaḥ śreyo bhaved iha ||
children.translated_text: knowledge and dispassion are generally not the means to the highest good here.

children.text: yat karmabhir yat tapasā jñānavairāgyataś ca yat
children.translated_text: Whatever is obtained by ritual actions, whatever by austerity, and whatever by knowledge and dispassion,
by yoga, by charity and <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), or by other means to blessedness,
my devotee obtains all of it easily through <s>bhakti-yoga</s> (discipline of devotion),
heaven, release, and my own abode, if in any way he desires them.

children.text: na kiṃcit sādhavo dhīrā bhaktā hy ekāntino mama
children.translated_text: Steady holy men, my one-pointed devotees, desire nothing at all,

children.text: vāñchanty api mayā dattaṃ kaivalyam apunarbhavam ||
children.translated_text: not even <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation), freedom from rebirth, when it is given by me.
They call nondependence the supreme and abundant <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (highest good);

children.text: tasmān nirāśiṣo bhaktir nirapekṣasya me bhavet ||
children.translated_text: therefore devotion to me belongs to one who is without wishes and without dependence.
For those who have exclusive devotion to me, virtues arising from merit and fault do not apply,
for they are holy men of equal mind who have reached beyond ordinary understanding.

children.text: evam etān mayā diṣṭān anutiṣṭhanti me pathaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, practicing these paths of mine that have been taught by me,

children.text: kṣemaṃ vindanti matsthānaṃ yad brahma paramaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: they find security, my own state, which they know as the supreme brahman.
The Blessed Lord said:
Those who abandon these paths of mine, consisting of devotion, knowledge, and action,

children.text: kṣudrān kāmāṃś calaiḥ prāṇair juṣantaḥ saṃsaranti te ||
children.translated_text: and enjoy petty desires with their unstable lives, wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> (rebirth).

children.text: sve sve 'dhikāre yā niṣṭhā sa guṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: Steadfastness in one's own proper sphere is declared a virtue,

children.text: viparyayas tu doṣaḥ syād ubhayor eṣa niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while the opposite is a fault; this is the settled conclusion concerning both.
Purity and impurity are prescribed even among things that are alike,
in order to distinguish a substance, as merit and fault, auspicious and inauspicious,
for the sake of <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty), practical dealings, and sustenance, O sinless one.
This conduct has been shown by me for those who bear the burden of <s>dharma</s>.
Earth, water, fire, air, and ether are the five elements of beings;
from <s>Brahmā</s> down to immovable things, bodies are made of them and joined with the self.
By the Veda, names and forms are imagined as diverse even among equal elements,
O <s>Uddhava</s>, for the accomplishment of the purposes of those beings.
For places, times, conditions, and things, O best among my people,
merit and fault are prescribed for the regulation of actions.
Among lands, one without the black antelope is impure and unfit for brahmins;
even one with the black antelope may be so if it is uncultivated, barren, or connected with <s>Sauvīra</s> and <s>Kīkaṭa</s>.

children.text: karmaṇyo guṇavān kālo dravyataḥ svata eva vā
children.translated_text: A time fit for action is virtuous by reason of the substance involved, or by its own nature;

children.text: yato nivartate karma sa doṣo 'karmakaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that by which an action ceases is remembered as faulty, a non-active time.

children.text: dravyasya śuddhyaśuddhī ca dravyeṇa vacanena ca
children.translated_text: The purity and impurity of a substance are determined by another substance and by injunction,
by consecration, by time, or by greatness and smallness.

children.text: śaktyāśaktyātha vā buddhyā samṛddhyā ca yad ātmane
children.translated_text: They are also determined by ability or inability, by understanding, and by prosperity,
according as people incur sin for themselves in accordance with place and condition.
For grain, wood, bone, thread, liquids, metals, and leather,
and for things made of earth, time, air, fire, earth, and water, singly or combined, serve as purifiers.
That by which a thing smeared with impurity removes its smell and stain,

children.text: bhajate prakṛtiṃ tasya tac chaucaṃ tāvad iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: and returns to its natural state, is regarded as its proper cleansing to that extent.
By bathing, charity, austerity, condition of life, strength, consecration, and ritual acts,

children.text: matsmṛtyā cātmanaḥ śaucaṃ śuddhaḥ karmācared dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by remembrance of me, the self is purified; being pure, a twice-born man should perform ritual action.
For a mantra, purification is correct understanding; for action, purification is offering it to me.

children.text: dharmaḥ sampadyate ṣaḍbhir adharmas tu viparyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (righteous order) is accomplished by six factors, while <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) is their opposite.

children.text: kvacid guṇo 'pi doṣaḥ syād doṣo 'pi vidhinā guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Sometimes even a virtue may be a fault, and even a fault may be a virtue by rule.
The regulation concerning merit and fault overrides merely their separate distinctions.
For fallen people, performing the same kind of action is not a further fall.

children.text: autpattiko guṇaḥ saṅgo na śayānaḥ pataty adhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Association that is innate is a quality; one who is already lying down does not fall lower.

children.text: yato yato nivarteta vimucyeta tatas tataḥ
children.translated_text: From whatever one withdraws, from that one is freed.
This is the secure <s>dharma</s> of human beings, removing sorrow, delusion, and fear.

children.text: viṣayeṣu guṇādhyāsāt puṃsaḥ saṅgas tato bhavet
children.translated_text: From attributing merit to sense objects, a person's attachment to them arises;

children.text: saṅgāt tatra bhavet kāmaḥ kāmād eva kalir nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: from attachment there arises desire for them, and from desire comes conflict among human beings.

children.text: kaler durviṣahaḥ krodhas tamas tam anuvartate
children.translated_text: From conflict comes anger, hard to endure, and darkness follows it.

children.text: tamasā grasyate puṃsaś cetanā vyāpinī drutam ||
children.translated_text: By that darkness a person's pervasive awareness is swiftly swallowed up.

children.text: tayā virahitaḥ sādho jantuḥ śūnyāya kalpate
children.translated_text: Deprived of that awareness, O holy one, a living being becomes as if empty.
Then, as if fainted or dead, he loses sight of his own good.
Through absorption in sense objects, he knows neither himself nor another.

children.text: vṛkṣajīvikayā jīvan vyarthaṃ bhastreva yaḥ śvasan ||
children.translated_text: Living like a tree, he breathes uselessly like a bellows.

children.text: phalaśrutir iyaṃ nṝṇāṃ na śreyo rocanaṃ param
children.translated_text: This praise of rewards for human beings is not the supreme good itself, but an inducement toward it.
It has been spoken with the intention of the highest good, like making medicine palatable.

children.text: utpattyaiva hi kāmeṣu prāṇeṣu svajaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: From their very birth, mortals have minds attached to pleasures, to their life-breaths, and to their own people,
to things that are causes of harm to the self.
A wise person would not again yoke to those rites people who do not know their own good and wander on the path of wrongdoing,

children.text: kathaṃ yuñjyāt punas teṣu tāṃs tamo viśato budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as they enter darkness; how could he join them again to those very things?
Some dull-minded people, not understanding this settled conclusion,

children.text: phalaśrutiṃ kusumitāṃ na vedajñā vadanti hi ||
children.translated_text: speak of the flowery statements of reward, for they are not knowers of the Veda.
Desirous, pitiable, and greedy, they think the blossoms are the fruit;

children.text: agnimugdhā dhūmatāntāḥ svaṃ lokaṃ na vidanti te ||
children.translated_text: bewildered by the fire and wearied by the smoke, they do not know their own true world.

children.text: na te mām aṅga jānanti hṛdisthaṃ ya idaṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: They do not know me, dear one, who am established in the heart and from whom this universe has come,
for they delight in hymns and recitations and are like people whose eyes are clouded by mist.

children.text: te me matam avijñāya parokṣaṃ viṣayātmakāḥ
children.translated_text: Not understanding my intention, which is indirect, and being absorbed in objects of sense,

children.text: hiṃsāyāṃ yadi rāgaḥ syād yajña eva na codanā ||
children.translated_text: they think that if there is a taste for violence, the sacrifice itself is the injunction.
The wicked, sporting in violence with slaughtered animals and desiring their own pleasure,
worship the gods, the ancestors, and the lords of beings with sacrifices.
This world is like a dream, unreal and pleasing merely to hear about;

children.text: āśiṣo hṛdi saṃkalpya tyajanty arthān yathā vaṇik ||
children.translated_text: having imagined blessings in their hearts, they abandon real goods, like merchants.
Established in <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, and attached to <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>tamas</s>,

children.text: upāsata indramukhyān devādīn na yathaiva mām ||
children.translated_text: they worship gods headed by <s>Indra</s> and the rest, but not me in that same way.

children.text: iṣṭveha devatā yajñair gatvā raṃsyāmahe divi
children.translated_text: They think, 'Having sacrificed to the deities here with sacrifices, we shall go and enjoy ourselves in heaven;
and when that ends, may we be born here again as great householders in great families.'
Thus, for men whose minds are distracted by flowery speech,
who are proud and excessively greedy, even talk of me is not pleasing.
The Vedas have <s>brahman</s> and the self as their subject, though these sections seem to have the three divisions as their subject;

children.text: parokṣavādā ṛṣayaḥ parokṣaṃ mama ca priyam ||
children.translated_text: the seers speak indirectly, and what is indirect is dear to me as well.
The <s>śabdabrahman</s> (brahman as sacred sound) is very hard to understand, made of breath, senses, and mind,
without end or far shore, deep and hard to enter, like the ocean.
Expanded by me through the infinite power of <s>brahman</s> in its vastness,
it is perceived among beings in the form of sound, like a fiber within a lotus stalk.
As a spider emits thread from its heart through its mouth,
so from space comes forth breath endowed with sound, joined with mind and having touch as its form.
The powerful one, made of meter and made of immortality, creates the thousandfold path,
adorned from <s>oṃkāra</s> with manifested consonants, vowels, sibilants, and semivowels.
Extending into diverse forms of speech and into meters increasing by four syllables,
it creates that great, endless, shoreless speech, and itself draws it back again.

children.text: gāyatry uṣṇig anuṣṭup ca bṛhatī paṅktir eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Uṣṇih</s>, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Paṅkti</s>,
<s>Triṣṭubh</s>, <s>Jagatī</s>, <s>Aticchandas</s>, <s>Atyaṣṭi</s>, <s>Atijagatī</s>, and <s>Virāṭ</s> are its meters.

children.text: kiṃ vidhatte kim ācaṣṭe kim anūdya vikalpayet
children.translated_text: What it enjoins, what it declares, what it restates and then differentiates,

children.text: ity asyā hṛdayaṃ loke nānyo mad veda kaścana ||
children.translated_text: no one in the world knows this heart of it except me.

children.text: māṃ vidhatte 'bhidhatte māṃ vikalpyāpohyate tv aham
children.translated_text: It enjoins me; it names me. Yet I am what is established after distinction has been imagined and then removed.

children.text: etāvān sarvavedārthaḥ śabda āsthāya māṃ bhidām
children.translated_text: This much is the whole meaning of the Veda: speech rests on me and makes distinctions,
then finally restates them as mere <s>māyā</s> (illusion) and, rejecting them, becomes clear.
